Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Abhidhammapiṭake

The Abhidhamma Piṭaka

Vibhaṅgapāḷi

The Book of Analysis

1. Khandhavibhaṅgo

1. Analysis of the Aggregates

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. Exposition in the Manner of the Suttas

1. Pañcakkhandhā [T 0.0001][M 0.0001][P 0.0001][V 0.0001] – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho.

1. The five aggregates are: the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.

1. Rūpakkhandho

1. The Aggregate of Form

2. Tattha [V 0.0002] katamo rūpakkhandho? Yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho.

2. Herein, what is the aggregate of form? Whatever form there is—past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; that which is far or near—all this, having been brought together and condensed, is called the aggregate of form.

3. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ atītaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgataṃ uppajjitvā vigataṃ atītaṃ atītaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ atītaṃ.

3. Herein, what is past form? Whatever form has passed, ceased, departed, changed, gone to cessation, utterly gone to cessation; having arisen, has departed; is past, included in the category of the past—the four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements—this is called past form.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ anāgataṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtaṃ anuppannaṃ asamuppannaṃ anuṭṭhitaṃ asamuṭṭhitaṃ anāgataṃ anāgataṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ anāgataṃ.

Herein, what is future form? Whatever form is not yet born, not yet become, not yet well born, not yet produced, not yet fully produced, not yet manifest, not yet arisen, not yet fully arisen, not yet established, not yet fully established; is future, included in the category of the future—the four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements—this is called future form.

Tattha [M 0.0002] katamaṃ rūpaṃ paccuppannaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtaṃ uppannaṃ [T 0.0002] samuppannaṃ uṭṭhitaṃ samuṭṭhitaṃ paccuppannaṃ paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cattāro [P 0.0002] ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ paccuppannaṃ.

Herein, what is present form? Whatever form is born, has become, is well born, is produced, is fully produced, is manifest, has arisen, has fully arisen, is established, is fully established; is present, included in the category of the present—the four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements—this is called present form.

4. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ ajjhattaṃ.

4. Herein, what is internal form? Whatever form, for those various beings, is internal, personal, one's own, pertaining to the individual, appropriated—the four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements—this is called internal form.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ bahiddhā? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ bahiddhā.

Herein, what is external form? Whatever form, for those various other beings, other persons, is internal, personal, one's own, pertaining to the individual, appropriated—the four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements—this is called external form.

5. Tattha [V 0.0003] katamaṃ rūpaṃ oḷārikaṃ? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ oḷārikaṃ.

5. Herein, what is gross form? The eye-base... to... the tangible-base—this is called gross form.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ sukhumaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro kabaḷiṃkāro (sī. syā.) āhāro – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ sukhumaṃ.

Herein, what is subtle form? The female faculty... to... edible food—this is called subtle form.

6. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ hīnaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ uññātaṃ avaññātaṃ hīḷitaṃ paribhūtaṃ acittīkataṃ hīnaṃ hīnamataṃ hīnasammataṃ aniṭṭhaṃ akantaṃ amanāpaṃ, rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ hīnaṃ.

6. Herein, what is inferior form? Whatever form, for those various beings, is despised, disregarded, reviled, scorned, treated without respect, is inferior, considered inferior, regarded as inferior, undesirable, unloved, and displeasing—visible objects, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangible objects—this is called inferior form.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ paṇītaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ anuññātaṃ anavaññātaṃ ahīḷitaṃ aparibhūtaṃ cittīkataṃ paṇītaṃ paṇītamataṃ paṇītasammataṃ iṭṭhaṃ kantaṃ manāpaṃ, rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ paṇītaṃ. Taṃ taṃ vā pana [T 0.0003] rūpaṃ upādāyupādāya rūpaṃ hīnaṃ paṇītaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Herein, what is superior form? Whatever form, for those various beings, is not despised, not disregarded, not reviled, not scorned, treated with respect, is superior, considered superior, regarded as superior, desirable, loved, and pleasing—visible objects, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangible objects—this is called superior form. Furthermore, with reference to this or that form, form should be understood as inferior and superior.

7. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ dūre? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ anāsanne anupakaṭṭhe dūre asantike – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ dūre.

7. Herein, what is distant form? The female faculty... to... edible food, or whatever other form there is that is not near, not in proximity, distant, not close—this is called distant form.

Tattha [M 0.0003][P 0.0003] katamaṃ rūpaṃ santike? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ āsanne upakaṭṭhe avidūre santike – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana rūpaṃ upādāyupādāya rūpaṃ dūre santike daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Herein, what is near form? The eye-base... to... the tangible-base, or whatever other form there is that is near, in proximity, not far, close—this is called near form. Furthermore, with reference to this or that form, form should be understood as distant or near.

2. Vedanākkhandho

2. The Aggregate of Feeling

8. Tattha katamo vedanākkhandho? Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanākkhandho.

8. Herein, what is the aggregate of feeling? Whatever feeling there is—past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; that which is far or near—all this, having been brought together and condensed, is called the aggregate of feeling.

9. Tattha [V 0.0004] katamā vedanā atītā? Yā vedanā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā atītā.

9. Herein, what is past feeling? Whatever feeling has passed, ceased, departed, changed, gone to cessation, utterly gone to cessation; having arisen, has departed; is past, included in the category of the past—pleasant feeling, painful feeling, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling—this is called past feeling.

Tattha katamā vedanā anāgatā? Yā vedanā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā anāgatā.

Herein, what is future feeling? Whatever feeling is not yet born, not yet become, not yet well born, not yet produced, not yet fully produced, not yet manifest, not yet arisen, not yet fully arisen, not yet established, not yet fully established; is future, included in the category of the future—pleasant feeling, painful feeling, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling—this is called future feeling.

Tattha katamā vedanā paccuppannā? Yā vedanā jātā bhūtā sañjātā [T 0.0004] nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā paccuppannā.

Herein, what is present feeling? Whatever feeling is born, has become, is well born, is produced, is fully produced, is manifest, has arisen, has fully arisen, is established, is fully established; is present, included in the category of the present—pleasant feeling, painful feeling, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling—this is called present feeling.

10. Tattha katamā vedanā ajjhattā? Yā vedanā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā ajjhattā.

10. Herein, what is internal feeling? Whatever feeling, for those various beings, is internal, personal, one's own, pertaining to the individual, appropriated—pleasant feeling, painful feeling, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling—this is called internal feeling.

Tattha katamā vedanā bahiddhā? Yā vedanā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā bahiddhā.

Herein, what is external feeling? Whatever feeling of those various other beings and other individuals is internal, personal, one's own, pertaining to the individual, and appropriated—pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling—this is called external feeling.

11. Tattha [M 0.0004] katamā vedanā oḷārikā sukhumā? Akusalā vedanā oḷārikā, kusalābyākatā vedanā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā vedanā oḷārikā, abyākatā vedanā sukhumā. Dukkhā [P 0.0004] vedanā oḷārikā, sukhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhā vedanā oḷārikā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā sukhumā. Asamāpannassa vedanā oḷārikā, samāpannassa vedanā sukhumā. Sāsavā vedanā oḷārikā, anāsavā vedanā sukhumā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana vedanaṃ upādāyupādāya vedanā oḷārikā sukhumā daṭṭhabbā.

11. Herein, what feeling is gross, what is subtle? Unwholesome feeling is gross; wholesome and indeterminate feeling is subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome feeling is gross; indeterminate feeling is subtle. Painful feeling is gross; pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is subtle. Pleasant and painful feeling is gross; neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is subtle. The feeling of one who has not attained absorption is gross; the feeling of one who has attained absorption is subtle. Feeling with taints is gross; feeling without taints is subtle. Or again, in consideration of this or that feeling, feeling should be understood as gross and subtle.

12. Tattha [V 0.0005] katamā vedanā hīnā paṇītā? Akusalā vedanā hīnā, kusalābyākatā [T 0.0005] vedanā paṇītā. Kusalākusalā vedanā hīnā, abyākatā vedanā paṇītā. Dukkhā vedanā hīnā, sukhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhā vedanā hīnā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā paṇītā. Asamāpannassa vedanā hīnā, samāpannassa vedanā paṇītā. Sāsavā vedanā hīnā, anāsavā vedanā paṇītā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana vedanaṃ upādāyupādāya vedanā hīnā paṇītā daṭṭhabbā.

12. Herein, what feeling is inferior, what is superior? Unwholesome feeling is inferior; wholesome and indeterminate feeling is superior. Wholesome and unwholesome feeling is inferior; indeterminate feeling is superior. Painful feeling is inferior; pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is superior. Pleasant and painful feeling is inferior; neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is superior. The feeling of one who has not attained absorption is inferior; the feeling of one who has attained absorption is superior. Feeling with taints is inferior; feeling without taints is superior. Or again, in consideration of this or that feeling, feeling should be understood as inferior and superior.

13. Tattha katamā vedanā dūre? Akusalā vedanā kusalābyākatāhi vedanāhi dūre; kusalābyākatā vedanā akusalāya vedanāya dūre; kusalā vedanā akusalābyākatāhi vedanāhi dūre; akusalābyākatā vedanā kusalāya vedanāya dūre; abyākatā vedanā kusalākusalāhi vedanāhi dūre; kusalākusalā vedanā abyākatāya vedanāya dūre. Dukkhā vedanā sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi dūre; sukhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā dukkhāya vedanāya dūre; sukhā vedanā dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi dūre; dukkhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā sukhāya vedanāya dūre; adukkhamasukhā vedanā sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi dūre; sukhadukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya dūre. Asamāpannassa vedanā samāpannassa vedanāya dūre; samāpannassa vedanā asamāpannassa vedanāya dūre. Sāsavā vedanā anāsavāya vedanāya dūre; anāsavā vedanā sāsavāya vedanāya dūre – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā dūre.

13. Herein, what feeling is distant? Unwholesome feeling is distant from wholesome and indeterminate feelings; wholesome and indeterminate feelings are distant from unwholesome feeling. Wholesome feeling is distant from unwholesome and indeterminate feelings; unwholesome and indeterminate feelings are distant from wholesome feeling. Indeterminate feeling is distant from wholesome and unwholesome feelings; wholesome and unwholesome feelings are distant from indeterminate feeling. Painful feeling is distant from pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are distant from painful feeling. Pleasant feeling is distant from painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are distant from pleasant feeling. Neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is distant from pleasant and painful feelings; pleasant and painful feelings are distant from neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The feeling of one who has not attained absorption is distant from the feeling of one who has attained absorption; the feeling of one who has attained absorption is distant from the feeling of one who has not attained absorption. Feeling with taints is distant from feeling without taints; feeling without taints is distant from feeling with taints—this is called distant feeling.

Tattha katamā vedanā santike? Akusalā vedanā akusalāya [T 0.0006] vedanāya santike; kusalā vedanā kusalāya vedanāya santike; abyākatā [M 0.0005] vedanā abyākatāya vedanāya santike. Dukkhā vedanā dukkhāya vedanāya santike; sukhā vedanā sukhāya vedanāya santike; adukkhamasukhā vedanā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya santike[P 0.0005]. Asamāpannassa vedanā asamāpannassa vedanāya santike; samāpannassa vedanā samāpannassa vedanāya santike. Sāsavā vedanā sāsavāya vedanāya santike; anāsavā vedanā anāsavāya vedanāya santike. Ayaṃ vuccati vedanā santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana vedanaṃ upādāyupādāya vedanā dūre santike daṭṭhabbā.

Herein, what feeling is near? Unwholesome feeling is near to unwholesome feeling; wholesome feeling is near to wholesome feeling; indeterminate feeling is near to indeterminate feeling. Painful feeling is near to painful feeling; pleasant feeling is near to pleasant feeling; neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is near to neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The feeling of one who has not attained absorption is near to the feeling of one who has not attained absorption; the feeling of one who has attained absorption is near to the feeling of one who has attained absorption. Feeling with taints is near to feeling with taints; feeling without taints is near to feeling without taints. This is called near feeling. Or again, in consideration of this or that feeling, feeling should be understood as distant and near.

3. Saññākkhandho

3. The Aggregate of Perception

14. Tattha [V 0.0006] katamo saññākkhandho? Yā kāci saññā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati saññākkhandho.

14. Herein, what is the aggregate of perception? Whatever perception there is, whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—having collected and grouped them together as one, this is called the aggregate of perception.

15. Tattha katamā saññā atītā? Yā saññā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā atītā.

15. Herein, what is past perception? Whatever perception has passed, ceased, vanished, changed, set, disappeared, having arisen has vanished, is past, and is included in the past portion—perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact—this is called past perception.

Tattha katamā saññā anāgatā? Yā saññā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā [T 0.0007] asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā anāgatā.

Herein, what is future perception? Whatever perception is not yet born, not yet become, not yet generated, not yet arisen, not yet newly arisen, not yet apparent, not yet produced, not yet well produced, not yet established, not yet well established, not yet come, and is included in the future portion—perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact—this is called future perception.

Tattha katamā saññā paccuppannā? Yā saññā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā paccuppannā.

Herein, what is present perception? Whatever perception is born, become, generated, arisen, newly arisen, apparent, produced, well produced, established, well established, present, and is included in the present portion—perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact—this is called present perception.

16. Tattha [M 0.0006] katamā saññā ajjhattā? Yā saññā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā ajjhattā.

16. Herein, what is internal perception? Whatever perception of those various beings is internal, personal, one's own, pertaining to the individual, and appropriated—perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact—this is called internal perception.

Tattha [V 0.0007] katamā saññā bahiddhā? Yā saññā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā bahiddhā.

Herein, what is external perception? Whatever perception of those various other beings, other persons, is internal, personal, their own, individual, and appropriated—perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-contact—this is called external perception.

17. Tattha [P 0.0006] katamā saññā oḷārikā sukhumā? Paṭighasamphassajā saññā oḷārikā, adhivacanasamphassajā saññā sukhumā. Akusalā saññā oḷārikā, kusalābyākatā saññā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā saññā oḷārikā, abyākatā saññā sukhumā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā oḷārikā, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā oḷārikā[T 0.0008], adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhumā. Asamāpannassa saññā oḷārikā, samāpannassa saññā sukhumā. Sāsavā saññā oḷārikā, anāsavā saññā sukhumā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana saññaṃ upādāyupādāya saññā oḷārikā sukhumā daṭṭhabbā.

17. Herein, what is gross and subtle perception? Perception born of sensory-impact-contact is gross; perception born of designation-contact is subtle. Unwholesome perception is gross; wholesome and indeterminate perception is subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome perception is gross; indeterminate perception is subtle. Perception associated with painful feeling is gross; perception associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings is subtle. Perception associated with pleasant and painful feelings is gross; perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is subtle. The perception of one not in meditative attainment is gross; the perception of one in meditative attainment is subtle. Perception with taints is gross; perception without taints is subtle. Or else, depending on this or that perception, perception should be understood as gross or subtle.

18. Tattha katamā saññā hīnā paṇītā? Akusalā saññā hīnā, kusalābyākatā saññā paṇītā. Kusalākusalā saññā hīnā, abyākatā saññā paṇītā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā hīnā, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā hīnā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā paṇītā. Asamāpannassa saññā hīnā, samāpannassa saññā paṇītā. Sāsavā saññā hīnā, anāsavā saññā paṇītā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana saññaṃ upādāyupādāya saññā hīnā paṇītā daṭṭhabbā.

18. Herein, what is inferior and superior perception? Unwholesome perception is inferior; wholesome and indeterminate perception is superior. Wholesome and unwholesome perception is inferior; indeterminate perception is superior. Perception associated with painful feeling is inferior; perception associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings is superior. Perception associated with pleasant and painful feelings is inferior; perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is superior. The perception of one not in meditative attainment is inferior; the perception of one in meditative attainment is superior. Perception with taints is inferior; perception without taints is superior. Or else, depending on this or that perception, perception should be understood as inferior or superior.

19. Tattha katamā saññā dūre? Akusalā saññā kusalābyākatāhi saññāhi dūre; kusalābyākatā saññā akusalāya saññāya [M 0.0007] dūre; kusalā saññā akusalābyākatāhi saññāhi dūre; akusalābyākatā saññā kusalāya saññāya dūre. Abyākatā saññā kusalākusalāhi saññāhi dūre; kusalākusalā saññā abyākatāya saññāya dūre. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya [T 0.0009] ca vedanāhi sampayuttāhi saññāhi dūre; sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya [V 0.0008] saññāya dūre; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttāhi saññāhi dūre; dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya dūre; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttāhi saññāhi dūre; sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya dūre. Asamāpannassa saññā samāpannassa saññāya dūre; samāpannassa [P 0.0007] saññā asamāpannassa saññāya dūre. Sāsavā saññā anāsavāya saññāya dūre; anāsavā saññā sāsavāya saññāya dūre – ayaṃ vuccati saññā dūre.

19. Herein, what is perception that is far? Unwholesome perception is far from wholesome and indeterminate perceptions; wholesome and indeterminate perceptions are far from unwholesome perception. Wholesome perception is far from unwholesome and indeterminate perceptions; unwholesome and indeterminate perceptions are far from wholesome perception. Indeterminate perception is far from wholesome and unwholesome perceptions; wholesome and unwholesome perceptions are far from indeterminate perception. Perception associated with painful feeling is far from perceptions associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; perceptions associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are far from perception associated with painful feeling. Perception associated with pleasant feeling is far from perceptions associated with painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; perceptions associated with painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are far from perception associated with pleasant feeling. Perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is far from perceptions associated with pleasant and painful feelings; perceptions associated with pleasant and painful feelings are far from perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The perception of one not in meditative attainment is far from the perception of one in meditative attainment; the perception of one in meditative attainment is far from the perception of one not in meditative attainment. Perception with taints is far from perception without taints; perception without taints is far from perception with taints—this is called perception that is far.

Tattha katamā saññā santike? Akusalā saññā akusalāya saññāya santike; kusalā saññā kusalāya saññāya santike; abyākatā saññā abyākatāya saññāya santike. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya santike; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya santike; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya santike. Asamāpannassa saññā asamāpannassa saññāya santike; samāpannassa saññā samāpannassa saññāya santike. Sāsavā saññā [T 0.0010] sāsavāya saññāya santike; anāsavā saññā anāsavāya saññāya santike. Ayaṃ vuccati saññā santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana saññaṃ upādāyupādāya saññā dūre santike daṭṭhabbā.

Therein, what is perception that is near? Unwholesome perception is near to unwholesome perception; wholesome perception is near to wholesome perception; indeterminate perception is near to indeterminate perception. Perception associated with painful feeling is near to perception associated with painful feeling; perception associated with pleasant feeling is near to perception associated with pleasant feeling; perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is near to perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The perception of one not in meditative attainment is near to the perception of one not in meditative attainment; the perception of one in meditative attainment is near to the perception of one in meditative attainment. Perception with taints is near to perception with taints; perception without taints is near to perception without taints. This is called perception that is near. Or else, depending on this or that perception, perception should be understood as far or near.

4. Saṅkhārakkhandho

4. The Aggregate of Formations

20. Tattha katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā [M 0.0008] vā paṇītā vā ye dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati saṅkhārakkhandho.

20. Therein, what is the aggregate of formations? Whatever formations there are—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—having gathered them together and collected them as one, this is called the aggregate of formations.

21. Tattha katame saṅkhārā atītā? Ye saṅkhārā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā [V 0.0009] sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā atītā.

21. Therein, what are past formations? Those formations that are past, have ceased, departed, changed, set, passed away, having arisen have departed, are past, and are included in the past portion—namely, volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact—these are called past formations.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā anāgatā? Ye saṅkhārā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā anāgatā.

Therein, what are future formations? Those formations that are not yet born, not yet become, not yet produced, not yet brought forth, not yet newly produced, not yet manifest, not yet arisen, not yet fully arisen, not yet established, not yet fully established, not yet come, and are included in the future portion—namely, volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact—these are called future formations.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā paccuppannā? Ye saṅkhārā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā [P 0.0008] paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā [T 0.0011] cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā paccuppannā.

Therein, what are present formations? Those formations that are born, have become, are produced, are brought forth, are newly produced, are manifest, have arisen, have fully arisen, are established, are fully established, are present, and are included in the present portion—namely, volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact—these are called present formations.

22. Tattha katame saṅkhārā ajjhattā? Ye saṅkhārā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā ajjhattā.

22. Therein, what are internal formations? Those formations of those various beings that are internal, personal, one's own, individual, and appropriated—namely, volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact—these are called internal formations.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā bahiddhā? Ye saṅkhārā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā bahiddhā.

Therein, what are external formations? Those formations of those various other beings, other persons, that are internal, personal, one's own, individual, and appropriated—namely, volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact—these are called external formations.

23. Tattha [M 0.0009] katame saṅkhārā oḷārikā sukhumā? Akusalā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, kusalābyākatā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, abyākatā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi [V 0.0010] sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā oḷārikā, samāpannassa saṅkhārā sukhumā. Sāsavā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, anāsavā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Te te vā pana saṅkhāre upādāyupādāya saṅkhārā oḷārikā sukhumā daṭṭhabbā.

23. Therein, what are gross and subtle formations? Unwholesome formations are gross; wholesome and indeterminate formations are subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome formations are gross; indeterminate formations are subtle. Formations associated with painful feeling are gross; formations associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are subtle. Formations associated with pleasant and painful feelings are gross; formations associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are subtle. The formations of one who has not entered attainment are gross; the formations of one who has entered attainment are subtle. Formations with taints are gross; formations without taints are subtle. Furthermore, depending on this or that formation, formations should be understood as gross or subtle.

24. Tattha katame saṅkhārā hīnā paṇītā? Akusalā saṅkhārā hīnā, kusalābyākatā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Kusalākusalā saṅkhārā hīnā, abyākatā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā hīnā[T 0.0012], sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā hīnā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā hīnā, samāpannassa saṅkhārā paṇītā. Sāsavā saṅkhārā hīnā, anāsavā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Te te vā pana saṅkhāre upādāyupādāya saṅkhārā hīnā paṇītā daṭṭhabbā.

24. Therein, what are inferior and superior formations? Unwholesome formations are inferior; wholesome and indeterminate formations are superior. Wholesome and unwholesome formations are inferior; indeterminate formations are superior. Formations associated with painful feeling are inferior; formations associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are superior. Formations associated with pleasant and painful feelings are inferior; formations associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are superior. The formations of one who has not entered attainment are inferior; the formations of one who has entered attainment are superior. Formations with taints are inferior; formations without taints are superior. Furthermore, depending on this or that formation, formations should be understood as inferior or superior.

25. Tattha katame saṅkhārā dūre? Akusalā saṅkhārā kusalābyākatehi saṅkhārehi dūre; kusalābyākatā saṅkhārā akusalehi saṅkhārehi dūre; kusalā saṅkhārā akusalābyākatehi saṅkhārehi dūre; akusalābyākatā saṅkhārā kusalehi saṅkhārehi dūre; abyākatā [P 0.0009] saṅkhārā kusalākusalehi saṅkhārehi dūre; kusalākusalā saṅkhārā abyākatehi saṅkhārehi dūre. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; adukkhamasukhāya [M 0.0010] vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre[T 0.0013]. Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā samāpannassa saṅkhārehi dūre; samāpannassa saṅkhārā asamāpannassa saṅkhārehi dūre. Sāsavā saṅkhārā anāsavehi saṅkhārehi dūre; anāsavā saṅkhārā sāsavehi saṅkhārehi dūre. Ime vuccanti saṅkhārā dūre.

25. Therein, what are distant formations? Unwholesome formations are distant from wholesome and indeterminate formations; wholesome and indeterminate formations are distant from unwholesome formations. Wholesome formations are distant from unwholesome and indeterminate formations; unwholesome and indeterminate formations are distant from wholesome formations. Indeterminate formations are distant from wholesome and unwholesome formations; wholesome and unwholesome formations are distant from indeterminate formations. Formations associated with painful feeling are distant from formations associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; formations associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are distant from formations associated with painful feeling. Formations associated with pleasant feeling are distant from formations associated with painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; formations associated with painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are distant from formations associated with pleasant feeling. Formations associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are distant from formations associated with pleasant and painful feelings; formations associated with pleasant and painful feelings are distant from formations associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The formations of one who has not entered attainment are distant from the formations of one who has entered attainment; the formations of one who has entered attainment are distant from the formations of one who has not entered attainment. Formations with taints are distant from formations without taints; formations without taints are distant from formations with taints. These are called distant formations.

Tattha [V 0.0011] katame saṅkhārā santike? Akusalā saṅkhārā akusalānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; kusalā saṅkhārā kusalānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; abyākatā saṅkhārā abyākatānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā asamāpannassa saṅkhārānaṃ santike; samāpannassa saṅkhārā samāpannassa saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Sāsavā saṅkhārā sāsavānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; anāsavā saṅkhārā anāsavānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Ime vuccanti saṅkhārā santike. Te te vā pana saṅkhāre upādāyupādāya saṅkhārā dūre santike daṭṭhabbā.

Herein, which formations are near? Unwholesome formations are near unwholesome formations; wholesome formations are near wholesome formations; indeterminate formations are near indeterminate formations. Formations associated with painful feeling are near formations associated with painful feeling; formations associated with pleasant feeling are near formations associated with pleasant feeling; formations associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are near formations associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The formations of one who has not attained are near the formations of one who has not attained; the formations of one who has attained are near the formations of one who has attained. Formations with taints are near formations with taints; formations without taints are near formations without taints. These are called near formations. Or again, with reference to those various formations, formations should be understood as distant or near.

5. Viññāṇakkhandho

5. The Aggregate of Consciousness

26. Tattha katamo viññāṇakkhandho? Yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇakkhandho.

26. Herein, what is the aggregate of consciousness? Whatever consciousness there is, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—having gathered and compacted all that into one, this is called the aggregate of consciousness.

27. Tattha [T 0.0014] katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ? Yaṃ [P 0.0010] viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgataṃ uppajjitvā vigataṃ atītaṃ atītaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ.

27. Herein, which consciousness is past? That consciousness which is past, has ceased, is gone, is transformed, has set, has completely set, having arisen is gone, is past, is included in the portion of the past—eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness—this is called past consciousness.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ anāgataṃ? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtaṃ anuppannaṃ asamuppannaṃ anuṭṭhitaṃ asamuṭṭhitaṃ [M 0.0011] anāgataṃ anāgataṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ anāgataṃ.

Herein, which consciousness is future? That consciousness which is not yet born, has not yet become, is not yet generated, is not yet produced, is not yet newly produced, has not yet appeared, has not yet arisen, has not yet fully arisen, has not yet come forth, has not yet fully come forth, has not yet come, is included in the portion of the future—eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness—this is called future consciousness.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ paccuppannaṃ? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtaṃ uppannaṃ samuppannaṃ uṭṭhitaṃ samuṭṭhitaṃ paccuppannaṃ paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [V 0.0012] sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ paccuppannaṃ.

Herein, which consciousness is present? That consciousness which is being born, is becoming, is being generated, is being produced, is being newly produced, is appearing, is arising, is fully arising, is coming forth, is fully coming forth, is present, is included in the portion of the present—eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness—this is called present consciousness.

28. Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ.

28. Herein, which consciousness is internal? That consciousness of those various beings which is internal, personal, one's own, individual, appropriated—eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness—this is called internal consciousness.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ bahiddhā? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ bahiddhā.

Herein, which consciousness is external? That consciousness of those various other beings, other persons, which is internal, personal, their own, individual, appropriated—eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness—this is called external consciousness.

29. Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ sukhumaṃ? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, kusalābyākatā viññāṇā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā viññāṇā oḷārikā[T 0.0015], abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā oḷārikā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Taṃ taṃ vā pana viññāṇaṃ upādāyupādāya viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ sukhumaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

29. Herein, which consciousness is gross, and which is subtle? Unwholesome consciousness is gross; wholesome and indeterminate consciousnesses are subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome consciousnesses are gross; indeterminate consciousness is subtle. Consciousness associated with painful feeling is gross; consciousnesses associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are subtle. Consciousnesses associated with pleasant and painful feelings are gross; consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is subtle. The consciousness of one who has not attained meditative absorption is gross; the consciousness of one who has attained meditative absorption is subtle. Consciousness with taints is gross; consciousness without taints is subtle. Or again, depending on this or that consciousness, gross consciousness and subtle consciousness are to be understood.

30. Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ paṇītaṃ? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, kusalābyākatā viññāṇā paṇītā[P 0.0011]. Kusalākusalā viññāṇā hīnā, abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā hīnā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya [M 0.0012] sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Taṃ taṃ vā pana viññāṇaṃ upādāyupādāya viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ paṇītaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

30. Herein, which consciousness is inferior, and which is superior? Unwholesome consciousness is inferior; wholesome and indeterminate consciousnesses are superior. Wholesome and unwholesome consciousnesses are inferior; indeterminate consciousness is superior. Consciousness associated with painful feeling is inferior; consciousnesses associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are superior. Consciousnesses associated with pleasant and painful feelings are inferior; consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is superior. The consciousness of one who has not attained meditative absorption is inferior; the consciousness of one who has attained meditative absorption is superior. Consciousness with taints is inferior; consciousness without taints is superior. Or again, depending on this or that consciousness, inferior consciousness and superior consciousness are to be understood.

31. Tattha [V 0.0013] katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ dūre? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ kusalābyākatehi viññāṇehi dūre; kusalābyākatā viññāṇā akusalā viññāṇā dūre; kusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ akusalābyākatehi viññāṇehi dūre; akusalābyākatā viññāṇā kusalā viññāṇā dūre; abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ kusalākusalehi [T 0.0016] viññāṇehi dūre; kusalākusalā viññāṇā abyākatā viññāṇā dūre. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi viññāṇehi dūre; sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā viññāṇā dūre; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi viññāṇehi dūre; dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā viññāṇā dūre; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttehi viññāṇehi dūre; sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā viññāṇā dūre. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇā dūre; samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ asamāpannassa viññāṇā dūre. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ anāsavā viññāṇā dūre; anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ sāsavā viññāṇā dūre – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ dūre.

31. Herein, which consciousness is distant? Unwholesome consciousness is distant from wholesome and indeterminate consciousnesses; wholesome and indeterminate consciousnesses are distant from unwholesome consciousness. Wholesome consciousness is distant from unwholesome and indeterminate consciousnesses; unwholesome and indeterminate consciousnesses are distant from wholesome consciousness. Indeterminate consciousness is distant from wholesome and unwholesome consciousnesses; wholesome and unwholesome consciousnesses are distant from indeterminate consciousness. Consciousness associated with painful feeling is distant from consciousnesses associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; consciousnesses associated with pleasant and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are distant from consciousness associated with painful feeling. Consciousness associated with pleasant feeling is distant from consciousnesses associated with painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings; consciousnesses associated with painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings are distant from consciousness associated with pleasant feeling. Consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is distant from consciousnesses associated with pleasant and painful feelings; consciousnesses associated with pleasant and painful feelings are distant from consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The consciousness of one who has not attained meditative absorption is distant from the consciousness of one who has attained meditative absorption; the consciousness of one who has attained meditative absorption is distant from the consciousness of one who has not attained meditative absorption. Consciousness with taints is distant from consciousnesses without taints; consciousness without taints is distant from consciousness with taints. This is said to be distant consciousness.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ santike? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ akusalassa viññāṇassa santike; kusalaṃ [P 0.0012] viññāṇaṃ kusalassa viññāṇassa santike; abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ abyākatassa viññāṇassa santike. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa viññāṇassa santike; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa viññāṇassa santike; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ [T 0.0017] viññāṇaṃ adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa viññāṇassa santike. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ asamāpannassa viññāṇassa santike; samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇassa santike. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ sāsavassa viññāṇassa [M 0.0013] santike; anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ anāsavassa viññāṇassa santike – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana viññāṇaṃ upādāyupādāya viññāṇaṃ dūre santike daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Herein, which consciousness is near? Unwholesome consciousness is near to unwholesome consciousness; wholesome consciousness is near to wholesome consciousness; indeterminate consciousness is near to indeterminate consciousness. Consciousness associated with painful feeling is near to consciousness associated with painful feeling; consciousness associated with pleasant feeling is near to consciousness associated with pleasant feeling; consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is near to consciousness associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The consciousness of one who has not attained meditative absorption is near to the consciousness of one who has not attained meditative absorption; the consciousness of one who has attained meditative absorption is near to the consciousness of one who has attained meditative absorption. Consciousness with taints is near to consciousness with taints; consciousness without taints is near to consciousness without taints. This is said to be near consciousness. Or again, with reference to this or that consciousness, distant consciousness and near consciousness are to be understood.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Suttanta Analysis is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Analysis

32. Pañcakkhandhā [V 0.0014] – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho.

32. The five aggregates are: the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.

1. Rūpakkhandho

1. The Aggregate of Form

33. Tattha katamo rūpakkhandho? Ekavidhena rūpakkhandho – sabbaṃ rūpaṃ na hetu, ahetukaṃ, hetuvippayuttaṃ, sappaccayaṃ, saṅkhataṃ, rūpaṃ, lokiyaṃ, sāsavaṃ, saṃyojaniyaṃ, ganthaniyaṃ, oghaniyaṃ, yoganiyaṃ, nīvaraṇiyaṃ, parāmaṭṭhaṃ, upādāniyaṃ, saṃkilesikaṃ, abyākataṃ, anārammaṇaṃ, acetasikaṃ, cittavippayuttaṃ, nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṃ, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikaṃ, na savitakkasavicāraṃ, na avitakkavicāramattaṃ, avitakkaavicāraṃ, na pītisahagataṃ, na sukhasahagataṃ, na upekkhāsahagataṃ, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ, nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī, nevasekkhanāsekkhaṃ, parittaṃ, kāmāvacaraṃ, na rūpāvacaraṃ, na arūpāvacaraṃ, pariyāpannaṃ, no apariyāpannaṃ, aniyataṃ, aniyyānikaṃ, uppannaṃ, chahi viññāṇehi [T 0.0018] viññeyyaṃ, aniccaṃ, jarābhibhūtaṃ. Evaṃ ekavidhena rūpakkhandho.

33. Herein, what is the aggregate of form? In one way, the aggregate of form is thus: all form is not a root, is without a root, is dissociated from roots, has conditions, is conditioned, is subject to affliction, is mundane, is subject to taints, is an object for fetters, is an object for ties, is an object for floods, is an object for yokes, is an object for hindrances, is subject to misapprehension, is an object for clinging, is an object for defilements, is indeterminate, does not take an object, is not a mental factor, is dissociated from mind, is neither a result nor the cause of a result, is undefiled but an object for defilements, is not with initial application and sustained application, is not without initial application but with only sustained application, is without initial application and without sustained application, is not accompanied by joy, is not accompanied by happiness, is not accompanied by equanimity, is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, has a root to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, leads neither to accumulation nor to decline, pertains neither to a trainee nor to one beyond training, is limited, is of the sense-sphere, is not of the form-sphere, is not of the formless-sphere, is included, is not excluded, is cognizable by the six consciousnesses, is impermanent, is overcome by aging. Thus, in one way, is the aggregate of form.

Duvidhena [P 0.0013] rūpakkhandho – atthi rūpaṃ upādā, atthi rūpaṃ no upādā nupādā (sī. ka.). Atthi rūpaṃ upādinnaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ anupādinnaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ sanidassanaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ sappaṭighaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ appaṭighaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ indriyaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ mahābhūtaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ na mahābhūtaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ viññatti, atthi rūpaṃ na viññatti. Atthi rūpaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ na cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ cittasahabhu, atthi rūpaṃ na cittasahabhu. Atthi rūpaṃ cittānuparivatti, atthi rūpaṃ na [M 0.0014] cittānuparivatti. Atthi rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ oḷārikaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ sukhumaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ dūre, atthi rūpaṃ santike…pe… atthi rūpaṃ kabaḷīkāro āhāro, atthi rūpaṃ na kabaḷīkāro āhāro. Evaṃ duvidhena rūpakkhandho.

In two ways, the aggregate of form is thus: there is derived form, there is non-derived form. There is form that is kammically acquired, there is form that is not kammically acquired. There is form that is kammically acquired and an object for clinging, there is form that is not kammically acquired but an object for clinging. There is form that is visible, there is form that is invisible. There is form that is resistant, there is form that is non-resistant. There is form that is a faculty, there is form that is not a faculty. There is form that is a great element, there is form that is not a great element. There is form that is intimation, there is form that is not intimation. There is form that is mind-originated, there is form that is not mind-originated. There is form that is co-arisen with mind, there is form that is not co-arisen with mind. There is form that is mind-consecutive, there is form that is not mind-consecutive. There is form that is internal, there is form that is external. There is form that is coarse, there is form that is subtle. There is form that is far, there is form that is near… and so on… there is form that is edible food, there is form that is not edible food. Thus, in two ways, is the aggregate of form.

(Yathā [V 0.0015] rūpakaṇḍe vibhattaṃ, tathā idha vibhajitabbaṃ.)

(Just as it was analyzed in the Section on Form, so it should be analyzed here.)

Tividhena rūpakkhandho – yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ upādā, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ atthi upādā, atthi no upādā. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ upādinnaṃ, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ atthi upādinnaṃ, atthi anupādinnaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ upādinnupādāniyaṃ, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ atthi upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi anupādinnupādāniyaṃ…pe… yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ na kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ [T 0.0019] atthi kabaḷīkāro āhāro, atthi na kabaḷīkāro āhāro. Evaṃ tividhena rūpakkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of form is: that form which is internal is derived form; as for that form which is external, some is derived form, and some is non-derived form. That form which is internal is kammically acquired; as for that form which is external, some is kammically acquired, and some is not kammically acquired. That form which is internal is kammically acquired and subject to clinging; as for that form which is external, some is kammically acquired and subject to clinging, and some is not kammically acquired but subject to clinging… and so on… that form which is internal is not edible food; as for that form which is external, some is edible food, and some is not edible food. Thus, in three ways, the aggregate of form is.

Catubbidhena rūpakkhandho – yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi upādinnaṃ, atthi anupādinnaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi upādinnaṃ, atthi anupādinnaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi anupādinnupādāniyaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi sappaṭighaṃ, atthi appaṭighaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi sappaṭighaṃ, atthi appaṭighaṃ[P 0.0014]. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi oḷārikaṃ, atthi sukhumaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi oḷārikaṃ, atthi sukhumaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi dūre, atthi santike; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi dūre, atthi santike…pe… diṭṭhaṃ, sutaṃ, mutaṃ, viññātaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ catubbidhena rūpakkhandho.

In four ways, the aggregate of form is: as for that form which is derived, some is kammically acquired, and some is not kammically acquired; as for that form which is non-derived, some is kammically acquired, and some is not kammically acquired. As for that form which is derived, some is kammically acquired and subject to clinging, and some is not kammically acquired but subject to clinging; as for that form which is non-derived, some is kammically acquired and subject to clinging, and some is not kammically acquired but subject to clinging. As for that form which is derived, some is with impact, and some is without impact; as for that form which is non-derived, some is with impact, and some is without impact. As for that form which is derived, some is coarse, and some is subtle; as for that form which is non-derived, some is coarse, and some is subtle. As for that form which is derived, some is far, and some is near; as for that form which is non-derived, some is far, and some is near… and so on… form that is seen, heard, sensed, cognized. Thus, in four ways, the aggregate of form is.

Pañcavidhena rūpakkhandho – pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, yañca rūpaṃ upādā. Evaṃ pañcavidhena rūpakkhandho.

In five ways, the aggregate of form is: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the wind element, and derived form. Thus, in five ways, the aggregate of form is.

Chabbidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, sotaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, ghānaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, jivhāviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, kāyaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manoviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ chabbidhena rūpakkhandho.

In six ways, the aggregate of form is: form cognizable by eye-consciousness, form cognizable by ear-consciousness, form cognizable by nose-consciousness, form cognizable by tongue-consciousness, form cognizable by body-consciousness, and form cognizable by mind-consciousness. Thus, in six ways, the aggregate of form is.

Sattavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, sotaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, ghānaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, jivhāviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, kāyaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manodhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manoviññāṇadhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ sattavidhena rūpakkhandho[T 0.0020].

In seven ways, the aggregate of form is: form cognizable by eye-consciousness, form cognizable by ear-consciousness, form cognizable by nose-consciousness, form cognizable by tongue-consciousness, form cognizable by body-consciousness, form cognizable by the mind-element, and form cognizable by the mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in seven ways, the aggregate of form is.

Aṭṭhavidhena [M 0.0015][V 0.0016] rūpakkhandho – cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, sotaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, ghānaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, jivhāviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, kāyaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ atthi sukhasamphassaṃ, atthi dukkhasamphassaṃ, manodhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manoviññāṇadhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena rūpakkhandho.

In eight ways, the aggregate of form is: form cognizable by eye-consciousness, form cognizable by ear-consciousness, form cognizable by nose-consciousness, form cognizable by tongue-consciousness; there is form cognizable by body-consciousness that is pleasant contact, and there is form cognizable by body-consciousness that is painful contact; form cognizable by the mind-element, and form cognizable by the mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in eight ways, the aggregate of form is.

Navavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, yañca rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ. Evaṃ navavidhena rūpakkhandho.

In nine ways, the aggregate of form is: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the female faculty, the male faculty, the life faculty, and whatever form is not a faculty. Thus, in nine ways, the aggregate of form is.

Dasavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, na indriyaṃ rūpaṃ atthi sappaṭighaṃ, atthi appaṭighaṃ. Evaṃ dasavidhena rūpakkhandho.

In ten ways, the aggregate of form is: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the female faculty, the male faculty, the life faculty; there is form that is not a faculty and is with impact, and there is form that is not a faculty and is without impact. Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of form is.

Ekādasavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ. Evaṃ ekādasavidhena rūpakkhandho.

In eleven ways, the aggregate of form is: the eye base, the ear base, the nose base, the tongue base, the body base, the form base, the sound base, the odor base, the taste base, the tangible base, and whatever form is invisible, without impact, and included in the mental-object base. Thus, in eleven ways, the aggregate of form is.

Ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho.

This is called the aggregate of form.

2. Vedanākkhandho

2. The Aggregate of Feeling

34. Tattha [P 0.0015] katamo vedanākkhandho? Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

34. Herein, what is the aggregate of feeling? In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: that which is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling with roots, and there is feeling without roots.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is wholesome feeling, there is unwholesome feeling, and there is indeterminate feeling.

Catubbidhena vedanākkhandho [T 0.0021] – atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno.

In four ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling of the sense-sphere, feeling of the form-sphere, feeling of the formless-sphere, and unincluded feeling.

Pañcavidhena [V 0.0017] vedanākkhandho – atthi sukhindriyaṃ, atthi dukkhindriyaṃ, atthi somanassindriyaṃ, atthi domanassindriyaṃ, atthi upekkhindriyaṃ. Evaṃ pañcavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In five ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is the faculty of pleasure, there is the faculty of pain, there is the faculty of gladness, there is the faculty of sadness, and there is the faculty of equanimity. Thus, in five ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Chabbidhena [M 0.0016] vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ chabbidhena vedanākkhandho.

In six ways, the aggregate of feeling is: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. Thus, in six ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Sattavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ sattavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In seven ways, the aggregate of feeling is: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-element-contact, and feeling born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, in seven ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Aṭṭhavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā atthi sukhā, atthi dukkhā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In eight ways, the aggregate of feeling is: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact; there is pleasant feeling born of body-contact, and there is painful feeling born of body-contact; feeling born of mind-element-contact, and feeling born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, in eight ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Navavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ navavidhena vedanākkhandho.

The aggregate of feeling is ninefold: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-element-contact; and of feeling born of mind-consciousness-element-contact, there is wholesome, there is unwholesome, and there is indeterminate. Thus, the aggregate of feeling is ninefold.

Dasavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā atthi sukhā, atthi dukkhā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

The aggregate of feeling is tenfold: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact; of feeling born of body-contact, there is pleasant and there is painful; feeling born of mind-element-contact; and of feeling born of mind-consciousness-element-contact, there is wholesome, there is unwholesome, and there is indeterminate. Thus, the aggregate of feeling is tenfold.

35. Ekavidhena [T 0.0022] vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

35. The aggregate of feeling is onefold: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0016][V 0.0018] vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

The aggregate of feeling is twofold: there is feeling with roots, and there is feeling without roots.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi [M 0.0017] avitakkaavicāro. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi [P 0.0017] parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho. Atthi [T 0.0023] ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

The aggregate of feeling is threefold: there is resultant feeling, feeling that is the cause for results, and feeling that is neither resultant nor the cause for results. There is feeling that is grasped and is an object of clinging, feeling that is not grasped but is an object of clinging, and feeling that is neither grasped nor an object of clinging. There is feeling that is defiled and an object of defilements, feeling that is undefiled but an object of defilements, and feeling that is undefiled and not an object of defilements. There is feeling with initial thought and sustained thought, feeling with only sustained thought, and feeling with neither initial thought nor sustained thought. There is feeling to be abandoned by seeing, feeling to be abandoned by development, and feeling to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. There is feeling with a cause to be abandoned by seeing, feeling with a cause to be abandoned by development, and feeling with a cause to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. There is feeling that leads to accumulation, feeling that leads to decumulation, and feeling that leads neither to accumulation nor to decumulation. There is feeling of a trainee, feeling of one beyond training, and feeling of one who is neither a trainee nor beyond training. There is limited feeling, exalted feeling, and immeasurable feeling. There is feeling with a limited object, feeling with an exalted object, and feeling with an immeasurable object. There is inferior feeling, middling feeling, and superior feeling. There is feeling fixed in wrongness, feeling fixed in rightness, and feeling that is unfixed. There is feeling with the path as its object, feeling with the path as its cause, and feeling with the path as its dominant condition. There is arisen feeling, unarisen feeling, and feeling that is bound to arise. There is past feeling, future feeling, and present feeling. There is feeling with a past object, feeling with a future object, and feeling with a present object. There is internal feeling, external feeling, and internal-external feeling. There is feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, and feeling with an internal-external object… and so on. Thus, the aggregate of feeling is tenfold.

36. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

36. The aggregate of feeling is onefold: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto…pe… atthi na hetusahetuko, atthi na hetuahetuko. Atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro. Atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo. Atthi [P 0.0018] sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. Atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto. Atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo. Atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo. Atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto. Atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo. Atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo. Atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto[V 0.0019]. Atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo. Atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo. Atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto. Atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo. Atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo. Atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto. Atthi [M 0.0018] yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi anīvaraṇiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇasampayutto, atthi nīvaraṇavippayutto. Atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyo, atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyo. Atthi parāmaṭṭho, atthi aparāmaṭṭho. Atthi parāmāsasampayutto, atthi parāmāsavippayutto[T 0.0024]. Atthi parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭho, atthi parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭho. Atthi upādinno, atthi anupādinno. Atthi upādāniyo, atthi anupādāniyo. Atthi upādānasampayutto, atthi upādānavippayutto. Atthi upādānavippayuttaupādāniyo, atthi upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkilesiko. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭho, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭho. Atthi kilesasampayutto, atthi kilesavippayutto. Atthi kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesiko, atthi kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi na dassanena pahātabbo. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi na dassanena pahātabbahetuko. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi savitakko, atthi avitakko. Atthi savicāro, atthi avicāro. Atthi [P 0.0019] sappītiko, atthi appītiko. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi na pītisahagato. Atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi na kāmāvacaro. Atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi na rūpāvacaro. Atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi na arūpāvacaro. Atthi pariyāpanno, atthi apariyāpanno. Atthi niyyāniko, atthi aniyyāniko. Atthi niyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi sauttaro, atthi anuttaro. Atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is associated with a root, and that which is dissociated from a root; there is that which is not a root but is with a root, and that which is not a root and is without a root; there is that which is worldly, and that which is supramundane; there is that which is cognizable by some means, and that which is not cognizable by some means; there is that which is with taints, and that which is without taints; there is that which is associated with taints, and that which is dissociated from taints; there is that which is dissociated from taints but is an object of taints, and that which is dissociated from taints and is not an object of taints; there is that which is an object of fetters, and that which is not an object of fetters; there is that which is associated with fetters, and that which is dissociated from fetters; there is that which is dissociated from fetters but is an object of fetters, and that which is dissociated from fetters and is not an object of fetters; there is that which is an object of bonds, and that which is not an object of bonds; there is that which is associated with bonds, and that which is dissociated from bonds; there is that which is dissociated from bonds but is an object of bonds, and that which is dissociated from bonds and is not an object of bonds; there is that which is an object of floods, and that which is not an object of floods; there is that which is associated with floods, and that which is dissociated from floods; there is that which is dissociated from floods but is an object of floods, and that which is dissociated from floods and is not an object of floods; there is that which is an object of yokes, and that which is not an object of yokes; there is that which is associated with yokes, and that which is dissociated from yokes; there is that which is dissociated from yokes but is an object of yokes, and that which is dissociated from yokes and is not an object of yokes; there is that which is an object of hindrances, and that which is not an object of hindrances; there is that which is associated with hindrances, and that which is dissociated from hindrances; there is that which is dissociated from hindrances but is an object of hindrances, and that which is dissociated from hindrances and is not an object of hindrances; there is that which is subject to misapprehension, and that which is not subject to misapprehension; there is that which is associated with misapprehension, and that which is dissociated from misapprehension; there is that which is dissociated from misapprehension but is subject to misapprehension, and that which is dissociated from misapprehension and is not subject to misapprehension; there is that which is taken up, and that which is not taken up; there is that which is an object of clinging, and that which is not an object of clinging; there is that which is associated with clinging, and that which is dissociated from clinging; there is that which is dissociated from clinging but is an object of clinging, and that which is dissociated from clinging and is not an object of clinging; there is that which is an object of defilements, and that which is not an object of defilements; there is that which is defiled, and that which is undefiled; there is that which is associated with defilements, and that which is dissociated from defilements; there is that which is dissociated from defilements but is an object of defilements, and that which is dissociated from defilements and is not an object of defilements; there is that which is to be abandoned by vision, and that which is not to be abandoned by vision; there is that which is to be abandoned by cultivation, and that which is not to be abandoned by cultivation; there is that which has a root to be abandoned by vision, and that which does not have a root to be abandoned by vision; there is that which has a root to be abandoned by cultivation, and that which does not have a root to be abandoned by cultivation; there is that which is with initial thought, and that which is without initial thought; there is that which is with sustained thought, and that which is without sustained thought; there is that which is with rapture, and that which is without rapture; there is that which is accompanied by rapture, and that which is not accompanied by rapture; there is that which pertains to the sense-sphere, and that which does not pertain to the sense-sphere; there is that which pertains to the form-sphere, and that which does not pertain to the form-sphere; there is that which pertains to the formless-sphere, and that which does not pertain to the formless-sphere; there is that which is included, and that which is not included; there is that which is leading out, and that which is not leading out;
