there is that which is determined, and that which is undetermined; there is that which is surpassable, and that which is unsurpassable; there is that which is with defilement, and that which is without defilement.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is wholesome, there is that which is unwholesome, and there is that which is indeterminate... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

37. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

37. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is with defilement, and that which is without defilement.

Tividhena [V 0.0020] vedanākkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Atthi upādinnupādāniyo…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo[M 0.0019], atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is resultant, there is that which has the nature of being a condition for resultants, and there is that which is neither resultant nor has the nature of being a condition for resultants. There is that which is taken up and an object of clinging... and so on... there is that with an internal object, there is that with an external object, and there is that with an internal-external object... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Dukamūlakaṃ.

Based on Dyads.

38. Ekavidhena [T 0.0025] vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

38. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0020] vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is with a root, and that which is without a root.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is wholesome, there is that which is unwholesome, and there is that which is indeterminate... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

39. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

39. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is associated with a root, and that which is dissociated from a root.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is wholesome, there is that which is unwholesome, and there is that which is indeterminate... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

40. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

40. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi na hetusahetuko, atthi na hetuahetuko. Atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro. Atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo. Atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. Atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto. Atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo…pe… atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is not a root but is with a root, and that which is not a root and is without a root; there is that which is worldly, and that which is supramundane; there is that which is cognizable by some means, and that which is not cognizable by some means; there is that which is with taints, and that which is without taints; there is that which is associated with taints, and that which is dissociated from taints; there is that which is dissociated from taints but is an object of taints, and that which is dissociated from taints and is not an object of taints... and so on... there is that which is with defilement, and that which is without defilement.

Tividhena [V 0.0021] vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is wholesome, there is that which is unwholesome, and there is that which is indeterminate... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

41. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

41. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is with a root, and that which is without a root.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. [T 0.0026] Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo[M 0.0020], atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is resultant, that which is a condition for result, and that which is neither resultant nor a condition for result. There is that which is taken up [by kamma] and is an object of clinging; that which is not taken up [by kamma] but is an object of clinging; and that which is neither taken up [by kamma] nor an object of clinging. There is that which is defiled and an object for defilements; that which is undefiled but an object for defilements; and that which is undefiled and not an object for defilements. There is that which is accompanied by initial and sustained application; that which is without initial application, with sustained application only; and that which is without initial or sustained application. There is that which is to be abandoned by vision; that which is to be abandoned by cultivation; and that which is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. There is that which has a cause to be abandoned by vision; that which has a cause to be abandoned by cultivation; and that which has a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. There is that which leads to accumulation; that which leads to decline; and that which leads neither to accumulation nor to decline. There is that of a trainee; that of one beyond training; and that of one who is neither a trainee nor beyond training. There is that which is limited; that which is exalted; and that which is immeasurable. There is that with a limited object; that with an exalted object; and that with Nibbāna as its object. There is that which is inferior; that which is middling; and that which is sublime. There is that which is fixed in wrongness; that which is fixed in rightness; and that which is unfixed. There is that with the path as object; that with the path as cause; and that with the path as predominant factor. There is that which has arisen; that which has not arisen; and that which is bound to arise. There is that which is past; that which is future; and that which is present. There is that with a past object; that with a future object; and that with a present object. There is that which is internal; that which is external; and that which is both internal and external. There is that with an internal object; that with an external object; and that with both an internal and an external object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

42. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

42. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto. Atthi na hetusahetuko, atthi na hetuahetuko. Atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro. Atthi kenaci viññeyyo[V 0.0022], atthi kenaci na viññeyyo. Atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. Atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto. Atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo. Atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo…pe… atthi saraṇo[P 0.0021], atthi araṇo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is associated with roots, and that which is dissociated from roots. There is that which is not a root but is accompanied by a root; and that which is not a root and is without a root. There is that which is mundane, and that which is supramundane. There is that which is cognizable by some means, and that which is not cognizable by any means. There is that which is an object for the taints, and that which is not an object for the taints. There is that which is associated with the taints, and that which is dissociated from the taints. There is that which is dissociated from the taints but is an object for the taints; and that which is dissociated from the taints and is not an object for the taints. There is that which is an object for the fetters, and that which is not an object for the fetters... and so on... there is that which is with defilements, and that which is without defilements.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that with an internal object, that with an external object, and that with both an internal and an external object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Tikamūlakaṃ.

The Root Section of the Triads.

43. Ekavidhena [M 0.0021] vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

43. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is with roots, and that which is without roots.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is wholesome, that which is unwholesome, and that which is indeterminate... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

44. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

44. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is associated with roots, and that which is dissociated from roots.

Tividhena [P 0.0022] vedanākkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is resultant, that which is a condition for result, and that which is neither resultant nor a condition for result... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

45. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

45. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi na hetusahetuko, atthi na hetuahetuko.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is not a root but is accompanied by a root, and that which is not a root and is without a root.

Tividhena [V 0.0023] vedanākkhandho – atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is taken up [by kamma] and is an object of clinging; that which is not taken up [by kamma] but is an object of clinging; and that which is neither taken up [by kamma] nor an object of clinging... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

46. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

46. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is mundane, and that which is supramundane.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is defiled and an object for defilements; that which is undefiled but an object for defilements; and that which is undefiled and not an object for defilements... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

47. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

47. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kenaci viññeyyo[T 0.0027], atthi kenaci na viññeyyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is cognizable by some means, and that which is not cognizable by any means.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is accompanied by initial and sustained application; that which is without initial application, with sustained application only; and that which is without initial or sustained application... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

48. Ekavidhena [M 0.0022] vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

48. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is an object for the taints, and that which is not an object for the taints.

Tividhena [P 0.0023] vedanākkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is to be abandoned by vision; that which is to be abandoned by cultivation; and that which is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

49. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

49. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is associated with the taints, and that which is dissociated from the taints.

Tividhena [V 0.0024] vedanākkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that with a cause to be abandoned by vision; that with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation; and that with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

50. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

50. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which is dissociated from the taints but is an object for the taints; and there is that which is dissociated from the taints and is not an object for the taints.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that which leads to accumulation, that which leads to decline, and that which leads neither to accumulation nor to decline... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

51. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

51. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling that is an object for the fetters, and there is feeling that is not an object for the fetters.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling of a trainee, there is feeling of one beyond training, and there is feeling of one who is neither a trainee nor beyond training... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

52. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

52. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto[T 0.0028].

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling associated with the fetters, and there is feeling dissociated from the fetters.

Tividhena [P 0.0024] vedanākkhandho – atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is limited feeling, there is exalted feeling, and there is immeasurable feeling... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

53. Ekavidhena [M 0.0023] vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

53. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0025] vedanākkhandho – atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling dissociated from the fetters but is an object for the fetters, and there is feeling dissociated from the fetters and is not an object for the fetters.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling that has a limited object, there is feeling that has an exalted object, and there is feeling that has an immeasurable object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

54. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

54. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling that is an object for the ties, and there is feeling that is not an object for the ties.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is inferior feeling, there is middling feeling, and there is sublime feeling... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

55. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

55. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling associated with the ties, and there is feeling dissociated from the ties.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling fixed in wrongness, there is feeling fixed in rightness, and there is unfixed feeling... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

56. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

56. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling dissociated from the ties but is an object for the ties, and there is feeling dissociated from the ties and is not an object for the ties.

Tividhena [P 0.0025] vedanākkhandho – atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling that has the path as its object, there is feeling that has the path as its cause, and there is feeling that has the path as its dominant condition... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

57. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

57. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0026] vedanākkhandho – atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling that is an object for the floods, and there is feeling that is not an object for the floods.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is arisen feeling, there is unarisen feeling, and there is feeling that is bound to arise... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

58. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

58. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho [T 0.0029] – atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling associated with the floods, and there is feeling dissociated from the floods.

Tividhena [M 0.0024] vedanākkhandho – atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is past feeling, there is future feeling, and there is present feeling... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

59. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

59. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling dissociated from the floods but is an object for the floods, and there is feeling dissociated from the floods and is not an object for the floods.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling that has the past as its object, there is feeling that has the future as its object, and there is feeling that has the present as its object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

60. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

60. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling that is an object for the yokes, and there is feeling that is not an object for the yokes.

Tividhena [P 0.0026] vedanākkhandho – atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is internal feeling, there is external feeling, and there is internal-and-external feeling... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

61. Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

61. In one way, the aggregate of feeling is: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0027] vedanākkhandho – atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling associated with the yokes, and there is feeling dissociated from the yokes.

Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, and feeling with an internal and external object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Ubhatovaḍḍhakaṃ.

The section of augmentation by both.

Sattavidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena vedanākkhandho.

In seven ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is wholesome feeling, there is unwholesome feeling, there is indeterminate feeling, there is feeling pertaining to the sense sphere, there is feeling pertaining to the form sphere, there is feeling pertaining to the formless sphere, and there is unincluded feeling. Thus, in seven ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Aparopi sattavidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo[T 0.0030], atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Furthermore, in seven ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is resultant feeling... and so on... there is feeling with an internal object, there is feeling with an external object, there is feeling with an internal and external object, there is feeling pertaining to the sense sphere, there is feeling pertaining to the form sphere, there is feeling pertaining to the formless sphere, and there is unincluded feeling. Thus, in seven ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Catuvīsatividhena [M 0.0025] vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; sotasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena vedanākkhandho.

In twenty-four ways, the aggregate of feeling is: conditioned by eye-contact, there is wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling in the aggregate of feeling; conditioned by ear-contact, there is the aggregate of feeling... and so on... conditioned by nose-contact, there is the aggregate of feeling... and so on... conditioned by tongue-contact, there is the aggregate of feeling... and so on... conditioned by body-contact, there is the aggregate of feeling... and so on... conditioned by mind-contact, there is wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate feeling in the aggregate of feeling. There is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. Thus, in twenty-four ways, the aggregate of feeling is.

Aparopi catuvīsatividhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā [P 0.0027] vedanākkhandho atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, cakkhusamphassajā vedanā…pe… manosamphassajā vedanā; sotasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho [V 0.0028] atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, cakkhusamphassajā vedanā…pe… manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena [T 0.0031] vedanākkhandho.

Furthermore, the feeling aggregate is of twenty-four kinds: the feeling aggregate conditioned by eye-contact is resultant…pe… with an internal object, with an external object, and with an internal and external object; so too for that conditioned by ear-contact…pe… nose-contact…pe… tongue-contact…pe… body-contact…pe… the feeling aggregate conditioned by mind-contact is resultant…pe… with an internal object, with an external object, and with an internal and external object. There is feeling born of eye-contact…pe… and feeling born of mind-contact. Thus the feeling aggregate is of twenty-four kinds.

Tiṃsavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ tiṃsavidhena vedanākkhandho.

The feeling aggregate is of thirty kinds: the feeling aggregate conditioned by eye-contact pertains to the sense-sphere, pertains to the form-sphere, pertains to the formless-sphere, and is unincluded; so too for that conditioned by ear-contact…pe… nose-contact…pe… tongue-contact…pe… body-contact…pe… the feeling aggregate conditioned by mind-contact pertains to the sense-sphere, pertains to the form-sphere, pertains to the formless-sphere, and is unincluded. There is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. Thus the feeling aggregate is of thirty kinds.

Bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo[M 0.0026], atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho.

The feeling aggregate is of many kinds: the feeling aggregate conditioned by eye-contact is wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate, pertaining to the sense-sphere, pertaining to the form-sphere, pertaining to the formless-sphere, and unincluded; so too for that conditioned by ear-contact…pe… nose-contact…pe… tongue-contact…pe… body-contact…pe… the feeling aggregate conditioned by mind-contact is wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate, pertaining to the sense-sphere, pertaining to the form-sphere, pertaining to the formless-sphere, and unincluded. There is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. Thus the feeling aggregate is of many kinds.

Aparopi bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro[T 0.0032], atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo[P 0.0028], atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro[V 0.0029], atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho.

Furthermore, the feeling aggregate is of many kinds: the feeling aggregate conditioned by eye-contact is resultant…pe… with an internal object, with an external object, with an internal and external object, pertaining to the sense-sphere, pertaining to the form-sphere, pertaining to the formless-sphere, and unincluded; so too for that conditioned by ear-contact…pe… nose-contact…pe… tongue-contact…pe… body-contact…pe… the feeling aggregate conditioned by mind-contact is resultant…pe… with an internal object, with an external object, with an internal and external object, pertaining to the sense-sphere, pertaining to the form-sphere, pertaining to the formless-sphere, and unincluded. There is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. Thus the feeling aggregate is of many kinds.

Ayaṃ vuccati vedanākkhandho.

This is called the feeling aggregate.

3. Saññākkhandho

3. The Aggregate of Perception

62. Tattha katamo saññākkhandho? Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

62. Herein, what is the aggregate of perception? In one way, the aggregate of perception is that which is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception with root-causes, and there is perception without root-causes.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is wholesome perception, there is unwholesome perception, and there is indeterminate perception.

Catubbidhena saññākkhandho – atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno.

The aggregate of perception is fourfold: there is perception belonging to the sense-sphere, there is perception belonging to the form-sphere, there is perception belonging to the formless-sphere, and there is unincluded perception.

Pañcavidhena [M 0.0027] saññākkhandho – atthi sukhindriyasampayutto, atthi dukkhindriyasampayutto, atthi somanassindriyasampayutto, atthi domanassindriyasampayutto, atthi upekkhindriyasampayutto. Evaṃ pañcavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is fivefold: there is perception associated with the faculty of pleasure, there is perception associated with the faculty of pain, there is perception associated with the faculty of joy, there is perception associated with the faculty of displeasure, and there is perception associated with the faculty of equanimity. Thus, the aggregate of perception is fivefold.

Chabbidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ chabbidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is sixfold: perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of perception is sixfold.

Sattavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā [V 0.0030] saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā [T 0.0033] saññā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ sattavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is sevenfold: perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-element-contact, and perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of perception is sevenfold.

Aṭṭhavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… kāyasamphassajā saññā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is eightfold: perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact accompanied by pleasure, perception born of body-contact accompanied by pain, perception born of mind-element-contact, and perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of perception is eightfold.

Navavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… kāyasamphassajā saññā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ navavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is ninefold: there is perception born of eye-contact... and so on... perception born of body-contact; there is perception born of mind-element-contact; and wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of perception is ninefold.

Dasavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… kāyasamphassajā saññā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is tenfold. There is perception born of eye-contact... and so on... perception born of tongue-contact; there is perception born of body-contact accompanied by pleasure, and perception born of body-contact accompanied by pain; there is perception born of mind-element-contact; and wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

63. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

63. In one way, the aggregate of perception is that which is associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0029] saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception with root-causes, and there is perception without root-causes.

Tividhena [V 0.0031] saññākkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is perception associated with pleasant feeling, there is perception associated with painful feeling, and there is perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

64. Ekavidhena [M 0.0028] saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

64. In one way, the aggregate of perception is that which is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception with root-causes, and there is perception without root-causes.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi [T 0.0034] asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is that which is resultant, that which is a condition for resultants, and that which is neither resultant nor a condition for resultants. There is that which is grasped and is fuel for clinging, that which is not grasped but is fuel for clinging, and that which is not grasped and is not fuel for clinging. There is that which is defiled and an object for defilements, that which is undefiled but an object for defilements, and that which is undefiled and not an object for defilements. There is that with initial and sustained thought, that without initial thought but with only sustained thought, and that with neither initial thought nor sustained thought. There is that accompanied by rapture, that accompanied by pleasure, and that accompanied by equanimity. There is that to be abandoned by seeing, that to be abandoned by development, and that to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. There is that with roots to be abandoned by seeing, that with roots to be abandoned by development, and that with roots to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. There is that leading to accumulation, that leading to de-accumulation, and that leading neither to accumulation nor to de-accumulation. There is that of a trainee, that of one beyond training, and that of one who is neither a trainee nor beyond training. There is that which is limited, that which is exalted, and that which is immeasurable. There is that with a limited object, that with an exalted object, and that with an immeasurable object. There is that which is inferior, that which is middling, and that which is superior. There is that fixed in wrongness, that fixed in rightness, and that which is unfixed. There is that with the path as object, that with the path as root-cause, and that with the path as dominant factor. There is that which has arisen, that which has not arisen, and that which is bound to arise. There is that which is past, that which is future, and that which is present. There is that with a past object, that with a future object, and that with a present object. There is that which is internal, that which is external, and that which is both internal and external. There is that with an internal object, that with an external object, and that with an object that is both internal and external... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

65. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

65. In one way, the aggregate of perception is that which is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto. Atthi na hetusahetuko, atthi na hetuahetuko. Atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro[T 0.0035]. Atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo. Atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. Atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto. Atthi [P 0.0030] āsavavippayuttasāsavo[M 0.0029], atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo. Atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo. Atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto. Atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo. Atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo. Atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto. Atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo. Atthi oghaniyo[V 0.0032], atthi anoghaniyo. Atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto. Atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo. Atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo. Atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto. Atthi yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi anīvaraṇiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇasampayutto, atthi nīvaraṇavippayutto. Atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyo, atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyo. Atthi parāmaṭṭho, atthi aparāmaṭṭho. Atthi parāmāsasampayutto, atthi parāmāsavippayutto. Atthi parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭho, atthi parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭho. Atthi upādinno, atthi anupādinno. Atthi upādāniyo, atthi anupādāniyo. Atthi upādānasampayutto, atthi upādānavippayutto. Atthi upādānavippayuttaupādāniyo, atthi upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkilesiko[T 0.0036], atthi asaṃkilesiko. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭho, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭho. Atthi kilesasampayutto, atthi kilesavippayutto. Atthi kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesiko, atthi kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi na dassanena pahātabbo. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi na dassanena pahātabbahetuko. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi savitakko, atthi avitakko. Atthi savicāro, atthi avicāro. Atthi sappītiko, atthi appītiko. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi na pītisahagato. Atthi sukhasahagato, atthi na sukhasahagato. Atthi upekkhāsahagato, atthi na upekkhāsahagato. Atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi na kāmāvacaro. Atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi na rūpāvacaro. Atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi na arūpāvacaro. Atthi pariyāpanno[M 0.0030], atthi apariyāpanno. Atthi [P 0.0031] niyyāniko, atthi aniyyāniko. Atthi niyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi sauttaro, atthi anuttaro. Atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is that associated with root causes, and there is that dissociated from root causes. There is that which is not a root but with root causes, and there is that which is not a root and without root causes. There is that which is mundane, and there is that which is supramundane. There is that which is knowable by some means, and there is that which is not knowable by any means. There is that which is an object for taints, and there is that which is not an object for taints. There is that associated with taints, and there is that dissociated from taints. There is that dissociated from taints but an object for taints, and there is that dissociated from taints and not an object for taints. There is that which is an object for fetters, and there is that which is not an object for fetters. There is that associated with fetters, and there is that dissociated from fetters. There is that dissociated from fetters but an object for fetters, and there is that dissociated from fetters and not an object for fetters. There is that which is an object for bonds, and there is that which is not an object for bonds. There is that associated with bonds, and there is that dissociated from bonds. There is that dissociated from bonds but an object for bonds, and there is that dissociated from bonds and not an object for bonds. There is that which is an object for floods, and there is that which is not an object for floods. There is that associated with floods, and there is that dissociated from floods. There is that dissociated from floods but an object for floods, and there is that dissociated from floods and not an object for floods. There is that which is an object for yokes, and there is that which is not an object for yokes. There is that associated with yokes, and there is that dissociated from yokes. There is that dissociated from yokes but an object for yokes, and there is that dissociated from yokes and not an object for yokes. There is that which is an object for hindrances, and there is that which is not an object for hindrances. There is that associated with hindrances, and there is that dissociated from hindrances. There is that dissociated from hindrances but an object for hindrances, and there is that dissociated from hindrances and not an object for hindrances. There is that which is grasped at, and there is that which is not grasped at. There is that associated with grasping, and there is that dissociated from grasping. There is that dissociated from grasping but grasped at, and there is that dissociated from grasping and not grasped at. There is that which is appropriated by kamma, and there is that which is not appropriated by kamma. There is that which is an object for clinging, and there is that which is not an object for clinging. There is that associated with clinging, and there is that dissociated from clinging. There is that dissociated from clinging but an object for clinging, and there is that dissociated from clinging and not an object for clinging. There is that which is an object for defilements, and there is that which is not an object for defilements. There is that which is defiled, and there is that which is undefiled. There is that associated with defilements, and there is that dissociated from defilements. There is that dissociated from defilements but an object for defilements, and there is that dissociated from defilements and not an object for defilements. There is that to be abandoned by seeing, and there is that not to be abandoned by seeing. There is that to be abandoned by development, and there is that not to be abandoned by development. There is that with roots to be abandoned by seeing, and there is that without roots to be abandoned by seeing. There is that with roots to be abandoned by development, and there is that without roots to be abandoned by development. There is that with initial thought, and there is that without initial thought. There is that with sustained thought, and there is that without sustained thought. There is that with joy, and there is that without joy. There is that accompanied by joy, and there is that not accompanied by joy. There is that accompanied by pleasure, and there is that not accompanied by pleasure. There is that accompanied by equanimity, and there is that not accompanied by equanimity. There is that belonging to the sense-sphere, and there is that not belonging to the sense-sphere. There is that belonging to the form-sphere, and there is that not belonging to the form-sphere. There is that belonging to the formless-sphere, and there is that not belonging to the formless-sphere. There is that which is included, and there is that which is not included. There is that which is leading to liberation, and there is that which is not leading to liberation. There is that which is fixed, and there is that which is unfixed. There is that with a superior, and there is that without a superior. There is that with defilement, and there is that without defilement.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, and there is the indeterminate... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

66. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

66. The aggregate of perception is of one kind: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0033] saññākkhandho – atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is that with defilement, and there is that without defilement.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo[T 0.0037], atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is that associated with pleasant feeling, there is that associated with painful feeling, and there is that associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. There is resultant... and so on... there is that with an internal object, there is that with an external object, and there is that with an internal and external object... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

(Yathā kusalattike vitthāro, evaṃ sabbepi tikā vitthāretabbā.)

(As the exposition in the wholesome triad, so too should all the triads be expounded.)

Dukamūlakaṃ.

The section rooted in the dyads.

67. The aggregate of perception is of one kind: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is that with root causes, and there is that without root causes.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, and there is the indeterminate... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.
