There is resultant... and so on... there is that with an internal object, there is that with an external object, and there is that with an internal and external object... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

70. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

70. The aggregate of perception is of one kind: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto…pe… atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is that associated with root causes, and there is that dissociated from root causes... and so on... there is that with defilement, and there is that without defilement.

Tividhena [P 0.0033] saññākkhandho…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena [T 0.0038] saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is... and so on... there is perception with an internal object, there is perception with an external object, there is perception with an internal-and-external object... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of perception is.

Tikamūlakaṃ.

Rooted in the Triads.

71. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

71. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception with roots, and there is perception without roots.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is wholesome perception, there is unwholesome perception, there is indeterminate perception... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

72. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

72. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception associated with roots, and there is perception dissociated from roots.

Tividhena [V 0.0035] saññākkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception associated with pleasant feeling, there is perception associated with painful feeling, and there is perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

73. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

73. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi na hetu sahetuko, atthi na hetu ahetuko.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is not a root but is with roots, and there is perception that is not a root and is without roots.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is a resultant, there is perception that is a condition for resultants, and there is perception that is neither a resultant nor a condition for resultants... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

74. Ekavidhena [M 0.0032] saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

74. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0034] saññākkhandho – atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is mundane perception, and there is supramundane perception.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is appropriated and is an object of clinging, there is perception that is not appropriated but is an object of clinging, and there is perception that is neither appropriated nor an object of clinging... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

75. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

75. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception cognizable by some consciousness, and there is perception not cognizable by some consciousness.

Tividhena saññākkhandho [T 0.0039] – atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is defiled and an object of defilement, there is perception that is undefiled but an object of defilement, and there is perception that is undefiled and not an object of defilement... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

76. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

76. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is an object for the taints, and there is perception that is not an object for the taints.

Tividhena [V 0.0036] saññākkhandho – atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception with applied and sustained thought, there is perception without applied thought but with only sustained thought, and there is perception without applied thought and without sustained thought... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

77. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

77. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception associated with the taints, and there is perception dissociated from the taints.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception accompanied by rapture, there is perception accompanied by pleasure, and there is perception accompanied by equanimity... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

78. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

78. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0035] saññākkhandho – atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception dissociated from the taints but an object for the taints, and there is perception dissociated from the taints and not an object for the taints.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception to be abandoned by vision, there is perception to be abandoned by development, and there is perception to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

79. Ekavidhena [M 0.0033] saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

79. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is an object for the fetters, and there is perception that is not an object for the fetters.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception with a root to be abandoned by vision, there is perception with a root to be abandoned by development, and there is perception with a root to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

80. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

80. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0037] saññākkhandho – atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto[T 0.0040].

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception associated with the fetters, and there is perception dissociated from the fetters.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that leads to accumulation, there is perception that leads to de-accumulation, and there is perception that leads neither to accumulation nor to de-accumulation... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

81. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

81. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is dissociated from the fetters but is an object for the fetters, and there is perception that is dissociated from the fetters and is not an object for the fetters.

Tividhena [P 0.0036] saññākkhandho – atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is the perception of a trainee, there is the perception of one beyond training, and there is the perception of one who is neither a trainee nor one beyond training... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

82. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

82. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception that is an object for the ties, and there is perception that is not an object for the ties.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is limited perception, there is exalted perception, and there is immeasurable perception... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

83. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

83. In one way, the aggregate of perception is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto.

In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is perception associated with the ties, and there is perception dissociated from the ties.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is perception with a limited object, there is perception with an exalted object, and there is perception with an immeasurable object... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

84. Ekavidhena [M 0.0034] saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

84. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0038] saññākkhandho – atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception that is dissociated from the bodily ties but is an object for the bodily ties, and there is perception that is dissociated from the bodily ties and is not an object for the bodily ties.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is inferior perception, there is middling perception, and there is superior perception... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

85. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

85. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception that is an object for the floods, and there is perception that is not an object for the floods.

Tividhena [P 0.0037] saññākkhandho – atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi [T 0.0041] aniyato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is perception fixed in wrongness, there is perception fixed in rightness, and there is unfixed perception... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

86. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

86. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception associated with the floods, and there is perception dissociated from the floods.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is perception with the path as its object, there is perception with the path as its cause, and there is perception with the path as its dominant factor... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

87. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

87. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception that is dissociated from the floods but is an object for the floods, and there is perception that is dissociated from the floods and is not an object for the floods.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is arisen perception, there is unarisen perception, and there is perception that is bound to arise... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

88. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

88. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0039] saññākkhandho – atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception that is an object for the yokes, and there is perception that is not an object for the yokes.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is past perception, there is future perception, and there is present perception... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

89. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

89. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception associated with the yokes, and there is perception dissociated from the yokes.

Tividhena [M 0.0035][P 0.0038] saññākkhandho – atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is perception with a past object, there is perception with a future object, and there is perception with a present object... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

90. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

90. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception that is dissociated from the yokes but is an object for the yokes, and there is perception that is dissociated from the yokes and is not an object for the yokes.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is internal perception, there is external perception, and there is internal-and-external perception…pe…. Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

91. Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto.

91. The aggregate of perception is onefold: it is associated with contact.

Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi [T 0.0042] anīvaraṇiyo.

The aggregate of perception is twofold: there is perception that is an object for the hindrances, and there is perception that is not an object for the hindrances.

Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is threefold: there is perception with an internal object, there is perception with an external object, and there is perception with an internal-and-external object…pe…. Thus, the aggregate of perception is tenfold.

Ubhatovaḍḍhakaṃ.

The Section of Paired Expansion.

Sattavidhena [V 0.0040] saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is sevenfold: there is wholesome perception, there is unwholesome perception, there is indeterminate perception; there is sense-sphere perception, there is form-sphere perception, there is formless-sphere perception, and there is supramundane perception. Thus, the aggregate of perception is sevenfold.

Aparopi sattavidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena saññākkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of perception is sevenfold: there is perception associated with pleasant feeling, there is perception associated with painful feeling, there is perception associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; there is sense-sphere perception, there is form-sphere perception, there is formless-sphere perception, and there is supramundane perception…pe… there is perception with an internal object, with an external object, and with an internal-and-external object; there is sense-sphere perception, there is form-sphere perception, there is formless-sphere perception, and there is supramundane perception. Thus, the aggregate of perception is sevenfold.

Catuvīsatividhena [P 0.0039] saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi [M 0.0036] akusalo, atthi abyākato; cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena [T 0.0043] saññākkhandho.

The aggregate of perception is twenty-fourfold: conditioned by eye-contact, there is a wholesome aggregate of perception, an unwholesome aggregate of perception, and an indeterminate aggregate of perception; so too for that conditioned by ear-contact…pe… and by mind-contact. Furthermore, there is perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of perception is twenty-fourfold.

Aparopi catuvīsatividhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo; cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena saññākkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of perception is twenty-fourfold: conditioned by eye-contact, there is perception associated with pleasant feeling…pe… perception with an internal object, with an external object, and with an internal-and-external object; and there is perception born of eye-contact…pe… and perception born of mind-contact. This is similarly applied for perception conditioned by ear-contact…pe… and by mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of perception is twenty-fourfold.

Tiṃsatividhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā [V 0.0041] …pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ tiṃsatividhena saññākkhandho.

In thirty ways, the aggregate of perception is. Conditioned by eye-contact, there is the aggregate of perception that is of the sense-sphere, of the form sphere, of the formless sphere, and supramundane. Conditioned by ear-contact... and so on... Conditioned by mind-contact, there is the aggregate of perception that is of the sense-sphere, of the form sphere, of the formless sphere, and supramundane. There is perception born of eye-contact... and so on... there is perception born of mind-contact. Thus, in thirty ways, the aggregate of perception is.

Bahuvidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, sotasamphassapaccayā [T 0.0044]…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro[P 0.0040], atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho.

In many ways, the aggregate of perception is. Conditioned by eye-contact, there is the aggregate of perception that is wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate, of the sense-sphere, of the form sphere, of the formless sphere, and supramundane. Conditioned by ear-contact... and so on... Conditioned by mind-contact, there is the aggregate of perception that is wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate, of the sense-sphere, of the form sphere, of the formless sphere, and supramundane. There is perception born of eye-contact... and so on... there is perception born of mind-contact. Thus, in many ways, the aggregate of perception is.

Aparopi [M 0.0037] bahuvidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho.

Furthermore, in many ways, the aggregate of perception is. Conditioned by eye-contact, there is the aggregate of perception that is associated with pleasant feeling... and so on... there is that which has an internal object, an external object, or an internal-and-external object; there is that which is of the sense-sphere, of the form sphere, of the formless sphere, and supramundane. Conditioned by ear-contact... and so on... Conditioned by mind-contact, there is the aggregate of perception that has an internal object, an external object, or an internal-and-external object; there is that which is of the sense-sphere, of the form sphere, of the formless sphere, and supramundane. There is perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact. Thus, in many ways, the aggregate of perception is.

Ayaṃ vuccati saññākkhandho.

This is called the aggregate of perception.

4. Saṅkhārakkhandho

4. The Aggregate of Formations

92. Tattha [V 0.0042] katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

92. Herein, what is the aggregate of formations? The aggregate of formations is of one kind: associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi na hetu.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there is that which is a root, and there is that which is not a root.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo[T 0.0045], atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there is that which is wholesome, there is that which is unwholesome, and there is that which is indeterminate.

Catubbidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno.

The aggregate of formations is fourfold: there is that which is of the sense-sphere, that which is of the form sphere, that which is of the formless sphere, and that which is supramundane.

Pañcavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sukhindriyasampayutto, atthi dukkhindriyasampayutto, atthi somanassindriyasampayutto, atthi domanassindriyasampayutto, atthi upekkhindriyasampayutto. Evaṃ pañcavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is fivefold: there is that which is associated with the faculty of pleasure, that which is associated with the faculty of pain, that which is associated with the faculty of joy, that which is associated with the faculty of displeasure, and that which is associated with the faculty of equanimity. Thus, the aggregate of formations is fivefold.

Chabbidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manosamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ chabbidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is sixfold: volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of formations is sixfold.

Sattavidhena [M 0.0038] saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manodhātusamphassajā [P 0.0041] cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ sattavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is sevenfold: volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, volition born of mind-element-contact, and volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of formations is sevenfold.

Aṭṭhavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… kāyasamphassajā cetanā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā[V 0.0043]. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is eightfold: volition born of eye-contact... and so on... there is volition born of body-contact accompanied by pleasure, and there is volition born of body-contact accompanied by pain; there is volition born of mind-element-contact, and there is volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of formations is eightfold.

Navavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ navavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is ninefold: volition born of eye-contact... and so on... volition born of mind-element-contact; there is wholesome volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact, there is unwholesome volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact, and there is indeterminate volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of formations is ninefold.

Dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… kāyasamphassajā cetanā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā atthi kusalā, atthi [T 0.0046] akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is tenfold: volition born of eye-contact... and so on... there is volition born of body-contact accompanied by pleasure, and there is volition born of body-contact accompanied by pain; there is volition born of mind-element-contact; there is wholesome volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact, there is unwholesome volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact, and there is indeterminate volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact. Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

93. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

93. The aggregate of formations is of one kind: associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi na hetu.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there is that which is a root, and there is that which is not a root.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena [M 0.0039] pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi [T 0.0047] uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho[V 0.0044]. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there is that which is associated with pleasant feeling, there is that which is associated with painful feeling, and there is that which is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. There is that which is resultant, there is that which is productive of result, and there is that which is neither resultant nor productive of result. There is that which is taken up and is an object of clinging, there is that which is not taken up but is an object of clinging, and there is that which is neither taken up nor an object of clinging. There is that which is defiled and an object of defilement, there is that which is undefiled but an object of defilement, and there is that which is undefiled and not an object of defilement. There is that which is with applied thought and sustained thought, there is that which is without applied thought but with sustained thought only, and there is that which is without applied thought and without sustained thought. There is that which is accompanied by rapture, there is that which is accompanied by pleasure, and there is that which is accompanied by equanimity. There is that which is to be abandoned by seeing, there is that which is to be abandoned by development, and there is that which is to be abandoned by neither seeing nor development. There is that which has roots to be abandoned by seeing, there is that which has roots to be abandoned by development, and there is that which has roots to be abandoned by neither seeing nor development. There is that which leads to accumulation, there is that which leads to depletion, and there is that which leads to neither accumulation nor depletion. There is that which is of a trainee, there is that which is of an adept, and there is that which is of neither a trainee nor an adept. There is that which is limited, there is that which is exalted, and there is that which is immeasurable. There is that which has a limited object, there is that which has an exalted object, and there is that which has an immeasurable object. There is that which is inferior, there is that which is intermediate, and there is that which is superior. There is that which is fixed in wrongness, there is that which is fixed in rightness, and there is that which is unfixed. There is that which has the path as object, there is that which has the path as root, and there is that which has the path as predominance. There is that which is arisen, there is that which is unarisen, and there is that which is bound to arise. There is that which is past, there is that which is future, and there is that which is present. There is that which has a past object, there is that which has a future object, and there is that which has a present object. There is that which is internal, there is that which is external, and there is that which is both internal and external. There is that which has an internal object, there is that which has an external object, and there is that which has both an internal and external object… and so on…. Thus, in ten ways, is the aggregate of formations.

94. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

94. The aggregate of formations is of one kind: associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Atthi [P 0.0042] hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto. Atthi hetu ceva sahetuko ca, atthi sahetuko ceva na ca hetu. Atthi hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, atthi hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetu. Atthi na hetu sahetuko, atthi na hetu ahetuko. Atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro. Atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo. Atthi āsavo, atthi no āsavo. Atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. Atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto. Atthi āsavo ceva sāsavo ca, atthi sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo. Atthi āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, atthi āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo. Atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo. Atthi saṃyojanaṃ, atthi no saṃyojanaṃ. Atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo. Atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto. Atthi saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo ca, atthi saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ. Atthi saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto ca, atthi saṃyojanasampayutto [T 0.0048][M 0.0040] ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ. Atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there is that which is with a root, and that which is without a root. There is that which is associated with a root, and that which is dissociated from a root. There is that which is both a root and with a root, and that which is with a root but not a root. There is that which is both a root and associated with a root, and that which is associated with a root but not a root. There is that which is not a root but with a root, and that which is not a root and without a root. There is the mundane, and there is the supramundane. There is that which is cognizable by some, and that which is not cognizable by some. There is that which is a taint, and that which is not a taint. There is that which is subject to taints, and that which is not subject to taints. There is that which is associated with taints, and that which is dissociated from taints. There is that which is both a taint and subject to taints, and that which is subject to taints but not a taint. There is that which is both a taint and associated with taints, and that which is associated with taints but not a taint. There is that which is dissociated from taints but subject to taints, and that which is dissociated from taints and not subject to taints. There is that which is a fetter, and that which is not a fetter. There is that which is subject to fetters, and that which is not subject to fetters. There is that which is both a fetter and subject to fetters, and that which is subject to fetters but not a fetter. There is that which is both a fetter and associated with fetters, and that which is associated with fetters but not a fetter. There is that which is dissociated from fetters but subject to fetters, and that which is dissociated from fetters and not subject to fetters.

Atthi gantho, atthi no gantho. Atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo. Atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto. Atthi gantho ceva ganthaniyo ca, atthi ganthaniyo ceva no ca gantho. Atthi gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca, atthi ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho. Atthi [P 0.0043] ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo. Atthi ogho, atthi no ogho. Atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo. Atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto. Atthi ogho ceva oghaniyo ca, atthi oghaniyo ceva no ca ogho. Atthi ogho ceva oghasampayutto ca, atthi oghasampayutto ceva no ca ogho. Atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo. Atthi yogo, atthi no yogo. Atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo. Atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto. Atthi yogo ceva yoganiyo ca, atthi [V 0.0045] yoganiyo ceva no ca yogo. Atthi yogo ceva yogasampayutto ca, atthi yogasampayutto ceva no ca yogo. Atthi yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇaṃ, atthi no nīvaraṇaṃ. Atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi anīvaraṇiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇasampayutto, atthi nīvaraṇavippayutto. Atthi nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyo ca, atthi nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ. Atthi nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca, atthi nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ. Atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyo, atthi [T 0.0049] nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyo.

There is that which is a tie, and that which is not a tie. There is that which is subject to ties, and that which is not subject to ties. There is that which is both a tie and associated with ties, and that which is associated with ties but not a tie. There is that which is dissociated from floods but subject to floods, and that which is dissociated from floods and not subject to floods. There is that which is a yoke, and that which is not a yoke. There is that which is subject to yokes, and that which is not subject to yokes. There is that which is associated with yokes, and that which is dissociated from yokes. There is that which is both a yoke and subject to yokes, and that which is subject to yokes but not a yoke. Atthi parāmāso, atthi no parāmāso. Atthi parāmaṭṭho, atthi aparāmaṭṭho. Atthi parāmāsasampayutto, atthi parāmāsavippayutto. Atthi parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭho ca, atthi parāmaṭṭho ceva no ca parāmāso. Atthi upādānasampayutto, atthi upādānavippayutto. Atthi upādānañceva upādāniyo ca, atthi upādāniyo ceva no ca upādānaṃ. There is adherence, and there is not adherence. There is that which is adhered to, and that which is not adhered to. There is that which is both clinging and subject to clinging, and that which is subject to clinging but is not clinging. Atthi kileso, atthi no kileso. Atthi saṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkilesiko. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭho, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭho. Atthi kilesasampayutto, atthi kilesavippayutto. Tividhena [V 0.0049] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations that are defiled and are objects of defilement; there are formations that are undefiled but are objects of defilement; and there are formations that are undefiled and are not objects of defilement... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

105. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

105. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi na hetu sahetuko, atthi na hetu ahetuko.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations that are not a root but are accompanied by a root; and there are formations that are not a root and are rootless.

Tividhena [M 0.0044] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought; there are formations without applied thought but with only sustained thought; and there are formations without applied thought and without sustained thought... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

106. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

106. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena [T 0.0053] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are mundane formations, and there are supramundane formations.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations accompanied by rapture; there are formations accompanied by happiness; and there are formations accompanied by equanimity... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

107. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

107. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations cognizable by some means, and there are formations not cognizable by any means.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations to be abandoned by vision; there are formations to be abandoned by cultivation; and there are formations to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

108. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

108. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi āsavo, atthi no āsavo.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations that are cankers, and there are formations that are not cankers.

Tividhena [V 0.0050] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations with a root to be abandoned by vision; there are formations with a root to be abandoned by cultivation; and there are formations with a root to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

109. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

109. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena [P 0.0049] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations that are objects of the cankers, and there are formations that are not objects of the cankers.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations that lead to accumulation; there are formations that lead to de-accumulation; and there are formations that lead neither to accumulation nor to de-accumulation... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

110. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

110. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations associated with the cankers, and there are formations dissociated from the cankers.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations of a trainee; there are formations of one beyond training; and there are formations of one who is neither a trainee nor one beyond training... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

111. Ekavidhena [M 0.0045] saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

111. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi āsavo ceva sāsavo ca, atthi sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo[T 0.0054].

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations that are a canker and are an object of the cankers; and there are formations that are an object of the cankers but are not a canker.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are limited formations; there are exalted formations; and there are immeasurable formations... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

112. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

112. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena [V 0.0051] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, atthi āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations that are a canker and are associated with a canker; and there are formations that are associated with a canker but are not a canker.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations with a limited object; there are formations with an exalted object; and there are formations with an immeasurable object... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

113. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

113. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena [P 0.0050] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavippayuttaanāsavo.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations dissociated from the cankers but are objects of the cankers; and there are formations dissociated from the cankers and are not objects of the cankers.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are inferior formations, middling formations, and superior formations... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

114. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

114. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃyojanaṃ, atthi no saṃyojanaṃ.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations that are fetters, and there are formations that are not fetters.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations fixed in wrongness, formations fixed in rightness, and indeterminate formations... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

115. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

115. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo.

The aggregate of formations is twofold: there are formations that are objects of the fetters, and there are formations that are not objects of the fetters.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is threefold: there are formations that have the path as their object, formations that have the path as their cause, and formations that have the path as their dominant condition... and so on.... Thus, the aggregate of formations is tenfold.

116. Ekavidhena [M 0.0046][V 0.0052] saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

116. The aggregate of formations is onefold: it is only associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto.

The aggregate of volitional formations is twofold: there is that which is associated with fetters, and there is that which is dissociated from fetters.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is threefold: there is that which has arisen, there is that which has not arisen, and there is that which is productive of a future result... Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is tenfold.

117. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto[T 0.0055].

117. The aggregate of volitional formations is onefold: associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena [P 0.0051] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo ca, atthi saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ.

The aggregate of volitional formations is twofold: there is that which is both a fetter and subject to fetters, and there is that which is subject to fetters but is not a fetter.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is threefold: there is the past, there is the future, and there is the present... Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is tenfold.

118. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

118. The aggregate of volitional formations is onefold: associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto ca, atthi saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ.

The aggregate of volitional formations is twofold: there is that which is a fetter and associated with fetters, and there is that which is associated with fetters but is not a fetter.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is threefold: there is that with a past object, there is that with a future object, and there is that with a present object... Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is tenfold.

119. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

119. The aggregate of volitional formations is onefold: associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo.

The aggregate of volitional formations is twofold: there is that which is dissociated from fetters but subject to fetters, and there is that which is dissociated from fetters and not subject to fetters.

Tividhena [V 0.0053] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is threefold: there is the internal, there is the external, and there is the internal-and-external... Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is tenfold.

120. Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto.

120. The aggregate of volitional formations is onefold: associated with consciousness.

Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi gantho, atthi no gantho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is twofold: there is that which is a bond, and there is that which is not a bond.

Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is threefold: there is that which has an internal object, that which has an external object, and that which has an internal-and-external object... Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is tenfold.

Ubhatovaḍḍhakaṃ.

The expansion on both sides.

Sattavidhena [M 0.0047][P 0.0052] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is sevenfold: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, and there is the indeterminate; there is that pertaining to the sense-sphere, there is that pertaining to the form-sphere, there is that pertaining to the formless-sphere, and there is that which is unincluded. Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is sevenfold.

Aparopi sattavidhena [T 0.0056] saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto; atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo; atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of volitional formations is sevenfold: there is that which is associated with pleasant feeling, there is that which is associated with painful feeling, and there is that which is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; there is that pertaining to the sense-sphere, that pertaining to the form-sphere, that pertaining to the formless-sphere, and that which is unincluded... there is that with an internal object, that with an external object, and that with an internal-and-external object; there is that pertaining to the sense-sphere, that pertaining to the form-sphere, that pertaining to the formless-sphere, and that which is unincluded. Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is sevenfold.

Catuvīsatividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… manosamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is of twenty-four kinds: conditioned by eye-contact, the aggregate of volitional formations is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate; conditioned by ear-contact… nose-contact… tongue-contact… body-contact… conditioned by mind-contact, the aggregate of volitional formations is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate; there is volition born of eye-contact… volition born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is of twenty-four kinds.

Aparopi [V 0.0054] catuvīsatividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo; cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… manosamphassajā cetanā; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo; cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manosamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of volitional formations is of twenty-four kinds: conditioned by eye-contact, the aggregate of volitional formations is associated with pleasant feeling… it has an internal object, an external object, or an internal-and-external object; there is volition born of eye-contact… volition born of mind-contact; conditioned by ear-contact… nose-contact… tongue-contact… body-contact… conditioned by mind-contact, the aggregate of volitional formations is associated with pleasant feeling… it has an internal object, an external object, or an internal-and-external object; there is volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is of twenty-four kinds.

Tiṃsatividhena [T 0.0057] saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno[M 0.0048]; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā [P 0.0053] …pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… manosamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ tiṃsatividhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of volitional formations is of thirty kinds. Conditioned by eye-contact, there is an aggregate of volitional formations that is of the sense-sphere, of the form-sphere, of the formless-sphere, and unincluded; conditioned by ear-contact… nose-contact… tongue-contact… body-contact… conditioned by mind-contact, there is an aggregate of volitional formations that is of the sense-sphere, of the form-sphere, of the formless-sphere, and unincluded; there is volition born of eye-contact… volition born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of volitional formations is of thirty kinds.

Bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manosamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

The aggregate of formations is of many kinds. Conditioned by eye-contact, there is a wholesome aggregate of formations, there is an unwholesome one, there is an indeterminate one; there is one of the sense sphere, one of the form sphere, one of the formless sphere, and one that is unincluded. Conditioned by ear-contact... and so on... nose-contact... and so on... tongue-contact... and so on... body-contact... and so on... Conditioned by mind-contact, there is a wholesome aggregate of formations, there is an unwholesome one, there is an indeterminate one; there is one of the sense sphere, one of the form sphere, one of the formless sphere, and one that is unincluded. There is volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of formations is of many kinds.

Aparopi bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi [T 0.0058] arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saṅkhārakkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto [V 0.0055] …pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manosamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of formations is of many kinds. Conditioned by eye-contact, there is an aggregate of formations associated with pleasant feeling, one associated with painful feeling, and one associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling... and so on... there is one with an internal object, one with an external object, and one with an internal-external object; there is one of the sense sphere, one of the form sphere, one of the formless sphere, and one that is unincluded. Conditioned by ear-contact... and so on... nose-contact... and so on... tongue-contact... and so on... body-contact... and so on... Conditioned by mind-contact, there is an aggregate of formations associated with pleasant feeling... and so on... there is one with an internal object, one with an external object, and one with an internal-external object; there is one of the sense sphere, one of the form sphere, one of the formless sphere, and one that is unincluded. There is volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, and volition born of mind-contact. Thus, the aggregate of formations is of many kinds.

Ayaṃ vuccati saṅkhārakkhandho.

This is called the aggregate of formations.

5. Viññāṇakkhandho

5. The Aggregate of Consciousness

121. Tattha [M 0.0049] katamo viññāṇakkhandho? Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

121. Therein, what is the aggregate of consciousness? The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0054] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that with a root and that without a root.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that which is wholesome, that which is unwholesome, and that which is indeterminate.

Catubbidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno.

The aggregate of consciousness is fourfold: there is that of the sense sphere, that of the form sphere, that of the formless sphere, and that which is unincluded.

Pañcavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sukhindriyasampayutto, atthi dukkhindriyasampayutto, atthi somanassindriyasampayutto, atthi domanassindriyasampayutto, atthi upekkhindriyasampayutto. Evaṃ pañcavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is of five kinds: there is that associated with the pleasure faculty, that associated with the pain faculty, that associated with the joy faculty, that associated with the displeasure faculty, and that associated with the equanimity faculty. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is of five kinds.

Chabbidhena [V 0.0056] viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ chabbidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is of six kinds: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is of six kinds.

Sattavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Evaṃ sattavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is of seven kinds: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-element, and mind-consciousness-element. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is of seven kinds.

Aṭṭhavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu[T 0.0059]. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is of eight kinds: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness accompanied by pleasure, body-consciousness accompanied by pain, mind-element, and mind-consciousness-element. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is of eight kinds.

Navavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. Evaṃ navavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is of nine kinds: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-element, wholesome mind-consciousness-element, unwholesome mind-consciousness-element, and indeterminate mind-consciousness-element. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is of nine kinds.

Dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is of ten kinds: eye-consciousness... and so on... body-consciousness accompanied by pleasure, body-consciousness accompanied by pain; mind-element; wholesome mind-consciousness-element, unwholesome mind-consciousness-element, and indeterminate mind-consciousness-element. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is of ten kinds.

122. Ekavidhena [M 0.0050] viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

122. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that with a root, and there is that without a root.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Atthi [P 0.0055] vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto[V 0.0057], atthi avitakkaavicāro. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi [T 0.0060] dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In a threefold way, the consciousness aggregate is: there is that associated with pleasant feeling, that associated with painful feeling, and that associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. There is that which is resultant, that which is a condition for resultants, and that which is neither resultant nor a condition for resultants. There is that which is grasped and an object of clinging, that which is not grasped but an object of clinging, and that which is neither grasped nor an object of clinging. There is that which is defiled and an object for defilements, that which is undefiled but an object for defilements, and that which is undefiled and not an object for defilements. There is that with applied and sustained thought, that without applied thought but with only sustained thought, and that without applied or sustained thought. There is that accompanied by rapture, that accompanied by pleasure, and that accompanied by equanimity. There is that to be abandoned by seeing, that to be abandoned by development, and that to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. There is that with a root to be abandoned by seeing, that with a root to be abandoned by development, and that with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. There is that which leads to accumulation, that which leads to de-accumulation, and that which leads neither to accumulation nor to de-accumulation. There is that of a trainee, that of one beyond training, and that of one who is neither a trainee nor beyond training. There is that which is limited, that which is exalted, and that which is immeasurable. There is that with a limited object, that with an exalted object, and that with an immeasurable object. There is that which is inferior, that which is middling, and that which is superior. There is that fixed in wrongness, that fixed in rightness, and that which is unfixed. There is that with the path as object, that with the path as root, and that with the path as dominant condition. There is that which has arisen, that which has not arisen, and that which is bound to arise. There is that which is past, that which is future, and that which is present. There is that with a past object, that with a future object, and that with a present object. There is that which is internal, that which is external, and that which is internal-and-external. There is that with an internal object, that with an external object, and that with an internal-and-external object… and so on. Thus, in a tenfold way, is the consciousness aggregate.

123. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

123. In a onefold way, the consciousness aggregate is: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto. Atthi na hetu sahetuko, atthi na hetu ahetuko. Atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro. Atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo. Atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. Atthi āsavasampayutto[M 0.0051], atthi āsavavippayutto. Atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo. Atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo. Atthi saṃyojanasampayutto[T 0.0061], atthi saṃyojanavippayutto. Atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo.

In a twofold way, the consciousness aggregate is: there is that associated with a root, and there is that dissociated from a root. There is that which is not a root but has a root, and there is that which is not a root and is without a root. There is that which is mundane, and there is that which is supramundane. There is that which is knowable by something, and there is that which is not knowable by anything. There is that which is an object for taints, and there is that which is not an object for taints. There is that associated with taints, and that dissociated from taints. There is that dissociated from taints which is an object for taints, and that dissociated from taints which is not an object for taints. There is that which is an object for fetters, and there is that which is not an object for fetters. There is that associated with fetters, and that dissociated from fetters. There is that dissociated from fetters which is an object for fetters, and that dissociated from fetters which is not an object for fetters.

Atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo. Atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto. Atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo. Atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo. Atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto. Atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo. Atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo. Atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto[V 0.0058]. Atthi yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi anīvaraṇiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇasampayutto, atthi nīvaraṇavippayutto. Atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyo, atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyo.

There is that which is an object for the bonds; there is that which is not an object for the bonds. There is that associated with the bonds; there is that dissociated from the bonds. There is that dissociated from the bonds which is an object for the bonds; there is that dissociated from the bonds which is not an object for the bonds. There is that which is an object for the floods; there is that which is not an object for the floods. There is that associated with the floods; there is that dissociated from the floods. There is that dissociated from the floods which is an object for the floods; there is that dissociated from the floods which is not an object for the floods. There is that which is an object for the yokes; there is that which is not an object for the yokes. There is that associated with the yokes; there is that dissociated from the yokes. There is that dissociated from the yokes which is an object for the yokes; there is that dissociated from the yokes which is not an object for the yokes. There is that which is an object for the hindrances; there is that which is not an object for the hindrances. There is that associated with the hindrances; there is that dissociated from the hindrances. There is that dissociated from the hindrances which is an object for the hindrances; there is that dissociated from the hindrances which is not an object for the hindrances.

Atthi [P 0.0056] parāmaṭṭho, atthi aparāmaṭṭho. Atthi parāmāsasampayutto, atthi parāmāsavippayutto. Atthi parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭho, atthi parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭho. Atthi upādinno, atthi anupādinno. Atthi upādāniyo, atthi anupādāniyo. Atthi upādānasampayutto, atthi upādānavippayutto. Atthi upādānavippayuttaupādāniyo, atthi upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkilesiko. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭho, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭho. Atthi kilesasampayutto, atthi kilesavippayutto. Atthi kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesiko, atthi kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi na dassanena pahātabbo. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo[T 0.0062], atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi na dassanena pahātabbahetuko. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko.

There is that which is an object for grasping; there is that which is not an object for grasping. There is that associated with grasping; there is that dissociated from grasping. There is that dissociated from grasping which is an object for grasping; there is that dissociated from grasping which is not an object for grasping. There is that grasped by wholesome and unwholesome kamma as its result; there is that not grasped by wholesome and unwholesome kamma as its result. There is that which is an object for clinging; there is that which is not an object for clinging. There is that associated with clinging; there is that dissociated from clinging. There is that dissociated from clinging which is an object for clinging; there is that dissociated from clinging which is not an object for clinging. There is that which is an object for the defilements; there is that which is not an object for the defilements. There is that which is defiled; there is that which is undefiled. There is that associated with the defilements; there is that dissociated from the defilements. There is that dissociated from the defilements which is an object for the defilements; there is that dissociated from the defilements which is not an object for the defilements. There is that to be abandoned by seeing; there is that not to be abandoned by seeing. There is that to be abandoned by development; there is that not to be abandoned by development. There is that which has a root to be abandoned by seeing; there is that which does not have a root to be abandoned by seeing. There is that which has a root to be abandoned by development; there is that which does not have a root to be abandoned by development.

Atthi savitakko, atthi avitakko. Atthi savicāro, atthi avicāro. Atthi sappītiko, atthi appītiko. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi na pītisahagato. Atthi sukhasahagato, atthi na sukhasahagato. Atthi upekkhāsahagato, atthi na upekkhāsahagato. Atthi kāmāvacaro[M 0.0052], atthi na kāmāvacaro. Atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi na rūpāvacaro. Atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi na arūpāvacaro, atthi pariyāpanno, atthi apariyāpanno. Atthi niyyāniko, atthi aniyyāniko. Atthi niyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi sauttaro, atthi anuttaro. Atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

There is that with initial application; there is that without initial application. There is that with sustained application; there is that without sustained application. There is that with rapture; there is that without rapture. There is that accompanied by rapture; there is that not accompanied by rapture. There is that accompanied by pleasant feeling; there is that not accompanied by pleasant feeling. There is that accompanied by equanimous feeling; there is that not accompanied by equanimous feeling. There is that which pertains to the sense-sphere; there is that which does not pertain to the sense-sphere. There is that which pertains to the form-sphere; there is that which does not pertain to the form-sphere. There is that which pertains to the formless-sphere; there is that which does not pertain to the formless-sphere. There is that which is mundane; there is that which is supramundane. There is that which leads to escape; there is that which does not lead to escape. There is that which is fixed; there is that which is not fixed. There is that which is surpassable; there is that which is unsurpassable. There is that with defilements; there is that without defilements.

Tividhena [P 0.0057] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, there is the indeterminate... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

124. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

124. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0059] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that with defilements, and there is that without defilements.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that associated with pleasant feeling; there is that associated with painful feeling; and there is that associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
