There is the resultant... and so on... there is that with an internal object; there is that with an external object; and there is that with both an internal and external object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

Dukamūlakaṃ.

The Root Section on Dyads.

125. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

125. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that with a root, and there is that without a root.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, there is the indeterminate... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

126. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

126. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto…pe… atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that associated with a root, and there is that dissociated from a root... and so on... there is that with defilements, and there is that without defilements.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, there is the indeterminate... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

127. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

127. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0058] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that with a root, and there is that without a root.

Tividhena [V 0.0060] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto[M 0.0053]. Atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that associated with pleasant feeling; there is that associated with painful feeling; and there is that associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. There is the resultant... and so on... there is that with an internal object; there is that with an external object; and there is that with both an internal and external object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

128. Ekavidhena [T 0.0063] viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

128. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto…pe… atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that associated with a root, and there is that dissociated from a root... and so on... there is that with defilements, and there is that without defilements.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that with an internal object; there is that with an external object; and there is that with both an internal and external object... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

Tikamūlakaṃ.

The Root Section on Triads.

129. Ekavidhena [T 0.0064] viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

129. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that with a root, and there is that without a root.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, there is the indeterminate... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

130. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

130. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [P 0.0059] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that associated with a root, and there is that dissociated from a root.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya [V 0.0061] sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that associated with pleasant feeling, there is that associated with painful feeling, and there is that associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

131. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

131. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi na hetu sahetuko, atthi na hetuahetuko.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that which is not a root but is accompanied by a root, and there is that which is not a root and is not accompanied by a root.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is the resultant, there is the result-producing, and there is that which is neither resultant nor result-producing... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

132. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

132. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is the mundane, and there is the supramundane.

Tividhena [M 0.0054] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that produced by grasping and subject to grasping; there is that not produced by grasping but subject to grasping; and there is that not produced by grasping and not subject to grasping... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

133. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

133. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that which is cognizable by some, and there is that which is not cognizable by some.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko…pe…. Evaṃ [T 0.0065] dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is the defiled and a basis for defilements; there is the undefiled but a basis for defilements; and there is the undefiled and not a basis for defilements... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

134. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

134. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that which is subject to the taints, and there is that which is not subject to the taints.

Tividhena [V 0.0062] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought; there is that without applied thought but with sustained thought only; and there is that without applied thought and without sustained thought... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

135. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

135. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto.

In two ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that associated with the taints, and there is that dissociated from the taints.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

In three ways is the aggregate of consciousness: there is that accompanied by joy; there is that accompanied by pleasure; and there is that accompanied by equanimity... and so on.... Thus, in ten ways is the aggregate of consciousness.

136. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

136. In one way is the aggregate of consciousness: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is dissociated from the taints but is an object for the taints, and there is that which is dissociated from the taints and is not an object for the taints.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that to be abandoned by seeing, that to be abandoned by development, and that to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

137. Ekavidhena [M 0.0055] viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

137. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is an object for the fetters, and there is that which is not an object for the fetters.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that with roots to be abandoned by seeing, there is that with roots to be abandoned by development, and there is that with roots to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

138. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

138. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0063] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that associated with fetters, and there is that dissociated from fetters.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī[T 0.0066], atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that which leads to accumulation, there is that which leads to de-accumulation, and there is that which leads neither to accumulation nor to de-accumulation… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

139. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

139. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is dissociated from fetters but is an object for the fetters, and there is that which is dissociated from fetters and is not an object for the fetters.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that of a trainee, there is that of one beyond training, and there is that of neither a trainee nor one beyond training… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

140. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

140. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is an object for the bonds, and there is that which is not an object for the bonds.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is the limited, there is the exalted, and there is the immeasurable… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

141. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

141. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that associated with bonds, and there is that dissociated from bonds.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that with a limited object, there is that with an exalted object, and there is that with an immeasurable object… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

142. Ekavidhena [M 0.0056] viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

142. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena [V 0.0064] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is dissociated from bonds but is an object for bonds, and there is that which is dissociated from bonds and is not an object for bonds.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is the inferior, there is the middling, and there is the superior… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

143. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

143. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is an object for the floods, and there is that which is not an object for the floods.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho[T 0.0067].

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that which is fixed in wrongness, there is that which is fixed in rightness, and there is that which is unfixed… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

144. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

144. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that associated with floods, and there is that dissociated from floods.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that which has the path as object, there is that which has the path as root, and there is that which has the path as dominant factor… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

145. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

145. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is dissociated from floods but is an object for the floods, and there is that which is dissociated from floods and is not an object for the floods.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that which has arisen, there is that which has not arisen, and there is that which is bound to arise… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

146. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

146. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is an object for the yokes, and there is that which is not an object for the yokes.

Tividhena [V 0.0065] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is the past, there is the future, and there is the present… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

147. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

147. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that associated with yokes, and there is that dissociated from yokes.

Tividhena [M 0.0057] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that which has the past as object, there is that which has the future as object, and there is that which has the present as object… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

148. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – phassasampayutto.

148. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is dissociated from yokes but is an object for the yokes, and there is that which is dissociated from yokes and is not an object for the yokes.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is the internal, there is the external, and there is the internal-external… Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

149. Ekavidhena viññāṇakkhandho [T 0.0068] – phassasampayutto.

149. The aggregate of consciousness is of one kind: associated with contact.

Duvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi anīvaraṇiyo.

The aggregate of consciousness is twofold: there is that which is an object for the hindrances, and there is that which is not an object for the hindrances.

Tividhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is threefold: there is that with an internal object, there is that with an external object, and there is that with an internal-external object... and so on... Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is tenfold.

Ubhatovaḍḍhakaṃ.

The method of expansion by both.

Sattavidhena [P 0.0060] viññāṇakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi [V 0.0066] kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is sevenfold: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, there is the indeterminate, there is that of the sensuous sphere, there is that of the fine-material sphere, there is that of the immaterial sphere, and there is that which is unincluded. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is sevenfold.

Aparopi sattavidhena viññāṇakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of consciousness is sevenfold: there is that associated with pleasant feeling, there is that associated with painful feeling, there is that associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; there is that of the sensuous sphere, there is that of the fine-material sphere, there is that of the immaterial sphere, and there is that which is unincluded... and so on... there is that with an internal object, there is that with an external object, there is that with an internal-external object; there is that of the sensuous sphere, there is that of the fine-material sphere, there is that of the immaterial sphere, and there is that which is unincluded. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is sevenfold.

Catuvīsatividhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ[M 0.0058], jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena viññāṇakkhandho[T 0.0069].

The aggregate of consciousness is twenty-fourfold: conditioned by eye-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness that is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate; conditioned by ear-contact… and so on… conditioned by mind-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness that is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate. There is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is twenty-fourfold.

Aparopi catuvīsatividhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo; cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo; cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena viññāṇakkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of consciousness is twenty-fourfold: conditioned by eye-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling… and so on… with an internal object, with an external object, and with an internal-external object; there is eye-consciousness… and so on… body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. Conditioned by ear-contact… and so on… conditioned by mind-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness with an internal object, with an external object, and with an internal-external object; there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is twenty-fourfold.

Tiṃsatividhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā [V 0.0067] …pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhuviññāṇaṃ[P 0.0061], sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ tiṃsatividhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is thirtyfold: conditioned by eye-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness that is of the sensuous sphere, of the fine-material sphere, of the immaterial sphere, or unincluded. Conditioned by ear-contact… and so on… conditioned by mind-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness that is of the sensuous sphere, of the fine-material sphere, of the immaterial sphere, or unincluded. There is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is thirtyfold.

Bahuvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā [T 0.0070] …pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ bahuvidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

The aggregate of consciousness is manifold: conditioned by eye-contact, the aggregate of consciousness is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate; of the sensuous sphere, of the fine-material sphere, of the immaterial sphere, or unincluded; there is eye-consciousness… and so on… mind-consciousness. Conditioned by ear-contact… and so on… conditioned by mind-contact, the aggregate of consciousness is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate; of the sensuous sphere, of the fine-material sphere, of the immaterial sphere, or unincluded; there is eye-consciousness… and so on… mind-consciousness. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is manifold.

Aparopi [M 0.0059] bahuvidhena viññāṇakkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā viññāṇakkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ bahuvidhena viññāṇakkhandho.

Furthermore, the aggregate of consciousness is manifold: conditioned by eye-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness associated with pleasant feeling… and so on… with an internal object, with an external object, with an internal-external object; that is of the sensuous sphere, of the fine-material sphere, of the immaterial sphere, or unincluded. Conditioned by ear-contact… and so on… conditioned by mind-contact, there is the aggregate of consciousness associated with pleasant feeling… and so on… with an internal object, with an external object, with an internal-external object; that is of the sensuous sphere, of the fine-material sphere, of the immaterial sphere, or unincluded. There is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. Thus, the aggregate of consciousness is manifold.

Ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇakkhandho.

This is called the aggregate of consciousness.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition is finished.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Section on Questions

150. Pañcakkhandhā [V 0.0068] – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho.

150. The five aggregates: the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.

151. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati kusalā, kati [T 0.0071] akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

151. Of the five aggregates, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate… and so on… how many are with defilements, how many without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. Triads

152. Rūpakkhandho [P 0.0062] abyākato. Cattāro khandhā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dve khandhā na vattabbā – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi. Tayo khandhā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Rūpakkhandho nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Cattāro khandhā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Rūpakkhandho siyā upādinnupādāniyo, siyā anupādinnupādāniyo[M 0.0060]. Cattāro khandhā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

152. The form aggregate is indeterminate. The four aggregates may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be indeterminate. The two aggregates are not to be designated as “associated with pleasant feeling,” nor “associated with painful feeling,” nor “associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.” The three aggregates may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The form aggregate is neither a resultant nor a condition for resultants. The four aggregates may be resultants, may be conditions for resultants, or may be neither resultants nor conditions for resultants. The form aggregate may be taken up and an object of clinging, or it may be not taken up but an object of clinging. The four aggregates may be taken up and an object of clinging, may be not taken up but an object of clinging, or may be not taken up and not an object of clinging.

Rūpakkhandho asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Rūpakkhandho avitakkaavicāro. Tayo khandhā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā savitakkasavicāro, siyā avitakkavicāramatto, siyā avitakkaavicāro, siyā na vattabbo – “savitakkasavicāro”tipi, “avitakkavicāramatto”tipi, “avitakkaavicāro”tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “pītisahagato”tipi, “sukhasahagato”tipi, “upekkhāsahagato”tipi. Vedanākkhandho siyā pītisahagato na sukhasahagato na upekkhāsahagato, siyā na vattabbo – “pītisahagato”ti. Tayo [V 0.0069] khandhā siyā [T 0.0072] pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – “pītisahagatā”tipi, “sukhasahagatā”tipi, “upekkhāsahagatā”tipi.

The form aggregate is undefiled but an object of defilement. The four aggregates may be defiled and an object of defilement, may be undefiled but an object of defilement, or may be undefiled and not an object of defilement. The form aggregate is without applied thought and without sustained thought. The three aggregates may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, may be without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or may be without applied thought and without sustained thought. The formations aggregate may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, may be without applied thought but with sustained thought only, may be without applied thought and without sustained thought, or it is not to be designated as “with applied thought and with sustained thought,” nor “without applied thought but with sustained thought only,” nor “without applied thought and without sustained thought.” The form aggregate is not to be designated as “accompanied by joy,” nor “accompanied by pleasure,” nor “accompanied by equanimity.” The feeling aggregate may be accompanied by joy but not by pleasure and not by equanimity, or it is not to be designated as “accompanied by joy.” The three aggregates may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by pleasure, may be accompanied by equanimity, or they are not to be designated as “accompanied by joy,” nor “accompanied by pleasure,” nor “accompanied by equanimity.”

Rūpakkhandho neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Cattāro khandhā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Rūpakkhandho neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Cattāro khandhā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Rūpakkhandho nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Cattāro khandhā siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Rūpakkhandho nevasekkhanāsekkho. Cattāro khandhā siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Rūpakkhandho paritto. Cattāro khandhā siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “parittārammaṇā”tipi[P 0.0063], “mahaggatārammaṇā”tipi, “appamāṇārammaṇā”tipi. Rūpakkhandho majjhimo. Cattāro khandhā siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Rūpakkhandho aniyato[M 0.0061]. Cattāro khandhā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā.

The form aggregate is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. The four aggregates may be abandoned by vision, may be abandoned by development, or may be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. The form aggregate is with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. The four aggregates may be with a cause to be abandoned by vision, may be with a cause to be abandoned by development, or may be with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. The form aggregate leads neither to accumulation nor to decline. The four aggregates may lead to accumulation, may lead to decline, or may lead neither to accumulation nor to decline. The form aggregate is neither of one in training nor of one beyond training. The four aggregates may be of those in training, may be of those beyond training, or may be of neither those in training nor those beyond training. The form aggregate is limited. The four aggregates may be limited, may be exalted, or may be immeasurable. The form aggregate is without an object. The four aggregates may have a limited object, may have an exalted object, may have an immeasurable object, or they are not to be designated as having a limited object, nor an exalted object, nor an immeasurable object. The form aggregate is middling. The four aggregates may be inferior, may be middling, or may be superior. The form aggregate is not fixed. The four aggregates may be fixed in wrongness, may be fixed in rightness, or may be not fixed.

Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – “maggārammaṇā”tipi, “maggahetukā”tipi[T 0.0073], “maggādhipatino”tipi; siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino; siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “atītārammaṇā”tipi, “anāgatārammaṇā”tipi, “paccuppannārammaṇā”tipi; siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Rūpakkhandho anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “ajjhattārammaṇā”tipi, “bahiddhārammaṇā”tipi, “ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā”tipi. Cattāro khandhā anidassanaappaṭighā. Rūpakkhandho siyā sanidassanasappaṭigho, siyā anidassanasappaṭigho, siyā anidassanaappaṭigho.

The form aggregate is without an object. The four aggregates may have the path as object, may have the path as a cause, may have the path as a dominant factor, or they are not to be designated as having the path as object, nor as having the path as a cause, nor as having the path as a dominant factor; they may be arisen, may be unarisen, or may be destined to arise; they may be past, may be future, or may be present. The form aggregate is without an object. The four aggregates may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or they are not to be designated as having a past object, nor a future object, nor a present object; they may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. The form aggregate is without an object. The four aggregates may have an internal object, may have an external object, may have both an internal and an external object, or they are not to be designated as having an internal object, nor an external object, nor both an internal and an external object. The four aggregates are invisible and non-resistant. The form aggregate may be visible and resistant, may be invisible and resistant, or may be invisible and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

153. Cattāro [V 0.0070] khandhā na hetū. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā hetu, siyā na hetu. Rūpakkhandho ahetuko. Cattāro khandhā siyā sahetukā, siyā ahetukā. Rūpakkhandho hetuvippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā hetusampayuttā, siyā hetuvippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “hetu ceva sahetuko cā”tipi, “sahetuko ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva sahetukā cā”ti, siyā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū, siyā na vattabbā – “sahetukā ceva na ca hetū”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā hetu ceva sahetuko ca, siyā [T 0.0074] sahetuko ceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbo – “hetu ceva sahetuko cā”tipi, “sahetuko ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “hetu ceva hetusampayutto cā”tipi, “hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”ti, siyā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū, siyā na vattabbā – “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, siyā hetusampayutto ceva na [M 0.0062] ca hetu, siyā na vattabbo – “hetu ceva hetusampayutto cā”tipi, “hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Rūpakkhandho na hetu ahetuko[P 0.0064]. Tayo khandhā siyā na hetū sahetukā, siyā na hetū ahetukā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā na hetu sahetuko, siyā na hetu ahetuko, siyā na vattabbo – “na hetu sahetuko”tipi, “na hetu ahetuko”tipi.

153. The four mental aggregates are not roots. The aggregate of formations, in some cases, is a root; in some cases, is not a root. The aggregate of form is without root. The four mental aggregates, in some cases, are with roots; in some cases, are without root. The aggregate of form is dissociated from roots. The four mental aggregates, in some cases, are associated with roots; in some cases, are dissociated from roots. Regarding the aggregate of form, it should not be said that 'it is both a root and with root,' nor that 'it is with root but not a root.' Regarding the three aggregates, it should not be said that 'they are both roots and with roots'; in some cases, they are with roots but not roots; in some cases, it should not be said that 'they are with roots but not roots.' The aggregate of formations, in some cases, is both a root and with root; in some cases, is with root but not a root; in some cases, it should not be said that 'it is both a root and with root,' nor that 'it is with root but not a root.' Regarding the aggregate of form, it should not be said that 'it is both a root and associated with a root,' nor that 'it is associated with a root but not a root.' Regarding the three aggregates, it should not be said that 'they are both roots and associated with roots'; in some cases, they are associated with roots but not roots; in some cases, it should not be said that 'they are associated with roots but not roots.' The aggregate of formations, in some cases, is both a root and associated with a root; in some cases, is associated with a root but not a root; in some cases, it should not be said that 'it is both a root and associated with a root,' nor that 'it is associated with a root but not a root.' The aggregate of form is not a root and is without root. The three aggregates, in some cases, are not roots but are with roots; in some cases, are not roots and are without root. The aggregate of formations, in some cases, is not a root but is with root; in some cases, is not a root and is without root; in some cases, it should not be said that 'it is not a root but is with root,' nor that 'it is not a root and is without root.'

Sappaccayā, saṅkhatā.

With conditions, conditioned.

Cattāro khandhā anidassanā. Rūpakkhandho siyā sanidassano, siyā anidassano. Cattāro khandhā appaṭighā. Rūpakkhandho siyā sappaṭigho, siyā appaṭigho. Rūpakkhandho rūpaṃ. Cattāro khandhā arūpā. Rūpakkhandho lokiyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā; kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

The four mental aggregates are invisible. The aggregate of form, in some cases, is visible; in some cases, is invisible. The four mental aggregates are without resistance. The aggregate of form, in some cases, is with resistance; in some cases, is without resistance. The aggregate of form is form. The four mental aggregates are formless. The aggregate of form is mundane. The four mental aggregates, in some cases, are mundane; in some cases, are supramundane; cognizable by a certain means, not cognizable by a certain means.

Cattāro khandhā no āsavā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā āsavo, siyā no āsavo. Rūpakkhandho sāsavo. Cattāro khandhā [T 0.0075] siyā sāsavā, siyā anāsavā. Rūpakkhandho āsavavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā āsavasampayuttā, siyā āsavavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho [V 0.0071] na vattabbo – “āsavo ceva sāsavo cā”ti, sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”ti, siyā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, siyā na vattabbā – “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā āsavo ceva sāsavo ca, siyā sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbo – “āsavo ceva sāsavo cā”tipi, “sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo”tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto cā”tipi, “āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo”tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā, siyā na vattabbā – “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, siyā āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbo – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto cā”tipi, “āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo”tipi. Rūpakkhandho āsavavippayuttasāsavo. Cattāro khandhā siyā āsavavippayuttasāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā, siyā [M 0.0063] na vattabbā – “āsavavippayuttasāsavā”tipi, “āsavavippayuttaanāsavā”tipi.

The four mental aggregates are not taints. The aggregate of formations, in some cases, is a taint; in some cases, is not a taint. The aggregate of form is an object for the taints. The four mental aggregates, in some cases, are objects for the taints; in some cases, are not objects for the taints. The aggregate of form is dissociated from taints. The four mental aggregates, in some cases, are associated with taints; in some cases, are dissociated from taints. Regarding the aggregate of form, it should not be said that 'it is both a taint and an object for the taints'; it is an object for the taints but not a taint. Regarding the three aggregates, it should not be said that 'they are both taints and objects for the taints'; in some cases, they are objects for the taints but not taints; in some cases, it should not be said that 'they are objects for the taints but not taints.' The aggregate of formations, in some cases, is both a taint and an object for the taints; in some cases, is an object for the taints but not a taint; in some cases, it should not be said that 'it is both a taint and an object for the taints,' nor that 'it is an object for the taints but not a taint.' Regarding the aggregate of form, it should not be said that 'it is both a taint and associated with taints,' nor that 'it is associated with taints but not a taint.' Regarding the three aggregates, it should not be said that 'they are both taints and associated with taints'; in some cases, they are associated with taints but not taints; in some cases, it should not be said that 'they are associated with taints but not taints.' The aggregate of formations, in some cases, is both a taint and associated with taints; in some cases, is associated with taints but not a taint; in some cases, it should not be said that 'it is both a taint and associated with taints,' nor that 'it is associated with taints but not a taint.' The aggregate of form is dissociated from taints but is an object for the taints. The four mental aggregates, in some cases, are dissociated from taints but are objects for the taints; in some cases, are dissociated from taints and are not objects for the taints; in some cases, it should not be said that 'they are dissociated from taints but are objects for the taints,' nor that 'they are dissociated from taints and are not objects for the taints.'

Cattāro khandhā no saṃyojanā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā saṃyojanaṃ, siyā no saṃyojanaṃ. Rūpakkhandho saṃyojaniyo. Cattāro khandhā [T 0.0076] siyā saṃyojaniyā, siyā asaṃyojaniyā. Rūpakkhandho saṃyojanavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo cā”ti, “saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ”. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cā”ti, siyā saṃyojaniyā ceva [P 0.0065] no ca saṃyojanā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo ca, siyā saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo cā”tipi, “saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto cā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto ca, siyā saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto [V 0.0072] cā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi. Rūpakkhandho saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā, siyā na [T 0.0077] vattabbā – “saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā”tipi, “saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā”tipi.

The four aggregates are not fetters. The aggregate of formations may be a fetter or not a fetter. The aggregate of form is subject to fetters. The four aggregates may be subject to fetters or not subject to fetters. The aggregate of form is dissociated from fetters. The four aggregates may be associated with fetters or dissociated from fetters. The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a fetter and subject to fetters'; it is 'subject to fetters but not a fetter'. The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both fetters and subject to fetters'; in some cases they are 'subject to fetters but not fetters,' while in other cases it is not to be stated that they are 'subject to fetters but not fetters.' The aggregate of formations is in some cases 'both a fetter and subject to fetters'; in other cases, 'subject to fetters but not a fetter'; and in yet other cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a fetter and subject to fetters,' nor as 'subject to fetters but not a fetter.' The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a fetter and associated with fetters,' nor as 'associated with fetters but not a fetter.' The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both fetters and associated with fetters'; in some cases they are 'associated with fetters but not fetters,' while in other cases it is not to be stated that they are 'associated with fetters but not fetters.' The aggregate of formations is in some cases 'both a fetter and associated with fetters'; in other cases, 'associated with fetters but not a fetter'; and in yet other cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a fetter and associated with fetters,' nor as 'associated with fetters but not a fetter.' The aggregate of form is dissociated from fetters but subject to fetters. The four aggregates are in some cases 'dissociated from fetters but subject to fetters'; in other cases, 'dissociated from fetters and not subject to fetters'; and in yet other cases, it is not to be stated that they are 'dissociated from fetters but subject to fetters,' nor 'dissociated from fetters and not subject to fetters.'

Cattāro khandhā no ganthā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā gantho, siyā no gantho. Rūpakkhandho ganthaniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā ganthaniyā, siyā aganthaniyā. Rūpakkhandho ganthavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā ganthasampayuttā, siyā ganthavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “gantho ceva ganthaniyo cā”ti, “ganthaniyo ceva no ca gantho”. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā [M 0.0064] – “ganthā ceva ganthaniyā cā”ti, siyā ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā gantho ceva ganthaniyo ca, siyā ganthaniyo ceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbo – “gantho ceva ganthaniyo cā”tipi, “ganthaniyo ceva no ca gantho”tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “gantho ceva ganthasampayutto cā”tipi, “ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho”tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca, siyā ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbo – “gantho ceva ganthasampayutto cā”tipi, “ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho”ti pi. Rūpakkhandho ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā[T 0.0078], siyā ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā”tipi, “ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā”tipi.

The four aggregates are not bondages. The aggregate of formations may be a bondage or not a bondage. The aggregate of form is subject to bondages. The four aggregates may be subject to bondages or not subject to bondages. The aggregate of form is dissociated from bondages. The four aggregates may be associated with bondages or dissociated from bondages. The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a bondage and subject to bondage'; it is 'subject to bondage but not a bondage'. The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both bondages and subject to bondages'; in some cases they are 'subject to bondages but not bondages,' while in other cases it is not to be stated that they are 'subject to bondages but not bondages.' The aggregate of formations is in some cases 'both a bondage and subject to bondage'; in other cases, 'subject to bondage but not a bondage'; and in yet other cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a bondage and subject to bondage,' nor as 'subject to bondage but not a bondage.' The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a bondage and associated with bondages,' nor as 'associated with bondages but not a bondage.' The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both bondages and associated with bondages'; in some cases they are 'associated with bondages but not bondages,' while in other cases it is not to be stated that they are 'associated with bondages but not bondages.' The aggregate of formations is in some cases 'both a bondage and associated with bondages'; in other cases, 'associated with bondages but not a bondage'; and in yet other cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a bondage and associated with bondages,' nor as 'associated with bondages but not a bondage.' The aggregate of form is dissociated from bondages but subject to bondages. The four aggregates are in some cases 'dissociated from bondages but subject to bondages'; in other cases, 'dissociated from bondages and not subject to bondages'; and in yet other cases, it is not to be stated that they are 'dissociated from bondages but subject to bondages,' nor 'dissociated from bondages and not subject to bondages.'

Cattāro khandhā no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no [P 0.0066] nīvaraṇā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā no nīvaraṇaṃ. Rūpakkhandho nīvaraṇiyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā nīvaraṇiyā, siyā anīvaraṇiyā. Rūpakkhandho nīvaraṇavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyo cā”ti, “nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ”. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”ti, siyā nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyo [V 0.0073] ca, siyā nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyo cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇa”ntipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayutto cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇa”ntipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca, siyā nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayutto cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no [M 0.0065] ca nīvaraṇa”ntipi. Rūpakkhandho [T 0.0079] nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā”tipi, “nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā”tipi.

The four aggregates are not floods... pe... not bonds... pe... not hindrances. The aggregate of formations may be a hindrance, or it may not be a hindrance. The aggregate of form is an object of the hindrances. The four aggregates may be objects of the hindrances, or they may not be objects of the hindrances. The aggregate of form is dissociated from the hindrances. The four aggregates may be associated with the hindrances, or they may be dissociated from the hindrances. The aggregate of form is not to be spoken of as 'both a hindrance and an object of the hindrances'; it is an object of the hindrances but not a hindrance. The three aggregates are not to be spoken of as 'both hindrances and objects of the hindrances'; in some cases, they are 'objects of the hindrances but not hindrances'; in some cases, they are not to be spoken of as 'objects of the hindrances but not hindrances.' The aggregate of formations may be 'both a hindrance and an object of the hindrances,' or it may be 'an object of the hindrances but not a hindrance'; in some cases, it is not to be spoken of as 'both a hindrance and an object of the hindrances,' nor as 'an object of the hindrances but not a hindrance.' The aggregate of form is not to be spoken of as 'both a hindrance and associated with the hindrances,' nor as 'associated with the hindrances but not a hindrance.' The three aggregates are not to be spoken of as 'both hindrances and associated with the hindrances'; in some cases, they are 'associated with the hindrances but not hindrances'; in some cases, they are not to be spoken of as 'associated with the hindrances but not hindrances.' The aggregate of formations may be 'both a hindrance and associated with the hindrances,' or it may be 'associated with the hindrances but not a hindrance'; in some cases, it is not to be spoken of as 'both a hindrance and associated with the hindrances,' nor as 'associated with the hindrances but not a hindrance.' The aggregate of form is dissociated from the hindrances and an object of the hindrances. The four aggregates may be 'dissociated from the hindrances and objects of the hindrances,' or they may be 'dissociated from the hindrances and not objects of the hindrances'; in some cases, they are not to be spoken of as 'dissociated from the hindrances and objects of the hindrances,' nor as 'dissociated from the hindrances and not objects of the hindrances.'

Cattāro khandhā no parāmāsā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā parāmāso, siyā no parāmāso. Rūpakkhandho parāmaṭṭho. Cattāro khandhā siyā parāmaṭṭhā, siyā aparāmaṭṭhā. Rūpakkhandho parāmāsavippayutto. Tayo khandhā siyā parāmāsasampayuttā, siyā parāmāsavippayuttā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā parāmāsasampayutto, siyā parāmāsavippayutto, siyā na vattabbo – “parāmāsasampayutto”tipi, “parāmāsavippayutto”tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭho cā”ti, “parāmaṭṭho ceva no ca parāmāso”. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “parāmāsā ceva parāmaṭṭhā cā”ti, siyā parāmaṭṭhā ceva no ca parāmāsā, siyā na vattabbā – “parāmaṭṭhā ceva no ca parāmāsā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭho ca, siyā parāmaṭṭho ceva no ca parāmāso, siyā na vattabbo – “parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭho cā”tipi, “parāmaṭṭho ceva no ca parāmāso”tipi. Rūpakkhandho parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭho. Cattāro khandhā siyā parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā, siyā parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā[P 0.0067], siyā na vattabbā – “parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā”tipi, “parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā”tipi.

The four aggregates are not graspings. The aggregate of formations may be a grasping, or it may not be a grasping. The aggregate of form is an object of grasping. The four aggregates may be objects of grasping, or they may not be objects of grasping. The aggregate of form is dissociated from grasping. The three aggregates may be associated with grasping, or they may be dissociated from grasping. The aggregate of formations may be associated with grasping, or it may be dissociated from grasping; in some cases, it is not to be spoken of as 'associated with grasping' nor as 'dissociated from grasping.' The aggregate of form is not to be spoken of as 'both a grasping and an object of grasping'; it is an object of grasping but not a grasping. The three aggregates are not to be spoken of as 'both graspings and objects of grasping'; in some cases, they are 'objects of grasping but not graspings'; in some cases, they are not to be spoken of as 'objects of grasping but not graspings.' The aggregate of formations may be 'both a grasping and an object of grasping,' or it may be 'an object of grasping but not a grasping'; in some cases, it is not to be spoken of as 'both a grasping and an object of grasping,' nor as 'an object of grasping but not a grasping.' The aggregate of form is dissociated from grasping and is an object of grasping. The four aggregates may be 'dissociated from grasping and objects of grasping,' or they may be 'dissociated from grasping and not objects of grasping'; in some cases, they are not to be spoken of as 'dissociated from grasping and objects of grasping,' nor as 'dissociated from grasping and not objects of grasping.'

Rūpakkhandho [T 0.0080] anārammaṇo. Cattāro khandhā sārammaṇā. Viññāṇakkhandho cittaṃ. Cattāro khandhā no cittā. Tayo khandhā cetasikā. Dve khandhā acetasikā. Tayo khandhā cittasampayuttā[V 0.0074]. Rūpakkhandho cittavippayutto. Viññāṇakkhandho na vattabbo – “cittena sampayutto”tipi, “cittena vippayutto”tipi. Tayo khandhā cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Rūpakkhandho cittavisaṃsaṭṭho. Viññāṇakkhandho na vattabbo – “cittena saṃsaṭṭho”tipi, “cittena visaṃsaṭṭho”tipi. Tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānā. Viññāṇakkhandho no cittasamuṭṭhāno. Rūpakkhandho siyā cittasamuṭṭhāno, siyā no cittasamuṭṭhāno. Tayo khandhā cittasahabhuno. Viññāṇakkhandho no cittasahabhū. Rūpakkhandho siyā cittasahabhū, siyā no cittasahabhū. Tayo khandhā cittānuparivattino. Viññāṇakkhandho no cittānuparivatti. Rūpakkhandho [M 0.0066] siyā cittānuparivatti, siyā no cittānuparivatti. Tayo khandhā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Dve khandhā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Tayo khandhā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Dve khandhā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Tayo khandhā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Dve khandhā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino.

The aggregate of form is without an object. The four aggregates are with an object. The aggregate of consciousness is mind. The four aggregates are not mind. The three aggregates are mental factors. The two aggregates are not mental factors. The three aggregates are associated with mind. The aggregate of form is dissociated from mind. The aggregate of consciousness is not to be spoken of as 'associated with mind' nor as 'dissociated from mind.' The three aggregates are mixed with mind. The aggregate of form is unmixed with mind. The aggregate of consciousness is not to be spoken of as 'mixed with mind' nor as 'unmixed with mind.' The three aggregates arise from mind. The aggregate of consciousness does not arise from mind. The aggregate of form may arise from mind, or it may not arise from mind. The three aggregates are co-arisen with mind. The aggregate of consciousness is not co-arisen with mind. The aggregate of form may be co-arisen with mind, or it may not be co-arisen with mind. The three aggregates are consequent upon mind. The aggregate of consciousness is not consequent upon mind. The aggregate of form may be consequent upon mind, or it may not be consequent upon mind. The three aggregates are mixed with mind and arise from mind. The two aggregates are not mixed with mind and do not arise from mind. The three aggregates are mixed with mind, arise from mind, and are co-arisen with mind. The two aggregates are not mixed with mind, do not arise from mind, and are not co-arisen with mind. The three aggregates are mixed with mind, arise from mind, and are consequent upon mind. The two aggregates are not mixed with mind, do not arise from mind, and are not consequent upon mind.

Viññāṇakkhandho ajjhattiko. Tayo khandhā bāhirā. Rūpakkhandho siyā ajjhattiko, siyā bāhiro. Cattāro khandhā no upādā. Rūpakkhandho siyā upādā, siyā no upādā, siyā upādinnā, siyā anupādinnā. Cattāro [T 0.0081] khandhā no upādānā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā upādānaṃ, siyā no upādānaṃ. Rūpakkhandho upādāniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā upādāniyā, siyā anupādāniyā. Rūpakkhandho upādānavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā upādānasampayuttā, siyā upādānavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “upādānañceva upādāniyo cā”ti, “upādāniyo ceva no ca upādānaṃ”. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “upādānañceva upādāniyā cā”ti, siyā upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā, siyā na vattabbā – “upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā upādānañceva upādāniyo ca, siyā upādāniyo ceva no ca upādānaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – “upādānañceva upādāniyo cā”tipi, “upādāniyo ceva no ca upādāna”ntipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “upādānañceva upādānasampayutto [P 0.0068] cā”tipi, “upādānasampayutto ceva no ca upādāna”ntipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā, siyā na vattabbā – “upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā upādānañceva upādānasampayutto ca, siyā upādānasampayutto ceva no ca upādānaṃ, siyā na vattabbo – “upādānañceva [V 0.0075] upādānasampayutto cā”tipi, “upādānasampayutto ceva no ca upādāna”ntipi. Rūpakkhandho upādānavippayuttaupādāniyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā, siyā upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā[T 0.0082], siyā na vattabbā – “upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā”tipi, “upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā”tipi.

The aggregate of consciousness is internal. The three aggregates are external. The aggregate of form may be internal or external. The four aggregates are not derived. The aggregate of form may be derived or not derived; it may be grasped by kamma or not grasped by kamma. The four aggregates are not clingings. The aggregate of formations may be a clinging or not a clinging. The aggregate of form is subject to clinging. The four aggregates may be subject to clinging or not subject to clinging. The aggregate of form is dissociated from clinging. The four aggregates may be associated with clinging or dissociated from clinging. The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a clinging and subject to clinging'; it is 'subject to clinging but not a clinging'. The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both clingings and subject to clinging'; in some cases, they are 'subject to clinging but not clingings'; in some cases, they are not to be stated as 'subject to clinging but not clingings'. The aggregate of formations may be 'both a clinging and subject to clinging', or 'subject to clinging but not a clinging'; or in some cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a clinging and subject to clinging', nor as 'subject to clinging but not a clinging'. The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a clinging and associated with clinging', nor as 'associated with clinging but not a clinging'. The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both clingings and associated with clinging'; in some cases, they are 'associated with clinging but not clingings'; in some cases, they are not to be stated as 'associated with clinging but not clingings'. The aggregate of formations may be 'both a clinging and associated with clinging', or 'associated with clinging but not a clinging'; or in some cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a clinging and associated with clinging', nor as 'associated with clinging but not a clinging'. The aggregate of form is dissociated from clinging and subject to clinging. The four aggregates may be 'dissociated from clinging and subject to clinging', or 'dissociated from clinging and not subject to clinging'; or in some cases, they are not to be stated as 'dissociated from clinging and subject to clinging', nor as 'dissociated from clinging and not subject to clinging'.

Cattāro khandhā no kilesā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā kileso, siyā no kileso. Rūpakkhandho saṃkilesiko. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃkilesikā[M 0.0067], siyā asaṃkilesikā. Rūpakkhandho asaṃkiliṭṭho. Cattāro khandhā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhā. Rūpakkhandho kilesavippayutto. Cattāro khandhā siyā kilesasampayuttā, siyā kilesavippayuttā. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “kileso ceva saṃkilesiko cā”ti, “saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso”. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā cā”ti, siyā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā kileso ceva saṃkilesiko ca, siyā saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbo – “kileso ceva saṃkilesiko cā”tipi, “saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso”tipi. Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho cā”tipi, “saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no [T 0.0083] ca kileso”tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā cā”ti, siyā saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca, siyā saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbo – “kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho cā”tipi, “saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso”tipi.

The four aggregates are not defilements. The aggregate of formations may be a defilement or not a defilement. The aggregate of form is subject to defilement. The four aggregates may be subject to defilement or not subject to defilement. The aggregate of form is undefiled. The four aggregates may be defiled or undefiled. The aggregate of form is dissociated from defilements. The four aggregates may be associated with defilements or dissociated from defilements. The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a defilement and subject to defilement'; it is 'subject to defilement but not a defilement'. The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both defilements and subject to defilement'; in some cases, they are 'subject to defilement but not defilements'; in some cases, they are not to be stated as 'subject to defilement but not defilements'. The aggregate of formations may be 'both a defilement and subject to defilement', or 'subject to defilement but not a defilement'; or in some cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a defilement and subject to defilement', nor as 'subject to defilement but not a defilement'. The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a defilement and defiled', nor as 'defiled but not a defilement'. The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both defilements and defiled'; in some cases, they are 'defiled but not defilements'; in some cases, they are not to be stated as 'defiled but not defilements'. The aggregate of formations may be 'both a defilement and defiled', or 'defiled but not a defilement'; or in some cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a defilement and defiled', nor as 'defiled but not a defilement'.

Rūpakkhandho na vattabbo – “kileso ceva kilesasampayutto cā”tipi, “kilesasampayutto ceva no ca kileso”tipi. Tayo khandhā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva kilesasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā, siyā na vattabbā – kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā”ti. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā kileso ceva kilesasampayutto ca, siyā kilesasampayutto ceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbo – “kileso ceva kilesasampayutto cā”tipi, “kilesasampayutto ceva no ca kileso”tipi. Rūpakkhandho kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesiko. Cattāro khandhā siyā kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā[P 0.0069], siyā [V 0.0076] kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā, siyā na vattabbā – “kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā”tipi, “kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā”tipi.

The aggregate of form is not to be stated as 'both a defilement and associated with defilement', nor as 'associated with defilement but not a defilement'. The three aggregates are not to be stated as 'both defilements and associated with defilements'; in some cases, they are 'associated with defilements but not defilements'; in some cases, they are not to be stated as 'associated with defilements but not defilements'. The aggregate of formations may be 'both a defilement and associated with defilement', or 'associated with defilement but not a defilement'; or in some cases, it is not to be stated as 'both a defilement and associated with defilement', nor as 'associated with defilement but not a defilement'. The aggregate of form is dissociated from defilements and subject to defilement. The four aggregates may be 'dissociated from defilements and subject to defilement', or 'dissociated from defilements and not subject to defilement'; or in some cases, they are not to be stated as 'dissociated from defilements and subject to defilement', nor as 'dissociated from defilements and not subject to defilement'.

Rūpakkhandho na dassanena pahātabbo. Cattāro khandhā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā na dassanena pahātabbā. Rūpakkhandho na bhāvanāya pahātabbo[M 0.0068]. Cattāro khandhā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Rūpakkhandho na dassanena pahātabbahetuko. Cattāro khandhā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Rūpakkhandho na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Cattāro khandhā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Rūpakkhandho avitakko. Cattāro khandhā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Rūpakkhandho avicāro. Cattāro [T 0.0084] khandhā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Rūpakkhandho appītiko, cattāro khandhā siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Rūpakkhandho na pītisahagato. Cattāro khandhā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Dve khandhā na sukhasahagatā. Tayo khandhā siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Dve khandhā na upekkhāsahagatā. Tayo khandhā siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā.

The aggregate of form is not to be abandoned by vision. The four mental aggregates may be abandoned by vision, or may not be abandoned by vision. The aggregate of form is not to be abandoned by development. The four mental aggregates may be abandoned by development, or may not be abandoned by development. The aggregate of form does not have a cause to be abandoned by vision. The four mental aggregates may have a cause to be abandoned by vision, or may not have a cause to be abandoned by vision. The aggregate of form does not have a cause to be abandoned by development. The four mental aggregates may have a cause to be abandoned by development, or may not have a cause to be abandoned by development. The aggregate of form is without applied thought. The four mental aggregates may be with applied thought, or without applied thought. The aggregate of form is without sustained thought. The four mental aggregates may be with sustained thought, or without sustained thought. The aggregate of form is without rapture. The four mental aggregates may be with rapture, or without rapture. The aggregate of form is not associated with rapture. The four mental aggregates may be associated with rapture, or not associated with rapture. Two aggregates are not associated with happiness. Three aggregates may be associated with happiness, or not associated with happiness. Two aggregates are not associated with equanimity. Three aggregates may be associated with equanimity, or not associated with equanimity.

Rūpakkhandho kāmāvacaro. Cattāro khandhā siyā kāmāvacarā, siyā na kāmāvacarā. Rūpakkhandho na rūpāvacaro. Cattāro khandhā siyā rūpāvacarā, siyā na rūpāvacarā. Rūpakkhandho na arūpāvacaro. Cattāro khandhā siyā arūpāvacarā, siyā na arūpāvacarā. Rūpakkhandho pariyāpanno. Cattāro khandhā siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā. Rūpakkhandho aniyyāniko. Cattāro khandhā siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Rūpakkhandho aniyato. Cattāro khandhā siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Rūpakkhandho sauttaro. Cattāro khandhā siyā sauttarā, siyā anuttarā. Rūpakkhandho araṇo. Cattāro khandhā siyā saraṇā, siyā araṇāti.

The aggregate of form belongs to the sense-sphere. The four mental aggregates may belong to the sense-sphere or may not belong to the sense-sphere. The aggregate of form does not belong to the form-sphere. The four mental aggregates may belong to the form-sphere or may not belong to the form-sphere. The aggregate of form does not belong to the formless-sphere. The four mental aggregates may belong to the formless-sphere or may not belong to the formless-sphere. The aggregate of form is included. The four mental aggregates may be included or may not be included. The aggregate of form does not lead to deliverance. The four mental aggregates may lead to deliverance or may not lead to deliverance. The aggregate of form is not fixed. The four mental aggregates may be fixed or not fixed. The aggregate of form has a superior. The four mental aggregates may have a superior or may be unsurpassed. The aggregate of form is without conflict. The four mental aggregates may be with conflict or without conflict.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Interrogation.

Khandhavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Aggregates is concluded.

2. Āyatanavibhaṅgo

2. Analysis of the Sense Bases

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. Sutta Exposition

154. Dvādasāyatanāni [T 0.0085][M 0.0069][P 0.0070][V 0.0077] – cakkhāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ.

154. There are twelve sense bases: the eye base, form base, ear base, sound base, nose base, odor base, tongue base, taste base, body base, tangible object base, mind base, and mental-object base.

Cakkhuṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā vipariṇāmadhammaṃ. Rūpā aniccā dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā. Sotaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā vipariṇāmadhammaṃ. Saddā aniccā dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā. Ghānaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā vipariṇāmadhammaṃ. Gandhā aniccā dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā. Jivhā aniccā dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā. Rasā aniccā dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā. Kāyo anicco dukkho anattā vipariṇāmadhammo. Phoṭṭhabbā aniccā dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā. Mano anicco dukkho anattā vipariṇāmadhammo. Dhammā aniccā dukkhā anattā vipariṇāmadhammā.

The eye is impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. Forms are impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. The ear is impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. Sounds are impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. The nose is impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. Odors are impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. The tongue is impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. Tastes are impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. The body is impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. Tangible objects are impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. The mind is impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change. Mental objects are impermanent, suffering, not-self, and of a nature to change.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Sutta Exposition is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. Abhidhamma Exposition

155. Dvādasāyatanāni [V 0.0078] – cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ.

155. There are twelve sense bases: the eye base, ear base, nose base, tongue base, body base, mind base, form base, sound base, odor base, taste base, tangible object base, and mental-object base.

156. Tattha katamaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cakkhu cakkhuṃ (sī. syā. ka.) dha. sa. 596-599 catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena cakkhunā [P 0.0071] anidassanena sappaṭighena rūpaṃ sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ passi vā passati vā passissati vā passe vā, cakkhumpetaṃ cakkhāyatanampetaṃ cakkhudhātupesā cakkhundriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ nettampetaṃ nayanampetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati “cakkhāyatanaṃ”[T 0.0086].

156. Herein, what is the eye base? That eye which is a sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included in one's individual existence, invisible and impinging; that invisible and impinging eye by which one has seen, sees, will see, or may see a visible and impinging form. This is also the eye, this is also the eye base, this is also the eye element, this is also the eye faculty, this is also the world, this is also the door, this is also the ocean, this is also pure, this is also the field, this is also the ground, this is also the guide, this is also the leader, this is also the near shore, this is also the empty village. This is called the 'eye base'.

157. Tattha [M 0.0070] katamaṃ sotāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ sotaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena sotena anidassanena sappaṭighena saddaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ suṇi vā suṇāti vā suṇissati vā suṇe vā, sotampetaṃ sotāyatanampetaṃ sotadhātupesā sotindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati “sotāyatanaṃ”.

157. Herein, what is the ear base? That ear which is a sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included in one's individual existence, invisible and impinging; that invisible and impinging ear by which one has heard, hears, will hear, or may hear an invisible and impinging sound. This is also the ear, this is also the ear base, this is also the ear element, this is also the ear faculty, this is also the world, this is also the door, this is also the ocean, this is also pure, this is also the field, this is also the ground, this is also the near shore, this is also the empty village. This is called the 'ear base'.

158. Tattha katamaṃ ghānāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ ghānaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena ghānena anidassanena sappaṭighena gandhaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ ghāyi vā ghāyati vā ghāyissati vā ghāye vā, ghānampetaṃ ghānāyatanampetaṃ ghānadhātupesā ghānindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati “ghānāyatanaṃ”.

158. Herein, what is the nose base? That nose which is a sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included in one's individual existence, invisible and impinging; that invisible and impinging nose by which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell an invisible and impinging odor. This is also the nose, this is also the nose base, this is also the nose element, this is also the nose faculty, this is also the world, this is also the door, this is also the ocean, this is also pure, this is also the field, this is also the ground, this is also the near shore, this is also the empty village. This is called the 'nose base'.

159. Tattha katamaṃ jivhāyatanaṃ?
