Yā jivhā catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yāya jivhāya anidassanāya sappaṭighāya rasaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ sāyi vā sāyati vā sāyissati vā sāye vā, jivhāpesā jivhāyatanampetaṃ [V 0.0079] jivhādhātupesā jīvhindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati “jivhāyatanaṃ”.

159. Herein, what is the tongue-base? That tongue which is a sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included in one's individual existence, invisible and impinging; that invisible and impinging tongue by which one has savored, savors, will savor, or may savor an invisible and impinging flavor. This is also the tongue, this is also the tongue-base, this is also the tongue-element, this is also the tongue-faculty, this is also the world, this is also the door, this is also the ocean, this is also the pure and bright, this is also the field, this is also the ground, this is also the near shore, this is also the empty village. This is called the 'tongue-base'.

160. Tattha katamaṃ kāyāyatanaṃ? Yo kāyo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho, yena kāyena anidassanena sappaṭighena phoṭṭhabbaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ phusi vā phusati vā phusissati vā phuse vā, kāyopeso kāyāyatanampetaṃ kāyadhātupesā kāyindriyampetaṃ lokopeso dvārāpesā samuddopeso paṇḍarampetaṃ khettampetaṃ vatthumpetaṃ orimaṃ tīrampetaṃ suñño gāmopeso. Idaṃ vuccati “kāyāyatanaṃ”.

160. Herein, what is the body-base? That body which is a sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included in one's individual existence, invisible and impinging; that invisible and impinging body by which one has touched, touches, will touch, or may touch an invisible and impinging tangible object. This is also the body, this is also the body-base, this is also the body-element, this is also the body-faculty, this is also the world, this is also the door, this is also the ocean, this is also the pure and bright, this is also the field, this is also the ground, this is also the near shore, this is also the empty village. This is called the 'body-base'.

161. Tattha [M 0.0071] katamaṃ manāyatanaṃ? Ekavidhena manāyatanaṃ – phassasampayuttaṃ.

161. Herein, what is the mind-base? In one way, the mind-base is that which is associated with contact.

Duvidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi sahetukaṃ, atthi ahetukaṃ.

In two ways, the mind-base is: there is that with root-conditions, and there is that without root-conditions.

Tividhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ.

In three ways, the mind-base is: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, and there is the indeterminate.

Catubbidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi kāmāvacaraṃ, atthi rūpāvacaraṃ, atthi arūpāvacaraṃ, atthi apariyāpannaṃ.

In four ways, the mind-base is: there is that of the sense-sphere, there is that of the fine-material sphere, there is that of the immaterial sphere, and there is that which is unincluded.

Pañcavidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi sukhindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi dukkhindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi somanassindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi domanassindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi upekkhindriyasampayuttaṃ.

In five ways, the mind-base is: there is that associated with the pleasure faculty, that associated with the pain faculty, that associated with the joy faculty, that associated with the displeasure faculty, and that associated with the equanimity faculty.

Chabbidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ chabbidhena manāyatanaṃ.

In six ways, the mind-base is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. Thus, in six ways, is the mind-base.

Sattavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Evaṃ sattavidhena manāyatanaṃ.

In seven ways, the mind-base is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind-element, and the mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in seven ways, is the mind-base.

Aṭṭhavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ [V 0.0080] atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena manāyatanaṃ.

In eight ways, the mind-base is: there is eye-consciousness, there is ear-consciousness, there is nose-consciousness, there is tongue-consciousness, there is body-consciousness accompanied by pleasure, there is body-consciousness accompanied by pain, there is the mind-element, and there is the mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in eight ways, is the mind-base.

Navavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. Evaṃ navavidhena manāyatanaṃ.

In nine ways, the mind-base is: there is eye-consciousness, there is ear-consciousness, there is nose-consciousness, there is tongue-consciousness, there is body-consciousness, there is the mind-element, there is the wholesome mind-consciousness-element, there is the unwholesome mind-consciousness-element, and there is the indeterminate mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in nine ways, is the mind-base.

Dasavidhena manāyatanaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. Evaṃ dasavidhena manāyatanaṃ.

In ten ways, the mind-base is: there is eye-consciousness, there is ear-consciousness, there is nose-consciousness, there is tongue-consciousness, there is body-consciousness accompanied by pleasure, there is body-consciousness accompanied by pain, there is the mind-element, there is the wholesome mind-consciousness-element, there is the unwholesome mind-consciousness-element, and there is the indeterminate mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in ten ways, is the mind-base.

Ekavidhena manāyatanaṃ – phassasampayuttaṃ.

In one way, the mind-base is that which is associated with contact.

Duvidhena manāyatanaṃ – atthi sahetukaṃ, atthi ahetukaṃ.

In two ways, the mind-base is: there is that with root-conditions, and there is that without root-conditions.

Tividhena [M 0.0072] manāyatanaṃ – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ…pe…. Evaṃ bahuvidhena manāyatanaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “manāyatanaṃ”.

In three ways, the mind-base is: there is that associated with pleasant feeling, there is that associated with painful feeling, and there is that associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling... and so on... Thus, the mind-base is manifold. This is called the 'mind-base'.

162. Tattha [P 0.0072] katamaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya vaṇṇanibhā sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ nīlaṃ pītakaṃ lohitakaṃ pītaṃ lohitaṃ (sī.) odātaṃ kāḷakaṃ mañjiṭṭhakaṃ mañjeṭṭhakaṃ (sī. syā.) hari harivaṇṇaṃ ambaṅkuravaṇṇaṃ dīghaṃ rassaṃ aṇuṃ thūlaṃ vaṭṭaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ caturassaṃ chaḷaṃsaṃ aṭṭhaṃsaṃ soḷasaṃsaṃ ninnaṃ thalaṃ chāyā ātapo āloko andhakāro abbhā mahikā dhūmo rajo candamaṇḍalassa vaṇṇanibhā sūriyamaṇḍalassa suriyamaṇḍalassa (sī. syā. kaṃ.) vaṇṇanibhā tārakarūpānaṃ vaṇṇanibhā ādāsamaṇḍalassa vaṇṇanibhā maṇisaṅkhamuttaveḷuriyassa vaṇṇanibhā jātarūparajatassa vaṇṇanibhā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya vaṇṇanibhā sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ, yaṃ rūpaṃ sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ cakkhunā anidassanena sappaṭighena passi vā passati vā passissati vā passe vā, rūpampetaṃ rūpāyatanampetaṃ rūpadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati “rūpāyatanaṃ”.

162. Therein, what is the form-base? Whatever form is derived from the four great primary elements, is an appearance of color, is visible and impinging—such as blue, yellow, red, white, black, crimson, tawny, green, the color of a mango shoot, long, short, minute, large, round, spherical, square, hexagonal, octagonal, sixteen-sided, low, high, shade, sunlight, light, darkness, cloud, mist, smoke, dust; the appearance of color of the moon's disk, the appearance of color of the sun's disk, the appearance of color of the forms of stars, the appearance of color of a mirror's disk, the appearance of color of gems, conches, pearls, and beryl, the appearance of color of gold and silver; or whatever other form there is that is derived from the four great primary elements, is an appearance of color, is visible and impinging; that form which is visible and impinging, which one has seen, is seeing, will see, or might see with the eye, which is invisible and impinging—this is form, this is the form-base, this is the form-element. This is called the 'form-base'.

163. Tattha [V 0.0081] katamaṃ saddāyatanaṃ? Yo saddo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho bherisaddo mudiṅgasaddo mutiṅgasaddho (sī.) saṅkhasaddo paṇavasaddo gītasaddo vāditasaddo sammasaddo pāṇisaddo sattānaṃ nigghosasaddo dhātūnaṃ sannighātasaddo vātasaddo udakasaddo manussasaddo amanussasaddo, yo vā panaññopi atthi saddo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho, yaṃ saddaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ sotena anidassanena sappaṭighena suṇi vā suṇāti vā suṇissati vā suṇe vā, saddopeso saddāyatanampetaṃ saddadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati “saddāyatanaṃ”.

163. Therein, what is the sound-base? Whatever sound is derived from the four great primary elements, is invisible and impinging—such as the sound of a large drum, the sound of a mudiṅga drum, the sound of a conch, the sound of a paṇava drum, the sound of singing, the sound of musical instruments, the sound of cymbals, the sound of clapping hands, the shouting of beings, the sound of the striking of elements, the sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans; or whatever other sound there is that is derived from the four great primary elements, is invisible and impinging; that sound which is invisible and impinging, which one has heard, is hearing, will hear, or might hear with the ear, which is invisible and impinging—this is sound, this is the sound-base, this is the sound-element. This is called the 'sound-base'.

164. Tattha katamaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ? Yo gandho catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho mūlagandho sāragandho tacagandho pattagandho pupphagandho phalagandho āmagandho vissagandho sugandho duggandho, yo vā panaññopi atthi gandho catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho[M 0.0073], yaṃ gandhaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ ghānena anidassanena sappaṭighena ghāyi vā ghāyati vā ghāyissati vā ghāye vā, gandhopeso gandhāyatanampetaṃ gandhadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati “gandhāyatanaṃ”.

164. Therein, what is the odor-base? Whatever odor is derived from the four great primary elements, is invisible and impinging—such as the odor of a root, the odor of heartwood, the odor of bark, the odor of a leaf, the odor of a flower, the odor of a fruit, the odor of rawness, a rank odor, a pleasant odor, an unpleasant odor; or whatever other odor there is that is derived from the four great primary elements, is invisible and impinging; that odor which is invisible and impinging, which one has smelled, is smelling, will smell, or might smell with the nose, which is invisible and impinging—this is odor, this is the odor-base, this is the odor-element. This is called the 'odor-base'.

165. Tattha katamaṃ rasāyatanaṃ? Yo raso catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho mūlaraso khandharaso tacaraso pattaraso puppharaso phalaraso ambilaṃ madhuraṃ tittakaṃ kaṭukaṃ loṇikaṃ lapilakaṃ (sī.), lampikaṃ (ka. sī.) khārikaṃ lambikaṃ kasāvo sādu asādu, yo vā panaññopi atthi raso catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho, yaṃ rasaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ jivhāya anidassanāya sappaṭighāya sāyi vā sāyati vā sāyissati vā sāye vā, rasopeso rasāyatanampetaṃ rasadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati “rasāyatanaṃ”.

165. Therein, what is the taste-base? Whatever taste is derived from the four great primary elements, is invisible and impinging—such as the taste of a root, the taste of a trunk, the taste of bark, the taste of a leaf, the taste of a flower, the taste of a fruit, sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, acrid, astringent, agreeable, disagreeable; or whatever other taste there is that is derived from the four great primary elements, is invisible and impinging; that taste which is invisible and impinging, which one has tasted, is tasting, will taste, or might taste with the tongue, which is invisible and impinging—this is taste, this is the taste-base, this is the taste-element. This is called the 'taste-base'.

166. Tattha katamaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ? Pathavīdhātu tejodhātu vāyodhātu kakkhaḷaṃ mudukaṃ saṇhaṃ pharusaṃ sukhasamphassaṃ dukkhasamphassaṃ garukaṃ lahukaṃ, yaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ anidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ kāyena anidassanena sappaṭighena phusi vā phusati vā phusissati vā phuse vā, phoṭṭhabbopeso phoṭṭhabbāyatanampetaṃ phoṭṭhabbadhātupesā. Idaṃ vuccati “phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ”.

166. Therein, what is the tangible-base? The earth element, the fire element, and the air element; the hard, the soft, the smooth, the rough, pleasant contact, painful contact, the heavy, and the light; whatever tangible object is invisible and impinging, which one has touched, is touching, will touch, or might touch with the body, which is invisible and impinging—this is the tangible, this is the tangible-base, this is the tangible-element. This is called the 'tangible-base'.

167. Tattha [V 0.0082] katamaṃ dhammāyatanaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu.

167. Therein, what is the mind-object-base? The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and whatever form is invisible and non-impinging and included in the mind-object-base, and the unconditioned element.

Tattha katamo vedanākkhandho? Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati “vedanākkhandho”.

Therein, what is the aggregate of feeling? In one way, the aggregate of feeling is that which is associated with contact. In two ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is that with a root, and there is that without a root. In three ways, the aggregate of feeling is: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, and there is the indeterminate... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of feeling is... and so on... Thus, in many ways, the aggregate of feeling is. This is called the 'aggregate of feeling'.

Tattha katamo saññākkhandho? Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi [M 0.0074] abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati “saññākkhandho”.

Therein, what is the aggregate of perception? In one way, the aggregate of perception is that which is associated with contact. In two ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is that with a root, and there is that without a root. In three ways, the aggregate of perception is: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, and there is the indeterminate... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of perception is... and so on... Thus, in many ways, the aggregate of perception is. This is called the 'aggregate of perception'.

Tattha katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi na hetu. Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārakkhandho”.

Therein, what is the aggregate of formations? In one way, the aggregate of formations is that which is associated with consciousness. In two ways, the aggregate of formations is: there is that which is a root, and there is that which is not a root. In three ways, the aggregate of formations is: there is the wholesome, there is the unwholesome, and there is the indeterminate... and so on... Thus, in ten ways, the aggregate of formations is... and so on... Thus, in many ways, the aggregate of formations is. This is called the 'aggregate of formations'.

Tattha katamaṃ [T 0.0087] rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ purisindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. Idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ “anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ”.

Therein, what is the form that is invisible, non-impinging, and included in the mind-object-base? The faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity... and so on... edible food. This is called the 'form that is invisible, non-impinging, and included in the mind-object-base'.

Tattha katamā asaṅkhatā dhātu? Rāgakkhayo[P 0.0073], dosakkhayo, mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati “asaṅkhatā dhātu”.

Therein, what is the unconditioned element? The extinction of lust, the extinction of hatred, and the extinction of delusion. This is called the 'unconditioned element'.

Idaṃ vuccati dhammāyatanaṃ.

This is called the 'mind-object-base'.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition is concluded.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Questioning Section

168. Dvādasāyatanāni [V 0.0083] – cakkhāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ.

168. The twelve bases are: the eye-base, the form-base, the ear-base, the sound-base, the nose-base, the odor-base, the tongue-base, the taste-base, the body-base, the tangible-base, the mind-base, and the mind-object-base.

169. Dvādasannaṃ āyatanānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

169. Of the twelve bases, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, how many are indeterminate... and so on... how many are with defilements, how many are without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

170. Dasāyatanā abyākatā. Dvāyatanā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya [M 0.0075] sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi. Dasāyatanā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Dvāyatanā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

170. The ten bases are indeterminate. Two bases may be wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate. The ten bases cannot be said to be "associated with pleasant feeling," "associated with painful feeling," or "associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling." The mind-base may be associated with pleasant feeling, painful feeling, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The mind-object-base may be associated with pleasant feeling, painful feeling, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; or it may be that which cannot be said to be "associated with pleasant feeling," "associated with painful feeling," or "associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling." The ten bases are neither result nor productive of result. Two bases may be result, productive of result, or neither result nor productive of result.

Pañcāyatanā upādinnupādāniyā. Saddāyatanaṃ [T 0.0088] anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Cattāro āyatanā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādāniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Dasāyatanā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Dvāyatanā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Dasāyatanā avitakkaavicārā. Manāyatanaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ[V 0.0084], siyā na vattabbaṃ – “savitakkasavicāra”ntipi, “avitakkavicāramatta”ntipi, “avitakkaavicāra”ntipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “pītisahagatā”tipi, “sukhasahagatā”tipi, “upekkhāsahagatā”tipi. Dvāyatanā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā [P 0.0074] sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – “pītisahagatā”tipi, “sukhasahagatā”tipi, “upekkhāsahagatā”tipi.

Five bases are taken up [by kamma] and are objects of clinging. The sound-base is not taken up [by kamma] but is an object of clinging. Four bases may be taken up [by kamma] and are objects of clinging, or may be not taken up [by kamma] but are objects of clinging. Two bases may be taken up [by kamma] and are objects of clinging, may be not taken up [by kamma] but are objects of clinging, or may be not taken up [by kamma] and are not objects of clinging. The ten bases are undefiled, but are objects for defilements. Two bases may be defiled and are objects for defilements, may be undefiled but are objects for defilements, or may be undefiled and are not objects for defilements. The ten bases are without initial thought and sustained thought. The mind-base may be with initial thought and sustained thought, may be without initial thought but with sustained thought only, or may be without initial thought and sustained thought. The mental-phenomena base may be with initial thought and sustained thought, may be without initial thought but with sustained thought only, may be without initial thought and sustained thought; or, at times, it cannot be said that it is "with initial thought and sustained thought," "without initial thought but with sustained thought only," or "without initial thought and sustained thought." The ten bases cannot be said to be "accompanied by joy," "accompanied by pleasure," or "accompanied by equanimity." Two bases may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by pleasure, may be accompanied by equanimity; or, at times, it cannot be said that they are "accompanied by joy," "accompanied by pleasure," or "accompanied by equanimity."

Dasāyatanā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dvāyatanā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dasāyatanā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dvāyatanā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dasāyatanā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dvāyatanā siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dasāyatanā [T 0.0089] nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dvāyatanā siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā[M 0.0076], siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dasāyatanā parittā. Dvāyatanā siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “parittārammaṇā”tipi, “mahaggatārammaṇā”tipi, “appamāṇārammaṇā”tipi. Dasāyatanā majjhimā. Dvāyatanā siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Dasāyatanā aniyatā. Dvāyatanā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā.

The ten bases are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Two bases may be abandoned by vision, may be abandoned by cultivation, or are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. The ten bases do not have roots to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation. Two bases may have roots to be abandoned by vision, may have roots to be abandoned by cultivation, or do not have roots to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation. The ten bases are conducive neither to accumulation nor to de-accumulation. Two bases may be conducive to accumulation, may be conducive to de-accumulation, or may be conducive neither to accumulation nor to de-accumulation. The ten bases are neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training. Two bases may be of a trainee, may be of one beyond training, or may be neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training. The ten bases are limited. Two bases may be limited, may be exalted, or may be immeasurable. The ten bases are without an object. Two bases may have a limited object, may have an exalted object, may have an immeasurable object; or, at times, it cannot be said that they "have a limited object," "have an exalted object," or "have an immeasurable object." The ten bases are medium. Two bases may be inferior, may be medium, or may be superior. The ten bases are unfixed. Two bases may be fixed on wrongness, may be fixed on rightness, or may be unfixed.

Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – “maggārammaṇā”tipi, “maggahetukā”tipi, “maggādhipatino”tipi. Pañcāyatanā siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino, na vattabbā – “anuppannā”ti. Saddāyatanaṃ siyā uppannaṃ, siyā anuppannaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “uppādī”ti. Pañcāyatanā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā uppannaṃ, siyā anuppannaṃ, siyā uppādi, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “uppanna”ntipi, “anuppanna”ntipi, “uppādī”tipi. Ekādasāyatanā siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā atītaṃ, siyā anāgataṃ, siyā paccuppannaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “atīta”ntipi, “anāgata”ntipi, “paccuppanna”ntipi. Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā [V 0.0085] atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā[T 0.0090], siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā [P 0.0075] – “atītārammaṇā”tipi, “anāgatārammaṇā”tipi, “paccuppannārammaṇā”tipi; siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “ajjhattārammaṇā”tipi, “bahiddhārammaṇā”tipi, “ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā”tipi. Rūpāyatanaṃ sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ. Navāyatanā anidassanasappaṭighā. Dvāyatanā anidassanaappaṭighā.

The ten bases are without an object. Two bases may have the path as object, may have the path as a root, may have the path as a dominant factor; or, at times, it cannot be said that they "have the path as object," "have the path as a root," or "have the path as a dominant factor." Five bases may be arisen, may be bound to arise, but it cannot be said that they are "unarisen." The sound-base may be arisen, may be unarisen, but it cannot be said that it is "bound to arise." Five bases may be arisen, may be unarisen, or may be bound to arise. The mental-phenomena base may be arisen, may be unarisen, may be bound to arise; or, at times, it cannot be said that it is "arisen," "unarisen," or "bound to arise." Eleven bases may be past, may be future, or may be present. The mental-phenomena base may be past, may be future, may be present; or, at times, it cannot be said that it is "past," "future," or "present." The ten bases are without an object. Two bases may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object; or, at times, it cannot be said that they "have a past object," "have a future object," or "have a present object." Some bases may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. The ten bases are without an object. Two bases may have an internal object, may have an external object, may have both an internal and an external object; or, at times, it cannot be said that they "have an internal object," "have an external object," or "have both an internal and an external object." The form-base is with manifestation and with resistance. The nine bases are without manifestation but with resistance. The two bases are without manifestation and without resistance.

2. Dukaṃ

2. Exposition of Dyads

171. Ekādasāyatanā na hetū. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā hetu, siyā na hetu. Dasāyatanā ahetukā. Dvāyatanā siyā sahetukā, siyā ahetukā. Dasāyatanā hetuvippayuttā. Dvāyatanā siyā hetusampayuttā, siyā hetuvippayuttā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “hetū [M 0.0077] ceva sahetukā cā”tipi, “sahetukā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “hetu ceva sahetukañcā”ti, siyā sahetukañceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “sahetukañceva na ca hetū”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā hetu ceva sahetukañca, siyā sahetukañceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “hetu ceva sahetukañcā”tipi, “sahetukañceva na ca hetū”tipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”tipi, “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “hetu ceva hetusampayuttañcā”ti, siyā hetusampayuttañceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “hetusampayuttañceva na [T 0.0091] ca hetū”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā hetu ceva hetusampayuttañca, siyā hetusampayuttañceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “hetu ceva hetusampayuttañcā”tipi, “hetusampayuttañceva na ca hetū”tipi. Dasāyatanā na hetūahetukā. Manāyatanaṃ siyā na hetusahetukaṃ, siyā na hetuahetukaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā na hetusahetukaṃ, siyā na hetuahetukaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “na hetusahetuka”ntipi, “na hetuahetuka”ntipi.

171. Eleven bases are not roots. The dhamma-base may be a root, or may not be a root. Ten bases are rootless. The two bases may be with roots, or may be rootless. Ten bases are dissociated from roots. The two bases may be associated with roots, or may be dissociated from roots. Ten bases are not to be stated as 'both roots and with roots' or 'with roots but not roots.' The mind-base is not to be stated as 'both a root and with a root'; it may be 'with a root but not a root'; sometimes it is not to be stated as 'with a root but not a root.' The dhamma-base may be 'both a root and with a root,' or it may be 'with a root but not a root,' or it is not to be stated as 'both a root and with a root' or 'with a root but not a root.' Ten bases are not to be stated as 'both roots and associated with roots' or 'associated with roots but not roots.' The mind-base is not to be stated as 'both a root and associated with a root'; it may be 'associated with a root but not a root'; sometimes it is not to be stated as 'associated with a root but not a root.' The dhamma-base may be 'both a root and associated with a root,' or it may be 'associated with a root but not a root,' or it is not to be stated as 'both a root and associated with a root' or 'associated with a root but not a root.' Ten bases are not roots and are rootless. The mind-base may be 'not a root but with a root,' or it may be 'not a root and rootless.' The dhamma-base may be 'not a root but with a root,' or it may be 'not a root and rootless,' or it is not to be stated as 'not a root but with a root' or 'not a root and rootless.'

Ekādasāyatanā sappaccayā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sappaccayaṃ, siyā appaccayaṃ. Ekādasāyatanā saṅkhatā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā saṅkhataṃ, siyā asaṅkhataṃ. Rūpāyatanaṃ sanidassanaṃ. Ekādasāyatanā [V 0.0086] anidassanā. Dasāyatanā [P 0.0076] sappaṭighā. Dvāyatanā appaṭighā. Dasāyatanā rūpā. Manāyatanaṃ arūpaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā rūpaṃ, siyā arūpaṃ. Dasāyatanā lokiyā. Dvāyatanā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā; kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

Eleven bases are with conditions. The dhamma-base may be with conditions, or may be without conditions. Eleven bases are conditioned. The dhamma-base may be conditioned, or may be unconditioned. The form-base is with manifestation. Eleven bases are without manifestation. Ten bases are with resistance. The two bases are without resistance. Ten bases are material form. The mind-base is immaterial. The dhamma-base may be material form, or may be immaterial. Ten bases are worldly. The two bases may be worldly, or may be supramundane; knowable by some, not knowable by some.

Ekādasāyatanā no āsavā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā āsavo, siyā no āsavo. Dasāyatanā sāsavā. Dvāyatanā siyā sāsavā, siyā anāsavā. Dasāyatanā āsavavippayuttā. Dvāyatanā siyā āsavasampayuttā, siyā āsavavippayuttā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”ti, “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā”. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “āsavo ceva sāsavañcā”ti, siyā sāsavañceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “sāsavañceva no ca āsavo”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā āsavo ceva sāsavañca, siyā sāsavañceva no ca [M 0.0078] āsavo, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “āsavo ceva sāsavañcā”tipi, “sāsavañceva no ca āsavo”tipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttañcā”ti, siyā āsavasampayuttañceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “āsavasampayuttañceva no ca āsavo”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā [T 0.0092] āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttañca, siyā āsavasampayuttañceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttañcā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttañceva no ca āsavo”tipi. Dasāyatanā āsavavippayuttasāsavā. Dvāyatanā siyā āsavavippayuttasāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā, siyā na vattabbā – “āsavavippayuttasāsavā”tipi, “āsavavippayuttaanāsavā”tipi.

Eleven bases are not taints. The dhamma-base may be a taint, or may not be a taint. Ten bases are objects for the taints. The two bases may be objects for the taints, or may not be objects for the taints. Ten bases are dissociated from taints. The two bases may be associated with taints, or may be dissociated from taints. Ten bases are not to be stated as 'both taints and objects for the taints' or 'objects for the taints but not taints.' The mind-base is not to be stated as 'both a taint and an object for the taints'; it may be 'an object for the taints but not a taint'; sometimes it is not to be stated as 'an object for the taints but not a taint.' The dhamma-base may be 'both a taint and an object for the taints,' or it may be 'an object for the taints but not a taint,' or it is not to be stated as 'both a taint and an object for the taints' or 'an object for the taints but not a taint.' Ten bases are not to be stated as 'both taints and associated with taints' or 'associated with taints but not taints.' The mind-base is not to be stated as 'both a taint and associated with a taint'; it may be 'associated with a taint but not a taint'; sometimes it is not to be stated as 'associated with a taint but not a taint.' The dhamma-base may be 'both a taint and associated with a taint,' or it may be 'associated with a taint but not a taint,' or it is not to be stated as 'both a taint and associated with a taint' or 'associated with a taint but not a taint.' Ten bases are dissociated from the taints but are objects for the taints. The two bases may be 'dissociated from the taints but are objects for the taints,' or they may be 'dissociated from the taints and not objects for the taints,' or they are not to be stated as 'dissociated from the taints but are objects for the taints' or 'dissociated from the taints and not objects for the taints.'

Ekādasāyatanā no saṃyojanā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā saṃyojanaṃ, siyā no saṃyojanaṃ. Dasāyatanā saṃyojaniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā saṃyojaniyā, siyā asaṃyojaniyā. Dasāyatanā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Dvāyatanā siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cā”ti, saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyañcā”ti, siyā saṃyojaniyañceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojaniyañceva no ca saṃyojana”nti. Dhammāyatanaṃ [T 0.0093] siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyañca, siyā saṃyojaniyañceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanañceva [V 0.0087] saṃyojaniya”ntipi, “saṃyojaniyañceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ [P 0.0077] na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttañcā”ti, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttañceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanasampayuttañceva no ca saṃyojana”nti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttañca, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttañceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttañcā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayuttañceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi. Dasāyatanā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā[M 0.0079]. Dvāyatanā siyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā”tipi, “saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā”tipi.

Eleven bases are not fetters. The dhamma-base may be a fetter or may not be a fetter. Ten bases are subject to fetters. Two bases may be subject to fetters or may not be subject to fetters. Ten bases are dissociated from fetters. Two bases may be associated with fetters or may be dissociated from fetters. Ten bases are not to be described as 'both fetters and subject to fetters'; they are subject to fetters but not fetters. The mind-base is not to be described as 'both a fetter and subject to fetters'; it may be subject to fetters but not a fetter, or it may not be described as 'subject to fetters but not a fetter.' The dhamma-base may be both a fetter and subject to fetters, or it may be subject to fetters but not a fetter, or it may not be described as 'both a fetter and subject to fetters' nor as 'subject to fetters but not a fetter.' Ten bases are not to be described as 'both fetters and associated with fetters' nor as 'associated with fetters but not fetters.' The mind-base is not to be described as 'both a fetter and associated with fetters'; it may be associated with fetters but not a fetter, or it may not be described as 'associated with fetters but not a fetter.' The dhamma-base may be both a fetter and associated with fetters, or it may be associated with fetters but not a fetter, or it may not be described as 'both a fetter and associated with fetters' nor as 'associated with fetters but not a fetter.' Ten bases are dissociated from fetters and subject to fetters. Two bases may be dissociated from fetters and subject to fetters, or they may be dissociated from fetters and not subject to fetters, or they may not be described as 'dissociated from fetters and subject to fetters' nor as 'dissociated from fetters and not subject to fetters.'

Ekādasāyatanā no ganthā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā gantho, siyā no gantho. Dasāyatanā ganthaniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā ganthaniyā, siyā aganthaniyā. Dasāyatanā ganthavippayuttā. Dvāyatanā siyā ganthasampayuttā, siyā ganthavippayuttā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthaniyā cā”ti, ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ [T 0.0094] – “gantho ceva ganthaniyañcā”ti, siyā ganthaniyañceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “ganthaniyañceva no ca gantho”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā gantho ceva ganthaniyañca, siyā ganthaniyañceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “gantho ceva ganthaniyañcā”tipi, “ganthaniyañceva no ca gantho”tipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā cā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “gantho ceva ganthasampayuttañcā”ti, siyā ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā gantho ceva ganthasampayuttañca, siyā ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “gantho ceva ganthasampayuttañcā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho”tipi. Dasāyatanā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā, siyā ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā”tipi, “ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā”tipi.

Eleven bases are not ties. The dhamma-base may be a tie or may not be a tie. Ten bases are subject to ties. Two bases may be subject to ties or may not be subject to ties. Ten bases are dissociated from ties. Two bases may be associated with ties or may be dissociated from ties. Ten bases are not to be described as 'both ties and subject to ties'; they are subject to ties but not ties. The mind-base is not to be described as 'both a tie and subject to ties'; it may be subject to ties but not a tie, or it may not be described as 'subject to ties but not a tie.' The dhamma-base may be both a tie and subject to ties, or it may be subject to ties but not a tie, or it may not be described as 'both a tie and subject to ties' nor as 'subject to ties but not a tie.' Ten bases are not to be described as 'both ties and associated with ties' nor as 'associated with ties but not ties.' The mind-base is not to be described as 'both a tie and associated with ties'; it may be associated with ties but not a tie, or it may not be described as 'associated with ties but not a tie.' The dhamma-base may be both a tie and associated with ties, or it may be associated with ties but not a tie, or it may not be described as 'both a tie and associated with ties' nor as 'associated with ties but not a tie.' Ten bases are dissociated from ties and subject to ties. Two bases may be dissociated from ties and subject to ties, or they may be dissociated from ties and not subject to ties, or they may not be described as 'dissociated from ties and subject to ties' nor as 'dissociated from ties and not subject to ties.'

Ekādasāyatanā no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā [V 0.0088] nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā no nīvaraṇaṃ. Dasāyatanā nīvaraṇiyā. Dvāyatanā siyā [P 0.0078] nīvaraṇiyā, siyā anīvaraṇiyā. Dasāyatanā nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Dvāyatanā siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”ti, nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyañcā”ti[T 0.0095], siyā nīvaraṇiyañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇiyañceva no ca nīvaraṇa”nti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyañca, siyā nīvaraṇiyañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā [M 0.0080] na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyañcā”tipi, “nīvaraṇiyañceva no ca nīvaraṇa”ntipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañcā”ti, siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇa”nti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañca, siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañcā”tipi, “nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇa”ntipi. Dasāyatanā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā. Dvāyatanā siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā”tipi, “nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā”tipi.

Eleven bases are not floods… nor yokes… nor hindrances. The phenomena base may be a hindrance, or may not be a hindrance. Ten bases are objects of the hindrances. Two bases may be objects of the hindrances, or may not be objects of the hindrances. Ten bases are dissociated from hindrances. Two bases may be associated with hindrances, or may be dissociated from hindrances. Ten bases are not to be stated as ‘both hindrances and objects of the hindrances’; rather, they are objects of the hindrances and not hindrances. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a hindrance and an object of the hindrances’; it may be an object of the hindrances and not a hindrance, or it is not to be stated as ‘an object of the hindrances and not a hindrance.’ The phenomena base may be both a hindrance and an object of the hindrances; it may be an object of the hindrances and not a hindrance; or it is not to be stated as ‘both a hindrance and an object of the hindrances’ or as ‘an object of the hindrances and not a hindrance.’ Ten bases are not to be stated as ‘both hindrances and associated with hindrances’ or as ‘associated with hindrances and not hindrances.’ The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a hindrance and associated with hindrances’; it may be associated with hindrances and not a hindrance, or it is not to be stated as ‘associated with hindrances and not a hindrance.’ The phenomena base may be both a hindrance and associated with hindrances; it may be associated with hindrances and not a hindrance; or it is not to be stated as ‘both a hindrance and associated with hindrances’ or as ‘associated with hindrances and not a hindrance.’ Ten bases are dissociated from hindrances and are objects of the hindrances. Two bases may be dissociated from hindrances and be objects of the hindrances; may be dissociated from hindrances and not be objects of the hindrances; or in some cases are not to be stated as ‘dissociated from hindrances and objects of the hindrances’ or as ‘dissociated from hindrances and not objects of the hindrances.’

Ekādasāyatanā no parāmāsā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā parāmāso, siyā no parāmāso. Dasāyatanā parāmaṭṭhā. Dvāyatanā siyā parāmaṭṭhā, siyā aparāmaṭṭhā. Dasāyatanā parāmāsavippayuttā. Manāyatanaṃ siyā parāmāsasampayuttaṃ, siyā parāmāsavippayuttaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā parāmāsasampayuttaṃ, siyā parāmāsavippayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “parāmāsasampayutta”ntipi, “parāmāsavippayutta”ntipi. Dasāyatanā na [T 0.0096] vattabbā – “parāmāsā ceva parāmaṭṭhā cā”ti, “parāmaṭṭhā ceva no ca parāmāsā”. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭhañcā”ti, siyā parāmaṭṭhañceva no ca parāmāso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “parāmaṭṭhañceva no ca parāmāso”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭhañca, siyā parāmaṭṭhañceva no ca parāmāso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭhañcā”tipi, “parāmaṭṭhañceva no ca parāmāso”tipi. Dasāyatanā parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā. Dvāyatanā siyā parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā[V 0.0089], siyā parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā, siyā na vattabbā – “parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā”tipi[P 0.0079], “parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā”tipi.

Eleven bases are not graspings. The phenomena base may be a grasping, or may not be a grasping. Ten bases are objects of grasping. Two bases may be objects of grasping, or may not be objects of grasping. Ten bases are dissociated from graspings. The mind base may be associated with graspings, or may be dissociated from graspings. The phenomena base may be associated with graspings, may be dissociated from graspings, or in some cases is not to be stated as ‘associated with graspings’ or as ‘dissociated from graspings.’ Ten bases are not to be stated as ‘both graspings and objects of grasping’; rather, they are objects of grasping and not graspings. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a grasping and an object of grasping’; it may be an object of grasping and not a grasping, or it is not to be stated as ‘an object of grasping and not a grasping.’ The phenomena base may be both a grasping and an object of grasping; it may be an object of grasping and not a grasping; or it is not to be stated as ‘both a grasping and an object of grasping’ or as ‘an object of grasping and not a grasping.’ Ten bases are dissociated from graspings and are objects of grasping. Two bases may be dissociated from graspings and be objects of grasping; may be dissociated from graspings and not be objects of grasping; or in some cases are not to be stated as ‘dissociated from graspings and objects of grasping’ or as ‘dissociated from graspings and not objects of grasping.’

Dasāyatanā anārammaṇā. Manāyatanaṃ sārammaṇaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. Manāyatanaṃ cittaṃ. Ekādasāyatanā no cittā. Ekādasāyatanā acetasikā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cetasikaṃ, siyā acetasikaṃ. Dasāyatanā cittavippayuttā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cittasampayuttaṃ, siyā cittavippayuttaṃ. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “cittena sampayutta”ntipi[M 0.0081], “cittena vippayutta”ntipi. Dasāyatanā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ, siyā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhaṃ. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “cittena saṃsaṭṭha”ntipi, “cittena visaṃsaṭṭha”ntipi. Chāyatanā no cittasamuṭṭhānā. Chāyatanā siyā cittasamuṭṭhānā, siyā no cittasamuṭṭhānā. Ekādasāyatanā no cittasahabhuno. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cittasahabhū[T 0.0097], siyā no cittasahabhū. Ekādasāyatanā no cittānuparivattino. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cittānuparivatti, siyā no cittānuparivatti. Ekādasāyatanā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānaṃ, siyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Ekādasāyatanā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhū, siyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhū. Ekādasāyatanā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivatti, siyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivatti.

Ten bases are without an object. The mind base has an object. The phenomena base may have an object, or may be without an object. The mind base is consciousness. Eleven bases are not consciousness. Eleven bases are not mental factors. The phenomena base may be a mental factor, or may not be a mental factor. Ten bases are dissociated from consciousness. The phenomena base may be associated with consciousness, or may be dissociated from consciousness. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘associated with consciousness’ or as ‘dissociated from consciousness.’ Ten bases are unmingled with consciousness. The phenomena base may be mingled with consciousness, or may be unmingled with consciousness. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘mingled with consciousness’ or as ‘unmingled with consciousness.’ Six bases do not originate from consciousness. Six bases may originate from consciousness, or may not originate from consciousness. Eleven bases are not co-arisen with consciousness. The phenomena base may be co-arisen with consciousness, or may not be co-arisen with consciousness. Eleven bases are not consequent upon consciousness. The phenomena base may be consequent upon consciousness, or may not be consequent upon consciousness. Eleven bases are not mingled with and originated from consciousness. The phenomena base may be mingled with and originated from consciousness, or may not be mingled with and originated from consciousness. Eleven bases are not mingled with, originated from, and co-arisen with consciousness. The phenomena base may be mingled with, originated from, and co-arisen with consciousness, or may not be mingled with, originated from, and co-arisen with consciousness. Eleven bases are not mingled with, originated from, and consequent upon consciousness. The phenomena base may be mingled with, originated from, and consequent upon consciousness, or may not be mingled with, originated from, and consequent upon consciousness.

Chāyatanā ajjhattikā. Chāyatanā bāhirā. Navāyatanā upādā. Dvāyatanā no upādā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā upādā, siyā no upādā. Pañcāyatanā upādinnā. Saddāyatanaṃ anupādinnaṃ. Chāyatanā siyā upādinnā, siyā anupādinnā. Ekādasāyatanā no upādānā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā upādānaṃ, siyā no upādānaṃ. Dasāyatanā upādāniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā upādāniyā, siyā anupādāniyā. Dasāyatanā upādānavippayuttā. Dvāyatanā siyā upādānasampayuttā, siyā upādānavippayuttā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādāniyā cā”ti, upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “upādānañceva upādāniyañcā”ti, siyā upādāniyañceva no ca upādānaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “upādāniyañceva no ca upādāna”nti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā upādānañceva [T 0.0098] upādāniyañca, siyā upādāniyañceva no ca upādānaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “upādānañceva [P 0.0080][V 0.0090] upādāniyañcā”tipi, “upādāniyañceva no ca upādāna”ntipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā cā”tipi, “upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “upādāniyañceva upādānasampayuttañcā”ti, siyā upādānasampayuttañceva no ca upādānaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “upādānasampayuttañceva no ca upādāna”nti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañca, siyā upādānasampayuttañceva no ca upādānaṃ[M 0.0082], siyā na vattabbaṃ – “upādānañceva upādānasampayuttañcā”tipi, “upādānasampayuttañceva no ca upādāna”ntipi. Dasāyatanā upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā upādānasampayuttaupādāniyā, siyā upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā”tipi, “upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā”tipi.

Six bases are internal. Six bases are external. Nine bases are derived. Two bases are not derived. The mind-object base is sometimes derived, sometimes not derived. Five bases are grasped by kamma. The sound base is not grasped by kamma. Six bases are sometimes grasped by kamma, sometimes not grasped by kamma. Eleven bases are not clingings. The mind-object base is sometimes a clinging, sometimes not a clinging. Ten bases are objects of clinging. Two bases are sometimes objects of clinging, sometimes not objects of clinging. Ten bases are dissociated from clinging. Two bases are sometimes associated with clinging, sometimes dissociated from clinging. Ten bases are not to be stated as ‘both clingings and objects of clinging’; they are objects of clinging but not clingings. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a clinging and an object of clinging’; it is sometimes an object of clinging but not a clinging; sometimes it is not to be stated as ‘an object of clinging but not a clinging’. The mind-object base is sometimes both a clinging and an object of clinging, sometimes an object of clinging but not a clinging; and sometimes it is not to be stated as either ‘both a clinging and an object of clinging’ or ‘an object of clinging but not a clinging’. Ten bases are not to be stated as either ‘both clingings and associated with clinging’ or ‘associated with clinging but not clingings’. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a clinging and associated with clinging’; it is sometimes associated with clinging but not a clinging; sometimes it is not to be stated as ‘associated with clinging but not a clinging’. The mind-object base is sometimes both a clinging and associated with clinging, sometimes associated with clinging but not a clinging; and sometimes it is not to be stated as either ‘both a clinging and associated with clinging’ or ‘associated with clinging but not a clinging’. Ten bases are dissociated from clinging and are objects of clinging. Two bases are sometimes dissociated from clinging and are objects of clinging, sometimes dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging; and sometimes they are not to be stated as either ‘dissociated from clinging and are objects of clinging’ or ‘dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging’.

Ekādasāyatanā no kilesā. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā kileso, siyā no kileso. Dasāyatanā saṃkilesikā. Dvāyatanā siyā saṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkilesikā. Dasāyatanā asaṃkiliṭṭhā. Dvāyatanā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhā. Dasāyatanā kilesavippayuttā. Dvāyatanā siyā kilesasampayuttā, siyā kilesavippayuttā. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā cā”ti, “saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā”. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “kileso ceva saṃkilesikañcā”ti, siyā saṃkilesikañceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃkilesikañceva no ca kileso”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā kileso ceva saṃkilesikañca, siyā saṃkilesikañceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “kileso ceva saṃkilesikañcā”tipi, “saṃkilesikañceva no ca kileso”tipi. Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā cā”tipi, “saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca [T 0.0099] kilesā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭhañcā”ti, siyā saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kileso”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭhañca, siyā saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭhañcā”tipi, “saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kileso”tipi.

Eleven bases are not defilements. The mind-object base is sometimes a defilement, sometimes not a defilement. Ten bases are objects of defilement. Two bases are sometimes objects of defilement, sometimes not objects of defilement. Ten bases are undefiled. Two bases are sometimes defiled, sometimes undefiled. Ten bases are dissociated from defilements. Two bases are sometimes associated with defilements, sometimes dissociated from defilements. Ten bases are not to be stated as ‘both defilements and objects of defilement’; they are objects of defilement but not defilements. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a defilement and an object of defilement’; it is sometimes an object of defilement but not a defilement; sometimes it is not to be stated as ‘an object of defilement but not a defilement’. The mind-object base is sometimes both a defilement and an object of defilement, sometimes an object of defilement but not a defilement; and sometimes it is not to be stated as either ‘both a defilement and an object of defilement’ or ‘an object of defilement but not a defilement’. Ten bases are not to be stated as either ‘both defilements and defiled’ or ‘defiled but not defilements’. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a defilement and defiled’; it is sometimes defiled but not a defilement; sometimes it is not to be stated as ‘defiled but not a defilement’. The mind-object base is sometimes both a defilement and defiled, sometimes defiled but not a defilement; and sometimes it is not to be stated as either ‘both a defilement and defiled’ or ‘defiled but not a defilement’.

Dasāyatanā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva kilesasampayuttā cā”tipi, “kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca na kilesā”tipi. Manāyatanaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañcā”ti[V 0.0091], siyā kilesasampayuttañceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “kilesasampayuttañceva no ca kileso”ti. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañca, siyā kilesasampayuttañceva no ca kileso, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañcā”tipi, “kilesasampayuttañceva no [M 0.0083] ca kileso”tipi. Dasāyatanā kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā. Dvāyatanā siyā kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā, siyā kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā[P 0.0081], siyā na vattabbā – “kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā”tipi, “kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā”tipi[T 0.0100].

Ten bases are not to be stated as either ‘both defilements and associated with defilements’ or ‘associated with defilements but not defilements’. The mind base is not to be stated as ‘both a defilement and associated with defilements’; it is sometimes associated with defilements but not a defilement; sometimes it is not to be stated as ‘associated with defilements but not a defilement’. The mind-object base is sometimes both a defilement and associated with defilements, sometimes associated with defilements but not a defilement; and sometimes it is not to be stated as either ‘both a defilement and associated with defilements’ or ‘associated with defilements but not a defilement’. Ten bases are dissociated from defilements but are objects of defilement. Two bases are sometimes dissociated from defilements but are objects of defilement, sometimes dissociated from defilements and are not objects of defilement; and sometimes they are not to be stated as either ‘dissociated from defilements and are objects of defilement’ or ‘dissociated from defilements and are not objects of defilement’.

Dasāyatanā na dassanena pahātabbā. Dvāyatanā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā na dassanena pahātabbā. Dasāyatanā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dvāyatanā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dasāyatanā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Dvāyatanā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Dasāyatanā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dvāyatanā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dasāyatanā avitakkā. Dvāyatanā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Dasāyatanā avicārā. Dvāyatanā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Dasāyatanā appītikā. Dvāyatanā siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Dasāyatanā na pītisahagatā. Dvāyatanā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Dasāyatanā na sukhasahagatā. Dvāyatanā siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Dasāyatanā na upekkhāsahagatā. Dvāyatanā siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā.

The ten sense bases are not to be abandoned by vision. The two sense bases may be abandoned by vision, or may not be abandoned by vision. The ten sense bases are not to be abandoned by cultivation. The two sense bases may be abandoned by cultivation, or may not be abandoned by cultivation. The ten sense bases do not have causes to be abandoned by vision. The two sense bases may have causes to be abandoned by vision, or may not have causes to be abandoned by vision. The ten sense bases do not have causes to be abandoned by cultivation. The two sense bases may have causes to be abandoned by cultivation, or may not have causes to be abandoned by cultivation. The ten sense bases are without initial application. The two sense bases may be with initial application, or may be without initial application. The ten sense bases are without sustained application. The two sense bases may be with sustained application, or may be without sustained application. The ten sense bases are without rapture. The two sense bases may be with rapture, or may be without rapture. The ten sense bases are not accompanied by rapture. The two sense bases may be accompanied by rapture, or may not be accompanied by rapture. The ten sense bases are not accompanied by pleasure. The two sense bases may be accompanied by pleasure, or may not be accompanied by pleasure. The ten sense bases are not accompanied by equanimity. The two sense bases may be accompanied by equanimity, or may not be accompanied by equanimity.

Dasāyatanā kāmāvacarā. Dvāyatanā siyā kāmāvacarā, siyā na kāmāvacarā. Dasāyatanā na rūpāvacarā. Dvāyatanā siyā rūpāvacarā, siyā na rūpāvacarā. Dasāyatanā na arūpāvacarā. Dvāyatanā siyā arūpāvacarā, siyā na arūpāvacarā. Dasāyatanā pariyāpannā. Dvāyatanā siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā. Dasāyatanā aniyyānikā. Dvāyatanā siyā niyyānikā[T 0.0101], siyā aniyyānikā. Dasāyatanā aniyatā. Dvāyatanā siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Dasāyatanā sauttarā. Dvāyatanā siyā sauttarā, siyā anuttarā. Dasāyatanā araṇā. Dvāyatanā siyā saraṇā, siyā araṇāti.

The ten sense bases are of the sense-sphere. The two sense bases may be of the sense-sphere, or may not be of the sense-sphere. The ten sense bases are not of the form-sphere. The two sense bases may be of the form-sphere, or may not be of the form-sphere. The ten sense bases are not of the formless-sphere. The two sense bases may be of the formless-sphere, or may not be of the formless-sphere. The ten sense bases are included in the round of existence. The two sense bases may be included in the round of existence, or may not be included in the round of existence. The ten sense bases do not lead to liberation. The two sense bases may lead to liberation, or may not lead to liberation. The ten sense bases are unfixed. The two sense bases may be fixed, or may be unfixed. The ten sense bases are surpassable. The two sense bases may be surpassable, or may be unsurpassable. The ten sense bases are without defilements. The two sense bases may be with defilements, or may be without defilements.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Section of Questions.

Āyatanavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Sense Bases is concluded.

3. Dhātuvibhaṅgo

3. The Analysis of the Elements

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. Analysis according to the Discourses

172. Cha [M 0.0084][P 0.0082][V 0.0092] dhātuyo – pathavīdhātu paṭhavīdhātu (sī. syā.) evamuparipi, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, ākāsadhātu, viññāṇadhātu.

172. There are six elements: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the air element, the space element, and the consciousness element.

173. Tattha katamā pathavīdhātu? Pathavīdhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru nahāru (sī.) aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhimiñjā (sī.) vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu’.

173. Herein, what is the earth element? The earth element is twofold: there is the internal and there is the external. Herein, what is the internal earth element? Whatever is internal, pertaining to oneself, hard, rough, hardness, the state of being hard, internal, and appropriated—namely: head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone-marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, large intestine, small intestine, undigested food, feces, or whatever else there is that is internal, pertaining to oneself, hard, rough, hardness, the state of being hard, internal, and appropriated—this is called the 'internal earth element'.

Tattha katamā bāhirā pathavīdhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ [T 0.0102] – ayo lohaṃ tipu sīsaṃ sajjhaṃ sajjhu (syā.) muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavāḷaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ lohitaṅko lohitaṅgo (syā. ka.), lohitako (?) masāragallaṃ tiṇaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sakkharā kaṭhalaṃ kathalaṃ (ka.) bhūmi pāsāṇo pabbato, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā pathavīdhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati “pathavīdhātu”.

Herein, what is the external earth element? Whatever is external, hard, rough, hardness, the state of being hard, external, and unappropriated—namely: iron, copper, tin, lead, silver, pearl, gem, beryl, conch, stone, coral, silver, gold, ruby, cat's-eye gem, grass, wood, gravel, potsherd, earth, rock, mountain, or whatever else there is that is external, hard, rough, hardness, the state of being hard, external, and unappropriated—this is called the 'external earth element'. Both the internal earth element and the external earth element, having been gathered and summarized together as one, are called the 'earth element'.

174. Tattha [P 0.0083][V 0.0093] katamā āpodhātu? Āpodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā āpodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ sneho snehagataṃ (syā.) bandhanattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ [M 0.0085] paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā āpodhātu’.

174. Herein, what is the water element? The water element is twofold: there is the internal and there is the external. Herein, what is the internal water element? Whatever is internal, pertaining to oneself, that is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the binding quality of matter, internal, and appropriated—namely: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, mucus, synovial fluid, urine, or whatever else there is that is internal, pertaining to oneself, water, watery, moisture, moistness, the binding quality of matter, internal, and appropriated—this is called the 'internal water element'.

Tattha katamā bāhirā āpodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – mūlaraso khandharaso tacaraso pattaraso puppharaso phalaraso khīraṃ dadhi sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ bhummāni vā udakāni antalikkhāni vā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ [T 0.0103] – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā āpodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā āpodhātu yā ca bāhirā āpodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati “āpodhātu”.

Herein, what is the external water element? Whatever is external, that is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the binding quality of matter, external, and unappropriated—namely: root-sap, trunk-sap, bark-sap, leaf-sap, flower-sap, fruit-sap, milk, curd, ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, molasses, and waters from the earth or from the sky, or whatever else there is that is external, water, watery, moisture, moistness, the binding quality of matter, external, and unappropriated—this is called the 'external water element'. Both the internal water element and the external water element, having been gathered and summarized together as one, are called the 'water element'.

175. Tattha katamā tejodhātu? Tejodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā tejodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – yena ca santappati yena ca jīrīyati yena ca pariḍayhati yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā tejodhātu’.

175. Among these, what is the fire element? The fire element is twofold: there is the internal fire element and there is the external fire element. Among these, what is the internal fire element? That which is internal, personal, is heat, the state of heat; vapor, the state of vapor; coarse vapor, the state of coarse vapor; which is internal and arisen from kamma—that is to say: that by which one is heated, that by which one ages, that by which one is burned up, and that by which what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted reaches proper digestion; or whatever else there is that is internal, personal, is heat, the state of heat; vapor, the state of vapor; coarse vapor, the state of coarse vapor; which is internal and arisen from kamma—this is called the ‘internal fire element’.

Tattha katamā bāhirā tejodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṭṭhaggi palālaggi sakalikaggi (sabbattha) tiṇaggi gomayaggi thusaggi saṅkāraggi indaggi aggisantāpo sūriyasantāpo kaṭṭhasannicayasantāpo tiṇasannicayasantāpo dhaññasannicayasantāpo bhaṇḍasannicayasantāpo, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā tejodhātu’. Yā [P 0.0084][V 0.0094] ca ajjhattikā tejodhātu yā ca bāhirā tejodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati “tejodhātu”.

Among these, what is the external fire element? That which is external is heat, the state of heat; vapor, the state of vapor; coarse vapor, the state of coarse vapor; which is external and not arisen from kamma—that is to say: wood-fire, straw-fire, grass-fire, cow-dung-fire, chaff-fire, rubbish-fire, lightning-fire, the heat of fire, the heat of the sun, the heat from a pile of wood, the heat from a pile of grass, the heat from a pile of grain, the heat from a pile of goods; or whatever else there is that is external is heat, the state of heat; vapor, the state of vapor; coarse vapor, the state of coarse vapor; which is external and not arisen from kamma—this is called the ‘external fire element’. That which is the internal fire element and that which is the external fire element—having combined and condensed them together, this is called the ‘fire element’.

176. Tattha [T 0.0104][M 0.0086] katamā vāyodhātu? Vāyodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – uddhaṅgamā vātā adhogamā vātā kucchisayā vātā koṭṭhāsayā koṭṭhasayā (sī. syā.) vātā aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā satthakavātā khurakavātā uppalakavātā assāso passāso iti vā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā vāyodhātu’.

176. Among these, what is the air element? The air element is twofold: there is the internal air element and there is the external air element. Among these, what is the internal air element? That which is internal, personal, is air, the state of air, the firmness of matter, which is internal and arisen from kamma—that is to say: upward-going winds, downward-going winds, winds in the belly, winds abiding in the bowels, winds that course through the major and minor limbs, knife-like winds, razor-like winds, winds that pull out the heart, in-breath, and out-breath; or whatever else there is that is internal, personal, is air, the state of air, the firmness of matter, which is internal and arisen from kamma—this is called the ‘internal air element’.

Tattha katamā bāhirā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – puratthimā vātā pacchimā vātā uttarā vātā dakkhiṇā vātā sarajā vātā arajā vātā sītā vātā uṇhā vātā parittā vātā adhimattā vātā kāḷavātā verambhavātā pakkhavātā supaṇṇavātā tālavaṇṭavātā vidhūpanavātā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā vāyodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā vāyodhātu yā ca bāhirā vāyodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati “vāyodhātu”.

Among these, what is the external air element? That which is external is air, the state of air, the firmness of matter, which is external and not arisen from kamma—that is to say: eastern winds, western winds, northern winds, southern winds, dusty winds, dustless winds, cold winds, hot winds, gentle winds, strong winds, winds from black clouds, winds that arise from on high, winds from wings, winds from Garuḷas, winds from palm-leaf fans, winds from bamboo-strip fans; or whatever else there is that is external is air, the state of air, the firmness of matter, which is external and not arisen from kamma—this is called the ‘external air element’. That which is the internal air element and that which is the external air element—having combined and condensed them together, this is called the ‘air element’.

177. Tattha katamā ākāsadhātu? Ākāsadhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ [T 0.0105] ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ maṃsalohitehi ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṇṇacchiddaṃ nāsacchiddaṃ mukhadvāraṃ, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ ajjhoharati, yattha ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ santiṭṭhati, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ adhobhāgaṃ nikkhamati, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ maṃsalohitehi ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu’.

177. Among these, what is the space element? The space element is twofold: there is the internal space element and there is the external space element. Among these, what is the internal space element? That which is internal, personal, is space, the state of space; the untouchable, the state of being untouchable; an aperture, the state of being an aperture; untouched by flesh and blood, which is internal and arisen from kamma—that is to say: the orifice of the ear, the orifice of the nose, the door of the mouth; and that by which what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is swallowed; and where what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is established; and that by which what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted exits from the lower part; or whatever else there is that is internal, personal, is space, the state of space; the untouchable, the state of being untouchable; an aperture, the state of being an aperture; untouched by flesh and blood, which is internal and arisen from kamma—this is called the ‘internal space element’.

Tattha katamā bāhirā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro [V 0.0095] vivaragataṃ [P 0.0085] asamphuṭṭhaṃ catūhi mahābhūtehi [M 0.0087] bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā ākāsadhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu yā ca bāhirā ākāsadhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati “ākāsadhātu”.

Among these, what is the external space element? That which is external is space, the state of space; the untouchable, the state of being untouchable; an aperture, the state of being an aperture; untouched by the four great elements, which is external and not arisen from kamma—this is called the ‘external space element’. That which is the internal space element and that which is the external space element—having combined and condensed them together, this is called the ‘space element’.

178. Tattha katamā viññāṇadhātu? Cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “viññāṇadhātu”.

178. Among these, what is the consciousness element? Eye-consciousness element, ear-consciousness element, nose-consciousness element, tongue-consciousness element, body-consciousness element, and mind-consciousness element—this is called the ‘consciousness element’.

Imā cha dhātuyo.

These are the six elements.

179. Aparāpi cha dhātuyo – sukhadhātu, dukkhadhātu, somanassadhātu, domanassadhātu, upekkhādhātu, avijjādhātu.

179. There are another six elements: the pleasure element, the pain element, the gladness element, the displeasure element, the equanimity element, and the ignorance element.

180. Tattha katamā sukhadhātu? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ sātaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “sukhadhātu”.

180. Among these, what is the pleasure element? Whatever bodily agreeableness, bodily pleasure; an agreeable, pleasant feeling born of bodily contact; an agreeable, pleasant feeling born of bodily contact—this is called the ‘pleasure element’.

Tattha katamā [T 0.0106] dukkhadhātu? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhadhātu”.

Among these, what is the pain element? Whatever bodily disagreeableness, bodily pain; a disagreeable, painful feeling born of bodily contact; a disagreeable, painful feeling born of bodily contact—this is called the ‘pain element’.

Tattha katamā somanassadhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “somanassadhātu”.

Among these, what is the gladness element? Whatever mental agreeableness, mental pleasure; an agreeable, pleasant feeling born of mind-contact; an agreeable, pleasant feeling born of mind-contact—this is called the ‘gladness element’.

Tattha katamā domanassadhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “domanassadhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of displeasure? Whatever is mental unpleasantness, mental pain; whatever unpleasant, painful feeling is born of mind-contact; whatever unpleasant, painful feeling is born of mind-contact—this is called the 'element of displeasure'.

Tattha katamā upekkhādhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ [V 0.0096] vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhādhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of equanimity? Whatever is mental and neither pleasant nor unpleasant; whatever feeling born of mind-contact is neither painful nor pleasant—this is called the 'element of equanimity'.

Tattha katamā avijjādhātu? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṅgāhaṇā apariyogāhaṇā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ [M 0.0088] moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ [P 0.0086] avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjādhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of ignorance? Whatever is unknowing, unseeing, non-realization, non-awakening, lack of full understanding, non-penetration, non-grasping, non-encompassing, non-scrutiny, non-reflection, non-direct-realization, poor wisdom, foolishness, lack of clear comprehension, delusion, great delusion, utter delusion, ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the bolt of ignorance, and delusion which is an unwholesome root—this is called the 'element of ignorance'.

Imā cha dhātuyo.

These are the six elements.

181. Aparāpi cha dhātuyo – kāmadhātu, byāpādadhātu, vihiṃsādhātu, nekkhammadhātu, abyāpādadhātu, avihiṃsādhātu.
