181. There are also another six elements: the element of sensual desire, the element of ill will, the element of harmfulness, the element of renunciation, the element of non-ill will, and the element of harmlessness.

182. Tattha katamā kāmadhātu? Kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati kāmadhātu. Heṭṭhato avīcinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā uparito paranimmitavasavattī deve anto karitvā yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā khandhadhātuāyatanā rūpā rūpaṃ (syā.) vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati [T 0.0107] “kāmadhātu”.

182. Among these, what is the element of sensual desire? Whatever thought, initial thought, intention, application, sustained application, placing of the mind, and wrong intention is connected with sensual desire—this is called the 'element of sensual desire'. Furthermore, having made the Avīci hell the lower limit and having included the Paranimmitavasavattī devas as the upper limit, whatever aggregates, elements, and sense bases that frequent and are included within this interval—namely form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness—this is also called the 'element of sensual desire'.

Tattha katamā byāpādadhātu? Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “byāpādadhātu”. Dasasu vā āghātavatthūsu cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “byāpādadhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of ill will? Whatever thought, initial thought, and so on, up to wrong intention, is connected with ill will—this is called the 'element of ill will'. Or, in regard to the ten grounds for resentment: animosity, repugnance, resistance, opposition, anger, great anger, extreme anger, hate, great hate, extreme hate, corruption of mind, mental corruption, anger, the act of being angry, the state of being angry, hate, the act of hating, the state of hating, corruption, the act of corrupting, opposition, counter-opposition, harshness, incivility, and discontent of mind—this is called the 'element of ill will'.

Tattha katamā vihiṃsādhātu? Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… micchāsaṅkappo [V 0.0097] – ayaṃ vuccati “vihiṃsādhātu”. Idhekacco pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā rajjuyā vā aññataraññatarena satte viheṭheti, yā evarūpā heṭhanā viheṭhanā hiṃsanā vihiṃsanā rosanā virosanā parūpaghāto – ayaṃ vuccati “vihiṃsādhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of harmfulness? Whatever thought, initial thought, and so on, up to wrong intention, is connected with harmfulness—this is called the 'element of harmfulness'. Here, a certain person harms beings with their hand, with a clod of earth, with a stick, with a knife, with a rope, or with some other weapon. Whatever such harming, injuring, tormenting, harassing, oppressing, great oppressing, or killing of others—this is called the 'element of harmfulness'.

Tattha katamā nekkhammadhātu? Nekkhammapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “nekkhammadhātu”. Sabbepi kusalā dhammā “nekkhammadhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of renunciation? Whatever thought, initial thought, and so on, up to right intention, is connected with renunciation—this is called the 'element of renunciation'. All wholesome states are the 'element of renunciation'.

Tattha [M 0.0089] katamā abyāpādadhātu? Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “abyāpādadhātu”. Yā sattesu metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “abyāpādadhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of non-ill will? Whatever thought, initial thought, and so on, up to right intention, is connected with non-ill will—this is called the 'element of non-ill will'. Whatever loving-kindness towards beings, the practice of loving-kindness, the state of having loving-kindness, and the liberation of mind through loving-kindness there is—this is called the 'element of non-ill will'.

Tattha katamā avihiṃsādhātu? Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā [P 0.0087] cetaso abhiniropanā sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “avihiṃsādhātu”[T 0.0108]. Yā sattesu karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “avihiṃsādhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of harmlessness? Whatever thought, initial thought, intention, application, sustained application, the placing of the mind, which is right intention, is connected with harmlessness—this is called the 'element of harmlessness'. Whatever compassion towards beings, the practice of compassion, the state of having compassion, and the liberation of mind through compassion there is—this is called the 'element of harmlessness'.

Imā cha dhātuyo.

These are the six elements.

Iti imāni tīṇi chakkāni tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo honti.

Thus, these three sets of six, when gathered together and summarized, become the eighteen elements.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Analysis according to the Suttas.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Analysis.

183. Aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo – cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu, gandhadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu, rasadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu[V 0.0098], kāyadhātu, phoṭṭhabbadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu.

183. There are eighteen elements: the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element; the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element; the nose-element, the odour-element, the nose-consciousness-element; the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element; the body-element, the tangible-element, the body-consciousness-element; the mind-element, the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element.

184. Tattha katamā cakkhudhātu? Yaṃ cakkhu catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati “cakkhudhātu”.

184. Among these, what is the eye-element? Whatever eye is the sensitivity dependent on the four great primary elements... like a deserted village—this is called the 'eye-element'.

Tattha katamā rūpadhātu? Yaṃ rūpaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya vaṇṇanibhā…pe… rūpadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati “rūpadhātu”.

Among these, what is the element of form? Whatever form, dependent on the four great primary elements, is colour and appearance... this is called the 'form-element'.

Tattha katamā cakkhuviññāṇadhātu? Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjācakkhuviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “cakkhuviññāṇadhātu”.

Among these, what is the eye-consciousness-element? Dependent on the eye and on forms, there arises that which is mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding eye-consciousness-element—this is called the 'eye-consciousness-element'.

Tattha [M 0.0090] katamā sotadhātu? Yaṃ sotaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati “sotadhātu”[T 0.0109].

Among these, what is the ear-element? Whatever ear is the sensitivity dependent on the four great primary elements... like a deserted village—this is called the 'ear-element'.

Tattha katamā saddadhātu? Yo saddo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho…pe… saddadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati “saddadhātu”.

Among these, what is the sound-element? Whatever sound, dependent on the four great primary elements, is invisible and possessed of impingement... this is called the 'sound-element'.

Tattha katamā sotaviññāṇadhātu? Sotañca paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāsotaviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “sotaviññāṇadhātu”.

Among these, what is the ear-consciousness-element? Dependent on the ear and on sounds, there arises that which is mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding ear-consciousness-element—this is called the 'ear-consciousness-element'.

Tattha katamā ghānadhātu? Yaṃ [P 0.0088] ghānaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati “ghānadhātu”.

Among these, what is the nose-element? Whatever nose is the sensitivity dependent on the four great primary elements... like a deserted village—this is called the 'nose-element'.

Tattha katamā gandhadhātu? Yo gandho catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho…pe… gandhadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati “gandhadhātu”.

Among these, what is the odour-element? Whatever odour, dependent on the four great primary elements, is invisible and possessed of impingement... this is called the 'odour-element'.

Tattha [V 0.0099] katamā ghānaviññāṇadhātu? Ghānañca paṭicca gandhe ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāghānaviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “ghānaviññāṇadhātu”.

Among these, what is the nose-consciousness-element? Dependent on the nose and on odours, there arises that which is mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding nose-consciousness-element—this is called the 'nose-consciousness-element'.

Tattha katamā jivhādhātu? Yā jivhā catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati “jivhādhātu”.

Among these, what is the tongue-element? Whatever tongue is the sensitivity dependent on the four great primary elements... like a deserted village—this is called the 'tongue-element'.

Tattha katamā rasadhātu? Yo raso catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho…pe… rasadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati “rasadhātu”.

Among these, what is the taste-element? Whatever taste, dependent on the four great primary elements, is invisible and possessed of impingement... this is called the 'taste-element'.

Tattha katamā jivhāviññāṇadhātu? Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ [T 0.0110] viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjājivhāviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “jivhāviññāṇadhātu”.

Among these, what is the tongue-consciousness-element? Dependent on the tongue and on tastes, there arises that which is mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding tongue-consciousness-element—this is called the 'tongue-consciousness-element'.

Tattha katamā kāyadhātu? Yo kāyo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati “kāyadhātu”.

Among these, what is the body-element? Whatever body is the sensitivity dependent on the four great primary elements... like a deserted village—this is called the 'body-element'.

Tattha [M 0.0091] katamā phoṭṭhabbadhātu? Pathavīdhātu…pe… phoṭṭhabbadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati “phoṭṭhabbadhātu”.

Among these, what is the tangible-element? The earth-element... this is called the 'tangible-element'.

Tattha katamā kāyaviññāṇadhātu? Kāyañca paṭicca phoṭṭhabbe ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjākāyaviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “kāyaviññāṇadhātu”.

Among these, what is the body-consciousness-element? Dependent on the body and on tangibles, there arises that which is mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding body-consciousness-element—this is called the 'body-consciousness-element'.

Tattha katamā manodhātu? Cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanodhātu; sotaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ [V 0.0100] hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanodhātu [P 0.0089] sabbadhammesu vā pana paṭhamasamannāhāro uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanodhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “manodhātu”.

Among these, what is the mind-element? Immediately after the eye-consciousness-element has arisen and ceased, there arises mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding mind-element. Similarly, after the ear-consciousness-element... after the body-consciousness-element has arisen and ceased, there arises mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding mind-element. Or again, with respect to all phenomena, the initial advertence arises as mind, mind, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness-aggregate, the corresponding mind-element—this is called the 'mind-element'.

Tattha katamā dhammadhātu? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu.

Among these, what is the dhamma-element? The feeling-aggregate, the perception-aggregate, the formations-aggregate, and that matter which is invisible, non-impinging, and included in the mental-object-base, and the unconditioned element.

Tattha katamo vedanākkhandho? Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto[T 0.0111]. Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati “vedanākkhandho”.

Among these, what is the feeling-aggregate? In one way, the feeling-aggregate is that which is associated with contact. In two ways, there is the feeling-aggregate with root-causes, and there is the feeling-aggregate without root-causes. In three ways, there is the wholesome feeling-aggregate, there is the unwholesome feeling-aggregate, and there is the indeterminate feeling-aggregate... Thus, in ten ways is the feeling-aggregate... Thus, in many ways is the feeling-aggregate. This is called the 'feeling-aggregate'.

Tattha katamo saññākkhandho? Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati “saññākkhandho”.

Among these, what is the perception-aggregate? In one way, the perception-aggregate is that which is associated with contact. In two ways, there is the perception-aggregate with root-causes, and there is the perception-aggregate without root-causes. In three ways, there is the wholesome perception-aggregate, there is the unwholesome perception-aggregate, and there is the indeterminate perception-aggregate... Thus, in ten ways is the perception-aggregate... Thus, in many ways is the perception-aggregate. This is called the 'perception-aggregate'.

Tattha katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi ahetu. Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ [M 0.0092] dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārakkhandho”.

Among these, what is the formations-aggregate? In one way, the formations-aggregate is that which is associated with consciousness. In two ways, there is the formations-aggregate that is a root-cause, and there is the formations-aggregate that is not a root-cause. In three ways, there is the wholesome formations-aggregate, there is the unwholesome formations-aggregate, and there is the indeterminate formations-aggregate... Thus, in ten ways is the formations-aggregate... Thus, in many ways is the formations-aggregate. This is called the 'formations-aggregate'.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ “anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ”.

Among these, what is the matter that is invisible, non-impinging, and included in the mental-object-base? The femininity faculty... edible food. This matter is called 'invisible, non-impinging, and included in the mental-object-base'.

Tattha katamā asaṅkhatā dhātu? Rāgakkhayo, dosakkhayo, mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati “asaṅkhatā dhātu”. Ayaṃ vuccati “dhammadhātu”.

Among these, what is the unconditioned element? The destruction of lust, the destruction of aversion, and the destruction of delusion. This is called the 'unconditioned element'. This is called the 'dhamma-element'.

Tattha [V 0.0101] katamā manoviññāṇadhātu? Cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati manodhātu, manodhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā [P 0.0090] uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu; sotaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā [T 0.0112] …pe… jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati manodhātu, manodhātuyāpi uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “manoviññāṇadhātu”.

Among these, what is the mind-consciousness-element? Immediately after the eye-consciousness-element has arisen and ceased, the mind-element arises. Immediately after the mind-element has arisen and ceased, there arises whatever is consciousness, mind, intellect... and so on... the mind-consciousness-element born of that. Likewise, immediately after the ear-consciousness-element... and so on... the nose-consciousness-element... and so on... the tongue-consciousness-element... and so on... the body-consciousness-element has arisen and ceased, the mind-element arises. And immediately after the mind-element has also arisen and ceased, there arises whatever is consciousness, mind, intellect... and so on... the mind-consciousness-element born of that. Dependent on the mind and on mental objects, there arises whatever is consciousness, mind, intellect, heart, the pure, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness aggregate, the mind-consciousness-element born of that. This is called the 'mind-consciousness-element'.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition is concluded.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Questioning Section

Aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo – cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu, gandhadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu, rasadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyadhātu, phoṭṭhabbadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu.

Eighteen elements: the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element; the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element; the nose-element, the smell-element, the nose-consciousness-element; the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element; the body-element, the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element; the mind-element, the mental-object-element, and the mind-consciousness-element.

186. Aṭṭhārasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

186. Of the eighteen elements, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate… and so on… how many are with defilements, how many are without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

187. Soḷasa [M 0.0093] dhātuyo abyākatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi. Pañca dhātuyo [V 0.0102] adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Kāyaviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā [T 0.0113] sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Dhammadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā na vattabbā – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi.

187. Sixteen elements are indeterminate. Two elements are sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate. Regarding the ten elements, it should not be said that they are ‘associated with pleasant feeling,’ ‘associated with painful feeling,’ or ‘associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Five elements are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The body-consciousness-element is sometimes associated with pleasant feeling and sometimes associated with painful feeling. The mind-consciousness-element is sometimes associated with pleasant feeling, sometimes with painful feeling, and sometimes with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The mental-object-element is sometimes associated with pleasant feeling, sometimes with painful feeling, sometimes with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; and sometimes it should not be said that it is ‘associated with pleasant feeling,’ ‘associated with painful feeling,’ or ‘associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’

Dasa dhātuyo nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Pañca [P 0.0091] dhātuyo vipākā. Manodhātu siyā vipākā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Dve dhātuyo siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

Ten elements are neither results nor result-producing dhammas. Five elements are results. The mind-element is sometimes a result, and sometimes neither a result nor a result-producing dhamma. Two elements are sometimes results, sometimes result-producing dhammas, and sometimes neither results nor result-producing dhammas.

Dasa dhātuyo upādinnupādāniyā. Saddadhātu anupādinnupādāniyā. Pañca dhātuyo siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

Ten elements are grasped by kamma and are objects of clinging. The sound-element is not grasped by kamma but is an object of clinging. Five elements are sometimes grasped by kamma and are objects of clinging, and sometimes not grasped by kamma but are objects of clinging. Two elements are sometimes grasped by kamma and are objects of clinging; sometimes not grasped by kamma but are objects of clinging; and sometimes neither grasped by kamma nor are they objects of clinging.

Soḷasa dhātuyo asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Dve dhātuyo siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Pannarasa dhātuyo avitakkaavicārā. Manodhātu savitakkasavicārā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Dhammadhātu siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā, siyā na vattabbā – “savitakkasavicārā”tipi, “avitakkavicāramattā”tipi, “avitakkaavicārā”tipi. Dasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “pītisahagatā”tipi, “sukhasahagatā”tipi, “upekkhāsahagatā”tipi[T 0.0114]. Pañca dhātuyo upekkhāsahagatā. Kāyaviññāṇadhātu na pītisahagatā, siyā [M 0.0094] sukhasahagatā, na upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – “sukhasahagatā”ti. Dve dhātuyo siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – “pītisahagatā”tipi, “sukhasahagatā”tipi, “upekkhāsahagatā”tipi.

Sixteen elements are undefiled but are objects of defilement. Two elements are sometimes defiled and objects of defilement; sometimes undefiled but objects of defilement; and sometimes undefiled and not objects of defilement. Fifteen elements are without initial thought and sustained thought. The mind-element is with initial thought and sustained thought. The mind-consciousness-element is sometimes with initial thought and sustained thought; sometimes without initial thought but with sustained thought only; and sometimes without initial thought and without sustained thought. The mental-object-element is sometimes with initial thought and sustained thought; sometimes without initial thought but with sustained thought only; sometimes without initial thought and without sustained thought; and sometimes it should not be said that it is ‘with initial thought and sustained thought,’ ‘without initial thought but with sustained thought only,’ or ‘without initial thought and without sustained thought.’ Regarding the ten elements, it should not be said that they are ‘accompanied by joy,’ ‘accompanied by pleasure,’ or ‘accompanied by equanimity.’ Five elements are accompanied by equanimity. The body-consciousness-element is not accompanied by joy; is sometimes accompanied by pleasure; is not accompanied by equanimity; and sometimes it should not be said that it is ‘accompanied by pleasure.’ Two elements are sometimes accompanied by joy, sometimes accompanied by pleasure, sometimes accompanied by equanimity; and sometimes it should not be said that they are ‘accompanied by joy,’ ‘accompanied by pleasure,’ or ‘accompanied by equanimity.’

Soḷasa [V 0.0103] dhātuyo neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dve dhātuyo siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Soḷasa dhātuyo neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dve dhātuyo siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Soḷasa dhātuyo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dve dhātuyo siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Soḷasa dhātuyo nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dve dhātuyo siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā.

Sixteen elements are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Two elements are sometimes to be abandoned by vision, sometimes to be abandoned by cultivation, and sometimes to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Sixteen elements are not dhammas with a root to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation. Two elements are sometimes dhammas with a root to be abandoned by vision, sometimes dhammas with a root to be abandoned by cultivation, and sometimes not dhammas with a root to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation. Sixteen elements lead neither to accumulation nor to diminution. Two elements sometimes lead to accumulation, sometimes lead to diminution, and sometimes lead neither to accumulation nor to diminution. Sixteen elements are neither of trainees nor of non-trainees. Two elements are sometimes of trainees, sometimes of non-trainees, and sometimes neither of trainees nor of non-trainees.

Soḷasa dhātuyo parittā. Dve dhātuyo siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Dasa [P 0.0092] dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Cha dhātuyo parittārammaṇā. Dve dhātuyo siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “parittārammaṇā”tipi, “mahaggatārammaṇā”tipi, “appamāṇārammaṇā”tipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo majjhimā. Dve dhātuyo siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Soḷasa dhātuyo aniyatā. Dve [T 0.0115] dhātuyo siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā.

Sixteen elements are of the limited sphere. Two elements are sometimes of the limited sphere, sometimes of the sublime sphere, and sometimes immeasurable. Ten elements are without an object. Six elements take an object of the limited sphere. Two elements sometimes take an object of the limited sphere, sometimes take an object of the sublime sphere, sometimes take an immeasurable object, and sometimes should not be said to ‘take an object of the limited sphere,’ ‘take an object of the sublime sphere,’ or ‘take an immeasurable object.’ Sixteen elements are of medium quality. Two elements are sometimes of inferior quality, sometimes of medium quality, and sometimes of superior quality. Sixteen elements are unfixed. Two elements are sometimes fixed in wrongness, sometimes fixed in rightness, and sometimes unfixed.

Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Cha dhātuyo na vattabbā – “maggārammaṇā”tipi, “maggahetukā”tipi, “maggādhipatino”tipi. Dve dhātuyo siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – “maggārammaṇā”tipi, “maggahetukā”tipi, “maggādhipatino”tipi. Dasa dhātuyo siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino, siyā na vattabbā – “anuppannā”ti. Saddadhātu siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā na vattabbā – “uppādinī”ti. Cha dhātuyo siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Dhammadhātu siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādinī, siyā na vattabbā – “uppannā”tipi, “anuppannā”tipi, “uppādinī”tipi.

Ten elements are without an object. Six elements should not be said to ‘have the path as object,’ ‘have the path as cause,’ or ‘have the path as dominant condition.’ Two elements may have the path as object, may have the path as cause, may have the path as dominant condition, or should not be said to ‘have the path as object,’ ‘have the path as cause,’ or ‘have the path as dominant condition.’ Ten elements may be arisen, may be productive, or should not be said to be ‘unarisen.’ The sound element may be arisen, may be unarisen, or should not be said to be ‘productive.’ Six elements may be arisen, may be unarisen, or may be productive. The dhamma-element may be arisen, may be unarisen, may be productive, or should not be said to be ‘arisen,’ ‘unarisen,’ or ‘productive.’

Sattarasa [M 0.0095] dhātuyo siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Dhammadhātu siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā, siyā na vattabbā – “atītā”tipi, “anāgatā”tipi, “paccuppannā”tipi. Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Cha dhātuyo paccuppannārammaṇā. Dve dhātuyo siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā[V 0.0104], siyā na vattabbā – “atītārammaṇā”tipi, “anāgatārammaṇā”tipi, “paccuppannārammaṇā”tipi; siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā.

Seventeen elements may be past, may be future, or may be present. The dhamma-element may be past, may be future, may be present, or it should not be said ‘past,’ ‘future,’ or ‘present.’ Ten elements are without an object. Six elements have a present object. Two elements may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or it should not be said ‘have a past object,’ ‘have a future object,’ or ‘have a present object’; they may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external.

Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Cha dhātuyo siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā. Dve dhātuyo siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, siyā [T 0.0116] na vattabbā – “ajjhattārammaṇā”tipi, “bahiddhārammaṇā”tipi, “ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā”tipi. Rūpadhātu sanidassanasappaṭighā. Nava dhātuyo anidassanaappaṭighā. Aṭṭha dhātuyo anidassanaappaṭighā.

Ten elements are without an object. Six elements may have an internal object, may have an external object, or may have both an internal and external object. Two elements may have an internal object, may have an external object, may have both an internal and external object, or should not be said to have an ‘internal object,’ ‘external object,’ or ‘both internal and external object.’ The form-element is visible and resistant. Nine elements are invisible and resistant. Eight elements are invisible and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

188. Sattarasa dhātuyo na hetū. Dhammadhātu siyā hetu, siyā na hetu. Soḷasa dhātuyo ahetukā. Dve dhātuyo siyā sahetukā, siyā ahetukā. Soḷasa dhātuyo ahetukā. Dve dhātuyo siyā sahetukā, siyā ahetukā. Soḷasa dhātuyo hetuvippayuttā[P 0.0093]. Dve dhātuyo siyā hetusampayuttā, siyā hetuvippayuttā. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “hetu ceva sahetukā cā”tipi, “sahetukā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “hetu ceva sahetukā cā”ti, siyā sahetukā ceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbā – “sahetukā ceva na ca hetū”ti. Dhammadhātu siyā hetu ceva sahetukā ca, siyā sahetukā ceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbā – “hetu ceva sahetukā cā”tipi, “sahetukā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”tipi, “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “hetu ceva hetusampayuttā cā”ti, siyā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbā – “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”ti. Dhammadhātu siyā hetu ceva hetusampayuttā ca, siyā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbā – “hetu ceva hetusampayuttā [M 0.0096] cā”tipi, “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo na hetuahetukā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā na hetusahetukā, siyā na hetuahetukā. Dhammadhātu siyā na hetusahetukā, siyā [T 0.0117] na hetuahetukā, siyā na vattabbā – “na hetusahetukā”tipi, “na hetuahetukā”tipi.

188. Seventeen elements are not roots. The dhamma-element may be a root, or may not be a root. Sixteen elements are rootless. Two elements may be rooted, or may be rootless. Sixteen elements are dissociated from roots. Two elements may be associated with roots, or may be dissociated from roots. Sixteen elements should not be said to be ‘both roots and rooted,’ or ‘rooted but not roots.’ The mind-consciousness-element should not be said to be ‘both a root and rooted’; it may be rooted but not a root, or it should not be said to be ‘rooted but not a root.’ The dhamma-element may be both a root and rooted, may be rooted but not a root, or it should not be said to be ‘both a root and rooted’ or ‘rooted but not a root.’ Sixteen elements should not be said to be ‘both roots and associated with roots,’ or ‘associated with roots but not roots.’ The mind-consciousness-element should not be said to be ‘both a root and associated with a root’; it may be associated with a root but not a root, or it should not be said to be ‘associated with a root but not a root.’ The dhamma-element may be both a root and associated with a root, may be associated with a root but not a root, or it should not be said to be ‘both a root and associated with a root’ or ‘associated with a root but not a root.’ Sixteen elements are not-roots and rootless. The mind-consciousness-element may be not-a-root and rooted, or it may be not-a-root and rootless. The dhamma-element may be not-a-root and rooted, may be not-a-root and rootless, or it should not be said to be ‘not-a-root and rooted’ or ‘not-a-root and rootless.’

Sattarasa [V 0.0105] dhātuyo sappaccayā. Dhammadhātu siyā sappaccayā, siyā appaccayā. Sattarasa dhātuyo saṅkhatā. Dhammadhātu siyā saṅkhatā, siyā asaṅkhatā. Rūpadhātu sanidassanā. Sattarasa dhātuyo anidassanā. Dasa dhātuyo sappaṭighā. Aṭṭha dhātuyo appaṭighā. Dasa dhātuyo rūpā. Satta dhātuyo arūpā. Dhammadhātu siyā rūpā, siyā arūpā. Soḷasa dhātuyo lokiyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā; kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

Seventeen elements are with conditions. The dhamma-element may be with conditions, or without conditions. Seventeen elements are conditioned. The dhamma-element may be conditioned, or unconditioned. The form-element is visible. Seventeen elements are invisible. Ten elements are resistant. Eight elements are non-resistant. Ten elements are material. Seven elements are immaterial. The dhamma-element may be material, or immaterial. Sixteen elements are worldly. Two elements may be worldly, or supramundane; knowable by some, and not knowable by some.

Sattarasa dhātuyo no āsavā. Dhammadhātu siyā āsavā, siyā no āsavā. Soḷasa dhātuyo sāsavā. Dve dhātuyo siyā sāsavā, siyā anāsavā. Soḷasa dhātuyo āsavavippayuttā. Dve dhātuyo siyā āsavasampayuttā, siyā āsavavippayuttā. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”ti, “sāsavā ceva [P 0.0094] no ca āsavā”. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “āsavo ceva sāsavā cā”ti, siyā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbā – “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavo”ti. Dhammadhātu siyā āsavo ceva sāsavā ca, siyā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbā – “āsavo ceva sāsavā cā”tipi, “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavo”tipi.

Seventeen elements are not taints. The dhamma-element may be a taint, or may not be a taint. Sixteen elements are objects for the taints. Two elements may be objects for the taints, or may not be objects for the taints. Sixteen elements are dissociated from taints. Two elements may be associated with taints, or may be dissociated from taints. Sixteen elements should not be said to be ‘both taints and objects for the taints’; they are objects for the taints but not taints. The mind-consciousness-element should not be said to be ‘both a taint and an object for the taints’; it may be an object for the taints but not a taint, or it may be that it should not be said to be ‘an object for the taints but not a taint.’ The dhamma-element may be both a taint and an object for the taints, may be an object for the taints but not a taint, or it may be that it should not be said to be ‘both a taint and an object for the taints’ or ‘an object for the taints but not a taint.’

Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā”tipi. Manoviññāṇadhātu na [T 0.0118] vattabbā – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbā – “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavo”ti. Dhammadhātu siyā āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttā ca, siyā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbā – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavo”tipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo āsavavippayuttasāsavā. Dve dhātuyo siyā āsavavippayuttasāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā[M 0.0097], siyā na vattabbā – “āsavavippayuttasāsavā”tipi, “āsavavippayuttaanāsavā”tipi.

Sixteen elements should not be said to be 'both taints and associated with taints,' nor 'associated with taints but not taints.' The mind-consciousness-element should not be said to be 'both a taint and associated with taints'; it may be associated with taints but not a taint, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'associated with taints but not a taint.' The dhamma-element may be both a taint and associated with taints, may be associated with taints but not a taint, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'both a taint and associated with taints,' nor 'associated with taints but not a taint.' Sixteen elements are dissociated from taints and are objects for the taints. Two elements may be dissociated from taints and are objects for the taints, may be dissociated from taints and are not objects for the taints, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'dissociated from taints and are objects for the taints,' nor 'dissociated from taints and are not objects for the taints.'

Sattarasa dhātuyo no saṃyojanā. Dhammadhātu siyā saṃyojanaṃ, siyā no saṃyojanaṃ. Soḷasa dhātuyo saṃyojaniyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā saṃyojaniyā, siyā asaṃyojaniyā. Soḷasa [V 0.0106] dhātuyo saṃyojanavippayuttā. Dve dhātuyo siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cā”ti, saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyā cā”ti, siyā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojana”nti. Dhammadhātu siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyā ca, siyā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyā cā”tipi, “saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā [T 0.0119] ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”tipi. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojana”nti. Dhammadhātu siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā. Dve [P 0.0095] dhātuyo siyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā”tipi, “saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā”tipi.

Seventeen elements are not fetters. The dhamma-element may be a fetter, or may not be a fetter. Sixteen elements are objects for the fetters. Two elements may be objects for the fetters, or may not be objects for the fetters. Sixteen elements are dissociated from fetters. Two elements may be associated with fetters, or may be dissociated from fetters. Sixteen elements should not be said to be 'both fetters and objects for the fetters'; they are objects for the fetters but not fetters. The mind-consciousness-element should not be said to be 'both a fetter and an object for the fetters'; it may be an object for the fetters but not a fetter, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'an object for the fetters but not a fetter.' The dhamma-element may be both a fetter and an object for the fetters, may be an object for the fetters but not a fetter, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'both a fetter and an object for the fetters,' nor 'an object for the fetters but not a fetter.' Sixteen elements should not be said to be 'both fetters and associated with fetters,' nor 'associated with fetters but not fetters.' The mind-consciousness-element should not be said to be 'both a fetter and associated with fetters'; it may be associated with fetters but not a fetter, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'associated with fetters but not a fetter.' The dhamma-element may be both a fetter and associated with fetters, may be associated with fetters but not a fetter, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'both a fetter and associated with fetters,' nor 'associated with fetters but not a fetter.' Sixteen elements are dissociated from fetters and are objects for the fetters. Two elements may be dissociated from fetters and are objects for the fetters, may be dissociated from fetters and are not objects for the fetters, or it may be that it should not be said to be 'dissociated from fetters and are objects for the fetters,' nor 'dissociated from fetters and are not objects for the fetters.'

Sattarasa dhātuyo no ganthā. Dhammadhātu siyā gantho, siyā no gantho. Soḷasa dhātuyo ganthaniyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā ganthaniyā, siyā aganthaniyā. Soḷasa dhātuyo ganthavippayuttā. Dve dhātuyo siyā ganthasampayuttā, siyā ganthavippayuttā. Soḷasa dhātuyo [M 0.0098] na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthaniyā cā”ti, ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “gantho ceva ganthaniyā cā”ti, siyā ganthaniyā ceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthaniyā ceva no ca gantho”ti. Dhammadhātu siyā gantho ceva ganthaniyā ca, siyā ganthaniyā ceva [T 0.0120] no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbā – “gantho ceva ganthaniyā cā”tipi, “ganthaniyā ceva no ca gantho”tipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā [V 0.0107] cā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā”tipi. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “gantho ceva ganthasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca gantho”ti. Dhammadhātu siyā gantho ceva ganthasampayuttā ca, siyā ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbā – “gantho ceva ganthasampayuttā cā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca gantho”tipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā, siyā ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā”tipi, “ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā”tipi.

Seventeen elements are not bonds. The dhamma-element is sometimes a bond, sometimes not a bond. Sixteen elements are objects of the bonds. Two elements are sometimes objects of the bonds, sometimes not objects of the bonds. Sixteen elements are dissociated from bonds. Two elements are sometimes associated with bonds, sometimes dissociated from bonds. The sixteen elements should not be said to be 'both bonds and objects of the bonds'; they are objects of the bonds but not bonds. The mind-consciousness-element should not be said to be 'both a bond and an object of the bonds'; it is sometimes an object of the bonds but not a bond, and sometimes it should not be said to be 'an object of the bonds but not a bond.' Sattarasa dhātuyo no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā. Dhammadhātu siyā nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā no nīvaraṇaṃ. Soḷasa dhātuyo nīvaraṇiyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā nīvaraṇiyā, siyā anīvaraṇiyā. Soḷasa dhātuyo nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Dve dhātuyo siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”ti, nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”ti, siyā nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇa”nti. Dhammadhātu siyā nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyā ca, siyā nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ[T 0.0121], siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇa”ntipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”tipi. Manoviññāṇadhātu na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no [M 0.0099] ca nīvaraṇa”nti. Dhammadhātu siyā nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca, siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇa”ntipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā”tipi, “nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā”tipi.

Sattarasa dhātuyo no parāmāsā. Dhammadhātu siyā parāmāso, siyā no parāmāso. Soḷasa dhātuyo parāmaṭṭhā. Dve dhātuyo siyā parāmaṭṭhā, siyā aparāmaṭṭhā. Soḷasa dhātuyo parāmāsavippayuttā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā parāmāsasampayuttā, siyā parāmāsavippayuttā. Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Satta dhātuyo sārammaṇā. Dhammadhātu siyā sārammaṇā, siyā anārammaṇā. Satta dhātuyo cittā. Ekādasa dhātuyo no cittā. Sattarasa dhātuyo acetasikā. Dhammadhātu siyā cetasikā, siyā acetasikā. Dasa dhātuyo cittavippayuttā. Dhammadhātu siyā cittasampayuttā, siyā cittavippayuttā. Ten elements are without an object. Seven elements are with an object. The element of phenomena is in some cases with an object, in some cases without an object. Seven elements are consciousness. Dvādasa dhātuyo no cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cha dhātuyo siyā cittasamuṭṭhānā, siyā no cittasamuṭṭhānā. Sattarasa [P 0.0096] dhātuyo no cittasahabhuno. Dhammadhātu siyā cittasahabhū, siyā no cittasahabhū. Twelve elements are not originated by mind. Six elements are in some cases originated by mind, in some cases not originated by mind. Seventeen elements are not co-nascent with mind. Sattarasa dhātuyo no kilesā. Dhammadhātu siyā kilesā, siyā no kilesā. Soḷasa dhātuyo saṃkilesikā. Dve dhātuyo siyā saṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkilesikā. Soḷasa dhātuyo asaṃkiliṭṭhā.
