Sixteen elements do not have a cause to be abandoned by cultivation. Two elements in some cases have a cause to be abandoned by cultivation, and in some cases do not have a cause to be abandoned by cultivation.

Pannarasa dhātuyo avitakkā. Manodhātu savitakkā. Dve dhātuyo siyā savitakkā, siyā [V 0.0111] avitakkā. Pannarasa dhātuyo avicārā. Manodhātu savicārā. Dve dhātuyo siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Soḷasa dhātuyo appītikā. Dve dhātuyo siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Soḷasa dhātuyo na pītisahagatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Pannarasa dhātuyo na sukhasahagatā. Tisso dhātuyo siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Ekādasa dhātuyo na upekkhāsahagatā. Pañca dhātuyo upekkhāsahagatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā [T 0.0127] upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā.

Fifteen elements are without initial application. The mind-element is with initial application. Two elements are in some cases with initial application, and in some cases without initial application. Fifteen elements are without sustained application. The mind-element is with sustained application. Two elements are in some cases with sustained application, and in some cases without sustained application. Sixteen elements are without rapture. Two elements are in some cases with rapture, and in some cases without rapture. Sixteen elements are not accompanied by rapture. Two elements are in some cases accompanied by rapture, and in some cases not accompanied by rapture. Fifteen elements are not accompanied by happiness. Three elements are in some cases accompanied by happiness, and in some cases not accompanied by happiness. Eleven elements are not accompanied by equanimity. Five elements are accompanied by equanimity. Two elements are in some cases accompanied by equanimity, and in some cases not accompanied by equanimity.

Soḷasa dhātuyo kāmāvacarā. Dve dhātuyo siyā kāmāvacarā, siyā na kāmāvacarā. Soḷasa dhātuyo na rūpāvacarā. Dve dhātuyo siyā rūpāvacarā, siyā na rūpāvacarā. Soḷasa dhātuyo na arūpāvacarā. Dve [M 0.0103] dhātuyo siyā arūpāvacarā, siyā na arūpāvacarā. Soḷasa dhātuyo pariyāpannā. Dve dhātuyo siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā. Soḷasa dhātuyo aniyyānikā. Dve dhātuyo siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Soḷasa dhātuyo aniyatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Soḷasa dhātuyo sauttarā. Dve dhātuyo siyā sauttarā, siyā anuttarā. Soḷasa [P 0.0098] dhātuyo araṇā. Dve dhātuyo siyā saraṇā, siyā araṇāti.

Sixteen elements are of the sense-sphere. Two elements are in some cases of the sense-sphere, and in some cases not of the sense-sphere. Sixteen elements are not of the form-sphere. Two elements are in some cases of the form-sphere, and in some cases not of the form-sphere. Sixteen elements are not of the formless-sphere. Two elements are in some cases of the formless-sphere, and in some cases not of the formless-sphere. Sixteen elements are included. Two elements are in some cases included, and in some cases not included. Sixteen elements are not leading out. Two elements are in some cases leading out, and in some cases not leading out. Sixteen elements are indeterminate. Two elements are in some cases determinate, and in some cases indeterminate. Sixteen elements are surpassable. Two elements are in some cases surpassable, and in some cases unsurpassable. Sixteen elements are without conflict. Two elements are in some cases with conflict, and in some cases without conflict.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Interrogation Section.

Dhātuvibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Elements is concluded.

4. Saccavibhaṅgo

4. The Analysis of the Truths

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Discourse Exposition

189. Cattāri [M 0.0104][P 0.0099][V 0.0112] ariyasaccāni – dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhasamudayo (syā.) ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ dukkhanirodho (syā.) ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ.

189. There are four Noble Truths: the Noble Truth of suffering, the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering, the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering, and the Noble Truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

1. Dukkhasaccaṃ

1. The Truth of Suffering

190. Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi dukkhā, maraṇampi dukkhaṃ, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsāpi dukkhā, appiyehi [T 0.0128] sampayogo dukkho, piyehi vippayogo dukkho, yaṃ picchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ, saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā.

190. Herein, what is the Noble Truth of suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are suffering; association with the disliked is suffering; separation from the liked is suffering; not getting what one desires is also suffering; in brief, the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering.

191. Tattha katamā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjāti okkanti abhinibbatti khandhānaṃ pātubhāvo āyatanānaṃ paṭilābho – ayaṃ vuccati “jāti”.

191. Herein, what is birth? Of those various beings in those various orders of beings, whatever is the birth, generation, conception, production, the manifestation of the aggregates, the acquisition of the sense bases—this is called 'birth.'

192. Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṃ pāliccaṃ valittacatā āyuno saṃhāni indriyānaṃ paripāko – ayaṃ vuccati “jarā”.

192. Herein, what is aging? Of those various beings in those various orders of beings, whatever is the aging, decrepitude, brokenness of teeth, graying of hair, wrinkling of skin, the decline of the life-span, the decay of the faculties—this is called 'aging.'

193. Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā [V 0.0113] bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccu maraṇaṃ kālakiriyā khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo jīvitindriyassupacchedo – idaṃ vuccati “maraṇaṃ”.

193. Herein, what is death? Of those various beings from those various orders of beings, whatever is the passing away, the state of passing away, the breaking up, the disappearance, death, dying, the completion of time, the breaking up of the aggregates, the casting off of the body, the cutting off of the life faculty—this is called 'death.'

194. Tattha katamo soko? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa [P 0.0100] diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa soko socanā socitattaṃ antosoko antoparisoko cetaso parijjhāyanā domanassaṃ sokasallaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “soko”.

194. Herein, what is sorrow? For one afflicted by the loss of relatives, or afflicted by the loss of wealth, or afflicted by the loss of health, or afflicted by the loss of virtue, or afflicted by the loss of right view; or for one endowed with some other misfortune, or afflicted by some other painful state, whatever is the sorrow, sorrowing, state of sorrow, inner sorrow, intense inner sorrow, the mind's burning, displeasure, the dart of sorrow—this is called 'sorrow.'

195. Tattha [M 0.0105] katamo paridevo? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā [T 0.0129] phuṭṭhassa diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa ādevo paridevo ādevanā paridevanā ādevitattaṃ paridevitattaṃ vācā palāpo vippalāpo lālappo lālappanā lālappitattaṃ lālapo lālapanā lālapitattaṃ (syā.) – ayaṃ vuccati “paridevo”.

195. Herein, what is lamentation? For one afflicted by the loss of relatives, or afflicted by the loss of wealth, or afflicted by the loss of health, or afflicted by the loss of virtue, or afflicted by the loss of right view; or for one endowed with some other misfortune, or afflicted by some other painful state, whatever is the wailing, lamenting, the act of wailing, the act of lamenting, the state of one who wails, the state of one who laments, speech, prattling, incoherent speech, babbling, the act of babbling, the state of one who babbles—this is called 'lamentation.'

196. Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

196. Herein, what is pain? Whatever is bodily unpleasantness, bodily pain; an unpleasant, painful feeling born of bodily contact; an unpleasant, painful feeling born of bodily contact—this is called 'pain.'

197. Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassaṃ”.

197. Herein, what is displeasure? Whatever is mental unpleasantness, mental pain; an unpleasant, painful feeling born of mind-contact; an unpleasant, painful feeling born of mind-contact—this is called 'displeasure.'

198. Tattha katamo upāyāso? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa āyāso upāyāso āyāsitattaṃ upāyāsitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “upāyāso”.

198. Herein, what is despair? For one afflicted by the loss of relatives, or afflicted by the loss of wealth, or afflicted by the loss of health, or afflicted by the loss of virtue, or afflicted by the loss of right view; or for one endowed with some other misfortune, or afflicted by some other painful state, whatever is the anguish, despair, the state of anguish, the state of despair—this is called 'despair.'

199. Tattha katamo appiyehi sampayogo dukkho? Idha yassa te honti aniṭṭhā akantā [V 0.0114] amanāpā rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā, ye vā panassa te honti anatthakāmā ahitakāmā aphāsukakāmā ayogakkhemakāmā; yā tehi saṅgati samāgamo samodhānaṃ missībhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati “appiyehi sampayogo dukkho”.

199. Herein, what is the suffering of association with the disliked? Here, for a person, there are undesirable, unpleasing, and disagreeable forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tactile objects; or there are those who wish one harm, who wish one ill, who wish one discomfort, who wish one insecurity from the yokes; whatever association, coming together, meeting, and mixing with them there is—this is called 'the suffering of association with the disliked.'

200. Tattha [T 0.0130] katamo piyehi vippayogo dukkho? Idha yassa te honti iṭṭhā kantā manāpā rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā, ye vā panassa te honti atthakāmā hitakāmā phāsukakāmā yogakkhemakāmā mātā vā pitā vā bhātā vā bhaginī vā mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā [M 0.0106] vā; yā tehi asaṅgati asamāgamo asamodhānaṃ amissībhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati “piyehi vippayogo dukkho”.

200. Therein, what is the suffering of separation from the beloved? In this world, for a certain person, there are forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangible objects that are desirable, dear, and agreeable. Or there are those who desire their welfare, benefit, comfort, and security from the yokes—such as mother or father, brother or sister, friends or companions, maternal relatives or paternal relatives. Whatever non-association, non-communion, non-reunion, and non-intermingling with them there is—this is called 'the suffering of separation from the beloved'.

201. Tattha [P 0.0101] katamaṃ yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ? Jātidhammānaṃ sattānaṃ evaṃ icchā uppajjati – “aho vata, mayaṃ na jātidhammā assāma; na ca, vata, no jāti āgaccheyyā”ti! Na kho panetaṃ icchāya pattabbaṃ. Idampi “yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ”.

201. Therein, what is 'not to get what one wants, that also is suffering'? For beings subject to the nature of birth, such a wish arises: 'Oh, if only we were not subject to the nature of birth! If only birth would not come to us!' But this is not to be obtained by wishing. This too is 'not to get what one wants, that also is suffering'.

Jarādhammānaṃ sattānaṃ…pe… byādhidhammānaṃ sattānaṃ…pe… maraṇadhammānaṃ sattānaṃ…pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammānaṃ sattānaṃ evaṃ icchā uppajjati – “aho vata, mayaṃ na sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā assāma; na ca, vata, no sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā āgaccheyyu”nti! Na kho panetaṃ icchāya pattabbaṃ. Idampi “yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ”.

For beings subject to the nature of aging... for beings subject to the nature of sickness... for beings subject to the nature of death... for beings subject to the nature of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair, such a wish arises: 'Oh, if only we were not subject to the nature of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair! If only sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair would not come to us!' But this is not to be obtained by wishing. This too is 'not to get what one wants, that also is suffering'.

202. Tattha katame saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā? Seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime vuccanti “saṃkhittena [T 0.0131] pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā”.

202. Therein, what, in brief, are the five aggregates subject to clinging that are suffering? They are as follows: the aggregate of form subject to clinging, the aggregate of feeling subject to clinging, the aggregate of perception subject to clinging, the aggregate of formations subject to clinging, and the aggregate of consciousness subject to clinging. These are called, in brief, 'the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering'.

Idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ”.

This is called 'the Noble Truth of Suffering.'

2. Samudayasaccaṃ

2. The Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering

203. Tattha [V 0.0115] katamaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobhavikā ponobbhavikā (syā. ka.) nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā.

203. Therein, what is the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering? It is this craving which leads to renewed existence, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights greatly in this and that. Namely: craving for sensual pleasure, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence.

Sā kho panesā taṇhā kattha uppajjamānā uppajjati, kattha nivisamānā nivisati? Yaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ, etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

Now, where does this craving arise when it is arising? Where does it settle when it is settling? Whatever in the world is of a dear and pleasant nature, it is there that this craving arises when it is arising; it is there that it settles when it is settling.

Kiñca loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ? Cakkhuṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotaṃ loke…pe… [M 0.0107] ghānaṃ loke… jivhā loke… kāyo loke… mano loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

And what in the world is of a dear and pleasant nature? The eye in the world is of a dear and pleasant nature. It is there that this craving arises when it is arising; it is there that it settles when it is settling. The ear in the world... the nose in the world... the tongue in the world... the body in the world... the mind in the world is of a dear and pleasant nature. It is there that this craving arises when it is arising; it is there that it settles when it is settling.

Rūpā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddā loke…pe… gandhā loke… rasā loke… phoṭṭhabbā loke… dhammā loke [P 0.0102] piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

Forms in the world are of a dear and pleasant nature. It is there that this craving arises when it is arising; it is there that it settles when it is settling. Sounds in the world... smells in the world... tastes in the world... tangible objects in the world... mental objects in the world are of a dear and pleasant nature. It is there that this craving arises when it is arising; it is there that it settles when it is settling.

Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotaviññāṇaṃ loke…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ loke… jivhāviññāṇaṃ loke… kāyaviññāṇaṃ loke… manoviññāṇaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, eye-consciousness is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, ear-consciousness... nose-consciousness... tongue-consciousness... body-consciousness... In the world, mind-consciousness is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Cakkhusamphasso loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotasamphasso loke…pe… ghānasamphasso loke… jivhāsamphasso loke… kāyasamphasso loke… manosamphasso loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha [T 0.0132] nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, eye-contact is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, ear-contact... nose-contact... tongue-contact... body-contact... In the world, mind-contact is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Cakkhusamphassajā [V 0.0116] vedanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotasamphassajā vedanā loke…pe… ghānasamphassajā vedanā loke… jivhāsamphassajā vedanā loke… kāyasamphassajā vedanā loke… manosamphassajā vedanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, feeling born of eye-contact is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, feeling born of ear-contact... feeling born of nose-contact... feeling born of tongue-contact... feeling born of body-contact... In the world, feeling born of mind-contact is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Rūpasaññā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddasaññā loke…pe… gandhasaññā loke… rasasaññā loke… phoṭṭhabbasaññā loke… dhammasaññā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, perception of forms is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, perception of sounds... perception of smells... perception of tastes... perception of tangible objects... In the world, perception of mental objects is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Rūpasañcetanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddasañcetanā loke…pe… gandhasañcetanā [M 0.0108] loke… rasasañcetanā loke… phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā loke… dhammasañcetanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, volition regarding forms is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, volition regarding sounds... volition regarding smells... volition regarding tastes... volition regarding tangible objects... In the world, volition regarding mental objects is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Rūpataṇhā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddataṇhā loke…pe… gandhataṇhā loke… rasataṇhā loke… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā loke… dhammataṇhā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, craving for forms is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, craving for sounds... craving for smells... craving for tastes... craving for tangible objects... In the world, craving for mental objects is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Rūpavitakko loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati[T 0.0133]. Saddavitakko loke…pe… gandhavitakko loke… rasavitakko loke… phoṭṭhabbavitakko loke… dhammavitakko loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, initial thought concerning forms is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, initial thought concerning sounds... initial thought concerning smells... initial thought concerning tastes... initial thought concerning tangible objects... In the world, initial thought concerning mental objects is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Rūpavicāro [P 0.0103] loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati[V 0.0117], ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Gandhavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Rasavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Phoṭṭhabbavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Dhammavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.

In the world, sustained thought concerning forms is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, sustained thought concerning sounds is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, sustained thought concerning smells is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, sustained thought concerning tastes is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, sustained thought concerning tangible objects is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles. In the world, sustained thought concerning mental objects is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving, when arising, arises; it is here that, when settling, it settles.

Idaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ”.

This is called the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering.

3. Nirodhasaccaṃ

3. The Noble Truth of Cessation

204. Tattha katamaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo.

204. And what, among these, is the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering? It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving, its relinquishment, abandonment, release, and freedom from it.

Sā [M 0.0109] kho panesā taṇhā kattha pahīyamānā pahīyati, kattha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati? Yaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ, etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Now, where is this craving abandoned when it is being abandoned, and where does it cease when it is ceasing? Whatever in the world is a dear form and a pleasing form, it is here that this craving is abandoned when it is being abandoned, and it is here that it ceases when it is ceasing.

Kiñca loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ? Cakkhuṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati. Sotaṃ loke…pe… ghānaṃ [T 0.0134] loke… jivhā loke… kāyo loke… mano loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

And what in the world is a dear form and a pleasing form? In the world, the eye is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is being abandoned, and it is here that it ceases when it is ceasing. In the world, the ear... the nose... the tongue... the body... In the world, the mind is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is being abandoned, and it is here that it ceases when it is ceasing.

Rūpā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati. Saddā loke…pe… gandhā loke… rasā loke… phoṭṭhabbā loke… dhammā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

In the world, forms are a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is being abandoned, and it is here that it ceases when it is ceasing. In the world, sounds... smells... tastes... tangible objects... In the world, mental objects are a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is being abandoned, and it is here that it ceases when it is ceasing.

Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [V 0.0118] loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati. Sotaviññāṇaṃ loke…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ loke… jivhāviññāṇaṃ loke… kāyaviññāṇaṃ loke… manoviññāṇaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

In the world, eye-consciousness is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is being abandoned, and it is here that it ceases when it is ceasing. In the world, ear-consciousness... nose-consciousness... tongue-consciousness... body-consciousness... In the world, mind-consciousness is a dear form and a pleasing form. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is being abandoned, and it is here that it ceases when it is ceasing.

Cakkhusamphasso loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati. Sotasamphasso loke…pe… ghānasamphasso loke… jivhāsamphasso loke… kāyasamphasso loke… manosamphasso loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Eye-contact in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases. Ear-contact in the world... nose-contact in the world... tongue-contact in the world... body-contact in the world... mind-contact in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases.

Cakkhusamphassajā vedanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati. Sotasamphassajā vedanā loke…pe… ghānasamphassajā vedanā loke… jivhāsamphassajā vedanā loke… kāyasamphassajā vedanā loke… manosamphassajā vedanā loke [P 0.0104] piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Feeling born of eye-contact in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases. Feeling born of ear-contact in the world... feeling born of nose-contact in the world... feeling born of tongue-contact in the world... feeling born of body-contact in the world... feeling born of mind-contact in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases.

Rūpasaññā loke… [T 0.0135] saddasaññā loke… gandhasaññā loke… rasasaññā loke… phoṭṭhabbasaññā loke… dhammasaññā loke piyarūpaṃ [M 0.0110] sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Perception of forms in the world... perception of sounds in the world... perception of smells in the world... perception of tastes in the world... perception of tangible objects in the world... perception of mental objects in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases.

Rūpasañcetanā loke… saddasañcetanā loke… gandhasañcetanā loke… rasasañcetanā loke… phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā loke… dhammasañcetanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Volition regarding forms in the world... volition regarding sounds in the world... volition regarding smells in the world... volition regarding tastes in the world... volition regarding tangible objects in the world... volition regarding mental objects in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases.

Rūpataṇhā loke… saddataṇhā loke… gandhataṇhā loke… rasataṇhā loke… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā loke… dhammataṇhā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Craving for forms in the world... craving for sounds in the world... craving for smells in the world... craving for tastes in the world... craving for tangible objects in the world... craving for mental objects in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases.

Rūpavitakko [V 0.0119] loke… saddavitakko loke… gandhavitakko loke… rasavitakko loke… phoṭṭhabbavitakko loke… dhammavitakko loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Initial thought concerning forms in the world... initial thought concerning sounds in the world... initial thought concerning smells in the world... initial thought concerning tastes in the world... initial thought concerning tangible objects in the world... initial thought concerning mental objects in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases.

Rūpavicāro loke… saddavicāro loke… gandhavicāro loke… rasavicāro loke… phoṭṭhabbavicāro loke… dhammavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā [T 0.0136] pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati.

Sustained thought concerning forms in the world... sustained thought concerning sounds in the world... sustained thought concerning smells in the world... sustained thought concerning tastes in the world... sustained thought concerning tangible objects in the world... sustained thought concerning mental objects in the world is a lovable thing and a delightful thing. Herein, when this craving is being abandoned, it is abandoned; herein, when it is ceasing, it ceases.

Idaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ”.

This is called the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering.

4. Maggasaccaṃ

4. The Truth of the Path

205. Tattha katamaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

205. Among these, what is the Noble Truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.

Tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”.

Among these, what is Right View? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, and knowledge of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering. This is called Right View.

Tattha [M 0.0111] katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Nekkhammasaṅkappo, abyāpādasaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsaṅkappo”.

Among these, what is Right Intention? The intention of renunciation, the intention of non-ill will, and the intention of non-harming. This is called Right Intention.

Tattha [P 0.0105] katamā sammāvācā? Musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvācā”.

Among these, what is Right Speech? Abstinence from false speech, abstinence from divisive speech, abstinence from harsh speech, and abstinence from frivolous chatter. This is called Right Speech.

Tattha katamo sammākammanto? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati “sammākammanto”.

Among these, what is Right Action? Abstinence from taking life, abstinence from taking what is not given, and abstinence from sexual misconduct. This is called Right Action.

Tattha [V 0.0120] katamo sammāājīvo? Idha ariyasāvako micchāājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāājīvo”.

Among these, what is Right Livelihood? Here, in this Dispensation, a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, makes a living by right livelihood. This is called Right Livelihood.

Tattha [T 0.0137] katamo sammāvāyāmo? Idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti, vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati, cittaṃ paggaṇhāti, padahati. Uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti, vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati, cittaṃ paggaṇhāti, padahati. Anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti, vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati, cittaṃ paggaṇhāti, padahati. Uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti, vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati, cittaṃ paggaṇhāti, padahati. Ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvāyāmo”.

Among these, what is Right Effort? Here, in this Dispensation, a monk, for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states, generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. For the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states, he generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. For the arising of unarisen wholesome states, he generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. For the stability, non-confusion, increase, expansion, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states, he generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. This is called Right Effort.

Tattha katamā sammāsati? Idha bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsati”.

Among these, what is Right Mindfulness? Here, in this Dispensation, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful—having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... phenomena in phenomena—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful—having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. This is called Right Mindfulness.

Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Idha bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi, vivicca akusalehi dhammehi, savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā, ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ, cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Pītiyā ca virāgā, upekkhako ca viharati, sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – “upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī”ti, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [T 0.0138] viharati. Sukhassa [M 0.0112] ca pahānā, dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”.

Among these, what is Right Concentration? Here, a monk—quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states—enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which has initial thought and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. With the stilling of initial and sustained thought, he enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, without initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration. With the fading away of rapture, he dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and he experiences pleasure with the body. He enters and dwells in the third jhāna, of which the Noble Ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, he has a pleasant abiding.’ With the abandoning of pleasure and pain—and with the previous disappearance of joy and displeasure—he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. This is called Right Concentration.

Idaṃ [P 0.0106] vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ”.

This is called the Noble Truth of the Path Leading to the Cessation of Suffering.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Analysis according to the Suttas.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Analysis according to the Abhidhamma

206. Cattāri [V 0.0121] saccāni – dukkhaṃ, dukkhasamudayo, dukkhanirodho, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā.

206. There are four truths: suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

Tattha katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving. This is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni, avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā, sāsavā ca kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints, the remaining wholesome states that are subject to the taints, the results of wholesome and unwholesome states that are subject to the taints, those states that are functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma—and all material form: this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving—this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.

Tattha katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā, vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ [T 0.0139] jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo hoti sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that leads out, that leads to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground, secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the eightfold path arises: right view… right concentration.

Tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”.

Among these, what is right view? Whatever is wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view; which is the awakening factor of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right view'.

Tattha katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Yo takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsaṅkappo”.

Among these, what is right intention? Whatever is thought, applied thought… right intention, which is a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right intention'.

Tattha [M 0.0113] katamā sammāvācā? Yā catūhi vacīduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī veramaṇi (ka.) evamuparipi akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammāvācā maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvācā”.

Among these, what is right speech? Whatever is the abstention, refraining, repeated refraining, abstinence from the four kinds of verbal misconduct; the non-doing, non-performance, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the destroying of the causeway, right speech, which is a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right speech'.

Tattha [V 0.0122] katamo sammākammanto? Yā tīhi kāyaduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammākammanto [P 0.0107] maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammākammanto”.

Among these, what is right action? Whatever is the abstention, refraining, repeated refraining, abstinence from the three kinds of bodily misconduct; the non-doing, non-performance, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the destroying of the causeway, right action, which is a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right action'.

Tattha katamo sammāājīvo? Yā micchā ājīvā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammāājīvo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati [T 0.0140] “sammāājīvo”.

Among these, what is right livelihood? Whatever is the abstention, refraining, repeated refraining, abstinence from wrong livelihood; the non-doing, non-performance, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the destroying of the causeway, right livelihood, which is a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right livelihood'.

Tattha katamo sammāvāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho viriyārambho (sī. syā.) …pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvāyāmo”.

Among these, what is right effort? Whatever is the mental arousal of energy… right effort, which is the awakening factor of energy, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right effort'.

Tattha katamā sammāsati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsati”.

Among these, what is right mindfulness? Whatever is mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness, which is the awakening factor of mindfulness, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right mindfulness'.

Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”. Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”. Avasesā dhammā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya sampayuttā.

Among these, what is right concentration? Whatever is the stability of mind, the firm stability of mind… right concentration, which is the awakening factor of concentration, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'right concentration'. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering'. The remaining states are associated with the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

207. Tattha katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā ca avasesā ca kilesā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

207. Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving and the remaining defilements—this is called "the origin of suffering."

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni, avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā, sāsavā ca kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints, the remaining wholesome states that are subject to the taints, the results of wholesome and unwholesome states that are subject to the taints, those states that are functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma—and all material form: this is called "suffering."

Tattha [M 0.0114][V 0.0123] katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya ca, avasesānañca kilesānaṃ [T 0.0141] pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving and of the remaining defilements—this is called "the cessation of suffering."

Tattha katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā, vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati – “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”. Avasesā [P 0.0108] dhammā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya sampayuttā.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that leads out, that leads to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground, secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the eightfold path arises: right view… right concentration. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering'. The remaining states are associated with the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

208. Tattha katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā ca avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

208. Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving, the remaining defilements, and the remaining unwholesome states—this is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni, avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā, sāsavā ca kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

The three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints, the remaining wholesome states that are subject to the taints, the results, subject to the taints, of wholesome and unwholesome states, those states that are functional, being neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, and all material form—this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya ca, avasesānañca kilesānaṃ, avasesānañca akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”. Avasesā dhammā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya sampayuttā.
