Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out, which leads to the destruction of accumulation—for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground, being secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the eight-factored path comes to be: Right View…pe… Right Concentration. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' The remaining states are associated with the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

209. Tattha [V 0.0124] katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā ca avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

209. Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving, the remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, and the three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints—this is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā, sāsavā ca kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The remaining wholesome states that are subject to the taints; the results, subject to the taints, of wholesome and unwholesome states; those states that are functional, being neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma; and all material form—this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha [M 0.0115][P 0.0109] katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya ca, avasesānañca kilesānaṃ, avasesānañca akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ, tiṇṇañca kusalamūlānaṃ sāsavānaṃ pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving, of the remaining defilements, of the remaining unwholesome states, and of the three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints—this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.

Tattha katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”. Avasesā dhammā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya [T 0.0143] sampayuttā.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out, which leads to the destruction of accumulation—for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground, being secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the eight-factored path comes to be: Right View…pe… Right Concentration. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' The remaining states are associated with the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

210. Tattha katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā ca, avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni, avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

210. Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving, the remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints, and the remaining wholesome states that are subject to the taints—this is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Sāsavā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The results, subject to the taints, of wholesome and unwholesome states; those states that are functional, being neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma; and all material form—this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya ca, avasesānañca kilesānaṃ, avasesānañca akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ, tiṇṇañca kusalamūlānaṃ sāsavānaṃ, avasesānañca sāsavānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving, of the remaining defilements, of the remaining unwholesome states, of the three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints, and of the remaining wholesome states that are subject to the taints—this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.

Tattha [V 0.0125] katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā, vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”. Avasesā dhammā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya sampayuttā.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out, which leads to the destruction of accumulation—for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground, being secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the eight-factored path comes to be: Right View…pe… Right Concentration. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' The remaining states are associated with the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

211. Cattāri [P 0.0110] saccāni – dukkhaṃ, dukkhasamudayo, dukkhanirodho, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā.

211. There are four truths: suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

Tattha [T 0.0144][M 0.0116] katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving—this is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni, avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā, sāsavā ca kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots that are subject to the taints, the remaining wholesome states that are subject to the taints, the results, subject to the taints, of wholesome and unwholesome states, those states that are functional, being neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, and all material form—this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving—this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.

Tattha katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā, vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out, which leads to the destruction of accumulation—for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground, being secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the five-factored path comes to be: Right View, Right Thought, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.

Tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”.

Among these, what is Right View? That which is wisdom, understanding…pe… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'Right View'.

Tattha katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Yo takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsaṅkappo”.

Among these, what is Right Thought? That which is thought, applied thought... right thought, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'Right Thought'.

Tattha [T 0.0145][V 0.0126] katamo sammāvāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvāyāmo”.

Among these, what is Right Effort? That which is the mental undertaking of energy... right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'Right Effort'.

Tattha katamā sammāsati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsati”.

Among these, what is Right Mindfulness? That which is mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'Right Mindfulness'.

Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”. Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”. Avasesā dhammā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya sampayuttā.

Among these, what is Right Concentration? Whatever is the stability of the mind... right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'Right Concentration.' This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' The remaining states are associated with the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

212. Tattha [P 0.0111] katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā ca, avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni[M 0.0117], avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

212. Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving, the remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots with taints, and the remaining wholesome states with taints—this is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Sāsavā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The results of wholesome and unwholesome states with taints, and those states that are functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, and all material form—this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya ca, avasesānañca kilesānaṃ, avasesānañca akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ, tiṇṇañca kusalamūlānaṃ sāsavānaṃ, avasesānañca sāsavānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati [T 0.0146] “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving, of the remaining defilements, of the remaining unwholesome states, of the three wholesome roots with taints, and of the remaining wholesome states with taints—this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.

Tattha katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā, vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”. Avasesā dhammā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya sampayuttā.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is leading out, leading to non-accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures... having attained, he abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and sluggish direct knowledge. At that time, the five-factored path arises: Right View, Right Thought, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' The remaining states are associated with the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

213. Cattāri [V 0.0127] saccāni – dukkhaṃ, dukkhasamudayo, dukkhanirodho, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā.

213. The Four Truths: suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

Tattha katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving—this is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni, avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā, sāsavā ca kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots with taints, the remaining wholesome states with taints, the results of wholesome and unwholesome states with taints, those states that are functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, and all material form—this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving—this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.

Tattha katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ [T 0.0147] samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ [P 0.0112] apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [M 0.0118] viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is leading out, leading to non-accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures... having attained, he abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and sluggish direct knowledge. At that time, there is contact... there is non-distraction. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering'.

214. Tattha katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā ca, avasesā ca kilesā, avasesā ca akusalā dhammā, tīṇi ca kusalamūlāni sāsavāni, avasesā ca sāsavā kusalā dhammā – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhasamudayo”.

214. Among these, what is the origin of suffering? Craving, the remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots with taints, and the remaining wholesome states with taints—this is called 'the origin of suffering'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Sāsavā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

Among these, what is suffering? The results of wholesome and unwholesome states with taints, and those states that are functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, and all material form—this is called 'suffering'.

Tattha katamo dukkhanirodho? Taṇhāya ca, avasesānañca kilesānaṃ, avasesānañca akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ, tiṇṇañca kusalamūlānaṃ sāsavānaṃ, avasesānañca sāsavānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodho”.

Among these, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving, of the remaining defilements, of the remaining unwholesome states, of the three wholesome roots with taints, and of the remaining wholesome states with taints—this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.

Tattha [V 0.0128] katamā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminī [T 0.0148] paṭipadā”.

Among these, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is leading out, leading to non-accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures... having attained, he abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and sluggish direct knowledge. At that time, there is contact... there is non-distraction. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering'.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition is concluded.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Questioning Section

215. Cattāri ariyasaccāni – dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ.

215. The four Noble Truths: the Noble Truth of suffering, the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering, the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering, and the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

216. Catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

216. Of the four Noble Truths, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, how many are indeterminate? …pe… How many are with conflict, how many are without conflict?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

217. Samudayasaccaṃ [M 0.0119] akusalaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ kusalaṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ abyākataṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā kusalaṃ, siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ. Dve saccā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya [P 0.0113] vedanāya sampayuttā. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi. Dve saccā vipākadhammadhammā. Nirodhasaccaṃ nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā vipākaṃ, siyā vipākadhammadhammaṃ, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ [V 0.0129] anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Dve saccā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā upādinnupādāniyaṃ, siyā anupādinnupādāniyaṃ.

217. The Truth of the Origin is unwholesome. The Truth of the Path is wholesome. The Truth of Cessation is indeterminate. The Truth of Suffering may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be indeterminate. The two truths [Origin and Path] may be associated with pleasant feeling, or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Regarding the Truth of Cessation, it should not be said that it is ‘associated with pleasant feeling,’ nor that it is ‘associated with painful feeling,’ nor that it is ‘associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ The Truth of Suffering may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; or it should not be said that it is ‘associated with pleasant feeling,’ nor that it is ‘associated with painful feeling,’ nor that it is ‘associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ The two truths [Origin and Path] are conditions for results. The Truth of Cessation is neither a result nor a condition for a result. The Truth of Suffering may be a result, may be a condition for a result, or may be neither a result nor a condition for a result. The Truth of the Origin is not a product of past grasping but is a basis for grasping. The two truths [Path and Cessation] are not a product of past grasping and not a basis for grasping. The Truth of Suffering may be a product of past grasping and a basis for grasping, or it may be not a product of past grasping but a basis for grasping.

Samudayasaccaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikaṃ. Dve saccā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Dukkhasaccaṃ [T 0.0149] siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikaṃ, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ savitakkasavicāraṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ avitakkaavicāraṃ. Maggasaccaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “savitakkasavicāra”ntipi, “avitakkavicāramatta”ntipi, “avitakkaavicāra”ntipi. Dve saccā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “pītisahagata”ntipi, “sukhasahagata”ntipi, “upekkhāsahagata”ntipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā pītisahagataṃ, siyā sukhasahagataṃ, siyā upekkhāsahagataṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “pītisahagata”ntipi, “sukhasahagata”ntipi, “upekkhāsahagata”ntipi.

The Truth of the Origin is defiled and conducive to defilement. The two truths [Path and Cessation] are undefiled and not conducive to defilement. The Truth of Suffering may be defiled and conducive to defilement, or it may be undefiled but conducive to defilement. The Truth of the Origin is with initial application and sustained application. The Truth of Cessation is without initial application and without sustained application. The Truth of the Path may be with initial application and sustained application, may be without initial application but with sustained application only, or may be without initial application and without sustained application. The Truth of Suffering may be with initial application and sustained application, may be without initial application but with sustained application only, or may be without initial application and without sustained application; or it should not be said that it is ‘with initial application and sustained application,’ nor that it is ‘without initial application but with sustained application only,’ nor that it is ‘without initial application and without sustained application.’ The two truths [Origin and Path] may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, or may be accompanied by equanimity. Regarding the Truth of Cessation, it should not be said that it is ‘accompanied by joy,’ nor that it is ‘accompanied by happiness,’ nor that it is ‘accompanied by equanimity.’ The Truth of Suffering may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, or may be accompanied by equanimity; or it should not be said that it is ‘accompanied by joy,’ nor that it is ‘accompanied by happiness,’ nor that it is ‘accompanied by equanimity.’

Dve saccā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Samudayasaccaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ. Dve saccā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Samudayasaccaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ[M 0.0120]. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ ācayagāmi. Maggasaccaṃ apacayagāmi. Nirodhasaccaṃ [P 0.0114] nevācayagāmināpacayagāmi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā ācayagāmi, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmi. Maggasaccaṃ sekkhaṃ. Tīṇi saccāni nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Samudayasaccaṃ parittaṃ[T 0.0150]. Dve saccā appamāṇā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā parittaṃ, siyā mahaggataṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ anārammaṇaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ appamāṇārammaṇaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ, siyā mahaggatārammaṇaṃ na appamāṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “parittārammaṇa”ntipi, “mahaggatārammaṇa”ntipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ, siyā mahaggatārammaṇaṃ, siyā appamāṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “parittārammaṇa”ntipi, “mahaggatārammaṇa”ntipi, “appamāṇārammaṇa”ntipi.

The two truths [Path and Cessation] are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. The Truth of the Origin may be abandoned by seeing, or it may be abandoned by development. The Truth of Suffering may be abandoned by seeing, may be abandoned by development, or it may be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. The two truths [Path and Cessation] are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing or by development. The Truth of the Origin may be rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, or it may be rooted in what is to be abandoned by development. The Truth of Suffering may be rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, may be rooted in what is to be abandoned by development, or it may not be rooted in what is to be abandoned by either seeing or by development. The Truth of the Origin is conducive to accumulation. The Truth of the Path is conducive to diminution. The Truth of Cessation is conducive neither to accumulation nor to diminution. The Truth of Suffering may be conducive to accumulation, or it may be conducive neither to accumulation nor to diminution. The Truth of the Path is of a trainee. The three truths [Origin, Suffering, and Cessation] are neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training. The Truth of the Origin is limited. The two truths [Path and Cessation] are immeasurable. The Truth of Suffering may be limited, or it may be sublime. The Truth of Cessation is without an object. The Truth of the Path has an immeasurable object. The Truth of the Origin may have a limited object or a sublime object, but not an immeasurable object; or it should not be said that it has a ‘limited object,’ nor that it has a ‘sublime object.’ The Truth of Suffering may have a limited object, a sublime object, or an immeasurable object; or it should not be said that it has a ‘limited object,’ nor that it has a ‘sublime object,’ nor that it has an ‘immeasurable object.’

Samudayasaccaṃ [V 0.0130] hīnaṃ. Dve saccā paṇītā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā hīnaṃ, siyā majjhimaṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ aniyataṃ. Maggasaccaṃ sammattaniyataṃ. Dve saccā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Nirodhasaccaṃ anārammaṇaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “maggārammaṇa”ntipi, “maggahetuka”ntipi, “maggādhipatī”tipi. Maggasaccaṃ na maggārammaṇaṃ maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “maggādhipatī”ti. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā maggārammaṇaṃ na maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “maggārammaṇa”ntipi, “maggādhipatī”tipi. Dve saccā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā – “uppādino”ti. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “uppanna”ntipi, “anuppanna”ntipi, “uppādī”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā uppannaṃ, siyā anuppannaṃ, siyā uppādi. Tīṇi saccāni siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “atīta”ntipi, “anāgata”ntipi, “paccuppanna”ntipi. Nirodhasaccaṃ anārammaṇaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “atītārammaṇa”ntipi, [T 0.0151] “anāgatārammaṇa”ntipi, “paccuppannārammaṇa”ntipi. Dve saccā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “atītārammaṇā”tipi, “anāgatārammaṇā”tipi, “paccuppannārammaṇā”tipi. Nirodhasaccaṃ [P 0.0115] bahiddhā. Tīṇi saccāni siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Nirodhasaccaṃ anārammaṇaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ bahiddhārammaṇaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ siyā ajjhattārammaṇaṃ, siyā bahiddhārammaṇaṃ, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā ajjhattārammaṇaṃ, siyā bahiddhārammaṇaṃ, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇaṃ[M 0.0121], siyā na vattabbaṃ – “ajjhattārammaṇa”ntipi, “bahiddhārammaṇa”ntipi, “ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇa”ntipi. Tīṇi saccāni anidassanaappaṭighā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ, siyā anidassanasappaṭighaṃ, siyā anidassanaappaṭighaṃ.

The Truth of the Origin is inferior. The two truths are superior. The Truth of Suffering may be inferior, or it may be middling. The Truth of Cessation is undetermined. The Truth of the Path is determinately right. The two truths may be determinately wrong, or they may be undetermined. The Truth of Cessation is objectless. The Truth of the Origin is not to be said to be 'having the path as its object,' nor 'having the path as its cause,' nor 'having the path as its dominant condition.' The Truth of the Path does not have the path as its object but has the path as its cause; it may have the path as its dominant condition, or it is not to be said to be 'having the path as its dominant condition.' The Truth of Suffering may have the path as its object but does not have the path as its cause; it may have the path as its dominant condition; or it is not to be said to be 'having the path as its object,' nor 'having the path as its dominant condition.' The two truths may be arisen, or they may be unarisen; they are not to be said to be 'productive.' The Truth of Cessation is not to be said to be 'arisen,' nor 'unarisen,' nor 'productive.' The Truth of Suffering may be arisen, or it may be unarisen, or it may be productive. The three truths may be past, or they may be future, or they may be present. The Truth of Cessation is not to be said to be 'past,' nor 'future,' nor 'present.' The Truth of Cessation is objectless. The Truth of the Path is not to be said to be 'having a past object,' nor 'having a future object,' nor 'having a present object.' The two truths may have a past object, or a future object, or a present object; or they are not to be said to be 'having a past object,' nor 'having a future object,' nor 'having a present object.' The Truth of Cessation is external. The three truths may be internal, or they may be external, or they may be both internal and external. The Truth of Cessation is objectless. The Truth of the Path has an external object. The Truth of the Origin may have an internal object, or an external object, or an internal-and-external object. The Truth of Suffering may have an internal object, or an external object, or an internal-and-external object; or it is not to be said to be 'having an internal object,' nor 'having an external object,' nor 'having an internal-and-external object.' The three truths are invisible and non-impinging. The Truth of Suffering may be visible and impinging, or it may be invisible but impinging, or it may be invisible and non-impinging.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyad

218. Samudayasaccaṃ hetu. Nirodhasaccaṃ na hetu. Dve saccā siyā hetū, siyā na hetū. Dve saccā sahetukā. Nirodhasaccaṃ ahetukaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sahetukaṃ, siyā ahetukaṃ. Dve saccā hetusampayuttā. Nirodhasaccaṃ hetuvippayuttaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā hetusampayuttaṃ, siyā hetuvippayuttaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ hetu ceva sahetukañca. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ [V 0.0131] – “hetu ceva sahetukañcā”tipi, “sahetukañceva na ca hetū”tipi. Maggasaccaṃ siyā hetu ceva sahetukañca, siyā sahetukañceva na ca hetu. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā hetu ceva sahetukañca, siyā sahetukañceva na ca hetu, siyā [T 0.0152] na vattabbaṃ – “hetu ceva sahetukañcā”tipi, “sahetukañceva na ca hetū”tipi. Samudayasaccaṃ hetu ceva hetusampayuttañca. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “hetu ceva hetusampayuttañcā”tipi, “hetusampayuttañceva na ca hetū”tipi. Maggasaccaṃ siyā hetu ceva hetusampayuttañca, siyā hetusampayuttañceva na ca hetu. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā hetu ceva hetusampayuttañca, siyā hetusampayuttañceva na ca hetu, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “hetu ceva hetusampayuttañcā”tipi, “hetusampayuttañceva na ca hetū”tipi. Nirodhasaccaṃ na hetuahetukaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “na hetusahetuka”ntipi, “na hetuahetuka”ntipi. Maggasaccaṃ siyā na hetusahetukaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “na hetusahetuka”ntipi, “na hetuahetuka”ntipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā na hetusahetukaṃ, siyā na hetuahetukaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “na hetusahetuka”ntipi, “na hetuahetuka”ntipi.

218. The Truth of the Origin is a cause. The Truth of Cessation is not a cause. The two truths may be causes, or they may not be causes. The two truths are with cause. The Truth of Cessation is without cause. The Truth of Suffering may be with cause, or it may be without cause. The two truths are associated with a cause. The Truth of Cessation is dissociated from a cause. The Truth of Suffering may be associated with a cause, or it may be dissociated from a cause. The Truth of the Origin is both a cause and with cause. The Truth of Cessation is not to be said to be 'both a cause and with cause,' nor 'with cause but not a cause.' The Truth of the Path may be both a cause and with cause, or it may be with cause but not a cause. The Truth of Suffering may be both a cause and with cause, or it may be with cause but not a cause; or it is not to be said to be 'both a cause and with cause,' nor 'with cause but not a cause.' The Truth of the Origin is both a cause and associated with a cause. The Truth of Cessation is not to be said to be 'both a cause and associated with a cause,' nor 'associated with a cause but not a cause.' The Truth of the Path may be both a cause and associated with a cause, or it may be associated with a cause but not a cause. The Truth of Suffering may be both a cause and associated with a cause, or it may be associated with a cause but not a cause; or it is not to be said to be 'both a cause and associated with a cause,' nor 'associated with a cause but not a cause.' The Truth of Cessation is not a cause and is without cause. The Truth of the Origin is not to be said to be 'not a cause and with cause,' nor 'not a cause and without cause.' The Truth of the Path may be not a cause and with cause; or it is not to be said to be 'not a cause and with cause,' nor 'not a cause and without cause.' The Truth of Suffering may be not a cause and with cause, or it may be not a cause and without cause; or it is not to be said to be 'not a cause and with cause,' nor 'not a cause and without cause'.

Tīṇi [P 0.0116] saccāni sappaccayā. Nirodhasaccaṃ appaccayaṃ. Tīṇi saccāni saṅkhatā. Nirodhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ. Tīṇi saccāni anidassanā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sanidassanaṃ, siyā anidassanaṃ. Tīṇi saccāni appaṭighā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sappaṭighaṃ, siyā appaṭighaṃ. Tīṇi saccāni arūpāni. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā rūpaṃ, siyā arūpaṃ. Dve saccā [M 0.0122] lokiyā. Dve saccā lokuttarā; kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

Three truths are with conditions. The Truth of Cessation is without conditions. Three truths are conditioned. The Truth of Cessation is unconditioned. Three truths are invisible. The Truth of Suffering may be visible, or it may be invisible. Three truths are non-impinging. The Truth of Suffering may be impinging, or it may be non-impinging. Three truths are formless. The Truth of Suffering may be form, or it may be formless. Two truths are worldly. Two truths are supramundane; knowable by some, not knowable by some.

Samudayasaccaṃ āsavo. Dve saccā no āsavā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā āsavo, siyā no āsavo. Dve saccā sāsavā. Dve saccā anāsavā[T 0.0153]. Samudayasaccaṃ āsavasampayuttaṃ. Dve saccā āsavavippayuttā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā āsavasampayuttaṃ, siyā āsavavippayuttaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ āsavo ceva sāsavañca. Dve saccā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”tipi, “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā āsavo ceva sāsavañca, siyā sāsavañceva no ca āsavo. Samudayasaccaṃ āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttañca. Dve saccā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttañca[V 0.0132], siyā āsavasampayuttañceva no ca āsavo, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttañcā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttañceva no ca āsavo”tipi. Dve saccā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā. Samudayasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “āsavavippayuttasāsava”ntipi, “āsavavippayuttaanāsava”ntipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā āsavavippayuttasāsavaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “āsavavippayuttasāsava”ntipi, “āsavavippayuttaanāsava”ntipi.

The Truth of Origin is a taint. The two truths are not taints. The Truth of Suffering, in some cases, is a taint; in some cases, is not a taint. The two truths are objects of the taints. The two truths are not objects of the taints. The Truth of Origin is associated with the taints. The two truths are dissociated from the taints. The Truth of Suffering, in some cases, is associated with the taints; in some cases, is dissociated from the taints. The Truth of Origin is both a taint and an object of the taints. Regarding the two truths, it should not be said that they are 'both taints and objects of the taints,' nor 'objects of the taints but not taints.' The Truth of Suffering, in some cases, is both a taint and an object of the taints; in some cases, it is an object of the taints but not a taint. The Truth of Origin is both a taint and associated with the taints. Regarding the two truths, it should not be said that they are 'both taints and associated with the taints,' nor 'associated with the taints but not taints.' The Truth of Suffering, in some cases, is both a taint and associated with the taints; in some cases, it is associated with the taints but not a taint; in some cases, it should not be said that it is 'both a taint and associated with the taints,' nor 'associated with the taints but not a taint.' The two truths are dissociated from the taints and not objects of the taints. Regarding the Truth of Origin, it should not be said that it is 'dissociated from the taints but an object of the taints,' nor 'dissociated from the taints and not an object of the taints.' Regarding the Truth of Suffering, in some cases, it is dissociated from the taints but an object of the taints; in some cases, it should not be said that it is 'dissociated from the taints but an object of the taints,' nor 'dissociated from the taints and not an object of the taints'.

Samudayasaccaṃ saṃyojanaṃ. Dve saccā no saṃyojanā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā saṃyojanaṃ, siyā no saṃyojanaṃ. Dve saccā saṃyojaniyā. Dve saccā asaṃyojaniyā. Samudayasaccaṃ saṃyojanasampayuttaṃ. Dve saccā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā saṃyojanasampayuttaṃ, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyañca. Dve saccā [P 0.0117] na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva [T 0.0154] saṃyojaniyā cā”tipi, “saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyañca, siyā saṃyojaniyañceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttañca. Dve saccā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttañca, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttañceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttañcā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayuttañceva no ca saṃyojana”ntipi[M 0.0123]. Dve saccā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā. Samudayasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniya”ntipi, “saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniya”ntipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniya”ntipi, “saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniya”ntipi.

The Truth of Origin is a fetter. The two truths are not fetters. The Truth of Suffering, in some cases, is a fetter; in some cases, is not a fetter. The two truths are objects of the fetters. The two truths are not objects of the fetters. The Truth of Origin is associated with the fetters. The two truths are dissociated from the fetters. Samudayasaccaṃ gantho. Dve saccā no ganthā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā gantho, siyā no gantho. Dve saccā ganthaniyā. Dve saccā aganthaniyā. Dve saccā ganthavippayuttā. Dve saccā siyā ganthasampayuttā, siyā ganthavippayuttā. Samudayasaccaṃ gantho ceva ganthaniyañca. Dve saccā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthaniyā cā”tipi, “ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā gantho ceva ganthaniyañca, siyā ganthaniyañceva no ca gantho. Samudayasaccaṃ gantho ceva ganthasampayuttañca[T 0.0155], siyā na vattabbaṃ – “gantho ceva ganthasampayuttañcā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho”tipi. Dve saccā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā cā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ [V 0.0133] siyā gantho ceva ganthasampayuttañca, siyā ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “gantho ceva ganthasampayuttañcā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho”tipi. Dve saccā ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā. Dve saccā siyā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā”tipi, “ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā”tipi.

Samudayasaccaṃ ogho…pe… yogo…pe… nīvaraṇaṃ. Dve saccā no nīvaraṇā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā nīvaraṇaṃ, siyā no nīvaraṇaṃ. Dve saccā nīvaraṇiyā dve saccā anīvaraṇiyā. Samudayasaccaṃ [P 0.0118] nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ. Dve saccā nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyañca. Dve saccā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”tipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyañca, siyā nīvaraṇiyañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ. Dve saccā nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā. Samudayasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiya”ntipi, “nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiya”ntipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiya”ntipi, “nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiya”ntipi.

Tīṇi saccāni no parāmāsā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā parāmāso, siyā no parāmāso. Dve saccā parāmaṭṭhā. Dve saccā aparāmaṭṭhā. Dve saccā parāmāsavippayuttā. Dve saccā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dve saccā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Dve saccā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Dve saccā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dve saccā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Samudayasaccaṃ savitakkaṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ avitakkaṃ. Dve saccā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Samudayasaccaṃ savicāraṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ avicāraṃ. Dve saccā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Nirodhasaccaṃ appītikaṃ. Tīṇi saccāni siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Nirodhasaccaṃ na pītisahagataṃ. Tīṇi saccāni siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Nirodhasaccaṃ [M 0.0127] na sukhasahagataṃ. Tīṇi [T 0.0161] saccāni siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Nirodhasaccaṃ na upekkhāsahagataṃ. Tīṇi saccāni siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā.

Two truths are not to be abandoned by vision. Two truths are in some cases to be abandoned by vision, and in some cases not to be abandoned by vision. Two truths are not to be abandoned by development. Two truths are in some cases to be abandoned by development, and in some cases not to be abandoned by development. Two truths do not have a cause to be abandoned by vision. Two truths in some cases have a cause to be abandoned by vision, and in some cases do not have a cause to be abandoned by vision. Two truths do not have a cause to be abandoned by development. Two truths in some cases have a cause to be abandoned by development, and in some cases do not have a cause to be abandoned by development. The truth of the origin is with applied thought. The truth of cessation is without applied thought. Two truths are in some cases with applied thought, and in some cases without applied thought. The truth of the origin is with sustained thought. The truth of cessation is without sustained thought. Two truths are in some cases with sustained thought, and in some cases without sustained thought. The truth of cessation is without rapture. Three truths are in some cases with rapture, and in some cases without rapture. The truth of cessation is not accompanied by rapture. Three truths are in some cases accompanied by rapture, and in some cases not accompanied by rapture. The truth of cessation is not accompanied by pleasure. Three truths are in some cases accompanied by pleasure, and in some cases not accompanied by pleasure. The truth of cessation is not accompanied by equanimity. Three truths are in some cases accompanied by equanimity, and in some cases not accompanied by equanimity.

Samudayasaccaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ. Dve saccā na kāmāvacarā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā kāmāvacaraṃ, siyā na kāmāvacaraṃ. Tīṇi saccāni na rūpāvacarā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā rūpāvacaraṃ, siyā na rūpāvacaraṃ. Tīṇi saccāni na arūpāvacarā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā arūpāvacaraṃ, siyā na arūpāvacaraṃ. Dve saccā pariyāpannā. Dve saccā apariyāpannā. Maggasaccaṃ niyyānikaṃ. Tīṇi saccāni aniyyānikā. Maggasaccaṃ niyataṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ aniyataṃ. Dve saccā siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Dve saccā sauttarā. Dve saccā anuttarā. Samudayasaccaṃ saraṇaṃ. Dve saccā araṇā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā saraṇaṃ, siyā araṇanti.

The truth of origin is of the sense-sphere. Two truths are not of the sense-sphere. The truth of suffering is sometimes of the sense-sphere, and sometimes not of the sense-sphere. Three truths are not of the form-sphere. The truth of suffering is sometimes of the form-sphere, and sometimes not of the form-sphere. Three truths are not of the formless-sphere. The truth of suffering is sometimes of the formless-sphere, and sometimes not of the formless-sphere. Two truths are included. Two truths are not included. The truth of the path leads out. Three truths do not lead out. The truth of the path is fixed. The truth of cessation is not fixed. Two truths are sometimes fixed, and sometimes not fixed. Two truths have a superior. Two truths are unsurpassed. The truth of origin is with defilements. Two truths are without defilements. The truth of suffering is sometimes with defilements, and sometimes without defilements.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Question Section.

Saccavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Truths is concluded.

5. Indriyavibhaṅgo

5. Analysis of the Faculties

1. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

1. Abhidhamma Classification

219. Bāvīsatindriyāni [M 0.0128][P 0.0122][V 0.0137] – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ, saddhindriyaṃ[T 0.0162], vīriyindriyaṃ viriyindriyaṃ (sī. syā.), satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ, anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ.

219. Twenty-two faculties: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the female faculty, the male faculty, the life faculty, the pleasure faculty, the pain faculty, the joy faculty, the displeasure faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, the wisdom faculty, the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown', the faculty of gnosis, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge.

220. Tattha katamaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ? Yaṃ cakkhu catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – idaṃ vuccati “cakkhundriyaṃ”.

220. Herein, what is the eye faculty? That eye which, derived from the four great elements, is the sensitivity... like an empty village... this is called the 'eye faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ sotindriyaṃ…pe… ghānindriyaṃ…pe… jivhindriyaṃ…pe… kāyindriyaṃ? Yo kāyo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – idaṃ vuccati “kāyindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the ear faculty? ... the nose faculty? ... the tongue faculty? ... what is the body faculty? That body which, derived from the four great elements, is the sensitivity... like an empty village... this is called the 'body faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ manindriyaṃ? Ekavidhena manindriyaṃ – phassasampayuttaṃ. Duvidhena manindriyaṃ – atthi sahetukaṃ, atthi ahetukaṃ. Tividhena manindriyaṃ – atthi kusalaṃ, atthi akusalaṃ, atthi abyākataṃ. Catubbidhena manindriyaṃ – atthi kāmāvacaraṃ, atthi rūpāvacaraṃ, atthi arūpāvacaraṃ, atthi apariyāpannaṃ. Pañcavidhena manindriyaṃ – atthi sukhindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi dukkhindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi somanassindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi domanassindriyasampayuttaṃ, atthi upekkhindriyasampayuttaṃ[V 0.0138]. Chabbidhena manindriyaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ. Evaṃ chabbidhena manindriyaṃ.

Herein, what is the mind faculty? In one way, the mind faculty is that which is associated with contact. In two ways, the mind faculty is that with a root and that without a root. In three ways, the mind faculty is wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. In four ways, the mind faculty is that which is of the sense-sphere, that which is of the form-sphere, that which is of the formless-sphere, and that which is supramundane. In five ways, the mind faculty is that associated with the pleasure faculty, that associated with the pain faculty, that associated with the joy faculty, that associated with the displeasure faculty, and that associated with the equanimity faculty. In six ways, the mind faculty is eye-consciousness... up to... mind-consciousness. Thus, in six ways, is the mind faculty.

Sattavidhena manindriyaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Evaṃ sattavidhena manindriyaṃ.

In seven ways, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... up to... body-consciousness, the mind-element, and the mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in seven ways, is the mind faculty.

Aṭṭhavidhena manindriyaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena manindriyaṃ.

In eight ways, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... up to... tongue-consciousness; body-consciousness accompanied by pleasure; body-consciousness accompanied by pain; the mind-element; and the mind-consciousness-element. Thus, in eight ways, is the mind faculty.

Navavidhena [M 0.0129] manindriyaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ navavidhena manindriyaṃ.

In nine ways, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... up to... body-consciousness; the mind-element; and the mind-consciousness-element that is wholesome, that which is unwholesome, and that which is indeterminate. Thus, in nine ways, is the mind faculty.

Dasavidhena manindriyaṃ – cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi sukhasahagataṃ, atthi dukkhasahagataṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ dasavidhena manindriyaṃ…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena manindriyaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “manindriyaṃ”.

In ten ways, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... up to... tongue-consciousness; body-consciousness accompanied by pleasure; body-consciousness accompanied by pain; the mind-element; and the mind-consciousness-element that is wholesome, that which is unwholesome, and that which is indeterminate. Thus, in ten ways, is the mind faculty... Thus, in many ways, is the mind faculty. This is called the 'mind faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ itthindriyaṃ? Yaṃ itthiyā itthiliṅgaṃ itthinimittaṃ itthikuttaṃ itthākappo itthattaṃ itthibhāvo – idaṃ vuccati “itthindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the female faculty? Whatever in a female is the female characteristic, the female sign, the female conduct, the female deportment, the state of being female, the nature of being female—this is called the 'female faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ purisindriyaṃ? Yaṃ purisassa purisaliṅgaṃ purisanimittaṃ purisakuttaṃ purisākappo [P 0.0123] purisattaṃ purisabhāvo – idaṃ vuccati “purisindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the male faculty? Whatever in a male is the male characteristic, the male sign, the male conduct, the male deportment, the state of being male, the nature of being male—this is called the 'male faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ? Jīvitindriyaṃ duvidhena – atthi rūpajīvitindriyaṃ, atthi arūpajīvitindriyaṃ.

Herein, what is the life faculty? The life faculty is twofold: there is the material life faculty and the immaterial life faculty.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpajīvitindriyaṃ? Yo tesaṃ rūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ āyu ṭhiti yapanā yāpanā iriyanā vattanā pālanā jīvitaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “rūpajīvitindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the material life faculty? Of those material phenomena, whatever is the life-span, duration, sustenance, subsistence, continuance, occurrence, preservation, life, and life faculty—this is called the 'material life faculty'.

Tattha [V 0.0139] katamaṃ arūpajīvitindriyaṃ? Yo tesaṃ arūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ [T 0.0163] āyu ṭhiti yapanā yāpanā iriyanā vattanā pālanā jīvitaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “arūpajīvatindriyaṃ”. Idaṃ vuccati “jīvitindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the immaterial life faculty? Of those immaterial phenomena, whatever is the life-span, duration, sustenance, subsistence, continuance, occurrence, preservation, life, and life faculty—this is called the 'immaterial life faculty'. This is called the 'life faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ sukhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ sātaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “sukhindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the pleasure faculty? Whatever is bodily pleasantness, bodily pleasure; the pleasant, agreeable feeling born of bodily contact; the pleasant, agreeable sensation born of bodily contact—this is called the 'pleasure faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the pain faculty? Whatever is bodily unpleasantness, bodily pain; the unpleasant, painful feeling born of bodily contact; the unpleasant, painful sensation born of bodily contact—this is called the 'pain faculty'.

Tattha katamaṃ somanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “somanassindriyaṃ”.

Herein, what is the joy faculty? Whatever is mental pleasantness, mental pleasure; the pleasant, agreeable feeling born of mental contact; the pleasant, agreeable sensation born of mental contact—this is called the 'joy faculty'.

Tattha [M 0.0130] katamaṃ domanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of displeasure? Whatever mental unpleasantness, mental suffering, unpleasant painful feeling born of mind-contact, or unpleasant painful sensation born of mind-contact there is—this is called the faculty of displeasure.

Tattha katamaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “upekkhindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of equanimity? Whatever mental neither-pleasant-nor-unpleasantness, whatever neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact, whatever neither-painful-nor-pleasant sensation born of mind-contact there is—this is called the faculty of equanimity.

Tattha katamaṃ saddhindriyaṃ? Yā saddhā saddahanā okappanā abhippasādo saddhā saddhindriyaṃ saddhābalaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “saddhindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of faith? Whatever faith, believing, conviction, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith, the power of faith there is—this is called the faculty of faith.

Tattha katamaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho nikkamo parakkamo uyyāmo vāyāmo ussāho ussoḷhī thāmo ṭhiti asithilaparakkamatā anikkhittachandatā anikkhittadhuratā dhurasampaggāho [T 0.0164] vīriyaṃ [P 0.0124] vīriyindriyaṃ vīriyabalaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “vīriyindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of energy? Whatever mental arousal of energy, exertion, striving, endeavor, effort, enthusiasm, extreme exertion, strength, steadfastness, unslackening persistence, not laying down the desire, not laying down the burden, the taking up of the burden, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy there is—this is called the faculty of energy.

Tattha [V 0.0140] katamaṃ satindriyaṃ? Yā sati anussati paṭissati sati saraṇatā dhāraṇatā apilāpanatā asammussanatā sati satindriyaṃ satibalaṃ sammāsati – idaṃ vuccati “satindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection, repeated mindfulness, the state of remembering, retention, non-superficiality, non-forgetfulness, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness there is—this is called the faculty of mindfulness.

Tattha katamaṃ samādhindriyaṃ? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti avaṭṭhiti avisāhāro avikkhepo avisāhaṭamānasatā samatho samādhindriyaṃ samādhibalaṃ sammāsamādhi – idaṃ vuccati “samādhindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of concentration? Whatever stability of mind, steadiness, composure, non-distraction, non-wavering, a state of undistracted mind, tranquility, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration there is—this is called the faculty of concentration.

Tattha katamaṃ paññindriyaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “paññindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of wisdom? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view there is—this is called the faculty of wisdom.

Tattha katamaṃ anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ? Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ anaññātānaṃ adiṭṭhānaṃ appattānaṃ aviditānaṃ asacchikatānaṃ sacchikiriyāya paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of ‘I shall know the unknown’? For the sake of realizing those phenomena that are unknown, unseen, unattained, uncomprehended, and unrealized, whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, which is a path factor and is included in the path, there is—this is called the faculty of ‘I shall know the unknown’.

Tattha katamaṃ aññindriyaṃ? Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ ñātānaṃ diṭṭhānaṃ pattānaṃ viditānaṃ sacchikatānaṃ sacchikiriyāya paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati aññindriyaṃ.

Among these, what is the faculty of final knowledge? For the sake of realizing those phenomena that are known, seen, attained, comprehended, and realized, whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, which is a path factor and is included in the path, there is—this is called the faculty of final knowledge.

Tattha [M 0.0131] katamaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ? Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aññātāvīnaṃ diṭṭhānaṃ pattānaṃ viditānaṃ sacchikatānaṃ sacchikiriyāya paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ [T 0.0165] vuccati “aññātāvindriyaṃ”.

Among these, what is the faculty of one who has final knowledge? For the sake of realizing those phenomena that have been known, seen, attained, comprehended, and realized, whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, which is a path factor and is included in the path, there is—this is called the faculty of one who has final knowledge.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition.

2. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

2. The Section of Questions

221. Bāvīsatindriyāni [V 0.0141] – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ, saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ[P 0.0125], anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ.

221. The twenty-two faculties are: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the female faculty, the male faculty, the life faculty, the pleasure faculty, the pain faculty, the joy faculty, the displeasure faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, the wisdom faculty, the faculty of ‘I shall know the unknown,’ the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge.

222. Bāvīsatīnaṃ indriyānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

222. Of the twenty-two faculties, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, how many are indeterminate… how many are with defilements, how many are without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. Triads

223. Dasindriyā abyākatā. Domanassindriyaṃ akusalaṃ. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ kusalaṃ. Cattārindriyā siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Cha indriyā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā.

223. Ten faculties are indeterminate. The faculty of displeasure is unwholesome. The faculty of ‘I shall know the unknown’ is wholesome. Four faculties are sometimes wholesome, sometimes indeterminate. Six faculties are sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, sometimes indeterminate.

Dvādasindriyā na vattabbā – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tipi. Cha indriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Tīṇindriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “sukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi[T 0.0166], “dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi, “adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutta”ntipi.

Twelve faculties should not be described as ‘associated with pleasant feeling,’ nor as ‘associated with painful feeling,’ nor as ‘associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Six faculties are sometimes associated with pleasant feeling, sometimes associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Three faculties are sometimes associated with pleasant feeling, sometimes associated with painful feeling, sometimes associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The life faculty is sometimes associated with pleasant feeling, sometimes associated with painful feeling, sometimes associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; and sometimes it should not be described as ‘associated with pleasant feeling,’ nor as ‘associated with painful feeling,’ nor as ‘associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’

Sattindriyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Tīṇindriyā vipākā. Dvindriyā vipākadhammadhammā. Aññindriyaṃ siyā vipākaṃ, siyā vipākadhammadhammaṃ. Navindriyā siyā [M 0.0132] vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Navindriyā upādinnupādāniyā[V 0.0142]. Domanassindriyaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Tīṇindriyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Navindriyā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

Seven faculties are neither resultant nor result-producing. Three faculties are resultant. Two faculties are result-producing. The faculty of final knowledge is sometimes resultant, sometimes result-producing. Nine faculties are sometimes resultant, sometimes result-producing, sometimes neither resultant nor result-producing. Nine faculties are produced by kamma and are objects of clinging. The faculty of displeasure is not produced by kamma but is an object of clinging. Three faculties are neither produced by kamma nor are objects of clinging. Nine faculties are sometimes produced by kamma and are objects of clinging; sometimes not produced by kamma but are objects of clinging; sometimes neither produced by kamma nor are objects of clinging.

Navindriyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Domanassindriyaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikaṃ. Tīṇindriyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Tīṇindriyā siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Cha indriyā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Navindriyā avitakkaavicārā. Domanassindriyaṃ savitakkasavicāraṃ. Upekkhindriyaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Ekādasindriyā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā.

Nine faculties are undefiled but are objects for defilement. The displeasure faculty is defiled and is an object for defilement. Three faculties are undefiled and are not objects for defilement. Three faculties are sometimes undefiled but are objects for defilement, and sometimes are undefiled and not objects for defilement. Six faculties are sometimes defiled and are objects for defilement; sometimes undefiled but are objects for defilement; and sometimes undefiled and are not objects for defilement. Nine faculties are without applied thought and without sustained thought. The displeasure faculty is with applied thought and with sustained thought. The equanimity faculty is sometimes with applied thought and with sustained thought, sometimes without applied thought and without sustained thought. Eleven faculties are sometimes with applied thought and with sustained thought; sometimes without applied thought but with sustained thought only; sometimes without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Ekādasindriyā na vattabbā – “pītisahagatā”tipi, “sukhasahagatā”tipi, “upekkhāsahagatā”tipi. Somanassindriyaṃ siyā pītisahagataṃ na sukhasahagataṃ na upekkhāsahagataṃ, siyā [P 0.0126] na vattabbaṃ – “pītisahagata”nti. Cha indriyā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Cattārindriyā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā[T 0.0167], siyā na vattabbā – “pītisahagatā”tipi, “sukhasahagatā”tipi, “upekkhāsahagatā”tipi.

Eleven faculties should not be described as 'accompanied by rapture,' nor as 'accompanied by pleasure,' nor as 'accompanied by equanimity.' The joy faculty is sometimes accompanied by rapture, but not by pleasure nor by equanimity; and sometimes it should not be described as 'accompanied by rapture.' Six faculties are sometimes accompanied by rapture, sometimes accompanied by pleasure, sometimes accompanied by equanimity. Four faculties are sometimes accompanied by rapture, sometimes accompanied by pleasure, sometimes accompanied by equanimity; and sometimes they should not be described as 'accompanied by rapture,' nor as 'accompanied by pleasure,' nor as 'accompanied by equanimity.'

Pannarasindriyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Pannarasindriyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.

Fifteen faculties are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. The displeasure faculty is sometimes to be abandoned by vision, sometimes by development. Six faculties are sometimes to be abandoned by vision, sometimes by development, and sometimes neither by vision nor by development. Fifteen faculties have a root that is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. The displeasure faculty sometimes has a root that is to be abandoned by vision, sometimes by development. Six faculties sometimes have a root to be abandoned by vision, sometimes have a root to be abandoned by development, and sometimes have a root to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development.

Dasindriyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Domanassindriyaṃ ācayagāmi. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ apacayagāmi. Aññindriyaṃ siyā apacayagāmi, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmi[V 0.0143]. Navindriyā siyā ācayagāmino, siyā [M 0.0133] apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dasindriyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dvindriyā sekkhā. Aññātāvindriyaṃ asekkhaṃ. Navindriyā siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā.

Ten faculties lead neither to accumulation nor to diminution. The displeasure faculty leads to accumulation. The faculty of 'I shall know what is not yet known' leads to diminution. The faculty of final knowledge sometimes leads to diminution, and sometimes leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution. Nine faculties sometimes lead to accumulation, sometimes lead to diminution, and sometimes lead neither to accumulation nor to diminution. Ten faculties are neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training. Two faculties are of a trainee. The faculty of one who has final knowledge is of one beyond training. Nine faculties are sometimes of a trainee, sometimes of one beyond training, and sometimes neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training.

Dasindriyā parittā. Tīṇindriyā appamāṇā. Navindriyā siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Dvindriyā parittārammaṇā. Tīṇindriyā appamāṇārammaṇā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ siyā mahaggatārammaṇaṃ, na appamāṇārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “parittārammaṇa”ntipi[T 0.0168], “mahaggatārammaṇa”nti pi. Navindriyā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “parittārammaṇā”tipi, “mahaggatārammaṇā”tipi, “appamāṇārammaṇā”tipi.

Ten faculties are limited. Three faculties are immeasurable. Nine faculties may be limited, or may be sublime, or may be immeasurable. Seven faculties are without an object. Two faculties have a limited object. Three faculties have an immeasurable object. The displeasure faculty may have a limited object or a sublime object, but not an immeasurable object, or it should not be described as 'having a limited object' or 'having a sublime object.' Nine faculties may have a limited object, or a sublime object, or an immeasurable object, or they should not be described as 'having a limited object,' nor as 'having a sublime object,' nor as 'having an immeasurable object.'

Navindriyā majjhimā. Domanassindriyaṃ hīnaṃ. Tīṇindriyā paṇītā. Tīṇindriyā siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Cha indriyā siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Dasindriyā aniyatā. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ sammattaniyataṃ. Cattārindriyā siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Domanassindriyaṃ siyā micchattaniyataṃ, siyā aniyataṃ[P 0.0127]. Cha indriyā siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Cattārindriyā na vattabbā – “maggārammaṇā”tipi, “maggahetukā”tipi, “maggādhipatino”tipi. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ na maggārammaṇaṃ, siyā maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “maggahetuka”ntipi, “maggādhipatī”tipi. Aññindriyaṃ na maggārammaṇaṃ, siyā maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ – “maggahetuka”ntipi, “maggādhipatī”tipi. Navindriyā siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – “maggārammaṇā”tipi, “maggahetukā”tipi, “maggādhipatino”tipi.

Nine faculties are middling. The displeasure faculty is inferior. Three faculties are superior. Three faculties may be middling or superior. Six faculties may be inferior, or middling, or superior. Ten faculties are indeterminate. The faculty of 'I shall know what is not yet known' is rightly determined. Four faculties may be rightly determined or indeterminate. The displeasure faculty may be wrongly determined or indeterminate. Six faculties may be wrongly determined, or rightly determined, or indeterminate. Seven faculties are without an object. Four faculties should not be described as 'with the path as object,' nor as 'with the path as cause,' nor as 'with the path as dominant condition.' The faculty of 'I shall know what is not yet known' does not have the path as object; it may have the path as cause, or the path as dominant condition, or it should not be described as 'with the path as cause' or 'with the path as dominant condition.' The faculty of final knowledge does not have the path as object; it may have the path as cause, or the path as dominant condition, or it should not be described as 'with the path as cause' or 'with the path as dominant condition.' Nine faculties may have the path as object, or the path as cause, or the path as dominant condition, or they should not be described as 'with the path as object,' nor as 'with the path as cause,' nor as 'with the path as dominant condition.'

Dasindriyā siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino, na vattabbā – “anuppannā”ti. Dvindriyā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā – “uppādino”ti. Dasindriyā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino[T 0.0169]; siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Sattindriyā [V 0.0144] anārammaṇā. Dvindriyā paccuppannārammaṇā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “atītārammaṇā”tipi, “anāgatārammaṇā”tipi[M 0.0134], “paccuppannārammaṇā”tipi. Dasindriyā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “atītārammaṇā”tipi, “anāgatārammaṇā”tipi, “paccuppannārammaṇā”tipi; siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Tīṇindriyā bahiddhārammaṇā. Cattārindriyā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, aṭṭhindriyā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “ajjhattārammaṇā”tipi, “bahiddhārammaṇā”tipi, “ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā”tipi. Pañcindriyā anidassanasappaṭighā. Sattarasindriyā anidassanaappaṭighā.

Ten faculties may have arisen, or are bound to arise; it should not be said of them that they are 'not arisen.' Two faculties may have arisen, or may not have arisen; it should not be said of them that they are 'bound to arise.' Ten faculties may have arisen, or may not have arisen, or are bound to arise; they may be past, or future, or present. Seven faculties are without an object. Two faculties have a present object. It should not be said of three faculties that they have 'a past object,' nor 'a future object,' nor 'a present object.' Ten faculties may have a past object, or may have a future object, or may have a present object, or it may be that it should not be said of them that they have 'a past object,' nor 'a future object,' nor 'a present object'; they may be internal, or external, or internal-external. Seven faculties are without an object. Three faculties have an external object. Four faculties may have an internal object, or an external object, or an internal-external object. Eight faculties may have an internal object, or an external object, or an internal-external object, or it may be that it should not be said of them that they have 'an internal object,' nor 'an external object,' nor 'an internal-external object.' Five faculties are invisible and with impingement. Seventeen faculties are invisible and without impingement.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

224. Cattārindriyā hetū. Aṭṭhārasindriyā na hetū. Sattindriyā sahetukā. Navindriyā ahetukā. Cha indriyā siyā sahetukā, siyā ahetukā. Sattindriyā hetusampayuttā. Navindriyā hetuvippayuttā. Cha indriyā siyā hetusampayuttā, siyā hetuvippayuttā. Cattārindriyā hetū ceva sahetukā ca. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva sahetukā cā”tipi, “sahetukā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva sahetukā cā”ti. Sahetukā [T 0.0170] ceva na ca hetū. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva sahetukā cā”ti, siyā sahetukā ceva na ca hetū, siyā na vattabbā – “sahetukā ceva na ca hetū”ti.

224. Four faculties are roots. Eighteen faculties are not roots. Seven faculties are with roots. Nine faculties are without roots. Six faculties may be with roots or without roots. Seven faculties are associated with roots. Nine faculties are dissociated from roots. Six faculties may be associated with roots or dissociated from roots. Four faculties are both roots and with roots. It should not be said of nine faculties that they are 'both roots and with roots,' nor 'with roots but not roots.' It should not be said of three faculties that they are 'both roots and with roots'; they are 'with roots but not roots.' It should not be said of six faculties that they are 'both roots and with roots'; some may be 'with roots but not roots,' and for others it may be that it should not be said that they are 'with roots but not roots.'

Cattārindriyā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca[P 0.0128]. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”tipi, “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”tipi. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”ti, “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”ti, siyā hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū, siyā na vattabbā – “hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū”ti.

Four faculties are both roots and associated with roots. It should not be said of nine faculties that they are 'both roots and associated with roots,' nor 'associated with roots but not roots.' It should not be said of three faculties that they are 'both roots and associated with roots'; they are 'associated with roots but not roots.' It should not be said of six faculties that they are 'both roots and associated with roots'; some may be 'associated with roots but not roots,' and for others it may be that it should not be said that they are 'associated with roots but not roots.'

Navindriyā [V 0.0145] na hetū ahetukā. Tīṇindriyā na hetū sahetukā. Cattārindriyā na vattabbā – “na hetū sahetukā”tipi, “na hetū ahetukā”tipi[M 0.0135]. Cha indriyā siyā na hetū sahetukā, siyā na hetū ahetukā.

Nine faculties are not roots and are without roots. Three faculties are not roots but are with roots. It should not be said of four faculties that they are 'not roots but with roots,' nor 'not roots and without roots.' Six faculties may be not roots but with roots, or may be not roots and without roots.

Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Pañcindriyā sappaṭighā. Sattarasindriyā appaṭighā. Sattindriyā rūpā. Cuddasindriyā arūpā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā rūpaṃ, siyā arūpaṃ. Dasindriyā lokiyā. Tīṇindriyā lokuttarā. Navindriyā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā; kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

They are with conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. Five faculties are with impingement. Seventeen faculties are without impingement. Seven faculties are material. Fourteen faculties are immaterial. The life faculty may be material or immaterial. Ten faculties are mundane. Three faculties are supramundane. Nine faculties may be mundane or supramundane. They are knowable by some consciousness, and not knowable by some consciousness.

No āsavā. Dasindriyā sāsavā. Tīṇindriyā anāsavā. Navindriyā siyā sāsavā, siyā anāsavā. Pannarasindriyā āsavavippayuttā. Domanassindriyaṃ āsavasampayuttaṃ. Cha indriyā [T 0.0171] siyā āsavasampayuttā, siyā āsavavippayuttā. Dasindriyā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”ti, “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā”. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”tipi, “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā”tipi. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”ti, siyā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, siyā na vattabbā – “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā”ti.

They are not taints. Ten faculties are subject to the taints. Three faculties are not subject to the taints. Nine faculties may be subject to the taints or not subject to the taints. Fifteen faculties are dissociated from taints. The faculty of displeasure is associated with taints. Six faculties may be associated with taints or dissociated from taints. It should not be said of ten faculties that they are 'both taints and subject to taints'; they are 'subject to taints but not taints.' It should not be said of three faculties that they are 'both taints and subject to taints,' nor 'subject to taints but not taints.' It should not be said of nine faculties that they are 'both taints and subject to taints'; some may be 'subject to taints but not taints,' and for others it may be that it should not be said that they are 'subject to taints but not taints.'

Pannarasindriyā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā”tipi. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “āsavo ceva āsavasampayuttañcā”ti, “āsavasampayuttañceva no ca āsavo”. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā, siyā na vattabbā – “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā”ti. Navindriyā āsavavippayuttasāsavā. Tīṇindriyā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “āsavavippayuttasāsava”ntipi, “āsavavippayuttaanāsava”ntipi. Tīṇindriyā siyā āsavavippayuttasāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā. Cha indriyā siyā āsavavippayuttasāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttaanāsavā, siyā na vattabbā – “āsavavippayuttasāsavā”tipi, “āsavavippayuttaanāsavā”tipi.
