It should not be said of fifteen faculties that they are 'both taints and associated with taints,' nor 'associated with taints but not taints.' It should not be said of the faculty of displeasure that it is 'both a taint and associated with taints'; it is 'associated with taints but not a taint.' It should not be said of six faculties that they are 'both taints and associated with taints'; some may be 'associated with taints but not taints,' and for others it may be that it should not be said that they are 'associated with taints but not taints.' Nine faculties are dissociated from taints but subject to the taints. Three faculties are dissociated from taints and not subject to the taints. It should not be said of the faculty of displeasure that it is 'dissociated from taints but subject to the taints,' nor 'dissociated from taints and not subject to the taints.' Three faculties may be dissociated from taints but subject to the taints, or dissociated from taints and not subject to the taints. Six faculties may be dissociated from taints but subject to the taints, or dissociated from taints and not subject to the taints, or it may be that it should not be said of them that they are 'dissociated from taints but subject to the taints,' nor 'dissociated from taints and not subject to the taints.'

No [V 0.0146] saṃyojanā. Dasindriyā saṃyojaniyā. Tīṇindriyā asaṃyojaniyā. Navindriyā siyā saṃyojaniyā, siyā asaṃyojaniyā. Pannarasindriyā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Domanassindriyaṃ saṃyojanasampayuttaṃ[T 0.0172]. Cha [M 0.0136] indriyā siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā[P 0.0129], siyā saṃyojanavippayuttā. Dasindriyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cā”ti, saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cā”tipi, “saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”tipi. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojaniyā cā”ti, siyā saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojaniyā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”ti.

They are not fetters. Ten faculties are objects of the fetters. Three faculties are not objects of the fetters. In some cases, nine faculties are objects of the fetters; in other cases, they are not objects of the fetters. Fifteen faculties are dissociated from fetters. The faculty of displeasure is associated with fetters. In some cases, six faculties are associated with fetters; in other cases, they are dissociated from fetters. Ten faculties should not be said to be 'both fetters and objects of the fetters'; they are 'objects of the fetters but not fetters'. Three faculties should not be said to be 'both fetters and objects of the fetters', nor 'objects of the fetters but not fetters'. Nine faculties should not be said to be 'both fetters and objects of the fetters'; in some cases, they are 'objects of the fetters but not fetters', and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'objects of the fetters but not fetters'.

Pannarasindriyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”tipi, “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”tipi. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayuttañcā”ti, saṃyojanasampayuttañceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanasampayuttā ceva no ca saṃyojanā”ti.

Fifteen faculties should not be said to be 'both fetters and associated with fetters', nor 'associated with fetters but not fetters'. The faculty of displeasure should not be said to be 'both a fetter and associated with fetters'; it is 'associated with fetters but not a fetter'. Six faculties should not be said to be 'both fetters and associated with fetters'; in some cases, they are 'associated with fetters but not fetters', and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'associated with fetters but not fetters'.

Navindriyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā. Tīṇindriyā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniya”ntipi, “saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniya”ntipi. Tīṇindriyā siyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā. Cha indriyā siyā saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā, siyā saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyā”tipi, “saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyā”tipi[T 0.0173].

Nine faculties are dissociated from fetters but are objects of the fetters. Three faculties are dissociated from fetters and are not objects of the fetters. The faculty of displeasure should not be said to be 'dissociated from fetters but an object of the fetters', nor 'dissociated from fetters and not an object of the fetters'. In some cases, three faculties are dissociated from fetters but are objects of the fetters; in other cases, they are dissociated from fetters and are not objects of the fetters. In some cases, six faculties are dissociated from fetters but are objects of the fetters; in other cases, they are dissociated from fetters and are not objects of the fetters; and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'dissociated from fetters but are objects of the fetters', nor that they are 'dissociated from fetters and are not objects of the fetters'.

No ganthā. Dasindriyā ganthaniyā. Tīṇindriyā aganthaniyā. Navindriyā siyā ganthaniyā, siyā aganthaniyā. Pannarasindriyā ganthavippayuttā. Domanassindriyaṃ ganthasampayuttaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā ganthasampayuttā, siyā ganthavippayuttā. Dasindriyā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthaniyā cā”ti, ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthaniyā cā”tipi, “ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā”tipi. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “ganthā [V 0.0147] ceva ganthaniyā cā”ti, siyā ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthaniyā ceva no ca ganthā”ti.

They are not knots. Ten faculties are objects of the knots. Three faculties are not objects of the knots. In some cases, nine faculties are objects of the knots; in other cases, they are not objects of the knots. Fifteen faculties are dissociated from knots. The faculty of displeasure is associated with knots. In some cases, six faculties are associated with knots; in other cases, they are dissociated from knots. Ten faculties should not be said to be 'both knots and objects of the knots'; they are 'objects of the knots but not knots'. Three faculties should not be said to be 'both knots and objects of the knots', nor 'objects of the knots but not knots'. Nine faculties should not be said to be 'both knots and objects of the knots'; in some cases, they are 'objects of the knots but not knots', and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'objects of the knots but not knots'.

Pannarasindriyā [M 0.0137] na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā cā”tipi, “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā”tipi. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “gantho ceva ganthasampayutta”ñcāti, ganthasampayuttañceva no ca gantho. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā, siyā na vattabbā – “ganthasampayuttā ceva no ca ganthā”ti.

Fifteen faculties should not be said to be 'both knots and associated with knots', nor 'associated with knots but not knots'. The faculty of displeasure should not be said to be 'both a knot and associated with knots'; it is 'associated with knots but not a knot'. Six faculties should not be said to be 'both knots and associated with knots'; in some cases, they are 'associated with knots but not knots', and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'associated with knots but not knots'.

Navindriyā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā. Tīṇindriyā ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā[P 0.0130]. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “ganthavippayuttaganthaniya”ntipi, “ganthavippayuttaaganthaniya”ntipi. Tīṇindriyā siyā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā, siyā ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā. Cha indriyā siyā ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā, siyā ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā, siyā na vattabbā [T 0.0174] – “ganthavippayuttaganthaniyā”tipi, “ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyā”tipi.

Nine faculties are dissociated from knots but are objects of the knots. Three faculties are dissociated from knots and are not objects of the knots. The faculty of displeasure should not be said to be 'dissociated from knots but an object of the knots', nor 'dissociated from knots and not an object of the knots'. In some cases, three faculties are dissociated from knots but are objects of the knots; in other cases, they are dissociated from knots and are not objects of the knots. In some cases, six faculties are dissociated from knots but are objects of the knots; in other cases, they are dissociated from knots and are not objects of the knots; and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'dissociated from knots but are objects of the knots', nor that they are 'dissociated from knots and are not objects of the knots'.

No oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā. Dasindriyā nīvaraṇiyā. Tīṇindriyā anīvaraṇiyā. Navindriyā siyā nīvaraṇiyā, siyā anīvaraṇiyā. Pannarasindriyā nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Domanassindriyaṃ nīvaraṇasampayuttaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttā. Dasindriyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”ti, nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”tipi. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇiyā cā”ti, siyā nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇiyā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”ti.

Not floods... and so on... not yokes... and so on... not hindrances. Ten faculties are objects of the hindrances. Three faculties are not objects of the hindrances. In some cases, nine faculties are objects of the hindrances; in other cases, they are not objects of the hindrances. Fifteen faculties are dissociated from the hindrances. The faculty of displeasure is associated with the hindrances. In some cases, six faculties are associated with the hindrances; in other cases, they are dissociated from the hindrances. Ten faculties should not be said to be 'both hindrances and objects of the hindrances'; they are 'objects of the hindrances but not hindrances'. Three faculties should not be said to be 'both hindrances and objects of the hindrances', nor 'objects of the hindrances but not hindrances'. Nine faculties should not be said to be 'both hindrances and objects of the hindrances'; in some cases, they are 'objects of the hindrances but not hindrances', and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'objects of the hindrances but not hindrances'.

Pannarasindriyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā cā”tipi, “nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”tipi. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayuttañcā”ti, nīvaraṇasampayuttañceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ. Cha indriyā na [V 0.0148] vattabbā – “nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva no ca nīvaraṇā”ti.

Fifteen faculties should not be said to be 'both hindrances and associated with hindrances', nor 'associated with hindrances but not hindrances'. The faculty of displeasure should not be said to be 'both a hindrance and associated with hindrances'; it is 'associated with hindrances but not a hindrance'. Six faculties should not be said to be 'both hindrances and associated with hindrances'; in some cases, they are 'associated with hindrances but not hindrances', and in other cases, it should not be said that they are 'associated with hindrances but not hindrances'.

Navindriyā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā. Tīṇindriyā nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiya”ntipi, “nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiya”ntipi. Tīṇindriyā siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā, siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā[T 0.0175]. Cha indriyā siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā[M 0.0138], siyā nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā, siyā na vattabbā – “nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyā”tipi, “nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyā”tipi.

Nine faculties are dissociated from the hindrances but are objects of the hindrances. Three faculties are dissociated from the hindrances and are not objects of the hindrances. The faculty of displeasure should not be said to be 'dissociated from the hindrances but an object of the hindrances,' nor 'dissociated from the hindrances and not an object of the hindrances.' Three faculties are in some cases dissociated from the hindrances but are objects of the hindrances, and in other cases are dissociated from the hindrances and are not objects of the hindrances. Six faculties are in some cases dissociated from the hindrances but are objects of the hindrances; in other cases are dissociated from the hindrances and are not objects of the hindrances; and in yet other cases it should not be said of them that they are 'dissociated from the hindrances but an object of the hindrances,' nor 'dissociated from the hindrances and not an object of the hindrances.'

No parāmāsā. Dasindriyā parāmaṭṭhā. Tīṇindriyā aparāmaṭṭhā. Navindriyā siyā parāmaṭṭhā, siyā aparāmaṭṭhā. Soḷasindriyā parāmāsavippayuttā. Cha indriyā siyā parāmāsasampayuttā, siyā parāmāsavippayuttā. Dasindriyā na vattabbā – “parāmāsā ceva parāmaṭṭhā cā”ti, parāmaṭṭhā ceva no ca parāmāsā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “parāmāsā ceva parāmaṭṭhā [P 0.0131] cā”tipi, “parāmaṭṭhā ceva no ca parāmāsā”tipi. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “parāmāsā ceva parāmaṭṭhā cā”ti, siyā parāmaṭṭhā ceva no ca parāmāsā, siyā na vattabbā – “parāmaṭṭhā ceva no ca parāmāsā”ti. Dasindriyā parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā. Tīṇindriyā parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā. Tīṇindriyā siyā parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā, siyā parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā. Cha indriyā siyā parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā, siyā parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā, siyā na vattabbā – “parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhā”tipi, “parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭhā”tipi.

The faculties are not misconceptions. Ten faculties are objects of misconception. Three faculties are not objects of misconception. Nine faculties are in some cases objects of misconception, and in other cases are not objects of misconception. Sixteen faculties are dissociated from misconception. Six faculties are in some cases associated with misconception, and in other cases are dissociated from misconception. Regarding the ten faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both misconceptions and objects of misconception'; they are objects of misconception but not misconceptions. Regarding the three faculties, it should not be said of them that they are 'both misconceptions and objects of misconception,' nor that they are 'objects of misconception but not misconceptions.' Regarding the nine faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both misconceptions and objects of misconception'; in some cases they are 'objects of misconception but not misconceptions,' and in other cases it should not be said of them that they are 'objects of misconception but not misconceptions.' Ten faculties are dissociated from misconception but are objects of misconception. Three faculties are dissociated from misconception and are not objects of misconception. Three faculties are in some cases dissociated from misconception but are objects of misconception, and in other cases are dissociated from misconception and are not objects of misconception. Six faculties are in some cases dissociated from misconception but are objects of misconception; in other cases are dissociated from misconception and are not objects of misconception; and in yet other cases it should not be said of them that they are 'dissociated from misconception but are objects of misconception,' nor that they are 'dissociated from misconception and are not objects of misconception.'

Sattindriyā anārammaṇā. Cuddasindriyā sārammaṇā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā sārammaṇaṃ, siyā anārammaṇaṃ. Ekavīsatindriyā no [T 0.0176] cittā. Manindriyaṃ cittaṃ. Terasindriyā cetasikā. Aṭṭhindriyā acetasikā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cetasikaṃ, siyā acetasikaṃ. Terasindriyā cittasampayuttā. Sattindriyā cittavippayuttā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittasampayuttaṃ, siyā cittavippayuttaṃ. Manindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “cittena sampayutta”ntipi, “cittena vippayutta”ntipi.

Seven faculties are without an object. Fourteen faculties are with an object. The life faculty may be with an object, or may be without an object. Twenty-one faculties are not mind. The mind-faculty is mind. Thirteen faculties are mental factors. Eight faculties are not mental factors. The life faculty may be a mental factor, or may not be a mental factor. Thirteen faculties are associated with mind. Seven faculties are dissociated from mind. The life faculty may be associated with mind, or may be dissociated from mind. Regarding the mind-faculty, it should not be said that it is 'associated with mind,' nor that it is 'dissociated from mind.'

Terasindriyā [V 0.0149] cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Sattindriyā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ, siyā cittavisaṃsaṭṭhaṃ. Manindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “cittena saṃsaṭṭha”ntipi, “cittena visaṃsaṭṭha”ntipi. Terasindriyā cittasamuṭṭhānā. Aṭṭhindriyā no cittasamuṭṭhānā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ, siyā no cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ.

Thirteen faculties are conjoined with mind. Seven faculties are disjoined from mind. The life faculty may be conjoined with mind, or may be disjoined from mind. Regarding the mind-faculty, it should not be said that it is 'conjoined with mind,' nor that it is 'disjoined from mind.' Thirteen faculties are mind-originated. Eight faculties are not mind-originated. The life faculty may be mind-originated, or may not be mind-originated.

Terasindriyā cittasahabhuno. Aṭṭhindriyā no cittasahabhuno. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittasahabhū, siyā no cittasahabhū. Terasindriyā cittānuparivattino. Aṭṭhindriyā no cittānuparivattino. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittānuparivatti, siyā no cittānuparivatti.

Thirteen faculties are co-nascent with mind. Eight faculties are not co-nascent with mind. The life faculty may be co-nascent with mind, or may not be co-nascent with mind. Thirteen faculties conform to mind. Eight faculties do not conform to mind. The life faculty may conform to mind, or may not conform to mind.

Terasindriyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Aṭṭhindriyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānaṃ, siyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Terasindriyā [M 0.0139] cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Aṭṭhindriyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhū, siyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhū. Terasindriyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Aṭṭhindriyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivatti[T 0.0177], siyā no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivatti. Cha indriyā ajjhattikā. Soḷasindriyā bāhirā.

Thirteen faculties are conjoined with and originate from mind. Eight faculties are neither conjoined with nor originate from mind. The life faculty may be conjoined with and originate from mind, or may be neither conjoined with nor originate from mind. Thirteen faculties are conjoined with, originate from, and are co-nascent with mind. Eight faculties are neither conjoined with, nor originate from, nor are co-nascent with mind. The life faculty may be conjoined with, originate from, and be co-nascent with mind; or may be neither conjoined with, nor originate from, nor be co-nascent with mind. Thirteen faculties are conjoined with, originate from, and conform to mind. Eight faculties are neither conjoined with, nor originate from, nor conform to mind. The life faculty may be conjoined with, originate from, and conform to mind; or may be neither conjoined with, nor originate from, nor conform to mind. Six faculties are internal. Sixteen faculties are external.

Sattindriyā [P 0.0132] upādā. Cuddasindriyā no upādā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā upādā, siyā no upādā. Navindriyā upādinnā. Cattārindriyā anupādinnā. Navindriyā siyā upādinnā, siyā anupādinnā. No upādānā. Dasindriyā upādāniyā. Tīṇindriyā anupādāniyā. Navindriyā siyā upādāniyā, siyā anupādāniyā. Soḷasindriyā upādānavippayuttā. Cha indriyā siyā upādānasampayuttā, siyā upādānavippayuttā. Dasindriyā na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādāniyā cā”ti, upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādāniyā cā”tipi, “upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā”tipi. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādāniyā cā”ti, siyā upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā. Dasindriyā siyā upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā, siyā na vattabbā – “upādāniyā ceva no ca upādānā”ti.

Seven faculties are derived. Fourteen faculties are not derived. The life faculty may be derived, or may not be derived. Nine faculties are produced by kamma. Four faculties are not produced by kamma. Nine faculties may be produced by kamma, or may not be produced by kamma. The faculties are not clingings. Ten faculties are liable to clinging. Three faculties are not liable to clinging. Nine faculties are in some cases liable to clinging, and in other cases are not liable to clinging. Sixteen faculties are dissociated from clinging. Six faculties are in some cases associated with clinging, and in other cases are dissociated from clinging. Regarding the ten faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both clingings and liable to clinging'; they are liable to clinging but not clingings. Regarding the three faculties, it should not be said of them that they are 'both clingings and liable to clinging,' nor that they are 'liable to clinging but not clingings.' Regarding the nine faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both clingings and liable to clinging'; in some cases they are 'liable to clinging but not clingings,' and in other cases it should not be said of them that they are 'liable to clinging but not clingings.'

Soḷasindriyā [V 0.0150] na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā cā”tipi, “upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā”tipi. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “upādānā ceva upādānasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā, siyā na vattabbā – “upādānasampayuttā ceva no ca upādānā”ti. Dasindriyā upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā. Tīṇindriyā upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā. Tīṇindriyā [T 0.0178] siyā upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā, siyā upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā. Cha indriyā siyā upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā, siyā upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā, siyā na vattabbā – “upādānavippayuttaupādāniyā”tipi, “upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyā”tipi.

Regarding the sixteen faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both clingings and associated with clinging,' nor that they are 'associated with clinging but not clingings.' Regarding the six faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both clingings and associated with clinging'; they may be associated with clinging but not clingings, or it should not be said that they are 'associated with clinging but not clingings.' Ten faculties are dissociated from clinging and are objects of clinging. Three faculties are dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging. Three faculties may be dissociated from clinging and are objects of clinging, or dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging. Six faculties may be dissociated from clinging and are objects of clinging, or dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging, or it should not be said that they are 'dissociated from clinging and are objects of clinging,' nor that they are 'dissociated from clinging and are not objects of clinging.'

No [M 0.0140] kilesā. Dasindriyā saṃkilesikā. Tīṇindriyā asaṃkilesikā. Navindriyā siyā saṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkilesikā. Pannarasindriyā asaṃkiliṭṭhā. Domanassindriyaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā saṃkiliṭṭhā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhā. Pannarasindriyā kilesavippayuttā. Domanassindriyaṃ kilesasampayuttaṃ. Cha indriyā siyā kilesasampayuttā, siyā kilesavippayuttā. Dasindriyā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā cā”ti, saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā. Tīṇindriyā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā cā”tipi, “saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā”tipi. Navindriyā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā cā”ti, siyā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā”ti.

[The faculties] are not defilements. Ten faculties are defiling. Three faculties are non-defiling. Nine faculties may be defiling or non-defiling. Fifteen faculties are undefiled. The faculty of displeasure is defiled. Six faculties may be defiled or undefiled. Fifteen faculties are dissociated from defilements. The faculty of displeasure is associated with defilements. Six faculties may be associated with defilements or dissociated from defilements. Regarding the ten faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both defilements and defiling'; they are defiling but not defilements. Regarding the three faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both defilements and defiling,' nor that they are 'defiling but not defilements.' Regarding the nine faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both defilements and defiling'; they may be defiling but not defilements, or it should not be said that they are 'defiling but not defilements'.

Pannarasindriyā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā cā”tipi, “saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā”tipi. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “kileso [P 0.0133] ceva saṃkiliṭṭhañcā”ti, saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kileso. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā cā”ti, siyā saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā, siyā na vattabbā – “saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva [T 0.0179] no ca kilesā”ti.

Regarding the fifteen faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both defilements and defiled,' nor that they are 'defiled but not defilements.' Regarding the faculty of displeasure, it should not be said that it is 'both a defilement and defiled'; it is defiled but not a defilement. Regarding the six faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both defilements and defiled'; they may be defiled but not defilements, or it should not be said that they are 'defiled but not defilements'.

Pannarasindriyā na vattabbā – “kilesā ceva kilesasampayuttā cā”tipi, “kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā”tipi. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “kileso ceva kilesasampayuttañcā”ti, kilesasampayuttañceva no ca kileso. Cha indriyā na vattabbā – “kilesā [V 0.0151] ceva kilesasampayuttā cā”ti, siyā kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā, siyā na vattabbā – “kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā”ti. Navindriyā kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā. Tīṇindriyā kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā. Domanassindriyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesika”ntipi, “kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesika”ntipi. Tīṇindriyā siyā kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā, siyā kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā. Cha indriyā siyā kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā, siyā kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā, siyā na vattabbā – “kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesikā”tipi, “kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesikā”tipi.

Regarding the fifteen faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both defilements and associated with defilements,' nor that they are 'associated with defilements but not defilements.' Regarding the faculty of displeasure, it should not be said that it is 'both a defilement and associated with defilements'; it is associated with defilements but not a defilement. Regarding the six faculties, it should not be said that they are 'both defilements and associated with defilements'; they may be associated with defilements but not defilements, or it should not be said that they are 'associated with defilements but not defilements.' Nine faculties are dissociated from defilements and defiling. Three faculties are dissociated from defilements and non-defiling. Regarding the faculty of displeasure, it should not be said that it is 'dissociated from defilements and defiling,' nor that it is 'dissociated from defilements and non-defiling.' Three faculties may be dissociated from defilements and defiling, or they may be dissociated from defilements and non-defiling. Six faculties may be dissociated from defilements and defiling, or they may be dissociated from defilements and non-defiling, or it should not be said that they are 'dissociated from defilements and defiling,' nor that they are 'dissociated from defilements and non-defiling.'

Pannarasindriyā [M 0.0141] na dassanena pahātabbā. Sattindriyā siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā na dassanena pahātabbā. Pannarasindriyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Sattindriyā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Pannarasindriyā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Sattindriyā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Pannarasindriyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Sattindriyā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā[T 0.0180], siyā na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.

Fifteen faculties are not to be abandoned by vision. Seven faculties may be abandoned by vision, or may not be abandoned by vision. Fifteen faculties are not to be abandoned by cultivation. Seven faculties may be abandoned by cultivation, or may not be abandoned by cultivation. Fifteen faculties do not have a cause to be abandoned by vision. Seven faculties may have a cause to be abandoned by vision, or may not have a cause to be abandoned by vision. Fifteen faculties do not have a cause to be abandoned by cultivation. Seven faculties may have a cause to be abandoned by cultivation, or may not have a cause to be abandoned by cultivation.

Navindriyā avitakkā. Domanassindriyaṃ savitakkaṃ. Dvādasindriyā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Navindriyā avicārā. Domanassindriyaṃ savicāraṃ. Dvādasindriyā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Ekādasindriyā appītikā. Ekādasindriyā siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Ekādasindriyā na pītisahagatā. Ekādasindriyā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Dvādasindriyā na sukhasahagatā. Dasindriyā siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Dvādasindriyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Dasindriyā siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā.

Nine faculties are without initial application. The faculty of displeasure is with initial application. Twelve faculties may be with initial application, or may be without initial application. Nine faculties are without sustained application. The faculty of displeasure is with sustained application. Twelve faculties may be with sustained application, or may be without sustained application. Eleven faculties are without rapture. Eleven faculties may be with rapture, or may be without rapture. Eleven faculties are not accompanied by rapture. Eleven faculties may be accompanied by rapture, or may not be accompanied by rapture. Twelve faculties are not accompanied by happiness. Ten faculties may be accompanied by happiness, or may not be accompanied by happiness. Twelve faculties are not accompanied by equanimity. Ten faculties may be accompanied by equanimity, or may not be accompanied by equanimity.

Dasindriyā kāmāvacarā. Tīṇindriyā na kāmāvacarā. Navindriyā siyā kāmāvacarā, siyā na kāmāvacarā. Terasindriyā na rūpāvacarā. Navindriyā siyā rūpāvacarā, siyā na rūpāvacarā. Cuddasindriyā na arūpāvacarā. Aṭṭhindriyā siyā arūpāvacarā, siyā na arūpāvacarā. Dasindriyā pariyāpannā. Tīṇindriyā apariyāpannā. Navindriyā siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā. Ekādasindriyā [P 0.0134] aniyyānikā. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ [V 0.0152] niyyānikaṃ. Dasindriyā siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Dasindriyā aniyatā. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ niyataṃ. Ekādasindriyā siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Dasindriyā sauttarā. Tīṇindriyā anuttarā. Navindriyā siyā sauttarā, siyā anuttarā. Pannarasindriyā araṇā. Domanassindriyaṃ saraṇaṃ. Cha [T 0.0181] indriyā siyā saraṇā, siyā araṇāti.

Ten faculties are of the sense-sphere. Three faculties are not of the sense-sphere. Nine faculties may be of the sense-sphere, or may not be of the sense-sphere. Thirteen faculties are not of the form-sphere. Nine faculties may be of the form-sphere, or may not be of the form-sphere. Fourteen faculties are not of the formless-sphere. Eight faculties may be of the formless-sphere, or may not be of the formless-sphere. Ten faculties are included. Three faculties are unincluded. Nine faculties may be included, or may be unincluded. Eleven faculties are not leading out. The faculty of 'I shall know the unknown' is leading out. Ten faculties may be leading out, or may not be leading out. Ten faculties are unfixed. The faculty of 'I shall know the unknown' is fixed. Eleven faculties may be fixed, or may be unfixed. Ten faculties are with a superior. Three faculties are without a superior. Nine faculties may be with a superior, or may be without a superior. Fifteen faculties are without defilement. The faculty of displeasure is with defilement. Six faculties may be with defilement, or may be without defilement.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Section of Questions.

Indriyavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Faculties is concluded.

6. Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgo

6. The Analysis of Dependent Origination

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. Discourse Analysis

225. Avijjāpaccayā [M 0.0142][P 0.0135][V 0.0153] saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

225. With ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form arises; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise; with the six sense bases as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, clinging arises; with clinging as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

226. Tattha katamā avijjā? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”.

226. Herein, what is ignorance? Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the way leading to the cessation of suffering—this is called 'ignorance'.

Tattha katame avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā? Puññābhisaṅkhāro, apuññābhisaṅkhāro, āneñjābhisaṅkhāro, kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsaṅkhāro, cittasaṅkhāro.

Herein, what are the volitional formations conditioned by ignorance? Meritorious volitional formation, demeritorious volitional formation, imperturbable volitional formation, bodily formation, verbal formation, mental formation.

Tattha katamo puññābhisaṅkhāro? Kusalā cetanā kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā dānamayā sīlamayā bhāvanāmayā – ayaṃ vuccati “puññābhisaṅkhāro”.

Herein, what is the meritorious volitional formation? Wholesome volition pertaining to the sense-sphere and the form-sphere, consisting of giving, virtue, and mental development—this is called 'meritorious volitional formation'.

Tattha katamo apuññābhisaṅkhāro? Akusalā cetanā kāmāvacarā [T 0.0182] – ayaṃ vuccati “apuññābhisaṅkhāro”.

Herein, what is the demeritorious volitional formation? Unwholesome volition pertaining to the sense-sphere—this is called 'demeritorious volitional formation'.

Tattha [V 0.0154] katamo āneñjābhisaṅkhāro? Kusalā cetanā arūpāvacarā – ayaṃ vuccati “āneñjābhisaṅkhāro”.

Herein, what is the imperturbable volitional formation? Wholesome volition pertaining to the formless-sphere—this is called 'imperturbable volitional formation'.

Tattha katamo kāyasaṅkhāro? Kāyasañcetanā kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsañcetanā vacīsaṅkhāro, manosañcetanā cittasaṅkhāro. Ime vuccanti “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”.

Herein, what is bodily formation? Bodily volition is bodily formation, verbal volition is verbal formation, mental volition is mental formation. These are called 'volitional formations conditioned by ignorance'.

227. Tattha [P 0.0136] katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”.

227. Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by volitional formations? Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by volitional formations'.

228. Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ? Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “nāmaṃ”[M 0.0143]. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cattāro mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “rūpaṃ”. Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ”.

228. Herein, what is name-and-form conditioned by consciousness? There is name, and there is form. Herein, what is name? The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the volitional formations aggregate—this is called 'name'. Herein, what is form? The four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements—this is called 'form'. Thus, this name and this form. This is called 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness'.

229. Tattha katamaṃ nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ”.

229. Herein, what are the six sense bases conditioned by name-and-form? The eye base, the ear base, the nose base, the tongue base, the body base, the mind base—this is called 'the six sense bases conditioned by name-and-form'.

230. Tattha katamo saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso? Cakkhusamphasso sotasamphasso ghānasamphasso jivhāsamphasso kāyasamphasso manosamphasso – ayaṃ vuccati “saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

230. Herein, what is contact conditioned by the six sense bases? Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-contact—this is called 'contact conditioned by the six sense bases'.

231. Tattha [T 0.0183] katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

231. Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

232. Tattha [V 0.0155] katamā vedanāpaccayā taṇhā? Rūpataṇhā, saddataṇhā, gandhataṇhā, rasataṇhā, phoṭṭhabbataṇhā, dhammataṇhā – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā taṇhā”.

232. Herein, what is craving conditioned by feeling? Craving for forms, craving for sounds, craving for smells, craving for tastes, craving for tangibles, craving for mental phenomena—this is called 'craving conditioned by feeling'.

233. Tattha katamaṃ taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ? Kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ”.

233. Herein, what is clinging conditioned by craving? Sensual clinging, clinging to views, clinging to rules and vows, clinging to a doctrine of self—this is called 'clinging conditioned by craving'.

234. Tattha katamo upādānapaccayā bhavo? Bhavo duvidhena [P 0.0137] – atthi kammabhavo, atthi upapattibhavo. Tattha katamo kammabhavo? Puññābhisaṅkhāro, apuññābhisaṅkhāro, āneñjābhisaṅkhāro – ayaṃ vuccati “kammabhavo”. Sabbampi bhavagāmikammaṃ kammabhavo.

234. Herein, what is becoming conditioned by clinging? Becoming is twofold: there is kamma-becoming, and there is rebirth-becoming. Herein, what is kamma-becoming? The meritorious volitional formation, the demeritorious volitional formation, the imperturbable volitional formation—this is called 'kamma-becoming'. All kamma leading to becoming is kamma-becoming.

Tattha katamo upapattibhavo? Kāmabhavo, rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo, saññābhavo, asaññābhavo, nevasaññānāsaññābhavo, ekavokārabhavo, catuvokārabhavo, pañcavokārabhavo – ayaṃ vuccati “upapattibhavo”. Iti ayañca kammabhavo, ayañca upapattibhavo. Ayaṃ vuccati “upādānapaccayā bhavo”.

Herein, what is rebirth-becoming? Sensual becoming, form-realm becoming, formless-realm becoming, percipient becoming, non-percipient becoming, neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient becoming, one-constituent becoming, four-constituent becoming, five-constituent becoming—this is called 'rebirth-becoming'. Thus, this kamma-becoming and this rebirth-becoming. This is called 'becoming conditioned by clinging'.

235. Tattha [M 0.0144] katamā bhavapaccayā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjāti okkanti abhinibbatti, khandhānaṃ pātubhāvo[T 0.0184], āyatanānaṃ paṭilābho – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavapaccayā jāti”.

235. Herein, what is birth conditioned by becoming? For those various beings in this or that group of beings, whatever is the birth, bringing forth, descent, production anew, the manifestation of the aggregates, the acquisition of the sense-bases—this is called 'birth conditioned by becoming'.

236. Tattha katamaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ? Atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ. Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṃ pāliccaṃ valittacatā āyuno saṃhāni indriyānaṃ paripāko – ayaṃ vuccati “jarā”.

236. Herein, what is aging-and-death conditioned by birth? There is aging, and there is death. Herein, what is aging? For those various beings in this or that group of beings, whatever is the aging, decrepitude, brokenness of teeth, grayness of hair, wrinkledness of skin, the dwindling of life, the decay of the faculties—this is called 'aging'.

Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccu maraṇaṃ kālakiriyā kālaṃkiriyā (ka.) khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo jīvitindriyassupacchedo – idaṃ vuccati “maraṇaṃ”. Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is death? For those various beings from this or that group of beings, whatever is the passing away, the state of passing away, dissolution, disappearance, dying, death, the completion of time, the breaking up of the aggregates, the laying down of the corpse, the cutting off of the life faculty—this is called 'death'. Thus, this aging and this death. This is called 'aging-and-death conditioned by birth'.

237. Tattha [V 0.0156] katamo soko? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa, aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa soko socanā socitattaṃ antosoko antoparisoko cetaso parijjhāyanā domanassaṃ sokasallaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “soko”.

237. Herein, what is sorrow? For one afflicted by the loss of relatives, or afflicted by the loss of wealth, or afflicted by the calamity of disease, or afflicted by the loss of virtue, or afflicted by the corruption of view; or for one beset with some other misfortune, or afflicted by some other painful state—the sorrow, sorrowing, state of being sorrowful, inward sorrow, deep inward sorrow, burning of the mind, mental displeasure, the arrow of sorrow—this is called 'sorrow'.

238. Tattha katamo paridevo? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa[P 0.0138], rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa, aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa ādevo paridevo [T 0.0185] ādevanā paridevanā ādevitattaṃ paridevitattaṃ vācā palāpo vippalāpo lālappo lālappanā lālappitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati paridevo”.

238. Herein, what is lamentation? For one afflicted by the loss of relatives, or afflicted by the loss of wealth, or afflicted by the calamity of disease, or afflicted by the loss of virtue, or afflicted by the corruption of view; or for one beset with some other misfortune, or afflicted by some other painful state—the wailing, lamenting, act of wailing, act of lamenting, state of one who has wailed, state of one who has lamented, utterance, chatter, incoherent speech, babbling, act of babbling, state of one who has babbled—this is called 'lamentation'.

239. Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”.

239. Herein, what is pain? Whatever is bodily disagreeable, bodily pain; the disagreeable painful feeling born of bodily contact that is experienced; the disagreeable painful feelings born of bodily contact—this is called 'pain'.

240. Tattha [M 0.0145] katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ, cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ, cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ, cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassaṃ”.

240. Herein, what is mental displeasure? Whatever is mentally disagreeable, mental pain; the disagreeable painful feeling born of mind-contact that is experienced; the disagreeable painful feelings born of mind-contact—this is called 'mental displeasure'.

241. Tattha katamo upāyāso? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa, aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa āyāso upāyāso āyāsitattaṃ upāyāsitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “upāyāso”.

241. Herein, what is despair? For one afflicted by the loss of relatives, or afflicted by the loss of wealth, or afflicted by the calamity of disease, or afflicted by the loss of virtue, or afflicted by the corruption of view; or for one beset with some other misfortune, or afflicted by some other painful state—the distress, great distress, the state of being distressed, the state of being greatly distressed—this is called 'despair'.

242. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotīti, evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa saṅgati hoti, samāgamo hoti, samodhānaṃ hoti, pātubhāvo hoti. Tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

242. Regarding the phrase, 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering,' it means: thus there is the coming together, the meeting, the combination, the manifestation of this entire mass of suffering. Therefore it is said: 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering'.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Sutta Exposition.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Exposition

1. Paccayacatukkaṃ

1. The Tetrad of Conditions

243. Avijjāpaccayā [V 0.0157] saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

243. With ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-base; with the sixth sense-base as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā [P 0.0139] bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

With ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā [M 0.0146] saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo [T 0.0187] hoti.

With ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality-materiality; with mentality-materiality as condition, the sixth sense-base; with the sixth sense-base as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

With ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality-materiality; with mentality-materiality as condition, the six sense-bases; with the sixth sense-base as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Paccayacatukkaṃ.

End of the Tetrad of Conditions.

2. Hetucatukkaṃ

2. The Tetrad of Causes

244. Avijjāpaccayā [V 0.0158] saṅkhāro avijjāhetuko, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārahetukaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ viññāṇahetukaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ nāmahetukaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanahetuko, phassapaccayā vedanā phassahetukā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāhetukā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāhetukaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

244. With ignorance as condition, volitional formations, which have ignorance as their cause; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness, which has volitional formations as its cause; with consciousness as condition, mentality, which has consciousness as its cause; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense base, which has mentality as its cause; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact, which has the sixth sense base as its cause; with contact as condition, feeling, which has contact as its cause; with feeling as condition, craving, which has feeling as its cause; with craving as condition, clinging, which has craving as its cause; with clinging as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro avijjāhetuko, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārahetukaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ viññāṇahetukaṃ, nāmapaccayā phasso nāmahetuko, phassapaccayā vedanā phassahetukā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāhetukā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāhetukaṃ; upādānapaccayā [T 0.0188] bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro avijjāhetuko, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārahetukaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ viññāṇahetukaṃ[P 0.0140], nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ [M 0.0147] nāmarūpahetukaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanahetuko, phassapaccayā vedanā phassahetukā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāhetukā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāhetukaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

3. Sampayuttacatukkaṃ

3. The Tetrad of Association

245. Avijjāpaccayā [V 0.0159] saṅkhāro avijjāsampayutto, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārasampayuttaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ viññāṇasampayuttaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ nāmasampayuttaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanasampayutto, phassapaccayā vedanā phassasampayuttā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāsampayuttā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāsampayuttaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

245. With ignorance as condition, volitional formations associated with ignorance arise. With volitional formations as condition, consciousness associated with volitional formations arises. With consciousness as condition, mentality associated with consciousness arises. With mentality as condition, the sixth sense base associated with mentality arises. With the sixth sense base as condition, contact associated with the sixth sense base arises. With contact as condition, feeling associated with contact arises. With feeling as condition, craving associated with feeling arises. With craving as condition, clinging associated with craving arises. With clinging as condition, becoming arises. With becoming as condition, birth arises. With birth as condition, aging-and-death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro avijjāsampayutto, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārasampayuttaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ viññāṇasampayuttaṃ[T 0.0189], nāmapaccayā phasso nāmasampayutto, phassapaccayā vedanā phassasampayuttā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāsampayuttā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāsampayuttaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

With ignorance as condition, volitional formations associated with ignorance arise. With volitional formations as condition, consciousness associated with volitional formations arises. With consciousness as condition, mentality associated with consciousness arises. With mentality as condition, contact associated with mentality arises. With contact as condition, feeling associated with contact arises. With feeling as condition, craving associated with feeling arises. With craving as condition, clinging associated with craving arises. With clinging as condition, becoming arises. With becoming as condition, birth arises. With birth as condition, aging-and-death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā [M 0.0148] saṅkhāro avijjāsampayutto, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārasampayuttaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ [P 0.0141] viññāṇasampayuttaṃ nāmaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ nāmarūpasampayuttaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanasampayutto, phassapaccayā vedanā phassasampayuttā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāsampayuttā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāsampayuttaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

With ignorance as condition, volitional formations associated with ignorance arise. With volitional formations as condition, consciousness associated with volitional formations arises. With consciousness as condition, name-and-form arises, of which the name-component is associated with consciousness. With name-and-form as condition, the sixth sense base arises, associated with name. With the sixth sense base as condition, contact associated with the sixth sense base arises. With contact as condition, feeling associated with contact arises. With feeling as condition, craving associated with feeling arises. With craving as condition, clinging associated with craving arises. With clinging as condition, becoming arises. With becoming as condition, birth arises. With birth as condition, aging-and-death arise. Thus arises this entire mass of suffering.

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro avijjāsampayutto, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārasampayuttaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ viññāṇasampayuttaṃ nāmaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ nāmasampayuttaṃ chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanasampayutto, phassapaccayā vedanā phassasampayuttā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāsampayuttā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ upādānasampayuttaṃ; upādānapaccayā [V 0.0160] bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa [T 0.0190] samudayo hoti.

With consciousness as condition, name-and-form arises, of which the name-component is associated with consciousness. With name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise, the sixth sense base being associated with name. With the sixth sense base as condition, contact associated with the sixth sense base arises. With contact as condition, feeling associated with contact arises. With feeling as condition, craving associated with feeling arises. With craving as condition, clinging associated with craving arises. With clinging as condition, becoming arises. With becoming as condition, birth arises. With birth as condition, aging-and-death arise. Thus arises this entire mass of suffering.

Sampayuttacatukkaṃ.

The Tetrad of Association is concluded.

4. Aññamaññacatukkaṃ

4. The Tetrad of Reciprocity

246. Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayāpi avijjā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayāpi saṅkhāro; viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayāpi viññāṇaṃ; nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayāpi nāmaṃ; chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayāpi chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ; phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayāpi phasso; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayāpi vedanā; taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayāpi taṇhā; upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

With contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, contact also arises. With feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, feeling also arises. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

With ignorance as condition, formations arise; with formations as condition, ignorance also arises. With formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, formations also arise. With consciousness as condition, name-and-form arises; with name-and-form as condition, consciousness also arises. With name-and-form as condition, the sixth sense base arises; with the sixth sense base as condition, name-and-form also arises. With the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, the sixth sense base also arises. With contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, contact also arises. With feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, feeling also arises. With craving as condition, clinging arises; with clinging as condition, craving also arises. With clinging as condition, existence arises. With existence as condition, birth arises. With the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, the sixth sense base also arises. With contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, contact also arises. With feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, feeling also arises. With birth as condition, aging-and-death arises. Thus is the origin of this sheer mass of suffering.

5. Paccayacatukkaṃ

5. The Tetrad of Conditions

248. Katame [P 0.0144][V 0.0162] dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

248. What are unwholesome states? At the time when an unwholesome mind arises, accompanied by gladness and associated with wrong view, having as its object a form, or a sound, or an odor, or a taste, or a tactile object, or a mental object—or whatever it may be that it takes as its object—at that time: with ignorance as condition, formations arise; with formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, name arises; with name as condition, the sixth sense base arises; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, clinging arises; with clinging as condition, existence arises; with existence as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging-and-death arises. Thus is the origin of this sheer mass of suffering.

249. Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”.

249. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not-knowing, not-seeing…pe… the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance'.

Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā [T 0.0193] sañcetayitattaṃ cetayitattaṃ (sī. ka.) – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro”.

Herein, what are the formations conditioned by ignorance? Whatever is volition, conation, the state of having willed—this is called 'formations conditioned by ignorance'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? Whatever is mind, intellect, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind base, the mind faculty, consciousness, the consciousness aggregate, the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations'.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ”.

Herein, what is name conditioned by consciousness? The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate—this is called 'name conditioned by consciousness'.

Tattha katamaṃ nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ”.

Herein, what is the sixth sense base conditioned by name? Whatever is mind, intellect, mentality, heart, that which is pure, mind, the mind base, the mind faculty, consciousness, the consciousness aggregate, the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'the sixth sense base conditioned by name'.

Tattha [M 0.0151][V 0.0163] katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is contact conditioned by the sixth sense-base? Whatever is contact, the manner of contacting, the manner of well contacting, the state of having well contacted—this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense-base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? Whatever is mental pleasantness, mental happiness, the pleasant, happy feeling born of mind-contact, the pleasant, happy feeling born of mind-contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

Tattha [P 0.0145] katamā vedanāpaccayā taṇhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandirāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā taṇhā”.

Herein, what is craving conditioned by feeling? Whatever is lust, passionate lust, compliance, non-opposition, delight, delight and lust, the intense lust of the mind—this is called 'craving conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha katamaṃ taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ? Yā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ [T 0.0194] diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkāyikaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ gāho patiṭṭhāho abhiniveso parāmāso kummaggo micchāpatho micchattaṃ titthāyatanaṃ vipariyāsaggāho vipariyesaggāho (bahūsu) – idaṃ vuccati “taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ”.

Herein, what is clinging conditioned by craving? Whatever is wrong view, that which is included in the views, the wilderness of views, the wasteland of views, the contortion of views, the vacillation of views, the fetter of views, grasping, establishment, adherence, misapprehension, the wrong path, the wrong way, wrongness, the ground of other doctrines, perverse grasping—this is called 'clinging conditioned by craving'.

Tattha katamo upādānapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā upādānaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “upādānapaccayā bhavo”.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by clinging? Setting aside clinging, there is the feeling-aggregate, the perception-aggregate, the formations-aggregate, the consciousness-aggregate—this is called 'becoming conditioned by clinging'.

Tattha katamā bhavapaccayā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jāti sañjāti nibbatti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavapaccayā jāti”.

Herein, what is birth conditioned by becoming? Of those various phenomena, whatever is birth, complete birth, coming into being, new coming into being, manifestation—this is called 'birth conditioned by becoming'.

Tattha katamaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ? Atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ. Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jarā jīraṇatā āyuno saṃhāni – ayaṃ vuccati “jarā”. Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yo tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ khayo vayo bhedo paribhedo aniccatā antaradhānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “maraṇaṃ”. Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is aging and death conditioned by birth? There is aging, and there is death. Herein, what is aging? Of those various phenomena, whatever is aging, the state of decrepitude, the decline of the life-span—this is called 'aging'. Herein, what is death? Of those various phenomena, whatever is exhaustion, passing away, breaking up, complete breaking up, impermanence, disappearance—this is called 'death'. Thus, this aging and this death. This is called 'aging and death conditioned by birth'.

Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotīti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa [V 0.0164] saṅgati hoti, samāgamo hoti, samodhānaṃ hoti, pātubhāvo hoti. Tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering. In this way, there is the gathering, meeting, combination, and manifestation of this entire mass of suffering. Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

250. Tasmiṃ [M 0.0152] samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā [T 0.0195] vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā [P 0.0146] upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

250. At that time, with ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, name; with name as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

251. Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”.

251. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not-knowing, not-seeing… the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance'.

Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro”.

Herein, what is the formation conditioned by ignorance? Whatever is volition, thorough volition, the state of having volited—this is called 'the formation conditioned by ignorance'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is the consciousness conditioned by formations? Whatever is mind, heart, intellect... the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'the consciousness conditioned by formations'.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ”.

Herein, what is name conditioned by consciousness? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations—this is called 'name conditioned by consciousness'.

Nāmapaccayā phassoti. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Ṭhapetvā phassaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “nāmaṃ”.

Regarding 'contact is conditioned by name': Herein, what is name? Setting aside contact, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'name'.

Tattha katamo nāmapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “nāmapaccayā phasso”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is the contact conditioned by name? Whatever is contact, touching, thorough touching, the state of having thoroughly touched—this is called 'the contact conditioned by name.' ... Therefore, it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

Tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ[V 0.0165], nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti[T 0.0196], jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

At that time, with ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form; with name-and-form as condition, the sixth sense base; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

253. Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”.

253. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not-knowing, not-seeing... the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance'.

Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro”.

Herein, what is the formation conditioned by ignorance? Whatever is volition, thorough volition, the state of having volited—this is called 'the formation conditioned by ignorance'.

Tattha [M 0.0153] katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is the consciousness conditioned by formations? Whatever is mind, heart, intellect... the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'the consciousness conditioned by formations'.

Tattha [P 0.0147] katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ? Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “nāmaṃ”. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cakkhāyatanassa upacayo, sotāyatanassa upacayo, ghānāyatanassa upacayo, jivhāyatanassa upacayo, kāyāyatanassa upacayo, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ cittajaṃ cittahetukaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “rūpaṃ”. Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ”.

Herein, what is name-and-form conditioned by consciousness? There is name, there is form. Herein, what is name? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations—this is called 'name.' Herein, what is form? The accumulation of the eye-base, the accumulation of the ear-base, the accumulation of the nose-base, the accumulation of the tongue-base, the accumulation of the body-base, or whatever other form there is that is mind-born, mind-caused, mind-originated—this is called 'form.' Thus, this is name, and this is form. This is called 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness'.

Nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatananti. Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “nāmaṃ”. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manoviññāṇadhātu vattati – idaṃ vuccati “rūpaṃ”. Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “nāmarūpaṃ”.

Regarding 'the sixth sense base is conditioned by name-and-form': There is name, there is form. Herein, what is name? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations—this is called 'name.' Herein, what is form? The form depending on which the mind-consciousness-element occurs—this is called 'form.' Thus, this is name, and this is form. This is called 'name-and-form'.

Tattha katamaṃ nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ [T 0.0197] cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ”.

Herein, what is the sixth sense base conditioned by name-and-form? Whatever is mind, intellect, mentation... the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'the sixth sense base conditioned by name-and-form'.

Tattha [V 0.0166] katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is the contact conditioned by the sixth sense base? Whatever is contact, touching, thorough touching, the state of having thoroughly touched—this is called 'the contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.' ... Therefore, it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

254. Tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

254. At that time, with ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

255. Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”.

255. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not-knowing, not-seeing... the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance'.

Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro”.

Herein, what is the formation conditioned by ignorance? Whatever is volition, thorough volition, the state of having willed—this is called 'the formation conditioned by ignorance'.

Tattha [M 0.0154] katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is the consciousness conditioned by formations? Whatever is mind, intellect, mentation... the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'the consciousness conditioned by formations'.

Tattha [P 0.0148] katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ? Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “nāmaṃ”. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cakkhāyatanassa upacayo, sotāyatanassa upacayo, ghānāyatanassa upacayo, jivhāyatanassa upacayo, kāyāyatanassa upacayo[T 0.0198], yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ cittajaṃ cittahetukaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “rūpaṃ”. Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ”.

Herein, what is name-and-form conditioned by consciousness? There is name, there is form. Herein, what is name? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations—this is called 'name.' Herein, what is form? The accumulation of the eye-base, the accumulation of the ear-base, the accumulation of the nose-base, the accumulation of the tongue-base, the accumulation of the body-base, or whatever other form there is that is mind-born, mind-caused, mind-originated—this is called 'form.' Thus, this is name, and this is form. This is called 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness'.

Nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatananti. Atthi nāmaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ. Tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “nāmaṃ”. Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cattāro [V 0.0167] ca mahābhūtā, yañca rūpaṃ nissāya manoviññāṇadhātu vattati – idaṃ vuccati “rūpaṃ”. Iti idañca nāmaṃ, idañca rūpaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “nāmarūpaṃ”.

Regarding “name-and-form is the condition for the six sense bases”: There is name, there is form. Therein, what is name? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations—this is called “name.” Therein, what is form? The four great elements, and the form dependent on which the mind-consciousness element occurs—this is called “form.” Thus, this is name and this is form. This is called “name-and-form.”

Tattha katamaṃ nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ”.

Therein, what are the six sense bases conditioned by name-and-form? The eye-base, the ear-base, the nose-base, the tongue-base, the body-base, the mind-base—this is called “the six sense bases conditioned by name-and-form.”

Tattha katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Therein, what is contact conditioned by the sixth sense base? Whatever is contact, touching, thorough touching, the state of having thoroughly touched—this is called “contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.” …pe… Therefore it is said: “Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.”

Paccayacatukkaṃ.

The Tetrad of Conditions is finished.

6. Hetucatukkaṃ

6. The Tetrad of Causes.

256. Tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro avijjāhetuko, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārahetukaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ viññāṇahetukaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ nāmahetukaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanahetuko, phassapaccayā vedanā phassahetukā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā vedanāhetukā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ taṇhāhetukaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ[T 0.0199]. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

256.
