At the time when an unwholesome consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, associated with wrong view, with prompting... or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from wrong view, having a form as object... or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from wrong view, with prompting, having as object a form, or a sound, or an odor, or a taste, or a tangible object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be; at that time, conditioned by ignorance, formation arises; conditioned by formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, craving arises; conditioned by craving, determination arises; conditioned by determination, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

285. Tattha katamā avijjā…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

285. Therein, what is ignorance?... and so on. Therefore, it is said: 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering'.

286. Katame [M 0.0173] dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti domanassasahagataṃ paṭighasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… domanassasahagataṃ paṭighasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā paṭighaṃ, paṭighapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

286. Which states are unwholesome? At the time when an unwholesome consciousness arises, accompanied by displeasure, associated with aversion, having a form as object... or accompanied by displeasure, associated with aversion, with prompting, having as object a form, or a sound, or an odor, or a taste, or a tangible object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be; at that time, conditioned by ignorance, formation arises; conditioned by formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, aversion arises; conditioned by aversion, determination arises; conditioned by determination, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

287. Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

287. Therein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not-knowing, not-seeing... the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance'... and so on. This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ [P 0.0167] cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? Whatever is mental unpleasantness, mental pain, an unpleasant, painful experience born of mental contact, an unpleasant, painful feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

Tattha katamaṃ vedanāpaccayā paṭighaṃ? Yo cittassa āghāto…pe… caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo asulopo (syā.) anattamanatā cittassa – idaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā paṭighaṃ”[T 0.0223].

Herein, what is aversion conditioned by feeling? Whatever is resentment of the mind... fierceness, shedding of tears, and displeasure of the mind—this is called 'aversion conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha katamo paṭighapaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “paṭighapaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is determination conditioned by aversion? Whatever is the mind's determination, the act of determining, the state of being determined on that—this is called 'determination conditioned by aversion'.

Tattha [V 0.0189] katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by determination? Excluding determination, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by determination.'… Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

288. Katame dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ vicikicchāsampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha[M 0.0174], tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā vicikicchā, vicikicchāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

288. What states are unwholesome? At a time when an unwholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity and associated with doubt, having as its object a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be; at that time, conditioned by ignorance, there are formations; conditioned by formations, there is consciousness; conditioned by consciousness, there is mentality; conditioned by mentality, there is the sixth sense base; conditioned by the sixth sense base, there is contact; conditioned by contact, there is feeling; conditioned by feeling, there is doubt; conditioned by doubt, there is becoming; conditioned by becoming, there is birth; conditioned by birth, there is aging and death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

289. Tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

289. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not knowing, not seeing... the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance.' ... This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ, cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That mental feeling which is neither pleasant nor unpleasant, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mental contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

Tattha [P 0.0168] katamā vedanāpaccayā vicikicchā? Yā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā kaṅkhāyitattaṃ vimati vicikicchā [T 0.0224] dveḷhakaṃ dvidhāpatho dvedhāpatho (sī. syā.) saṃsayo anekaṃsaggāho āsappanā parisappanā apariyogāhaṇā apariyogāhanā (sī. syā. ka.) chambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā vicikicchā”.

Herein, what is doubt conditioned by feeling? Whatever is doubt, doubting, the state of doubt, uncertainty, skepticism, being of two minds, a divided path, indecision, inability to grasp decisively, hesitation, wriggling, lack of penetration, rigidity, a scratching of the mind—this is called 'doubt conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha katamo vicikicchāpaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā vicikicchaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “vicikicchāpaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by doubt? Excluding doubt, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by doubt.'… Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

290. Katame [V 0.0190] dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ uddhaccasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā uddhaccaṃ, uddhaccapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

290. What states are unwholesome? At a time when an unwholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity and associated with restlessness, having as its object a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be; at that time, conditioned by ignorance, there are formations; conditioned by formations, there is consciousness; conditioned by consciousness, there is mentality; conditioned by mentality, there is the sixth sense base; conditioned by the sixth sense base, there is contact; conditioned by contact, there is feeling; conditioned by feeling, there is restlessness; conditioned by restlessness, there is determination; conditioned by determination, there is becoming; conditioned by becoming, there is birth; conditioned by birth, there is aging and death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

291. Tattha [M 0.0175] katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

291. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not knowing, not seeing... the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance.' ... This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That mental feeling which is neither pleasant nor unpleasant, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mental contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

Tattha katamaṃ vedanāpaccayā uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa [T 0.0225] – idaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā uddhaccaṃ”.

Herein, what is restlessness conditioned by feeling? Whatever is the mind's restlessness, its lack of calm, the scattering of consciousness, the agitation of the mind—this is called 'restlessness conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha katamo uddhaccapaccayā adhimokkho? Yo [P 0.0169] cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “uddhaccapaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is determination conditioned by restlessness? Whatever is the mind's determination, its resolving, its state of being resolved on that—this is called 'determination conditioned by restlessness'.

Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by determination? Excluding determination, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by determination.'… Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

Akusalaniddeso.

The Exposition of the Unwholesome is finished.

10. Kusalaniddeso

10. Exposition of the Wholesome

292. Katame [V 0.0191] dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

292. What are wholesome states? When a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness arises, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge—having as its object a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tactile object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be—at that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, formation arises; conditioned by formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

293. Tattha katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso, amoho.

293. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-aversion, and non-delusion.

Tattha [M 0.0176] katamo alobho? Yo alobho alubbhanā alubbhitattaṃ asārāgo asārajjanā asārajjitattaṃ anabhijjhā alobho kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “alobho”.

Herein, what is non-greed? Whatever is non-greed, the act of not being greedy, the state of not being greedy; non-passion, the manner of not being passionate, the state of not being passionate; non-covetousness, that non-greed which is a wholesome root—this is called 'non-greed'.

Tattha katamo adoso? Yo adoso adussanā adussitattaṃ abyāpādo [T 0.0226] abyāpajjo adoso kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “adoso”.

Herein, what is non-aversion? Whatever is non-aversion, the manner of not being averse, the state of not being averse; non-ill-will, the state of not having ill-will; that non-aversion which is a wholesome root—this is called 'non-aversion'.

Tattha katamo amoho? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “amoho”. Ime vuccanti “kusalamūlā”.

Herein, what is non-delusion? That which is wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'non-delusion'. These are called 'wholesome roots'.

Tattha [P 0.0170] katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”.

Herein, what is formation conditioned by wholesome roots? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'formation conditioned by wholesome roots'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ…pe… nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ…pe… chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso…pe… phassapaccayā vedanā…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by formation? ... What is mentality conditioned by consciousness? ... What is the sixth sense base conditioned by mentality? ... What is contact conditioned by the sixth sense base? ... What is feeling conditioned by contact? ...

Tattha [V 0.0192] katamo vedanāpaccayā pasādo? Yā saddhā saddahanā okappanā abhippasādo – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā pasādo”.

Herein, what is confidence conditioned by feeling? That which is faith, believing, acceptance, exceptional confidence—this is called 'confidence conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha katamo pasādapaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “pasādapaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is resolution conditioned by confidence? That which is the mind's deciding, the manner of resolving, the state of being resolved on that—this is called 'resolution conditioned by confidence'.

Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by resolution? Setting aside resolution, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by resolution'. ... Therefore, it is said: 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering'.

294. Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā [T 0.0227] viññāṇaṃ[M 0.0177], viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

294. What are wholesome states? When a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness arises, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and prompted, having as its object a form... or accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge... or accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, and prompted, having as its object a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tactile object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be—at that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, formation arises; conditioned by formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

295. Tattha [P 0.0171] katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso.

295. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed and non-aversion.

Tattha katamo alobho? Yo alobho alubbhanā alubbhitattaṃ asārāgo asārajjanā asārajjitattaṃ anabhijjhā alobho kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “alobho”.

Herein, what is non-greed? Whatever is non-greed, the act of not being greedy, the state of not being greedy; non-passion, the manner of not being passionate, the state of not being passionate; non-covetousness, that non-greed which is a wholesome root—this is called 'non-greed'.

Tattha katamo adoso? Yo adoso adussanā adussitattaṃ abyāpādo abyāpajjo adoso kusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “adoso”. Ime vuccanti “kusalamūlā”.

Herein, what is non-aversion? Whatever is non-aversion, the manner of not being averse, the state of not being averse; non-ill-will, the state of not having ill-will; that non-aversion which is a wholesome root—this is called 'non-aversion'. These are called 'wholesome roots'.

Tattha [V 0.0193] katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is formation conditioned by wholesome roots? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'formation conditioned by wholesome roots'. ... This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is mental agreeableness, mental pleasure, the agreeable pleasant feeling born of mental contact, the agreeable pleasant feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'. ... Therefore, it is said: 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering'.

296. Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā [T 0.0228] bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

296. What are wholesome states? When a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, having as its object a form... or accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, and prompted, having as its object a form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tactile object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be—at that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, formation arises; conditioned by formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

297. Tattha [M 0.0178] katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso, amoho – ime vuccanti “kusalamūlā”.

297. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-aversion, and non-delusion—these are called 'wholesome roots'.

Tattha katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati – “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is the volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots? Volition, the act of volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots'... this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? Whatever mental state is neither agreeable nor disagreeable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is born of mental contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'... Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ [V 0.0194] ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā saddārammaṇaṃ vā gandhārammaṇaṃ vā rasārammaṇaṃ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

What are wholesome states? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with a form as its object… or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting, with a form as its object, or a sound as its object, or an odor as its object, or a taste as its object, or a tangible object as its object, or a mental object as its object, or whatever it may be that it takes as its object—at that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, there is volitional formation; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness; conditioned by consciousness, name; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact; conditioned by contact, feeling; conditioned by feeling, confidence; conditioned by confidence, resolution; conditioned by resolution, becoming; conditioned by becoming, birth; conditioned by birth, aging-and-death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

299. Tattha katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso – ime vuccanti [T 0.0229] “kusalamūlā”.

299. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed and non-aversion—these are called 'wholesome roots'.

Tattha katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is the volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots? Volition, the act of volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots.'... Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.'

300. Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ paṭhavīkasiṇaṃ (sī. syā.), tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā [P 0.0172] viññāṇaṃ[M 0.0179], viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

300. What are wholesome states? At a time when one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures... one attains and dwells in the first jhāna which has the earth kasiṇa as its object—at that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, there is volitional formation; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness; conditioned by consciousness, name; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact; conditioned by contact, feeling; conditioned by feeling, confidence; conditioned by confidence, resolution; conditioned by resolution, becoming; conditioned by becoming, birth; conditioned by birth, aging-and-death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

301. Tattha katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso, amoho – ime vuccanti “kusalamūlā”.

301. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-aversion, and non-delusion—these are called 'wholesome roots'.

Tattha katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is the volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots? Volition, the act of volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots.'... Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.'

302. Katame [V 0.0195] dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [T 0.0230] viharati, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

302. What are wholesome states? At a time when one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, completely transcending the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, with the abandoning of pleasure... one attains and dwells in the fourth jhāna—at that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, there is volitional formation; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness; conditioned by consciousness, name; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact; conditioned by contact, feeling; conditioned by feeling, confidence; conditioned by confidence, resolution; conditioned by resolution, becoming; conditioned by becoming, birth; conditioned by birth, aging-and-death. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

303. Tattha katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso, amoho – ime vuccanti “kusalamūlā”.

303. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-aversion, and non-delusion—these are called 'wholesome roots'.

Tattha katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots? Volition, the act of volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots'... this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? Whatever is mental agreeableness, mental happiness; the agreeable, happy feeling born of mind-contact; the agreeable, happy feeling that is born of mind-contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'... Therefore it is said, 'Thus arises this entire mass of suffering.'

304. Katame [M 0.0180] dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ [P 0.0173] upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā [T 0.0231] jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayo hoti.

304. What are wholesome states? At a time when one develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the undoing of kamma, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, quite secluded from sensual pleasures... one attains and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge—at that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, there is volitional formation; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness; conditioned by consciousness, name; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact; conditioned by contact, feeling; conditioned by feeling, confidence; conditioned by confidence, resolution; conditioned by resolution, becoming; conditioned by becoming, birth; conditioned by birth, aging-and-death. Thus is the arising of these states.

305. Tattha katame kusalamūlā? Alobho, adoso, amoho.

305. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-aversion, non-delusion.

Tattha [V 0.0196] katamo alobho…pe… adoso…pe… amoho? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “amoho”. Ime vuccanti “kusalamūlā”.

Herein, what is non-greed?…pe… non-hatred?…pe… non-delusion? That which is wisdom, understanding…pe… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'non-delusion.' These are called 'wholesome roots.'

Tattha katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'volitional formation conditioned by wholesome roots'…pe… this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.'

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is mental agreeableness, mental pleasure, born of mind-contact, agreeable and pleasant feeling, born of mind-contact, agreeable and pleasant feeling—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā pasādo? Yā saddhā saddahanā okappanā abhippasādo – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā pasādo”.

Herein, what is confidence conditioned by feeling? That which is faith, the act of believing, conviction, serene confidence—this is called 'confidence conditioned by feeling.'

Tattha katamo pasādapaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “pasādapaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is resolution conditioned by confidence? That which is the mind's resolution, the act of resolving, the state of having thus resolved—this is called 'resolution conditioned by confidence.'

Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is existence conditioned by resolution? Setting aside resolution, there is the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate—this is called 'existence conditioned by resolution'…pe… this is called 'aging and death conditioned by birth.'

Evametesaṃ [M 0.0181] dhammānaṃ samudayo hotīti. Evametesaṃ dhammānaṃ saṅgati hoti, samāgamo hoti, samodhānaṃ hoti, pātubhāvo hoti. Tena vuccati “evametesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayo hotī”ti.

Thus is the origination of these phenomena. Thus there is the combination of these phenomena, there is the coming together, there is the convergence, there is the manifestation. Therefore, it is said, 'Thus is the origination of these phenomena.'

Kusalaniddeso.

The Exposition of the Wholesome.

11. Abyākataniddeso

11. The Exposition of the Indeterminate.

306. Katame [T 0.0232][V 0.0197] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

306. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to a wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere having been done and accumulated, its resultant eye-consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity and having a form as its object—at that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name arises; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, existence arises; conditioned by existence, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

307. Tattha katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”.

307. Herein, what is volitional formation? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having intended—this is called 'volitional formation.'

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjācakkhuviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by volitional formations? That which is mind, mentation, the heart…pe… the eye-consciousness element born of that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by volitional formations.'

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho[P 0.0174], saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ”.

Herein, what is name conditioned by consciousness? The feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, and the formations aggregate—this is called 'name conditioned by consciousness.'

Tattha katamaṃ nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjācakkhuviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ”.

Herein, what is the sixth sense base conditioned by name? That which is mind, mentation, the heart…pe… the eye-consciousness element born of that—this is called 'the sixth sense base conditioned by name.'

Tattha katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is contact conditioned by the sixth sense base? That which is contact, the act of touching, thorough touching, the state of having thoroughly touched—this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.'

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is mental, neither agreeable nor disagreeable; born of mind-contact, a feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure; born of mind-contact, a feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha [M 0.0182] katamo vedanāpaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā vedanaṃ, saññākkhandho [T 0.0233] saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho [V 0.0198] – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is existence conditioned by feeling? Setting aside feeling, there is the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate—this is called 'existence conditioned by feeling'…pe… Therefore it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

308. Tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārahetukaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ viññāṇahetukaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ nāmahetukaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanahetuko, phassapaccayā vedanā phassahetukā, vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

308. At that time: conditioned by formations, consciousness arises, with formations as its cause; conditioned by consciousness, name arises, with consciousness as its cause; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises, with name as its cause; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises, with the sixth sense base as its cause; conditioned by contact, feeling arises, with contact as its cause; conditioned by feeling, existence arises; conditioned by existence, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

309. Tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārasampayuttaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ viññāṇasampayuttaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ nāmasampayuttaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso chaṭṭhāyatanasampayutto, phassapaccayā vedanā phassasampayuttā, vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

309. At that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises, associated with formations; conditioned by consciousness, name arises, associated with consciousness; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises, associated with name; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises, associated with the sixth sense base; conditioned by contact, feeling arises, associated with contact; conditioned by feeling, existence arises; conditioned by existence, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

310. Tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayāpi saṅkhāro; viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayāpi [P 0.0175] viññāṇaṃ; nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayāpi nāmaṃ; chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayāpi chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ; phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayāpi phasso; vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā [T 0.0234] jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

310. At that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; and conditioned by consciousness, formations arise. Conditioned by consciousness, name arises; and conditioned by name, consciousness arises. Conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises; and conditioned by the sixth sense base, name arises. Conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; and conditioned by contact, the sixth sense base arises. Conditioned by contact, feeling arises; and conditioned by feeling, contact arises. Conditioned by feeling, existence arises; conditioned by existence, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

311. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ saddārammaṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ gandhārammaṇaṃ…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rasārammaṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti sukhasahagataṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

311. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, on account of a wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere having been performed and accumulated, resultant ear-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, with sound as its object... or nose-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, with odor as its object... or tongue-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, with taste as its object... or body-consciousness arises, accompanied by pleasure, with a tangible object as its object—at that time: conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

312. Tattha [M 0.0183][V 0.0199] katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

312. Herein, what is formation? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having volited—this is called 'formation.'... This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.'

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ sātaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is bodily agreeable, bodily pleasant, the agreeable and pleasant feeling born of bodily contact that is experienced, and the agreeable, pleasant feeling born of bodily contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā vedanaṃ, saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by feeling? Setting aside feeling, there are the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by feeling.'... Therefore it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

313. Katame [T 0.0235] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manodhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā saddārammaṇā vā gandhārammaṇā vā rasārammaṇā vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā [P 0.0176] viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

313. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, on account of a wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere having been performed and accumulated, a resultant mind-element arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a visible form, a sound, an odor, a taste, or a tangible object as its object, or whatever other object it may take—at that time: conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

314. Tattha katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”.

314. Herein, what is formation? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having volited—this is called 'formation.'

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanodhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? That which is mind, mentation, intellect... the mind-element corresponding to that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations.'... This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.'

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ [V 0.0200] vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is mental, neither agreeable nor disagreeable; the feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure born of mind-contact that is experienced; and the feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure born of mind-contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is resolution conditioned by feeling? That which is the mind's resolution, the act of resolving, the state of having resolved upon that—this is called 'resolution conditioned by feeling.'

Tattha [M 0.0184] katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by resolution? Setting aside resolution, there are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by resolution.'... Therefore it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

315. Katame [T 0.0236] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā saddārammaṇā vā gandhārammaṇā vā rasārammaṇā vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

315. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, on account of a wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere having been performed and accumulated, a resultant mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by joy, with a visible form, a sound, an odor, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental object as its object, or whatever other object it may take—at that time: conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

316. Tattha katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”.

316. Herein, what is formation? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having volited—this is called 'formation.'

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? That which is mind, mentation, intellect... the mind-consciousness-element corresponding to that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations.'... This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.'

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is mentally agreeable, mentally pleasant; the agreeable and pleasant feeling born of mind-contact that is experienced; and the agreeable, pleasant feeling born of mind-contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha [V 0.0201] katamo vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is resolution conditioned by feeling? That which is the mind's resolution, the act of resolving, the state of having resolved upon that—this is called 'resolution conditioned by feeling.'

Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by resolution? Setting aside resolution, there are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by resolution.'... Therefore it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

317. Katame [T 0.0237][M 0.0185][P 0.0177] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā saddārammaṇā vā gandhārammaṇā vā rasārammaṇā vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

317. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when, on account of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere having been done and accumulated, the resultant mind-consciousness element arises, accompanied by equanimity, having a visible object, or a sound object, or an odor object, or a taste object, or a tangible object, or a mental object, or whatever it may be that it is based upon; at that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

318. Tattha katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”.

318. Herein, what is formation? That which is volition, the act of intending, the state of having intended—this is called 'formation'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? That which is mind, mentation, heart... the mind-consciousness element born of that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations.'... This is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.'

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is the mental, neither pleasant nor unpleasant; the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact; the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is born of mind-contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is resolution conditioned by feeling? That which is the mind's resolution, the act of resolving, the state of being resolved upon that—this is called 'resolution conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha [V 0.0202] katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by resolution? Setting aside resolution, there are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by resolution.'... Therefore it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

319. Katame [T 0.0238] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā [M 0.0186] ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

319. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when, on account of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere having been done and accumulated, the resultant mind-consciousness element arises, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge... or accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge... or accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge... or accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge... or accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting; having a visible object... or a mental object, or whatever it may be that it is based upon; at that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

320. Tattha katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”.

320. Herein, what is formation? That which is volition, the act of intending, the state of having intended—this is called 'formation'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? That which is mind, mentation, heart... the mind-consciousness element born of that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations.'... This is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā pasādo? Yā [P 0.0178] saddhā saddahanā okappanā abhippasādo – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā pasādo”.

Herein, what is confidence conditioned by feeling? That which is faith, conviction, settled assurance, clear confidence—this is called 'confidence conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha katamo pasādapaccayā adhimokkho[T 0.0239]? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “pasādapaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is resolution conditioned by confidence? That which is the mind's resolution, the act of resolving, the state of being resolved upon that—this is called 'resolution conditioned by confidence'.

Tattha [V 0.0203] katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by resolution? Setting aside resolution, there are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by resolution.'... Therefore it is said: 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

321. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti – ime dhammā kusalā.

321. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the Form Realm, being quite secluded from sensual pleasures... one enters and dwells in the first jhāna which has the earth kasiṇa as its object; at that time there is contact... there is non-distraction—these phenomena are wholesome.

Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ[M 0.0187], chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo[P 0.0179], bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

On account of that same wholesome kamma pertaining to the Form Sphere having been done and accumulated, one enters and dwells in the resultant first jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object, being quite secluded from sensual pleasures...; at that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

322. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [T 0.0240] viharati, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti – ime dhammā kusalā.

322. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the Formless Realm, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, one enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, through the abandoning of pleasure...; at that time there is contact... there is non-distraction—these phenomena are wholesome.

Tasseva arūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

Due to that very wholesome formless-sphere kamma having been done and accumulated, having completely transcended the base of nothingness, one attains and dwells in the resultant fourth jhāna, which is accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and is due to the abandoning of pleasure… At that time: due to formations as condition, consciousness arises; due to consciousness as condition, mentality arises; due to mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; due to the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; due to contact as condition, feeling arises; due to feeling as condition, confidence arises; due to confidence as condition, resolution arises; due to resolution as condition, becoming arises; due to becoming as condition, birth arises; due to birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

323. Katame [V 0.0204] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti – ime dhammā kusalā.

323. What states are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out, leads to non-accumulation—for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, being quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one attains and dwells in the first jhāna, which has painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome.

Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo[T 0.0241], bhavapaccayā [P 0.0180] jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayo hoti.

Due to that very supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, being quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one attains and dwells in the resultant first jhāna, which has painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time: due to formations as condition, consciousness arises; due to consciousness as condition, mentality arises; due to mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; due to the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; due to contact as condition, feeling arises; due to feeling as condition, confidence arises; due to confidence as condition, resolution arises; due to resolution as condition, becoming arises; due to becoming as condition, birth arises; due to birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of these states.

324. Katame [M 0.0188] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ…pe… sotaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ saddārammaṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ gandhārammaṇaṃ…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rasārammaṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti dukkhasahagataṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

324. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to unwholesome kamma having been done and accumulated, resultant eye-consciousness accompanied by equanimity with a visible form as object has arisen… resultant ear-consciousness accompanied by equanimity with a sound as object has arisen… resultant nose-consciousness accompanied by equanimity with an odor as object has arisen… resultant tongue-consciousness accompanied by equanimity with a taste as object has arisen… resultant body-consciousness accompanied by pain with a tangible object as object has arisen. At that time: due to formations as condition, consciousness arises; due to consciousness as condition, mentality arises; due to mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; due to the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; due to contact as condition, feeling arises; due to feeling as condition, becoming arises; due to becoming as condition, birth arises; due to birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

325. Tattha katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”.

325. Therein, what is formation? Whatever is volition, co-volition, the state of having willed—this is called 'formation'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjākāyaviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Therein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? Whatever is mind, the heart, mentality… the body-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations'… this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha [V 0.0205] katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Therein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? Whatever is bodily displeasure, bodily pain, the unpleasant painful feeling born of bodily contact, the unpleasant painful feeling born of bodily contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā [T 0.0242] vedanaṃ, saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Therein, what is becoming conditioned by feeling? Setting aside feeling, there are the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness. This is called 'becoming conditioned by feeling'… Therefore, it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

326. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ [P 0.0181] samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manodhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā saddārammaṇā vā gandhārammaṇā vā rasārammaṇā vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

326. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to unwholesome kamma having been done and accumulated, the resultant mind-element has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, with a visible form, or a sound, or an odor, or a taste, or a tangible object, or whatever object it takes as support. At that time: due to formations as condition, consciousness arises; due to consciousness as condition, mentality arises; due to mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; due to the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; due to contact as condition, feeling arises; due to feeling as condition, resolution arises; due to resolution as condition, becoming arises; due to becoming as condition, birth arises; due to birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

327. Tattha [M 0.0189] katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati saṅkhāro.

327. Therein, what is formation? Whatever is volition, co-volition, the state of having willed—this is called 'formation'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanodhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Therein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? Whatever is mind, the heart, mentality… the mind-element born of that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations'… this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense base'.

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Therein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? Whatever is mental, neither pleasant nor unpleasant; the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact; the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact'.

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho”.

Therein, what is resolution conditioned by feeling? Whatever is the mind's resolution, the manner of resolving, the state of being resolved on that object—this is called 'resolution conditioned by feeling'.

Tattha [V 0.0206] katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ[T 0.0243], vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Therein, what is becoming conditioned by resolution? Setting aside resolution, there are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness. This is called 'becoming conditioned by resolution'… Therefore, it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering'.

328. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

328. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when, due to unwholesome kamma having been done and accumulated, the resultant mind-consciousness element arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a visible object... or a mental object, or whatever it takes as its object—at that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, decision arises; conditioned by decision, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

329. Tattha katamo saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāro”.

329. Herein, what is formation? Whatever is volition, intending, the state of having intended—this is called 'formation'.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is consciousness conditioned by formations? Whatever is consciousness, mind, mentality... the mind-consciousness element born from that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formations'... Therefore, it is said, 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering'.

330. Katame [M 0.0190][P 0.0182] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye manodhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā [T 0.0244] neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā somanassasahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

330. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when the mind-element arises, which is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma, accompanied by equanimity, with a visible object... or a tangible object as its object... or when the mind-consciousness element arises, which is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma, accompanied by joy, with a visible object... or a mental object as its object... or when the mind-consciousness element arises, which is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma, accompanied by equanimity, with a visible object... or a mental object as its object, or whatever it takes as its object—at that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, decision arises; conditioned by decision, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

331. Katame [V 0.0207] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā [T 0.0245] chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā [P 0.0183] jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

331. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when the mind-consciousness element arises, which is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma—accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge… accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge… accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge… accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting—with a visible object... or a mental object, or whatever it takes as its object—at that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, decision arises; conditioned by decision, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

332. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā [M 0.0191] jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

332. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the form-sphere jhāna, which is functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma—for a pleasant abiding in the here and now, quite secluded from sensual pleasures... one enters and abides in the first jhāna with the earth kasiṇa. At that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, decision arises; conditioned by decision, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

333. Katame dhammā abyākatā?
