Yasmiṃ samaye arūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ[P 0.0184], viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā [T 0.0246] jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

333. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the formless-sphere jhāna, which is functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not the result of kamma—for a pleasant abiding in the here and now, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, one enters and abides in the fourth jhāna accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. At that time, conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, decision arises; conditioned by decision, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

Abyākataniddeso.

The Exposition of the Indeterminate.

12. Avijjāmūlakakusalaniddeso

12. Exposition of Wholesome States Rooted in Ignorance.

334. Katame [V 0.0208] dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

334. What are wholesome states? At the time when a wholesome consciousness pertaining to the sense-sphere arises, accompanied by gladness and associated with knowledge, having a form as its object... or... a mental object as its object, or whatever it takes as an object, at that time, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, mentality arises; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, confidence arises; with confidence as condition, determination arises; with determination as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

335. Tattha katamo avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

335. Herein, what is the volitional formation conditioned by ignorance? That which is volition, that which is intending, that which is the state of having intended—this is called ‘volitional formation conditioned by ignorance’… This is called ‘contact conditioned by the sixth sense base.’

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Herein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is mental pleasantness, mental happiness, pleasant and happy feeling born of mind-contact that is experienced, pleasant and happy feeling born of mind-contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha [M 0.0192] katamo vedanāpaccayā pasādo? Yā saddhā saddahanā okappanā abhippasādo – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā pasādo”.

Herein, what is confidence conditioned by feeling? That which is faith, that which is conviction, that which is acceptance, that which is serene confidence—this is called 'confidence conditioned by feeling.'

Tattha katamo pasādapaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “pasādapaccayā adhimokkho”.

Herein, what is determination conditioned by confidence? That which is the determination of the mind, that which is the act of determining, that which is the state of being resolved on that object—this is called 'determination conditioned by confidence.'

Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho [T 0.0247] saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Herein, what is becoming conditioned by determination? Setting aside determination, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by determination'... Therefore, it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

336. Tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā [V 0.0209] nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

336. At that time, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, mentality arises; with mentality as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, confidence arises; with confidence as condition, determination arises; with determination as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

337. Tasmiṃ [P 0.0185] samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

337. At that time, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, mentality-materiality arises; with mentality-materiality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, confidence arises; with confidence as condition, determination arises; with determination as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

338. Tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

338. At that time, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, mentality-materiality arises; with mentality-materiality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, confidence arises; with confidence as condition, determination arises; with determination as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

339. Katame [T 0.0248] dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ [M 0.0193] sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

339. What are wholesome states? At the time when a wholesome consciousness pertaining to the sense-sphere arises, accompanied by gladness, associated with knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by gladness, dissociated from knowledge... or accompanied by gladness, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge... or accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge... or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting, having a form as its object... or... a mental object as its object, or whatever it takes as an object—at that time, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, mentality arises; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, confidence arises; with confidence as condition, determination arises; with determination as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

340. Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi [P 0.0186] …pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā [V 0.0210] saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

340. What are wholesome states? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures... and enters and dwells in the first jhāna, having the earth kasiṇa as its object, at that time, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, mentality arises; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises; with the sixth sense base as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, confidence arises; with confidence as condition, determination arises; with determination as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death arise. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

341. Katame [T 0.0249] dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

341. What are wholesome states? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, having completely transcended the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and due to the abandoning of pleasure... enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna—at that time, conditioned by ignorance, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name arises; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, determination arises; conditioned by determination, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

342. Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā[P 0.0187], vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho[M 0.0194], adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayo hoti.

342. What are wholesome states? At the time when one develops the supramundane jhāna that leads out, leading to the wearing away, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first plane, being quite secluded from sensual pleasures... enters and dwells in the first jhāna with painful practice and slow direct knowledge—at that time, conditioned by ignorance, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name arises; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, determination arises; conditioned by determination, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of these states.

Avijjāmūlakakusalaniddeso.

The exposition of wholesome states rooted in ignorance.

13. Kusalamūlakavipākaniddeso

13. Exposition of the Resultant States Rooted in the Wholesome

343. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa [T 0.0250] kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye [V 0.0211] kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

343. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to having been done and accumulated as wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere, resultant eye-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity and having a form-object—at that time, conditioned by a wholesome root, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name arises; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

344. Tattha katamo kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

344. Therein, what is the volitional formation conditioned by a wholesome root? Volition, the act of volition, and the state of having intended—this is called 'volitional formation conditioned by a wholesome root.' … Therefore, it is said: 'Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.'

345. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ saddārammaṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ gandhārammaṇaṃ…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rasārammaṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti sukhasahagataṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ…pe… manodhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā [T 0.0251] rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro[M 0.0195], saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā[P 0.0188], vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

345. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to having been done and accumulated as wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere, resultant ear-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity and having a sound-object... resultant nose-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity and having an odor-object... resultant tongue-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity and having a taste-object... resultant body-consciousness arises, accompanied by pleasure and having a tangible-object... the mind-element arises, accompanied by equanimity and having a form-object or... a tangible-object... the mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by joy and having a form-object or... a mental-object... the mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by equanimity and having a form-object or... a mental-object, or whatever object it is dependent on—at that time, conditioned by a wholesome root, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name arises; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, determination arises; conditioned by determination, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

346. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā [V 0.0212] vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

346. What states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to having been done and accumulated as wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere, the resultant mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge... accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, with prompting... accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge... accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting... accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge... accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge, with prompting... accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge... accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting, having a form-object or... a mental-object, or whatever object it is dependent on—at that time, conditioned by a wholesome root, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name arises; conditioned by name, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, confidence arises; conditioned by confidence, determination arises; conditioned by determination, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

347. Katame [T 0.0252] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti – ime dhammā kusalā.

347. What states are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, being quite secluded from sensual pleasures... enters and dwells in the first jhāna having the earth kasiṇa as its object—at that time there is contact... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome.

Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ[P 0.0189]. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

As the result of that very wholesome kamma pertaining to the form realm, it having been done and accumulated, one, being secluded from sensual pleasures... and so on... enters and abides in the first jhāna with the earth kasiṇa as object. At that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, faith arises; conditioned by faith, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

348. Katame [M 0.0196] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti – ime dhammā kusalā.

348. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the path for arising in the formless realm, which is accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, and due to the abandoning of pleasure... and so on... enters and abides in the fourth jhāna; at that time, contact occurs... and so on... non-distraction occurs—these phenomena are wholesome.

Tasseva arūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ[T 0.0253], chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo[V 0.0213], bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

As the result of that very wholesome kamma pertaining to the formless realm, it having been done and accumulated, one, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, due to the abandoning of pleasure... and so on... enters and abides in the fourth jhāna. At that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, faith arises; conditioned by faith, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

349. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti – ime dhammā kusalā.

349. Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the supramundane jhāna that is liberating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, being secluded from sensual pleasures... and so on... one enters and abides in the first jhāna of painful practice and slow direct knowledge; at that time, contact occurs... and so on... non-distraction occurs—these phenomena are wholesome.

Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye kusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā pasādo, pasādapaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudayo hoti.

As the result of that very wholesome supramundane jhāna, it having been done and developed, one, being secluded from sensual pleasures... and so on... enters and abides in the first jhāna that is of painful practice, slow direct knowledge, and is empty. At that time, conditioned by wholesome roots, volitional formation arises; conditioned by volitional formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, faith arises; conditioned by faith, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging and death arise. Thus is the origin of these phenomena.

Kusalamūlakavipākaniddeso.

Exposition of the Resultant of Wholesome Roots.

14. Akusalamūlakavipākaniddeso

14. Exposition of the Resultant of Unwholesome Roots.

350. Katame [M 0.0197][P 0.0190] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā [T 0.0254] viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

350. Which states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to unwholesome kamma having been done and accumulated, resultant eye-consciousness accompanied by equanimity, having a form-object, has arisen—at that time, conditioned by unwholesome roots, formations arise; conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense-base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense-base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging-and-death arises. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

351. Tattha katamo akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ [V 0.0214] – ayaṃ vuccati “akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”…pe… tena vuccati “evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

351. Therein, what is the formation conditioned by an unwholesome root? That which is volition, deliberation, the state of having willed—this is called 'the formation conditioned by an unwholesome root.' … Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

352. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ saddārammaṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ gandhārammaṇaṃ…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rasārammaṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti dukkhasahagataṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ…pe… manodhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo [T 0.0255] hoti.

352. Which states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to unwholesome kamma having been done and accumulated, resultant ear-consciousness accompanied by equanimity, having a sound-object, has arisen… or nose-consciousness accompanied by equanimity, having an odor-object, has arisen… or tongue-consciousness accompanied by equanimity, having a taste-object, has arisen… or body-consciousness accompanied by pain, having a tangible-object, has arisen… or mind-element accompanied by equanimity, having a form-object… or a tangible-object, or whatever object it is dependent on, has arisen—at that time, conditioned by unwholesome roots, formations arise; conditioned by formations, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense-base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense-base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, resolution arises; conditioned by resolution, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging-and-death arises. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

353. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ, nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso[M 0.0198], phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho, adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti[P 0.0191], jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.

353. Which states are indeterminate? At the time when, due to unwholesome kamma having been done and accumulated, the resultant mind-consciousness-element has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, having a form-object… or a mind-object, or whatever object it is dependent on—at that time, conditioned by unwholesome roots, formation arises; conditioned by formation, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, mentality arises; conditioned by mentality, the sixth sense-base arises; conditioned by the sixth sense-base, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, determination arises; conditioned by determination, becoming arises; conditioned by becoming, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging-and-death arises. Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.

354. Tattha katamo akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro? Yā cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “akusalamūlapaccayā saṅkhāro”.

354. Therein, what is the formation conditioned by an unwholesome root? That which is volition, thorough volition, the state of having willed—this is called 'the formation conditioned by an unwholesome root.'

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ”.

Therein, what is consciousness conditioned by formation? That which is mind, mentation, heart… the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'consciousness conditioned by formation.'

Tattha [V 0.0215] katamaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho – idaṃ vuccati “viññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ”.

Therein, what is mentality conditioned by consciousness? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of formations—this is called 'mentality conditioned by consciousness.'

Tattha katamaṃ nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatanaṃ”.

Therein, what is the sixth sense-base conditioned by mentality? That which is mind, mentation, heart… the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called 'the sixth sense-base conditioned by mentality.'

Tattha [T 0.0256] katamo chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso? Yo phasso phusanā samphusanā samphusitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”.

Therein, what is contact conditioned by the sixth sense-base? That which is contact, touching, thorough touching, the state of having been thoroughly touched—this is called 'contact conditioned by the sixth sense-base.'

Tattha katamā phassapaccayā vedanā? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati “phassapaccayā vedanā”.

Therein, what is feeling conditioned by contact? That which is mental, neither pleasant nor unpleasant; a felt experience born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant; a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'feeling conditioned by contact.'

Tattha katamo vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho? Yo cittassa adhimokkho adhimuccanā tadadhimuttatā – ayaṃ vuccati “vedanāpaccayā adhimokkho”.

Therein, what is determination conditioned by feeling? The mind's determination, the act of determining, the state of being determined upon that object—this is called 'determination conditioned by feeling.'

Tattha katamo adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo? Ṭhapetvā adhimokkhaṃ, vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimokkhapaccayā bhavo”.

Therein, what is becoming conditioned by determination? Excluding determination, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'becoming conditioned by determination.'

Tattha katamā bhavapaccayā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jāti sañjāti nibbatti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavapaccayā jāti”.

Therein, what is birth conditioned by becoming? The birth, origination, production, reproduction, and manifestation of those various states—this is called 'birth conditioned by becoming.'

Tattha katamaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ? Atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ. Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ jarā jīraṇatā āyuno saṃhāni [M 0.0199] – ayaṃ vuccati jarā. Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yo tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ khayo vayo bhedo paribhedo aniccatā antaradhānaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “maraṇaṃ”. Iti ayañca jarā, idañca maraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ”.

Therein, what is aging-and-death conditioned by birth? There is aging, and there is death. Therein, what is aging? The aging, decrepitude, and decline of the life-faculty of those various states—this is called aging. Therein, what is death? The exhaustion, passing away, breaking up, complete breaking up, impermanence, and disappearance of those various states—this is called death. Thus, this aging and this death—this is called 'aging-and-death conditioned by birth'.

Evametassa [V 0.0216] kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotīti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa saṅgati hoti, samāgamo hoti, samodhānaṃ [T 0.0257] hoti, pātubhāvo hoti. Tena [P 0.0192] vuccati evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī”ti.

Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering. Thus is the conjunction, the coming together, the combination, the manifestation of this entire mass of suffering. Therefore it is said, 'Thus is the arising of this entire mass of suffering.'

Akusalamūlakavipākaniddeso.

Exposition of the Resultant of Unwholesome Roots.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Division.

Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgo paccayākāravibhaṅgo (sī. syā.) niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of Dependent Origination is concluded.

7. Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgo

7. Analysis of the Establishments of Mindfulness

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. Suttanta Division

355. Cattāro [M 0.0200][P 0.0193][V 0.0217] satipaṭṭhānā – idha bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharati bahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, ajjhattaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati bahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, ajjhattaṃ citte cittānupassī viharati bahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, ajjhattaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati bahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

355. There are four establishments of mindfulness. Here, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body internally, dwells contemplating the body in the body externally, dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally—ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings internally, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings externally, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings both internally and externally—ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating the mind in the mind internally, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind externally, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind both internally and externally—ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating dhammas in dhammas internally, dwells contemplating dhammas in dhammas externally, dwells contemplating dhammas in dhammas both internally and externally—ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

1. Kāyānupassanāniddeso

1. Exposition of the Contemplation of the Body

356. Kathañca [T 0.0258] bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – “atthi imasmiṃ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru nahāru (sī.) aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhimiñjā (sī.) vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta”nti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So [V 0.0218] taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā bahiddhā kāye cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

356. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the body in the body internally? Here, a bhikkhu reflects upon this very body from the soles of the feet upward and from the top of the head downward, enclosed by skin and full of various kinds of impurities: 'In this body there are head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, and urine.' He attends to that sign, develops it, and practices it frequently, establishing it well. Having attended to, developed, and frequently practiced that sign, and having established it well, he directs his mind to the body externally.

Kathañca [P 0.0194] bhikkhu bahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu bahiddhā kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – “atthissa kāye kesā lomā [M 0.0201] nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta”nti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā ajjhattabahiddhā kāye cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the body in the body externally? Here, a bhikkhu reflects upon an external body from the soles of the feet upward and from the top of the head downward, enclosed by skin and full of various kinds of impurities: 'In that one's body there are head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, and urine.' He attends to that sign, develops it, and practices it frequently, establishing it well. Having attended to, developed, and frequently practiced that sign, and having established it well, he directs his mind to the body both internally and externally.

Kathañca [T 0.0259] bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – “atthi imasmiṃ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta”nti. Evaṃ bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally? Here, a bhikkhu reflects upon the body both internally and externally from the soles of the feet upward and from the top of the head downward, enclosed by skin and full of various kinds of impurities: 'In this body there are head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, and urine.' Thus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

357. Anupassīti. Tattha katamā anupassanā? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “anupassanā”. Imāya anupassanāya upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “anupassī”ti.

357. Contemplating: What, herein, is contemplation? It is wisdom, discernment… and so on… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'contemplation.' With this contemplation one is endowed, fully endowed, possessed, fully possessed, furnished, accomplished, and complete. Therefore, one is called a 'contemplator.'

358. Viharatīti. Iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

358. Dwells: One moves, proceeds, maintains, supports, carries on, goes about, and dwells. Therefore, it is said 'dwells'.

359. Ātāpīti. Tattha katamo ātāpo katamaṃ ātāpaṃ (sabbattha)? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo [V 0.0219] – ayaṃ vuccati “ātāpo”. Iminā ātāpena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “ātāpī”ti.

359. Ardent: What, herein, is ardor? It is the mental undertaking of energy… and so on… right effort—this is called 'ardor.' With this ardor one is endowed, fully endowed, possessed, fully possessed, furnished, accomplished, and complete. Therefore, one is called 'ardent.'

360. Sampajānoti[T 0.0260][M 0.0202]. Tattha katamaṃ sampajaññaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “sampajaññaṃ”. Iminā sampajaññena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno [P 0.0195] sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “sampajāno”ti.

360. Clearly comprehending: What, herein, is clear comprehension? It is wisdom, discernment… and so on… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'clear comprehension.' With this clear comprehension one is endowed, fully endowed, possessed, fully possessed, furnished, accomplished, and complete. Therefore, one is called 'clearly comprehending.'

361. Satimāti. Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”. Imāya satiyā upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “satimā”ti.

361. Mindful: What, herein, is mindfulness? It is mindfulness, recollection… and so on… right mindfulness—this is called 'mindfulness.' With this mindfulness one is endowed, fully endowed, possessed, fully possessed, furnished, accomplished, and complete. Therefore, one is called 'mindful.'

362. Vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassanti. Tattha katamo loko? Sveva kāyo loko. Pañcapi upādānakkhandhā loko. Ayaṃ vuccati “loko”. Tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “abhijjhā”. Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassaṃ”. Iti ayañca abhijjhā idañca domanassaṃ imamhi loke vinītā honti paṭivinītā santā samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassa”nti.

362. Having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world: Herein, what is the world? This very body is the world. The five aggregates subject to clinging are also the world. This is called 'the world.' Herein, what is covetousness? Whatever is lust, strong lust… and so on… strong lust of the mind—this is called 'covetousness.' Herein, what is displeasure? Whatever is mental unpleasantness, mental pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of mind-contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of mind-contact—this is called 'displeasure.' Thus, this covetousness and this displeasure, in this world, are subdued, thoroughly subdued, calmed, stilled, pacified, gone to cessation, completely gone to cessation, removed, thoroughly removed, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore, it is said, 'having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.'

Kāyānupassanāniddeso.

The Exposition on the Contemplation of the Body is concluded.

2. Vedanānupassanāniddeso

2. The Exposition on the Contemplation of Feelings

363. Kathañca [T 0.0261] bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu sukhaṃ vedanaṃ [V 0.0220] vedayamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “sāmisaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “sāmisaṃ dukkhaṃ [M 0.0203] vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “nirāmisaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “sāmisaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno “nirāmisaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti [P 0.0196] pajānāti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā bahiddhā vedanāsu cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

363. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating feelings in feelings internally? Here, a bhikkhu, when experiencing a pleasant feeling, knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling.’ When experiencing a painful feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a painful feeling.’ When experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Or, when experiencing a carnal pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a carnal pleasant feeling.’ Or, when experiencing a spiritual pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a spiritual pleasant feeling.’ Or, when experiencing a carnal painful feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a carnal painful feeling.’ Or, when experiencing a spiritual painful feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a spiritual painful feeling.’ Or, when experiencing a carnal neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a carnal neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Or, when experiencing a spiritual neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘I am experiencing a spiritual neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ He attends to that sign, develops it, and cultivates it frequently, establishing it well. Having attended to that sign, developed it, and cultivated it frequently, and having established it well, he directs his mind to external feelings.

Kathañca bhikkhu bahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ [T 0.0262] vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “sāmisaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “sāmisaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “nirāmisaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “sāmisaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamānaṃ “nirāmisaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayatī”ti pajānāti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā ajjhattabahiddhā vedanāsu cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating feelings in external feelings? Here, a bhikkhu, when another is experiencing a pleasant feeling, knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a pleasant feeling.’ When another is experiencing a painful feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a painful feeling.’ When another is experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Or, when another is experiencing a carnal pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a carnal pleasant feeling.’ Or, when another is experiencing a spiritual pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a spiritual pleasant feeling.’ Or, when another is experiencing a carnal painful feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a carnal painful feeling.’ Or, when another is experiencing a spiritual painful feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a spiritual painful feeling.’ Or, when another is experiencing a carnal neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a carnal neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Or, when another is experiencing a spiritual neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows distinctly: ‘He is experiencing a spiritual neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ He resorts to that sign, develops it, and cultivates it frequently, establishing it well. Having resorted to that sign, developed it, and cultivated it frequently, and having established it well, he directs his mind to feelings both internal and external.

Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu sukhaṃ vedanaṃ “sukhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ “dukkhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ “adukkhamasukhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ “sāmisā [V 0.0221] sukhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ vedanaṃ “nirāmisā sukhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ “sāmisā dukkhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ “nirāmisā dukkhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, sāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ “sāmisā adukkhamasukhā vedanā”ti pajānāti, nirāmisaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ [M 0.0204] “nirāmisā adukkhamasukhā vedanā”ti pajānāti. Evaṃ bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating feelings in feelings both internal and external? Here, a bhikkhu knows distinctly of a pleasant feeling: ‘It is a pleasant feeling.’ He knows distinctly of a painful feeling: ‘It is a painful feeling.’ He knows distinctly of a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling: ‘It is a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Or, he knows distinctly of a carnal pleasant feeling: ‘It is a carnal pleasant feeling.’ Or, he knows distinctly of a spiritual pleasant feeling: ‘It is a spiritual pleasant feeling.’ Or, he knows distinctly of a carnal painful feeling: ‘It is a carnal painful feeling.’ Or, he knows distinctly of a spiritual painful feeling: ‘It is a spiritual painful feeling.’ Or, he knows distinctly of a carnal neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling: ‘It is a carnal neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Or, he knows distinctly of a spiritual neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling: ‘It is a spiritual neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’ Thus a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings both internal and external—ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.

364. Anupassīti [T 0.0263] …pe… viharatīti…pe… ātāpīti…pe… sampajānoti…pe… [P 0.0197] satimāti…pe… vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassanti. Tattha katamo loko? Sāyeva vedanā loko. Pañcapi upādānakkhandhā loko. Ayaṃ vuccati “loko”. Tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “abhijjhā”. Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassaṃ”. Iti ayañca abhijjhā idañca domanassaṃ imamhi loke vinītā honti paṭivinītā santā samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassa”nti.

364. ‘One who contemplates’ …pe… ‘dwells’ …pe… ‘ardent’ …pe… ‘clearly comprehending’ …pe… ‘mindful’ …pe… ‘having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.’ Herein, what is the world? That very feeling is the world. The five aggregates of clinging are also the world. This is called ‘the world.’ Herein, what is covetousness? Whatever is lust, intense lust …pe… intense lust of the mind—this is called ‘covetousness.’ Herein, what is displeasure? Whatever is mental unpleasantness, mental suffering, the unpleasant painful experience born of mind-contact, and the unpleasant painful feeling born of mind-contact—this is called ‘displeasure.’ Thus, this covetousness and this displeasure are, in this world, removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, quieted, gone to cessation, completely gone to cessation, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore, it is said, ‘having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.’

Vedanānupassanāniddeso.

The Exposition of the Contemplation of Feelings.

3. Cittānupassanāniddeso

3. Exposition of the Contemplation of Mind

365. Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ citte cittānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ “sarāgaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītarāgaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ “sadosaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītadosaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, samohaṃ vā cittaṃ “samohaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, vītamohaṃ [V 0.0222] vā cittaṃ “vītamohaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ “saṃkhittaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ “vikkhittaṃ me citta”nti [T 0.0264] pajānāti, mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ “mahaggataṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ “amahaggataṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ “sauttaraṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ “anuttaraṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ “samāhitaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, asamāhitaṃ [M 0.0205] vā cittaṃ “asamāhitaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ “vimuttaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ “avimuttaṃ me citta”nti pajānāti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā bahiddhā citte cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

365. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the mind in the mind internally? Here, a bhikkhu knows a mind with lust as ‘my mind is with lust,’ or a mind without lust as ‘my mind is without lust’; he knows a mind with hate as ‘my mind is with hate,’ or a mind without hate as ‘my mind is without hate’; he knows a mind with delusion as ‘my mind is with delusion,’ or a mind without delusion as ‘my mind is without delusion’; he knows a contracted mind as ‘my mind is contracted,’ or a scattered mind as ‘my mind is scattered’; he knows a sublime mind as ‘my mind is sublime,’ or an unsublime mind as ‘my mind is unsublime’; he knows a surpassable mind as ‘my mind is surpassable,’ or an unsurpassable mind as ‘my mind is unsurpassable’; he knows a concentrated mind as ‘my mind is concentrated,’ or an unconcentrated mind as ‘my mind is unconcentrated’; he knows a liberated mind as ‘my mind is liberated,’ or an unliberated mind as ‘my mind is unliberated.’ He attends to that sign, develops it, and makes much of it; he makes it well established. Having attended to that sign, developed it, made much of it, and made it well established, he directs his mind to the mind externally.

Kathañca bhikkhu bahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu sarāgaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “sarāgamassa citta”nti pajānāti, vītarāgaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “vītarāgamassa citta”nti pajānāti, sadosaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “sadosamassa citta”nti [P 0.0198] pajānāti, vītadosaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “vītadosamassa citta”nti pajānāti, samohaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “samohamassa citta”nti pajānāti, vītamohaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “vītamohamassa citta”nti pajānāti, saṃkhittaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “saṃkhittamassa citta”nti pajānāti, vikkhittaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “vikkhittamassa citta”nti pajānāti, mahaggataṃ vāssa cittaṃ “mahaggatamassa citta”nti pajānāti, amahaggataṃ vāssa cittaṃ “amahaggatamassa citta”nti pajānāti, sauttaraṃ vāssa cittaṃ “sauttaramassa citta”nti pajānāti, anuttaraṃ vāssa [T 0.0265] cittaṃ “anuttaramassa citta”nti pajānāti, samāhitaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “samāhitamassa citta”nti pajānāti, asamāhitaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “asamāhitamassa citta”nti pajānāti, vimuttaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “vimuttamassa citta”nti pajānāti, avimuttaṃ vāssa cittaṃ “avimuttamassa citta”nti pajānāti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā ajjhattabahiddhā citte cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the mind in the mind externally? Here, a bhikkhu knows the mind of another with lust as ‘this person’s mind is with lust,’ or the mind of another without lust as ‘this person’s mind is without lust’; he knows the mind of another with hate as ‘this person’s mind is with hate,’ or the mind of another without hate as ‘this person’s mind is without hate’; he knows the mind of another with delusion as ‘this person’s mind is with delusion,’ or the mind of another without delusion as ‘this person’s mind is without delusion’; he knows a contracted mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is contracted,’ or a scattered mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is scattered’; he knows a sublime mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is sublime,’ or an unsublime mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is unsublime’; he knows a surpassable mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is surpassable,’ or an unsurpassable mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is unsurpassable’; he knows a concentrated mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is concentrated,’ or an unconcentrated mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is unconcentrated’; he knows a liberated mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is liberated,’ or an unliberated mind of another as ‘this person’s mind is unliberated.’ He attends to that sign, develops it, and makes much of it; he establishes it well. Having attended to that sign, developed it, made much of it, and established it well, he brings his mind to bear on the mind internally and externally.

Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ “sarāgaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītarāgaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, sadosaṃ [V 0.0223] vā cittaṃ “sadosaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītadosaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, samohaṃ vā cittaṃ “samohaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītamohaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ “saṃkhittaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ “vikkhittaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ “mahaggataṃ citta”nti pajānāti, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ “amahaggataṃ citta”nti pajānāti, sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ “sauttaraṃ citta”nti pajānāti, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ “anuttaraṃ citta”nti pajānāti[M 0.0206], samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ “samāhitaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ “asamāhitaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ “vimuttaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ “avimuttaṃ citta”nti pajānāti. Evaṃ bhikkhu [T 0.0266] ajjhattabahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the mind in the mind internally and externally? Here, a bhikkhu knows a mind with lust as ‘a mind with lust’; a mind without lust as ‘a mind without lust’; a mind with hate as ‘a mind with hate’; a mind without hate as ‘a mind without hate’; a mind with delusion as ‘a mind with delusion’; a mind without delusion as ‘a mind without delusion’; a contracted mind as ‘a contracted mind’; a scattered mind as ‘a scattered mind’; a sublime mind as ‘a sublime mind’; an unsublime mind as ‘an unsublime mind’; a surpassable mind as ‘a surpassable mind’; an unsurpassed mind as ‘an unsurpassed mind’; a concentrated mind as ‘a concentrated mind’; an unconcentrated mind as ‘an unconcentrated mind’; a liberated mind as ‘a liberated mind’; an unliberated mind as ‘an unliberated mind.’ Thus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the mind in the mind internally and externally, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

366. Anupassīti…pe… viharatīti…pe… ātāpīti…pe… sampajānoti…pe… satimāti…pe… vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassanti. Tattha katamo loko? Taṃyeva cittaṃ loko. Pañcapi upādānakkhandhā loko – tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo [P 0.0199] rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “abhijjhā”. Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassaṃ”. Iti ayañca abhijjhā idañca domanassaṃ imamhi loke vinītā honti paṭivinītā santā samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassa”nti.

366. ‘Contemplating’... and so on... ‘dwells’... and so on... ‘ardent’... and so on... ‘clearly comprehending’... and so on... ‘mindful’... and so on... ‘having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.’ Herein, what is the world? That very mind is the world. The five aggregates of clinging are also the world. Herein, what is covetousness? Whatever is lust, strong lust... the strong lust of the mind—this is called ‘covetousness.’ Herein, what is displeasure? Whatever is mental unpleasantness, mental suffering, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of mind-contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is born of mind-contact—this is called ‘displeasure.’ Thus, this covetousness and this displeasure are removed in this world, utterly removed, calmed, stilled, pacified, gone to setting, completely gone to setting, abandoned, completely abandoned, dried up, utterly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore, it is said, ‘having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.’

Cittānupassanāniddeso.

The Exposition of the Contemplation of the Mind is finished.

4. Dhammānupassanāniddeso

4. The Exposition of the Contemplation of Phenomena

367. Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu santaṃ vā [V 0.0224] ajjhattaṃ kāmacchandaṃ “atthi me ajjhattaṃ kāmacchando”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ kāmacchandaṃ “natthi me ajjhattaṃ kāmacchando”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa kāmacchandassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa [T 0.0267] kāmacchandassa pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa kāmacchandassa āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti. Santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ byāpādaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ thinamiddhaṃ thīnamiddhaṃ (sī. syā.) …pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ uddhaccakukkuccaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ vicikicchaṃ “atthi me ajjhattaṃ vicikicchā”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ vicikicchaṃ “natthi me ajjhattaṃ vicikicchā”ti [M 0.0207] pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannāya vicikicchāya uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannāya vicikicchāya pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnāya vicikicchāya āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.

367. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating phenomena in phenomena internally? Here, a bhikkhu, when sensual desire is present in him internally, knows: ‘There is sensual desire in me internally.’ When sensual desire is not present in him internally, he knows: ‘There is no sensual desire in me internally.’ He knows how unarisen sensual desire arises, how arisen sensual desire is abandoned, and how abandoned sensual desire will not arise in the future. When ill will is present in him internally... and so on... when sloth and torpor are present in him internally... and so on... when restlessness and remorse are present in him internally... and so on... when doubt is present in him internally, he knows: ‘There is doubt in me internally.’ When doubt is not present in him internally, he knows: ‘There is no doubt in me internally.’ He knows how unarisen doubt arises, how arisen doubt is abandoned, and how abandoned doubt will not arise in the future.

Santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ “atthi me ajjhattaṃ satisambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ “natthi me ajjhattaṃ satisambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti, santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ viriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ (sī. syā.) …pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ [P 0.0200] …pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ “atthi me ajjhattaṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ [T 0.0268] “natthi me ajjhattaṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā bahiddhā dhammesu cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

When the mindfulness enlightenment factor is present in him internally, he knows distinctly: ‘The mindfulness enlightenment factor is present in me internally.’ When the mindfulness enlightenment factor is not present in him internally, he knows distinctly: ‘The mindfulness enlightenment factor is not present in me internally.’ He also knows distinctly how the arising of the unarisen mindfulness enlightenment factor comes to be, and he knows distinctly how the arisen mindfulness enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment through development. When the investigation-of-phenomena enlightenment factor is present in him internally... and so on... when the energy enlightenment factor is present in him internally... and so on... when the joy enlightenment factor is present in him internally... and so on... when the tranquility enlightenment factor is present in him internally... and so on... when the concentration enlightenment factor is present in him internally... and so on... when the equanimity enlightenment factor is present in him internally, he knows distinctly: ‘The equanimity enlightenment factor is present in me internally.’ When the equanimity enlightenment factor is not present in him internally, he knows distinctly: ‘The equanimity enlightenment factor is not present in me internally.’ He also knows distinctly how the arising of the unarisen equanimity enlightenment factor comes to be, and he knows distinctly how the arisen equanimity enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment through development. He frequents that sign, develops it, makes much of it, and establishes it well. Having frequented that sign, developed it, made much of it, and established it well, he directs his mind to external phenomena.

Kathañca bhikkhu bahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu santaṃ vāssa kāmacchandaṃ “atthissa kāmacchando”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vāssa kāmacchandaṃ “natthissa kāmacchando”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa kāmacchandassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti[V 0.0225], yathā ca uppannassa kāmacchandassa pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnassa kāmacchandassa āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti. Santaṃ vāssa byāpādaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa thinamiddhaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa uddhaccakukkuccaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa vicikicchaṃ “atthissa vicikicchā”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vāssa vicikicchaṃ “natthissa vicikicchā”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannāya vicikicchāya [M 0.0208] uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannāya vicikicchāya pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnāya vicikicchāya āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating phenomena as phenomena externally? Here, when sensual desire is present in another, a bhikkhu understands: 'There is sensual desire in him.' When sensual desire is not present in another, he understands: 'There is no sensual desire in him.' He understands how unarisen sensual desire comes to arise; he understands how arisen sensual desire comes to be abandoned; and he understands how abandoned sensual desire will not arise in the future. When ill will is present in another... and so on... when sloth and torpor are present in another... and so on... when restlessness and remorse are present in another... and so on... when doubt is present in another, he understands: 'There is doubt in him.' When doubt is not present in another, he understands: 'There is no doubt in him.' He understands how unarisen doubt comes to arise; he understands how arisen doubt comes to be abandoned; and he understands how abandoned doubt will not arise in the future.

Santaṃ vāssa satisambojjhaṅgaṃ “atthissa satisambojjhaṅgo”ti [T 0.0269] pajānāti, asantaṃ vāssa satisambojjhaṅgaṃ “natthissa satisambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti. Santaṃ vāssa dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vāssa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ “atthissa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vāssa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ [P 0.0201] “natthissa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapeti. So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevitvā bhāvetvā bahulīkaritvā svāvatthitaṃ vavatthapetvā ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu cittaṃ upasaṃharati.

When the mindfulness enlightenment factor is present in another, he understands: 'The mindfulness enlightenment factor is present in him.' When the mindfulness enlightenment factor is not present in another, he understands: 'The mindfulness enlightenment factor is not present in him.' He understands how the unarisen mindfulness enlightenment factor comes to arise, and he understands how the arisen mindfulness enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment through cultivation. When the investigation-of-phenomena enlightenment factor is present in another... and so on... when the energy enlightenment factor is present in another... and so on... when the joy enlightenment factor is present in another... and so on... when the tranquility enlightenment factor is present in another... and so on... when the concentration enlightenment factor is present in another... and so on... when the equanimity enlightenment factor is present in another, he understands: 'The equanimity enlightenment factor is present in him.' When the equanimity enlightenment factor is not present in another, he understands: 'The equanimity enlightenment factor is not present in him.' He understands how the unarisen equanimity enlightenment factor comes to arise, and he understands how the arisen equanimity enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment through cultivation. He frequents that sign, develops it, makes much of it, and establishes it well. Having frequented that sign, developed it, made much of it, and established it well, he directs his mind to internal and external phenomena.

Kathañca bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu santaṃ vā kāmacchandaṃ “atthi kāmacchando”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā kāmacchandaṃ “natthi kāmacchando”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa kāmacchandassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa kāmacchandassa pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti[T 0.0270], yathā ca pahīnassa kāmacchandassa āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti. Santaṃ vā byāpādaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā thinamiddhaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā vicikicchaṃ “atthi vicikicchā”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā vicikicchaṃ “natthi vicikicchā”ti [V 0.0226] pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannāya vicikicchāya uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannāya vicikicchāya pahānaṃ hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca pahīnāya vicikicchāya āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti tañca pajānāti.

And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating phenomena as phenomena internally and externally? Here, when sensual desire is present, a bhikkhu understands: 'There is sensual desire.' When sensual desire is not present, he understands: 'There is no sensual desire.' He understands how unarisen sensual desire comes to arise; he understands how arisen sensual desire comes to be abandoned; and he understands how abandoned sensual desire will not arise in the future. When ill will is present... and so on... when sloth and torpor are present... and so on... when restlessness and remorse are present... and so on... when doubt is present, he understands: 'There is doubt.' When doubt is not present, he understands: 'There is no doubt.' He understands how unarisen doubt comes to arise; he understands how arisen doubt comes to be abandoned; and he understands how abandoned doubt will not arise in the future.

Santaṃ [M 0.0209] vā satisambojjhaṅgaṃ “atthi satisambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā satisambojjhaṅgaṃ “natthi satisambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti. Santaṃ vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ…pe… santaṃ vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ “atthi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, asantaṃ vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ “natthi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti pajānāti, yathā ca anuppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti tañca pajānāti, yathā ca uppannassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti tañca pajānāti. Evaṃ bhikkhu ajjhattabahiddhā [T 0.0271] dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

When the enlightenment factor of mindfulness is present, he understands: 'The enlightenment factor of mindfulness is present.' When the enlightenment factor of mindfulness is not present, he understands: 'The enlightenment factor of mindfulness is not present.' He understands how the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness comes to arise, and he understands how the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness comes to fulfillment through cultivation. When the enlightenment factor of investigation-of-phenomena is present... when the enlightenment factor of energy is present... when the enlightenment factor of joy is present... when the enlightenment factor of tranquility is present... when the enlightenment factor of concentration is present... when the enlightenment factor of equanimity is present, he understands: 'The enlightenment factor of equanimity is present.' When the enlightenment factor of equanimity is not present, he understands: 'The enlightenment factor of equanimity is not present.' He understands how the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity comes to arise, and he understands how the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity comes to fulfillment through cultivation. Thus a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena internally and externally—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having dispelled covetousness and displeasure in the world.

368. Anupassīti. Tattha katamā anupassanā? Yā [P 0.0202] paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati anupassanā. Imāya anupassanāya upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “anupassī”ti.

368. Regarding 'contemplating' (anupassī). Herein, what is contemplation (anupassanā)? It is the wisdom, the act of knowing... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called contemplation. One is endowed with this contemplation, fully endowed, has arrived at it, has fully arrived at it, is furnished with it, is accomplished in it, and is completely endowed with it. Therefore, one is called 'contemplating'.

369. Viharatīti. Iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.
