369. Regarding 'he dwells' (viharati). He moves, proceeds, maintains, keeps going, causes to go on, conducts himself, and dwells. Therefore, it is said, 'he dwells'.

370. Ātāpīti. Tattha katamo ātāpo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati “ātāpo”. Iminā ātāpena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “ātāpī”ti.

370. Regarding 'ardent' (ātāpī). Herein, what is ardor (ātāpa)? It is the mental arousal of energy... right effort—this is called 'ardor'. One is endowed with this ardor... is completely endowed with it. Therefore, one is called 'ardent'.

371. Sampajānoti[V 0.0227]. Tattha katamaṃ sampajaññaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “sampajaññaṃ”. Iminā sampajaññena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “sampajāno”ti.

371. Regarding 'clearly comprehending' (sampajāno). Herein, what is clear comprehension (sampajaññaṃ)? It is the wisdom, the act of knowing... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'clear comprehension'. One is endowed with this clear comprehension... is completely endowed with it. Therefore, one is called 'clearly comprehending'.

372. Satimāti[M 0.0210]. Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”. Imāya satiyā upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “satimā”ti.

372. Regarding 'mindful' (satimā). Herein, what is mindfulness (sati)? It is the mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness—this is called 'mindfulness'. One is endowed with this mindfulness... is completely endowed with it. Therefore, one is called 'mindful'.

373. Vineyya [T 0.0272] loke abhijjhādomanassanti. Tattha katamo loko? Teva dhammā loko. Pañcapi upādānakkhandhā loko. Ayaṃ vuccati “loko”. Tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “abhijjhā”. Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassaṃ”. Iti ayañca abhijjhā idañca domanassaṃ imamhi loke vinītā honti paṭivinītā santā samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassa”nti.

373. Regarding 'having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world' (vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ). Herein, what is the world (loko)? Those very phenomena are the world. The five aggregates subject to clinging are also the world. This is called 'the world'. Herein, what is covetousness (abhijjhā)? It is the lust, intense lust... the mind’s intense lust—this is called 'covetousness'. Herein, what is displeasure (domanassaṃ)? Whatever is mental unpleasantness, mental suffering, an unpleasant, painful feeling born of mind-contact, an unpleasant, painful sensation born of mind-contact—this is called 'displeasure'. Thus, this covetousness and this displeasure have been subdued in this world, thoroughly subdued, calmed, stilled, pacified, ceased, completely ceased, given up, utterly given up, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and made an end of. Therefore, it is said, 'having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world'.

Dhammānupassanāniddeso.

End of the Exposition on the Contemplation of Phenomena.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

End of the Sutta-Style Analysis.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Analysis.

374. Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā – idha bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati, vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, citte cittānupassī viharati, dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati.

374. There are four establishments of mindfulness: here a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, and dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena.

375. Kathañca [P 0.0203] bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ [V 0.0228] jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ kāye kāyānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati [T 0.0273] satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

375. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the body in the body? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... having entered and dwelling in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge, he dwells contemplating the body in the body. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining phenomena are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

376. Kathañca [M 0.0211] bhikkhu vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati satipaṭṭhānaṃ. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

376. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating feelings in feelings? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... having entered and dwelling in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge, he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining phenomena are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

377. Kathañca bhikkhu citte cittānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ citte cittānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

377. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the mind in the mind? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... having entered and dwelling in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge, he dwells contemplating the mind in the mind. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining phenomena are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

378. Kathañca bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ [T 0.0274] – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

378. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating phenomena in phenomena? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge, contemplating phenomena in phenomena. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining phenomena are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

379. Tattha katamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ [V 0.0229] apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

379. Therein, what is the establishment of mindfulness? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge, contemplating phenomena in phenomena. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining phenomena are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

380. Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā – idha bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati, vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, citte cittānupassī viharati, dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati.

380. There are four establishments of mindfulness: here a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, and dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena.

381. Kathañca [M 0.0212][P 0.0204] bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ kāye kāyānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ [T 0.0275] – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

381. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the body in the body? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, contact arises... non-distraction arises. These states are wholesome. On account of that very supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, as its resultant—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice, slow direct knowledge, and is empty, contemplating the body in the body. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining states are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

382. Kathañca bhikkhu vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

382. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating feelings in feelings? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, contact arises... non-distraction arises. These states are wholesome. On account of that very supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, as its resultant—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice, slow direct knowledge, and is empty, contemplating feelings in feelings. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining states are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

383. Kathañca bhikkhu citte cittānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā [V 0.0230] vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ citte cittānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo [T 0.0276] maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

383. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating the mind in the mind? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, contact arises... non-distraction arises. These states are wholesome. On account of that very supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, as its resultant—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice, slow direct knowledge, and is empty, contemplating the mind in the mind. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining states are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

384. Kathañca [M 0.0213][P 0.0205] bhikkhu dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

384. And how does a bhikkhu dwell contemplating phenomena in phenomena? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, contact arises... non-distraction arises. These states are wholesome. On account of that very supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, as its resultant—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice, slow direct knowledge, and is empty, contemplating phenomena in phenomena. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining states are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

385. Tattha katamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo [T 0.0277] maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “satipaṭṭhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā satipaṭṭhānasampayuttā.

385. Therein, what is the establishment of mindfulness? Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which is emancipating, which leads to the decrease of rebirths—for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, quite secluded from sensual pleasures... having entered, he dwells in the first jhāna, which has painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, contact arises... non-distraction arises. These states are wholesome. On account of that very supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and having been developed, its resultant—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... having entered, he dwells in the first jhāna, which has painful practice, slow direct knowledge, and is empty. At that time, whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, that which is included in the path, there is—this is called 'the establishment of mindfulness'. The remaining states are associated with the establishment of mindfulness.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Method of Analysis

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Questioning Section

386. Cattāro [V 0.0231] satipaṭṭhānā – idha bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

386. There are four establishments of mindfulness. Here, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating dhammas in dhammas, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.

387. Catunnaṃ [M 0.0214][P 0.0206] satipaṭṭhānānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

387. Of the four establishments of mindfulness, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, how many are indeterminate... and so on... how many are with defilements, how many are without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

388. Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā siyā vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā[T 0.0278], siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

388. Some are wholesome; some are indeterminate. Some are associated with pleasant feeling; some are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Some are resultant; some are result-producing dhammas. Not taken up and not an object for clinging. Undefiled and not an object for defilements. Some are with initial and sustained application; some are with sustained application only; some are without initial and sustained application. Some are accompanied by joy; some are accompanied by happiness; some are accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. They do not have a cause that is to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation. Some are conducive to decrease; some are conducive neither to increase nor to decrease. Some are of trainees; some are of non-trainees. Immeasurable. Having an immeasurable object. Sublime. Some are fixed in rightness; some are unfixed. They do not have the path as object; some have the path as cause; some have the path as dominant factor; but it should not be said that they have the path as cause, nor that they have the path as dominant factor. Some are arisen; some are not arisen; some are liable to arise. Some are past; some are future; some are present; but it should not be said that they have a past object, nor a future object, nor a present object. Some are internal; some are external; some are internal-external. They have an external object. Non-manifestative and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

389. Na [V 0.0232] hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Na hetū sahetukā.

389. They are not causes. They are with causes. They are associated with causes. It should not be said that they are both causes and with causes; they are with causes but are not causes. It should not be said that they are both causes and associated with causes; they are associated with causes but are not causes. They are not causes but are with causes.

Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavācātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttācātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no [M 0.0215] yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā[T 0.0279]. No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.

They are with conditions. They are conditioned. Non-manifestative. Non-resistant. Immaterial. Supramundane. Cognizable by some consciousness, not cognizable by some consciousness. They are not taints. They are not objects of taints. They are dissociated from taints. It should not be said that they are both taints and objects of taints, nor that they are objects of taints but are not taints. It should not be said that they are both taints and associated with taints, nor that they are associated with taints but are not taints. They are dissociated from taints and are not objects of taints. They are not fetters... and so on... not bonds... and so on... not floods... and so on... not yokes... and so on... not hindrances... and so on... not misapprehensions... and so on... They are with an object. They are not mind. They are mental factors. Associated with mind. Conjoined with mind. Arisen from mind. Coexistent with mind. Following mind. Conjoined with and arisen from mind. Conjoined with, arisen from, and coexistent with mind. Conjoined with, arisen from, and following mind. They are external. Not derivative. Not taken up. They are not clingings... and so on... not defilements... and so on... Not to be abandoned by vision, not to be abandoned by cultivation. Not having a cause to be abandoned by vision. Not having a cause to be abandoned by cultivation.

Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā[P 0.0207]. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

Some are with initial application; some are without initial application. Some are with sustained application; some are without sustained application. Some are with joy; some are without joy. Some are accompanied by joy; some are not accompanied by joy. Some are accompanied by happiness; some are not accompanied by happiness. Some are accompanied by equanimity; some are not accompanied by equanimity. They are not of the sense-sphere. They are not of the form-sphere. They are not of the formless-sphere. They are unincluded. Some are emancipating; some are not emancipating. Some are fixed; some are unfixed. They are unsurpassed. They are without defilements.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

End of the Questioning Section.

Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Establishments of Mindfulness is concluded.

8. Sammappadhānavibhaṅgo

8. The Analysis of the Right Strivings

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Sutta Method of Analysis

390. Cattāro [M 0.0216][P 0.0208][V 0.0233] sammappadhānā – idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ [T 0.0280] dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

390. There are four Right Strivings. Here, a monk, for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen, generates zeal, strives, arouses energy, uplifts his mind, and makes a resolute effort. For the abandoning of evil, unwholesome states that have arisen, he generates zeal, strives, arouses energy, uplifts his mind, and makes a resolute effort. For the arising of wholesome states that have not yet arisen, he generates zeal, strives, arouses energy, uplifts his mind, and makes a resolute effort. For the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, abundance, development, and fulfillment of wholesome states that have arisen, he generates zeal, strives, arouses energy, uplifts his mind, and makes a resolute effort.

391. Kathañca bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Tattha katame anuppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime vuccanti “anuppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā”. Iti imesaṃ anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

391. And how does a monk, for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen, generate zeal, strive, arouse energy, uplift his mind, and make a resolute effort? Therein, what are the evil, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen? The three unwholesome roots: greed, hatred, and delusion. And the defilements that are associated with them; the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily action, verbal action, and mental action originating from them—these are called 'evil, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen.' Thus, for the non-arising of these evil, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen, he generates zeal, strives, arouses energy, uplifts his mind, and makes a resolute effort.

392. Chandaṃ janetīti. Tattha katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā chandīkatā (syā.) kattukamyatā kusalo [V 0.0234] dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati “chando”. Imaṃ chandaṃ janeti sañjaneti uṭṭhapeti samuṭṭhapeti uṭṭhāpeti samuṭṭhāpeti (syā.) evamuparipi nibbatteti abhinibbatteti. Tena vuccati “chandaṃ janetī”ti.

392. 'He generates zeal.' Therein, what is zeal? Whatever zeal, state of zeal, wish to act, wholesome zeal for the Dhamma—this is called 'zeal.' He generates, well generates, raises up, well raises up, produces, and fully produces this zeal. Therefore, it is said, 'he generates zeal.'

393. Vāyamatīti. Tattha katamo vāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ [P 0.0209] vuccati “vāyāmo”. Iminā vāyāmena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vāyamatī”ti.

393. 'He strives.' Therein, what is striving? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and so forth... right effort—this is called 'striving.' He is endowed, well endowed, possessed, well possessed, furnished, fully furnished, and supplied with this striving. Therefore, it is said, 'he strives.'

394. Vīriyaṃ [T 0.0281][M 0.0217] ārabhatīti. Tattha katamaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati “vīriyaṃ”. Imaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhati samārabhati āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “vīriyaṃ ārabhatī”ti.

394. 'He arouses energy.' Therein, what is energy? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and so forth... right effort—this is called 'energy.' He arouses, fully arouses, pursues, develops, and makes much of this energy. Therefore, it is said, 'he arouses energy.'

395. Cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Imaṃ cittaṃ paggaṇhāti sampaggaṇhāti upatthambheti paccupatthambheti. Tena vuccati “cittaṃ paggaṇhātī”ti.

395. 'He uplifts his mind.' Therein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, intellect, mentality... and so forth... the mind-consciousness element corresponding to that—this is called 'mind.' He uplifts, uplifts well, supports, and repeatedly supports this mind. Therefore, it is said, 'he uplifts his mind.'

396. Padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ padhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati “padhānaṃ”. Iminā padhānena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “padahatī”ti.

396. 'He makes a resolute effort.' Therein, what is resolute effort? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and so forth... right effort—this is called 'resolute effort.' He is endowed with... and so forth... and supplied with this resolute effort. Therefore, it is said, 'he makes a resolute effort.'

397. Kathañca bhikkhu uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Tattha katame uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā? Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho, doso, moho. Tadekaṭṭhā ca kilesā. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho, taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime vuccanti “uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā”. Iti imesaṃ uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

397. And how does a monk, for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome states that have arisen, generate zeal, strive, arouse energy, uplift his mind, and make a resolute effort? Therein, what are the evil, unwholesome states that have arisen? The three unwholesome roots: greed, hatred, and delusion. And the defilements that are associated with them; the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate associated with them; and the bodily action, verbal action, and mental action originating from them—these are called 'evil, unwholesome states that have arisen.' Thus, for the abandoning of these evil, unwholesome states that have arisen, he generates zeal, strives, arouses energy, uplifts his mind, and makes a resolute effort.

398. Chandaṃ [T 0.0282] janetīti. Tattha katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo [V 0.0235] dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati “chando”. Imaṃ chandaṃ janeti sañjaneti uṭṭhapeti samuṭṭhapeti nibbatteti abhinibbatteti. Tena vuccati “chandaṃ janetī”ti.

398. 'He generates zeal.' Therein, what is zeal? Whatever zeal, state of zeal, wish to act, wholesome zeal for the Dhamma—this is called 'zeal.' He generates, well generates, raises up, well raises up, produces, and fully produces this zeal. Therefore, it is said, 'he generates zeal.'

399. Vāyamatīti. Tattha katamo vāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati “vāyāmo”. Iminā vāyāmena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vāyamatī”ti.

399. 'He strives.' Therein, what is striving? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and so forth... right effort—this is called 'striving.' He is endowed with... and so forth... and supplied with this striving. Therefore, it is said, 'he strives.'

400. Vīriyaṃ [M 0.0218] ārabhatīti. Tattha katamaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati “vīriyaṃ”. Imaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhati samārabhati āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “vīriyaṃ ārabhatī”ti.

400. 'He arouses energy.' Therein, what is energy? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and so forth... right effort—this is called 'energy.' He arouses, fully arouses, pursues, develops, and makes much of this energy. Therefore, it is said, 'he arouses energy.'

401. Cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Imaṃ cittaṃ paggaṇhāti sampaggaṇhāti upatthambheti paccupatthambheti. Tena vuccati “cittaṃ paggaṇhātī”ti.

401. 'He uplifts his mind.' Therein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, intellect, mentality... and so forth... the mind-consciousness element corresponding to that—this is called 'mind.' He uplifts, uplifts well, supports, and repeatedly supports this mind. Therefore, it is said, 'he uplifts his mind.'

402. Padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ padhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati “padhānaṃ”. Iminā padhānena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “padahatī”ti.

402. 'He makes a resolute effort.' Therein, what is resolute effort? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and so forth... right effort—this is called 'resolute effort.' He is endowed with... and so forth... and supplied with this resolute effort. Therefore, it is said, 'he makes a resolute effort.'

403. Kathañca bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Tattha [P 0.0210] katame [T 0.0283] anuppannā kusalā dhammā? Tīṇi kusalamūlāni – alobho, adoso, amoho. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho. Taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, manokammaṃ – ime vuccanti “anuppannā kusalā dhammā”. Iti imesaṃ anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

403. And how does a bhikkhu generate desire, strive, arouse energy, uplift the mind, and exert himself for the arising of unarisen wholesome states? Herein, what are the unarisen wholesome states? The three wholesome roots: non-greed, non-aversion, and non-delusion. Associated with them are the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate. Originating from them are bodily action, verbal action, and mental action—these are called 'unarisen wholesome states.' Thus, for the arising of these unarisen wholesome states, he generates desire, strives, arouses energy, uplifts the mind, and exerts himself.

404. Chandaṃ janetīti…pe… vāyamatīti…pe… vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti…pe… cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti…pe… padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ padhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho [V 0.0236] …pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati “padhānaṃ”. Iminā padhānena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “padahatī”ti.

404. 'He generates desire'... 'he strives'... 'he arouses energy'... 'he uplifts the mind'... 'he exerts himself.' Herein, what is exertion? Whatever mental arousal of energy... right effort—this is called 'exertion.' He is endowed with this exertion... possessed of it. Therefore, it is said, 'he exerts himself.'

405. Kathañca bhikkhu uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Tattha katame uppannā kusalā dhammā? Tīṇi kusalamūlāni – alobho, adoso, amoho. Taṃsampayutto vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho[M 0.0219], taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ime vuccanti “uppannā kusalā dhammā”. Iti imesaṃ uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

405. And how does a bhikkhu generate desire, strive, arouse energy, uplift the mind, and exert himself for the stability, for the non-confusion, for the increase, for the expansion, for the development, and for the fulfillment of arisen wholesome states? Herein, what are the arisen wholesome states? The three wholesome roots: non-greed, non-aversion, and non-delusion. Associated with them are the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate; originating from them are bodily action, verbal action, and mental action—these are called 'arisen wholesome states.' Thus, for the stability, for the non-confusion, for the increase, for the expansion, for the development, and for the fulfillment of these arisen wholesome states, he generates desire, strives, arouses energy, uplifts the mind, and exerts himself.

406. Ṭhitiyāti. Yā ṭhiti so asammoso, yo asammoso so bhiyyobhāvo[T 0.0284], yo bhiyyobhāvo taṃ vepullaṃ, yaṃ vepullaṃ sā bhāvanā, yā bhāvanā sā pāripūrī.

406. As for 'stability': Whatever is stability is non-confusion; whatever is non-confusion is increase; whatever is increase is expansion; whatever is expansion is development; whatever is development is fulfillment.

407. Chandaṃ janetīti…pe… vāyamatīti…pe… vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti…pe… cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti…pe… padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ padhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati “padhānaṃ”. Iminā padhānena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “padahatī”ti.

407. 'He generates desire'... 'he strives'... 'he arouses energy'... 'he uplifts the mind'... 'he exerts himself.' Herein, what is exertion? Whatever mental arousal of energy... right effort—this is called 'exertion.' He is endowed with this exertion... possessed of it. Therefore, it is said, 'he exerts himself.'

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Suttanta Analysis is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Analysis

408. Cattāro [P 0.0211] sammappadhānā – idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ [V 0.0237] akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

408. There are four right exertions. Here, a bhikkhu generates desire, strives, undertakes effort, uplifts the mind, and exerts himself for the non-arising of unarisen, evil, unwholesome states. He generates desire, strives, undertakes effort, uplifts the mind, and exerts himself for the abandoning of arisen, evil, unwholesome states. He generates desire, strives, undertakes effort, uplifts the mind, and exerts himself for the arising of unarisen wholesome states. He generates desire, strives, undertakes effort, uplifts the mind, and exerts himself for the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, abundance, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states.

409. Kathañca bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ [T 0.0285] diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā [M 0.0220] vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

409. And how does a bhikkhu generate desire, strive, undertake effort, uplift the mind, and exert himself for the non-arising of unarisen, evil, unwholesome states? Here, when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of accumulation, for the abandonment of views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, he generates desire, strives, undertakes effort, uplifts the mind, and exerts himself for the non-arising of unarisen, evil, unwholesome states.

410. Chandaṃ janetīti. Tattha katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati “chando”. Imaṃ chandaṃ janeti sañjaneti uṭṭhapeti samuṭṭhapeti nibbatteti abhinibbatteti. Tena vuccati “chandaṃ janetī”ti.

410. 'He generates desire.' Herein, what is desire? That which is desire, a state of desiring, a wish to do, a wholesome desire for the Dhamma—this is called 'desire.' He generates this desire, produces it, arouses it, brings it forth, brings it into being, and brings it into being anew. Therefore, it is said, 'he generates desire.'

411. Vāyamatīti. Tattha katamo vāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vāyāmo”. Iminā vāyāmena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vāyamatī”ti.

411. 'He strives.' Herein, what is striving? That which is the mental arousal of energy… right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'striving.' With this striving, he is endowed, well endowed, has approached, has well approached, is possessed of, is accomplished in, and is fully possessed of. Therefore, it is said, 'he strives.'

412. Vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti. Tattha katamaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ [P 0.0212] vuccati “vīriyaṃ”. Imaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhati samārabhati āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “vīriyaṃ ārabhatī”ti.

412. 'He undertakes effort.' Herein, what is effort? That which is the mental arousal of energy… right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'effort.' He undertakes this effort, fully undertakes it, cultivates it, develops it, and makes much of it. Therefore, it is said, 'he undertakes effort.'

413. Cittaṃ [T 0.0286] paggaṇhātīti. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu [V 0.0238] – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Imaṃ cittaṃ paggaṇhāti sampaggaṇhāti upatthambheti paccupatthambheti. Tena vuccati “cittaṃ paggaṇhātī”ti.

413. 'He uplifts the mind.' Herein, what is the mind? Whatever is mind, intellect, mentality… the mind-consciousness element corresponding to that—this is called 'the mind.' He uplifts this mind, thoroughly uplifts it, supports it, and firmly supports it. Therefore, it is said, 'he uplifts the mind.'

414. Padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ sammappadhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “sammappadhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā sammappadhānasampayuttā.

414. Regarding 'he exerts himself': Herein, what is right striving? That which is the mental undertaking of energy... right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right striving.' The remaining states are associated with right striving.

415. Kathañca bhikkhu uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye [M 0.0221] uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

415. And how does a monk generate desire, strive, undertake energy, uplift his mind, and exert himself for the abandoning of arisen, evil, unwholesome states? Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of accumulation, for the abandonment of views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, he generates desire, strives, undertakes energy, uplifts his mind, and exerts himself for the abandoning of arisen, evil, unwholesome states.

416. Chandaṃ [P 0.0213] janetīti…pe… vāyamatīti…pe… vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti…pe… cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti…pe… padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ sammappadhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “sammappadhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā [T 0.0287] sammappadhānasampayuttā.

416. Regarding 'he generates desire'... regarding 'he strives'... regarding 'he undertakes energy'... regarding 'he uplifts the mind'... regarding 'he exerts himself': Herein, what is right striving? That which is the mental undertaking of energy... right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right striving.' The remaining states are associated with right striving.

417. Kathañca bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

417. And how does a monk generate desire, strive, undertake energy, uplift his mind, and exert himself for the arising of unarisen wholesome states? Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of accumulation, for the abandonment of views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, he generates desire, strives, undertakes energy, uplifts his mind, and exerts himself for the arising of unarisen wholesome states.

418. Chandaṃ janetīti…pe… vāyamatīti…pe… vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti…pe… cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti…pe… padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ sammappadhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho [V 0.0239] …pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “sammappadhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā sammappadhānasampayuttā.

418. Regarding 'he generates desire'... regarding 'he strives'... regarding 'he undertakes energy'... regarding 'he uplifts the mind'... regarding 'he exerts himself': Herein, what is right striving? That which is the mental undertaking of energy... right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right striving.' The remaining states are associated with right striving.

419. Kathañca bhikkhu uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya [T 0.0288] vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

419. And how does a monk, for the stability, non-confusion, increase, expansion, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states, generate desire, strive, undertake energy, uplift his mind, and exert himself? Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of accumulation, for the abandonment of views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, for the stability, non-confusion, increase, expansion, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states, he generates desire, strives, undertakes energy, uplifts his mind, and exerts himself.

420. Ṭhitiyāti[M 0.0222]. Yā ṭhiti so asammoso, yo asammoso so bhiyyobhāvo, yo bhiyyobhāvo taṃ vepullaṃ, yaṃ vepullaṃ sā bhāvanā, yā bhāvanā sā pāripūrī.

420. Regarding 'stability': Whatever is stability, that is non-confusion. Whatever is non-confusion, that is increase. Whatever is increase, that is expansion. Whatever is expansion, that is development. Whatever is development, that is fulfillment.

421. Chandaṃ janetīti. Tattha katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati “chando”. Imaṃ chandaṃ janeti sañjaneti uṭṭhapeti samuṭṭhapeti nibbatteti abhinibbatteti. Tena vuccati “chandaṃ janetī”ti.

421. Regarding 'he generates desire': Herein, what is desire? Whatever is desire, the state of desiring, the wish to act, wholesome desire for the Dhamma—this is called 'desire.' He generates this desire, produces it well, arouses it, arouses it well, brings it into being, and brings it forth anew. Therefore, it is said, 'he generates desire.'

422. Vāyamatīti. Tattha katamo vāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vāyāmo”. Iminā vāyāmena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vāyamatī”ti.

422. Regarding 'he strives': Herein, what is striving? That which is the mental undertaking of energy... right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'striving.' He is endowed with this striving... is fully endowed. Therefore, it is said, 'he strives.'

423. Vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti. Tattha katamaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “vīriyaṃ”. Imaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhati samārabhati āsevati [P 0.0214] bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “vīriyaṃ ārabhatī”ti.

423. Regarding 'he undertakes energy': Herein, what is energy? That which is the mental undertaking of energy... right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'energy.' He undertakes this energy, undertakes it well, cultivates it, develops it, and makes much of it. Therefore, it is said, 'he undertakes energy.'

424. Cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu [V 0.0240] – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Imaṃ cittaṃ paggaṇhāti sampaggaṇhāti upatthambheti paccupatthambheti. Tena [T 0.0289] vuccati “cittaṃ paggaṇhātī”ti.

424. Regarding 'he uplifts the mind': Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, heart, mentality... the mind-consciousness-element corresponding to that—this is called 'mind.' He uplifts this mind, uplifts it well, supports it, and repeatedly supports it. Therefore, it is said, 'he uplifts the mind.'

425. Padahatīti. Tattha katamaṃ sammappadhānaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “sammappadhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā sammappadhānasampayuttā.

425. Regarding 'he exerts himself': Herein, what is right striving? That which is the mental undertaking of energy... right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right striving.' The remaining states are associated with right striving.

426. Tattha katamaṃ sammappadhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yo tasmiṃ samaye cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “sammappadhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā sammappadhānasampayuttā.

426. Herein, what is right striving? Here, a bhikkhu, at a time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which is leading out, leading to the cessation of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage—being secluded from sensual pleasures… enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge; at that time, whatever is the mental initiation of energy… right effort, the energy enlightenment factor, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right striving'. The remaining states are associated with right striving.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition is concluded.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Questioning Section

427. Cattāro [M 0.0223] sammappadhānā – idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya…pe… uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya [T 0.0290] bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

427. There are four Right Strivings. Here, a bhikkhu generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen, evil, unwholesome states; for the abandoning of arisen, evil, unwholesome states... for the arising of unarisen wholesome states... for the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, abundance, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states, he generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives.

428. Catunnaṃ sammappadhānānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

428. Of the four Right Strivings, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate... how many with defilements, how many without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

429. Kusalāyeva[V 0.0241]. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Vipākadhammadhammā[P 0.0215]. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Apacayagāmino. Sekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Sammattaniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā. Maggahetukā. Siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggādhipatinoti. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

429. They are exclusively wholesome. They may be associated with pleasant feeling, or they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are states that have the nature of producing a result. They are not appropriated and not objects of clinging. They are undefiled and not a basis for defilement. They may be with applied and sustained thought; or they may be without applied thought but with sustained thought only; or they may be without applied and without sustained thought. They may be accompanied by joy, or they may be accompanied by happiness, or they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. They do not have a cause that is to be abandoned either by seeing or by development. They lead to the cessation of accumulation. They belong to trainees. They are immeasurable. They have an immeasurable object. They are excellent. They are fixed in rightness. They do not have the path as their object. They have the path as their cause. They may have the path as their predominant condition, or it cannot be said that they have the path as their predominant condition. They may be arisen, or they may be unarisen; it cannot be said that they are bound to arise. They may be past, or they may be future, or they may be present. It cannot be said that they have a past object, nor a future object, nor a present object. They may be internal, or they may be external, or they may be both internal and external. They have an external object. They are invisible and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

430. Na hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Na [M 0.0224] hetū sahetukā. Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā[T 0.0291]. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā. No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā[V 0.0242]. Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Niyyānikā. Niyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

430. Not causes. With causes. Associated with causes. It cannot be said that they are both causes and with causes; rather, they are with causes but are not causes. It cannot be said that they are both causes and associated with causes; rather, they are associated with causes but are not causes. Not causes, but with causes. With conditions. Conditioned. Invisible. Non-resistant. Formless. Supramundane. Knowable through a certain consciousness, not knowable through a certain consciousness. Not taints. Not objects of the taints. Disjoined from taints. It cannot be said that they are both taints and objects of taints, nor that they are objects of taints but not taints. It cannot be said that they are both taints and associated with taints, nor that they are associated with taints but not taints. Disjoined from taints and not objects of the taints. Not fetters... not bonds... not floods... not yokes... not hindrances... not graspings... With an object. Not mind. Mental factors. Associated with mind. Intermixed with mind. Originating from mind. Co-existent with mind. Following mind. Originating from the intermixture with mind. Co-existent with that which originates from the intermixture with mind. Following that which originates from the intermixture with mind. External. Not derived. Not appropriated. Not clinging... not defilements... Not to be abandoned by seeing. Not to be abandoned by development. Not having a cause to be abandoned by seeing. Not having a cause to be abandoned by development. They may be with applied thought, or they may be without applied thought. They may be with sustained thought, or they may be without sustained thought. They may be with rapture, or they may be without rapture. They may be accompanied by rapture, or they may not be accompanied by rapture. They may be accompanied by happiness, or they may not be accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity, or they may not be accompanied by equanimity. Not of the sense-sphere. Not of the form-sphere. Not of the formless-sphere. Unincluded. Leading out. Fixed. Unsurpassed. Without defilements.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Questioning Section is concluded.

Sammappadhānavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Right Strivings is concluded.

9. Iddhipādavibhaṅgo

9. The Analysis of the Bases of Power

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Discourse Analysis

431. Cattāro [M 0.0225][P 0.0216][V 0.0243] iddhipādā – idha bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti.

431. There are four bases of power. Here, a bhikkhu develops the basis of power endowed with concentration based on desire and striving-formations. He develops the basis of power endowed with concentration based on energy and striving-formations. He develops the basis of power endowed with concentration based on mind and striving-formations. He develops the basis of power endowed with concentration based on investigation and striving-formations.

1. Chandiddhipādo

1. The Basis of Power of Desire

432. Kathañca bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Chandaṃ ce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ, labhati cittassekaggataṃ cittassa ekaggataṃ (sī. syā.) – ayaṃ vuccati “chandasamādhi”. So anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Ime vuccanti “padhānasaṅkhārā”. Iti ayañca chandasamādhi, ime ca padhānasaṅkhārā. Tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññahitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārotveva saṅkhyaṃ saṅkhaṃ (sī.) gacchati.

432. And how does a monk develop the basis of power endowed with concentration based on desire and striving-formations? A monk, having made desire predominant, obtains concentration, obtains one-pointedness of mind—this is called 'concentration based on desire.' He generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen, evil, unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. He generates desire for the abandoning of arisen, evil, unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. He generates desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. He generates desire for the stability, non-confusion, increase, abundance, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. These are called 'striving-formations.' Thus, this concentration based on desire and these striving-formations—having gathered and condensed them together, are reckoned as 'concentration based on desire and striving-formations'.

433. Tattha [V 0.0244] katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati “chando”.

433. Herein, what is desire? Whatever desire, zeal, wish to act, and wholesome desire for the Dhamma there is—this is called 'desire'.

Tattha [P 0.0217] katamo samādhi? Yā [T 0.0293] cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti avaṭṭhiti avisāhāro avikkhepo avisāhaṭamānasatā samatho samādhindriyaṃ samādhibalaṃ sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Herein, what is concentration? Whatever stability of mind, firm stability, steadfastness, non-distraction, non-scattering, the state of an undistracted mind, tranquility, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration there is—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho nikkamo parakkamo uyyāmo vāyāmo ussāho ussoḷhī thāmo ṭhiti asithilaparakkamatā anikkhittachandatā anikkhittadhuratā dhurasampaggāho [M 0.0226] vīriyaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ vīriyabalaṃ sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti iminā ca chandena, iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti.

Herein, what is a striving-formation? Whatever mental arousal of energy, setting forth, striving, endeavor, effort, diligence, firm exertion, strength, stability, unremitting effort, not abandoning desire, not relinquishing the burden, taking up the burden, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort there is—this is called a 'striving-formation.' Thus, with this desire, with this concentration, and with this striving-formation, one is endowed, well endowed, possessed, well possessed, furnished, accomplished, and fully endowed. Therefore, it is said, 'endowed with concentration based on desire and striving-formations'.

434. Iddhīti. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

434. 'Power' (iddhi): Whatever, regarding those states, is success, thorough success, achievement, thorough achievement, gain, acquisition, attainment, full attainment, contact, realization, and full acquisition.

“Iddhipādo”ti. Tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho.

'Basis of Power' (Iddhipāda): For one who has become so, it is the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate.

“Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

'Develops the basis of power': one resorts to, develops, and makes much of those states. Therefore, it is said, 'develops the basis of power'.

2. Vīriyiddhipādo

2. The Basis of Power through Energy

435. Kathañca bhikkhu vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Vīriyaṃ ce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ labhati cittassekaggataṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vīriyasamādhi”. So anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ [V 0.0245] pahānāya…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya…pe… uppannānaṃ [T 0.0294] kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Ime vuccanti “padhānasaṅkhārā”. Iti ayañca vīriyasamādhi, ime ca padhānasaṅkhārā; tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

435. And how does a monk develop the basis of power endowed with concentration based on energy and striving-formations? A monk, having made energy predominant, obtains concentration, obtains one-pointedness of mind—this is called 'concentration based on energy.' He generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen, evil, unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. For the abandoning of arisen, evil, unwholesome states... for the arising of unarisen wholesome states... for the stability, non-confusion, increase, abundance, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states, he generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. These are called 'striving-formations.' Thus, this concentration based on energy and these striving-formations—having gathered and condensed them together, are reckoned as 'concentration based on energy and striving-formations'.

436. Tattha katamaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – idaṃ vuccati “vīriyaṃ”.

436. Herein, what is energy? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and right effort there is—this is called 'energy'.

Tattha [P 0.0218] katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti avaṭṭhiti avisāhāro avikkhepo avisāhaṭamānasatā samatho samādhindriyaṃ samādhibalaṃ sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Herein, what is concentration? Whatever stability of mind, firm stability, steadfastness, non-distraction, non-scattering, the state of an undistracted mind, tranquility, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration there is—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha [M 0.0227] katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti iminā ca vīriyena, iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti.

Herein, what is a striving-formation? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and right effort there is—this is called a 'striving-formation.' Thus, with this energy, with this concentration, and with this striving-formation, one is endowed... and fully endowed. Therefore, it is said, 'endowed with concentration based on energy and striving-formations'.

437. Iddhīti. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

437. 'Power' (iddhi): Whatever, regarding those states, is success, thorough success, achievement, thorough achievement, gain, acquisition, attainment, full attainment, contact, realization, and full acquisition.

Iddhipādoti. Tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho.

'Basis of Power' (Iddhipāda): For one who has become so, it is the feeling aggregate... and the consciousness aggregate.

Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetīti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

'Develops the basis of power': one resorts to, develops, and makes much of those states. Therefore, it is said, 'develops the basis of power'.

3. Cittiddhipādo

3. The Basis of Power through Mind

438. Kathañca [T 0.0295][V 0.0246] bhikkhu cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Cittaṃ ce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ labhati cittassekaggataṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “cittasamādhi”. So anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya…pe… uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Ime vuccanti “padhānasaṅkhārā”. Iti ayañca cittasamādhi, ime ca padhānasaṅkhārā; tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

438. And how does a bhikkhu develop the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by mind and the formations of striving? If a bhikkhu, making mind the dominant factor, gains concentration, gains one-pointedness of mind—this is called 'concentration predominated by mind.' He generates zeal, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; for the maintenance, non-degeneration, increase, abundance, development, and perfection of arisen wholesome states, he generates zeal, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. These are called 'the formations of striving.' Thus, this concentration predominated by mind and these formations of striving—having been gathered and condensed together—are reckoned simply as 'concentration predominated by mind and the formations of striving'.

439. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”.

439. Herein, what is mind? That which is mind, mentation... and the mind-consciousness element born of that—this is called 'mind'.

Tattha katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Herein, what is concentration? The mind’s standing, its firm standing... right concentration—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti iminā ca cittena, iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena [P 0.0219] upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti.

Herein, what is the formation of striving? It is the mental undertaking of energy… right effort—this is called 'the formation of striving.' Thus, he is endowed and furnished with this mind, with this concentration, and with this formation of striving. Therefore, he is said to be 'endowed with concentration predominated by mind and the formations of striving'.

440. Iddhīti[M 0.0228]. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā [T 0.0296] lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

440. Spiritual power: It is, in regard to those states, the success, the thorough success, the accomplishment, the thorough accomplishment, the gain, the acquisition, the attainment, the complete attainment, the contact, the realization, and the full accomplishment.

Iddhipādoti. Tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho.

Base of spiritual power: Of one who has become so, it is the feeling aggregate… the consciousness aggregate.

Iddhipādaṃ [V 0.0247] bhāvetīti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

‘He develops the base of spiritual power’: He resorts to, develops, and makes much of those states. Therefore, it is said, ‘he develops the base of spiritual power’.

4. Vīmaṃsiddhipādo

4. The Base of Spiritual Power of Investigation

441. Kathañca bhikkhu vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Vīmaṃsaṃ ce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ labhati cittassekaggataṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vīmaṃsāsamādhi”. So anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya…pe… uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Ime vuccanti “padhānasaṅkhārā”. Iti ayañca vīmaṃsāsamādhi, ime ca padhānasaṅkhārā; tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

441. And how does a bhikkhu develop the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by investigation and the formations of striving? If a bhikkhu, making investigation the dominant factor, gains concentration, gains one-pointedness of mind—this is called 'concentration predominated by investigation.' He generates zeal, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; for the maintenance, non-degeneration, increase, abundance, development, and perfection of arisen wholesome states, he generates zeal, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. These are called 'the formations of striving.' Thus, this concentration predominated by investigation and these formations of striving—having been gathered and condensed together—are reckoned simply as 'concentration predominated by investigation and the formations of striving'.

442. Tattha katamā vīmaṃsā? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “vīmaṃsā”.

442. Herein, what is investigation? It is the wisdom, the act of discerning… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'investigation'.

Tattha katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Herein, what is concentration? The mind’s standing, its firm standing… right concentration—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho [T 0.0297] …pe… sammāvāyāmo – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti imāya ca vīmaṃsāya, iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti.

Herein, what is the formation of striving? It is the mental arousal of energy… right effort—this is called 'the formation of striving.' Thus, one is endowed and well endowed with this investigation, with this concentration, and with this formation of striving. Therefore, one is said to be 'endowed with concentration predominated by investigation and the formations of striving'.

443. Iddhīti. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

443. Spiritual power: It is, in regard to those states, the success, thorough success, accomplishment, thorough accomplishment, gain, acquisition, attainment, complete attainment, contact, realization, and consummation.

Iddhipādoti[M 0.0229][P 0.0220][V 0.0248]. Tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakhandho.

Base of spiritual power: Of one who has become so, it is the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate.

Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetīti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

‘He develops the base of spiritual power’: He resorts to, develops, and makes much of those states. Therefore, it is said, ‘he develops the base of spiritual power’.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

End of the Sutta-Style Analysis.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma-Style Analysis
