444. Cattāro iddhipādā – idha bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti.

444. There are four bases of spiritual power. Here, a bhikkhu develops the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration and formations of striving, with desire as the predominant factor; he develops the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration and formations of striving, with energy as the predominant factor; he develops the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration and formations of striving, with mind as the predominant factor; he develops the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration and formations of striving, with investigation as the predominant factor.

1. Chandiddhipādo

1. The Base of Spiritual Power of Desire

445. Kathañca bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ [T 0.0298] bhāveti.

445. And how does a bhikkhu develop the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration and formations of striving, with desire as the predominant factor? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out, leads to diminution, is for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first ground—quite secluded from sensual pleasures… and so on… he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which has painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, he develops the base of spiritual power endowed with concentration and formations of striving, with desire as the predominant factor.

446. Tattha katamo chando? Yo chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati “chando”.

446. Therein, what is desire? Whatever desire, zeal, wish-to-do, wholesome desire for the Dhamma—this is called 'desire'.

Tattha katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Therein, what is concentration? Whatever stability of mind, steadfastness… right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha [V 0.0249] katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti iminā ca chandena, iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti.

Therein, what is the striving-formation? Whatever mental arousal of energy… right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called ‘the striving-formation’. Thus, one is endowed with… possessed of this desire, this concentration, and this striving-formation. Therefore, it is said, ‘endowed with concentration predominated by desire and with the striving-formation’.

447. Iddhīti[M 0.0230]. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

447. 'Spiritual power': The spiritual power, success, accomplishment, thriving, gain, acquisition, attainment, complete attainment, contact, realization, and full possession of those states.

Iddhipādoti[P 0.0221]. Tathābhūtassa phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo.

'Basis of spiritual power': The contact of one who has become thus… exertion, non-distraction.

Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetīti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

'One develops the basis of spiritual power': One resorts to, develops, and cultivates those states. Therefore it is said, 'one develops the basis of spiritual power'.

2. Vīriyiddhipādo

2. The Basis of Spiritual Power of Energy

448. Kathañca bhikkhu vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ [T 0.0299] bhāveti.

448. And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by energy and with the striving-formation? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to diminution, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first ground—quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and sluggish direct knowledge—at that time one develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by energy and with the striving-formation.

449. Tattha katamaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “vīriyaṃ”.

449. Therein, what is energy? Whatever mental arousal of energy… right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'energy'.

Tattha katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Therein, what is concentration? Whatever stability of mind, steadfastness… right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti iminā ca vīriyena[V 0.0250], iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti.

Therein, what is the striving-formation? Whatever mental arousal of energy… right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called ‘the striving-formation’. Thus, one is endowed with… possessed of this energy, this concentration, and this striving-formation. Therefore, it is said, ‘endowed with concentration predominated by energy and with the striving-formation’.

450. Iddhīti. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

450. 'Spiritual power': The spiritual power, success, accomplishment, thriving, gain, acquisition, attainment, complete attainment, contact, realization, and full possession of those states.

Iddhipādoti. Tathābhūtasa phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo.

'Basis of spiritual power': The contact of one who has become thus… exertion, non-distraction.

Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetīti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

'One develops the basis of spiritual power': One resorts to, develops, and cultivates those states. Therefore it is said, 'one develops the basis of spiritual power'.

3. Cittiddhipādo

3. The Basis of Spiritual Power of Consciousness

451. Kathañca [M 0.0231] bhikkhu cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ [P 0.0222] apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ [T 0.0300] bhāveti.

451. And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by consciousness and with the striving-formation? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to diminution, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first ground—quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and sluggish direct knowledge—at that time one develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by consciousness and with the striving-formation.

452. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”.

452. Therein, what is consciousness? Whatever is consciousness, mind, mentality… the mind-consciousness element corresponding to that—this is called 'consciousness'.

Tattha katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Therein, what is concentration? Whatever stability of mind, steadfastness… right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti iminā ca cittena[V 0.0251], iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti.

Therein, what is the striving-formation? Whatever mental arousal of energy… right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called ‘the striving-formation’. Thus, one is endowed with… possessed of this consciousness, this concentration, and this striving-formation. Therefore, it is said, ‘endowed with concentration predominated by consciousness and with the striving-formation’.

453. Iddhīti. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

453. 'Spiritual power': The spiritual power, success, accomplishment, thriving, gain, acquisition, attainment, complete attainment, contact, realization, and full possession of those states.

Iddhipādoti. Tathābhūtassa phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo.

'Basis of spiritual power': The contact of one who has become thus… exertion, non-distraction.

Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetīti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

'One develops the basis of spiritual power': One resorts to, develops, and cultivates those states. Therefore it is said, 'one develops the basis of spiritual power'.

4. Vīmaṃsiddhipādo

4. The Basis of Spiritual Power of Investigation

454. Kathañca bhikkhu vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ [T 0.0301] iddhipādaṃ bhāveti.

454. And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by investigation and with the striving-formation? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to diminution, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground—secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and sluggish direct knowledge. At that time, one develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration predominated by investigation and with the striving-formation.

455. Tattha [M 0.0232] katamā vīmaṃsā? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vīmaṃsā”.

455. Therein, what is investigation? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'investigation'.

Tattha katamo samādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo [P 0.0223] maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhi”.

Therein, what is concentration? Whatever stability of mind, steadfastness… right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called 'concentration'.

Tattha katamo padhānasaṅkhāro? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “padhānasaṅkhāro”. Iti imāya ca vīmaṃsāya, iminā ca samādhinā, iminā ca padhānasaṅkhārena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato [V 0.0252] upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgato”ti

Therein, what is the striving-formation? Whatever mental inception of energy… right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'the striving-formation.' Thus, with this investigation, with this concentration, and with this striving-formation, one is endowed, fully endowed, approached, fully approached, furnished, possessed, and fully possessed. Therefore, one is called 'endowed with investigation, concentration, and the striving-formation.'

456. Iddhīti. Yā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ iddhi samiddhi ijjhanā samijjhanā lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

456. Spiritual power: Whatever accomplishment, full accomplishment, success, full success, gain, acquisition, attainment, full attainment, contact, realization, and consummation of those states.

Iddhipādoti. Tathābhūtassa phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo.

Basis of spiritual power: The contact… exertion, and non-distraction of one who has become thus.

Iddhipādaṃ bhāvetīti. Te dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

“He develops the basis of spiritual power”: He resorts to, develops, and makes much of those states. Therefore it is said, “he develops the basis of spiritual power.”

457. Cattāro iddhipādā – chandiddhipādo, vīriyiddhipādo, cittiddhipādo, vīmaṃsiddhipādo.

457. There are four bases of spiritual power: the basis of spiritual power of desire, the basis of spiritual power of energy, the basis of spiritual power of consciousness, and the basis of spiritual power of investigation.

458. Tattha katamo chandiddhipādo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya [T 0.0302] bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yo tasmiṃ samaye chando chandikatā kattukamyatā kusalo dhammacchando – ayaṃ vuccati “chandiddhipādo”. Avasesā dhammā chandiddhipādasampayuttā.

458. Therein, what is the basis of spiritual power of desire? Here, a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to diminution, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground; secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and sluggish direct knowledge. Whatever desire, zeal, wish to act, and wholesome desire for the Dhamma there is at that time—this is called 'the basis of spiritual power of desire.' The remaining states are associated with the basis of spiritual power of desire.

459. Tattha katamo vīriyiddhipādo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [M 0.0233] viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yo tasmiṃ samaye cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vīriyiddhipādo”. Avasesā dhammā vīriyiddhipādasampayuttā.

459. Therein, what is the basis of spiritual power of energy? Here, a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to diminution, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground; secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and sluggish direct knowledge. Whatever mental inception of energy… right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'the basis of spiritual power of energy.' The remaining states are associated with the basis of spiritual power of energy.

460. Tattha katamo cittiddhipādo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ [P 0.0224] apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi [V 0.0253] …pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yaṃ tasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati “cittiddhipādo”. Avasesā dhammā cittiddhipādasampayuttā.

460. Therein, what is the basis of spiritual power of consciousness? Here, a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to diminution, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground; secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and sluggish direct knowledge. Whatever at that time is consciousness, mind, mentality… the mind-consciousness element born of that—this is called 'the basis of spiritual power of consciousness.' The remaining states are associated with the basis of spiritual power of consciousness.

461. Tattha katamo vīmaṃsiddhipādo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [T 0.0303] viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vīmaṃsiddhipādo”. Avasesā dhammā vīmaṃsiddhipādasampayuttā.

461. Therein, what is the basis of spiritual power of investigation? Here, a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to diminution, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground; secluded from sensual pleasures… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and sluggish direct knowledge. Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'the basis of spiritual power of investigation.' The remaining states are associated with the basis of spiritual power of investigation.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Section of Questions

462. Cattāro iddhipādā – idha bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti.

462. Four are the bases of spiritual power. Here, a bhikkhu develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving-formations; …with concentration founded on energy…; …with concentration founded on consciousness…; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on investigation and with striving-formations.

463. Catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

463. Of the four bases of spiritual power, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate… how many with defilements, how many without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

464. Kusalāyeva. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā[M 0.0234], siyā avitakkaavicārā. Siyā [V 0.0254] pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Apacayagāmino. Sekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Sammattaniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā, maggahetukā, na maggādhipatino. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi[T 0.0304], paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

464. They are exclusively wholesome. They may be associated with pleasant feeling, or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are states that are causes of resultants. Not taken up by clinging and not objects of clinging. Unstained and not causing stains. They may be accompanied by applied and sustained thought, or by sustained thought only, or without applied and sustained thought. They may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity. To be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. Not having a cause to be abandoned by vision, nor by development. Leading to non-accumulation. Pertaining to a trainee. Immeasurable. With an immeasurable object. Superior. Fixed in rightness. Not having the path as object, having the path as cause, not having the path as dominant condition. They may be arisen, they may be unarisen; it cannot be said that they are arising. They may be past, they may be future, they may be present. It cannot be said that they have a past object, nor that they have a future object, nor that they have a present object. They may be internal, they may be external, or internal-and-external. With an external object. Invisible and non-impinging.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

465. Vīmaṃsiddhipādo [P 0.0225] hetu, tayo iddhipādā na hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Vīmaṃsiddhipādo hetu ceva sahetuko ca, tayo iddhipādā na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Vīmaṃsiddhipādo hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, tayo iddhipādā na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Tayo iddhipādā na hetū sahetukā, vīmaṃsiddhipādo na vattabbo na hetu sahetukotipi, na hetu ahetukotipi. Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā.

465. The basis of spiritual power of investigation is a root; the three bases of spiritual power are not roots. They are with a root. They are associated with a root. The basis of spiritual power of investigation is both a root and is with a root; of the three bases of spiritual power it cannot be said that they are both roots and are with a root—they are with a root but are not roots. The basis of spiritual power of investigation is both a root and is associated with a root; of the three bases of spiritual power it cannot be said that they are both roots and are associated with a root—they are associated with a root but are not roots. The three bases of spiritual power are not roots but are with a root; of the basis of spiritual power of investigation it cannot be said that it is 'not a root but with a root' or 'not a root and without a root.' They are with conditions. They are conditioned. Invisible. Non-impinging. Immaterial. Supramundane. Cognizable by some consciousness, not cognizable by some. Not taints. Not objects of taints. Dissociated from taints. It cannot be said that they are both taints and with taints, nor that they are with taints but not taints. It cannot be said that they are both taints and associated with taints, nor that they are associated with taints but not taints. Dissociated from taints. Not objects of taints.

No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. Tayo iddhipādā no cittā, cittiddhipādo [T 0.0305] cittaṃ. Tayo iddhipādā cetasikā, cittiddhipādo acetasiko. Tayo iddhipādā cittasampayuttā, cittiddhipādo na vattabbo cittena sampayuttotipi, cittena vippayuttotipi. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhā, cittiddhipādo na vattabbo cittena saṃsaṭṭhotipi, cittena visaṃsaṭṭhotipi. Tayo iddhipādā cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittiddhipādo no cittasamuṭṭhāno[M 0.0235]. Tayo iddhipādā cittasahabhuno, cittiddhipādo no cittasahabhū. Tayo iddhipādā cittānuparivattino[V 0.0255], cittiddhipādo no cittānuparivatti. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittiddhipādo no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhāno. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittiddhipādo no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhū. Tayo iddhipādā cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino, cittiddhipādo no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivatti.

They are not fetters... not bodily ties... not floods... not yokes... not hindrances... not misapprehensions... They have an object. Three bases of spiritual power are not consciousness; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power are mental factors; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is not a mental factor. Three bases of spiritual power are associated with consciousness; of the basis of spiritual power of consciousness it cannot be said that it is associated with or dissociated from consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power are conjoined with consciousness; of the basis of spiritual power of consciousness it cannot be said that it is conjoined with or disjoined from consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power are originated by consciousness; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is not originated by consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power are co-existent with consciousness; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is not co-existent with consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power follow the movement of consciousness; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness does not follow the movement of consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power are conjoined with and originated by consciousness; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is not conjoined with and is not originated by consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power are conjoined with, originated by, and co-existent with consciousness; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is not conjoined with, is not originated by, and is not co-existent with consciousness. Three bases of spiritual power are conjoined with, originated by, and follow the movement of consciousness; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is not conjoined with, is not originated by, and does not follow the movement of consciousness.

Tayo iddhipādā bāhirā, cittiddhipādo ajjhattiko. No upādā. Anupādinnā. No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā[P 0.0226]. Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā[T 0.0306]. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Niyyānikā. Niyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

The three bases of spiritual power are external; the basis of spiritual power of consciousness is internal. Not derived. Not clung-to. Not clingings... not defilements... Not to be abandoned by vision. Not to be abandoned by development. Not having roots to be abandoned by vision. Not having roots to be abandoned by development. They may be with applied thought or without applied thought. They may be with sustained thought or without sustained thought. They may be with joy or without joy. They may be accompanied by joy or not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness or not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity or not accompanied by equanimity. Not of the sense sphere. Not of the form sphere. Not of the formless sphere. Unincluded. Leading out. Certain. Unsurpassed. Passionless.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Section of Questions.

Iddhipādavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Bases of Spiritual Power is finished.

10. Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgo

10. Analysis of the Factors of Enlightenment

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Analysis

466. Satta [M 0.0236][P 0.0227][V 0.0256] bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

466. Seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

467. Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā hoti anussaritā – ayaṃ vuccati “satisambojjhaṅgo”.

467. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? Here, a bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and prudence; he is one who can remember and repeatedly recollect what was done long ago and what was said long ago. This is called the enlightenment factor of mindfulness.

So tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati – ayaṃ vuccati “dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo”.

Dwelling thus mindful, he investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, and arrives at a full inquiry. This is called the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.

Tassa taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vīriyasambojjhaṅgo”.

In him who investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, and arrives at a full inquiry, energy is aroused and unflagging. This is called the enlightenment factor of energy.

Āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā – ayaṃ vuccati “pītisambojjhaṅgo”.

In him with aroused energy, unworldly rapture arises. This is called the enlightenment factor of rapture.

Pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati – ayaṃ vuccati “passaddhisambojjhaṅgo”.

In him with a rapturous mind, the body becomes tranquil and the mind also becomes tranquil. This is called the enlightenment factor of tranquility.

Passaddhakāyassa [V 0.0257] sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhisambojjhaṅgo”[T 0.0307].

In him whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. This is called the enlightenment factor of concentration.

So tathā samāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”.

He is one who well looks on with equanimity at the mind that is thus concentrated. This is called the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

468. Satta bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

Seven are the enlightenment factors: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

469. Tattha [P 0.0228] katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu sati, atthi bahiddhā dhammesu sati. Yadapi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu sati tadapi satisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi bahiddhā [M 0.0237] dhammesu sati tadapi satisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

468. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? There is mindfulness in regard to internal dhammas; there is mindfulness in regard to external dhammas. Whatever mindfulness there is in regard to internal dhammas, that too is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Whatever mindfulness there is in regard to external dhammas, that too is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

Tattha katamo dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo? Atthi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu pavicayo, atthi bahiddhā dhammesu pavicayo. Yadapi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu pavicayo tadapi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu pavicayo tadapi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

469. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena? There is investigation in regard to internal dhammas; there is investigation in regard to external dhammas. Whatever investigation there is in regard to internal dhammas, that too is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Whatever investigation there is in regard to external dhammas, that too is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

Tattha katamo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo? Atthi kāyikaṃ vīriyaṃ, atthi cetasikaṃ vīriyaṃ. Yadapi kāyikaṃ vīriyaṃ tadapi vīriyasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi cetasikaṃ vīriyaṃ tadapi vīriyasambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati[T 0.0308].

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of energy? There is physical energy; there is mental energy. Whatever physical energy there is, that too is the enlightenment factor of energy; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Whatever mental energy there is, that too is the enlightenment factor of energy; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

Tattha katamo pītisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi savitakkasavicārā pīti, atthi avitakkaavicārā pīti. Yadapi savitakkasavicārā pīti tadapi pītisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi avitakkaavicārā pīti tadapi pītisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of rapture? There is rapture with applied thought and sustained thought; there is rapture without applied thought and sustained thought. Whatever rapture there is with applied thought and sustained thought, that too is the enlightenment factor of rapture; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Whatever rapture there is without applied thought and sustained thought, that too is the enlightenment factor of rapture; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

Tattha [V 0.0258] katamo passaddhisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi kāyapassaddhi kāyappassaddhi (syā. ka.), atthi cittapassaddhi cittappassaddhi (syā. ka.). Yadapi kāyapassaddhi tadapi passaddhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi cittapassaddhi tadapi passaddhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of tranquility? There is tranquility of body; there is tranquility of mind. Whatever tranquility of body there is, that too is the enlightenment factor of tranquility; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Whatever tranquility of mind there is, that too is the enlightenment factor of tranquility; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

Tattha katamo samādhisambojjhaṅgo? Atthi savitakko savicāro samādhi, atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi. Yadapi savitakko savicāro samādhi tadapi samādhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi avitakko avicāro samādhi tadapi samādhisambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of concentration? There is concentration with applied thought and sustained thought; there is concentration without applied thought and sustained thought. Whatever concentration there is with applied thought and sustained thought, that too is the enlightenment factor of concentration; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Whatever concentration there is without applied thought and sustained thought, that too is the enlightenment factor of concentration; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

Tattha katamo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo? Atthi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu upekkhā, atthi bahiddhā dhammesu upekkhā. Yadapi ajjhattaṃ dhammesu upekkhā tadapi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Yadapi [M 0.0238] bahiddhā dhammesu upekkhā tadapi [T 0.0309] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity? There is equanimity in regard to internal dhammas; there is equanimity in regard to external dhammas. Whatever equanimity there is in regard to internal dhammas, that too is the enlightenment factor of equanimity; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. Whatever equanimity there is in regard to external dhammas, that too is the enlightenment factor of equanimity; it conduces to higher knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

470. Satta [P 0.0229] bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

470. Seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

471. Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.

471. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? Here, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment; he develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena...pe... he develops the enlightenment factor of energy... he develops the enlightenment factor of rapture... he develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility... he develops the enlightenment factor of concentration... he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Suttanta Analysis is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Analysis

472. Satta [V 0.0259] bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

472. Seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

473. Tattha katame satta bojjhaṅgā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye satta bojjhaṅgā honti – satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

473. Therein, what are the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, a bhikkhu, when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, that leads to the undoing [of defilements], for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage; secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, there are seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness...pe... the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

474. Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “satisambojjhaṅgo”.

474. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? That which is mindfulness, recollection...pe... right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path—this is called the enlightenment factor of mindfulness.

Tattha [T 0.0310][M 0.0239] katamo dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo”.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena? That which is wisdom, understanding...pe... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path—this is called the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.

Tattha katamo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vīriyasambojjhaṅgo”.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of energy? That which is mental arousal of energy...pe... right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path—this is called the enlightenment factor of energy.

Tattha katamo pītisambojjhaṅgo? Yā pīti pāmojjaṃ āmodanā pamodanā hāso pahāso vitti odagyaṃ odaggaṃ (sī.) dha. sa. 9 attamanatā cittassa pītisambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati “pītisambojjhaṅgo”.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of rapture? The rapture, gladness, delight, joy, mirth, merriment, satisfaction, elation, and joyfulness of mind, which is the enlightenment factor of rapture—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of rapture’.

Tattha [P 0.0230] katamo passaddhisambojjhaṅgo? Yā vedanākkhandhassa saññākkhandhassa saṅkhārakkhandhassa viññāṇakkhandhassa passaddhi paṭippassaddhi passambhanā paṭippassambhanā paṭippassambhitattaṃ passaddhisambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati “passaddhisambojjhaṅgo”.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of tranquility? The tranquility, complete tranquility, calming, complete calming, and the state of being completely calmed of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness, which is the enlightenment factor of tranquility—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of tranquility’.

Tattha [V 0.0260] katamo samādhisambojjhaṅgo? Yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “samādhisambojjhaṅgo”.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of concentration? The stability of mind…pe… right concentration, which is the enlightenment factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of concentration’.

Tattha katamo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”. Ime vuccanti satta bojjhaṅgā. Avasesā dhammā sattahi bojjhaṅgehi [T 0.0311] sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity? The equanimity, observing with equanimity, looking upon, and neutrality of mind, which is the enlightenment factor of equanimity—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of equanimity.’ These are called the seven factors of enlightenment. The remaining states are associated with the seven factors of enlightenment.

475. Satta bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

475. Seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness…pe… the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

476. Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “satisambojjhaṅgo”. Avasesā dhammā satisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā [M 0.0240] dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā vīriyasambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā pītisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā passaddhisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā samādhisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā.

476. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, that leads to the undoing of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first plane; secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge; whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, which is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path, exists at that time—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of mindfulness.’ The remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of mindfulness…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of energy…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of rapture…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of tranquility…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of concentration.

Tattha katamo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”. Avasesā dhammā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgasampayuttā.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, that leads to the undoing of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first plane; secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge; whatever equanimity, observing with equanimity, looking upon, neutrality of mind, which is the enlightenment factor of equanimity, exists at that time—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of equanimity.’ The remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

477. Satta [T 0.0312][P 0.0231] bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

477. Seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness…pe… the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

478. Tattha katame satta bojjhaṅgā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi [V 0.0261] …pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yo tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti – ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye satta bojjhaṅgā honti – satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

478. Therein, what are the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, that leads to the undoing of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first plane; secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time there is contact…pe… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Because that same supramundane wholesome jhāna has been performed and developed, as its result, secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna which is empty, of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the seven factors of enlightenment are present: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness…pe… the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

479. Tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “satisambojjhaṅgo”…pe….

479. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? Whatever is mindfulness, recollection…pe… right mindfulness, which is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of mindfulness.’…pe…

Tattha katamo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”. Ime vuccanti “satta bojjhaṅgā”. Avasesā dhammā sattahi bojjhaṅgehi sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity? Whatever is equanimity, observing with equanimity, looking upon, neutrality of mind, which is the enlightenment factor of equanimity—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of equanimity.’ These are called the ‘seven factors of enlightenment.’ The remaining states are associated with the seven factors of enlightenment.

480. Satta bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

480. Seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness…pe… the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

481. Tattha [M 0.0241] katamo satisambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ [T 0.0313] upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye sati anussati sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “satisambojjhaṅgo”. Avasesā dhammā satisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgasampayuttā [P 0.0232] …pe… avasesā dhammā vīriyasambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā pītisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā passaddhisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā samādhisambojjhaṅgasampayuttā.

481. Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, that leads to the undoing of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first plane; secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time there is contact…pe… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Because that supramundane wholesome jhāna has been performed and developed, as its result, secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. Whatever mindfulness, recollection, right mindfulness, which is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path, exists at that time—this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of mindfulness.’ The remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of mindfulness…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of energy…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of rapture…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of tranquility…pe… the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of concentration.

Tattha katamo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ [V 0.0262] apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”[T 0.0314]. Avasesā dhammā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgasampayuttā.

Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first plane; being secluded from sensual pleasures… and so on… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time there is contact… and so on… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Because that supramundane wholesome jhāna has been performed and developed, as its resultant, being secluded from sensual pleasures… and so on… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is empty, of painful practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time, whatever equanimity, the act of observing with equanimity, superior equanimity, neutrality of mind, exists—this is the enlightenment factor of equanimity; this is called the ‘enlightenment factor of equanimity.’ The remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Section of Questions.

482. Satta bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

482. The seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

483. Sattannaṃ [M 0.0242] bojjhaṅgānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

483. Of the seven factors of enlightenment, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, how many are indeterminate… and so on… how many are with conflict, how many are without conflict?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads.

484. Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto; cha bojjhaṅgā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo na pītisahagato, sukhasahagato, na upekkhāsahagato; cha bojjhaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena [V 0.0263] na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā[P 0.0233], siyā aniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino; siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā [T 0.0315] anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

484. Some are wholesome, some are indeterminate. The enlightenment factor of rapture is associated with pleasant feeling; the six enlightenment factors may be associated with pleasant feeling, or they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Some are resultants, some are states that produce resultants. They are not kammically acquired and are not objects of clinging. They are undefiled and are not objects for defiling states. Some are with applied and sustained thought, some are without applied thought and with only sustained thought, some are without applied and without sustained thought. The enlightenment factor of rapture is not accompanied by rapture, but is accompanied by pleasure, and is not accompanied by equanimity; the six enlightenment factors may be accompanied by rapture, or they may be accompanied by pleasure, or they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are not to be abandoned by vision nor by development. They do not have causes to be abandoned by vision, nor do they have causes to be abandoned by development. Some lead to the destruction of rebirth, some lead neither to accumulation nor to the destruction of rebirth. Some pertain to a trainee, some to one beyond training. They are immeasurable. They have an immeasurable object. They are sublime. Some are fixed in rightness, some are unfixed. They do not have the path as object; some have the path as cause, some have the path as predominance; of some it cannot be said that they have the path as cause, nor that they have the path as predominance. Some have arisen, some have not arisen, some are arising. Some are past, some future, some present. It cannot be said that they have a past object, nor a future object, nor a present object. Some are internal, some are external, some are internal-and-external. They have an external object. They are invisible and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads.

485. Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo hetu, cha bojjhaṅgā hetusampayuttā. Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo hetu ceva sahetuko ca, cha bojjhaṅgā na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, cha bojjhaṅgā na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Cha bojjhaṅgā na hetū sahetukā, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo na vattabbo na hetusahetukotipi, na hetuahetukotipi. Sappaccayā. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci [M 0.0243] na viññeyyā. No āsavā. Anāsavā āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā. No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā[T 0.0316]. Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā. No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā.

485. The enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena is a root; the six enlightenment factors are associated with a root. The enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena is both a root and has a root; of the six enlightenment factors, it cannot be said that they are both roots and have a root; they have a root but are not roots. The enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena is both a root and associated with a root; of the six enlightenment factors, it cannot be said that they are both roots and associated with a root; they are associated with a root but are not roots. The six enlightenment factors are not roots but have a root; of the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, it cannot be said that it is ‘not a root but has a root,’ nor that it is ‘not a root and has no root.’ They are with conditions. They are constructed. They are invisible. They are non-resistant. They are immaterial. They are supramundane. They are cognizable by some, not cognizable by others. They are not taints. They are without taints and are dissociated from taints. It cannot be said that they are both taints and objects for taints, nor that they are objects for taints but not taints. It cannot be said that they are both taints and associated with taints, nor that they are associated with taints but not taints. They are dissociated from taints and are not objects for taints. They are not fetters… and so on… not bonds… and so on… not floods… and so on… not yokes… and so on… not hindrances… and so on… not adherences… and so on… They have an object. They are not consciousness. They are mental factors. They are associated with consciousness. They are conjoined with consciousness. They originate from consciousness. They are co-arisen with consciousness. They follow consciousness. They are conjoined with and originate from consciousness. They are conjoined with, originate from, and are co-arisen with consciousness. They are conjoined with, originate from, and follow consciousness. They are external. They are not derived matter. They are not kammically acquired. They are not objects of clinging… and so on… they are not defilements… and so on… They are not to be abandoned by vision. They are not to be abandoned by development. They do not have causes to be abandoned by vision. They do not have causes to be abandoned by development. Some are with applied thought, some are without applied thought. Some are with sustained thought, some are without sustained thought.

Pītisambojjhaṅgo [V 0.0264] appītiko, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo na pītisahagato, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo sukhasahagato, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā [P 0.0234] sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Pītisambojjhaṅgo na upekkhāsahagato, cha bojjhaṅgā siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

The enlightenment factor of rapture is without rapture; the six enlightenment factors may be with rapture or without rapture. The enlightenment factor of rapture is not accompanied by rapture; the six enlightenment factors may be accompanied by rapture or not accompanied by rapture. The enlightenment factor of rapture is accompanied by pleasure; the six enlightenment factors may be accompanied by pleasure or not accompanied by pleasure. The enlightenment factor of rapture is not accompanied by equanimity; the six enlightenment factors may be accompanied by equanimity or not accompanied by equanimity. They are not of the sense sphere. They are not of the form sphere. They are not of the formless sphere. They are unincluded. Some are emancipating, some are not emancipating. Some are fixed, some are unfixed. They are unsurpassed. They are without conflict.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Section of Questions.

Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Exposition of the Factors of Enlightenment is finished.

11. Maggaṅgavibhaṅgo

11. Analysis of the Path Factors

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Exposition

486. Ariyo [T 0.0317][M 0.0244][P 0.0235][V 0.0265] aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

486. The Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.

487. Tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”.

487. Among them, what is right view? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering—this is called right view.

Tattha katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Nekkhammasaṅkappo, abyāpādasaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsaṅkappo”.

Among them, what is right intention? The intention of renunciation, the intention of non-ill will, and the intention of non-harming—this is called right intention.

Tattha katamā sammāvācā? Musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvācā”.

Among them, what is right speech? Abstinence from false speech, abstinence from slanderous speech, abstinence from harsh speech, and abstinence from frivolous talk—this is called right speech.

Tattha katamo sammākammanto? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati “sammākammanto”.

Among them, what is right action? Abstinence from killing living beings, abstinence from taking what is not given, and abstinence from sexual misconduct—this is called right action.

Tattha katamo sammāājīvo? Idha ariyasāvako micchāājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāājīvo”.

Among them, what is right livelihood? Here, a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, earns his living by right livelihood—this is called right livelihood.

Tattha [V 0.0266] katamo sammāvāyāmo? Idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ [T 0.0318] ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvāyāmo”.

Among them, what is right effort? Here, a monk generates will, strives, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and endeavors for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; he generates will, strives, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and endeavors for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; he generates will, strives, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and endeavors for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; he generates will, strives, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and endeavors for the maintenance, non-disappearance, increase, expansion, and the fulfillment by development of arisen wholesome states—this is called right effort.

Tattha [P 0.0236] katamā sammāsati? Idha bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, vedanāsu [M 0.0245] vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsati”.

Among them, what is right mindfulness? Here, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world. He dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world. He dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world—this is called right mindfulness.

Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Idha bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā [T 0.0319] ācikkhanti “upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī”ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”.

Among them, what is right concentration? Here, a monk, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has internal clarity and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration. With the fading away of rapture, he dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and abides in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: 'Equanimous and mindful, he dwells happily.' With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity—this is called right concentration.

488. Ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

488. The noble eightfold path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

489. Tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Idha bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ [V 0.0267] nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ, sammāsaṅkappaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāvācaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammākammantaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāājīvaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāvāyāmaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsatiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.

489. Among them, what is right view? Here, a monk develops right view that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and resulting in relinquishment. He develops right intention... [and so forth]... He develops right concentration that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and resulting in relinquishment.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Sutta Analysis is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Analysis.

490. Aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

490. The Eightfold Path: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.

491. Tattha [M 0.0246] katamo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ [P 0.0237] jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

491. Among them, what is the eightfold path? Here, at the time when a monk develops a supramundane jhāna—which is emancipating and leading to the destruction of rebirth—for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the eightfold path exists: right view... [and so forth]... right concentration.

492. Tattha [T 0.0320] katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”.

492. Among them, what is right view? Whatever wisdom, understanding... [and so forth]... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path—this is called right view.

Tattha katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Yo takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā sammāsaṅkappo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsaṅkappo”.

Among them, what is right intention? Whatever thought, applied thought, intention, absorption, full absorption, the directing of the mind, right intention, a path factor, included in the path—this is called right intention.

Tattha katamā sammāvācā? Yā catūhi vacīduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammāvācā maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvācā”.

Among them, what is right speech? Whatever abstinence from the four kinds of verbal misconduct, refraining, abstaining, avoidance, non-doing, not performing, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the breaking of the bridge—right speech, a path factor, included in the path—this is called right speech.

Tattha katamo sammākammanto? Yā tīhi kāyaduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī [V 0.0268] akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammākammanto maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammākammanto”.

Herein, what is right action? Whatever abstinence from the three kinds of bodily misconduct, refraining, abstention, avoidance, non-doing, not performing, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the breaking of the bridge—right action, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right action'.

Tattha katamo sammāājīvo? Yā micchāājīvā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto sammāājīvo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāājīvo”.

Herein, what is right livelihood? Whatever abstinence from wrong livelihood, refraining, abstention, avoidance, non-doing, not performing, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the breaking of the bridge—right livelihood, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right livelihood'.

Tattha katamo sammāvāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ [T 0.0321] vuccati “sammāvāyāmo”.

Herein, what is right effort? Whatever mental arousal of energy... and so forth... right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right effort'.

Tattha katamā sammāsati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsati”.

Herein, what is right mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection... and so forth... right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right mindfulness'.

Tattha [M 0.0247] katamo sammāsamādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”. Ayaṃ vuccati “aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo”. Avasesā dhammā aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena sampayuttā.

Herein, what is right concentration? Whatever stability of mind... right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right concentration'. This is called the 'eight-factored path'. The remaining states are associated with the eight-factored path.

493. Pañcaṅgiko maggo – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

493. The five-factored path: right view, right thought, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

494. Tattha [P 0.0238] katamo pañcaṅgiko maggo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

494. Herein, what is the five-factored path? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhana—which leads out, which leads to the dispersal of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground—having become secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the first jhana, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the five-factored path comes to be: right view, right thought, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

495. Tattha [V 0.0269] katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”.

495. Herein, what is right view? Whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right view'.

Tattha katamo sammāsaṅkappo? Yo takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsaṅkappo”.

Herein, what is right thought? Whatever thought, initial application of mind... right thought, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right thought'.

Tattha katamo [T 0.0322] sammāvāyāmo? Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāvāyāmo”.

Herein, what is right effort? Whatever mental arousal of energy... right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right effort'.

Tattha katamā sammāsati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsati”.

Herein, what is right mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right mindfulness'.

Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”. Ayaṃ vuccati “pañcaṅgiko maggo”. Avasesā dhammā pañcaṅgikena maggena sampayuttā.

Herein, what is right concentration? Whatever stability of mind... right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path—this is called 'right concentration'. This is called the 'five-factored path'. The remaining states are associated with the five-factored path.

496. Pañcaṅgiko maggo – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

496. The five-factored path: right view, right thought, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

497. Tattha [M 0.0248] katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”. Avasesā dhammā sammādiṭṭhiyā sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā sammāsaṅkappena sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā sammāvāyāmena sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā sammāsatiyā sampayuttā.

497. Herein, what is right view? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhana—which leads out, which leads to the dispersal of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground—having become secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the first jhana, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge; whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path there is at that time—this is called 'right view'. The remaining states are associated with right view... the remaining states are associated with right thought... the remaining states are associated with right effort... the remaining states are associated with right mindfulness.

Tattha [P 0.0239] katamo sammāsamādhi? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya [T 0.0323] paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye [V 0.0270] cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”.
