Avasesā dhammā sammāsamādhinā sampayuttā.

Herein, what is right concentration? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhana—which leads out, which leads to the dispersal of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground—having become secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the first jhana, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge; whatever stability of mind... right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path there is at that time—this is called 'right concentration'. The remaining states are associated with right concentration.

498. Aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

498. The eight-factored path: right view... right concentration.

499. Tattha katamo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati “aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo”. Avasesā dhammā aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena sampayuttā.

499. Herein, what is the eight-factored path? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhana—which leads out, which leads to the dispersal of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first ground—having become secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the first jhana, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, there is contact... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Because that same supramundane wholesome jhana has been performed and developed, as its result, being secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the void first jhana, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the eight-factored path comes to be: right view... right concentration. This is called the 'eight-factored path'. The remaining states are associated with the eight-factored path.

500. Pañcaṅgiko maggo – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

500. The five-factored path: right view, right thought, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

501. Tattha katamo pañcaṅgiko maggo? Idha [P 0.0240] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ [T 0.0324] jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati [M 0.0249] dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgiko maggo hoti – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati “pañcaṅgiko maggo”. Avasesā dhammā pañcaṅgikena maggena sampayuttā.

501. Herein, what is the five-factored path? Here, at the time when a bhikkhu develops the supramundane jhāna—which is emancipating, which leads to the waning [of the round of rebirth]—for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful progress and slow direct knowledge. At that time, there is contact... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Because that same supramundane wholesome jhāna has been performed and developed, as its result, being secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the void first jhāna, which is of painful progress and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the five-factored path comes to be: Right View, Right Thought, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration. This is called the 'five-factored path'. The remaining states are associated with the five-factored path.

502. Pañcaṅgiko maggo – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

502. The five-factored path: Right View, Right Thought, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration.

503. Tattha [V 0.0271] katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammādiṭṭhi”. Avasesā dhammā sammādiṭṭhiyā sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā sammāsaṅkappena [T 0.0325] sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā sammāvāyāmena sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā sammāsatiyā sampayuttā.

503. Therein, what is Right View? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, that leads to the waning [of the round of rebirth], for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful progress and slow direct knowledge. At that time, there is contact…pe… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the void first jhāna, which is of painful progress and slow direct knowledge. At that time, whatever wisdom, understanding…pe… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, Right View, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a path factor, included in the path, there is—this is called ‘Right View.’ The remaining states are associated with Right View…pe… the remaining states are associated with Right Thought…pe… the remaining states are associated with Right Effort…pe… the remaining states are associated with Right Mindfulness.

Tattha katamo sammāsamādhi? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo [P 0.0241] hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye cittassa ṭhiti saṇṭhiti avaṭṭhiti avisāhāro avikkhepo avisāhaṭamānasatā [M 0.0250] samatho samādhindriyaṃ samādhibalaṃ sammāsamādhi samādhisambojjhaṅgo maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sammāsamādhi”. Avasesā dhammā sammāsamādhinā sampayuttā.

Therein, what is Right Concentration? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, that leads to the waning [of the round of rebirth], for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of painful progress and slow direct knowledge. At that time, there is contact…pe… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same supramundane wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… he enters and abides in the void first jhāna, which is of painful progress and slow direct knowledge. At that time, whatever stability of mind, firm stability, establishment, non-wavering, non-distraction, a state of unwavering mind, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, Right Concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path, there is—this is called ‘Right Concentration.’ The remaining states are associated with Right Concentration.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Interrogation.

504. Ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

504. The Noble Eightfold Path, namely: Right View, Right Thought, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration.

505. Aṭṭhannaṃ [V 0.0272] maggaṅgānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

505. Of the eight path factors, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, how many are indeterminate…pe… how many are with defilements, how many are without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads.

506. Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Sammāsaṅkappo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto; satta maggaṅgā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā[T 0.0326], siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā. Anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Sammāsaṅkappo avitakkavicāramatto; satta maggaṅgā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Sammāsaṅkappo pītisahagato, sukhasahagato, na upekkhāsahagato; satta maggaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā. Appamāṇā. Appamāṇārammaṇā. Paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino; siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā [M 0.0251] paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Bahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

506. Some are wholesome, some are indeterminate. Right Thought is associated with pleasant feeling; the seven path factors may be associated with pleasant feeling, or they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Some are resultant, some are result-producing states. They are not clung to and are not objects of clinging. They are undefiled and not productive of defilement. Right Thought is without initial application and with only sustained application; the seven path factors may be with initial and sustained application, or without initial application and with only sustained application, or without initial and sustained application. Right Thought is accompanied by rapture, accompanied by happiness, and not accompanied by equanimity; the seven path factors may be accompanied by rapture, or accompanied by happiness, or accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. They do not have a cause that is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Some lead to the waning [of the round of rebirth], some lead neither to accumulation nor to the waning [of the round of rebirth]. Some are of trainees, some are of non-trainees. They are immeasurable. They have an immeasurable object. They are sublime. Some are of right fixed-destiny, some are of unfixed destiny. They do not have the path as an object; some have the path as a cause, some have the path as a dominant condition; or it cannot be said that they have the path as a cause or have the path as a dominant condition. Some have arisen, some have not arisen, some are arising. Some are past, some are future, some are present. It cannot be said that they have a past object, a future object, or a present object. Some are internal, some are external, some are internal-and-external. They have an external object. They are invisible and non-impingent.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads.

507. Sammādiṭṭhi [P 0.0242] hetu, satta maggaṅgā na hetū. Sahetukā. Hetusampayuttā. Sammādiṭṭhi hetu ceva sahetukā ca, satta maggaṅgā na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Sammādiṭṭhi hetu ceva hetusampayuttā ca, satta maggaṅgā [T 0.0327] na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Satta maggaṅgā na hetū sahetukā, sammādiṭṭhi na vattabbā na hetu sahetukātipi, na hetu ahetukātipi.

507. Right View is a root; the other seven path factors are not roots. They are with roots. They are root-associated. Right View is both a root and with roots; of the seven path factors, it cannot be said that they are ‘both a root and with roots,’ but rather that they are ‘with roots but not a root.’ Right View is both a root and root-associated; of the seven path factors, it cannot be said that they are ‘both a root and root-associated,’ but rather that they are ‘root-associated but not a root.’ The seven path factors are not roots but are with roots; of Right View, it cannot be said that it is ‘not a root but with roots,’ nor that it is ‘not a root and rootless.’

Sappaccayā[V 0.0273]. Saṅkhatā. Anidassanā. Appaṭighā. Arūpā. Lokuttarā. Kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

They are with conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They are non-impingent. They are immaterial. They are supramundane. They are cognizable by some consciousness and not cognizable by some consciousness.

No āsavā. Anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cātipi, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā. Anāsavā.

They are not taints. They are taintless. They are dissociated from the taints. It cannot be said that they are ‘both taints and subject to taints,’ nor that they are ‘subject to taints but not taints.’ It cannot be said that they are ‘both taints and associated with taints,’ nor that they are ‘associated with taints but not taints.’ They are dissociated from the taints. They are taintless.

No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā. Cetasikā. Cittasampayuttā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā. Cittasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasahabhuno. Cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino. Bāhirā. No upādā. Anupādinnā.

They are not fetters...pe... not bonds...pe... not floods...pe... not yokes...pe... not hindrances...pe... not misapprehensions...pe... They have an object. They are not consciousness. They are mental factors. They are associated with consciousness. They are conjoined with consciousness. They are produced by consciousness. They are co-existent with consciousness. They follow consciousness. They are conjoined with and produced by consciousness. They are conjoined with, produced by, and co-existent with consciousness. They are conjoined with, produced by, and follow consciousness. They are external. They are not derived. They are unacquired.

No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Sammāsaṅkappo avitakko, satta maggaṅgā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Sammāsaṅkappo savicāro, satta maggaṅgā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Sammāsaṅkappo sappītiko[M 0.0252], satta maggaṅgā siyā [T 0.0328] sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Sammāsaṅkappo pītisahagato, satta maggaṅgā siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Sammāsaṅkappo sukhasahagato, satta maggaṅgā siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Sammāsaṅkappo na upekkhāsahagato, satta maggaṅgā siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Na [P 0.0243] kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā. Apariyāpannā. Siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā. Anuttarā. Araṇāti.

They are not clingings...pe... not defilements...pe... They are not to be abandoned by vision. They are not to be abandoned by cultivation. They do not have roots to be abandoned by vision. They do not have roots to be abandoned by cultivation. Right Thought is without initial application; the other seven path factors may be with initial application, or they may be without initial application. Right Thought is with sustained application; the other seven path factors may be with sustained application, or they may be without sustained application. Right Thought is with rapture; the other seven path factors may be with rapture, or they may be without rapture. Right Thought is accompanied by rapture; the other seven path factors may be accompanied by rapture, or they may not be accompanied by rapture. Right Thought is accompanied by happiness; the other seven path factors may be accompanied by happiness, or they may not be accompanied by happiness. Right Thought is not accompanied by equanimity; the other seven path factors may be accompanied by equanimity, or they may not be accompanied by equanimity. They are not of the sense-sphere. They are not of the form-sphere. They are not of the formless-sphere. They are unincluded. Some are leading out, some are not leading out. Some are of fixed destiny, some are of unfixed destiny. They are unexcelled. They are without conflict.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Questionnaire.

Maggaṅgavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Path Factors is concluded.

12. Jhānavibhaṅgo

12. 12. Analysis of Jhāna

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Exposition

508. Idha [M 0.0253][P 0.0244][V 0.0274] bhikkhu pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati, ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu indriyesu guttadvāro bhojane mattaññū pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto sātaccaṃ nepakkaṃ bodhipakkhikānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto. So abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite sammiñjite (sī. syā.) pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī [T 0.0329] hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ vijanavātaṃ manussarāhasseyyakaṃ manussarāhaseyyakaṃ (sī. syā.) paṭisallānasāruppaṃ. So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodheti. Byāpādapadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādapadosā cittaṃ parisodheti. Thinamiddhaṃ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodheti. Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto[P 0.0245], uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodheti. Vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodheti. So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe vivicceva kāmehi [V 0.0275] vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; vitakkavicārānaṃ [M 0.0254] vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti [T 0.0330] – “upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī”ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā “ananto ākāso”ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma “anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma “natthi kiñcī”ti ākiñcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati; sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati.

508. Here, a bhikkhu dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint, accomplished in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults; undertaking and training in the training rules, with guarded sense faculties, moderate in eating, devoted to wakefulness in the early and late watches of the night, and devoted to the practice of the qualities conducive to enlightenment with persistence and prudence. He acts with clear comprehension in going forward and returning; in looking ahead and looking around; in bending and stretching; in wearing the outer robe, bowl, and robes; in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; in defecating and urinating; in walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent. He resorts to a secluded lodging: a forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a glen, a hillside cave, a charnel ground, a forest thicket, the open air, a heap of straw—a place that is quiet, free from noise, secluded from people, private, and suitable for solitary retreat. Having gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty place, he sits down, folds his legs crosswise, holds his body erect, and establishes mindfulness before him. Abandoning covetousness for the world, he dwells with a mind free from covetousness; he purifies his mind from covetousness. Abandoning ill will and aversion, he dwells with a mind free from ill will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; he purifies his mind from ill will and aversion. Abandoning sloth and torpor, he dwells free from sloth and torpor, percipient of light, mindful and clearly comprehending; he purifies his mind from sloth and torpor. Abandoning restlessness and remorse, he dwells unagitated, with a mind inwardly pacified; he purifies his mind from restlessness and remorse. Abandoning doubt, he dwells having crossed over doubt, without perplexity about wholesome states; he purifies his mind from doubt. Having abandoned these five hindrances, defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. With the stilling of initial and sustained thought, he enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without initial and sustained thought, and has rapture and pleasure born of concentration. With the fading away of rapture, he abides in equanimity, and, mindful and clearly comprehending, he experiences pleasure with the body; he enters and abides in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, he abides pleasantly.’ With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and displeasure, he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has the purification of mindfulness by equanimity. With the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the passing away of perceptions of resistance, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ he enters and abides in the base of infinite space. By completely surmounting the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ he enters and abides in the base of infinite consciousness. By completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ he enters and abides in the base of nothingness. By completely surmounting the base of nothingness, he enters and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Mātikā

The Matrix

509. “Idhā”ti imissā diṭṭhiyā, imissā khantiyā, imissā ruciyā, imasmiṃ ādāye, imasmiṃ dhamme, imasmiṃ vinaye, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, imasmiṃ pāvacane, imasmiṃ brahmacariye, imasmiṃ satthusāsane. Tena vuccati “idhā”ti.

509. “Here” means: in this view, in this forbearance, in this preference, in this adoption, in this Dhamma, in this Discipline, in this Dhamma and Discipline, in this teaching, in this holy life, in this Teacher’s Dispensation. Therefore it is said, “here.”

510. “Bhikkhū”ti samaññāya bhikkhu, paṭiññāya bhikkhu, bhikkhatīti bhikkhu, bhikkhakoti bhikkhu, bhikkhācariyaṃ ajjhupagatoti bhikkhu, bhinnapaṭadharoti bhikkhu, bhindati pāpake akusale dhammeti bhikkhu, bhinnattā pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhikkhu, odhiso [P 0.0246] kilesānaṃ pahānā bhikkhu, anodhiso kilesānaṃ pahānā bhikkhu, sekkho bhikkhu, asekkho bhikkhu, nevasekkhanāsekkho [T 0.0331] bhikkhu, aggo bhikkhu, bhadro bhikkhu, maṇḍo bhikkhu, sāro bhikkhu, samaggena saṅghena ñatticatutthena kammena akuppena ṭhānārahena upasampanno bhikkhu.

510. “Bhikkhu” means: a bhikkhu by designation; a bhikkhu by acknowledgement; one who begs is a bhikkhu; one who is a beggar is a bhikkhu; one who has entered upon the mendicant life is a bhikkhu; one who wears ragged robes is a bhikkhu; one who breaks up evil, unwholesome states is a bhikkhu; because of having broken up evil, unwholesome states, he is a bhikkhu; a bhikkhu by the partial abandonment of the defilements; a bhikkhu by the non-limited abandonment of the defilements; a bhikkhu who is a trainee; a bhikkhu who is an adept; a bhikkhu who is neither a trainee nor an adept; the foremost is a bhikkhu; the auspicious is a bhikkhu; the pure is a bhikkhu; the essence is a bhikkhu; one who has been given the higher ordination by a united Saṅgha by means of a formal act consisting of a motion as the fourth, which is unshakeable and fit for the occasion, is a bhikkhu.

511. “Pātimokkha”nti sīlaṃ patiṭṭhā ādi caraṇaṃ saṃyamo saṃvaro mokkhaṃ pāmokkhaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā. Saṃvaroti. Kāyiko [M 0.0255] avītikkamo, vācasiko avītikkamo[V 0.0276], kāyikavācasiko avītikkamo. Saṃvutoti. Iminā pātimokkhasaṃvarena upeto hoti samupeto upāgato samupāgato upapanno sampanno samannāgato. Tena vuccati “pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto”ti.

511. “Pātimokkha” means: virtue, foundation, beginning, conduct, restraint, control, liberation, the foremost for the attainment of wholesome states. “Restraint” means: bodily non-transgression, verbal non-transgression, bodily and verbal non-transgression. “Restrained” means: he is endowed with this Pātimokkha restraint, fully endowed, has reached it, has fully reached it, is possessed of it, is accomplished, is characterized by it. Therefore he is called “one restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint.”

512. “Viharatī”ti iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

512. “Dwells” means: he comports himself, proceeds, maintains, keeps going, carries on, lives, abides. Therefore it is said, “dwells.”

513. “Ācāragocarasampanno”ti atthi ācāro, atthi anācāro.

513. “Accomplished in conduct and resort” means: there is conduct, and there is misconduct.

Tattha katamo anācāro? Kāyiko vītikkamo, vācasiko vītikkamo, kāyikavācasiko vītikkamo – ayaṃ vuccati “anācāro”. Sabbampi dussīlyaṃ anācāro. Idhekacco veḷudānena vā pattadānena vā pupphadānena vā phaladānena vā sinānadānena vā dantakaṭṭhadānena vā cāṭukamyatāya vā muggasūpyatāya muggasuppatāya (sī.) vā pāribhaṭayatāya vā jaṅghapesanikena vā aññataraññatarena vā buddhapaṭikuṭṭhena micchāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ vuccati “anācāro”.

Therein, what is misconduct? Bodily transgression, verbal transgression, and bodily and verbal transgression—this is called 'misconduct'. All immorality is misconduct. In this Dispensation, a certain bhikkhu makes a living by giving bamboo, or by giving leaves, or by giving flowers, or by giving fruit, or by giving bath powder, or by giving tooth-wood; or by servility, or by bean-soup-like conduct, or by acting as a plaything, or by running messages, or by any other wrong livelihood condemned by the Buddha—this is also called 'misconduct'.

Tattha katamo ācāro? Kāyiko avītikkamo, vācasiko avītikkamo, kāyikavācasiko avītikkamo – ayaṃ vuccati “ācāro”[T 0.0332]. Sabbopi sīlasaṃvaro ācāro. Idhekacco na veḷudānena na pattadānena na pupphadānena na phaladānena na sinānadānena na dantakaṭṭhadānena na cāṭukamyatāya na muggasūpyatāya na pāribhaṭayatāya na jaṅghapesanikena na aññataraññatarena buddhapaṭikuṭṭhena micchāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ vuccati “ācāro”.

Therein, what is conduct? Bodily non-transgression, verbal non-transgression, and bodily and verbal non-transgression—this is called 'conduct'. All restraint in virtue is conduct. In this Dispensation, a certain bhikkhu does not make a living by giving bamboo, nor by giving leaves, nor by giving flowers, nor by giving fruit, nor by giving bath powder, nor by giving tooth-wood; nor by servility, nor by bean-soup-like conduct, nor by acting as a plaything, nor by running messages, nor by any other wrong livelihood condemned by the Buddha—this is called 'conduct'.

514. “Gocaro”ti atthi gocaro, atthi agocaro.

514. Regarding 'resort' (gocara): there is proper resort, and there is improper resort.

Tattha katamo agocaro? Idhekacco [P 0.0247] vesiyāgocaro vā hoti vidhavāgocaro vā thullakumārigocaro vā paṇḍakagocaro vā bhikkhunigocaro vā pānāgāragocaro vā, saṃsaṭṭho viharati rājūhi rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi ananulomikena saṃsaggena[M 0.0256]; yāni vā [V 0.0277] pana tāni kulāni assaddhāni appasannāni anopānabhūtāni akkosakaparibhāsakāni anatthakāmāni ahitakāmāni aphāsukakāmāni ayogakkhemakāmāni bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, tathārūpāni kulāni sevati bhajati payirupāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “agocaro”.

Therein, what is an improper resort? In this Dispensation, a certain bhikkhu resorts to prostitutes, or resorts to widows, or resorts to mature spinsters, or resorts to pandakas, or resorts to bhikkhunīs, or resorts to taverns. He dwells associated with kings, great royal ministers, sectarians, and the disciples of sectarians, with an inappropriate association. And whatever families are faithless, displeased, not like a well, abusive and reviling, who desire what is not beneficial, who desire what is not for the welfare, who desire what is not comfortable, who do not desire security from bondage for bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, and female lay followers—he resorts to, associates with, and repeatedly attends upon such families. This is called 'an improper resort'.

Tattha katamo gocaro? Idhekacco na vesiyāgocaro hoti na vidhavāgocaro na thullakumārigocaro na paṇḍakagocaro na bhikkhunigocaro na pānāgāragocaro, asaṃsaṭṭho viharati rājūhi rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi ananulomikena saṃsaggena; yāni vā pana tāni kulāni saddhāni pasannāni opānabhūtāni kāsāvapajjotāni isivātapaṭivātāni atthakāmāni hitakāmāni phāsukakāmāni yogakkhemakāmāni bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, tathārūpāni kulāni sevati bhajati payirupāsati – ayaṃ vuccati [T 0.0333] “gocaro”. Iti iminā ca ācārena iminā ca gocarena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “ācāragocarasampanno”ti.

Therein, what is a proper resort? In this Dispensation, a certain bhikkhu does not resort to prostitutes, nor widows, nor mature spinsters, nor pandakas, nor bhikkhunīs, nor taverns. He dwells unassociated with kings, great royal ministers, sectarians, and the disciples of sectarians, with an inappropriate association. And whatever families are faithful, pleased, like a well, illumined by the saffron robes, fragrant with the air of sages; families that desire what is beneficial, desire what is for the welfare, desire what is comfortable, desire security from bondage for bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, and female lay followers—he resorts to, associates with, and repeatedly attends upon such families. This is called 'a proper resort'. Thus, he is endowed... and well endowed with this conduct and this resort. Therefore, he is called 'one accomplished in conduct and resort'.

515. “Aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī”ti tattha katame aṇumattā vajjā? Yāni tāni vajjāni appamattakāni oramattakāni lahusāni lahusammatāni saṃyamakaraṇīyāni saṃvarakaraṇīyāni cittuppādakaraṇīyāni manasikārapaṭibaddhāni – ime vuccanti “aṇumattā vajjā”. Iti imesu aṇumattesu vajjesu vajjadassāvī ca hoti bhayadassāvī ca ādīnavadassāvī ca nissaraṇadassāvī ca. Tena vuccati “aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī”ti.

515. “One who sees danger in the slightest faults” means: Therein, what are the slightest faults? Those faults that are of small measure, of very small measure, light, considered light, requiring restraint, requiring guarding, requiring an act of mind, connected with attention—these are called 'the slightest faults'. Thus, in regard to these slightest faults, one sees them as a fault, sees danger, sees the drawback, and sees the escape. Therefore, one is called 'one who sees danger in the slightest faults'.

516. “Samādāya [P 0.0248] sikkhati sikkhāpadesū”ti tattha katamā sikkhā? Catasso sikkhā – bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhusikkhā, bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhunisikkhā, upāsakānaṃ upāsakasikkhā, upāsikānaṃ upāsikasikkhā. Imā vuccanti “sikkhāyo”. Iti imāsu sikkhāsu sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ samādāya vattati. Tena vuccati “samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesū”ti.

516. “Having undertaken them, he trains in the training rules” means: Therein, what is the training? There are four trainings: the training for bhikkhus, the training for bhikkhunīs, the training for male lay followers, and the training for female lay followers. These are called 'the trainings'. Thus, in regard to these training rules, he undertakes and practices them in their entirety, in every way, completely and without remainder. Therefore, it is said, 'having undertaken them, he trains in the training rules'.

517. “Indriyesu guttadvāro”ti atthi indriyesu guttadvāratā, atthi aguttadvāratā.

517. “One who has the doors of his sense faculties guarded” means: there is the state of having guarded doors in regard to the sense faculties, and there is the state of having unguarded doors.

Tattha [M 0.0257][V 0.0278] katamā indriyesu aguttadvāratā? Idhekacco cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya [T 0.0334] rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Yā imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ agutti agopanā anārakkho asaṃvaro – ayaṃ vuccati “indriyesu aguttadvāratā”.

Therein, what is the state of having unguarded doors in the sense faculties? In this Dispensation, a certain bhikkhu, having seen a form with the eye, grasps its signs and features. Because of which, while he dwells with his eye faculty unrestrained, evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him; he does not practice for its restraint, he does not guard the eye faculty, he does not attain restraint in the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear... having smelled an odor with the nose... having tasted a flavor with the tongue... having touched a tangible object with the body... having cognized a mental object with the mind, he grasps its signs and features. Because of which, while he dwells with his mind faculty unrestrained, evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him; he does not practice for its restraint, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not attain restraint in the mind faculty. Whatever is the non-guarding, non-protecting, non-watching over, and non-restraint of these six sense faculties—this is called 'the state of having unguarded doors in the sense faculties'.

Tattha katamā indriyesu guttadvāratā? Idhekacco cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Ñatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Yā imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ gutti gopanā ārakkho saṃvaro – ayaṃ vuccati “indriyesu [P 0.0249] guttadvāratā”. Imāya indriyesu guttadvāratāya upeto hoti samupeto…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “indriyesu guttadvāro”ti.

Therein, what is the state of having guarded doors in the sense faculties? Here, a certain bhikkhu, having seen a form with the eye, does not grasp its signs or its features. Since, if he were to dwell with the eye faculty unrestrained, evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him, he practices for its restraint, guards the eye faculty, and attains restraint in the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear... having smelled an odor with the nose... having tasted a flavor with the tongue... having touched a tangible object with the body... having cognized a mental object with the mind, he does not grasp its signs or its features. Since, if he were to dwell with the mind faculty unrestrained, evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him, he practices for its restraint, guards the mind faculty, and attains restraint in the mind faculty. Whatever is the guarding, protection, watching over, and restraint of these six sense faculties—this is called 'the state of having guarded doors in the sense faculties.' He is endowed, fully endowed... possessed of this state of having guarded doors in the sense faculties. Therefore, he is called 'one who has guarded doors in the sense faculties'.

518. “Bhojane mattaññū”ti atthi bhojane mattaññutā, atthi bhojane amattaññutā.

518. Regarding the term 'knowing the measure in eating': there is knowing the measure in eating, and there is not knowing the measure in eating.

Tattha katamā bhojane amattaññutā? Idhekacco appaṭisaṅkhā ayoniso āhāraṃ āhāreti davāya madāya maṇḍanāya vibhūsanāya. Yā tattha asantuṭṭhitā amattaññutā appaṭisaṅkhā bhojane – ayaṃ vuccati “bhojane amattaññutā”ti.

Therein, what is not knowing the measure in eating? Here, a certain bhikkhu consumes food without reflection and improperly: for amusement, for intoxication, for physical charm, and for beautification. Whatever lack of contentment, lack of knowing the measure, and lack of reflection there is in regard to food—this is called 'not knowing the measure in eating'.

Tattha [M 0.0258][V 0.0279] katamā bhojane mattaññutā? Idhekacco paṭisaṅkhā yoniso āhāraṃ āhāreti – “neva davāya na madāya na maṇḍanāya na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya vihiṃsūparatiyā brahmacariyānuggahāya, iti purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsu vihāro cā”ti. Yā tattha santuṭṭhitā mattaññutā paṭisaṅkhā bhojane – ayaṃ vuccati “bhojane mattaññutā”. Imāya bhojane mattaññutāya upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “bhojane mattaññū”ti.

Therein, what is knowing the measure in eating? Here, a certain bhikkhu, reflecting wisely, consumes food properly: 'Not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for physical charm, not for beautification, but only for the maintenance of this body, for its sustenance, for the cessation of the affliction of hunger, and for the support of the holy life. Thus, I will ward off the old feeling and not give rise to a new feeling; there will be sustenance for me, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.' Whatever contentment, knowing the measure, and reflection there is in regard to food—this is called 'knowing the measure in eating.' He is endowed... possessed of this state of knowing the measure in eating. Therefore, he is called 'one who knows the measure in eating'.

519. Kathañca bhikkhu pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto hoti? Idha bhikkhu divasaṃ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti, rattiyā paṭhamayāmaṃ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti, rattiyā majjhimayāmaṃ dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappeti pāde pādaṃ pādena pādaṃ (syā.) accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasikaritvā, rattiyā pacchimayāmaṃ paccuṭṭhāya caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti. Evaṃ bhikkhu [T 0.0336] pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto.

519. And how is a bhikkhu devoted to the practice of wakefulness during the earlier and later watches of the night? Here, a bhikkhu cleanses his mind of obstructive states during the day while walking and sitting. During the first watch of the night, he cleanses his mind of obstructive states while walking and sitting. During the middle watch of the night, he adopts the lion's posture on his right side, placing one foot on the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having fixed his mind on the perception of rising. During the last watch of the night, having risen, he cleanses his mind of obstructive states while walking and sitting. In this way, a bhikkhu is devoted to the practice of wakefulness during the earlier and later watches of the night.

520. “Sātacca”nti. Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo.

520. Regarding the term 'perseverance': it is whatever mental exertion of energy... and so on... right effort there is.

521. “Nepakka”nti. Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi.

521. Regarding the term 'prudence': it is whatever wisdom, discernment... and so on... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view there is.

522. “Bodhipakkhikānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto”ti. Tattha katame bodhipakkhikā dhammā? Satta bojjhaṅgā – satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo[P 0.0250]. Ime vuccanti “bodhipakkhikā dhammā”. Iti te bodhipakkhike dhamme āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tena vuccati “bodhipakkhikānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto”ti.

522. Regarding the phrase 'one who is devoted to the development of the qualities pertaining to enlightenment': Therein, what are the qualities pertaining to enlightenment? The seven factors of enlightenment: the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity. These are called 'the qualities pertaining to enlightenment.' Thus, he resorts to, develops, and cultivates these qualities pertaining to enlightenment. Therefore, he is called 'one who is devoted to the development of the qualities pertaining to enlightenment'.

523. Kathañca [M 0.0259] bhikkhu abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti[V 0.0280], uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti; gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti? Idha bhikkhu sato sampajāno abhikkamati, sato sampajāno paṭikkamati, sato sampajāno āloketi, sato sampajāno viloketi, sato sampajāno samiñjeti, sato sampajāno pasāreti, sato sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe [T 0.0337] sato sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sato sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sato sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sato sampajānakārī hotīti.

523. And how is a bhikkhu one who acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning, when looking straight ahead and looking sideways, when bending and stretching, in wearing the double-robe, bowl, and robes, when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, in the act of defecating and urinating, when going, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and in being silent? Here, a bhikkhu, being mindful and clearly comprehending, goes forward; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he returns; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks straight ahead; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks sideways; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he bends; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he stretches. He acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension in wearing the double-robe, bowl, and robes; he acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension in the act of defecating and urinating; he acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension when going, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and in being silent.

524. Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati paṭissati sati saraṇatā dhāraṇatā apilāpanatā asammusanatā sati satindriyaṃ satibalaṃ sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”.

524. Among these, what is mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection, remembrance, the state of remembering, the state of retaining, non-superficiality, and non-forgetfulness there is; mindfulness as the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, and right mindfulness—this is called 'mindfulness'.

525. “Sampajāno”ti tattha katamaṃ sampajaññaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo sallakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇā paṇḍiccaṃ kosallaṃ nepuññaṃ vebhabyā cintā upaparikkhā bhūrīmedhā pariṇāyikā vipassanā sampajaññaṃ patodo paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ paññāsatthaṃ paññāpāsādo paññāāloko paññāobhāso paññāpajjoto paññāratanaṃ amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “sampajaññaṃ”. Iti imāya ca satiyā iminā ca sampajaññena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Evaṃ bhikkhu sato sampajāno abhikkamati, sato sampajāno paṭikkamati, sato sampajāno āloketi, sato sampajāno viloketi, sato sampajāno samiñjeti, sato sampajāno pasāreti, sato sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sato sampajānakārī [P 0.0251] hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sato sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sato sampajānakārī [M 0.0260] hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti.

525. “Clearly comprehending”: therein, what is clear comprehension? It is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment, repeated close discernment, learnedness, skillfulness, ingenuity, analysis, reflection, scrutiny, vast wisdom, penetrating wisdom, guiding wisdom, insight, clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the wisdom faculty, the wisdom power, the sword of wisdom, the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view—this is called “clear comprehension.” Thus, one is endowed with this mindfulness and with this clear comprehension… possessed of it. In this way, a bhikkhu, being mindful and clearly comprehending, goes forward; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he returns; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks straight ahead; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks sideways; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he bends; being mindful and clearly comprehending, he stretches. He is one who acts with clear comprehension; he is one who acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension in wearing the double-robe, bowl, and robe. He is one who acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting. He is one who acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension in the act of defecating and urinating. He is one who acts with mindfulness and clear comprehension when going, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and remaining silent.

526. “Vivitta”nti [T 0.0338] santike cepi senāsanaṃ hoti, tañca anākiṇṇaṃ gahaṭṭhehi pabbajitehi. Tena taṃ vivittaṃ. Dūre cepi senāsanaṃ hoti, tañca anākiṇṇaṃ gahaṭṭhehi pabbajitehi. Tena taṃ vivittaṃ.

526. “Secluded”: even if a lodging is nearby, it is not frequented by householders and monastics. For that reason it is secluded. Even if a lodging is far away, it is not frequented by householders and monastics. For that reason it is secluded.

527. “Senāsana”nti mañcopi senāsanaṃ, pīṭhampi senāsanaṃ, bhisipi senāsanaṃ, bibbohanampi [V 0.0281] bimbohanampi (sī. syā.) senāsanaṃ, vihāropi senāsanaṃ, aḍḍhayogopi senāsanaṃ, pāsādopi senāsanaṃ, aṭṭopi senāsanaṃ, māḷopi senāsanaṃ, leṇampi senāsanaṃ, guhāpi senāsanaṃ, rukkhamūlampi senāsanaṃ, veḷugumbopi senāsanaṃ. Yattha vā pana bhikkhū paṭikkamanti sabbametaṃ senāsanaṃ.

527. “Lodging”: a bed is a lodging, a chair is a lodging, a mattress is a lodging, a pillow is a lodging, a dwelling is a lodging, a lean-to is a lodging, a mansion is a lodging, a watchtower is a lodging, a hall is a lodging, a shelter is a lodging, a cave is a lodging, the foot of a tree is a lodging, a bamboo grove is a lodging. Or wherever bhikkhus congregate, all that is a lodging.

528. “Vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajatī”ti imaṃ vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati sambhajati sevati nisevati saṃsevati. Tena vuccati “vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajatī”ti.

528. “He resorts to a secluded lodging”: he resorts to, frequently resorts to, frequents, constantly frequents, and thoroughly frequents this secluded lodging. Therefore it is said: “he resorts to a secluded lodging.”

529. “Arañña”nti nikkhamitvā bahi indakhīlā sabbametaṃ araññaṃ.

529. “Forest”: having gone out beyond the threshold, all that is forest.

530. “Rukkhamūla”nti rukkhamūlaṃyeva rukkhamūlaṃ. Pabbatoyeva pabbato. Kandarāyeva kandarā. Giriguhāyeva giriguhā. Susānaṃyeva susānaṃ. Abbhokāsoyeva abbhokāso. Palālapuñjoyeva palālapuñjo.

530. “The foot of a tree”: is just the foot of a tree. “A mountain”: is just a mountain. “A ravine”: is just a ravine. “A mountain cave”: is just a mountain cave. “A charnel ground”: is just a charnel ground. “The open air”: is just the open air. “A heap of straw”: is just a heap of straw.

531. “Vanapattha”nti dūrānametaṃ senāsanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. “Vanapattha”nti vanasaṇḍānametaṃ senāsanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. “Vanapattha”nti bhīsanakānametaṃ bhiṃsanakānametaṃ (sī. syā.) senāsanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. “Vanapattha”nti salomahaṃsānametaṃ senāsanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. “Vanapattha”nti pariyantānametaṃ senāsanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. “Vanapattha”nti na manussūpacārānametaṃ senāsanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. “Vanapattha”nti durabhisambhavānametaṃ [T 0.0339] senāsanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

531. “Forest tracts”: this is a designation for remote lodgings. “Forest tracts”: this is a designation for lodgings in forest groves. “Forest tracts”: this is a designation for frightening lodgings. “Forest tracts”: this is a designation for lodgings that make one’s hair stand on end. “Forest tracts”: this is a designation for peripheral lodgings. “Forest tracts”: this is a designation for lodgings not frequented by people. “Forest tracts”: this is a designation for lodgings that are difficult to reach.

532. “Appasadda”nti [M 0.0261] santike cepi senāsanaṃ hoti, tañca anākiṇṇaṃ gahaṭṭhehi pabbajitehi. Tena taṃ appasaddaṃ. Dūre cepi senāsanaṃ hoti, tañca anākiṇṇaṃ gahaṭṭhehi pabbajitehi. Tena taṃ appasaddaṃ.

532. “With little sound”: even if a lodging is nearby, it is not frequented by householders and monastics. For that reason it has little sound. Even if a lodging is far away, it is not frequented by householders and monastics. For that reason it has little sound.

533. “Appanigghosa”nti yadeva taṃ appasaddaṃ tadeva taṃ appanigghosaṃ. Yadeva taṃ appanigghosaṃ tadeva [P 0.0252] taṃ vijanavātaṃ. Yadeva taṃ vijanavātaṃ tadeva taṃ manussarāhasseyyakaṃ. Yadeva taṃ manussarāhasseyyakaṃ tadeva taṃ paṭisallānasāruppaṃ.

533. “With little noise”: whatever has little sound, that has little noise. Whatever has little noise, that is secluded from people. Whatever is secluded from people, that is fit for human privacy. Whatever is fit for human privacy, that is suitable for seclusion.

534. “Araññagato [V 0.0282] vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā”ti araññagato vā hoti rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā.

534. “Gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling”: he has gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling.

535. “Nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā”ti nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā.

535. “He sits down, having folded his legs crosswise”: he is seated, having folded his legs crosswise.

536. “Ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāyā”ti ujuko hoti kāyo ṭhito paṇihito.

536. “Holding his body erect”: his body is straight, established, and set upright.

537. “Parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā”ti tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati paṭissati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”. Ayaṃ sati upaṭṭhitā hoti supaṭṭhitā nāsikagge vā mukhanimitte vā. Tena vuccati “parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā”ti.

537. “Having established mindfulness before him”: herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever is mindfulness, recollection, remembrance… right mindfulness—this is called “mindfulness.” This mindfulness is established, well established, at the tip of the nose or at the sign of the mouth. Therefore it is said: “having established mindfulness before him.”

538. “Abhijjhaṃ loke pahāyā”ti tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo [T 0.0340] sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “abhijjhā”.

538. “Having abandoned covetousness for the world”: herein, what is covetousness? Whatever is lust, strong lust… lust of the mind—this is called “covetousness.”

Tattha katamo loko? Pañcupādānakkhandhā loko – ayaṃ vuccati “loko”. Ayaṃ abhijjhā imamhi loke santā hoti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “abhijjhaṃ loke pahāyā”ti.

Herein, what is the world? The five aggregates subject to clinging are the world—this is called “the world.” This covetousness in regard to this world is stilled, quieted, pacified, has set, has completely set, is given up, relinquished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is said: “having abandoned covetousness for the world.”

539. “Vigatābhijjhena cetasā”ti tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ vigatābhijjhaṃ hoti. Tena vuccati “vigatābhijjhena cetasā”ti.

539. “With a mind free from covetousness”: herein, what is the mind? That which is mind, mentality, consciousness… the mind-consciousness element that arises from that—this is called “the mind.” This mind is free from covetousness. Therefore it is said: “with a mind free from covetousness.”

540. “Viharatī”ti [M 0.0262] iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

540. “He dwells”: he comports himself, proceeds, maintains himself, keeps himself going, carries on, behaves, and dwells. Therefore it is said: “he dwells.”

541. “Abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti tattha katamā abhijjhā? Yo rāgo sārāgo…pe… cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “abhijjhā”.

541. “He purifies his mind from covetousness”: herein, what is covetousness? Whatever is lust, strong lust… lust of the mind—this is called “covetousness.”

Tattha [V 0.0283] katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya abhijjhāya sodheti visodheti parisodheti moceti vimoceti parimoceti. Tena vuccati “abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti.

Herein, what is the mind? That which is mind, mentality, consciousness… the mind-consciousness element that arises from that—this is called “the mind.” From this covetousness he cleanses this mind, purifies it, completely purifies it; he releases it, sets it free, and completely sets it free. Therefore it is said: “he purifies his mind from covetousness.”

542. “Byāpādapadosaṃ [P 0.0253] pahāyā”ti atthi byāpādo, atthi padoso.

542. “Having abandoned ill will and malice”: there is ill will, and there is malice.

Tattha katamo byāpādo? Yo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso [T 0.0341] dussanā dussitattaṃ dūsanā dūsitattaṃ (syā.) byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “byāpādo”.

Herein, what is ill will? Whatever is animosity of mind, repugnance, resistance, opposition, anger, fierce anger, furious anger, hatred, intense hatred, extreme hatred, ill will of mind, malevolence of mind, wrath, wrathfulness, the state of being wrathful, hatred, hatefulness, the state of being hateful, ill will, the manner of ill will, the state of having ill will, antagonism, opposition, fierceness, surliness, displeasure of mind—this is called “ill will.”

Tattha katamo padoso? Yo byāpādo so padoso, yo padoso so byāpādo. Iti ayañca byāpādo ayañca padoso santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “byāpādapadosaṃ pahāyā”ti.

Herein, what is malice? Whatever is ill will is malice, and whatever is malice is ill will. Thus this ill will and this malice are stilled, quieted, pacified, have set, have completely set, are given up, relinquished, dried up, completely dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is said: “having abandoned ill will and malice.”

543. “Abyāpannacitto”ti tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ abyāpannaṃ hoti. Tena vuccati “abyāpannacitto”ti.

543. “With a mind free from ill will”: Herein, what is the mind? That which is mind, mentality, consciousness… the mind-consciousness element that arises from that—this is called “the mind.” This mind is free from ill will. Therefore it is said: “with a mind free from ill will.”

544. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

544. “He dwells”: …pe… Therefore it is said: “he dwells.”

545. “Byāpādapadosā [M 0.0263] cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti. Atthi byāpādo atthi padoso.

545. “He purifies his mind from ill will and malice”: There is ill will, and there is malice.

Tattha katamo byāpādo? Yo cittassa āghāto…pe… caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “byāpādo”.

Herein, what is ill will? Whatever is animosity of mind… fierceness, surliness, displeasure of mind—this is called “ill will.”

Tattha katamo padoso? Yo byāpādo so padoso, yo padoso so byāpādo.

Herein, what is malice? Whatever is ill will is malice, and whatever is malice is ill will.

Tattha [V 0.0284] katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ [T 0.0342] vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imamhā byāpādapadosā sodheti visodheti parisodheti moceti vimoceti parimoceti. Tena vuccati “byāpādapadosā cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti.

Herein, what is the mind? That which is mind, mentality, consciousness… the mind-consciousness element that arises from that—this is called “the mind.” From this ill will and malice he cleanses this mind, purifies it, completely purifies it; he releases it, sets it free, and completely sets it free. Therefore it is said: “he purifies his mind from ill will and malice.”

546. “Thinamiddhaṃ pahāyā”ti atthi thinaṃ thīnaṃ (sī. syā.), atthi middhaṃ.

546. “Having abandoned sloth and torpor”: there is sloth, and there is torpor.

Tattha katamaṃ thinaṃ? Yā cittassa akalyatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnaṃ līyanā līyitattaṃ thinaṃ thiyanā thiyitattaṃ thīyanā thīyitattaṃ (sī. syā.) cittassa – idaṃ vuccati “thinaṃ”.

Herein, what is sloth? Whatever is the mind’s unfitness, unwieldiness, sluggishness, clinging, shrinking, the manner of shrinking, the state of shrinking, sloth, the manner of being slothful, the state of being slothful of mind—this is called “sloth.”

Tattha katamaṃ middhaṃ? Yā [P 0.0254] kāyassa akalyatā akammaññatā onāho pariyonāho antosamorodho middhaṃ suppaṃ pacalāyikā suppaṃ suppanā suppitattaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “middhaṃ”. Iti idañca thinaṃ idañca middhaṃ santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “thinamiddhaṃ pahāyā”ti.

Herein, what is torpor? Whatever is the body’s unfitness, unworkability, shrouding, enveloping, internal obstruction, torpor, sleep, nodding, sleep, the manner of sleeping, the state of being asleep—this is called “torpor.” Thus both this sloth and this torpor are stilled, quieted, pacified, have set, have completely set, are given up, relinquished, dried up, completely dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is said: “having abandoned sloth and torpor.”

547. “Vigatathinamiddho”ti. Tassa thinamiddhassa cattattā vantattā muttattā pahīnattā paṭinissaṭṭhattā pahīnapaṭinissaṭṭhattā. Tena vuccati “vigatathinamiddho”ti.

547. “Devoid of sloth and torpor”: because that sloth and torpor have been given up, ejected, released, abandoned, relinquished, abandoned and relinquished. Therefore it is said: “devoid of sloth and torpor.”

548. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

548. “He dwells”: …pe… Therefore it is said: “he dwells.”

549. “Ālokasaññī”ti. Tattha katamā saññā? Yā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “saññā”. Ayaṃ saññā ālokā hoti [M 0.0264] vivaṭā parisuddhā pariyodātā. Tena vuccati “ālokasaññī”ti.

549. “Percipient of light”: Herein, what is perception? Whatever is perception, perceiving, the state of having perceived—this is called “perception.” This perception is of light, open, pure, and cleansed. Therefore it is said: “percipient of light.”

550. “Sato sampajāno”ti. Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati [T 0.0343] …pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”.

550. “Mindful and clearly comprehending”: Herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever is mindfulness, recollection …pe… right mindfulness—this is called “mindfulness.”

Tattha katamaṃ sampajaññaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi [V 0.0285] – idaṃ vuccati “sampajaññaṃ”. Iti imāya ca satiyā iminā ca sampajaññena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “sato sampajāno”ti.

Herein, what is clear comprehension? Whatever is wisdom, understanding …pe… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called “clear comprehension.” Thus he is endowed with this mindfulness and with this clear comprehension …pe… possessed of them. Therefore he is said to be “mindful and clearly comprehending.”

551. “Thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti. Atthi thinaṃ, atthi middhaṃ.

551. “He purifies his mind from sloth and torpor”: There is sloth, and there is torpor.

Tattha katamaṃ thinaṃ…pe… idaṃ vuccati “thinaṃ”.

Herein, what is sloth? …pe… This is called “sloth.”

Tattha katamaṃ middhaṃ…pe… idaṃ vuccati “middhaṃ”.

Herein, what is torpor? …pe… This is called “torpor.”

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ…pe… idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imamhā thinamiddhā sodheti visodheti parisodheti moceti vimoceti parimoceti. Tena vuccati “thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti.

Herein, what is the mind? …pe… This is called “the mind.” From this sloth and torpor he cleanses this mind, purifies it, and completely purifies it; he releases it, sets it free, and completely sets it free. Therefore, it is said: “he purifies his mind from sloth and torpor.”

552. “Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāyā”ti atthi uddhaccaṃ, atthi kukkuccaṃ.

552. “Having abandoned restlessness and remorse”: There is restlessness, and there is remorse.

Tattha [P 0.0255] katamaṃ uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati “uddhaccaṃ”.

Herein, what is restlessness? Whatever is the mind’s restlessness, lack of calm, mental distraction, and agitation of mind—this is called “restlessness.”

Tattha katamaṃ kukkuccaṃ? Akappiye kappiyasaññitā, kappiye akappiyasaññitā, avajje vajjasaññitā, vajje avajjasaññitā, yaṃ evarūpaṃ kukkuccaṃ kukkuccāyanā kukkuccāyitattaṃ cetaso vippaṭisāro manovilekhā – idaṃ vuccati “kukkuccaṃ”. Iti idañca uddhaccaṃ idañca kukkuccaṃ [T 0.0344] santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāyā”ti.

Herein, what is remorse? Perceiving the unsuitable as suitable; perceiving the suitable as unsuitable; perceiving the blameless as blameworthy; perceiving the blameworthy as blameless; whatever is such remorse, worrying, state of worry, regret of mind, mental scruple—this is called “remorse.” Thus, both this restlessness and this remorse are calmed, quelled, pacified, set, gone to rest, given up, relinquished, dried up, completely dried up, and made an end of. Therefore, it is said: “having abandoned restlessness and remorse.”

553. “Anuddhato”ti tassa uddhaccakukkuccassa cattattā vantattā muttattā pahīnattā paṭinissaṭṭhattā pahīnapaṭinissaṭṭhattā. Tena vuccati “anuddhato”ti.

553. “Unagitated”: Because that restlessness and remorse have been given up, ejected, released, abandoned, relinquished, abandoned and relinquished. Therefore, it is said: “unagitated.”

554. “Viharatī”ti [V 0.0286] …pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

554. “He dwells”: …pe… Therefore, it is said: “he dwells.”

555. “Vūpasantacitto”ti[M 0.0265]. Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ ajjhattaṃ santaṃ hoti samitaṃ vūpasantaṃ. Tena vuccati “ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto”ti.

555. “With a pacified mind”: Herein, what is the mind? That which is mind, intellect, consciousness…pe… the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called “mind.” This mind is inwardly calmed, quelled, and pacified. Therefore, it is said “with a mind inwardly pacified.”

556. “Uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti atthi uddhaccaṃ, atthi kukkuccaṃ.

556. “He purifies his mind from restlessness and remorse”: There is restlessness, and there is remorse.

Tattha katamaṃ uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati “uddhaccaṃ”.

Herein, what is restlessness? Whatever is the mind’s restlessness, lack of calm, mental distraction, and agitation of mind—this is called “restlessness.”

Tattha katamaṃ kukkuccaṃ…pe… idaṃ vuccati “kukkuccaṃ”.

Herein, what is remorse? …pe… This is called “remorse.”

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ…pe… idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imamhā uddhaccakukkuccā sodheti visodheti parisodheti moceti vimoceti parimoceti. Tena vuccati “uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti.

Herein, what is the mind? …pe… This is called “mind.” From this restlessness and remorse he cleanses this mind, purifies it, and completely purifies it; he releases it, sets it free, and completely sets it free. Therefore, it is said: “he purifies his mind from restlessness and remorse.”

557. “Vicikicchaṃ pahāyā”ti, tattha katamā vicikicchā? Yā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā [T 0.0345] kaṅkhāyitattaṃ vimati vicikicchā dveḷhakaṃ dvidhāpatho saṃsayo anekaṃsaggāho āsappanā parisappanā apariyogāhaṇā chambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati “vicikicchā”. Ayaṃ vicikicchā [P 0.0256] santā hoti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “vicikicchaṃ pahāyā”ti.

557. “Having abandoned doubt”: Herein, what is doubt? Whatever is doubt, doubting, the state of doubt, perplexity, uncertainty, wavering, being at a crossroads, indecisiveness, inability to take a definite stance, floundering, stumbling, inability to grasp, stiffness of mind, and mental scruple—this is called “doubt.” This doubt is calmed, quelled, pacified, set, gone to rest, given up, relinquished, dried up, completely dried up, and made an end of. Therefore, it is said: “having abandoned doubt.”

558. “Tiṇṇavicikiccho”ti, imaṃ vicikicchaṃ tiṇṇo hoti uttiṇṇo nittiṇṇo pāraṅgato pāramanuppatto. Tena vuccati “tiṇṇavicikiccho”ti.

558. “One who has crossed over doubt”: He has crossed over this doubt, transcended it, gone beyond it, has gone to the far shore, has reached the far shore. Therefore, it is said: “one who has crossed over doubt.”

559. “Akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesū”ti imāya vicikicchāya kusalesu dhammesu na kaṅkhati [V 0.0287] na vicikicchati akathaṃkathī hoti nikkathaṃkathī vikathaṃkatho. Tena vuccati “akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesū”ti.

559. “Not perplexed about wholesome states”: Regarding wholesome states, he does not doubt, is not uncertain; he is not perplexed, is devoid of perplexity, has put away perplexity. Therefore, it is said: “not perplexed about wholesome states.”

560. “Vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti, tattha katamā vicikicchā? Yā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā kaṅkhāyitattaṃ chambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati “vicikicchā”.

560. “He purifies his mind of doubt”: Herein, what is doubt? Whatever is doubt, doubting, the state of doubt, stiffness of mind, and mental scruple—this is called “doubt.”

Tattha [M 0.0266] katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya vicikicchāya sodheti visodheti parisodheti moceti vimoceti parimoceti. Tena vuccati “vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodhetī”ti.

Herein, what is the mind? That which is mind, intellect, consciousness…pe… the mind-consciousness-element born of that—this is called “mind.” From this doubt he cleanses this mind, purifies it, and completely purifies it; he releases it, sets it free, and completely sets it free. Therefore, it is said: “he purifies his mind of doubt.”

561. “Ime[T 0.0346] pañca nīvaraṇe pahāyā”ti ime pañca nīvaraṇā santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāyā”ti.

561. “Having abandoned these five hindrances”: These five hindrances are calmed, quelled, pacified, set, gone to rest, given up, relinquished, dried up, completely dried up, and made an end of. Therefore, it is said: “having abandoned these five hindrances.”

562. “Cetaso upakkilese”ti ime pañca nīvaraṇā cittassa upakkilesā.

562. “Defilements of the mind”: These five hindrances are defilements of the mind.

563. “Paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe”ti imehi pañcahi nīvaraṇehi anuppannā ceva paññā na uppajjati uppannā ca paññā nirujjhati. Tena vuccati “paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe”ti.

563. “Weakeners of wisdom”: Because of these five hindrances, unarisen wisdom does not arise, and arisen wisdom ceases. Therefore, it is said: “weakeners of wisdom.”

564. “Vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehī”ti tattha katame kāmā? Chando kāmo, rāgo kāmo, chandarāgo kāmo, saṅkappo kāmo, rāgo kāmo, saṅkapparāgo kāmo – ime vuccanti “kāmā”.

564. “Secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states”: Herein, what are sensual pleasures? Desire is a sensual pleasure, lust is a sensual pleasure, desire and lust are a sensual pleasure; intention is a sensual pleasure, lust is a sensual pleasure, intention and lust are a sensual pleasure—these are called “sensual pleasures.”

Tattha katame akusalā dhammā? Kāmacchando, byāpādo, thinaṃ, middhaṃ, uddhaccaṃ, kukkuccaṃ, vicikicchā – ime vuccanti “akusalā dhammā”. Iti [P 0.0257] imehi ca kāmehi imehi ca akusalehi dhammehi vivitto hoti. Tena vuccati “vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehī”ti.

Herein, what are unwholesome states? Sensual desire, ill will, sloth, torpor, restlessness, remorse, and doubt—these are called “unwholesome states.” Thus, one is secluded from these sensual pleasures and from these unwholesome states. Therefore, it is said: “secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states.”

565. “Savitakkaṃ [V 0.0288] savicāra”nti atthi vitakko, atthi vicāro.

565. “With applied thought and sustained thought”: There is applied thought, and there is sustained thought.

Tattha katamo vitakko? Yo takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “vitakko”.

Herein, what is applied thought? Whatever is reasoning, applied thought, intention, application, complete application, directing of the mind, and right intention—this is called “applied thought.”

Tattha katamo vicāro? Yo cāro vicāro anuvicāro upavicāro cittassa [T 0.0347] anusandhanatā anupekkhanatā – ayaṃ vuccati vicāro. Iti [M 0.0267] iminā ca vitakkena iminā ca vicārena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “savitakkaṃ savicāra”nti.

Herein, what is sustained thought? Whatever is examination, sustained thought, sequential examination, close examination, the mind’s application, and scrutiny—this is called 'sustained thought.' Thus, one is endowed with this applied thought and with this sustained thought... (etc.)... possessed of them. Therefore, it is said: 'accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought'.

566. “Vivekaja”nti vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā – te imasmiṃ viveke jātā honti sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā. Tena vuccati “vivekaja”nti.

566. 'Born of seclusion' means: applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind—these states are born, well-born, produced, newly produced, and manifested in this seclusion. Therefore, it is said: 'born of seclusion'.

567. “Pītisukha”nti atthi pīti, atthi sukhaṃ.

567. 'Having rapture and pleasure' means: there is rapture, and there is pleasure.

Tattha katamā pīti? Yā pīti pāmojjaṃ āmodanā pamodanā hāso pahāso vitti odagyaṃ attamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “pīti”.

Herein, what is rapture? Whatever is rapture, joy, gladness, rejoicing, mirth, exhilaration, delight, elation, and satisfaction of mind—this is called 'rapture'.

Tattha katamaṃ sukhaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “sukhaṃ”. Idaṃ sukhaṃ imāya pītiyā sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “pītisukha”nti.

Herein, what is pleasure? Whatever is mental gratification, mental pleasure, the gratifying and pleasant experience born of mental contact, and the gratifying and pleasant feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'pleasure.' This pleasure is accompanied by this rapture, co-arisen with it, conjoined with it, and associated with it. Therefore, it is said: 'having rapture and pleasure'.

568. “Paṭhama”nti gaṇanānupubbatā gaṇanānupubbato (syā.) evamuparipi paṭhamaṃ. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ samāpajjatīti paṭhamaṃ.

568. 'First' means: it is first in the sequence of counting. Because one attains this first, it is the first.

569. “Jhāna”nti vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā.

569. 'Jhāna' is: applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind.

570. “Upasampajjā”ti yo paṭhamassa jhānassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

570. 'Enters upon' means: the gaining, regaining, reaching, attainment, touching, realization, and acquisition of the first jhāna.

571. “Viharatī”ti [V 0.0289] …pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

571. 'Dwells' means... (etc.)... Therefore, it is said: 'dwells'.

572. “Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā”ti, atthi vitakko, atthi vicāro.

572. 'With the stilling of applied thought and sustained thought' means: there is applied thought, and there is sustained thought.

Tattha [T 0.0348] katamo vitakko? Yo takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “vitakko”.

Herein, what is applied thought? Whatever is thinking, applied thought... (etc.)... right intention—this is called 'applied thought'.

Tattha katamo vicāro? Yo [P 0.0258] cāro vicāro anuvicāro upavicāro cittassa anusandhanatā anupekkhanatā – ayaṃ vuccati “vicāro”. Iti ayañca vitakko ayañca vicāro santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā [M 0.0268] abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā”ti.

Herein, what is sustained thought? Whatever is examination, sustained thought, sequential examination, close examination, the mind’s application, and scrutiny—this is called 'sustained thought.' Thus, this applied thought and this sustained thought are calmed, stilled, quieted, have ceased, have completely ceased, are done away with, are completely done away with, are dried up, are thoroughly dried up, and have been brought to an end. Therefore, it is said: 'with the stilling of applied thought and sustained thought'.

573. “Ajjhatta”nti yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ.

573. 'Internal' means: whatever is internal, personal.

574. “Sampasādana”nti yā saddhā saddahanā okappanā abhippasādo.

574. 'Confidence' means: whatever is faith, the act of believing, commitment, and serene faith.

575. “Cetaso ekodibhāva”nti yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi.

575. 'Unification of mind' means: whatever is the stability of mind... (etc.)... right concentration.

576. “Avitakkaṃ avicāra”nti atthi vitakko, atthi vicāro.

576. 'Without applied thought, without sustained thought' means: there is applied thought, and there is sustained thought.

Tattha katamo vitakko? Yo takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “vitakko”.

Herein, what is applied thought? Whatever is thinking, applied thought... (etc.)... right intention—this is called 'applied thought'.

Tattha katamo vicāro? Yo cāro anucāro vicāro anuvicāro upavicāro cittassa anusandhanatā anupekkhanatā – ayaṃ vuccati “vicāro”. Iti ayañca vitakko ayañca vicāro santā hoti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “avitakkaṃ avicāra”nti.

Herein, what is sustained thought? Whatever is examination, sequential examination, sustained thought, repeated examination, close examination, the mind’s application, and scrutiny—this is called 'sustained thought.' Thus, this applied thought and this sustained thought are calmed, stilled, quieted, have ceased, have completely ceased, are done away with, are completely done away with, are dried up, are thoroughly dried up, and have been brought to an end. Therefore, it is said: 'without applied thought, without sustained thought'.

577. “Samādhija”nti [V 0.0290] sampasādo pītisukhaṃ – te imasmiṃ samādhimhi jātā honti sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā. Tena vuccati “samādhija”nti.

577. 'Born of concentration' means: confidence, rapture, and pleasure. These states are born, well-born, produced, newly produced, and manifested in this concentration. Therefore, it is said: 'born of concentration'.

578. “Pītisukha”nti [T 0.0349] atthi pīti, atthi sukhaṃ.

578. 'Having rapture and pleasure' means: there is rapture, and there is pleasure.

Tattha katamā pīti…pe… ayaṃ vuccati “pīti”.

Herein, what is rapture? ... (etc.) ... This is called 'rapture'.

Tattha katamaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… idaṃ vuccati “sukhaṃ”. Idaṃ sukhaṃ imāya pītiyā sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “pītisukha”nti.

Herein, what is pleasure? ... (etc.) ... This is called 'pleasure.' This pleasure is accompanied by this rapture, co-arisen with it, conjoined with it, and associated with it. Therefore, it is said: 'having rapture and pleasure'.

579. “Dutiya”nti gaṇanānupubbatā dutiyaṃ. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ samāpajjatīti dutiyaṃ.

579. 'Second' means: it is second in the sequence of counting. Because one attains this for the second time, it is the second.

580. “Jhāna”nti sampasādo, pītisukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā.

580. 'Jhāna' is: confidence, rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind.

581. “Upasampajjā”ti [M 0.0269] yo dutiyassa jhānassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

581. 'Enters upon' means: the gaining, regaining, reaching, attainment, touching, realization, and acquisition of the second jhāna.

582. “Viharatī”ti [P 0.0259] …pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

582. 'Dwells' means... (etc.)... Therefore, it is said: 'dwells'.

583. “Pītiyā ca virāgā”ti tattha katamā pīti? Yā pīti pāmojjaṃ āmodanā pamodanā hāso pahāso vitti odagyaṃ attamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “pīti”. Ayaṃ pīti santā hoti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “pītiyā ca virāgā”ti.
