583. 'And with the fading away of rapture' means: Herein, what is rapture? Whatever is rapture, joy, gladness, rejoicing, mirth, exhilaration, delight, elation, and satisfaction of mind—this is called 'rapture.' This rapture is calmed, stilled, quieted, has ceased, has completely ceased, is done away with, is completely done away with, is dried up, is thoroughly dried up, and has been brought to an end. Therefore, it is said: 'and with the fading away of rapture'.

584. “Upekkhako”ti tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”. Imāya upekkhāya upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “upekkhako”ti.

584. 'Equanimous' means: Herein, what is equanimity? Whatever is equanimity, onlooking, close onlooking, and neutrality of mind—this is called 'equanimity.' One is endowed with this equanimity... (etc.)... possessed of it. Therefore, it is said: 'equanimous'.

585. “Viharatī”ti [T 0.0350][V 0.0291] …pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

585. 'Dwells' means... (etc.)... Therefore, it is said: 'dwells'.

586. “Sato ca sampajāno”ti tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”.

586. 'And is mindful and clearly comprehending' means: Herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever is mindfulness, recollection... (etc.)... right mindfulness—this is called 'mindfulness'.

Tattha katamaṃ sampajaññaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “sampajaññaṃ”. Iti imāya ca satiyā iminā ca sampajaññena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato. Tena vuccati “sato ca sampajāno”ti.

Herein, what is clear comprehension? Whatever is wisdom, understanding... (etc.)... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'clear comprehension.' Thus, one is endowed with this mindfulness and this clear comprehension... (etc.)... possessed of them. Therefore, it is said: 'and is mindful and clearly comprehending'.

587. “Sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedetī”ti tattha katamaṃ sukhaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “sukhaṃ”.

587. 'And feels pleasure with the body' means: Herein, what is pleasure? Whatever is mental gratification, mental pleasure, the gratifying and pleasant experience born of mental contact, and the gratifying and pleasant feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'pleasure'.

Tattha katamo kāyo? Saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati “kāyo”. Idaṃ sukhaṃ iminā kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti. Tena vuccati “sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedetī”ti.

Herein, what is the body? The aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—this is called 'the body'. One feels this happiness with this body. Therefore, it is said, 'and feels happiness with the body'.

588. “Yaṃ [M 0.0270] taṃ ariyā ācikkhantī”ti tattha katame ariyā? Ariyā vuccanti buddhā ca buddhasāvakā ca. Te imaṃ ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paññāpenti (sī. syā.) paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttāniṃ karonti pakāsenti. Tena vuccati “yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhantī”ti.

588. “That which the noble ones describe”: Herein, who are the noble ones? The noble ones are said to be the Buddhas and the disciples of the Buddhas. They describe this, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, analyze it, make it plain, and manifest it. Therefore, it is said, 'that which the noble ones describe'.

589. “Upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī”ti tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”.

589. “Equanimous, mindful, a happy dweller”: Herein, what is equanimity? Whatever is equanimity, the state of equanimity, the state of deep equanimity, and neutrality of mind—this is called 'equanimity'.

Tattha [P 0.0260] katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati [T 0.0351] – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”.

Herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever is mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness—this is called 'mindfulness'.

Tattha katamaṃ sukhaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ [V 0.0292] cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “sukhaṃ”. Iti imāya ca upekkhāya imāya ca satiyā iminā ca sukhena samannāgato iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī”ti.

Herein, what is happiness? Whatever is mental pleasure, mental happiness, a pleasant happy feeling born of mental contact, a pleasant happy feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'happiness'. Thus, endowed with this equanimity, this mindfulness, and this happiness, one comports oneself, proceeds, maintains oneself, keeps going, carries on, moves about, and dwells. Therefore, it is said, 'equanimous, mindful, a happy dweller'.

590. “Tatiya”nti gaṇanānupubbatā tatiyaṃ. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ samāpajjatīti tatiyaṃ.

590. “Third”: It is third by way of numerical sequence. One attains this jhāna for the third time; therefore, it is called 'third'.

591. “Jhāna”nti upekkhā, sati, sampajaññaṃ, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā.

591. “Jhāna” is equanimity, mindfulness, clear comprehension, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind.

592. “Upasampajjā”ti yo tatiyassa jhānassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

592. “Enters upon” means the gaining, re-gaining, reaching, attainment, touching, realization, and accomplishment of the third jhāna.

593. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

593. “Dwells”... therefore it is said, “dwells.”

594. “Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā”ti, atthi sukhaṃ, atthi dukkhaṃ.

594. “With the abandoning of pleasure and pain”: There is pleasure, there is pain.

Tattha katamaṃ sukhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ sātaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “sukhaṃ”.

Herein, what is pleasure? Whatever is bodily pleasure, bodily happiness, the pleasant and happy feeling born of bodily contact, a pleasant and happy feeling born of bodily contact—this is called 'pleasure'.

Tattha [M 0.0271] katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhaṃ”. Iti idañca sukhaṃ idañca dukkhaṃ santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā [T 0.0352] appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā”ti.

Herein, what is pain? Whatever is bodily displeasure, bodily pain, the unpleasant and painful feeling born of bodily contact, an unpleasant and painful feeling born of bodily contact—this is called 'pain'. Thus, this pleasure and this pain are calmed, stilled, quieted, have disappeared, have utterly disappeared, are rid of, are completely rid of, are dried up, are thoroughly dried up, and are brought to an end. Therefore it is said, 'with the abandoning of pleasure and pain'.

595. “Pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā”ti atthi somanassaṃ, atthi domanassaṃ.

595. “With the earlier disappearance of joy and sorrow”: There is joy, there is sorrow.

Tattha [V 0.0293] katamaṃ somanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “somanassaṃ”.

Herein, what is joy? Whatever is mental pleasure, mental happiness, the pleasant and happy feeling born of mental contact, a pleasant and happy feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'joy'.

Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati “domanassaṃ”. Iti idañca somanassaṃ idañca domanassaṃ pubbeva santā [P 0.0261] honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā”ti.

Herein, what is sorrow? Whatever is mental displeasure, mental pain, the unpleasant and painful feeling born of mental contact, an unpleasant and painful feeling born of mental contact—this is called 'sorrow'. Thus, this joy and this sorrow have already before been calmed, stilled, quieted, have disappeared, have utterly disappeared, are rid of, are completely rid of, are dried up, are thoroughly dried up, and are brought to an end. Therefore it is said, 'with the earlier disappearance of joy and sorrow'.

596. “Adukkhamasukha”nti yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Tena vuccati “adukkhamasukha”nti.

596. “Neither-painful-nor-pleasant”: This is the mental state that is neither agreeable nor disagreeable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact. Therefore it is called 'neither-painful-nor-pleasant'.

597. “Upekkhāsatipārisuddhi”nti, tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā upekkhā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā majjhattatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”.

597. “Purity of mindfulness due to equanimity”: Herein, what is equanimity? Whatever is equanimity, the state of equanimity, the state of deep equanimity, and neutrality of mind—this is called 'equanimity'.

Tattha katamā sati? Yā sati anussati…pe… sammāsati – ayaṃ vuccati “sati”. Ayaṃ sati imāya upekkhāya vivaṭā hoti parisuddhā pariyodātā. Tena vuccati “upekkhāsatipārisuddhi”nti.

Herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever is mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness—this is called 'mindfulness'. This mindfulness is unobscured, purified, and cleansed by this equanimity. Therefore it is called 'purity of mindfulness due to equanimity'.

598. “Catuttha”nti [T 0.0353] gaṇanānupubbatā catutthaṃ, idaṃ catutthaṃ samāpajjatīti catutthaṃ.

598. “Fourth”: It is the fourth in numerical sequence; one attains this fourth, thus it is called 'fourth'.

599. “Jhāna”nti upekkhā, sati, cittassekaggatā.

599. “Jhāna” is equanimity, mindfulness, and one-pointedness of mind.

600. “Upasampajjā”ti [M 0.0272] yo catutthassa jhānassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

600. “Enters upon” means the gaining, re-gaining, reaching, attainment, touching, realization, and accomplishment of the fourth jhāna.

601. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

601. “Dwells”... therefore it is said, “dwells.”

602. “Sabbaso [V 0.0294] rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā”ti tattha katamā rūpasaññā? Rūpāvacarasamāpattiṃ samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – imā vuccanti “rūpasaññāyo”. Imā rūpasaññāyo atikkanto hoti vītikkanto samatikkanto. Tena vuccati “sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā”ti.

602. “With the complete surmounting of perceptions of form”: Herein, what are perceptions of form? The perception, the act of perceiving, and the state of having perceived of one who has attained a form-sphere attainment, or has been reborn there, or is dwelling happily in the present life—these are called 'perceptions of form'. These perceptions of form one has surmounted, passed beyond, and overcome. Thus it is said: 'with the complete surmounting of perceptions of form'.

603. “Paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā”ti tattha katamā paṭighasaññā? Rūpasaññā saddasaññā…pe… phoṭṭhabbasaññā – imā vuccanti paṭighasaññāyo. Imā paṭighasaññāyo santā honti samitā vūpasantā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā appitā byappitā sositā visositā byantīkatā. Tena vuccati “paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā”ti.

603. “With the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact”: Herein, what are perceptions of sensory impact? Perceptions of form, perceptions of sound... perceptions of tangibles—these are called 'perceptions of sensory impact'. These perceptions of sensory impact are calmed, stilled, quieted, have disappeared, have utterly disappeared, are rid of, are completely rid of, are dried up, are thoroughly dried up, and are brought to an end. Thus it is said: 'with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact'.

604. “Nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā”ti tattha katamā nānattasaññā? Asamāpannassa manodhātu samaṅgissa vā manoviññāṇadhātu [T 0.0354][P 0.0262] samaṅgissa vā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – imā vuccanti “nānattasaññāyo”. Imā nānattasaññāyo na manasi karoti. Tena vuccati “nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā”ti.

604. "By non-attention to perceptions of diversity": Herein, what are perceptions of diversity? The perception, the act of perceiving, and the state of having perceived of one who has not attained absorption but is endowed with the mind-element or the mind-consciousness-element—these are called "perceptions of diversity." One does not attend to these perceptions of diversity. Thus it is said: "by non-attention to perceptions of diversity."

605. “Ananto ākāso”ti, tattha katamo ākāso? Yo ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ catūhi mahābhūtehi – ayaṃ vuccati “ākāso”. Tasmiṃ ākāse cittaṃ ṭhapeti saṇṭhapeti anantaṃ pharati. Tena vuccati “ananto ākāso”ti.

605. "Infinite space": Herein, what is space? That which is space, pertaining to space, the void, pertaining to the void, an aperture, pertaining to an aperture, untouched by the four great elements—this is called "space." In that space one places the mind, establishes it, and pervades it as infinite. Thus it is said: "infinite space."

606. “Ākāsānañcāyatana”nti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā.

606. "The base of the infinity of space": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the base of the infinity of space, or has been reborn there, or is dwelling happily in the present life.

607. “Upasampajjā”ti yo ākāsānañcāyatanassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

607. "Enters upon": this is the gaining, re-gaining, reaching, attainment, touching, realization, and accomplishment of the base of the infinity of space.

608. “Viharatī”ti…pe… [M 0.0273] tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

608. "Dwells": …pe… thus it is said, "dwells."

609. “Sabbaso [V 0.0295] ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkammā”ti imaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ atikkanto hoti vītikkanto samatikkanto. Tena vuccati “sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkammā”ti.

609. "By completely surmounting the base of the infinity of space": this base of the infinity of space one has surmounted, passed beyond, and overcome. Thus it is said: "by completely surmounting the base of the infinity of space."

610. “Anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti taṃyeva ākāsaṃ viññāṇena phuṭṭhaṃ manasi karoti anantaṃ pharati. Tena vuccati “anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti.

610. "Infinite consciousness": one attends to that very space as pervaded by consciousness and pervades it as infinite. Thus it is said: "infinite consciousness."

611. “Viññāṇañcāyatana”nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā.

611. "The base of the infinity of consciousness": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the base of the infinity of consciousness, or has been reborn there, or is dwelling happily in the present life.

612. “Upasampajjā”ti [T 0.0355] yo viññāṇañcāyatanassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

612. "Enters upon": this is the gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and full attainment of the base of the infinity of consciousness.

613. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

613. "Dwells": …pe… thus it is said, "dwells."

614. “Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkammā”ti imaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ atikkanto hoti vītikkanto samatikkanto. Tena vuccati “sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkammā”ti.

614. "By completely surmounting the base of the infinity of consciousness": this base of the infinity of consciousness one has surmounted, passed beyond, and overcome. Thus it is said: "by completely surmounting the base of the infinity of consciousness."

615. “Natthi kiñcī”ti taṃyeva viññāṇaṃ bhāveti vibhāveti antarabhāveti, “natthi kiñcī”ti passati. Tena vuccati “natthi kiñcī”ti.

615. "There is nothing": one develops, develops intensely, and makes that very consciousness disappear; one sees, “There is nothing.” Thus it is said: “There is nothing.”

616. “Ākiñcaññāyatana”nti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā.

616. "The base of nothingness": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the base of nothingness, or has been reborn there, or is dwelling happily in this very life.

617. “Upasampajjā”ti [P 0.0263] yo ākiñcaññāyatanassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

617. "Enters upon": this is the gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and full attainment of the base of nothingness.

618. “Viharatī”ti [V 0.0296] …pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

618. "Dwells": …pe… thus it is said, "dwells."

619. “Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkammā”ti imaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ atikkanto hoti vītikkanto samatikkanto. Tena vuccati “sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkammā”ti.

619. "By completely surmounting the base of nothingness": this base of nothingness one has surmounted, passed beyond, and overcome. Thus it is said: "by completely surmounting the base of nothingness."

“Nevasaññīnāsaññī”ti [M 0.0274] taṃyeva ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ santato manasi karoti saṅkhārāvasesasamāpattiṃ bhāveti. Tena vuccati “nevasaññīnāsaññī”ti ayaṃ pāṭho mātikāyaṃ natthi, niddese pana sabbapotthakesu dissati.

"Neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient": one attends to that very base of nothingness as peaceful and develops the attainment that has formations as a residue. Thus it is said: "neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient."

620. “Nevasaññānāsaññāyatana”nti [T 0.0356] nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa vā upapannassa vā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārissa vā cittacetasikā dhammā.

620. "The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, or has been reborn there, or is dwelling happily in this very life.

621. “Upasampajjā”ti yo nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa lābho paṭilābho patti sampatti phusanā sacchikiriyā upasampadā.

621. "Enters upon": this is the gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and full attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

622. “Viharatī”ti iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

622. "Dwells": one moves, proceeds, maintains oneself, sustains oneself, carries on, comports oneself, dwells. Thus it is said: "dwells."

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Sutta Exposition.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Exposition

1. Rūpāvacarakusalaṃ

1. Fine-Material Sphere Wholesome States

623. Cattāri [V 0.0297] jhānāni – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

623. There are four jhānas: the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna.

624. Tattha katamaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

624. Herein, what is the first jhāna? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, secluded from sensual pleasures …pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has five factors: initial application, sustained application, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'first jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha katamaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ[M 0.0275], tasmiṃ samaye tivaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the second jhāna? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, with the stilling of initial and sustained application …pe… he enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has three factors: rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'second jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha [P 0.0264][T 0.0357] katamaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the third jhāna? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, with the fading away of rapture …pe… he enters and abides in the third jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has two factors: happiness and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'third jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha katamaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “catutthaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the fourth jhāna? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, with the abandoning of happiness …pe… he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fourth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Catukkaṃ.

The Tetrad.

625. Idha [V 0.0298] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

625. Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, secluded from sensual pleasures …pe… he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has five factors: initial application, sustained application, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'first jhāna.' The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi avitakkaṃ vicāramattaṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye caturaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome phenomena, without initial application but with sustained application, born of seclusion, accompanied by rapture and happiness, he enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has four factors: sustained application, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'second jhāna.' The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Idha [T 0.0358] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye tivaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, with the stilling of initial and sustained application …pe… he enters and abides in the third jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has three factors: rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'third jhāna.' The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “catutthaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, with the fading away of rapture …pe… he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has two factors: happiness and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fourth jhāna.' The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Idha [M 0.0276] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, with the abandoning of happiness …pe… he enters and abides in the fifth jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fifth jhāna.' The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Pañcakaṃ.

The Pentad.

2. Arūpāvacarakusalaṃ

2. Wholesome States of the Immaterial Sphere

626. Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti [P 0.0265] sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ [V 0.0299] samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “catutthaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

626. Here, at a time when a bhikkhu is developing the path for rebirth in the formless realm, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna—attained with the abandoning of happiness …pe…—which is accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fourth jhāna.' The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

3. Lokuttarakusalaṃ

3. Supramundane Wholesome States

627. Cattāri [T 0.0359] jhānāni – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

627. The four jhānas—the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, the fourth jhāna.

628. Tattha katamaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

628. Herein, what is the first jhāna? Here, a bhikkhu at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna, which is emancipating and leads to the waning of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, having secluded himself from sensual pleasures… enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is painful practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has five factors: initial application, sustained application, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the “first jhāna.” The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha katamaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye tivaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the second jhāna? Here, a bhikkhu at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna, which is emancipating and leads to the waning of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, with the subsiding of initial application and sustained application… enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which is painful practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has three factors: rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the “second jhāna.” The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha [M 0.0277] katamaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the third jhāna? Here, a bhikkhu at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna, which is emancipating and leads to the waning of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, with the fading away of rapture… enters and dwells in the third jhāna, which is painful practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: happiness and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the “third jhāna.” The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha [T 0.0360] katamaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā sukhassa ca pahānā [V 0.0300] …pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “catutthaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the fourth jhāna? Here, a bhikkhu at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna, which is emancipating and leads to the waning of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage, with the abandoning of happiness… enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is painful practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the “fourth jhāna.” The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Catukkaṃ.

The Tetrad.

629. Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya [P 0.0266] bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

629. Here, a bhikkhu at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which is emancipating and leads to the waning of accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures… enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is painful practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has five factors: initial application, sustained application, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the “first jhāna.” The remaining phenomena are associated with the jhāna.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi avitakkaṃ vicāramattaṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye caturaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti vicāro pīti sukhaṃ cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

In this Dispensation, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out from the round of rebirths and leads to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage—having become quite secluded from sensual pleasures and secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the second jhāna, which is without initial application but with only sustained application, born of seclusion, accompanied by rapture and pleasure, and is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has four factors: sustained application, rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'second jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vitakkavicārānaṃ [T 0.0361] vūpasamā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye tivaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

In this Dispensation, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out from the round of rebirths and leads to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage—with the stilling of initial and sustained application... enters and abides in the third jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has three factors: rapture, pleasure, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'third jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… [M 0.0278] catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “catutthaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

In this Dispensation, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out from the round of rebirths and leads to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage—with the fading away of rapture... enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: pleasure and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fourth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Idha [V 0.0301] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

In this Dispensation, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the supramundane jhāna—which leads out from the round of rebirths and leads to the destruction of rebirth, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first stage—by the abandoning of pleasure... enters and abides in the fifth jhāna, which is of painful practice and slow direct knowledge. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fifth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Pañcakaṃ.

The Pentad.

4. Rūpāvacaravipākā

4. Resultants of the Form Sphere

630. Cattāri jhānāni – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

630. There are four jhānas: the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna.

631. Tattha katamaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja [T 0.0362] viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye [P 0.0267] pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

631. Herein, what is the first jhāna? In this Dispensation, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... enters and abides in the first jhāna based on the earth kasiṇa. At that time there is contact...pe...there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the resultant of that same form-sphere wholesome kamma, because it has been performed and accumulated, quite secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... he enters and abides in the first jhāna based on the earth kasiṇa. At that time, the jhāna has five factors: applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'first jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha katamaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā…pe….

Herein, what is the second jhāna? In this Dispensation, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought...pe... enters and abides in the second jhāna based on the earth kasiṇa. At that time there is contact...pe...there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the resultant of that same form-sphere wholesome kamma, because it has been performed and accumulated, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought...pe... he enters and abides in the second jhāna...pe... the third jhāna...pe... the fourth jhāna...pe... the first jhāna...pe... the fifth jhāna based on the earth kasiṇa. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fifth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna...pe...

5. Arūpāvacaravipākā

5. Resultants of the Formless Sphere

632. Idha [M 0.0279][V 0.0302] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva arūpāvacarassa kusalassa [T 0.0363] kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “catutthaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

632. In this Dispensation, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, with the abandoning of pleasure...pe... enters and abides in the fourth jhāna. At that time, there is contact...pe...there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the resultant of that same formless-sphere wholesome kamma, because it has been performed and accumulated, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, with the abandoning of pleasure...pe... he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called 'the fourth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

6. Lokuttaravipākā

6. Supramundane Resultants

633. Cattāri jhānāni – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

633. There are four jhānas: the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna.

634. Tattha katamaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo [P 0.0268] hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

634. Herein, what is the first jhāna? Here, a bhikkhu, at a time when he is developing the supramundane jhāna that is liberating, leading to the non-accumulation of kamma, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... attains and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice with sluggish direct knowledge. At that time there is contact...pe...there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same supramundane wholesome jhāna, because it has been performed and developed, its resultant is that, quite secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... he attains and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice with sluggish direct knowledge, accompanied by emptiness. At that time, the jhāna has five factors: applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'first jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha katamaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati [T 0.0364] dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa jhānassa [M 0.0280] katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ [V 0.0303] …pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the second jhāna? Here, a bhikkhu, at a time when he is developing the supramundane jhāna that is liberating, leading to the non-accumulation of kamma, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage, with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought...pe... attains and abides in the second jhāna, which is of difficult practice with sluggish direct knowledge. At that time there is contact...pe...there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same supramundane wholesome jhāna, because it has been performed and developed, its resultant is that, with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought...pe... the second jhāna...pe... the third jhāna...pe... the fourth jhāna...pe... the first jhāna...pe... he attains and abides in the fifth jhāna, which is of difficult practice with sluggish direct knowledge, accompanied by emptiness. At that time, the jhāna has two factors: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fifth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

7. Rūpārūpāvacarakiriyā

7. Functional Consciousness of the Form and Formless Spheres

635. Cattāri jhānāni – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

635. There are four jhānas: the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna.

636. Tattha katamaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye pañcaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – vitakko, vicāro, pīti, sukhaṃ, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

636. Herein, what is the first jhāna? Here, at a time when a bhikkhu develops a functional form-sphere jhāna—which is neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, a pleasant abiding in the present life—he, secluded from sensual pleasures …pe… enters and abides in the first jhāna which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time, the jhāna with five factors arises: applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'first jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Tattha katamaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… pañcamaṃ [T 0.0365] jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “pañcamaṃ [P 0.0269] jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttā.

Herein, what is the second jhāna? Here, a bhikkhu, at a time when he develops a functional form-sphere jhāna—which is neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, a pleasant abiding in the present life—with the stilling of applied and sustained thought …pe… the second jhāna …pe… the third jhāna …pe… the fourth jhāna …pe… the first jhāna …pe… enters and abides in the fifth jhāna which has the earth kasiṇa as its object. At that time, the jhāna with two factors arises: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fifth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

637. Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye arūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye duvaṅgikaṃ jhānaṃ hoti – upekkhā, cittassekaggatā. Idaṃ vuccati “catutthaṃ jhānaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā jhānasampayuttāti.

637. Here, a bhikkhu, at a time when he develops a functional formless-sphere jhāna—which is neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, a pleasant abiding in the present life—by completely transcending the base of nothingness, and with the abandoning of happiness …pe… enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. At that time, the jhāna with two factors arises: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called the 'fourth jhāna.' The remaining states are associated with the jhāna.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition is concluded.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Section of Questions

638. Cattāri [M 0.0281][V 0.0304] jhānāni – idha bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – “upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī”ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.

638. There are four jhānas. Here, a bhikkhu, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the first jhāna, which has applied thought and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. …pe… With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied thought and sustained thought, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration. …pe… With the fading away of rapture, he abides equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and he experiences happiness with the body; he enters and abides in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, one abides pleasantly.’ …pe… With the abandoning of happiness and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and displeasure, he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.

639. Catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati [T 0.0366] abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

639. Of the four jhānas, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, how many are indeterminate…pe… how many are with defilements, how many are without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

640. Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Tīṇi jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ ṭhapetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Paṭhamaṃ [P 0.0270] jhānaṃ – etthuppanne vitakkavicāre ṭhapetvā savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ, tīṇi jhānāni avitakkaavicārā. Dve jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā pītisahagatā, tīṇi jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā sukhasahagatā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā upekkhāsahagataṃ. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Tīṇi jhānāni na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā[M 0.0282], siyā na vattabbā appamāṇārammaṇāti; catutthaṃ [V 0.0305] jhānaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ, siyā mahaggatārammaṇaṃ, siyā appamāṇārammaṇaṃ; siyā na vattabbaṃ parittārammaṇantipi, mahaggatārammaṇantipi, appamāṇārammaṇantipi[T 0.0367]. Siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Tīṇi jhānāni na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi; catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā maggārammaṇaṃ, siyā maggahetukaṃ, siyā maggādhipati, siyā na vattabbaṃ maggārammaṇantipi, maggahetukantipi maggādhipatītipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Tīṇi jhānāni na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi; catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā atītārammaṇaṃ, siyā anāgatārammaṇaṃ, siyā paccuppannārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ atītārammaṇantipi, anāgatārammaṇantipi, paccuppannāramaṇantipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Tīṇi jhānāni bahiddhārammaṇā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā ajjhattārammaṇaṃ, siyā bahiddhārammaṇaṃ, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ ajjhattārammaṇantipi, bahiddhārammaṇantipi, ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇantipi. Anidassanaappaṭighā.

640. They may be wholesome or indeterminate. The three jhānas—except for the pleasant feeling arisen therein—are associated with pleasant feeling; the fourth jhāna—except for the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arisen therein—is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be resultants, may be states that produce a result, or may be states that are neither resultants nor produce a result. They may be affected by clinging and objects of clinging, may be unaffected by clinging but objects of clinging, or may be unaffected by clinging and not objects of clinging. They may be undefiled but conducive to defilements, or may be undefiled and not conducive to defilements. The first jhāna—except for the initial and sustained application arisen therein—has initial and sustained application; the three jhānas are without initial and sustained application. Two jhānas—except for the rapture arisen therein—are accompanied by rapture; three jhānas—except for the pleasure arisen therein—are accompanied by pleasure; the fourth jhāna—except for the equanimity arisen therein—is accompanied by equanimity. They are not to be abandoned by seeing nor by developing. They have roots that are not to be abandoned by seeing nor by developing. They may be conducive to accumulation, may be conducive to de-accumulation, or may be conducive to neither accumulation nor de-accumulation. They may be of the trainees, may be of the adepts, or may be of neither trainees nor adepts. They may be exalted or may be immeasurable. Regarding the three jhānas, it cannot be said that they have sense-sphere objects or exalted objects; they may have immeasurable objects, or it cannot be said that they have immeasurable objects. The fourth jhāna may have a sense-sphere object, an exalted object, or an immeasurable object; or it cannot be said that it has a sense-sphere object, an exalted object, or an immeasurable object. They may be medium or may be superior. They may be fixed in rightness or may be unfixed. Regarding the three jhānas, they do not have the path as object; they may have the path as root-condition, may have the path as dominance-condition, or it cannot be said that they have the path as root-condition or as dominance-condition. The fourth jhāna may have the path as object, may have the path as root-condition, may have the path as dominance-condition; or it cannot be said that it has the path as object, as root-condition, or as dominance-condition. They may be arisen, may be unarisen, or may be about to arise. They may be past, may be future, or may be present. Regarding the three jhānas, it cannot be said that they have past objects, future objects, or present objects. The fourth jhāna may have a past object, a future object, or a present object; or it cannot be said that it has a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. The three jhānas have external objects. The fourth jhāna may have an internal object, an external object, or an internal-and-external object; or it cannot be said that it has an internal object, an external object, or an internal-and-external object. They are invisible and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyad

641. Na hetū, sahetukā, hetusampayuttā, na vattabbā “hetū ceva sahetukā cā”ti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū, na vattabbā “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”ti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū, na hetū sahetukā.

641. They are not roots; they are with roots; they are associated with roots. It should not be said that they are 'both roots and with roots.' They are with roots but not roots. It should not be said that they are 'both roots and associated with roots.' They are associated with roots but not roots. They are not roots but are with roots.

Sappaccayā, saṅkhatā, anidassanā, appaṭighā, arūpā[T 0.0368], siyā [P 0.0271] lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā, kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

They have conditions, are conditioned, invisible, non-resistant, formless; they may be worldly, or they may be supramundane; they are knowable by some consciousness, and not knowable by some consciousness.

No āsavā, siyā sāsavā, siyā anāsavā, āsavavippayuttā, na vattabbā “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”ti, siyā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, siyā na vattabbā “sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā”ti. Na vattabbā “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cāti”pi, āsavasampayuttā ceva [M 0.0283] no ca āsavātipi. Siyā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā.

They are not āsavas. They may be objects of the āsavas, or they may not be objects of the āsavas. They are dissociated from the āsavas. It should not be said that they are 'both āsavas and objects of the āsavas.' They may be objects of the āsavas but not āsavas. It may be that it should not be said that they are 'objects of the āsavas but not āsavas.' It should not be said that they are 'both āsavas and associated with the āsavas,' nor that they are 'associated with the āsavas but not āsavas.' They may be dissociated from the āsavas and be objects of the āsavas; they may be dissociated from the āsavas and not be objects of the āsavas.

No [V 0.0306] saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā, no cittā, cetasikā, cittasampayuttā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhā, cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittasahabhuno, cittānuparivattino, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino, bāhirā, no upādā, siyā upādinnā, siyā anupādinnā.

They are not fetters… not bonds… not floods… not yokes… not hindrances… not graspings… They have an object, are not mind, are mental factors, associated with mind, conjoined with mind, arisen from mind, co-arisen with mind, following after mind, conjoined with mind and arisen from mind, conjoined with mind and arisen from mind and co-arisen with mind, conjoined with mind and arisen from mind and following after mind, external, not derived matter; they may be grasped, or they may be ungrasped.

No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbā, na dassanena pahātabbahetukā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ vitakkaṃ ṭhapetvā savitakkaṃ, tīṇi jhānāni avitakkā. Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ vicāraṃ ṭhapetvā savicāraṃ, tīṇi jhānāni avicārā. Dve jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā [T 0.0369] sappītikā, dve jhānāni appītikā. Dve jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ pītiṃ ṭhapetvā pītisahagatā, dve jhānāni na pītisahagatā. Tīṇi jhānāni – etthuppannaṃ sukhaṃ ṭhapetvā sukhasahagatā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ na sukhasahagataṃ. Catutthaṃ jhānaṃ – etthuppannaṃ upekkhaṃ ṭhapetvā upekkhāsahagataṃ, tīṇi jhānāni upekkhāsahagatā, na kāmāvacarā, siyā rūpāvacarā, siyā na rūpāvacarā, tīṇi jhānāni na arūpāvacarā, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ siyā arūpāvacaraṃ, siyā na arūpāvacaraṃ, siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā, siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā, siyā niyatā, siyā aniyatā, siyā sauttarā, siyā anuttarā, araṇāti.

They are not clingings...pe... not defilements...pe... not to be abandoned by seeing, not to be abandoned by development, not having a cause to be abandoned by seeing, not having a cause to be abandoned by development. The first jhāna—except for the initial thought that has arisen therein, is with initial thought; the three jhānas are without initial thought. The first jhāna—except for the sustained thought that has arisen therein, is with sustained thought; the three jhānas are without sustained thought. Two jhānas—except for the rapture that has arisen therein, are with rapture; two jhānas are without rapture. Two jhānas—except for the rapture that has arisen therein, are accompanied by rapture; two jhānas are not accompanied by rapture. Three jhānas—except for the happiness that has arisen therein, are accompanied by happiness; the fourth jhāna is not accompanied by happiness. The fourth jhāna—except for the equanimity that has arisen therein, is accompanied by equanimity; three jhānas are not accompanied by equanimity. They are not of the sense-sphere; they may be of the form-sphere, or they may not be of the form-sphere. Three jhānas are not of the formless-sphere; the fourth jhāna may be of the formless-sphere, or it may not be of the formless-sphere. They may be included, or they may be unincluded. They may be leading outwards, or they may not be leading outwards. They may be definite, or they may be indefinite. They may be surpassable, or they may be unsurpassed. They are without defilements.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Section of Questions.

Jhānavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Exposition of Jhāna is finished.

13. Appamaññāvibhaṅgo

13. The Exposition of the Immeasurables

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. Discourse Analysis

642. Catasso [M 0.0284][P 0.0272][V 0.0307] appamaññāyo – idha bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ catutthiṃ (sī.). Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena abyāpajjhena (sī. syā.) pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā vipulena [T 0.0370] mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Muditāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ muditāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

642. The four immeasurables—here a monk dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and for all as for himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and for all as for himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and for all as for himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and for all as for himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will.

1. Mettā

1. Loving-kindness

643. Kathañca bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati? Seyyathāpi nāma ekaṃ puggalaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ disvā mettāyeyya, evameva sabbe satte mettāya pharati.

643. And how does a monk dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness? Just as, upon seeing a dear and agreeable person, one would feel loving-kindness, in the same way, he pervades all beings with loving-kindness.

Tattha [V 0.0308] katamā mettā? Yā sattesu metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”.

Herein, what is loving-kindness? Whatever loving-kindness, act of loving-kindness, state of loving-kindness, and liberation of mind that is loving-kindness there is towards beings—this is called 'loving-kindness'.

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu [P 0.0273] – idaṃ [M 0.0285] vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya mettāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “mettāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality, intellect, heart, the luminous, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the consciousness aggregate, the corresponding mind-consciousness-element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this loving-kindness, co-nascent with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore, it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness'.

644. “Ekaṃ disa”nti puratthimaṃ vā disaṃ pacchimaṃ vā disaṃ uttaraṃ vā disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ vā disaṃ uddhaṃ vā adho vā tiriyaṃ vā vidisaṃ vā.

644. 'One direction' means the eastern direction, or the western direction, or the northern direction, or the southern direction, or the upward direction, or the downward direction, or a transverse direction, or an intermediate direction.

645. “Pharitvā”ti [T 0.0371] pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

645. 'Having pervaded' means having resolved upon.

646. “Viharatī”ti iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

646. 'He dwells' means he comports himself, proceeds, maintains, sustains, keeps going, conducts himself, and dwells. Therefore, it is said: 'he dwells'.

647. “Tathā dutiya”nti yatheva ekaṃ disaṃ tathā dutiyaṃ disaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ disaṃ tathā catutthaṃ disaṃ tathā uddhaṃ tathā adho tathā tiriyaṃ tathā vidisaṃ.

647. 'Likewise the second' means: just as with one direction, so with the second direction, so with the third direction, so with the fourth direction; so above, so below, so across, so with the intermediate directions.

648. “Sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ. Pariyādāyavacanametaṃ – “sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti.

648. 'Everywhere, for all beings as for oneself, the entire world' means all with all, all in every way, completely, without remainder. This is a term of complete inclusion: 'everywhere, for all beings as for oneself, the entire world'.

649. “Mettāsahagatena cetasā”ti tattha katamā mettā? Yā sattesu metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”.

649. 'With a mind accompanied by loving-kindness': Herein, what is loving-kindness? Whatever loving-kindness, act of loving-kindness, state of loving-kindness, and liberation of mind that is loving-kindness there is towards beings—this is called 'loving-kindness'.

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya mettāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “mettāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality...pe... the corresponding mind-consciousness-element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this loving-kindness, co-nascent with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore, it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness'.

650. “Vipulenā”ti [V 0.0309] yaṃ vipulaṃ taṃ mahaggataṃ, yaṃ mahaggataṃ taṃ appamāṇaṃ, yaṃ appamāṇaṃ so avero, yo avero so abyāpajjo abyāpajjho (sī. syā.).

650. 'Vast' means: what is vast is exalted; what is exalted is immeasurable; what is immeasurable is without enmity; what is without enmity is without affliction.

651. “Pharitvā”ti pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

651. 'Having pervaded' means having resolved upon.

652. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

652. 'He dwells' ...pe... Therefore, it is said: 'he dwells'.

2. Karuṇā

2. Compassion

653. Kathañca [M 0.0286] bhikkhu karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati? Seyyathāpi nāma ekaṃ puggalaṃ duggataṃ durūpetaṃ disvā karuṇāyeyya, evameva sabbe satte karuṇāya pharati.

653. And how does a monk dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion? Just as one would feel compassion on seeing an afflicted and miserable person, so one pervades all beings with compassion.

Tattha katamā karuṇā? Yā sattesu karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”.

Herein, what is compassion? Whatever compassion there is for beings, the act of being compassionate, the state of being compassionate, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion'.

Tattha katamaṃ [T 0.0372] cittaṃ? Yaṃ [P 0.0274] cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya karuṇāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “karuṇāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality... the corresponding mind-consciousness element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this compassion, co-nascent with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by compassion'.

654. “Ekaṃ disa”nti puratthimaṃ vā disaṃ pacchimaṃ vā disaṃ uttaraṃ vā disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ vā disaṃ uddhaṃ vā adho vā tiriyaṃ vā vidisaṃ vā.

654. 'One direction' means the eastern direction, or the western direction, or the northern direction, or the southern direction, or the upward direction, or the downward direction, or a transverse direction, or an intermediate direction.

655. “Pharitvā”ti pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

655. 'Having pervaded' means having pervaded and having resolved upon.

656. “Viharatī”ti iriyati vattati pāleti yapeti yāpeti carati viharati. Tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

656. 'Dwells' means comports oneself, proceeds, maintains oneself, sustains oneself, keeps going, conducts oneself, and dwells. Therefore it is said: 'dwells'.

657. “Tathā [V 0.0310] dutiya”nti yatheva ekaṃ disaṃ tathā dutiyaṃ disaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ disaṃ tathā catutthaṃ disaṃ tathā uddhaṃ tathā adho tathā tiriyaṃ tathā vidisaṃ.

657. 'Similarly the second' means: just as one direction, so the second direction, so the third direction, so the fourth direction; so above, so below, so across, so the intermediate direction.

658. “Sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ. Pariyādāyavacanametaṃ – “sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti.

658. 'Everywhere, for all, the entire world' means in every respect, in every way, completely, without remainder. This is a term of complete inclusion: 'everywhere, for all, the entire world'.

659. “Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā”ti tattha katamā karuṇā? Yā sattesu karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”.

659. 'With a mind accompanied by compassion': Herein, what is compassion? Whatever compassion there is for beings, the act of being compassionate, the state of being compassionate, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion'.

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya karuṇāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ [M 0.0287] saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “karuṇāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality... the corresponding mind-consciousness element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this compassion, co-nascent with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by compassion'.

660. “Vipulenā”ti yaṃ vipulaṃ taṃ mahaggataṃ, yaṃ mahaggataṃ taṃ appamāṇaṃ, yaṃ appamāṇaṃ so avero, yo avero so abyāpajjo.

660. 'Vast' means: what is vast is exalted; what is exalted is immeasurable; what is immeasurable is without enmity; what is without enmity is without ill will.

661. “Pharitvā”ti pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

661. 'Having pervaded' means having pervaded and having resolved upon.

662. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati [T 0.0373] “viharatī”ti.

662. 'Dwells' ... Therefore it is said: 'dwells'.

3. Muditā

3. Altruistic Joy

663. Kathañca bhikkhu muditāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati? Seyyathāpi nāma ekaṃ puggalaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ disvā mudito assa, evameva sabbe satte muditāya pharati.

663. And how does a bhikkhu dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by altruistic joy? Just as one would be joyful on seeing a dear and beloved person, so he pervades all beings with altruistic joy.

Tattha katamā muditā? Yā sattesu muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”.

Herein, what is altruistic joy? Whatever altruistic joy there is for beings, the act of rejoicing, the state of being joyful, the liberation of mind that is altruistic joy—this is called 'altruistic joy'.

Tattha [P 0.0275][V 0.0311] katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya muditāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “muditāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality... the corresponding mind-consciousness element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this altruistic joy, co-nascent with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by altruistic joy'.

664. “Ekaṃ disa”nti puratthimaṃ vā disaṃ pacchimaṃ vā disaṃ uttaraṃ vā disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ vā disaṃ uddhaṃ vā adho vā tiriyaṃ vā vidisaṃ vā.

664. 'One direction' means the eastern direction, or the western direction, or the northern direction, or the southern direction, or the upward direction, or the downward direction, or a transverse direction, or an intermediate direction.

665. “Pharitvā”ti pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

665. 'Having pervaded' means having pervaded and having resolved upon.

666. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

666. 'Dwells' ... Therefore it is said: 'dwells'.

667. “Tathā dutiya”nti yatheva ekaṃ disaṃ tathā dutiyaṃ disaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ disaṃ tathā catutthaṃ disaṃ tathā uddhaṃ tathā adho tathā tiriyaṃ tathā vidisaṃ.

667. 'Similarly the second' means: just as one direction, so the second direction, so the third direction, so the fourth direction; so above, so below, so across, so the intermediate direction.

668. “Sabbadhi [M 0.0288] sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ. Pariyādāyavacanametaṃ – “sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti.

668. 'Everywhere, for all, the entire world' means in every respect, in every way, completely, without remainder. This is a term of complete inclusion: 'everywhere, for all, the entire world'.

669. “Muditāsahagatena cetasā”ti tattha katamā muditā? Yā sattesu muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”.

669. 'With a mind accompanied by altruistic joy': Herein, what is altruistic joy? Whatever altruistic joy there is for beings, the act of rejoicing, the state of being joyful, the liberation of mind that is altruistic joy—this is called 'altruistic joy'.

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ [T 0.0374] vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya muditāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “muditāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality... the corresponding mind-consciousness element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this altruistic joy, co-nascent with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by altruistic joy'.

670. “Vipulenā”ti yaṃ vipulaṃ taṃ mahaggataṃ, yaṃ mahaggataṃ taṃ appamāṇaṃ, yaṃ appamāṇaṃ so avero, yo avero so abyāpajjo.

670. 'Vast': what is vast is exalted; what is exalted is immeasurable; what is immeasurable is without enmity; what is without enmity is without ill will.

671. “Pharitvā”ti pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

671. 'Having pervaded' means having pervaded and having resolved upon.

672. “Viharatī”ti [V 0.0312] …pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

672. 'Dwells' ... Therefore it is said: 'dwells'.

4. Upekkhā

4. Equanimity

673. Kathañca bhikkhu upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati? Seyyathāpi nāma ekaṃ puggalaṃ neva manāpaṃ na amanāpaṃ disvā upekkhako assa, evameva sabbe satte upekkhāya pharati.

673. And how does a bhikkhu dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity? Just as one would be equanimous on seeing a person who is neither agreeable nor disagreeable, so he pervades all beings with equanimity.

Tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā [P 0.0276] sattesu upekkhā upekkhāyanā upekkhāyitattaṃ upekkhācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”.

Herein, what is equanimity? Whatever equanimity there is for beings, the act of being equanimous, the state of being equanimous, the liberation of mind that is equanimity—this is called 'equanimity'.

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya upekkhāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “upekkhāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality... the corresponding mind-consciousness element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this equanimity, co-nascent with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by equanimity'.

674. “Ekaṃ disa”nti puratthimaṃ vā disaṃ pacchimaṃ vā disaṃ uttaraṃ vā disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ vā disaṃ uddhaṃ vā adho vā tiriyaṃ vā vidisaṃ vā.

674. 'One direction' means the eastern direction, or the western direction, or the northern direction, or the southern direction, or the upward direction, or the downward direction, or a transverse direction, or an intermediate direction.

675. “Pharitvā”ti [M 0.0289] pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

675. 'Having pervaded' means having pervaded and having resolved upon.

676. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

676. 'Dwells' ... Therefore it is said: 'dwells'.

677. “Tathā dutiya”nti yatheva ekaṃ disaṃ tathā dutiyaṃ disaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ disaṃ tathā catutthaṃ disaṃ tathā uddhaṃ tathā adho tathā tiriyaṃ tathā vidisaṃ.

677. 'Similarly the second' means: just as one direction, so the second direction, so the third direction, so the fourth direction; so above, so below, so across, so the intermediate direction.

678. “Sabbadhi sabbattatāya [T 0.0375] sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ asesaṃ nissesaṃ. Pariyādāyavacanametaṃ – “sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ loka”nti.

678. 'Everywhere, identifying with all, the entire world' means all with all, in every way all, without remainder, completely. This is a term of complete inclusion: 'everywhere, identifying with all, the entire world.'

679. “Upekkhāsahagatena [V 0.0313] cetasā”ti, tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā sattesu upekkhā upekkhāyanā upekkhāyitattaṃ upekkhācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”.

679. 'With a mind accompanied by equanimity': Herein, what is equanimity? Whatever equanimity, manner of being equanimous, state of being equanimous, liberation of mind that is equanimity, there is in regard to beings—this is called 'equanimity'.

Tattha katamaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “cittaṃ”. Idaṃ cittaṃ imāya upekkhāya sahagataṃ hoti sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ. Tena vuccati “upekkhāsahagatena cetasā”ti.

Herein, what is mind? Whatever is mind, mentality, heart…pe… the corresponding mind-consciousness element—this is called 'mind.' This mind is accompanied by this equanimity, co-nascent, blended, and associated with it. Therefore it is said: 'with a mind accompanied by equanimity.'

680. “Vipulenā”ti yaṃ vipulaṃ taṃ mahaggataṃ, yaṃ mahaggataṃ taṃ appamāṇaṃ, yaṃ appamāṇaṃ so avero, yo avero so abyāpajjo.

680. 'Vast': what is vast is exalted; what is exalted is immeasurable; what is immeasurable is without enmity; what is without enmity is without ill will.

681. “Pharitvā”ti pharitvā adhimuccitvā.

681. 'Having pervaded': having pervaded, having resolved upon.

682. “Viharatī”ti…pe… tena vuccati “viharatī”ti.

682. 'He dwells': …pe… therefore it is said, 'he dwells.'

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

The Suttanta Exposition is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. The Abhidhamma Exposition.

683. Catasso appamaññāyo – mettā, karuṇā, muditā, upekkhā.

683. The four immeasurables are: loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.

684. Tattha katamā mettā?
