Idha [P 0.0277] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ[M 0.0290], yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

684. Therein, what is loving-kindness? In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and dwells in the first jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, an act of loving-kindness, a state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind that is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

Tattha katamā mettā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ [V 0.0314] vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ [T 0.0376] jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is loving-kindness? In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought…pe… enters and dwells in the second jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, an act of loving-kindness, a state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind that is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

Tattha katamā mettā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is loving-kindness? In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, and with the fading away of rapture…pe… enters and dwells in the third jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, an act of loving-kindness, a state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind that is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

685. Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

685. In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and dwells in the first jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, an act of loving-kindness, a state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind that is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi avitakkaṃ vicāramattaṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which is without applied thought, with sustained thought only, born of seclusion, and has rapture and happiness, accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, an act of loving-kindness, a state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind that is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought…pe… enters and dwells in the third jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, an act of loving-kindness, a state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind that is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā [T 0.0377] ca virāgā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye [M 0.0291] metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, and with the fading away of rapture…pe… enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, an act of loving-kindness, a state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind that is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

686. Tattha [P 0.0278][V 0.0315] katamā karuṇā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

686. Therein, what is compassion? In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and dwells in the first jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, an act of compassion, a state of compassion, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

Tattha katamā karuṇā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is compassion? In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought…pe… enters and dwells in the second jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, an act of compassion, a state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

Tattha katamā karuṇā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is compassion? In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, and with the fading away of rapture…pe… enters and dwells in the third jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, an act of compassion, a state of compassion, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

687. Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti [T 0.0378] – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

687. In this Dispensation, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures…pe… enters and dwells in the first jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, an act of compassion, a state of compassion, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi avitakkaṃ vicāramattaṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which is without applied thought, with sustained thought only, born of seclusion, and has rapture and happiness, accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, an act of compassion, a state of compassion, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ [M 0.0292] samaye karuṇā [V 0.0316] karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... etc... enters and dwells in the third jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, an act of compassion, a state of compassion, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā [P 0.0279] karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

Here, a monk, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, and with the fading away of rapture... etc... enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, an act of compassion, a state of compassion, the liberation of mind that is compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

688. Tattha katamā muditā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

688. Therein, what is sympathetic joy? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, secluded from sensual pleasures... etc... having entered, abides in the first jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of sympathetic joy, the state of sympathetic joy, the liberation of mind which is sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

Tattha katamā muditā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ [T 0.0379] jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyatanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is sympathetic joy? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... etc... having entered, abides in the second jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of sympathetic joy, the state of sympathetic joy, the liberation of mind which is sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

Tattha katamā muditā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is sympathetic joy? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, and with the fading away of rapture... etc... having entered, abides in the third jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of sympathetic joy, the state of sympathetic joy, the liberation of mind which is sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

689. Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

689. Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, secluded from sensual pleasures... etc... having entered, abides in the first jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of sympathetic joy, the state of sympathetic joy, the liberation of mind which is sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

Idha [V 0.0317] bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi avitakkaṃ vicāramattaṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ [M 0.0293] dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, having entered, abides in the second jhāna—which is without applied thought, with only sustained thought, born of seclusion, with rapture and happiness—accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of sympathetic joy, the state of sympathetic joy, the liberation of mind which is sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... etc... having entered, abides in the third jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of sympathetic joy, the state of sympathetic joy, the liberation of mind which is sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti pītiyā [T 0.0380] ca virāgā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, and with the fading away of rapture... etc... having entered, abides in the fourth jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of sympathetic joy, the state of sympathetic joy, the liberation of mind which is sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

690. Tattha katamā upekkhā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati upekkhāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye upekkhā upekkhāyanā upekkhāyitattaṃ upekkhācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”. Avasesā dhammā upekkhāya sampayuttā.

690. Therein, what is equanimity? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the abandoning of pleasure... etc... having entered, abides in the fourth jhāna accompanied by equanimity. Whatever at that time is equanimity, the manner of being equanimous, the state of being equanimous, the liberation of mind which is equanimity—this is called 'equanimity.' The remaining states are associated with equanimity.

691. Catasso appamaññāyo – mettā, karuṇā, muditā, upekkhā.

691. The four immeasurables are: loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.

692. Tattha katamā mettā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

692. Therein, what is loving-kindness? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, secluded from sensual pleasures... etc... having entered, abides in the first jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. At that time there is contact... etc... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome form-sphere kamma that has been performed and accumulated, secluded from sensual pleasures... etc... he, having entered, abides in the resultant first jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, the manner of loving-kindness, the state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind which is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

Tattha [V 0.0318] katamā mettā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ [P 0.0280] upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ[T 0.0381], tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā [M 0.0294] upacitattā vipākaṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

Herein, what is loving-kindness? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought...pe... having entered, dwells in the second jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. At that time there is contact...pe... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome form-sphere kamma that has been performed and accumulated, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought...pe... the resultant second jhāna...pe... the third jhāna...pe... the first jhāna...pe... the second jhāna...pe... the third jhāna...pe... having entered, he dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, the manner of loving-kindness, the state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind which is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

693. Tattha katamā karuṇā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

693. Herein, what is compassion? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... having entered, dwells in the first jhāna accompanied by compassion. At that time there is contact...pe... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome form-sphere kamma that has been performed and accumulated, secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... having entered, he dwells in the resultant first jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, the manner of compassion, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind which is compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

Tattha katamā karuṇā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ [T 0.0382] jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati karuṇāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “karuṇā”. Avasesā dhammā karuṇāya sampayuttā.

Herein, what is compassion? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the subsiding of initial and sustained thought… having entered, he dwells in the second jhāna accompanied by compassion. At that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome form-sphere kamma that has been performed and accumulated, with the subsiding of initial and sustained thought… the resultant second jhāna… the third jhāna… the first jhāna… the second jhāna… the third jhāna… having entered, he dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by compassion. Whatever at that time is compassion, the manner of compassion, the state of compassion, liberation of mind by compassion—this is called 'compassion.' The remaining states are associated with compassion.

694. Tattha [P 0.0281] katamā muditā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa [V 0.0319] kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

694. Herein, what is sympathetic joy? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… having entered, he dwells in the first jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. At that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome form-sphere kamma that has been performed and accumulated, secluded from sensual pleasures… having entered, he dwells in the resultant first jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of rejoicing, the state of rejoicing, liberation of mind by sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

Tattha [M 0.0295] katamā muditā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati muditāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye muditā muditāyanā muditāyitattaṃ muditācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “muditā”. Avasesā dhammā muditāya sampayuttā.

Herein, what is sympathetic joy? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the subsiding of initial and sustained thought… having entered, he dwells in the second jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. At that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome form-sphere kamma that has been performed and accumulated, with the subsiding of initial and sustained thought… the resultant second jhāna… the third jhāna… the first jhāna… the second jhāna… the third jhāna… having entered, he dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by sympathetic joy. Whatever at that time is sympathetic joy, the manner of rejoicing, the state of rejoicing, liberation of mind by sympathetic joy—this is called 'sympathetic joy.' The remaining states are associated with sympathetic joy.

695. Tattha [T 0.0383] katamā upekkhā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati upekkhāsahagataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati upekkhāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye upekkhā upekkhāyanā upekkhāyitattaṃ upekkhācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”. Avasesā dhammā upekkhāya sampayuttā.

695. Herein, what is equanimity? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the abandoning of pleasure… having entered, he dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by equanimity. At that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome form-sphere kamma that has been performed and accumulated, with the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain… having entered, he dwells in the resultant fourth jhāna accompanied by equanimity. Whatever at that time is equanimity, the manner of equanimity, the state of equanimity, the liberation of mind which is equanimity—this is called 'equanimity.' The remaining states are associated with equanimity.

696. Catasso appamaññāyo – mettā, karuṇā, muditā, upekkhā.

696. There are four immeasurables: loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.

697. Tattha [V 0.0320] katamā mettā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā [P 0.0282] tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

697. Herein, what is loving-kindness? Here, a bhikkhu, at the time when he develops a form-sphere jhāna that is functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, for a pleasant abiding in the here-and-now—secluded from sensual pleasures… having entered, he dwells in the first jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, the manner of loving-kindness, the state of loving-kindness, the liberation of mind which is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

Tattha katamā mettā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati mettāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti [T 0.0384] – ayaṃ vuccati “mettā”. Avasesā dhammā mettāya sampayuttā.

Herein, what is loving-kindness? Here, a bhikkhu, at a time when he develops a form-sphere jhāna that is functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, for a pleasant abiding in the here-and-now—with the subsiding of initial and sustained thought… the second jhāna… the third jhāna… the first jhāna… the second jhāna… the third jhāna… he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by loving-kindness. Whatever at that time is loving-kindness, the manner of loving, the state of loving, the liberation of mind which is loving-kindness—this is called 'loving-kindness.' The remaining states are associated with loving-kindness.

698. Tattha [M 0.0296] katamā karuṇā…pe… tattha katamā muditā…pe… tattha katamā upekkhā? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati upekkhāsahagataṃ, yā tasmiṃ samaye upekkhā upekkhāyanā upekkhāyitattaṃ upekkhācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati “upekkhā”. Avasesā dhammā upekkhāya sampayuttā.

698. Herein, what is compassion?… Herein, what is sympathetic joy?… Herein, what is equanimity? Here, a bhikkhu, at a time when he develops a form-sphere jhāna that is functional—neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of kamma, for a pleasant abiding in the here-and-now—with the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain… he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna accompanied by equanimity. Whatever at that time is equanimity, the manner of being equanimous, the state of being equanimous, the liberation of mind which is equanimity—this is called 'equanimity.' The remaining states are associated with equanimity.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Exposition.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Questioning

699. Catasso appamaññāyo – idha bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā [V 0.0321] vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; muditāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ muditāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena [T 0.0385] appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

699. Four are the immeasurables. Here, a bhikkhu dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all beings as for oneself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all beings as for oneself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all beings as for oneself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all beings as for oneself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, without ill will.

700. Catunnaṃ appamaññānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

700. Of the four immeasurables, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate?… How many are with defilements, how many without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

701. Siyā [M 0.0297][P 0.0283] kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Tisso appamaññāyo sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, upekkhā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā. Asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā; upekkhā avitakkaavicārā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, na upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā pītisahagatāti; upekkhā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Siyā ācayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino, nevasekkhanāsekkhā, mahaggatā, na vattabbā parittārammaṇātipi, mahaggatārammaṇātipi, appamāṇārammaṇātipi. Majjhimā, aniyatā, na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi[T 0.0386], maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā, bahiddhārammaṇā, anidassanaappaṭighā.

701. They may be wholesome or indeterminate. The three immeasurables are associated with pleasant feeling; equanimity is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be resultant, may be states that are causes of result, or may be neither resultant nor causes of result. They may be grasped by kamma and are objects of clinging, or not grasped by kamma but are objects of clinging. They are undefiled but are objects for defilements. The three immeasurables may be accompanied by applied and sustained thought, may be with sustained thought only, or may be without applied and sustained thought; equanimity is without applied and sustained thought. The three immeasurables may be accompanied by joy or by happiness, but not by equanimity, and sometimes they are not to be described as accompanied by joy; equanimity is accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development. They do not have roots to be abandoned either by vision or by development. They may be conducive to accumulation or conducive to neither accumulation nor decline. They are neither for trainees nor for non-trainees. They are sublime. It is not to be said that they have limited objects, or sublime objects, or immeasurable objects. They are intermediate; undetermined. It is not to be said that they have the path as object, or the path as cause, or the path as a dominant factor. They may be arisen, unarisen, or arising. They may be past, future, or present. It is not to be said that they have past objects, or future objects, or present objects. They may be internal, external, or internal-and-external; they have external objects; they are invisible and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Pairs

702. Mettā hetu, tisso appamaññāyo na hetū, sahetukā, hetusampayuttā. Mettā hetu [V 0.0322] ceva sahetukā ca; tisso appamaññāyo na vattabbā hetū ceva sahetukā cāti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū. Mettā hetu ceva hetusampayuttā ca; tisso appamaññāyo na vattabbā hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cāti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū. Tisso appamaññāyo na hetū sahetukā; mettā na vattabbā na hetu sahetukātipi, na hetu ahetukātipi.

702. Loving-kindness is a root; the three immeasurables are not roots. They are with a root, associated with a root. Loving-kindness is both a root and with a root. Regarding the three immeasurables, it should not be said that they are 'both a root and with a root'; they are with a root, but not a root. Loving-kindness is both a root and associated with a root. Regarding the three immeasurables, it should not be said that they are 'both a root and associated with a root'; they are associated with a root, but not a root. The three immeasurables are not a root, but are with a root. Regarding loving-kindness, it should not be said that it is 'not a root but with a root,' nor that it is 'not a root and rootless'.

Sappaccayā, saṅkhatā, anidassanā, appaṭighā, arūpā, lokiyā, kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā, no āsavā, sāsavā, āsavavippayuttā[M 0.0298], na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cāti, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, na vattabbā āsavā [P 0.0284] ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Āsavavippayuttā sāsavā.

They are with conditions, conditioned, invisible, non-impinging, formless, worldly, knowable by some consciousness and not knowable by some consciousness. They are not taints, but are objects for the taints; they are dissociated from the taints. It should not be said that they are 'both taints and objects for the taints'; they are objects for the taints, but not taints. It should not be said that they are 'both taints and associated with the taints,' nor that they are 'associated with the taints, but not taints.' They are dissociated from the taints, but are objects for the taints.

No saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā [T 0.0387] …pe… sārammaṇā, no cittā, cetasikā, cittasampayuttā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhā, cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittasahabhuno, cittānuparivattino, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino, bāhirā, no upādā, siyā upādinnā, siyā anupādinnā.

They are not fetters... etc... not bonds... etc... not floods... etc... not yokes... etc... not hindrances... etc... not misapprehensions... etc. They have an object, are not consciousness, are mental concomitants, associated with consciousness, conjoined with consciousness, originated from consciousness, co-arisen with consciousness, following in sequence with consciousness, conjoined with and originated from consciousness, conjoined with, originated from, and co-arisen with consciousness, conjoined with, originated from, and following in sequence with consciousness. They are external. They are not derived matter. In some cases, they are kammically produced; in some cases, they are not kammically produced.

No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbā, na dassanena pahātabbahetukā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā; upekkhā avitakkā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā; upekkhā avicārā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā; upekkhā appītikā. Tisso appamaññāyo siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā; upekkhā na pītisahagatā. Tisso appamaññāyo sukhasahagatā, upekkhā na sukhasahagatā. Upekkhā upekkhāsahagatā, tisso appamaññāyo na upekkhāsahagatā, na kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, na arūpāvacarā, pariyāpannā, aniyyānikā, aniyatā, sauttarā, araṇāti.

They are not clingings... etc... not defilements... etc. They are not to be abandoned by vision, nor to be abandoned by development; they do not have a root to be abandoned by vision, nor a root to be abandoned by development. The three immeasurables are in some cases with initial application, in some cases without initial application; equanimity is without initial application. The three immeasurables are in some cases with sustained application, in some cases without sustained application; equanimity is without sustained application. The three immeasurables are in some cases with rapture, in some cases without rapture; equanimity is without rapture. The three immeasurables are in some cases accompanied by rapture, in some cases not accompanied by rapture; equanimity is not accompanied by rapture. The three immeasurables are accompanied by pleasure; equanimity is not accompanied by pleasure. Equanimity is accompanied by equanimity; the three immeasurables are not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense-sphere, they belong to the fine-material sphere, they do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are mundane, not leading to emancipation, unfixed, surpassable, and without conflict.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Interrogation.

Appamaññāvibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Exposition of the Immeasurables is concluded.

14. Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgo

14. Analysis of the Training Rules

1. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Abhidhamma Analysis

703 . Pañca [T 0.0388][M 0.0299][P 0.0285][V 0.0323] sikkhāpadāni – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ.

1. 703. There are five training rules: the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life, the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct, the training rule of abstaining from false speech, and the training rule of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a cause for heedlessness.

704. Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye pāṇātipātā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who is abstaining from the destruction of life, that which at that time is refraining, restraint, repeated abstinence, abstention, non-action, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and the destruction of the causeway regarding the destruction of life—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life.' The remaining states are associated with the abstention.

Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā.

704. Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who is abstaining from the destruction of life, that which at that time is volition, thorough volition, and the state of having willed—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life.' The remaining states are associated with the volition.

Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yo tasmiṃ samaye [V 0.0324] phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”[T 0.0389].

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who is abstaining from the destruction of life, that which at that time is contact… and so on… exertion, and non-distraction—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life.'

Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… [P 0.0286] somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye pāṇātipātā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto [M 0.0300] – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen—accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and prompted… and so on… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge… and so on… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, and prompted… and so on… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge… and so on… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, and prompted… and so on… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge… and so on… or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and prompted—for one who is abstaining from the destruction of life, that which at that time is refraining, restraint, repeated abstinence, abstention, non-action, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and the destruction of the causeway regarding the destruction of life—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life.' The remaining states are associated with the abstention.

705. Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and prompted, for one who is abstaining from the destruction of life, that which at that time is volition, thorough volition, and the state of having willed—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life.' The remaining states are associated with the volition.

Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena pāṇātipātā viramantassa phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”.

705. Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and prompted, for one who is abstaining from the destruction of life, that which at that time is contact… and so on… exertion, and non-distraction—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life.'

706. Tattha katamaṃ adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ…pe… kāmesumicchācārā [T 0.0390] veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ…pe… musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ…pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given?… and so on… What is the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct?… and so on… What is the training rule of abstaining from false speech?… and so on… What is the training rule of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a cause for heedlessness? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who is abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a cause for heedlessness, that which at that time is refraining, restraint, repeated abstinence, abstention, non-action, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and the destruction of the causeway regarding distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a cause for heedlessness—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a cause for heedlessness.' The remaining states are associated with the abstention.

Tattha [V 0.0325] katamaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who is abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness, whatever volition, complete volition, state of having intended there is at that time—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness.' The remaining states are associated with volition.

Tattha katamaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti [P 0.0287] somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yo tasmiṃ samaye phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who is abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness, whatever contact... and so on... exertion, non-distraction there is at that time—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness.'

Tattha [M 0.0301] katamaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ [T 0.0391] ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with prompting... and so on... accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge... and so on... accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with prompting... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting, for one who is abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness, whatever at that time is the abstaining, refraining, repeated refraining, avoidance, non-action, non-performance, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the destroying of the cause—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness.' The remaining states are associated with abstinence.

707. Tattha katamaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā.

707. Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with prompting, for one who is abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness, whatever volition, complete volition, state of having intended there is at that time—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness.' The remaining states are associated with volition.

Tattha katamaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa[V 0.0326], yo tasmiṃ samaye phasso…pe… [P 0.0288] paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with prompting, for one who is abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness, whatever contact... and so on... exertion, non-distraction there is at that time—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness.'

708. Pañca sikkhāpadāni – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ[T 0.0392], musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ.

708. The five training rules: the training rule of abstaining from taking life, the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct, the training rule of abstaining from false speech, and the training rule of abstaining from intoxicants, liquors and spirits, which are a basis for heedlessness.

709. Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ [M 0.0302] hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye pāṇātipātā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā.

709. Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from taking life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge—inferior... medium... superior... with zeal as its dominant factor... with energy as its dominant factor... with consciousness as its dominant factor... with investigation as its dominant factor... with zeal as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior... with energy as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior... with consciousness as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior... with investigation as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior—for one who is abstaining from taking life, whatever at that time is the abstaining, refraining, repeated refraining, avoidance, non-action, non-performance, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, the destroying of the cause—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from taking life.' The remaining states are associated with abstinence.

Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye cetanā sañcetanā sañcetayitattaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā.

Therein, what is the training rule of abstaining from taking life? At a time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, inferior... medium... superior... with zeal as its dominant factor... with energy as its dominant factor... with consciousness as its dominant factor... with investigation as its dominant factor... with zeal as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior... with energy as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior... with consciousness as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior... with investigation as its dominant factor, inferior... medium... superior—for one who is abstaining from taking life, whatever volition, complete volition, state of having intended there is at that time—this is called 'the training rule of abstaining from taking life.' The remaining states are associated with volition.

Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ [T 0.0393][P 0.0289] samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ [V 0.0327] … paṇītaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yo tasmiṃ samaye phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”.

Herein, what is the training precept of abstaining from destroying life? At the time when a wholesome sense-sphere mind arises for one who abstains from destroying life—accompanied by gladness, associated with knowledge, which is inferior... medium... superior... having desire as the dominant factor... having energy as the dominant factor... having mind as the dominant factor... having investigation as the dominant factor... having desire as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having energy as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having mind as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having investigation as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior—at that time there is contact... and so on... exertion, non-distraction. This is called 'the training precept of abstaining from destroying life.'

Tattha katamaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ pāṇātipātā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ [M 0.0303] samaye pāṇātipātā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā…pe… phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo [T 0.0394] – idaṃ vuccati “pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”.

Herein, what is the training precept of abstaining from destroying life? At the time when a wholesome sense-sphere mind arises for one who abstains from destroying life—accompanied by gladness, associated with knowledge, prompted... and so on... accompanied by gladness, dissociated from knowledge... and so on... accompanied by gladness, dissociated from knowledge, prompted... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, prompted... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, prompted, which is inferior... medium... superior... having desire as the dominant factor... having energy as the dominant factor... having mind as the dominant factor... having desire as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having energy as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having mind as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior—whatever at that time is the verbal abstention from destroying life, the mental abstention, repeated abstention, abstention, non-performance, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, and destruction of the cause—this is called 'the training precept of abstaining from destroying life.' The remaining states are associated with abstention... and so on... the remaining states are associated with volition... and so on... contact... and so on... exertion, non-distraction. This is called 'the training precept of abstaining from destroying life.'

710. Tattha katamaṃ adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ…pe… kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ…pe… musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ…pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ [P 0.0290]… cittādhipateyyaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo setughāto – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā [V 0.0328] …pe… avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā…pe… phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”.

710. Herein, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking what is not given?... and so on... what is the training precept of abstaining from sexual misconduct?... and so on... what is the training precept of abstaining from false speech?... and so on... what is the training precept of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness? At the time when a wholesome sense-sphere mind arises for one who abstains from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness—accompanied by gladness, associated with knowledge, which is inferior... medium... superior... having desire as the dominant factor... having energy as the dominant factor... having mind as the dominant factor... having investigation as the dominant factor... having desire as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having energy as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having mind as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having investigation as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior—whatever at that time is the verbal abstention, mental abstention, repeated abstention, abstention, non-performance, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, and destruction of the cause—this is called 'the training precept of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness.' The remaining states are associated with abstention... and so on... the remaining states are associated with volition... and so on... contact... and so on... exertion, non-distraction. This is called 'the training precept of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness.'

711. Tattha katamaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacare kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ [T 0.0395] ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ… chandādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… vīriyādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ… paṇītaṃ… cittādhipateyyaṃ hīnaṃ… majjhimaṃ paṇītaṃ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā viramantassa, yā tasmiṃ samaye surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī akiriyā akaraṇaṃ anajjhāpatti velāanatikkamo [M 0.0304] setughāto – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”. Avasesā dhammā veramaṇiyā sampayuttā…pe… avasesā dhammā cetanāya sampayuttā…pe… phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo – idaṃ vuccati “surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ”.

711. Herein, what is the training precept of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness? At the time when a wholesome sense-sphere mind arises for one who abstains from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness—accompanied by gladness, associated with knowledge, prompted... and so on... accompanied by gladness, dissociated from knowledge... and so on... accompanied by gladness, dissociated from knowledge, prompted... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, prompted... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge... and so on... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, prompted, which is inferior... medium... superior... having desire as the dominant factor... having energy as the dominant factor... having mind as the dominant factor... having desire as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having energy as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior... having mind as the dominant factor, which is inferior... medium... superior—whatever at that time is the verbal abstention, mental abstention, repeated abstention, abstention, non-performance, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the boundary, and destruction of the cause—this is called 'the training precept of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness.' The remaining states are associated with abstention... and so on... the remaining states are associated with volition... and so on... contact... and so on... exertion, non-distraction. This is called 'the training precept of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are a basis for heedlessness.'

712. Katame dhammā sikkhā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā sikkhā.

712. Which states are 'training'? At the time when a wholesome sense-sphere mind arises, accompanied by gladness, associated with knowledge, having a form as its object... and so on... or a dhamma-object as its object, or whatever it takes as its object; at that time there is contact... and so on... there is non-distraction. These states are 'training'.

Katame [P 0.0291] dhammā sikkhā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ [T 0.0396] ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā sikkhā.

Which states are 'training'? At the time when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness arises, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, prompted… and so on… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge… and so on… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, prompted… and so on… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge… and so on… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, prompted… and so on… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge… and so on… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, prompted, having a form as its object… and so on… or a mind-object as its object, or whatever it takes as its object; at that time there is contact… and so on… there is non-distraction. These states are 'training'.

713. Katame [V 0.0329] dhammā sikkhā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti…pe… arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti…pe… lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā sikkhā.

713. What are the states of training? At the time when one develops the path for arising in the form realm... and so on... or develops the path for arising in the formless realm... and so on... or develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to waning, for the abandoning of wrong views, for the attainment of the first stage—quite secluded from sensual pleasures... and so on... enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is painful practice with slow direct knowledge—at that time there is contact... and so on... there is non-distraction. These are the states of training.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Analysis is concluded.

2. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

2. The Chapter on Questions

714. Pañca sikkhāpadāni – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ.

714. The five training rules: the training rule of abstaining from destroying life, the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct, the training rule of abstaining from false speech, and the training rule of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness.

715. Pañcannaṃ [M 0.0305] sikkhāpadānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

715. Of the five training rules, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate… and so on… how many are with conflict, how many without conflict?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

716. Kusalāyeva. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, vipākadhammadhammā, anupādinnupādāniyā, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, savitakkasavicārā, siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā.

716. They are exclusively wholesome. They may be associated with pleasant feeling or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are states that are conditions for resultant states. They are not appropriated by clinging and are fuel for clinging. They are undefiled but are subject to defilement. They are with applied thought and sustained thought. They may be accompanied by rapture, or by happiness, or by equanimity.

Neva dassanena na [T 0.0397] bhāvanāya pahātabbā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, ācayagāmino[P 0.0292], nevasekkhanāsekkhā, parittā, parittārammaṇā, majjhimā, aniyatā, na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinotipi. Siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā[V 0.0330], na vattabbā uppādinoti, siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā, paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā, bahiddhārammaṇā, anidassanaappaṭighā.

They are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation; they do not have roots to be abandoned by vision or by cultivation. They lead to accumulation. They are neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training. They are limited. They have limited objects. They are medium. They are indefinite. It cannot be said that they have the path as object, or have the path as cause, or have the path as their predominant condition. They may have arisen, or they may not have arisen. It cannot be said that they are arising. They may be past, future, or present. They have present objects. They may be internal, external, or both internal and external. They have external objects. They are non-manifestative and non-resistant.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

717. Na hetū sahetukā, hetusampayuttā. Na vattabbā “hetū ceva sahetukā cā”ti, sahetukā ceva na ca hetū, na vattabbā “hetū ceva hetusampayuttā cā”ti, hetusampayuttā ceva na ca hetū, na hetu sahetūkā, sappaccayā, saṅkhatā, anidassanā, appaṭighā, arūpā, lokiyā, kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

717. They are not roots but are with roots; they are associated with roots. It should not be said that they are 'both roots and with roots'; they are with roots but are not roots. It should not be said that they are 'both roots and associated with roots'; they are associated with roots but are not roots. They are not roots but are with roots; they are with a condition; they are conditioned; they are non-manifestative; they are non-resistant; they are formless; they are worldly; they are cognizable by some consciousness, not cognizable by some consciousness.

No āsavā, sāsavā, āsavavippayuttā, na vattabbā “āsavā ceva sāsavā cā”ti, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā, na vattabbā “āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cā”tipi, “āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavā”tipi. Āsavavippayuttā sāsavā, no saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā, no cittā, cetasikā, cittasampayuttā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhā[M 0.0306], cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittasahabhuno, cittānuparivattino, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino[T 0.0398], bāhirā, no upādā, anupādinnā, no upādānā…pe… no kilesā.

They are not taints, but are subject to taints; they are dissociated from taints. It should not be said that they are 'both taints and subject to taints'; they are subject to taints but are not taints. It should not be said either that they are 'both taints and associated with taints' or that they are 'associated with taints but are not taints.' They are dissociated from taints but are subject to taints. They are not fetters… and so on… not bodily knots… and so on… not floods… and so on… not yokes… and so on… not hindrances… and so on… not misapprehensions… and so on… They have an object. They are not consciousness, but are mental factors, associated with consciousness, conjoined with consciousness, originated from consciousness, coexistent with consciousness, consequential to consciousness, originated from what is conjoined with consciousness, coexistent with what is originated from what is conjoined with consciousness, consequential to what is originated from what is conjoined with consciousness. They are external. They are not derived matter, they are not appropriated by clinging. They are not clingings… and so on… not defilements.

Na dassanena pahātabbā, na bhāvanāyapahātabbā, na dassanena pahātabbahetukā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, savitakkā, savicārā, siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā, siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā, kāmāvacarā, na rūpāvacarā, na arūpāvacarā, pariyāpannā, aniyyānikā, aniyatā, sauttarā, araṇāti.

They are not to be abandoned by vision, nor to be abandoned by cultivation; they do not have roots to be abandoned by vision, nor do they have roots to be abandoned by cultivation. They are with applied thought and with sustained thought. They may be with rapture or without rapture; may be accompanied by rapture or not accompanied by rapture; may be accompanied by happiness or not accompanied by happiness; may be accompanied by equanimity or not accompanied by equanimity. They are of the sense sphere, not of the fine-material sphere, not of the immaterial sphere. They are included, non-liberating, unfixed, surpassable, and without conflict.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Chapter on Questions is concluded.

Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Training Rules is concluded.

15. Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅgo

15. The Analysis of the Analytical Knowledges

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. Sutta-Based Analysis

1. Saṅgahavāro

1. The Compilation Chapter

718. Catasso [M 0.0307][P 0.0293][V 0.0331] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā paṭibhāṇapaṭisambhidā (syā.) evamuparipi. Atthe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, dhamme ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ saṅgahavāro.

718. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Knowledge of the result is the analytical knowledge of result; knowledge of the cause is the analytical knowledge of cause; knowledge of the language in which that Dhamma is expressed is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

2. Saccavāro

2. The Chapter on the Truths

719. Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā[T 0.0399], dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ saccavāro.

719. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Knowledge of suffering is the analytical knowledge of result; knowledge of the origin of suffering is the analytical knowledge of cause; knowledge of the cessation of suffering is the analytical knowledge of result; knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge of the language in which that Dhamma is expressed is the analytical knowledge of language. Knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

3. Hetuvāro

3. The Section on Cause
