720. Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Hetumhi ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, hetuphale ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe [V 0.0332] ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ hetuvāro.

720. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Knowledge of the cause is the analytical knowledge of cause; knowledge of the result of the cause is the analytical knowledge of result; knowledge of the linguistic expression for that Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit. This is the Section on Cause.

4. Dhammavāro

4. The Section on Phenomena

721. Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ye dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā, imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā; yamhā dhammā te dhammā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā, tesu [M 0.0308] dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā; tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā; ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ dhammavāro.

721. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Knowledge about those phenomena that have been born, come to be, originated, arisen, produced, and appeared: this is the analytical knowledge of result. Knowledge about the phenomena from which those phenomena have been born, come to be, originated, arisen, produced, and appeared: this is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge of the linguistic expression for those phenomena is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit. This is the Section on Phenomena.

5. Paṭiccasamuppādavāro

5. The Section on Dependent Origination

722. Catasso [P 0.0294] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, jarāmaraṇasamudaye ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, jarāmaraṇanirodhe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

722. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Knowledge of aging-and-death is the analytical knowledge of result; knowledge of the origin of aging-and-death is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge of the cessation of aging-and-death is the analytical knowledge of result; knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of aging-and-death is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge of the linguistic expression for those phenomena is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

723. Catasso [T 0.0400] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Jātiyā ñāṇaṃ…pe… bhave ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādāne ñāṇaṃ…pe… taṇhāya ñāṇaṃ…pe… vedanāya ñāṇaṃ…pe… phasse ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatane ñāṇaṃ…pe… nāmarūpe ñāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇe ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, saṅkhārasamudaye ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, saṅkhāranirodhe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ paṭiccasamuppādavāro.

723. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Knowledge of birth… of existence… of clinging… of craving… of feeling… of contact… of the six sense bases… of name-and-form… of consciousness… of volitional formations is the analytical knowledge of result. Knowledge of the origin of volitional formations is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge of the cessation of volitional formations is the analytical knowledge of result. Knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of volitional formations is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge of the linguistic expression for those phenomena is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit. This is the Section on Dependent Origination.

6. Pariyattivāro

6. The Section on Study

724. Catasso [V 0.0333] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

724. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Tattha katamā dhammapaṭisambhidā? Idha bhikkhu dhammaṃ jānāti – suttaṃ geyyaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ gāthaṃ udānaṃ itivuttakaṃ jātakaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ vedallaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati “dhammapaṭisambhidā”. So tassa tasseva bhāsitassa atthaṃ jānāti – “ayaṃ imassa bhāsitassa attho, ayaṃ imassa bhāsitassa attho”ti. Ayaṃ vuccati “atthapaṭisambhidā”. Tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Ayaṃ pariyattivāro.

Herein, what is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma? Here, a bhikkhu knows the Dhamma: discourses, mixed prose and verse, expositions, verses, inspired utterances, sayings, birth stories, marvelous phenomena, and catechisms. This is called the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma. He knows the meaning of each particular statement: 'This is the meaning of this statement; this is the meaning of that statement.' This is called the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge of the linguistic expression for that Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language. Knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit. This is the Section on Study.

Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.

Analysis According to the Suttas.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

2. Analysis According to the Abhidhamma

1. Kusalavāro

1. The Section on the Wholesome

725. Catasso [M 0.0309] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

725. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ [T 0.0401] samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha[P 0.0295], tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti, ime dhammā kusalā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā. Tesaṃ vipāke ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni [V 0.0334] ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are wholesome? At the time when a wholesome consciousness of the sense-sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, having a visible form as its object… or… a mental phenomenon as its object, or whatever object it has taken; at that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge in their result is the analytical knowledge of result. By whichever language those states are designated, knowledge in that linguistic expression is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—‘these knowledges illuminate this meaning’—the knowledge in the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

726. Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

726. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ ñāṇavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā. Tesaṃ vipāke ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena [T 0.0402] ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are wholesome? At the time when a wholesome consciousness of the sense-sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with prompting… or accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge… or accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting… or accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge… or accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with prompting… or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge… or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting, having a visible form as its object… or… a mental phenomenon as its object, or whatever object it has taken; at that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of cause. Knowledge in their result is the analytical knowledge of result. By whichever language those states are designated, knowledge in that linguistic expression is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—‘these knowledges illuminate this meaning’—the knowledge in the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

727. Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

727. Four are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of result, the analytical knowledge of cause, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame [M 0.0310] dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā. Tesaṃ vipāke ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are wholesome? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and abides in the first jhāna, which has the earth kasiṇa as its object; at that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. The knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma. The knowledge in their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. By whichever language those states are designated, the knowledge in that expression of the language of the Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—‘these knowledges illuminate this meaning’—the knowledge in the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

728. Catasso [P 0.0296][V 0.0335] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

728. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā. Tesaṃ vipāke ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni [T 0.0403] jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are wholesome? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, with the abandoning of pleasure… one enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which is accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; at that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. The knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma. The knowledge in their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. By whichever language those states are designated, the knowledge in that expression of the language of the Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—‘these knowledges illuminate this meaning’—the knowledge in the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

729. Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

729. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā. Tesaṃ vipāke ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena [T 0.0404] ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are wholesome? At the time when one develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to non-accumulation, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first plane, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge; at that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. The knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma. The knowledge in their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. By whichever language those states are designated, the knowledge in that expression of the language of the Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—‘these knowledges illuminate this meaning’—the knowledge in the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

2. Akusalavāro

2. The Section on the Unwholesome

730. Catasso [M 0.0311] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

730. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatasampayuttaṃ [V 0.0336] rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā akusalā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā. Tesaṃ vipāke ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are unwholesome? At the time when an unwholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with wrong view, having a form as its object… or a mental phenomenon as its object, or whatever it may be that it takes as its object, at that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are unwholesome. The knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma. The knowledge in their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. By whichever language those states are designated, the knowledge in that expression of the language of the Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—‘these knowledges illuminate this meaning’—the knowledge in the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

731. Catasso [P 0.0297] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

731. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā akusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ hoti somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatavippayuttaṃ…pe… somanassasahagataṃ diṭṭhigatavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ diṭṭhigatasampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ diṭṭhigatasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ diṭṭhigatavippayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ diṭṭhigatavippayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… domanassasahagataṃ paṭighasampayuttaṃ…pe… domanassasahagataṃ paṭighasampayuttaṃ sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ vicikicchāsampayuttaṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ uddhaccasampayuttaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā…pe… dhammārammaṇaṃ vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā akusalā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā. Tesaṃ vipāke ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are unwholesome? At the time when an unwholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with wrong view, with prompting… accompanied by joy, dissociated from wrong view… accompanied by joy, dissociated from wrong view, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, associated with wrong view… accompanied by equanimity, associated with wrong view, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from wrong view… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from wrong view, with prompting… accompanied by displeasure, associated with aversion… accompanied by displeasure, associated with aversion, with prompting… accompanied by equanimity, associated with doubt… accompanied by equanimity, associated with restlessness, having a form as its object… or a mental phenomenon as its object, or whatever it may be that it takes as its object—at that time there is contact… there is non-distraction. These states are unwholesome. The knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma. The knowledge in their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. By whichever language those states are designated, the knowledge in that expression of the language of the Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—‘these knowledges illuminate this meaning’—the knowledge in the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

3. Vipākavāro

3. The Section on Resultants

732. Tisso [M 0.0312] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā[T 0.0405].

732. Three are the analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame [V 0.0337] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, upekkhā hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, upekkhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are indeterminate? At a time when, because of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere that has been done and accumulated, resultant eye-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a form as its object—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of equanimity, there is the faculty of life, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states there are at that time. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge in the expression of the language by which the designation of those states occurs is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—knowledge in those knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

733. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

733. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ [P 0.0298] saddārammaṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ gandhārammaṇaṃ…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rasārammaṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti sukhasahagataṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, sukhaṃ hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, sukhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti[T 0.0406], ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are indeterminate? At a time when, because of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere that has been done and accumulated, resultant ear-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a sound as its object… or resultant nose-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, with an odor as its object… or resultant tongue-consciousness arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a taste as its object… or resultant body-consciousness arises, accompanied by pleasure, with a tangible object as its object—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is pleasure, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of pleasure, there is the faculty of life, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states there are at that time. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge in the expression of the language by which the designation of those states occurs is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—knowledge in those knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

734. Tisso [M 0.0313] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manodhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, vitakko hoti, vicāro hoti, upekkhā hoti[V 0.0338], cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, upekkhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

734. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Which states are indeterminate? At a time when, because of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere that has been done and accumulated, resultant mind-element arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a form as its object… or with a tangible object as its object, or whatever object it may arise in relation to—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is initial application, there is sustained application, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of equanimity, there is the faculty of life, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states there are at that time. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge in the expression of the language by which the designation of those states occurs is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—knowledge in those knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

735. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

735. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ [T 0.0407] samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, vitakko hoti, vicāro hoti, pīti hoti, sukhaṃ hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, somanassindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā[P 0.0299]. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which states are indeterminate? At a time when, because of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere that has been done and accumulated, resultant mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by joy, with a form as its object… or… with a mental phenomenon as its object, or whatever object it may arise in relation to—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is initial application, there is sustained application, there is joy, there is happiness, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of joy, there is the faculty of life, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states there are at that time. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge in the expression of the language by which the designation of those states occurs is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—knowledge in those knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

736. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

736. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā [M 0.0314] hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, vitakko hoti, vicāro hoti, upekkhā hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, upekkhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana [V 0.0339] tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi [T 0.0408] paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What are the indeterminate states? At a time when, as a result of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere that has been done and accumulated, a resultant mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a form as its object... or... with a mental phenomenon as its object, or whatever it may be that it takes as its object—at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is initial application, there is sustained application, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of equanimity, there is the faculty of life, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states there are at that time. These are the indeterminate states. In these states, the knowledge is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The knowledge, in the verbal expression of the Dhamma's language, of the language by which those states are designated, is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—the knowledge about knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

737. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

737. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What are the indeterminate states? At the time when, as a result of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere that has been performed and accumulated, a resultant mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge... or accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge... or accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge... or accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge, with prompting... or accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge... or accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge, with prompting, having a form as object... or having a mental object as object, or whatever it may take as an object, at that time there is contact... and non-distraction. These are the indeterminate states. In these states, the knowledge is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The knowledge, in the verbal expression of the Dhamma's language, of the language by which those states are designated, is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—the knowledge about knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

738. Tisso [T 0.0409] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

738. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye rūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā[M 0.0315]. Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati pathavīkasiṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti [V 0.0340] tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena [P 0.0300] tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What are the indeterminate states? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and abides in the first jhana with the earth kasiṇa as object—at that time there is contact… and non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome kamma pertaining to the form-sphere, which has been performed and accumulated, its resultant state is: quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and abides in the first jhana with the earth kasiṇa as object—at that time there is contact… and non-distraction. These states are indeterminate. In these states, the knowledge is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The knowledge, in the verbal expression of the Dhamma's language, of the language by which those states are designated, is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—the knowledge about knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

739. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

739. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye arūpūpapattiyā maggaṃ bhāveti sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva arūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ [T 0.0410] samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What are the indeterminate states? At the time when one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, one enters and abides in the fourth jhana—by the abandoning of pleasure…—accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. At that time there is contact… and non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same wholesome kamma pertaining to the formless-sphere, which has been performed and accumulated, its resultant state is: by completely transcending the base of nothingness, one enters and abides in the fourth jhana—by the abandoning of pleasure…—accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. At that time there is contact… and non-distraction. These states are indeterminate. In these states, the knowledge is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The knowledge, in the verbal expression of the Dhamma's language, of the language by which those states are designated, is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—the knowledge about knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

740. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

740. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti niyyānikaṃ apacayagāmiṃ diṭṭhigatānaṃ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā kusalā. Tasseva lokuttarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā bhāvitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati [M 0.0316] dukkhapaṭipadaṃ dandhābhiññaṃ suññataṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni [V 0.0341] ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What states are indeterminate? At the time when one develops the supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction of death and rebirth, for the abandoning of views, for the attainment of the first plane, then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult practice with slow direct knowledge. At that time there is contact… and non-distraction. These states are wholesome. As the result of that same supramundane wholesome kamma having been performed and developed, its resultant state is: quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult practice with slow direct knowledge, and is voidness. At that time there is contact… and non-distraction. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in regard to these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge of the language by which these states are designated is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—this knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

741. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

741. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame [P 0.0301] dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa [T 0.0411] kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ…pe… sotaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ saddārammaṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ gandhārammaṇaṃ…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti upekkhāsahagataṃ rasārammaṇaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti dukkhasahagataṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, dukkhaṃ hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, dukkhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What states are indeterminate? At the time when, as a result of unwholesome kamma that has been performed and accumulated, a resultant eye-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity, with a form as its object… a resultant ear-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity, with a sound as its object… a resultant nose-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity, with an odor as its object… a resultant tongue-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity, with a taste as its object… a resultant body-consciousness arises accompanied by pain, with a tangible object as its object—at that time there is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, pain, one-pointedness of mind, the mind faculty, the pain faculty, the life faculty, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states exist at that time. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in regard to these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge of the language by which these states are designated is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—this knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

742. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

742. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākā manodhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti[T 0.0412], vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, vitakko hoti, vicāro [M 0.0317] hoti, upekkhā hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, upekkhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu [V 0.0342] dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What states are indeterminate? At the time when, as a result of unwholesome kamma that has been performed and accumulated, a resultant mind-element arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a form as object… or a tangible object as object… or a resultant mind-consciousness-element arises, accompanied by equanimity, with a form as object… or a mental object as object, or whatever it may take as object—at that time there is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, applied thought, sustained thought, equanimity, one-pointedness of mind, the mind faculty, the equanimity faculty, the life faculty, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states exist at that time. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in regard to these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge of the language by which these states are designated is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—this knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

4. Kiriyavāro

4. Section on the Functional

743. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

743. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye manodhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā [P 0.0302] vā…pe… phoṭṭhabbārammaṇā vā yaṃ yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, vitakko hoti, vicāro hoti, upekkhā hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, upekkhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā[T 0.0413]. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

What states are indeterminate? At the time when the functional mind-element arises, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor the result of kamma, accompanied by equanimity, with a form as object… or… a tangible object as object… or whatever it takes as an object—at that time there is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, initial application, sustained application, equanimity, one-pointedness of mind, the mind faculty, the faculty of equanimity, the life faculty, and whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states exist at that time. These states are indeterminate. Knowledge in regard to these states is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge of the language by which these states are designated is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—this knowledge about the knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

744. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

744. There are three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā somanassasahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā upekkhāsahagatā rūpārammaṇā vā…pe… dhammārammaṇā vā yaṃ [M 0.0318] yaṃ vā panārabbha, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṃ hoti, vitakko hoti, vicāro hoti, upekkhā hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti, vīriyindriyaṃ hoti[V 0.0343], samādhindriyaṃ hoti, manindriyaṃ hoti, upekkhindriyaṃ hoti, jīvitindriyaṃ hoti, ye vā pana tasmiṃ samaye aññepi atthi paṭiccasamuppannā arūpino dhammā. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when the mind-consciousness element arises as functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor the result of kamma, accompanied by joy, with a form as object… or… with a mental object… or when the mind-consciousness element arises as functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor the result of kamma, accompanied by equanimity, with a form as object… or… with a mental object… or whatever else it may take as object—at that time there is contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, initial application, sustained application, equanimity, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the mind faculty, the faculty of equanimity, the life faculty, and whatever other dependently arisen formless phenomena there are at that time. These phenomena are indeterminate. Knowledge in regard to these phenomena is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge of the expression in language by which those phenomena are designated is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—knowledge about the knowledges, is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

745. Tisso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

745. Three analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

Katame dhammā abyākatā? Yasmiṃ samaye manoviññāṇadhātu [T 0.0414] uppannā hoti kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā…pe… upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena…pe… rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti…pe… arūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti kiriyaṃ neva kusalaṃ nākusalaṃ na ca kammavipākaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ…pe… sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, tasmiṃ samaye phasso hoti…pe… avikkhepo hoti. Ime dhammā abyākatā. Imesu dhammesu ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Yāya niruttiyā [P 0.0303] tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hoti tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā. Yena ñāṇena tāni ñāṇāni jānāti – “imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānī”ti, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

Which phenomena are indeterminate? At the time when the mind-consciousness element arises as functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor the result of kamma, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge…pe… accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, with prompting…pe… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge…pe… accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting…pe… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge…pe… accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with prompting…pe… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge…pe… accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with prompting…pe… or when one develops the form-sphere jhāna…pe… or the formless-sphere jhāna as functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor the result of kamma, for a pleasant abiding in this very life…pe… or having completely transcended the base of nothingness, one enters and dwells in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, accompanied by the perception of that base; or by the abandoning of pleasure…pe… one enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna—at that time there is contact…pe… non-distraction. These phenomena are indeterminate. Knowledge in regard to these phenomena is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge of the expression in language by which those phenomena are designated is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges—'These knowledges illuminate this meaning'—knowledge about the knowledges, is the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

746. Catasso paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Tisso paṭisambhidā kāmāvacarakusalato catūsu [M 0.0319] ñāṇasampayuttesu cittuppādesu, kiriyato catūsu ñāṇasampayuttesu [T 0.0415] cittuppādesu uppajjanti. Atthapaṭisambhidā etesu ceva uppajjati, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu ca uppajjati.

746. Four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit. Three analytical knowledges arise in the four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses associated with knowledge and in the four functional consciousnesses associated with knowledge. The analytical knowledge of meaning arises in these, and it also arises in the four paths and the four fruits.

Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.

The Abhidhamma Analysis.

3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

3. The Questioning Section

747. Catasso [V 0.0344] paṭisambhidā – atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā.

747. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of ready wit.

748. Catunnaṃ paṭisambhidānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?

748. Of the four analytical knowledges, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate… and so on… how many are with defilements, how many without defilements?

1. Tikaṃ

1. The Triads

749. Siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Tisso paṭisambhidā siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Tisso paṭisambhidā anupādinnupādāniyā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Tisso paṭisambhidā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā.

749. They may be wholesome or indeterminate. They may be associated with pleasant feeling or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Three of the analytical knowledges may be resultant-producing dhammas or neither resultant nor resultant-producing dhammas; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be a resultant, a resultant-producing dhamma, or neither a resultant nor a resultant-producing dhamma. Three of the analytical knowledges are not grasped by kamma but are objects of clinging; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be not grasped by kamma but an object of clinging, or not grasped by kamma and not an object of clinging. Three of the analytical knowledges are undefiled and non-defiling; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be undefiled but defiling, or undefiled and non-defiling.

Tisso paṭisambhidā savitakkasavicārā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā.

Three of the analytical knowledges are with applied thought and sustained thought. The analytical knowledge of meaning may be with applied thought and sustained thought, or without applied thought and with only sustained thought, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. They may be accompanied by rapture, or accompanied by happiness, or accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. They do not have a root to be abandoned either by seeing or by development.

Tisso paṭisambhidā siyā ācayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā [P 0.0304] ācayagāminī[T 0.0416], siyā apacayagāminī, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī.

Three of the analytical knowledges may be conducive to accumulation or conducive neither to accumulation nor to decline; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be conducive to accumulation, conducive to decline, or conducive neither to accumulation nor to decline.

Tisso [M 0.0320] paṭisambhidā nevasekkhanāsekkhā, atthapaṭisambhidā siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā[V 0.0345], siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Tisso paṭisambhidā parittā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā parittā, siyā appamāṇā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā parittārammaṇā; tisso paṭisambhidā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā.

Three of the analytical knowledges are neither of a trainee nor of a perfected one; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be of a trainee, of a perfected one, or neither of a trainee nor of a perfected one. Three of the analytical knowledges are limited; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be limited or immeasurable. The analytical knowledge of language has a limited object; three of the analytical knowledges may have a limited object, a lofty object, or an immeasurable object.

Tisso paṭisambhidā majjhimā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Tisso paṭisambhidā aniyatā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā na vattabbā – maggārammaṇātipi, maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinītipi; atthapaṭisambhidā na maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatinī, siyā na vattabbā maggahetukātipi, maggādhipatinītipi; dve paṭisambhidā siyā maggārammaṇā, na maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggārammaṇātipi, maggādhipatinotipi.

Three of the analytical knowledges are medium; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be medium or superior. Three of the analytical knowledges are unfixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed in rightness or unfixed. It should not be said of the analytical knowledge of language that it has the path as its object, or has the path as its cause, or has the path as its predominance. The analytical knowledge of meaning does not have the path as its object; it may have the path as its cause or have the path as its predominance, or it should not be said that it has the path as its cause or has the path as its predominance. Two of the analytical knowledges may have the path as their object but not as their cause; they may have the path as their predominance, or it should not be said that they have the path as their object or have the path as their predominance.

Tisso paṭisambhidā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinoti; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādinī. Siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā paccuppannārammaṇā; dve paṭisambhidā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā[T 0.0417]; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā atītārammaṇā, siyā anāgatārammaṇā, siyā paccuppannārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā atītārammaṇātipi, anāgatārammaṇātipi, paccuppannārammaṇātipi. Siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā bahiddhārammaṇā; tisso paṭisambhidā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā, siyā bahiddhārammaṇā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā. Anidassanaapaṭighā.

Three of the analytical knowledges may be arisen or unarisen; it should not be said that they are arising. The analytical knowledge of meaning may be arisen, unarisen, or arising. They may be past, future, or present. The analytical knowledge of language has a present object. Two of the analytical knowledges may have a past object, a future object, or a present object. The analytical knowledge of meaning may have a past object, a future object, or a present object; or it should not be said that it has a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal, external, or internal-and-external. The analytical knowledge of language has an external object. Three of the analytical knowledges may have an internal object, an external object, or an internal-and-external object. They are invisible and non-impinging.

2. Dukaṃ

2. The Dyads

750. Hetū, sahetukā, hetusampayuttā, hetū ceva sahetukā ca, hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca, na vattabbā na hetū sahetukātipi, nahetūahetukātipi.

750. They are roots, with roots, associated with roots; both roots and with roots, and both roots and associated with roots. It should not be said that they are not roots but are with roots, nor that they are not roots and are without roots.

Sappaccayā[M 0.0321], saṅkhatā, anidassanā, appaṭighā, arūpā, tisso paṭisambhidā lokiyā, atthapaṭisambhidā [V 0.0346] siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā, kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

They are with conditions, conditioned, invisible, non-impinging, and immaterial. Three of the analytical knowledges are mundane. The analytical knowledge of meaning may be mundane or supramundane. They are knowable by some consciousness, not knowable by some consciousness.

No āsavā. Tisso paṭisambhidā sāsavā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā sāsavā, siyā anāsavā. Āsavavippayuttā. Tisso paṭisambhidā [P 0.0305] na vattabbā āsavā ceva sāsavā cāti, sāsavā ceva no ca āsavā; atthapaṭisambhidā na vattabbā āsavo āsavā (sī.) dhātuvibhaṅge pana pāṭhanānattaṃ natthi ceva sāsavā cāti, siyā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavo āsavā (sī.) dhātuvibhaṅge pana pāṭhanānattaṃ natthi, siyā na vattabbā sāsavā ceva no ca āsavāti. Na vattabbā āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā cātipi, āsavasampayuttā ceva no ca āsavātipi. Tisso paṭisambhidā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā, siyā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā.

They are not taints. Three of the analytical knowledges are objects of the taints; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be an object of the taints or not an object of the taints. They are dissociated from taints. It should not be said of the three analytical knowledges that they are both taints and objects of the taints; they are objects of the taints but not taints. Of the analytical knowledge of meaning, it should not be said that it is both a taint and an object of the taints; it may be an object of the taints but not a taint, or it should not be said that it is an object of the taints but not a taint. It should not be said that they are both taints and associated with taints, or that they are associated with taints but not taints. Three of the analytical knowledges are dissociated from taints and are objects of the taints; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be dissociated from taints and an object of the taints, or dissociated from taints and not an object of the taints.

No [T 0.0418] saṃyojanā…pe… no ganthā…pe… no oghā…pe… no yogā…pe… no nīvaraṇā…pe… no parāmāsā…pe… sārammaṇā. No cittā, cetasikā, cittasampayuttā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhā, cittasamuṭṭhānā, cittasahabhuno, cittānuparivattino. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno, cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino, bāhirā, no upādā, anupādinnā.

Not fetters… and so on… not bodily ties… and so on… not floods… and so on… not yokes… and so on… not hindrances… and so on… not misapprehensions… and so on… They have an object. They are not mind; they are mental factors, associated with mind, mixed with mind, originated from mind, co-arisen with mind, and following in sequence with mind. They are mixed with mind and originated from mind; mixed with mind, originated from mind, and co-arisen with mind; mixed with mind, originated from mind, and following in sequence with mind. They are external, not derived, and unappropriated.

No upādānā…pe… no kilesā…pe… na dassanena pahātabbā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Na dassanena pahātabbahetukā. Na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Tisso paṭisambhidā savitakkā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā savitakkā, siyā avitakkā. Tisso paṭisambhidā savicārā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā savicārā, siyā avicārā. Siyā sappītikā, siyā appītikā. Siyā pītisahagatā, siyā na pītisahagatā. Siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā na sukhasahagatā. Siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na upekkhāsahagatā. Tisso paṭisambhidā kāmāvacarā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā kāmāvacarā, siyā na kāmāvacarā. Na rūpāvacarā. Na arūpāvacarā[M 0.0322]. Tisso paṭisambhidā pariyāpannā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā pariyāpannā, siyā apariyāpannā. Tisso paṭisambhidā aniyyānikā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā niyyānikā, siyā aniyyānikā. Tisso paṭisambhidā aniyatā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā niyatā[V 0.0347], siyā aniyatā. Tisso paṭisambhidā sauttarā; atthapaṭisambhidā siyā sauttarā[T 0.0419], siyā anuttarā. Araṇāti.

Not clingings… and so on… not defilements… and so on… Not to be abandoned by seeing. Not to be abandoned by development. Not having a cause to be abandoned by seeing. Not having a cause to be abandoned by development. Three of the analytical knowledges are with applied thought; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with applied thought or without applied thought. Three of the analytical knowledges are with sustained thought; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with sustained thought or without sustained thought. They may be with rapture or without rapture. They may be accompanied by rapture or not accompanied by rapture. They may be accompanied by happiness or not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity or not accompanied by equanimity. Three of the analytical knowledges pertain to the sense sphere; the analytical knowledge of meaning may pertain to the sense sphere or may not. They do not pertain to the form sphere. They do not pertain to the formless sphere. Three of the analytical knowledges are included; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be included or not included. Three of the analytical knowledges are non-leading-out; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be leading-out or non-leading-out. Three of the analytical knowledges are unfixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed or unfixed. Three of the analytical knowledges are surpassable; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be surpassable or unsurpassable. They are without conflict.

Pañhāpucchakaṃ.

The Questioning Section.

Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Analytical Knowledges is finished.

16. Ñāṇavibhaṅgo

16. The Analysis of Knowledge

1. Ekakamātikā

1. The Single Matrix

751. Ekavidhena [M 0.0323][P 0.0306][V 0.0348] ñāṇavatthu – pañca viññāṇā na hetū, ahetukā, hetuvippayuttā, sappaccayā, saṅkhatā, arūpā, lokiyā, sāsavā, saṃyojaniyā, ganthaniyā, oghaniyā, yoganiyā, nīvaraṇiyā, parāmaṭṭhā, upādāniyā, saṃkilesikā, abyākatā, sārammaṇā, acetasikā, vipākā, upādinnupādāniyā, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, na savitakkasavicārā, na avitakkavicāramattā, avitakkaavicārā, na pītisahagatā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino, nevasekkhanāsekkhā[P 0.0307], parittā, kāmāvacarā, na rūpāvacarā, na arūpāvacarā, pariyāpannā, no apariyāpannā, aniyatā, aniyyānikā,

751. In one way, there is the basis of knowledge—the five consciousnesses are not roots, rootless, dissociated from roots, with conditions, conditioned, immaterial, mundane, subject to taints, subject to fetters, subject to ties, subject to floods, subject to yokes, subject to hindrances, misapprehended, subject to clinging, subject to defilement, indeterminate, with an object, not mental factors, resultant, appropriated and subject to clinging, undefiled but subject to defilement, not with applied and sustained thought, not without applied thought but with only sustained thought, without applied and sustained thought, not accompanied by rapture, to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, not having a cause to be abandoned either by seeing or by development, neither leading to accumulation nor to decline, neither of trainees nor of those beyond training, limited, pertaining to the sense sphere, not pertaining to the form sphere, not pertaining to the formless sphere, included, not unincluded, unfixed, not leading out,

Uppannavatthukā uppannārammaṇā,

Having an arisen basis, having an arisen object,

(3) Purejātavatthukā purejātārammaṇā

Having a pre-nascent basis, having a pre-nascent object.

(4) Ajjhattikavatthukā bāhirārammaṇā

Having an internal basis, having an external object.

(5) Asambhinnavatthukā asambhinnārammaṇā

With a distinct basis, with a distinct object,

(6) Nānāvatthukā nānārammaṇā

Having various bases, having various objects,

(7) Na aññamaññassa [T 0.0420] gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti

They do not experience one another's resort and range.

(8) Na asamannāhārā uppajjanti

They do not arise without adverting.

(9) Na [V 0.0349] amanasikārā uppajjanti

They do not arise without attention.

(10) Na abbokiṇṇā uppajjanti

They do not arise intermingled.

(11) Na apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjanti

They do not arise simultaneously.

(12) Na aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjanti

They do not arise in immediate succession to one another.

(13) Pañca viññāṇā anābhogā

The five consciousnesses are without deliberation.

(14) Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci kiñci (sī. ka.) dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti aññatra abhinipātamattā

With the five consciousnesses, one does not cognize any phenomenon except for mere impingement.

(15) Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not cognize any phenomenon.

(16) Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappeti

With the five consciousnesses, one does not adopt any bodily posture.

(17) Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappeti

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not adopt any bodily posture.

(18) Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapeti

With the five consciousnesses, one initiates neither bodily action nor verbal action.

(19) Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapeti

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one initiates neither bodily action nor verbal action.

(20) Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyati

With the five consciousnesses, one does not undertake any wholesome or unwholesome state.

(21) Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyati

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not undertake any wholesome or unwholesome state.

(22) Pañcahi [P 0.0308] viññāṇehi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhāti

With the five consciousnesses, one neither enters into nor emerges from an attainment.

(23) Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhāti

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one neither enters into nor emerges from an attainment.

(24) Pañcahi viññāṇehi na cavati na uppajjati

With the five consciousnesses, one neither passes away nor is reborn.

(25) Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na cavati na uppajjati

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one neither passes away nor is reborn.

(26) Pañcahi viññāṇehi na supati na [M 0.0324] paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passati

With the five consciousnesses, one neither sleeps, nor awakens, nor sees a dream.

(27) Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na supati na paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passati, yāthāvakavatthuvibhāvanā paññā

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one neither sleeps, nor awakens, nor sees a dream; there is wisdom that is the clarification of things as they really are.

Evaṃ ekavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, in one way, is the basis of knowledge.

2. Dukamātikā

2. The Matrix of Dyads

752. Duvidhena [V 0.0350] ñāṇavatthu –

752. The basis of knowledge is twofold:

(1) Lokiyā paññā, lokuttarā paññā

Worldly wisdom, supramundane wisdom.

(2) Kenaci viññeyyā paññā, kenaci na viññeyyā paññā

Wisdom that is knowable by some, wisdom that is not knowable by some.

(3) Sāsavā paññā[T 0.0421], anāsavā paññā

Wisdom subject to the taints, wisdom not subject to the taints.

(4) Āsavavippayuttā sāsavā paññā, āsavavippayuttā anāsavā paññā

Wisdom dissociated from the taints but subject to the taints; wisdom dissociated from the taints and not subject to the taints.

(5) Saṃyojaniyā paññā, asaṃyojaniyā paññā

Wisdom subject to fetters, wisdom not subject to fetters.

(6) Saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā paññā, saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyā paññā

Wisdom dissociated from the fetters but subject to fetters; wisdom dissociated from the fetters and not subject to fetters.

(7) Ganthaniyā paññā, aganthaniyā paññā

Wisdom subject to ties, wisdom not subject to ties.

(8) Ganthavippayuttā ganthaniyā paññā, ganthavippayuttā aganthaniyā paññā

Wisdom dissociated from the ties but subject to ties; wisdom dissociated from the ties and not subject to ties.

(9) Oghaniyā paññā, anoghaniyā paññā

Wisdom subject to the floods, wisdom not subject to the floods.

(10) Oghavippayuttā oghaniyā paññā, oghavippayuttā anoghaniyā paññā

Wisdom dissociated from the floods but subject to the floods; wisdom dissociated from the floods and not subject to the floods.

(11) Yoganiyā paññā, ayoganiyā paññā

Wisdom subject to the yokes, wisdom not subject to the yokes.

(12) Yogavippayuttā yoganiyā paññā, yogavippayuttā ayoganiyā paññā

Wisdom dissociated from the yokes but subject to the yokes; wisdom dissociated from the yokes and not subject to the yokes.

(13) Nīvaraṇiyā paññā, anīvaraṇiyā paññā

Wisdom subject to the hindrances, wisdom not subject to the hindrances.

(14) Nīvaraṇavippayuttā nīvaraṇiyā paññā, nīvaraṇavippayuttā anīvaraṇiyā paññā

Wisdom dissociated from the hindrances but subject to the hindrances; wisdom dissociated from the hindrances and not subject to the hindrances.

(15) Parāmaṭṭhā [P 0.0309] paññā, aparāmaṭṭhā paññā

(15) Wisdom that is wrongly grasped, wisdom that is not wrongly grasped.

(16) Parāmāsavippayuttā parāmaṭṭhā paññā, parāmāsavippayuttā aparāmaṭṭhā paññā

(16) Wisdom dissociated from grasping but wrongly grasped, wisdom dissociated from grasping and not wrongly grasped.

(17) Upādinnā paññā, anupādinnā paññā

(17) Wisdom produced by kamma that is clung to, wisdom not produced by kamma that is clung to.

(18) Upādāniyā paññā, anupādāniyā paññā

(18) Wisdom that is an object of clinging, wisdom that is not an object of clinging.

(19) Upādānavippayuttā [V 0.0351] upādāniyā paññā, upādānavippayuttā anupādāniyā paññā

(19) Wisdom dissociated from clinging but an object of clinging, wisdom dissociated from clinging and not an object of clinging.

(20) Saṃkilesikā paññā, asaṃkilesikā paññā

(20) Wisdom that is an object of defilement, wisdom that is not an object of defilement.

(21) Kilesavippayuttā saṃkilesikā paññā, kilesavippayuttā asaṃkilesikā paññā

(21) Wisdom dissociated from the defilements but an object of defilement, wisdom dissociated from the defilements and not an object of defilement.

(22) Savitakkā paññā, avitakkā paññā

(22) Wisdom with applied thought, wisdom without applied thought.

(23) Savicārā paññā, avicārā paññā

(23) Wisdom with sustained thought, wisdom without sustained thought.

(24) Sappītikā paññā, appītikā paññā

(24) Wisdom with rapture, wisdom without rapture.

(25) Pītisahagatā paññā, na pītisahagatā paññā

(25) Wisdom accompanied by rapture, wisdom not accompanied by rapture.

(26) Sukhasahagatā paññā, na sukhasahagatā paññā

(26) Wisdom accompanied by pleasure, wisdom not accompanied by pleasure.

(27) Upekkhāsahagatā paññā, na upekkhāsahagatā paññā

(27) Wisdom accompanied by equanimity, wisdom not accompanied by equanimity.

(28) Kāmāvacarā paññā[T 0.0422], na kāmāvacarā paññā

(28) Wisdom pertaining to the sense-sphere, wisdom not pertaining to the sense-sphere.

(29) Rūpāvacarā paññā, na rūpāvacarā paññā

(29) Wisdom pertaining to the form-sphere, wisdom not pertaining to the form-sphere.

(30) Arūpāvacarā paññā, na arūpāvacarā paññā

(30) Wisdom pertaining to the formless-sphere, wisdom not pertaining to the formless-sphere.

(31) Pariyāpannā paññā, apariyāpannā paññā

(31) Wisdom that is included, wisdom that is not included.

(32) Niyyānikā paññā, aniyyānikā paññā

(32) Wisdom that leads to deliverance, wisdom that does not lead to deliverance.

(33) Niyatā paññā, aniyatā paññā

(33) Wisdom that is fixed, wisdom that is unfixed.

(34) Sauttarā paññā[M 0.0325], anuttarā paññā

(34) Wisdom that has a superior, wisdom that has no superior.

(35) Atthajāpikā paññā, jāpitatthā paññā

(35) Wisdom that produces a benefit, wisdom that has a produced benefit.

Evaṃ duvidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the grounds of knowledge are twofold.

3. Tikamātikā

3. The Matrix of Triads

753. Tividhena [P 0.0310][V 0.0352] ñāṇavatthu –

753. The grounds of knowledge are threefold:

(1) Cintāmayā paññā, sutamayā paññā, bhāvanāmayā paññā

(1) Wisdom consisting of thinking, wisdom consisting of learning, and wisdom consisting of mental development.

(2) Dānamayā paññā, sīlamayā paññā, bhāvanāmayā paññā

(2) Wisdom consisting of giving, wisdom consisting of virtue, and wisdom consisting of mental development.

(3) Adhisīle paññā, adhicitte paññā, adhipaññāya paññā

(3) Wisdom in higher virtue, wisdom in higher mind, and wisdom in higher wisdom.

(4) Āyakosallaṃ, apāyakosallaṃ, upāyakosallaṃ

(4) Skill in progress, skill in decline, and skill in the means.

(5) Vipākā paññā, vipākadhammadhammā paññā, nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā paññā

(5) Wisdom that is a resultant, wisdom that is result-producing, and wisdom that is neither a resultant nor result-producing.

(6) Upādinnupādāniyā paññā, anupādinnupādāniyā paññā, anupādinnaanupādāniyā paññā

(6) Wisdom that is appropriated and an object of clinging, wisdom that is not appropriated but an object of clinging, and wisdom that is neither appropriated nor an object of clinging.

(7) Savitakkasavicārā paññā, avitakkavicāramattā paññā, avitakkaavicārā paññā

(7) Wisdom with applied thought and sustained thought, wisdom without applied thought but with sustained thought only, and wisdom without applied thought and without sustained thought.

(8) Pītisahagatā paññā, sukhasahagatā paññā, upekkhāsahagatā paññā

(8) Wisdom accompanied by rapture, wisdom accompanied by happiness, and wisdom accompanied by equanimity.

(9) Ācayagāminī paññā, apacayagāminī paññā, nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī paññā

(9) Wisdom that leads to accumulation, wisdom that leads to non-accumulation, and wisdom that leads neither to accumulation nor to non-accumulation.

(10) Sekkhā paññā, asekkhā paññā, nevasekkhanāsekkhā paññā

(10) Wisdom of a trainee, wisdom of an adept, and wisdom that is neither of a trainee nor of an adept.

(11) Parittā paññā, mahaggatā paññā, appamāṇā paññā

(11) Limited wisdom, exalted wisdom, and immeasurable wisdom.

(12) Parittārammaṇā paññā, mahaggatārammaṇā paññā, appamāṇārammaṇā paññā

(12) Wisdom with a limited object, wisdom with an exalted object, and wisdom with an immeasurable object.

(13) Maggārammaṇā paññā, maggahetukā paññā, maggādhipatinī paññā

(13) Wisdom that has the path as its object, wisdom that has the path as its cause, and wisdom that has the path as its dominant factor.

(14) Uppannā paññā[T 0.0423], anuppannā paññā, uppādinī paññā

(14) Arisen wisdom, unarisen wisdom, and wisdom that is to arise.

(15) Atītā [P 0.0311] paññā, anāgatā paññā, paccuppannā paññā

(15) Past wisdom, future wisdom, and present wisdom.

(16) Atītārammaṇā paññā, anāgatārammaṇā paññā, paccuppannārammaṇā paññā

(16) Wisdom with a past object, wisdom with a future object, and wisdom with a present object.

(17) Ajjhattā [V 0.0353] paññā, bahiddhā paññā, ajjhattabahiddhā paññā

Internal wisdom, external wisdom, and internal-and-external wisdom.

(18) Ajjhattārammaṇā paññā, bahiddhārammaṇā paññā, ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā paññā

Wisdom with an internal object, wisdom with an external object, and wisdom with an internal-and-external object.

(19) Savitakkasavicārā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā

Wisdom accompanied by initial and sustained thought exists as resultant, as result-producing, and as neither resultant nor result-producing.

(20) Atthi upādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyā

It exists as appropriated and serving as a basis for clinging, as unappropriated but serving as a basis for clinging, and as unappropriated and not serving as a basis for clinging.

(21) Atthi pītisahagatā, atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi upekkhāsahagatā

It exists as accompanied by rapture, as accompanied by the feeling of happiness, and as accompanied by the feeling of equanimity.

(22) Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī

It exists as leading to the round of rebirth, as leading to Nibbāna, and as leading neither to the round of rebirth nor to Nibbāna.

(23) Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā

It exists as a trainee’s, as an adept’s, and as neither a trainee’s nor an adept’s.

(24) Atthi parittā, atthi mahaggatā, atthi appamāṇā
