It exists as limited, as exalted, and as immeasurable.

(25) Atthi parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā

It exists as having a limited object, as having an exalted object, and as having an immeasurable object.

(26) Atthi maggārammaṇā, atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī

It exists as having the path as its object, as having the path as its cause, and as having the path as its dominant factor.

(27) Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī

It exists as arisen, as unarisen, and as bound to arise.

(28) Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā[M 0.0326], atthi paccuppannā

It exists as past, as future, and as present.

(29) Atthi [P 0.0312] atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā

It exists as having a past object, as having a future object, and as having a present object.

(30) Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā

It exists as internal, as external, and as internal-and-external.

(31) Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā

It exists as having an internal object, as having an external object, and as having an internal-and-external object.

(32) Avitakkavicāramattā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā

Wisdom without initial thought but with sustained thought only exists as resultant, as result-producing, and as neither resultant nor result-producing.

(33) Atthi upādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyā

It exists as appropriated and serving as a basis for clinging, as unappropriated but serving as a basis for clinging, and as unappropriated and not serving as a basis for clinging.

(34) Atthi [V 0.0354] ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī

It exists as leading to the round of rebirth, as leading to Nibbāna, and as leading neither to the round of rebirth nor to Nibbāna.

(35) Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā

It exists as a trainee’s, as an adept’s, and as neither a trainee’s nor an adept’s.

(36) Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī

It exists as arisen, as unarisen, and as bound to arise.

(37) Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā

It exists as past, as future, and as present.

(38) Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā

It exists as internal, as external, and as internal-and-external.

(39) Avitakkaavicārā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā

Wisdom without initial and sustained thought exists as resultant, as result-producing, and as neither resultant nor result-producing.

(40) Atthi upādinnupādāniyā, atthi anuppādinnupādāniyā, atthi anuppādinnaanupādāniyā

It exists as appropriated and serving as a basis for clinging, as unappropriated but serving as a basis for clinging, and as unappropriated and not serving as a basis for clinging.

(41) Atthi pītisahagatā, atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi upekkhāsahagatā

It exists as accompanied by rapture, as accompanied by the feeling of happiness, and as accompanied by the feeling of equanimity.

(42) Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī

It exists as leading to the round of rebirth, as leading to Nibbāna, and as leading neither to the round of rebirth nor to Nibbāna.

(43) Atthi [P 0.0313] sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā

It exists as a trainee’s, as an adept’s, and as neither a trainee’s nor an adept’s.

(44) Atthi parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā

It exists as having a limited object, as having an exalted object, and as having an immeasurable object.

(45) Atthi maggārammaṇā, atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī

It exists as having the path as its object, as having the path as its cause, and as having the path as its dominant factor.

(46) Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī

It exists as arisen, as unarisen, and as bound to arise.

(47) Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā

It exists as past, as future, and as present.

(48) Atthi atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā

It exists as having a past object, as having a future object, and as having a present object.

(49) Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā

It exists as internal, as external, and as internal-and-external.

(50) Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā

It exists as having an internal object, as having an external object, and as having an internal-and-external object.

(51) Pītisahagatā [V 0.0355] paññā sukhasahagatā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā [T 0.0424]

Wisdom accompanied by rapture and wisdom accompanied by pleasant feeling exist as resultant, as result-producing, and as neither resultant nor result-producing.

(52) Atthi [T 0.0425] upādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyā

They exist as appropriated and serving as a basis for clinging, as unappropriated but serving as a basis for clinging, and as unappropriated and not serving as a basis for clinging.

(53) Atthi savitakkasavicārā, atthi avitakkavicāramattā, atthi avitakkaavicārā

They exist as accompanied by initial and sustained thought, as without initial thought but with sustained thought only, and as without initial and sustained thought.

(54) Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī

They exist as leading to the round of rebirth, as leading to Nibbāna, and as leading neither to the round of rebirth nor to Nibbāna.

(55) Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā

They exist as a trainee’s, as an adept’s, and as neither a trainee’s nor an adept’s.

(56) Atthi parittā, atthi mahaggatā, atthi appamāṇā

They exist as limited, as exalted, and as immeasurable.

(57) Atthi [P 0.0314] parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā

There is wisdom with a limited object, there is wisdom with an exalted object, and there is wisdom with an immeasurable object.

(58) Atthi maggārammaṇā[M 0.0327], atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī

There is wisdom with the path as its object, there is wisdom with the path as its cause, and there is wisdom with the path as its dominant factor.

(59) Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī

There is wisdom that has arisen, there is wisdom that has not arisen, and there is wisdom that is bound to arise.

(60) Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā

There is wisdom that is past, there is wisdom that is future, and there is wisdom that is present.

(61) Atthi atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā

There is wisdom with a past object, there is wisdom with a future object, and there is wisdom with a present object.

(62) Atthi ajjhatā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā

There is wisdom that is internal, there is wisdom that is external, and there is wisdom that is both internal and external.

(63) Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā

There is wisdom with an internal object, there is wisdom with an external object, and there is wisdom with an object that is both internal and external.

(64) Upekkhāsahagatā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā

Wisdom accompanied by equanimity exists as a resultant, as a condition for resultants, and as neither a resultant nor a condition for resultants.

(65) Atthi upādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnupādāniyā, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyā

There is wisdom that is appropriated and serves as a basis for clinging, there is wisdom that is unappropriated but serves as a basis for clinging, and there is wisdom that is unappropriated and does not serve as a basis for clinging.

(66) Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī

There is wisdom that leads to accumulation, there is wisdom that leads to dispersal, and there is wisdom that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal.

(67) Atthi [V 0.0356] sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā

There is the wisdom of a trainee, there is the wisdom of an adept, and there is wisdom that is of neither a trainee nor an adept.

(68) Atthi parittā, atthi mahaggatā, atthi appamāṇā

There is wisdom that is limited, there is wisdom that is exalted, and there is wisdom that is immeasurable.

(69) Atthi parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā

There is wisdom with a limited object, there is wisdom with an exalted object, and there is wisdom with an immeasurable object.

(70) Atthi maggārammaṇā, atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī

There is wisdom with the path as its object, there is wisdom with the path as its cause, and there is wisdom with the path as its dominant factor.

(71) Atthi [T 0.0426][P 0.0315] uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī

There is wisdom that has arisen, there is wisdom that has not arisen, and there is wisdom that is bound to arise.

(72) Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā

There is wisdom that is past, there is wisdom that is future, and there is wisdom that is present.

(73) Atthi atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā

There is wisdom with a past object, there is wisdom with a future object, and there is wisdom with a present object.

(74) Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā

There is wisdom that is internal, there is wisdom that is external, and there is wisdom that is both internal and external.

(75) Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā

There is wisdom with an internal object, there is wisdom with an external object, and there is wisdom with an object that is both internal and external.

Evaṃ tividhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the ground of knowledge is threefold.

4. Catukkamātikā

4. The Matrix of Tetrads

754. Catubbidhena ñāṇavatthu –

754. The ground of knowledge is fourfold:

(1) Kammassakatañāṇaṃ, saccānulomikaṃ ñāṇaṃ, maggasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ, phalasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ

(1) Knowledge of kamma as one's own property, knowledge in conformity with the truths, knowledge of one endowed with the path, and knowledge of one endowed with fruition.

(2) Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ

(2) Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, and knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

(3) Kāmāvacarā paññā, rūpāvacarā paññā, arūpāvacarā paññā, apariyāpannā paññā

(3) Sense-sphere wisdom, form-sphere wisdom, formless-sphere wisdom, and unincluded wisdom.

(4) Dhamme ñāṇaṃ, anvaye ñāṇaṃ, pariye paricce (sabbattha) passa dīghanikāye ñāṇaṃ, sammutiñāṇaṃ sammatiñāṇaṃ (syā.) passa dīghanikāye

(4) Knowledge of the text, knowledge of inference, knowledge of analysis, and knowledge of convention.

(5) Atthi [V 0.0357] paññā ācayāya no apacayāya, atthi paññā apacayāya no ācayāya, atthi paññā ācayāya ceva apacayāya ca, atthi paññā nevācayāya no apacayāya

(5) There is wisdom for accumulation and not for dispersal; there is wisdom for dispersal and not for accumulation; there is wisdom for both accumulation and dispersal; and there is wisdom for neither accumulation nor dispersal.

(6) Atthi paññā nibbidāya no paṭivedhāya, atthi paññā paṭivedhāya no nibbidāya, atthi paññā nibbidāya ceva paṭivedhāya ca, atthi paññā neva nibbidāya no paṭivedhāya

(6) There is wisdom for disenchantment and not for penetration; there is wisdom for penetration and not for disenchantment; there is wisdom for both disenchantment and penetration; and there is wisdom for neither disenchantment nor penetration.

(7) Hānabhāginī [P 0.0316] paññā, ṭhitibhāginī paññā, visesabhāginī paññā, nibbedhabhāginī paññā

(7) There is wisdom partaking of decline, wisdom partaking of stability, wisdom partaking of distinction, and wisdom partaking of penetration.

(8) Catasso [M 0.0328] paṭisambhidā

(8) The four analytical knowledges.

(9) Catasso paṭipadā

(9) The four ways of practice.

(10) Cattāri ārammaṇāni

(10) The four objects.

(11) Jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya [T 0.0427] ñāṇaṃ

(11) Knowledge of aging and death, knowledge of the origin of aging and death, knowledge of the cessation of aging and death, and knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of aging and death.

(12-21) Jātiyā ñāṇaṃ…pe… bhave ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādāne ñāṇaṃ…pe… taṇhāya ñāṇaṃ…pe… vedanāya ñāṇaṃ…pe… phasse ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatane ñāṇaṃ…pe… nāmarūpe ñāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇe ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhārasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhe ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Evaṃ catubbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

(12-21) Knowledge of birth… and so on… knowledge of becoming… and so on… knowledge of clinging… and so on… knowledge of craving… and so on… knowledge of feeling… and so on… knowledge of contact… and so on… knowledge of the six sense bases… and so on… knowledge of name-and-form… and so on… knowledge of consciousness… and so on… knowledge of volitional formations, knowledge of the origin of volitional formations, knowledge of the cessation of volitional formations, and knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of volitional formations. Thus, the ground of knowledge is fourfold.

5. Pañcakamātikā

5. The Matrix of Pentads

755. Pañcavidhena ñāṇavatthu –

755. The ground of knowledge is fivefold:

(1) Pañcaṅgiko sammāsamādhi (2) pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi

(1) Right concentration with five factors, and (2) right concentration with five knowledges.

Evaṃ pañcavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the ground of knowledge is fivefold.

6. Chakkamātikā

6. The Matrix of Hexads

756. Chabbidhena [V 0.0358] ñāṇavatthu –

756. The ground of knowledge is sixfold:

(1) Chasu abhiññāsu paññā

Wisdom in the six direct knowledges.

Evaṃ chabbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the ground of knowledge is sixfold.

7. Sattakamātikā

7. The Septad Matrix

757. Sattavidhena ñāṇavatthu –

757. The ground of knowledge is sevenfold:

(1) Sattasattati ñāṇavatthūni

The seventy-seven grounds of knowledge.

Evaṃ sattavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the ground of knowledge is sevenfold.

8. Aṭṭhakamātikā

8. The Octad Matrix

758. Aṭṭhavidhena [P 0.0317] ñāṇavatthu –

758. The ground of knowledge is eightfold:

(1) Catūsu maggesu, catūsu phalesu paññā

Wisdom in the four paths and in the four fruits.

Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the ground of knowledge is eightfold.

9. Navakamātikā

9. The Nonad Matrix

759. Navavidhena ñāṇavatthu –

759. The ground of knowledge is ninefold:

(1) Navasu anupubbavihārasamāpattīsu paññā

Wisdom in the nine successive abiding attainments.

Evaṃ navavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the ground of knowledge is ninefold.

10. Dasakamātikā

10. The Decad Matrix

760.Dasavidhena [V 0.0359] ñāṇavatthu – dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu [M 0.0329] sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Katamāni dasa?

760. The ground of knowledge is tenfold: the ten powers of the Tathāgata. Endowed with these powers, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma. What are the ten?

(1) Idha tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti[T 0.0428].

Here, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is a cause as a cause, and what is not a cause as not a cause. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is a cause as a cause, and what is not a cause as not a cause, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(2) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the results of past, future, and present kamma undertakings with their grounds and causes. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the results of past, future, and present kamma undertakings with their grounds and causes, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(3) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the path that leads to all destinations. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the path that leads to all destinations, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(4) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato anekadhātu nānādhātulokaṃ anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ lokaṃ (syā.) ma. ni. 1.148 yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato anekadhātu nānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the world with its many and diverse elements. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the world with its many and diverse elements, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(5) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato sattānaṃ [V 0.0360] nānādhimuttikataṃ [P 0.0318] yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the diverse dispositions of beings. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the diverse dispositions of beings, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(6) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti[T 0.0429], idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ [M 0.0330] hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the maturity and immaturity of the faculties of other beings and persons. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the maturity and immaturity of the faculties of other beings and persons, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(7) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the defilement, cleansing, and emergence in regard to the jhānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the defilement, cleansing, and emergence in regard to the jhānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(8) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato pubbenivāsānussatiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato pubbenivāsānussatiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the recollection of past lives. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the recollection of past lives, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(9) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the passing away and reappearance of beings. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the passing away and reappearance of beings, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

(10) Puna caparaṃ tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Imāni [V 0.0361] dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ [T 0.0430] nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Again, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the destruction of the taints. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the destruction of the taints, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma. These are the ten powers of the Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

Evaṃ dasavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the ground of knowledge is tenfold.

Mātikā

Matrix

1. Ekakaniddeso

1. Exposition of the Ones

761. Pañca [M 0.0331] viññāṇā [P 0.0319] na hetumeva, ahetukameva, hetuvippayuttameva, sappaccayameva, saṅkhatameva, arūpameva, lokiyameva, sāsavameva, saṃyojaniyameva, ganthaniyameva, oghaniyameva, yoganiyameva, nīvaraṇiyameva, parāmaṭṭhameva, upādāniyameva, saṃkilesikameva, abyākatameva, sārammaṇameva, acetasikameva, vipākameva, upādinnupādāniyameva, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikameva, na savitakkasavicārameva, na avitakkavicāramattameva, avitakkaavicārameva, na pītisahagatameva, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbameva, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukameva, nevācayagāmināpacayagāmimeva, nevasekkhanāsekkhameva, parittameva, kāmāvacarameva, na rūpāvacarameva, na arūpāvacarameva, pariyāpannameva, no apariyāpannameva, aniyatameva, aniyyānikameva, uppannaṃ manoviññāṇaviññeyyameva, aniccameva, jarābhibhūtameva.

761. The five consciousnesses are not a root, are rootless, dissociated from roots, with a condition, conditioned, immaterial, mundane, an object for the taints, an object for the fetters, an object for the bonds, an object for the floods, an object for the yokes, an object for the hindrances, wrongly grasped, an object for clinging, an object for defilements, indeterminate, with an object, not a mental factor, resultant, taken up and an object for clinging, undefiled but an object for defilements, not with applied thought and sustained thought, not without applied thought and with only sustained thought, without applied thought and without sustained thought, not accompanied by joy, to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, neither leading to accumulation nor to diminution, neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training, limited, pertaining to the sense sphere, not pertaining to the fine-material sphere, not pertaining to the immaterial sphere, included, not unincluded, unfixed, not leading to deliverance, arisen, cognizable by mind-consciousness, impermanent, and overcome by old age.

762. Pañca viññāṇā uppannavatthukā, uppannārammaṇāti uppannasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ uppanne ārammaṇe uppajjanti.

762. The five consciousnesses have an arisen basis and an arisen object; that is, they arise in an arisen basis and on an arisen object.

Purejātavatthukā, purejātārammaṇāti purejātasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ purejāte ārammaṇe uppajjanti.

They have a pre-arisen basis and a pre-arisen object; that is, they arise in a pre-arisen basis and on a pre-arisen object.

Ajjhattikavatthukā[V 0.0362], bāhirārammaṇāti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ vatthu ajjhattikā ārammaṇā bāhirā.

They have an internal basis and an external object; that is, the basis of the five consciousnesses is internal, their objects are external.

Asambhinnavatthukā, asambhinnārammaṇāti asambhinnasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ asambhinne [T 0.0431] ārammaṇe uppajjanti.

They have an unbroken basis and an unbroken object; that is, they arise in an unbroken basis and on an unbroken object.

Nānāvatthukā, nānārammaṇāti aññaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa vatthu ca ārammaṇañca, aññaṃ sotaviññāṇassa vatthu ca ārammaṇañca, aññaṃ ghānaviññāṇassa vatthu ca ārammaṇañca, aññaṃ jivhāviññāṇassa vatthu ca ārammaṇañca, aññaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa vatthu ca ārammaṇañca.

They have diverse bases and diverse objects; that is, the basis and object of eye-consciousness are different, the basis and object of ear-consciousness are different, the basis and object of nose-consciousness are different, the basis and object of tongue-consciousness are different, and the basis and object of body-consciousness are different.

763. Na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhontīti cakkhuviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti, sotaviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti. Cakkhuviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti, ghānaviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [M 0.0332] na paccanubhoti. Cakkhuviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ na [P 0.0320] paccanubhoti, jivhāviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti. Cakkhuviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti, kāyaviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti. Sotaviññāṇassa…pe… ghānaviññāṇassa…pe… jivhāviññāṇassa…pe… kāyaviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti, cakkhuviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi kāyaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti. Kāyaviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti, sotaviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi kāyaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti. Kāyaviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti, ghānaviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi kāyaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti. Kāyaviññāṇassa gocaravisayaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ na [T 0.0432] paccanubhoti, jivhāviññāṇassa gocaravisayampi kāyaviññāṇaṃ na paccanubhoti.

763. They do not experience each other's domain and sphere: that is, ear-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of nose-consciousness. Tongue-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of tongue-consciousness. Body-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of body-consciousness. Ear-consciousness… and so on… nose-consciousness… and so on… tongue-consciousness… and so on… eye-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of nose-consciousness. Tongue-consciousness does not experience the domain and sphere of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the domain and sphere of tongue-consciousness.

764. Na asamannāhārā uppajjantīti samannāharantassa uppajjanti.

764. They do not arise without application of mind; that is, they arise for one who applies the mind.

Na [V 0.0363] amanasikārā uppajjantīti manasikarontassa uppajjanti.

They do not arise without attention; that is, they arise for one who attends.

Na abbokiṇṇā uppajjantīti na paṭipāṭiyā uppajjanti.

They do not arise intermingled; that is, they do not arise in sequence.

Na apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjantīti na ekakkhaṇe uppajjanti.

They do not arise simultaneously; that is, they do not arise in a single moment.

765. Na aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjantīti cakkhuviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā sotaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, sotaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarāpi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati. Cakkhuviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā ghānaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, ghānaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarāpi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati. Cakkhuviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā jivhāviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, jivhāviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarāpi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati. Cakkhuviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā kāyaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, kāyaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarāpi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati. Sotaviññāṇassa…pe… ghānaviññāṇassa…pe… jivhāviññāṇassa…pe… kāyaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, cakkhuviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarāpi kāyaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati. Kāyaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā sotaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, sotaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarāpi [M 0.0333] kāyaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati. Kāyaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā ghānaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, ghānaviññāṇassa [T 0.0433][P 0.0321] uppannasamanantarāpi kāyaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati. Kāyaviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarā jivhāviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati, jivhāviññāṇassa uppannasamanantarāpi kāyaviññāṇaṃ na uppajjati.

765. They do not arise immediately after one another: that is, ear-consciousness does not arise immediately after eye-consciousness has arisen, nor does eye-consciousness arise immediately after ear-consciousness has arisen. Nose-consciousness does not arise immediately after eye-consciousness has arisen, nor does eye-consciousness arise immediately after nose-consciousness has arisen. Tongue-consciousness does not arise immediately after eye-consciousness has arisen, nor does eye-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness has arisen. Body-consciousness does not arise immediately after eye-consciousness has arisen, nor does eye-consciousness arise immediately after body-consciousness has arisen. Ear-consciousness… and so on… nose-consciousness… and so on… tongue-consciousness… and so on… eye-consciousness does not arise immediately after body-consciousness has arisen, nor does body-consciousness arise immediately after eye-consciousness has arisen. Ear-consciousness does not arise immediately after body-consciousness has arisen, nor does body-consciousness arise immediately after ear-consciousness has arisen. Nose-consciousness does not arise immediately after body-consciousness has arisen, nor does body-consciousness arise immediately after nose-consciousness has arisen. Tongue-consciousness does not arise immediately after body-consciousness has arisen, nor does body-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness has arisen.

766. Pañca viññāṇā anābhogāti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ natthi āvaṭṭanā vā ābhogo vā samannāhāro vā manasikāro vā.

766. The five consciousnesses are without advertence; that is, for the five consciousnesses there is no turning towards, no adverting, no application, or no attention.

Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānātīti pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti.

One does not discern any phenomenon with the five consciousnesses: that is, with the five consciousnesses one does not discern any phenomenon.

Aññatra abhinipātamattāti aññatra āpātamattā.

Except for mere impact: that is, except for mere impingement.

Pañcannaṃ [V 0.0364] viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānātīti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarā manodhātuyāpi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti.

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not discern any phenomenon: that is, even immediately after the five consciousnesses, with the mind-element one does not discern any phenomenon.

Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappetīti pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappeti – gamanaṃ vā ṭhānaṃ vā nisajjaṃ vā seyyaṃ vā.

One does not adopt any posture with the five consciousnesses: that is, with the five consciousnesses one does not adopt any posture—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.

Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappetīti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarā manodhātuyāpi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappeti – gamanaṃ vā ṭhānaṃ vā nisajjaṃ vā seyyaṃ vā.

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not adopt any posture: that is, even immediately after the five consciousnesses, with the mind-element one does not adopt any posture—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.

Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapetīti pañcahi viññāṇehi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapeti.

One does not initiate bodily action or verbal action with the five consciousnesses: that is, with the five consciousnesses one does not initiate bodily action or verbal action.

Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapetīti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarā manodhātuyāpi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapeti.

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not initiate bodily action or verbal action: that is, even immediately after the five consciousnesses, with the mind-element one does not initiate bodily action or verbal action.

Pañcahi viññāṇehi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyatīti [T 0.0434] pañcahi viññāṇehi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyati.

One does not undertake wholesome or unwholesome states with the five consciousnesses: that is, with the five consciousnesses one does not undertake wholesome or unwholesome states.

Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyatīti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarā manodhātuyāpi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyati.

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not undertake wholesome or unwholesome states: that is, even immediately after the five consciousnesses, with the mind-element one does not undertake wholesome or unwholesome states.

Pañcahi viññāṇehi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhātīti pañcahi viññāṇehi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhāti.

With the five consciousnesses one neither enters upon nor emerges from an attainment: that is, with the five consciousnesses one neither enters upon nor emerges from an attainment.

Pañcannaṃ [M 0.0334] viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhātīti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ [P 0.0322] samanantarā manodhātuyāpi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhāti.

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one neither enters upon nor emerges from an attainment: that is, even immediately after the five consciousnesses, with the mind-element one neither enters upon nor emerges from an attainment.

Pañcahi [V 0.0365] viññāṇehi na cavati na uppajjatīti pañcahi viññāṇehi na cavati na uppajjati.

With the five consciousnesses one neither passes away nor is reborn: that is, with the five consciousnesses one neither passes away nor is reborn.

Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na cavati na uppajjatīti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarā manodhātuyāpi na cavati na uppajjati.

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one neither passes away nor is reborn: that is, even immediately after the five consciousnesses, with the mind-element one neither passes away nor is reborn.

Pañcahi viññāṇehi na supati na paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passatīti pañcahi viññāṇehi na supati na paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passati.

With the five consciousnesses one neither falls asleep, nor awakens, nor sees a dream: that is, with the five consciousnesses one neither falls asleep, nor awakens, nor sees a dream.

Pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na supati na paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passatīti pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarā manodhātuyāpi na supati na paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passati. Evaṃ yāthāvakavatthuvibhāvanā paññā.

Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one neither falls asleep, nor awakens, nor sees a dream: that is, even immediately after the five consciousnesses, with the mind-element one neither falls asleep, nor awakens, nor sees a dream. Thus is the wisdom that clarifies the subject matter as it truly is.

Evaṃ ekavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus in one way is the ground for knowledge.

Ekakaṃ.

The Section on the Ones.

2. Dukaniddeso

2. Exposition of the Dyads

767. (1) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā lokiyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā lokuttarā paññā.

767. (1) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is mundane wisdom; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is supramundane wisdom.

(2) Sabbāva paññā [T 0.0435] kenaci viññeyyā, kenaci na viññeyyā.

(2) All wisdom is knowable by some means, and not knowable by some means.

(3) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā sāsavā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā anāsavā paññā.

(3) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of the taints; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of the taints.

(4) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā āsavavippayuttā sāsavā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā āsavavippayuttā anāsavā paññā.

(4) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is dissociated from the taints but is an object of the taints; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is dissociated from the taints and is not an object of the taints.

(5) Tīsu [V 0.0366] bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā saṃyojaniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā asaṃyojaniyā paññā.

(5) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of the fetters; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of the fetters.

(6) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyā paññā.

(6) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is dissociated from the fetters but is an object of the fetters; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is dissociated from the fetters and is not an object of the fetters.

(7) Tīsu [M 0.0335] bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā ganthaniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā aganthaniyā paññā.

(7) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of the ties; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of the ties.

(8) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā ganthavippayuttā ganthaniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā ganthavippayuttā aganthaniyā paññā.

(8) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is dissociated from the ties but is an object of the ties; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is dissociated from the ties and is not an object of the ties.

(9) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā oghaniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā anoghaniyā paññā.

(9) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of the floods; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of the floods.

(10) Tīsu [P 0.0323] bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā oghavippayuttā oghaniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā oghavippayuttā anoghaniyā paññā.

(10) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is dissociated from the floods but is an object of the floods; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is dissociated from the floods and is not an object of the floods.

(11) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā yoganiyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā ayoganiyā paññā.

(11) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of the yokes; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of the yokes.

(12) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā yogavippayuttā yoganiyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu [T 0.0436] paññā yogavippayuttā ayoganiyā paññā.

(12) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is dissociated from the yokes but is an object of the yokes; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is dissociated from the yokes and is not an object of the yokes.

(13) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā nīvaraṇiyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā anīvaraṇiyā paññā.

(13) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of the hindrances; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of the hindrances.

(14) Tīsu [V 0.0367] bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā nīvaraṇavippayuttā nīvaraṇiyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā nīvaraṇavippayuttā anīvaraṇiyā paññā.

(14) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is dissociated from the hindrances but is an object of the hindrances; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is dissociated from the hindrances and is not an object of the hindrances.

(15) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā parāmaṭṭhā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā aparāmaṭṭhā paññā.

(15) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of misapprehension; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of misapprehension.

(16) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā parāmāsavippayuttā parāmaṭṭhā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā parāmāsavippayuttā aparāmaṭṭhā paññā.

(16) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is dissociated from misapprehension but is an object of misapprehension; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is dissociated from misapprehension and is not an object of misapprehension.

(17) Tīsu bhūmīsu vipāke paññā upādinnā paññā, tīsu bhūmīsu kusale tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā anupādinnā paññā.

Wisdom in resultant states in the three planes is kammically produced wisdom; wisdom in wholesome states in the three planes, in functional-indeterminate states in the three planes, in the four paths, and in the four fruits is not kammically produced wisdom.

(18) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā upādāniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā anupādāniyā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of clinging; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of clinging.

(19) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā upādānavippayuttā upādāniyā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā upādānavippayuttā anupādāniyā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is dissociated from clinging but is wisdom that is an object of clinging; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is dissociated from clinging and is wisdom that is not an object of clinging.

(20) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā saṃkilesikā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā asaṃkilesikā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is an object of defilement; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is wisdom that is not an object of defilement.

(21) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate [M 0.0336] paññā kilesavippayuttā saṃkilesikā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā kilesavippayuttā asaṃkilesikā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is dissociated from the defilements but is wisdom that is an object of defilement; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is dissociated from the defilements and is wisdom that is not an object of defilement.

(22) Vitakkasampayuttā paññā savitakkā paññā, vitakkavippayuttā [T 0.0437] paññā avitakkā paññā.

Wisdom associated with applied thought is wisdom with applied thought; wisdom dissociated from applied thought is wisdom without applied thought.

(23) Vicārasampayuttā [V 0.0368] paññā savicārā paññā, vicāravippayuttā paññā avicārā paññā.

Wisdom associated with sustained thought is wisdom with sustained thought; wisdom dissociated from sustained thought is wisdom without sustained thought.

(24) Pītisampayuttā paññā sappītikā paññā, pītivippayuttā paññā appītikā paññā.

Wisdom associated with rapture is wisdom with rapture; wisdom dissociated from rapture is wisdom without rapture.

(25) Pītisampayuttā paññā pītisahagatā paññā, pītivippayuttā paññā na pītisahagatā paññā.

Wisdom associated with rapture is wisdom accompanied by rapture; wisdom dissociated from rapture is wisdom not accompanied by rapture.

(26) Sukhasampayuttā [P 0.0324] paññā sukhasahagatā paññā, sukhavippayuttā paññā na sukhasahagatā paññā.

Wisdom associated with pleasure is wisdom accompanied by pleasure; wisdom dissociated from pleasure is wisdom not accompanied by pleasure.

(27) Upekkhāsampayuttā paññā upekkhāsahagatā paññā, upekkhāvippayuttā paññā na upekkhāsahagatā paññā.

Wisdom associated with equanimity is wisdom accompanied by equanimity; wisdom dissociated from equanimity is wisdom not accompanied by equanimity.

(28) Kāmāvacarakusalābyākate paññā kāmāvacarā paññā, rūpāvacarā paññā arūpāvacarā paññā, apariyāpannā paññā na kāmāvacarā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states of the sense sphere is sense-sphere wisdom; form-sphere wisdom, formless-sphere wisdom, and unincluded wisdom are not sense-sphere wisdom.

(29) Rūpāvacarakusalābyākate paññā rūpāvacarā paññā, kāmāvacarā paññā arūpāvacarā paññā apariyāpannā paññā na rūpāvacarā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states of the form sphere is form-sphere wisdom; sense-sphere wisdom, formless-sphere wisdom, and unincluded wisdom are not form-sphere wisdom.

(30) Arūpāvacarakusalābyākate paññā arūpāvacarā paññā, kāmāvacarā paññā rūpāvacarā paññā apariyāpannā paññā na arūpāvacarā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states of the formless sphere is formless-sphere wisdom; sense-sphere wisdom, form-sphere wisdom, and unincluded wisdom are not formless-sphere wisdom.

(31) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā pariyāpannā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā apariyāpannā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is included wisdom; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is unincluded wisdom.

(32) Catūsu [V 0.0369] maggesu paññā niyyānikā paññā, tīsu bhūmīsu kusale catūsu bhūmīsu vipāke tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate paññā aniyyānikā paññā.

Wisdom in the four paths is leading-out wisdom; wisdom in wholesome states in the three planes, in resultant states in the four planes, and in functional-indeterminate states in the three planes is non-leading-out wisdom.

(33) Catūsu maggesu paññā niyatā paññā, tīsu bhūmīsu kusale catūsu bhūmīsu vipāke tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate paññā aniyatā [T 0.0438] paññā.

Wisdom in the four paths is fixed wisdom; wisdom in wholesome states in the three planes, in resultant states in the four planes, and in functional-indeterminate states in the three planes is unfixed wisdom.

(34) Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalābyākate paññā sauttarā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā anuttarā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate states in the three planes is surpassable wisdom; wisdom in the four paths and four fruits is unsurpassable wisdom.

(35) Tattha katamā atthajāpikā paññā?

Therein, what is the wisdom that generates a result?

Catūsu bhūmīsu kusale arahato abhiññaṃ uppādentassa samāpattiṃ uppādentassa kiriyābyākate paññā atthajāpikā paññā, catūsu bhūmīsu vipāke arahato uppannāya abhiññāya uppannāya samāpattiyā kiriyābyākate paññā jāpitatthā paññā.

Wisdom in wholesome states in the four planes, and wisdom in the functional-indeterminate consciousness of an Arahant who is producing higher knowledge and producing attainment, is wisdom that generates a result. Wisdom in resultant states in the four planes, and wisdom in the functional-indeterminate consciousness of an Arahant for whom higher knowledge has arisen and for whom attainment has arisen, is wisdom that has a generated result.

Evaṃ duvidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus the ground of knowledge is twofold.

Dukaṃ.

The Dyad.

3. Tikaniddeso

3. Exposition of the Triads

768. (1. Ka) tattha [M 0.0337] katamā cintāmayā paññā?

768. Therein, what is the wisdom consisting of thought?

Yogavihitesu vā kammāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā sippāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā vijjāṭṭhānesu kammassakataṃ vā saccānulomikaṃ vā rūpaṃ aniccanti vā vedanā…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ [P 0.0325] aniccanti vā, yaṃ evarūpiṃ anulomikaṃ khantiṃ diṭṭhiṃ ruciṃ [V 0.0370] mudiṃ pekkhaṃ dhammanijjhānakkhantiṃ parato assutvā paṭilabhati – ayaṃ vuccati “cintāmayā paññā”.

In suitable spheres of work, or in suitable spheres of crafts, or in suitable spheres of knowledge, concerning ownership of kamma, or in conformity with the truths—such as 'form is impermanent,' or 'feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent'—whatever such acceptance, view, inclination, approval, consideration, and acceptance through contemplating phenomena one acquires without having heard it from another—this is called 'wisdom consisting of thought'.

(Kha) tattha katamā sutamayā paññā? Yogavihitesu vā kammāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā sippāyatanesu yogavihitesu vā vijjāṭṭhānesu kammassakataṃ vā saccānulomikaṃ vā rūpaṃ aniccanti vā vedanā…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ aniccanti vā, yaṃ evarūpiṃ anulomikaṃ khantiṃ diṭṭhiṃ ruciṃ mudiṃ pekkhaṃ dhammanijjhānakkhantiṃ parato sutvā paṭilabhati – ayaṃ vuccati “sutamayā paññā”.

Therein, what is the wisdom consisting of hearing? In suitable spheres of work, or in suitable spheres of crafts, or in suitable spheres of knowledge, concerning ownership of kamma, or in conformity with the truths—such as 'form is impermanent,' or 'feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent'—whatever such acceptance, view, inclination, approval, consideration, and acceptance through contemplating phenomena one acquires after having heard it from another—this is called 'wisdom consisting of hearing'.

(Ga) sabbāpi samāpannassa paññā bhāvanāmayā [T 0.0439] paññā.

All wisdom of one in meditative attainment is wisdom consisting of mental development.

769. (2. Ka) tattha katamā dānamayā paññā? Dānaṃ ārabbha dānādhigaccha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “dānamayā paññā”.

769. Therein, what is the wisdom consisting of giving? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises for one who attains giving, with giving as the object—this is called 'wisdom consisting of giving'.

(Kha) tattha katamā sīlamayā paññā? Sīlaṃ ārabbha sīlādhigaccha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “sīlamayā paññā”.

Therein, what is the wisdom consisting of virtue? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises for one who attains virtue, with virtue as the object—this is called 'wisdom consisting of virtue'.

(Ga) sabbāpi samāpannassa paññā bhāvanāmayā paññā.

All wisdom of one who has attained absorption is wisdom consisting of mental development.

770. (3. Ka) tattha katamā adhisīle paññā? Pātimokkhasaṃvaraṃ saṃvarantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “adhisīle paññā”.

770. Therein, what is the wisdom in higher virtue? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises in one who is restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint—this is called 'wisdom in higher virtue'.

(Kha) tattha katamā adhicitte paññā? Rūpāvacarārūpāvacarasamāpattiṃ samāpajjantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “adhicitte paññā”.

Therein, what is the wisdom in the higher mind? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises in one who is attaining the form-sphere and formless-sphere attainments—this is called 'wisdom in the higher mind'.

(Ga) tattha [M 0.0338][V 0.0371] katamā adhipaññāya paññā? Catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā – ayaṃ vuccati “adhipaññāya paññā”.

Therein, what is the wisdom in higher wisdom? The wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits—this is called 'wisdom in higher wisdom'.

771. (4. Ka) tattha katamaṃ āyakosallaṃ? “Ime dhamme manasikaroto anuppannā ceva akusalā dhammā na uppajjanti, uppannā ca akusalā dhammā pahīyanti. Ime vā panime dhamme manasikaroto anuppannā ceva kusalā dhammā uppajjanti, uppannā ca kusalā dhammā [T 0.0440] bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṃvattantī”ti – yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho [P 0.0326] dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “āyakosallaṃ”.

771. (4. Ka) Therein, what is skill in progress? 'When one attends to these dhammas, unarisen unwholesome states do not arise, and arisen unwholesome states are abandoned. Or, when one attends to these dhammas, unarisen wholesome states arise, and arisen wholesome states conduce to growth, increase, development, and fulfillment.' Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view is therein—this is called 'skill in progress'.

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ apāyakosallaṃ? “Ime dhamme manasikaroto anuppannā ceva kusalā dhammā na uppajjanti, uppannā ca kusalā dhammā nirujjhanti. Ime vā panime dhamme manasikaroto anuppannā ceva akusalā dhammā uppajjanti, uppannā ca akusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattantī”ti – yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “apāyakosallaṃ”.

(Kha) Therein, what is skill in decline? 'When one attends to these dhammas, unarisen wholesome states do not arise, and arisen wholesome states cease. Or, when one attends to these dhammas, unarisen unwholesome states arise, and arisen unwholesome states conduce to growth and increase.' Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view is therein—this is called 'skill in decline'.

(Ga) sabbāpi tatrupāyā paññā upāyakosallaṃ.

(Ga) All wisdom that is a means for that is skill in means.

772. (5. Ka) catūsu bhūmīsu vipāke paññā vipākā paññā.

772. (5. Ka) Wisdom in resultant states in the four planes is resultant wisdom.

(Kha) catūsu bhūmīsu kusale paññā vipākadhammadhammā paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom in wholesome states in the four planes is wisdom in states that produce a result.

(Ga) tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate paññā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā paññā.

(Ga) Wisdom in functional-indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is neither resultant nor produces a result.

773. (6. Ka) tīsu bhūmīsu vipāke paññā upādinnupādāniyā paññā.

773. (6. Ka) Wisdom in resultant states in the three planes is wisdom that is produced by kamma and is fuel for clinging.

(Kha) tīsu bhūmīsu kusale tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate paññā anupādinnupādāniyā paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom in wholesome states in the three planes and in functional-indeterminate states in the three planes is wisdom that is not produced by kamma but is fuel for clinging.

(Ga) catūsu [V 0.0372] maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā anupādinnaanupādāniyā paññā.

(Ga) Wisdom in the four paths and in the four fruits is wisdom that is not produced by kamma and is not fuel for clinging.

774. (7. Ka) vitakkavicārasampayuttā paññā savitakkasavicārā paññā.

774. (7. Ka) Wisdom associated with applied thought and sustained thought is wisdom with applied thought and sustained thought.

(Kha) vitakkavippayuttā vicārasampayuttā paññā avitakkavicāramattā paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom dissociated from applied thought but associated with sustained thought is wisdom with only sustained thought.

(Ga) vitakkavicāravippayuttā paññā avitakkaavicārā paññā.

(Ga) Wisdom dissociated from applied thought and sustained thought is wisdom without applied thought and without sustained thought.

775. (8. Ka) pītisampayuttā paññā pītisahagatā paññā.

775. (8. Ka) Wisdom associated with rapture is wisdom accompanied by rapture.

(Kha) sukhasampayuttā [T 0.0441] paññā sukhasahagatā paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom associated with happiness is wisdom accompanied by happiness.

(Ga) upekkhāsampayuttā paññā upekkhāsahagatā paññā.

(Ga) Wisdom associated with equanimity is wisdom accompanied by equanimity.

776. (9. Ka) tīsu [M 0.0339] bhūmīsu kusale paññā ācayagāminī paññā.

776. (9. Ka) Wisdom in the wholesome in the three planes is wisdom that leads to accumulation.

(Kha) catūsu maggesu paññā apacayagāminī paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom in the four paths is wisdom that leads to non-accumulation.

(Ga) catūsu bhūmīsu vipāke tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate paññā nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī paññā.

(Ga) Wisdom in the resultant in the four planes and in the functional-indeterminate in the three planes is wisdom that leads neither to accumulation nor to non-accumulation.

777. (10. Ka) catūsu maggesu tīsu phalesu paññā sekkhā paññā.

777. (10. Ka) Wisdom in the four paths and the three fruits is a trainee's wisdom.

(Kha) upariṭṭhimā upariṭṭhime (syā.), upariṭṭhimaṃ (ka.) arahattaphale paññā asekkhā paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom in the highest fruit, the fruit of arahantship, is the wisdom of one beyond training.

(Ga) tīsu bhūmīsu kusale tīsu bhūmīsu vipāke tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate paññā nevasekkhanāsekkhā paññā.

(Ga) Wisdom in the wholesome in the three planes, in the resultant in the three planes, and in the functional-indeterminate in the three planes is wisdom that is neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training.

778. (11. Ka) kāmāvacarakusalābyākate [V 0.0373] paññā parittā paññā.

778. (11. Ka) Wisdom in the wholesome and the indeterminate of the sense-sphere is limited wisdom.

(Kha) rūpāvacarārūpāvacarakusalābyākate paññā mahaggatā paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom in the wholesome and the indeterminate of the form-sphere and the formless-sphere is exalted wisdom.

(Ga) catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā appamāṇā paññā.

(Ga) Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is immeasurable wisdom.

779. (12. Ka) tattha katamā parittārammaṇā paññā? Paritte [P 0.0327] dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “parittārammaṇā paññā”.

779. (12. Ka) Therein, what is wisdom with a limited object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking a limited phenomenon as its object—this is called 'wisdom with a limited object'.

780. (Kha) tattha katamā mahaggatārammaṇā paññā? Mahaggate dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “mahaggatārammaṇā paññā”.

780. (Kha) Therein, what is wisdom with an exalted object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking an exalted phenomenon as its object—this is called 'wisdom with an exalted object'.

781. (Ga) tattha katamā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā? Appamāṇe dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “appamāṇārammaṇā [T 0.0442] paññā”.

781. (Ga) Therein, what is wisdom with an immeasurable object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking an immeasurable phenomenon as its object—this is called 'wisdom with an immeasurable object'.

782. (13. Ka) tattha katamā maggārammaṇā paññā? Ariyamaggaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “maggārammaṇā paññā”.

782. (13. Ka) Therein, what is wisdom with the path as its object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking the noble path as its object—this is called 'wisdom with the path as its object'.

(Kha) catūsu maggesu paññā maggahetukā paññā.

(Kha) Wisdom in the four paths is wisdom that has the path as its cause.

783. (Ga) tattha katamā maggādhipatinī paññā? Ariyamaggaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “maggādhipatinī paññā”.

783. (Ga) Therein, what is wisdom that has the path as its dominant factor? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises having made the noble path the dominant factor—this is called 'wisdom that has the path as its dominant factor'.

784. (14) Catūsu [M 0.0340][V 0.0374] bhūmīsu vipāke paññā siyā uppannā, siyā uppādinī, na vattabbā anuppannāti. Catūsu bhūmīsu kusale tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākate paññā siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, na vattabbā uppādinīti.

784. (14) Wisdom in the resultant in the four planes may be arisen or it may be productive; it should not be said to be 'unarisen.' Wisdom in the wholesome in the four planes and in the functional-indeterminate in the three planes may be arisen or it may be unarisen; it should not be said to be 'productive.'

785. (15) Sabbāva paññā siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā.

785. (15) All wisdom may be past, may be future, or may be present.

786. (16. Ka) tattha katamā atītārammaṇā paññā? Atīte dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “atītārammaṇā paññā”.

786. (16. Ka) Therein, what is wisdom with a past object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking a past phenomenon as its object—this is called 'wisdom with a past object'.

787. (Kha) tattha katamā anāgatārammaṇā paññā? Anāgate dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “anāgatārammaṇā paññā”.

787. (Kha) Therein, what is wisdom with a future object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking a future phenomenon as its object—this is called 'wisdom with a future object'.

788. (Ga) tattha katamā paccuppannārammaṇā paññā? Paccuppanne dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā [T 0.0443] …pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “paccuppannārammaṇā paññā”.

788. (Ga) Therein, what is wisdom with a present object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking a present phenomenon as its object—this is called 'wisdom with a present object'.

789. (17) Sabbāva paññā siyā ajjhattā, siyā bahiddhā, siyā ajjhattabahiddhā.

789. (17) All wisdom may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external.

790. (18. Ka) tattha katamā ajjhattārammaṇā paññā? Ajjhatte dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… [P 0.0328] amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “ajjhattārammaṇā paññā”.

790. (18. Ka) Therein, what is wisdom with an internal object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking internal phenomena as its object—this is called 'wisdom with an internal object'.

791. (Kha) tattha katamā bahiddhārammaṇā paññā? Bahiddhādhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “bahiddhārammaṇā paññā”.

791. (Kha) Therein, what is wisdom with an external object? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking external phenomena as its object—this is called 'wisdom with an external object'.

792. (Ga) tattha [V 0.0375] katamā ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā paññā? Ajjhattabahiddhā dhamme ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā paññā”.

792. (Ga) Therein, what is wisdom with internal and external objects? Whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking internal and external phenomena as its object—this is called 'wisdom with internal and external objects'.

Evaṃ tividhena ñāṇavatthu.

Thus, the basis of knowledge is threefold.

Tikaṃ.

The Triad.

4. Catukkaniddeso

4. Exposition of the Tetrad

793. (1. Ka) tattha [M 0.0341] katamaṃ kammassakatañāṇaṃ? “Atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ, atthi hutaṃ, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, atthi ayaṃ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī”ti – yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho [T 0.0444] dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “kammassakatañāṇaṃ”. Ṭhapetvā saccānulomikaṃ ñāṇaṃ, sabbāpi sāsavā kusalā paññā kammassakatañāṇaṃ.

793. (1. Ka) Herein, what is the knowledge of kamma as one's own? 'There is what is given, there is what is offered, there is what is sacrificed; there is fruit and result of actions well done and badly done; there is this world, there is the other world; there is mother, there is father; there are beings of spontaneous birth; there are in the world ascetics and brahmins who are well-gone and well-practicing, who, having realized it for themselves through direct knowledge, make known this world and the other world'—such wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'knowledge of kamma as one's own'. Setting aside the knowledge that conforms to the truths, all wholesome wisdom that is subject to the taints is knowledge of kamma as one's own.

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ saccānulomikaṃ ñāṇaṃ? “Rūpaṃ anicca”nti vā vedanā…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… “viññāṇaṃ anicca”nti vā yā evarūpī anulomikā khanti diṭṭhi ruci mudi pekkhā dhammanijjhānakkhanti – idaṃ vuccati “saccānulomikaṃ ñāṇaṃ”.

(Kha) Herein, what is knowledge that conforms to the truths? 'Form is impermanent,' or 'feeling... perception... formations... consciousness is impermanent'—whatever such conforming patient acceptance, view, liking, gladness, consideration, and patient acceptance of the contemplation of phenomena there is—this is called 'knowledge that conforms to the truths'.

(Ga) catūsu maggesu paññā maggasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ.

(Ga) Wisdom in the four paths is the knowledge of one possessed of the path.

(Gha) catūsu phalesu paññā phalasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ.

(Gha) Wisdom in the four fruits is the knowledge of one possessed of the fruit.

794. (2) Maggasamaṅgissa [V 0.0376] ñāṇaṃ dukkhepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudayepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

794. (2) The knowledge of one possessed of the path is knowledge in suffering, knowledge in the origin of suffering, knowledge in the cessation of suffering, and knowledge in the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

(Ka) tattha katamaṃ dukkhe ñāṇaṃ? Dukkhaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhe ñāṇaṃ”.

(Ka) Herein, what is knowledge in suffering? Whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises taking suffering as its object—this is called 'knowledge in suffering'.

(Kha-gha) dukkhasamudayaṃ ārabbha…pe… dukkhanirodhaṃ ārabbha…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ [P 0.0329] paṭipadaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ”.

(Kha-gha) Taking the origin of suffering as its object… taking the cessation of suffering as its object… taking the path leading to the cessation of suffering as its object, whatever wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises—this is called 'knowledge in the path leading to the cessation of suffering'.

795. (3) Kāmāvacarakusalābyākate paññā kāmāvacarā paññā, rūpāvacarakusalābyākate paññā rūpāvacarā paññā, arūpāvacarakusalābyākate paññā arūpāvacarā paññā, catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā apariyāpannā paññā.

795. (3) Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate sense-sphere states is sense-sphere wisdom. Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate form-sphere states is form-sphere wisdom. Wisdom in wholesome and indeterminate formless-sphere states is formless-sphere wisdom. Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is unincluded wisdom.

796. (4. Ka) tattha [T 0.0445] katamaṃ dhamme ñāṇaṃ? Catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā dhamme ñāṇaṃ.

796. (4. Ka) Herein, what is knowledge in the Dhamma? Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is knowledge in the Dhamma.

(Kha) so iminā dhammena ñātena diṭṭhena pattena viditena pariyogāḷhena atītānāgatena nayaṃ neti. “Ye hi keci atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā [M 0.0342] brāhmaṇā vā dukkhaṃ abbhaññaṃsu abbhaññiṃsu (syā.) evamuparipi, dukkhasamudayaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, dukkhanirodhaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, imaññeva te dukkhaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, imaññeva te dukkhasamudayaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, imaññeva te dukkhanirodhaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, imaññeva te dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abbhaññaṃsu. Ye hi keci anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā dukkhaṃ abhijānissanti, dukkhasamudayaṃ abhijānissanti, dukkhanirodhaṃ abhijānissanti, dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhijānissanti, imaññeva te dukkhaṃ abhijānissanti, imaññeva te dukkhasamudayaṃ abhijānissanti, imaññeva te dukkhanirodhaṃ abhijānissanti, imaññeva te dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ abhijānissantī”ti – yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “anvaye ñāṇaṃ”.

(Kha) By this Dhamma that has been known, seen, attained, realized, and fathomed, one draws an inference concerning the past and the future thus: 'Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past directly knew suffering, directly knew the origin of suffering, directly knew the cessation of suffering, and directly knew the path leading to the cessation of suffering, they all directly knew just this suffering, just this origin of suffering, just this cessation of suffering, and just this path leading to the cessation of suffering. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will directly know suffering, will directly know the origin of suffering, will directly know the cessation of suffering, and will directly know the path leading to the cessation of suffering, they all will directly know just this suffering, just this origin of suffering, just this cessation of suffering, and just this path leading to the cessation of suffering.' Whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view arises therein—this is called 'inferential knowledge'.

(Ga) tattha [V 0.0377] katamaṃ pariye ñāṇaṃ? Idha bhikkhu parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti. Sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ “sarāgaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītarāgaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ “sadosaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītadosaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, samohaṃ vā cittaṃ “samohaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ “vītamohaṃ citta”nti pajānāti[T 0.0446], saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ “saṃkhittaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ “vikkhittaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ “mahaggataṃ citta”nti pajānāti, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ “amahaggataṃ citta”nti pajānāti, sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ “sauttaraṃ citta”nti pajānāti, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ “anuttaraṃ citta”nti pajānāti, samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ “samāhitaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ “asamāhitaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ “vimuttaṃ citta”nti pajānāti, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ “avimuttaṃ citta”nti pajānātīti – yā tattha paññā [P 0.0330] pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “pariye ñāṇaṃ”.

(Ga) Herein, what is the knowledge of encompassing? Here, a bhikkhu, encompassing with his own mind the minds of other beings, other persons, understands them. He understands a mind with lust as 'a mind with lust'; a mind without lust as 'a mind without lust'; a mind with hatred as 'a mind with hatred'; a mind without hatred as 'a mind without hatred'; a mind with delusion as 'a mind with delusion'; a mind without delusion as 'a mind without delusion'; a constricted mind as 'a constricted mind'; a distracted mind as 'a distracted mind'; a sublime mind as 'a sublime mind'; an unsublime mind as 'an unsublime mind'; a surpassable mind as 'a surpassable mind'; an unsurpassable mind as 'an unsurpassable mind'; a concentrated mind as 'a concentrated mind'; an unconcentrated mind as 'an unconcentrated mind'; a liberated mind as 'a liberated mind'; an unliberated mind as 'an unliberated mind.' The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view that there is in this case—this is called 'knowledge of encompassing'.

(Gha) ṭhapetvā dhamme ñāṇaṃ anvaye ñāṇaṃ pariye ñāṇaṃ, avasesā paññā sammutiñāṇaṃ.

(Gha) Setting aside knowledge of phenomena, inferential knowledge, and knowledge of encompassing, the remaining wisdom is conventional knowledge.

797. (5. Ka) tattha katamā paññā ācayāya no apacayāya? Kāmāvacarakusale paññā ācayāya no apacayāya.

797. (5. Ka) Herein, what is the wisdom that is for accumulation and not for diminution? Wisdom in the sense-sphere wholesome is for accumulation and not for diminution.

(Kha) catūsu maggesu paññā apacayāya [M 0.0343] no ācayāya.

(Kha) Wisdom in the four paths is for diminution, not for accumulation.

(Ga) rūpāvacarārūpāvacarakusale paññā ācayāya ceva apacayāya ca.

(Ga) Wisdom in the form-sphere and formless-sphere wholesome is for both accumulation and diminution.

(Gha) avasesā paññā neva ācayāya no apacayāya.

(Gha) The remaining wisdom is neither for accumulation nor for diminution.

798. (6. Ka) tattha katamā paññā nibbidāya no paṭivedhāya? Yāya paññāya kāmesu vītarāgo hoti, na ca abhiññāyo paṭivijjhati na ca saccāni – ayaṃ vuccati “paññā nibbidāya no paṭivedhāya”.

798. (6. Ka) Herein, what is the wisdom that is for disenchantment but not for penetration? It is the wisdom by which one becomes free from lust for sensual pleasures, but penetrates neither the direct knowledges nor the truths. This is called 'wisdom for disenchantment but not for penetration'.

(Kha) sveva [V 0.0378] paññāya kāmesu vītarāgo samāno abhiññāyo paṭivijjhati na ca saccāni – ayaṃ vuccati “paññā paṭivedhāya no nibbidāya”.

(Kha) That very person, with wisdom, being free from lust for sensual pleasures, penetrates the direct knowledges but does not penetrate the truths. This is called 'wisdom for penetration but not for disenchantment'.

(Ga) catūsu [T 0.0447] maggesu paññā nibbidāya ceva paṭivedhāya ca.

(Ga) Wisdom in the four paths is for both disenchantment and penetration.

(Gha) avasesā paññā neva nibbidāya no paṭivedhāya.

(Gha) The remaining wisdom is neither for disenchantment nor for penetration.

799. (7. Ka) tattha katamā hānabhāginī paññā? Paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhiṃ kāmasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti hānabhāginī paññā.

799. (7. Ka) Herein, what is wisdom partaking of decline? For an attainer of the first jhāna, perceptions and attention accompanied by sensual desire arise. This is wisdom partaking of decline.

(Kha) tadanudhammatā sati santiṭṭhati ṭhitibhāginī paññā.

(Kha) When mindfulness is established in conformity with that state, this is wisdom partaking of stability.

(Ga) avitakkasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti visesabhāginī paññā.

(Ga) When perceptions and attention unaccompanied by initial thought arise, this is wisdom partaking of distinction.

(Gha) nibbidāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti virāgūpasañhitā nibbedhabhāginī paññā. Dutiyassa jhānassa lābhiṃ vitakkasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti hānabhāginī paññā. Tadanudhammatā sati santiṭṭhati ṭhitibhāginī paññā. Upekkhāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti visesabhāginī paññā. Nibbidāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti virāgūpasañhitā nibbedhabhāginī paññā. Tatiyassa jhānassa lābhiṃ pītisukhasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti hānabhāginī paññā. Tadanudhammatā sati santiṭṭhati ṭhitibhāginī paññā. Adukkhamasukhasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti visesabhāginī [P 0.0331] paññā. Nibbidāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti virāgūpasañhitā nibbedhabhāginī paññā. Catutthassa jhānassa lābhiṃ upekkhāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti hānabhāginī paññā. Tadanudhammatā sati santiṭṭhati ṭhitibhāginī paññā. Ākāsānañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā [V 0.0379] samudācaranti visesabhāginī paññā. Nibbidāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti virāgūpasañhitā nibbedhabhāginī [T 0.0448] paññā. Ākāsānañcāyatanassa lābhiṃ rūpasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti hānabhāginī paññā. Tadanudhammatā sati santiṭṭhati ṭhitibhāginī [M 0.0344] paññā. Viññāṇañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti visesabhāginī paññā. Nibbidāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti virāgūpasañhitā nibbedhabhāginī paññā. Viññāṇañcāyatanassa lābhiṃ ākāsānañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti hānabhāginī paññā. Tadanudhammatā sati santiṭṭhati ṭhitibhāginī paññā. Ākiñcaññāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti visesabhāginī paññā. Nibbidāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti virāgūpasañhitā nibbedhabhāginī paññā. Ākiñcaññāyatanassa lābhiṃ viññāṇañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti hānabhāginī paññā. Tadanudhammatā sati santiṭṭhati ṭhitibhāginī paññā. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti visesabhāginī paññā. Nibbidāsahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti virāgūpasañhitā nibbedhabhāginī paññā.

(Gha) When perceptions and attention accompanied by disenchantment arise, this is wisdom connected with dispassion, partaking of penetration. For an attainer of the second jhāna, when perceptions and attention accompanied by initial thought arise, this is wisdom partaking of decline. When mindfulness is established in conformity with that state, this is wisdom partaking of stability. When perceptions and attention accompanied by equanimity arise, this is wisdom partaking of distinction. When perceptions and attention accompanied by disenchantment arise, this is wisdom connected with dispassion, partaking of penetration. For an attainer of the third jhāna, when perceptions and attention accompanied by rapture and happiness arise, this is wisdom partaking of decline. When mindfulness is established in conformity with that state, this is wisdom partaking of stability. When perceptions and attention accompanied by neither-pain-nor-pleasure arise, this is wisdom partaking of distinction. When perceptions and attention accompanied by disenchantment arise, this is wisdom connected with dispassion, partaking of penetration. For an attainer of the fourth jhāna, when perceptions and attention accompanied by equanimity arise, this is wisdom partaking of decline. When mindfulness is established in conformity with that state, this is wisdom partaking of stability. When perceptions and attention accompanied by the base of the infinity of space arise, this is wisdom partaking of distinction. When perceptions and attention accompanied by disenchantment arise, this is wisdom connected with dispassion, partaking of penetration.
