For an attainer of the base of the infinity of space, when perceptions and attention accompanied by form arise, this is wisdom partaking of decline. When mindfulness is established in conformity with that state, this is wisdom partaking of stability. When perceptions and attention accompanied by the base of the infinity of consciousness arise, this is wisdom partaking of distinction. When perceptions and attention accompanied by disenchantment arise, this is wisdom connected with dispassion, partaking of penetration. For an attainer of the base of the infinity of consciousness, when perceptions and attention accompanied by the base of the infinity of space arise, this is wisdom partaking of decline. When mindfulness is established in conformity with that state, this is wisdom partaking of stability. When perceptions and attention accompanied by the base of nothingness arise, this is wisdom partaking of distinction. When perceptions and attention accompanied by disenchantment arise, this is wisdom connected with dispassion, partaking of penetration. For an attainer of the base of nothingness, when perceptions and attention accompanied by the base of the infinity of consciousness arise, this is wisdom partaking of decline. When mindfulness is established in conformity with that state, this is wisdom partaking of stability. When perceptions and attention accompanied by the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception arise, this is wisdom partaking of distinction. When perceptions and attention accompanied by disenchantment arise, this is wisdom connected with dispassion, partaking of penetration.

800. (8) Tattha katamā catasso paṭisambhidā? Atthapaṭisambhidā, dhammapaṭisambhidā, niruttipaṭisambhidā, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Atthe ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, dhamme ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, tatra dhammaniruttābhilāpe ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā, ñāṇesu ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā[T 0.0449]. Imā catasso paṭisambhidā.

800. Herein, what are the four analytical knowledges? The analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, the analytical knowledge of language, and the analytical knowledge of perspicuity. Knowledge in the meaning is the analytical knowledge of meaning. Knowledge in the Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma. Knowledge in the linguistic expression of that Dhamma is the analytical knowledge of language. Knowledge in the preceding knowledges is the analytical knowledge of perspicuity. These are the four analytical knowledges.

801. (9) Tattha katamā catasso paṭipadā? Dukkhapaṭipadā dandhābhiññā paññā, dukkhapaṭipadā khippābhiññā paññā, sukhapaṭipadā dandhābhiññā paññā, sukhapaṭipadā khippābhiññā paññā.

801. Herein, what are the four courses of practice? The wisdom of painful practice with sluggish direct knowledge, the wisdom of painful practice with quick direct knowledge, the wisdom of pleasant practice with sluggish direct knowledge, and the wisdom of pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge.

(Ka) tattha katamā dukkhapaṭipadā dandhābhiññā paññā? Kicchena [P 0.0332] kasirena samādhiṃ uppādentassa dandhaṃ taṇṭhānaṃ abhijānantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhapaṭipadā dandhābhiññā paññā”.

Herein, what is the wisdom of painful practice with sluggish direct knowledge? For one who generates concentration with difficulty and hardship and who sluggishly knows that state directly, there arises wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view. This is called 'the wisdom of painful practice with sluggish direct knowledge'.

(Kha) tattha katamā dukkhapaṭipadā khippābhiññā paññā? Kicchena kasirena samādhiṃ uppādentassa khippaṃ taṇṭhānaṃ abhijānantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “dukkhapaṭipadā khippābhiññā paññā”.

Herein, what is the wisdom of painful practice with quick direct knowledge? For one who generates concentration with difficulty and hardship but who quickly knows that state directly, there arises wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view. This is called 'the wisdom of painful practice with quick direct knowledge'.

(Ga) tattha [M 0.0345][V 0.0380] katamā sukhapaṭipadā dandhābhiññā paññā? Akicchena akasirena samādhiṃ uppādentassa dandhaṃ taṇṭhānaṃ abhijānantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “sukhapaṭipadā dandhābhiññā paññā”.

Herein, what is the wisdom of pleasant practice with sluggish direct knowledge? For one who generates concentration without difficulty and hardship and who sluggishly knows that state directly, there arises wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view. This is called 'the wisdom of pleasant practice with sluggish direct knowledge'.

(Gha) tattha katamā sukhapaṭipadā khippābhiññā paññā? Akicchena akasirena samādhiṃ uppādentassa khippaṃ taṇṭhānaṃ abhijānantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “sukhapaṭipadā khippābhiññā paññā”. Imā catasso paṭipadā.

Herein, what is the wisdom of pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge? For one who generates concentration without difficulty and hardship and who quickly has direct knowledge of that state, the wisdom that arises—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'the wisdom of pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge.' These are the four courses of practice.

802. (10) Tattha [T 0.0450] katamāni cattāri ārammaṇāni? Parittā parittārammaṇā paññā, parittā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā, appamāṇā parittārammaṇā paññā, appamāṇā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā.

802. Herein, what are the four objects? There is wisdom that is limited with a limited object, wisdom that is limited with an immeasurable object, wisdom that is immeasurable with a limited object, and wisdom that is immeasurable with an immeasurable object.

(Ka) tattha katamā parittā parittārammaṇā paññā? Samādhissa na nikāmalābhissa ārammaṇaṃ thokaṃ pharantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “parittā parittārammaṇā paññā”.

Herein, what is wisdom that is limited with a limited object? For one who does not attain concentration at will and who pervades a slight object, the wisdom that arises—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'wisdom that is limited with a limited object.'

(Kha) tattha katamā parittā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā? Samādhissa na nikāmalābhissa ārammaṇaṃ vipulaṃ pharantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “parittā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā”.

Herein, what is wisdom that is limited with an immeasurable object? For one who does not attain concentration at will and who pervades a vast object, the wisdom that arises—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'wisdom that is limited with an immeasurable object.'

(Ga) tattha katamā appamāṇā parittārammaṇā paññā? Samādhissa nikāmalābhissa ārammaṇaṃ thokaṃ pharantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati “appamāṇā parittārammaṇā paññā”.

Herein, what is wisdom that is immeasurable with a limited object? For one who attains concentration at will and who pervades a slight object, the wisdom that arises—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'wisdom that is immeasurable with a limited object.'

(Gha) tattha katamā appamāṇā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā? Samādhissa nikāmalābhissa ārammaṇaṃ vipulaṃ pharantassa yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo [P 0.0333] sammādiṭṭhi [V 0.0381] – ayaṃ vuccati “appamāṇā appamāṇārammaṇā paññā”. Imāni cattāri ārammaṇāni.

Herein, what is wisdom that is immeasurable with an immeasurable object? For one who attains concentration at will and who pervades a vast object, the wisdom that arises—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'wisdom that is immeasurable with an immeasurable object.' These are the four objects.

(11) Maggasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ jarāmaraṇepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudayepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā [T 0.0451] paṭipadāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

For one endowed with the path, this knowledge is knowledge in regard to aging and death, this knowledge is knowledge in regard to the origin of aging and death, this knowledge is knowledge in regard to the cessation of aging and death, and this knowledge is knowledge in regard to the path leading to the cessation of aging and death.

(Ka) tattha [M 0.0346] katamaṃ jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ? Jarāmaraṇaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is knowledge in regard to aging and death? The wisdom that arises taking aging and death as its object—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'knowledge in regard to aging and death.'

(Kha-gha) jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ ārabbha…pe… jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ ārabbha…pe… jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ”.

Taking the origin of aging and death as its object... taking the cessation of aging and death as its object... taking the path leading to the cessation of aging and death as its object, the wisdom that arises—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'knowledge in the path leading to the cessation of aging and death.'

803. (12-21) Dhammasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ jātiyāpetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… bhavepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādānepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… taṇhāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… vedanāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… phassepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatanepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… nāmarūpepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhāresupetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhārasamudayepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhepetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapetaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

803. For one endowed with the path, this knowledge is knowledge in regard to birth... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to existence... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to clinging... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to craving... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to feeling... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to contact... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to the six sense bases... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to name-and-form... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to consciousness... this knowledge is knowledge in regard to formations, this knowledge is knowledge in regard to the origin of formations, this knowledge is knowledge in regard to the cessation of formations, and this knowledge is knowledge in regard to the path leading to the cessation of formations.

Tattha katamaṃ saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ? Saṅkhāre ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ”.

Herein, what is knowledge in regard to formations? The wisdom that arises taking formations as its object—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'knowledge in regard to formations.'

Saṅkhārasamudayaṃ ārabbha…pe… saṅkhāranirodhaṃ ārabbha…pe… saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Evaṃ catubbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Taking the origin of formations as its object... taking the cessation of formations as its object... taking the path leading to the cessation of formations as its object, the wisdom that arises—understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is called 'knowledge in the path leading to the cessation of formations.' Thus, the ground of knowledge is fourfold.

Catukkaṃ.

The Chapter on Fours.

5. Pañcakaniddeso

5. Exposition of the Pentad

804. (1) Tattha [T 0.0452][P 0.0334][V 0.0382] katamo pañcaṅgiko sammāsamādhi? Pītipharaṇatā, sukhapharaṇatā, cetopharaṇatā, ālokapharaṇatā, paccavekkhaṇānimittaṃ. Dvīsu jhānesu paññā pītipharaṇatā. Tīsu jhānesu paññā sukhapharaṇatā. Paracitte ñāṇaṃ cetopharaṇatā. Dibbacakkhu ālokapharaṇatā. Tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhitassa paccavekkhaṇāñāṇaṃ paccavekkhaṇānimittaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati pañcaṅgiko sammāsamādhi.

804. Herein, what is right concentration with five factors? Pervasion by rapture, pervasion by happiness, pervasion of mind, pervasion by light, and the sign of reviewing. In two jhānas, wisdom is pervasion by rapture. In three jhānas, wisdom is pervasion by happiness. Knowledge of others' minds is pervasion of mind. The divine eye is pervasion by light. The knowledge of reviewing on emerging from that very concentration is the sign of reviewing. This is called right concentration with five factors.

(2) Tattha [M 0.0347] katamo pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi? “Ayaṃ samādhi paccuppannasukho ceva āyatiñca sukhavipāko”ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. “Ayaṃ samādhi ariyo nirāmiso”ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. “Ayaṃ samādhi akāpurisasevito”ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. “Ayaṃ samādhi santo paṇīto paṭippassaddhaladdho ekodibhāvādhigato na sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagato”ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. So kho panāhaṃ imaṃ samādhiṃ sato samāpajjāmi sato vuṭṭhahāmī”ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi. Evaṃ pañcavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Herein, what is right concentration with five knowledges? Knowledge arises within oneself: 'This concentration is pleasant in the present and has a pleasant result in the future.' Knowledge arises within oneself: 'This concentration is noble and unworldly.' Knowledge arises within oneself: 'This concentration is resorted to by great men.' Knowledge arises within oneself: 'This concentration is peaceful, sublime, attained through tranquility, achieved through unification, and not arrived at by striving with forcible suppression and restraint.' Knowledge arises within oneself: 'I mindfully enter this concentration and mindfully emerge from it.' This is right concentration with five knowledges. Thus, the basis of knowledge is fivefold.

Pañcakaṃ.

The Pentad.

6. Chakkaniddeso

6. Exposition of the Hexad

805. Tattha katamā chasu abhiññāsu paññā? Iddhividhe ñāṇaṃ, sotadhātuvisuddhiyā ñāṇaṃ, paracitte ñāṇaṃ, pubbenivāsānussatiyā ñāṇaṃ, sattānaṃ cutūpapāte ñāṇaṃ, āsavānaṃ khaye ñāṇaṃ – imā chasu abhiññāsu paññā. Evaṃ chabbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Herein, what is wisdom in the six direct knowledges? Knowledge of the kinds of psychic power, knowledge in the purity of the ear element, knowledge of others’ minds, knowledge of the recollection of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, knowledge of the destruction of the taints—this is wisdom in the six direct knowledges. Thus, the basis of knowledge is sixfold.

Chakkaṃ.

The Hexad.

7. Sattakaniddeso

7. Exposition of the Heptad

806. Tattha [T 0.0453][V 0.0383] katamāni sattasattati ñāṇavatthūni? Jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, atītampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, anāgatampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ. Yampissa taṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ tampi khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti ñāṇaṃ; bhavapaccayā jātīti ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādānapaccayā [P 0.0335] bhavoti ñāṇaṃ…pe… taṇhāpaccayā upādānanti ñāṇaṃ…pe… vedanāpaccayā taṇhāti ñāṇaṃ…pe… phassapaccayā vedanāti ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatanapaccayā phassoti ñāṇaṃ…pe… nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatananti ñāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇanti ñāṇaṃ…pe… avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, atītampi addhānaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, anāgatampi addhānaṃ [M 0.0348] avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ, asati avijjāya natthi saṅkhārāti ñāṇaṃ. Yampissa taṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ tampi khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti ñāṇaṃ. Imāni sattasattati ñāṇavatthūni. Evaṃ sattavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

6. Herein, what are the seventy-seven bases of knowledge? The knowledge that 'with birth as condition, aging-and-death comes to be'; the knowledge that 'when there is no birth, there is no aging-and-death'; the knowledge that 'in the past, too, with birth as condition, aging-and-death came to be'; the knowledge that 'when there was no birth, there was no aging-and-death'; the knowledge that 'in the future, too, with birth as condition, aging-and-death will come to be'; the knowledge that 'when there is no birth, there will be no aging-and-death'; and the knowledge that this knowledge of the stability of the Dhamma is also subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation. The knowledge that 'with existence as condition, birth comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with clinging as condition, existence comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with craving as condition, clinging comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with feeling as condition, craving comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with contact as condition, feeling comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with the six sense bases as condition, contact comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases come to be'… The knowledge that 'with consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with volitional formations as condition, consciousness comes to be'… The knowledge that 'with ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be'; the knowledge that 'when there is no ignorance, there are no volitional formations'; the knowledge that 'in the past, too, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations came to be'; the knowledge that 'when there was no ignorance, there were no volitional formations'; the knowledge that 'in the future, too, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations will come to be'; the knowledge that 'when there is no ignorance, there will be no volitional formations'; and the knowledge that this knowledge of the stability of the Dhamma is also subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation. These are the seventy-seven bases of knowledge. Thus, the basis of knowledge is sevenfold.

Sattakaṃ.

The Heptad.

8. Aṭṭhakaniddeso

8. Exposition of the Octad

807. Tattha katamā catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā? Sotāpattimagge paññā, sotāpattiphale paññā[T 0.0454], sakadāgāmimagge paññā, sakadāgāmiphale paññā, anāgāmimagge paññā, anāgāmiphale paññā, arahattamagge paññā, arahattaphale paññā – imā catūsu maggesu catūsu phalesu paññā. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

805. Herein, what is wisdom in the four paths and four fruits? Wisdom in the path of stream-entry, wisdom in the fruit of stream-entry, wisdom in the path of once-returning, wisdom in the fruit of once-returning, wisdom in the path of non-returning, wisdom in the fruit of non-returning, wisdom in the path of arahantship, wisdom in the fruit of arahantship—this is wisdom in the four paths and four fruits. Thus, the basis of knowledge is eightfold.

Aṭṭhakaṃ.

The Octad.

9. Navakaniddeso

9. Exposition of the Ennead

808. Tattha [V 0.0384] katamā navasu anupubbavihārasamāpattīsu paññā? Paṭhamajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, dutiyajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, tatiyajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, catutthajjhānasamāpattiyā paññā, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā paññā, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa paccavekkhaṇāñāṇaṃ – imā navasu anupubbavihārasamāpattīsu paññā. Evaṃ navavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Herein, what is wisdom in the nine successive dwelling attainments? Wisdom in the attainment of the first jhāna, wisdom in the attainment of the second jhāna, wisdom in the attainment of the third jhāna, wisdom in the attainment of the fourth jhāna, wisdom in the attainment of the base of infinite space, wisdom in the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness, wisdom in the attainment of the base of nothingness, wisdom in the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and the reviewing knowledge of one who has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling—this is wisdom in the nine successive dwelling attainments. Thus, the basis of knowledge is ninefold.

Navakaṃ.

The Ennead.

10. Dasakaniddeso

10. Exposition of the Decad

809. (1) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato “aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyya, netaṃ [P 0.0336] ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṃ sukhato upagaccheyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṃ sukhato upagaccheyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ [M 0.0349] anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci dhammaṃ atthato upagaccheyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano kañci dhammaṃ atthato upagaccheyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno [T 0.0455] puggalo mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti.

809. (1) Herein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the possible as the possible and the impossible as the impossible, as it actually is? Here, the Tathāgata understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a person accomplished in view would regard any formation as permanent—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that an ordinary person would regard any formation as permanent—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a person accomplished in view would regard any formation as pleasurable—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that an ordinary person would regard any formation as pleasurable—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a person accomplished in view would regard any phenomenon as self—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that an ordinary person would regard any phenomenon as self—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a person accomplished in view would deprive his mother of life—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that an ordinary person would deprive his mother of life—this possibility exists."

Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo pitaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya…pe… arahantaṃ [V 0.0385] jīvitā voropeyya…pe… paduṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppādeyya…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindeyya…pe… aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddiseyya…pe… aṭṭhamaṃ bhavaṃ nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puthujjano aṭṭhamaṃ bhavaṃ nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti.

He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a person accomplished in view would deprive his father of life… and so on… deprive an arahant of life… and so on… with a corrupt mind, would cause the Tathāgata’s blood to flow… and so on… would split the Saṅgha… and so on… would point to another teacher… and so on… would bring about an eighth existence—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that an ordinary person would bring about an eighth existence—this possibility exists."

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā eko arahaṃ sammāsambuddho uppajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve rājāno cakkavattī cakkavatti (sī. syā.) apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā eko rājā cakkavattī uppajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti.

He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that in one world-system two Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, would arise simultaneously—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that in one world-system one Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, would arise—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that in one world-system two wheel-turning monarchs would arise simultaneously—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that in one world-system one wheel-turning monarch would arise—this possibility exists."

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso [T 0.0456] yaṃ itthī arahaṃ assa sammāsambuddho, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso arahaṃ assa sammāsambuddho, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso rājā assa cakkavattī, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī sakkattaṃ kareyya, mārattaṃ [P 0.0337] kareyya, brahmattaṃ kareyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso sakkattaṃ kareyya, mārattaṃ kareyya, brahmattaṃ kareyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti.

He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a woman would be an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that a man would be an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a woman would be a wheel-turning monarch—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that a man would be a wheel-turning monarch—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that a woman would become Sakka, Māra, or Brahmā—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that a man would become Sakka, Māra, or Brahmā—this possibility exists."

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ [M 0.0350] anavakāso yaṃ kāyaduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyaduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīduccaritassa…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīduccaritassa…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti.

He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that from bodily misconduct a desired, pleasant, and agreeable result would be produced—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that from bodily misconduct an undesired, unpleasant, and disagreeable result would be produced—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that from verbal misconduct… and so on… that from mental misconduct a desired, pleasant, and agreeable result would be produced—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that from verbal misconduct… and so on… that from mental misconduct an undesired, unpleasant, and disagreeable result would be produced—this possibility exists."

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyasucaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyasucaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko [T 0.0457] nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīsucaritassa…pe… yaṃ manosucaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati [V 0.0386] yaṃ vacīsucaritassa…pe… yaṃ manosucaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti.

He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that from good bodily conduct an undesired, unpleasant, and disagreeable result would be produced—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that from good bodily conduct a desired, pleasant, and agreeable result would be produced—this possibility exists." He understands: "It is impossible, it is not a possibility that from good verbal conduct… and so on… that from good mental conduct an undesired, unpleasant, and disagreeable result would be produced—this possibility does not exist." He understands: "But it is indeed a possibility that from good verbal conduct… and so on… that from good mental conduct a desired, pleasant, and agreeable result would be produced—this possibility exists."

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīduccaritasamaṅgī…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīduccaritasamaṅgī…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti.

He knows: 'It is impossible, it is causeless, that one endowed with bodily misconduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world; such a case does not exist.' He knows: 'It is indeed a possible case that one endowed with bodily misconduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell; such a case exists.' He knows: 'It is impossible, it is causeless, that one endowed with verbal misconduct... or with mental misconduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world; such a case does not exist.' He knows: 'It is indeed a possible case that one endowed with verbal misconduct... or with mental misconduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell; such a case exists.'

“Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyasucaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyasucaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ [M 0.0351] saggaṃ [P 0.0338] lokaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ [T 0.0458] vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīsucaritasamaṅgī…pe… yaṃ manosucaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīsucaritasamaṅgī [V 0.0387] …pe… yaṃ manosucaritasamaṅgī tannidānaṃ tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti pajānāti. “Ye ye dhammā yesaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ hetū paccayā upādāya taṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ, ye ye dhammā yesaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ na hetū appaccayā upādāya taṃ taṃ aṭṭhāna”nti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

He knows: 'It is impossible, it is causeless, that one endowed with good bodily conduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell; such a case does not exist.' He knows: 'It is indeed a possible case that one endowed with good bodily conduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world; such a case exists.' He knows: 'It is impossible, it is causeless, that one endowed with good verbal conduct... or with good mental conduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell; such a case does not exist.' He knows: 'It is indeed a possible case that one endowed with good verbal conduct... or with good mental conduct, for that reason, on that account, with the breaking up of the body, after death, would be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world; such a case exists.' Whatever phenomena are the causes and conditions for other phenomena, based on them, that is a possible case; whatever phenomena are not causes and are without conditions for other phenomena, based on them, that is an impossible case. The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view that arise therein—this is called the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible, as it truly is.

810. (2) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato pajānāti – “atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni gatisampattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni upadhisampattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni kālasampattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni payogasampattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti.

810. (2) Therein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the result of past, future, and present undertakings of kamma, by way of possibility and cause, as it truly is? Here, the Tathāgata knows: 'There are some evil undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by excellence of destination, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by excellence of the basis of existence, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by excellence of time, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by excellence of endeavor, do not ripen.'

“Atthekaccāni [T 0.0459] pāpakāni kammasamādānāni gativipattiṃ āgamma vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni upadhivipattiṃ āgamma vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni kālavipattiṃ āgamma vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni payogavipattiṃ āgamma vipaccanti.

'There are some evil undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on a failure of destination. There are some evil undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on a failure of the basis of existence. There are some evil undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on a failure of time. There are some evil undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on a failure of endeavor.'

“Atthekaccāni kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni gativipattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni upadhivipattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni kālavipattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni payogavipattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccanti.

'There are some good undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by a failure of destination, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by a failure of the basis of existence, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by a failure of time, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of kamma that, being obstructed by a failure of endeavor, do not ripen.'

“Atthekaccāni kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni gatisampattiṃ āgamma vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni upadhisampattiṃ āgamma vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni [P 0.0339] kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni kālasampattiṃ āgamma vipaccanti. Atthekaccāni [M 0.0352] kalyāṇāni kammasamādānāni payogasampattiṃ āgamma vipaccantī”ti. Yā tattha [V 0.0388] paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

'There are some good undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on excellence of destination. There are some good undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on excellence of the basis of existence. There are some good undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on excellence of time. There are some good undertakings of kamma that ripen depending on excellence of endeavor.' The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view that arise therein—this is called the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the result of past, future, and present undertakings of kamma, by way of possibility and cause, as it truly is.

811. (3) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato “ayaṃ maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā nirayagāmī”ti nirayagāminīti (syā.) pajānāti, “ayaṃ maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tiracchānayonigāmī”ti tiracchānagāminīti (syā.) evamuparipi. aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā pajānāti, “ayaṃ maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā pettivisayagāmī”ti pajānāti, “ayaṃ maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā manussalokagāmī”ti pajānāti, “ayaṃ maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā devalokagāmī”ti pajānāti, “ayaṃ maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā nibbānagāmī”ti pajānātīti[T 0.0460]. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

811. (3) Therein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the practice leading to all destinations, as it truly is? Here, the Tathāgata knows: 'This is the path, this is the practice leading to hell.' He knows: 'This is the path, this is the practice leading to the animal realm.' He knows: 'This is the path, this is the practice leading to the realm of spirits.' He knows: 'This is the path, this is the practice leading to the human world.' He knows: 'This is the path, this is the practice leading to the celestial world.' He knows: 'This is the path, this is the practice leading to Nibbāna.' The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view that arise therein—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the practice leading to all destinations, as it truly is.

812. (4) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato khandhanānattaṃ pajānāti, āyatananānattaṃ pajānāti, dhātunānattaṃ pajānāti, anekadhātunānādhātulokanānattaṃ pajānātīti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

812. Herein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the world with its many and various elements as it really is? Here, the Tathāgata knows the diversity of aggregates, the diversity of sense bases, the diversity of elements, and the diversity of the world with its many and various elements. Whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view there is—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the world with its many and various elements as it really is.

813. (5) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato pajānāti – “santi sattā hīnādhimuttikā, santi sattā paṇītādhimuttikā. Hīnādhimuttikā sattā hīnādhimuttike satte sevanti bhajanti payirupāsanti. Paṇītādhimuttikā sattā paṇītādhimuttike satte sevanti bhajanti payirupāsanti.

813. Herein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the diversity in beings’ inclinations as it really is? Here, the Tathāgata knows: 'There are beings with inferior inclinations, and there are beings with superior inclinations. Beings with inferior inclinations associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with inferior inclinations. Beings with superior inclinations associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with superior inclinations.'

“Atītampi addhānaṃ hīnādhimuttikā sattā hīnādhimuttike satte seviṃsu bhajiṃsu payirupāsiṃsu, paṇītādhimuttikā sattā paṇītādhimuttike satte seviṃsu bhajiṃsu payirupāsiṃsu.

In the past, too, beings with inferior inclinations associated with, frequented, and attended upon beings with inferior inclinations; and beings with superior inclinations associated with, frequented, and attended upon beings with superior inclinations.

“Anāgatampi addhānaṃ hīnādhimuttikā sattā hīnādhimuttike satte sevissanti bhajissanti payirupāsissanti, paṇītādhimuttikā sattā paṇītādhimuttike [M 0.0353] satte [P 0.0340] sevissanti bhajissanti payirupāsissantī”ti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

In the future, too, beings with inferior inclinations will associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with inferior inclinations; and beings with superior inclinations will associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with superior inclinations.” Whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view there is—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the diversity in beings’ inclinations as it really is.

814. (6) Tattha [T 0.0461][V 0.0389] katamaṃ tathāgatassa parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato sattānaṃ āsayaṃ pajānāti, anusayaṃ pajānāti, caritaṃ pajānāti, adhimuttiṃ pajānāti, apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye bhabbābhabbe satte pajānāti.

814. Herein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of the faculties of other beings and other persons as it really is? Here, the Tathāgata knows the dispositions of beings, their underlying tendencies, their character, and their inclinations; he knows beings as being with little dust or much dust, with keen faculties or dull faculties, with good qualities or bad qualities, easy to teach or difficult to teach, and capable or incapable.

815. Katamo ca sattānaṃ āsayo? “Sassato loko”ti vā, “asassato loko”ti vā, “antavā loko”ti vā, “anantavā loko”ti vā, “taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra”nti vā, “aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra”nti vā, “hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, “na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti vā, “hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti vā, “neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti vā, iti bhavadiṭṭhisannissitā vā sattā honti vibhavadiṭṭhisannissitā vā. Ete vā pana ubho ante anupagamma idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu anulomikā khanti paṭiladdhā hoti yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ. Ayaṃ sattānaṃ āsayo.

815. And what is the disposition of beings? Some hold: ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’ or ‘The world is finite,’ or ‘The world is infinite,’ or ‘The soul and the body are the same,’ or ‘The soul is one thing and the body another,’ or ‘A Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘A Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘A Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ Thus, beings are reliant on the view of existence or reliant on the view of non-existence. But some, without approaching either of these two extremes, have obtained conformable acceptance and knowledge as it really is concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently from this conditionality. This is the disposition of beings.

816. Katamo ca sattānaṃ anusayo? Sattānusayā – kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo, mānānusayo, diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo. Yaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ ettha sattānaṃ rāgānusayo anuseti. Yaṃ loke appiyarūpaṃ asātarūpaṃ ettha sattānaṃ paṭighānusayo anuseti. Iti imesu dvīsu dhammesu avijjānupatitā. Tadekaṭṭho māno ca diṭṭhi ca vicikicchā ca daṭṭhabbā. Ayaṃ sattānaṃ anusayo.

816. And what are the underlying tendencies of beings? There are seven underlying tendencies: the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to lust for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance. In regard to what is agreeable and pleasant in the world, the underlying tendency to lust lies latent in beings. In regard to what is disagreeable and unpleasant in the world, the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent in beings. Thus, in regard to these two things, ignorance is involved. Conceit, views, and doubt are to be understood as being of a single nature with that. This is the underlying tendency of beings.

817. Katamañca sattānaṃ caritaṃ? Puññābhisaṅkhāro, apuññābhisaṅkhāro[T 0.0462], āneñjābhisaṅkhāro, parittabhūmako vā mahābhūmako vā – idaṃ sattānaṃ caritaṃ.

817. And what is the character of beings? Meritorious formations, demeritorious formations, imperturbable formations; and whether of a limited plane or a lofty plane—this is the character of beings.

818. Katamā [M 0.0354] ca sattānaṃ adhimutti? Santi sattā hīnādhimuttikā, santi sattā paṇītādhimuttikā. Hīnādhimuttikā sattā hīnādhimuttike satte sevanti bhajanti [P 0.0341] payirupāsanti. Paṇītādhimuttikā sattā paṇītādhimuttike satte sevanti bhajanti payirupāsanti.

818. And what is the inclination of beings? There are beings with inferior inclinations, and there are beings with superior inclinations. Beings with inferior inclinations associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with inferior inclinations. Beings with superior inclinations associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with superior inclinations.

Atītampi [V 0.0390] addhānaṃ hīnādhimuttikā sattā hīnādhimuttike satte seviṃsu bhajiṃsu payirupāsiṃsu. Paṇītādhimuttikā sattā paṇītādhimuttike satte seviṃsu bhajiṃsu payirupāsiṃsu.

In the past, too, beings with inferior inclinations associated with, frequented, and attended upon beings with inferior inclinations; and beings with superior inclinations associated with, frequented, and attended upon beings with superior inclinations.

Anāgatampi addhānaṃ hīnādhimuttikā sattā hīnādhimuttike satte sevissanti bhajissanti payirupāsissanti. Paṇītādhimuttikā sattā paṇītādhimuttike satte sevissanti bhajissanti payirupāsissanti. Ayaṃ sattānaṃ adhimutti.

In the future, too, beings with inferior inclinations will associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with inferior inclinations; and beings with superior inclinations will associate with, frequent, and attend upon beings with superior inclinations. This is the inclination of beings.

819. Katame te sattā mahārajakkhā? Dasa kilesavatthūni – lobho, doso, moho, māno, diṭṭhi, vicikicchā, thinaṃ, uddhaccaṃ, ahirikaṃ, anottappaṃ. Yesaṃ sattānaṃ imāni dasa kilesavatthūni āsevitāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni ussadagatāni, ime te sattā mahārajakkhā.

819. Which are the beings with much dust? There are ten bases of defilement: greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, views, doubt, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and lack of moral dread. Those beings in whom these ten bases of defilement are pursued, developed, cultivated, and have become abundant—these are the beings with much dust.

820. Katame te sattā apparajakkhā? Yesaṃ sattānaṃ imāni dasa kilesavatthūni anāsevitāni abhāvitāni abahulīkatāni anussadagatāni, ime te sattā apparajakkhā.

820. Which are the beings with little dust? Those beings in whom these ten bases of defilement are not pursued, not developed, not cultivated, and have not become abundant—these are the beings with little dust.

821. Katame te sattā mudindriyā? Pañcindriyāni – saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ. Yesaṃ sattānaṃ imāni pañcindriyāni anāsevitāni abhāvitāni abahulīkatāni anussadagatāni, ime [T 0.0463] te sattā mudindriyā.

821. Which are the beings with dull faculties? The five faculties are: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. Those beings in whom these five faculties are not pursued, not developed, not cultivated, and have not become abundant—these are the beings with dull faculties.

822. Katame te sattā tikkhindriyā? Yesaṃ sattānaṃ imāni pañcindriyāni āsevitāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni ussadagatāni, ime te sattā tikkhindriyā.

822. Which are the beings with keen faculties? Those beings in whom these five faculties are pursued, developed, cultivated, and have become abundant—these are the beings with keen faculties.

823. Katame [M 0.0355] te sattā dvākārā? Ye te sattā pāpāsayā pāpānusayā pāpacaritā pāpādhimuttikā mahārajakkhā mudindriyā, ime te sattā dvākārā.

823. Which are the beings with bad qualities? Those beings who have a bad disposition, bad underlying tendencies, a bad character, and bad inclinations, who are with much dust and with dull faculties—these are the beings with bad qualities.

824. Katame te sattā svākārā? Ye te sattā kalyāṇāsayā kalyāṇacaritā kalyāṇādhimuttikā apparajakkhā tikkhindriyā, ime te sattā svākārā.

824. Which are the beings with good qualities? Those beings who have a good disposition, a good character, and good inclinations, who are with little dust and with keen faculties—these are the beings with good qualities.

825. Katame [V 0.0391] te sattā duviññāpayā? Ye ca te sattā dvākārā, teva te sattā duviññāpayā. Ye ca te sattā svākārā, teva te sattā suviññāpayā.

825. Which are the beings who are difficult to instruct? Those beings who have bad qualities are the very beings who are difficult to instruct. And those beings who have good qualities are the very beings who are easy to instruct.

826. Katame te sattā abhabbā? Ye te sattā kammāvaraṇena samannāgatā kilesāvaraṇena samannāgatā vipākāvaraṇena samannāgatā assaddhā acchandikā duppaññā abhabbā niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṃ, ime te sattā abhabbā.

826. Which are the beings who are incapable? Those beings who are endowed with the obstruction of kamma, with the obstruction of defilements, and with the obstruction of results, who are faithless, lack desire, are of little wisdom, and are incapable of entering the path of certainty, the path of rightness, in wholesome states—these are the beings who are incapable.

827. Katame [P 0.0342] te sattā bhabbā? Ye te sattā na kammāvaraṇena samannāgatā na kilesāvaraṇena samannāgatā na vipākāvaraṇena samannāgatā saddhā chandikā paññavanto bhabbā niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṃ, ime te sattā bhabbāti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

827. Which are the beings who are capable? Those beings who are not endowed with the obstruction of kamma, not with the obstruction of defilements, and not with the obstruction of results, who are faithful, have desire, are wise, and are capable of entering the path of certainty, the path of rightness, in wholesome states—these are the beings who are capable. The wisdom that is there, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the maturity of the faculties of other beings and other individuals as it truly is.

828. (7) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ [T 0.0464] vodānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Jhāyīti. Cattāro jhāyī. Atthekacco jhāyī sampattiyeva sampattiyeva (ka.) samānaṃ vipattīti pacceti, atthekacco jhāyī vipattiṃyeva vipattiyeva (ka.) samānaṃ sampattīti pacceti, atthekacco jhāyī sampattiyeva samānaṃ sampattīti pacceti, atthekacco jhāyī vipattiyeva samānaṃ vipattīti pacceti – ime cattāro jhāyī.

828. Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge of the defilement, purification, and emergence of the absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments as it truly is? 'Meditator.' There are four meditators. There is a certain meditator who, being in a state of attainment, perceives it as a failure. There is a certain meditator who, being in a state of failure, perceives it as an attainment. There is a certain meditator who, being in a state of attainment, perceives it as an attainment. There is a certain meditator who, being in a state of failure, perceives it as a failure. These are the four meditators.

Aparepi cattāro jhāyī. Atthekacco jhāyī dandhaṃ samāpajjati khippaṃ vuṭṭhāti, atthekacco jhāyī khippaṃ samāpajjati dandhaṃ vuṭṭhāti, atthekacco jhāyī [M 0.0356] dandhaṃ samāpajjati dandhaṃ vuṭṭhāti, atthekacco jhāyī khippaṃ samāpajjati khippaṃ vuṭṭhāti – ime cattāro jhāyī.

There are also another four meditators. There is a certain meditator who enters concentration slowly and emerges quickly. There is a certain meditator who enters quickly and emerges slowly. There is a certain meditator who enters slowly and emerges slowly. There is a certain meditator who enters quickly and emerges quickly. These are the four meditators.

Aparepi cattāro jhāyī. Atthekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo; atthekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo; atthekacco jhāyī samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo ca hoti, samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo ca; atthekacco jhāyī neva samādhismiṃ samādhikusalo hoti, na samādhismiṃ samāpattikusalo – ime cattāro jhāyī.

There are also another four meditators. There is a certain meditator who is skilled in concentration but not skilled in the attainment of concentration. There is a certain meditator who is skilled in the attainment of concentration but not skilled in concentration. There is a certain meditator who is skilled in both concentration and the attainment of concentration. There is a certain meditator who is skilled in neither concentration nor the attainment of concentration. These are the four meditators.

“Jhāna”nti[V 0.0392]. Cattāri jhānāni – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ.

'Absorption.' There are four absorptions: the first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, and the fourth absorption.

“Vimokkho”ti. Aṭṭha vimokkhā. Rūpī rūpāni passati – ayaṃ paṭhamo vimokkho.

'Liberation.' There are eight liberations. (1) Possessing form, one sees forms: this is the first liberation.

Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati – ayaṃ dutiyo vimokkho.

(2) Perceiving the formless internally, one sees forms externally: this is the second liberation.

Subhanteva adhimutto hoti – ayaṃ tatiyo vimokkho.

(3) One is resolved only on the beautiful: this is the third liberation.

Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā “ananto [T 0.0465] ākāso”ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ catuttho vimokkho.

(4) With the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, perceiving ‘space is infinite,’ one enters and abides in the base of infinite space: this is the fourth liberation.

Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma “anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ pañcamo vimokkho.

(5) By completely surmounting the base of infinite space, perceiving ‘consciousness is infinite,’ one enters and abides in the base of infinite consciousness: this is the fifth liberation.

Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma [P 0.0343] “natthi kiñci”ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ chaṭṭho vimokkho.

(6) By completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness, perceiving ‘there is nothing,’ one enters and abides in the base of nothingness: this is the sixth liberation.

Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ sattamo vimokkho.

(7) By completely surmounting the base of nothingness, one enters and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception: this is the seventh liberation.

Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho.

(8) By completely surmounting the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling: this is the eighth liberation.

“Samādhī”ti. Tayo samādhī – savitakkasavicāro samādhi, avitakkavicāramatto samādhi, avitakkaavicāro samādhi.

'Concentration.' There are three kinds of concentration: concentration with applied thought and sustained thought; concentration without applied thought but with only sustained thought; and concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought.

“Samāpattī”ti[M 0.0357][V 0.0393]. Nava anupubbavihārasamāpattiyo – paṭhamajjhānasamāpatti, dutiyajjhānasamāpatti, tatiyajjhānasamāpatti, catutthajjhānasamāpatti, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpatti, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpatti, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpatti, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpatti, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti.

“Attainment.” The nine successive abiding-attainments are: the attainment of the first jhāna, the attainment of the second jhāna, the attainment of the third jhāna, the attainment of the fourth jhāna, the attainment of the base of infinite space, the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness, the attainment of the base of nothingness, the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.

“Saṃkilesa”nti hānabhāgiyo dhammo. “Vodāna”nti visesabhāgiyo dhammo. “Vuṭṭhāna”nti. Vodānampi vuṭṭhānaṃ, tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhānampi vuṭṭhānanti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

“Defilement” is a state partaking of decline. “Purification” is a state partaking of distinction. “Emergence”: purification is also emergence, and emerging from each particular concentration is also emergence. The wisdom that is there, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge as it truly is of the defilement, purification, and emergence in regard to the jhānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments.

829. (8) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa pubbenivāsānussati yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ[T 0.0466]? Idha tathāgato anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe “amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno”ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaratīti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa pubbenivāsānussati yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

829. Therein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the recollection of past abodes as it actually is? Here, the Tathāgata recollects his manifold past abodes, that is: one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many eons of contraction, many eons of expansion, many eons of contraction and expansion: ‘There I was so-named, of such a clan, with such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span. Passing away from there, I was reborn elsewhere. There, too, I was so-named, of such a clan, with such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span. Passing away from there, I have been reborn here.’ Thus he recollects his manifold past abodes with their aspects and details. The wisdom that is there, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the recollection of past abodes as it actually is.

830. (9) Tattha [P 0.0344] katamaṃ tathāgatassa sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – “ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena [M 0.0358] samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ [T 0.0467] upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto [V 0.0394] sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā”ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānātīti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

830. Therein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it actually is? Here, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, the Tathāgata sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate—and he understands beings as faring according to their kamma: ‘Indeed, venerable sirs, these beings were endowed with misconduct of body, speech, and mind, were revilers of the noble ones, held wrong view, and undertook actions based on wrong view. With the breakup of the body, after death, they have been reborn in the plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a state of ruin, in hell. Or, indeed, venerable sirs, these beings were endowed with good conduct of body, speech, and mind, were not revilers of the noble ones, held right view, and undertook actions based on right view. With the breakup of the body, after death, they have been reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world.’ Thus with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate—and he understands beings as faring according to their kamma. The wisdom that is there, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it actually is.

831. (10) Tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa āsavānaṃ khayaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatīti. Yā tattha paññā pajānanā…pe… amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ tathāgatassa āsavānaṃ khayaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇanti.

831. Therein, what is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it actually is? Here, through the destruction of the taints, the Tathāgata, in this very life, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, enters and abides in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. The wisdom that is there, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—this is the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it actually is.

Dasakaṃ.

The Decad.

Ñāṇavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of Knowledge is concluded.

The Decads.

842. Aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni ajjhattikassa upādāya, aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni bāhirassa [V 0.0400] upādāya, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni honti. Iti atītāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, anāgatāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, paccuppannāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā aṭṭha taṇhāvicaritasataṃ hoti. Yāni ca dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle veyyākaraṇe vuttāni bhagavatā.

842. There are eighteen courses of craving dependent on what is internal and eighteen courses of craving dependent on what is external; when these are gathered and condensed, they become thirty-six courses of craving. Thus there are thirty-six courses of craving in the past, thirty-six in the future, and thirty-six in the present; when these are gathered and condensed, they become one hundred and eight courses of craving. And there are the sixty-two views spoken of by the Blessed One in the exposition of the Brahmajāla.

Mātikā.

The Table of Contents.

1. Ekakaniddeso

1. Exposition of the Monads

(1) Jātimado

(1) Intoxication with birth

843. Tattha [M 0.0363][P 0.0350] katamo jātimado? Jātiṃ paṭicca mado majjanā majjitattaṃ māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo uṇṇati uṇṇāmo (syā. ka.) dha. sa. 1121 dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “jātimado”.

843. Herein, what is intoxication with birth? Dependent on birth, there is intoxication, being intoxicated, the state of being intoxicated, conceit, conceiving, the state of conceiving, arrogance, haughtiness, a banner, self-exaltation, and the mind's desire for prominence—this is called 'intoxication with birth'.

(2-27) Gottamadādī

(2-27) Intoxication with lineage, etc.

844. Tattha katamo gottamado? Gottaṃ paṭicca…pe… ārogyaṃ paṭicca…pe… yobbanaṃ paṭicca…pe… jīvitaṃ paṭicca…pe… lābhaṃ [T 0.0472] paṭicca…pe… sakkāraṃ paṭicca…pe… garukāraṃ paṭicca…pe… purekkhāraṃ paṭicca…pe… parivāraṃ paṭicca…pe… bhogaṃ paṭicca…pe… vaṇṇaṃ paṭicca…pe… sutaṃ paṭicca…pe… paṭibhānaṃ paṭicca…pe… rattaññutaṃ paṭicca…pe… piṇḍapātikattaṃ paṭicca…pe… anavaññātaṃ paṭicca…pe… iriyāpathaṃ paṭicca…pe… iddhiṃ paṭicca…pe… yasaṃ paṭicca…pe… sīlaṃ paṭicca…pe… jhānaṃ paṭicca…pe… sippaṃ paṭicca…pe… ārohaṃ paṭicca…pe… pariṇāhaṃ paṭicca…pe… saṇṭhānaṃ paṭicca…pe… pāripūriṃ paṭicca [V 0.0401] mado majjanā majjitattaṃ māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “pāripūrimado”.

844. Herein, what is intoxication with lineage? Dependent on lineage… and so on… dependent on health… and so on… dependent on youth… and so on… dependent on long life… and so on… dependent on gain… and so on… dependent on honor… and so on… dependent on respect… and so on… dependent on being foremost… and so on… dependent on retinue… and so on… dependent on wealth… and so on… dependent on appearance… and so on… dependent on learning… and so on… dependent on intelligence… and so on… dependent on seniority… and so on… dependent on being an alms-food-eater… and so on… dependent on not being despised… and so on… dependent on deportment… and so on… dependent on psychic power… and so on… dependent on fame… and so on… dependent on virtue… and so on… dependent on jhāna… and so on… dependent on craft… and so on… dependent on height… and so on… dependent on breadth… and so on… dependent on figure… and so on… dependent on completeness: intoxication, being intoxicated, the state of being intoxicated, conceit, conceiving, the state of conceiving, arrogance, haughtiness, a banner, self-exaltation, and the mind's desire for prominence—this is called 'intoxication with completeness'.

(28) Mado

(28) Intoxication

845. Tattha katamo mado? Yo mado majjanā majjitattaṃ māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “mado”.

845. Herein, what is intoxication? Whatever is intoxication, being intoxicated, the state of being intoxicated; conceit, conceiving, the state of conceiving; arrogance, haughtiness; a banner, self-exaltation, and the mind's desire for prominence—this is called 'intoxication.'

(29) Pamādo

(29) Heedlessness

846. Tattha katamo pamādo? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppadānaṃ kusalānaṃ vā dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo, yo evarūpo pamādo pamajjanā pamajjitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati [T 0.0473] “pamādo”.

846. Herein, what is heedlessness? The letting loose of the mind in regard to bodily, verbal, or mental misconduct, or in regard to the five strands of sensual pleasure; the giving of it free rein; and, in the development of wholesome states, lack of thoroughness, lack of perseverance, lack of steadfastness, sluggish conduct, the abandoning of enthusiasm, the abandoning of the burden, non-cultivation, non-development, infrequent practice, lack of determination, lack of application, and heedlessness. Whatever heedlessness of such a kind, being heedless, the state of being heedless—this is called 'heedlessness.'

(30) Thambho

(30) Rigidity

847. Tattha katamo thambho? Yo thambho thambhanā thambhitattaṃ kakkhaḷiyaṃ phārusiyaṃ ujucittatā amudutā – ayaṃ vuccati “thambho”.

847. Herein, what is rigidity? Whatever is rigidity, being rigid, the state of being rigid; hardness, harshness, inflexibility of mind, and lack of pliancy—this is called 'rigidity.'

(31) Sārambho

(31) Contentiousness

848. Tattha [M 0.0364] katamo sārambho? Yo sārambho paṭisārambho sārambhanā paṭisārambhanā paṭisārambhitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “sārambho”.

848. Herein, what is contentiousness? Whatever is contentiousness, rivalry, being contentious, being rivalrous, the state of being rivalrous—this is called 'contentiousness.'

(32) Atricchatā

(32) Excessive Desire

849. Tattha katamā atricchatā? Itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi [V 0.0402] pañcahi vā kāmaguṇehi asantuṭṭhassa bhiyyokamyatā[P 0.0351], yā evarūpā icchā icchāgatā atricchatā rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “atricchatā”.

849. Herein, what is excessive desire? The desire for more on the part of one who is discontented with whatever kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal provisions for the sick, or with the five sensual pleasures. Whatever desire of such a kind, being desirous, excessive desire, lust, intense lust, intense lust of the mind—this is called 'excessive desire.'

(33) Mahicchatā

(33) Great Desire

850. Tattha katamā mahicchatā? Itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi pañcahi vā kāmaguṇehi asantuṭṭhassa bhiyyokamyatā, yā evarūpā icchā icchāgatā mahicchatā rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “mahicchatā”.

850. Herein, what is great desire? The desire for more on the part of one who is discontented with whatever kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal provisions for the sick, or with the five sensual pleasures. Whatever desire of such a kind, being desirous, great desire, lust, intense lust, intense lust of the mind—this is called 'great desire.'

(34) Pāpicchatā

(34) Evil Desire

851. Tattha katamā pāpicchatā? Idhekacco assaddho samāno “saddhoti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, dussīlo samāno “sīlavāti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, appassuto samāno “bahussutoti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, saṅgaṇikārāmo samāno “pavivittoti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, kusīto samāno “āraddhavīriyoti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, muṭṭhassatī samāno “upaṭṭhitassatīti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, asamāhito samāno “samāhitoti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, duppañño [T 0.0474] samāno “paññavāti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati, akhīṇāsavo samāno “khīṇāsavoti maṃ jano jānātū”ti icchati – yā evarūpā icchā icchāgatā pāpicchatā rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “pāpicchatā”.

851. Herein, what is evil desire? Here, a certain person, being faithless, wishes, 'May people know me as faithful'; being immoral, they wish, 'May people know me as virtuous'; having little learning, they wish, 'May people know me as very learned'; delighting in company, they wish, 'May people know me as secluded'; being lazy, they wish, 'May people know me as energetic'; being muddled in mindfulness, they wish, 'May people know me as having mindfulness established'; being unconcentrated, they wish, 'May people know me as concentrated'; being unwise, they wish, 'May people know me as wise'; not being one whose taints are destroyed, they wish, 'May people know me as one whose taints are destroyed.' Whatever desire of such a kind, being desirous, evil desire, lust, intense lust, intense lust of the mind—this is called 'evil desire.'

(35) Siṅgaṃ

(35) Cunning

852. Tattha katamaṃ siṅgaṃ? Yaṃ siṅgaṃ siṅgāratā cāturatā cāturiyaṃ parikkhattatā pārikkhattiyaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “siṅgaṃ”.

852. Herein, what is cunning? Whatever is cunning, being cunning; cleverness, craftiness; being entrenched, the state of being entrenched—this is called 'cunning.'

(36) Tintiṇaṃ

(36) Disparagement

853. Tattha [V 0.0403] katamaṃ tintiṇaṃ? Yaṃ tintiṇaṃ tintiṇāyanā tintiṇāyitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā sādhukamyatā – idaṃ vuccati “tintiṇaṃ”.

853. Herein, what is disparagement? Whatever is disparagement, the act of disparaging, the state of being disparaging; greediness, the act of being greedy, the state of being greedy; sycophancy, desire for praise—this is called 'disparagement.'

(37) Cāpalyaṃ

(37) Frivolity

854. Tattha [M 0.0365] katamaṃ cāpalyaṃ? Cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanā imassa vā pūtikāyassa bāhirānaṃ vā parikkhārānaṃ maṇḍanā vibhūsanā keḷanā parikeḷanā giddhikatā giddhikattaṃ capalatā cāpalyaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “cāpalyaṃ”.

854. Herein, what is frivolity? The adorning of robes, the adorning of the bowl, the adorning of the lodging; the adorning and embellishing of this putrid body or of external requisites; play, playfulness, the state of being playful; fickleness, frivolity—this is called 'frivolity.'

(38) Asabhāgavutti

(38) Improper Conduct

855. Tattha katamaṃ asabhāgavutti? Mātari vā pitari vā jeṭṭhe vā bhātari vā ācariyesu vā upajjhāye vā buddhe vā sāvakesu vā aññataraññataresu garuṭṭhāniyesu vippaṭikūlaggāhitā vipaccanīkasātatā anādariyaṃ [P 0.0352] anādariyatā agāravatā appatissavatā – ayaṃ vuccati “asabhāgavutti”.

855. Herein, what is improper conduct? It is the adoption of a contrary attitude, continuous opposition, disrespect, the state of being disrespectful, irreverence, and lack of deference towards one's mother, father, elder brother, teachers, preceptor, the Buddha, his disciples, or any other person deserving of respect. This is called 'improper conduct.'

(39) Arati

(39) Discontent

856. Tattha katamā arati? Pantesu vā senāsanesu aññataraññataresu vā adhikusalesu dhammesu arati aratitā anabhirati anabhiramaṇā ukkaṇṭhitā [T 0.0475] paritassitā – ayaṃ vuccati “arati”.

856. Herein, what is discontent? In regard to remote lodgings or to any of various highly wholesome states, it is discontent, the state of being discontented; dissatisfaction, not taking delight; weariness, and agitation—this is called 'discontent.'

(40) Tandī

(40) Lethargy

857. Tattha katamā tandī? Yā tandī tandiyanā tandimanakatā ālasyaṃ ālasyāyanā ālasyāyitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “tandī”.

857. Herein, what is lethargy? Whatever lethargy, being lethargic, a lethargic state; laziness, being lazy, a state of laziness—this is called 'lethargy'.

(41) Vijambhitā

(41) Stretching

858. Tattha [V 0.0404] katamā vijambhitā? Yā kāyassa jambhanā vijambhanā ānamanā vinamanā sannamanā paṇamanā byādhiyakaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vijambhitā”.

858. Herein, what is stretching? Whatever stretching of the body, stretching out, bending forward, bending backward, stooping, bowing down, physical malaise—this is called 'stretching'.

(42) Bhattasammado

(42) Drowsiness After a Meal

859. Tattha katamo bhattasammado? Yā bhuttāvissa bhattamucchā bhattakilamatho bhattapariḷāho kāyaduṭṭhullaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “bhattasammado”.

859. Herein, what is drowsiness after a meal? For one who has eaten, whatever stupor from food, weariness from food, burning from food, and bodily sluggishness—this is called 'drowsiness after a meal'.

(43) Cetaso ca līnattaṃ

(43) And Sluggishness of Mind

860. Tattha katamaṃ cetaso ca līnattaṃ? Yā cittassa akalyatā akammaññatā olīyanā sallīyanā līnaṃ līyanā līyitattaṃ thinaṃ thīyanā thīyitattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati “cetaso ca līnattaṃ”.

860. Herein, what is sluggishness of mind? Whatever unfitness of mind, unwieldiness, shrinking, utter shrinking, sluggishness, being sluggish, the state of being sluggish; stiffness, being stiff, the state of being stiff of mind—this is called 'and sluggishness of mind'.

(44) Kuhanā

(44) Deceit

861. Tattha katamā kuhanā? Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa paccayapaṭisevanasaṅkhātena paccayapaṭisedhanasaṅkhātena (sī.) vā sāmantajappitena vā iriyāpathassa vā aṭhapanā āṭhapanā (ka.) ṭhapanā saṇṭhapanā bhākuṭitā bhākuṭiyaṃ kuhanā kuhāyanā kuhitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kuhanā”.

861. Herein, what is deceit? In the case of one dependent on gain, honor, and renown, one of evil desires, overcome by wishes: whatever scheming in the use of requisites, or insinuating talk, or the composing, maintaining, or establishing of a posture; whatever scowling, making a scowl, deceit, deceiving, state of deceit—this is called 'deceit'.

(45) Lapanā

(45) Flattery

862. Tattha [M 0.0366] katamā lapanā? Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā anuppiyabhāṇitā cāṭukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭayatā – ayaṃ vuccati “lapanā”.

862. Herein, what is flattery? In the case of one dependent on gain, honor, and renown, one of evil desires, overcome by wishes: whatever ingratiating speech to others, chattering, coaxing, extolling, greatly extolling, entangling speech, greatly entangling speech, praising, greatly praising, endearing speech, adulation, speech like bean soup, and coddling children—this is called 'flattery'.

(46) Nemittikatā

(46) Hinting

863. Tattha [T 0.0476][V 0.0405] katamā nemittikatā? Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa [P 0.0353] yaṃ paresaṃ nimittaṃ nimittakammaṃ obhāso obhāsakammaṃ sāmantajappā parikathā – ayaṃ vuccati “nemittikatā”.

863. Herein, what is hinting? In the case of one dependent on gain, honor, and renown, one of evil desires, overcome by wishes: whatever hinting at others, the act of making a hint, making an allusion, the act of making an allusion, talking around the subject, and circumlocution—this is called 'hinting'.

(47) Nippesikatā

(47) Disparagement

864. Tattha katamā nippesikatā? Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa yā paresaṃ akkosanā vambhanā garahaṇā ukkhepanā samukkhepanā khipanā saṅkhipanā pāpanā sampāpanā avaṇṇahārikā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā – ayaṃ vuccati “nippesikatā”.

864. Herein, what is disparagement? In the case of one dependent on gain, honor, and renown, one of evil desires, overcome by wishes: whatever reviling of others, disparaging, reproaching, dismissal, thorough dismissal, scorning, severely scorning, debasing, thoroughly debasing, carrying tales of dispraise, and backbiting—this is called 'disparagement'.

(48) Lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatā

(48) Pursuit of Gain with Gain

865. Tattha katamā lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatā? Lābhasakkārasilokasannissito pāpiccho icchāpakato ito laddhaṃ āmisaṃ amutra harati amutra vā laddhaṃ āmisaṃ idha āharati, yā evarūpā āmisassa eṭṭhi gaveṭṭhi pariyeṭṭhi esanā gavesanā pariyesanā – ayaṃ vuccati “lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatā”.

865. Herein, what is the pursuit of gain with gain? One dependent on gain, honor, and renown, one of evil desires, overcome by wishes, takes material gain obtained here and brings it there, or takes material gain obtained there and brings it here. Whatever such desiring, seeking, thoroughly seeking, searching, searching out, and thoroughly searching for material gain—this is called 'the pursuit of gain with gain'.

(49) Seyyohamasmīti māno
