(49) The Conceit 'I Am Better'

866. Tattha katamo seyyohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vijjaṭṭhānena (syā.) vā sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā mānaṃ jappeti, yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “seyyohamasmīti māno”.

866. Herein, what is the conceit 'I am better'? Here, someone, on the basis of birth, clan, family status, beauty of complexion, wealth, recitation, field of work, field of craft, branch of knowledge, learning, quick-wittedness, or some other reason whatsoever, generates conceit. Whatever such conceit, conceiving, a state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, a flag, self-exaltation, and a desire for prominence of the mind—this is called 'the conceit "I am better"'.

(50) Sadisohamasmīti māno

(50) The Conceit 'I Am Equal'

867. Tattha [T 0.0477][V 0.0406] katamo sadisohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vā [M 0.0367] sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā mānaṃ jappeti, yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “sadisohamasmīti māno”.

867. Herein, what is the conceit 'I am equal'? Here, someone, on the basis of birth, clan, family status, beauty of complexion, wealth, recitation, field of work, field of craft, branch of knowledge, learning, quick-wittedness, or some other reason whatsoever, generates conceit. Whatever such conceit, conceiving, a state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, a flag, self-exaltation, and a desire for prominence of the mind—this is called 'the conceit "I am equal"'.

(51) Hīnohamasmīti māno

(51) The Conceit 'I Am Inferior'

868. Tattha katamo hīnohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vā sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā omānaṃ jappeti, yo evarūpo omāno omaññanā omaññitattaṃ hīḷanā ohīḷanā ohīḷitattaṃ attuññā attavaññā attaparibhavo – ayaṃ vuccati “hīnohamasmīti māno”.

868. Herein, what is the conceit 'I am inferior'? Here, someone, on the basis of birth, clan, family status, beauty of complexion, wealth, recitation, field of work, field of craft, branch of knowledge, learning, quick-wittedness, or some other reason whatsoever, generates self-disparagement. Whatever such self-disparagement, thinking little of oneself, the state of thinking little of oneself, despising, looking down upon, the state of looking down upon, self-reproach, self-contempt, self-scorn—this is called 'the conceit "I am inferior"'.

(52) Seyyassa seyyohamasmīti māno

(52) The Conceit ‘I Am Better Than a Superior’

869. Tattha [P 0.0354] katamo seyyassa seyyohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco seyyo hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vā sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi seyyaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya mānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati [T 0.0478] unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “seyyassa seyyohamasmīti māno”.

869. Herein, what is the conceit ‘I am better than a superior’? Here, someone is superior by birth, clan, family status, beauty of complexion, wealth, recitation, field of work, field of craft, branch of knowledge, learning, quick-wittedness, or by some other reason whatsoever; he regards himself as superior to others. Relying on that, he generates conceit. Whatever in such a case is the conceit, conceiving, a state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, a flag, self-exaltation, and a desire for prominence of the mind—this is called the conceit ‘I am better than a superior’.

(53) Seyyassa sadisohamasmīti māno

(53) The Conceit ‘I Am Equal to a Superior’

870. Tattha katamo seyyassa sadisohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco seyyo hoti jātiyā [V 0.0407] vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vā sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi sadisaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya mānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “seyyassa sadisohamasmīti māno”.

870. Therein, what is the conceit of a superior person, ‘I am equal’? Here, a certain person is superior by birth, clan, noble birth, beauty of complexion, wealth, recitation, field of work, field of craft, branch of knowledge, learning, or quick-wittedness, or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as equal to others. Relying on that, he generates conceit. Whatever conceit of such a kind, conceiving, the state of having conceived, loftiness, haughtiness, a banner, extolling, the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called the conceit of a superior person, ‘I am equal’.

(54) Seyyassa hīnohamasmīti māno

(54) The conceit of a superior person, ‘I am inferior’

871. Tattha katamo seyyassa hīnohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco seyyo hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā [M 0.0368] vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vā sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi hīnaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya omānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo omāno omaññanā omaññitattaṃ hīḷanā ohīḷanā ohīḷitattaṃ attuññā attavaññā attaparibhavo – ayaṃ vuccati “seyyassa hīnohamasmīti māno”.

871. Therein, what is the conceit of a superior person, ‘I am inferior’? Here, a certain person is superior by birth, clan, noble birth, beauty of complexion, wealth, recitation, field of work, field of craft, branch of knowledge, learning, or quick-wittedness, or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as inferior to others. Relying on that, he generates self-disparagement. Whatever self-disparagement of such a kind, thinking oneself inferior, the state of thinking oneself inferior, contempt, disdain, the state of being disdained, knowing oneself as inferior, self-contempt, and self-abasement—this is called the conceit of a superior person, ‘I am inferior’.

(55) Sadisassa seyyohamasmīti māno

(55) The conceit of an equal person, ‘I am superior’

872. Tattha katamo sadisassa seyyohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco sadiso hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena [T 0.0479] vatthunā parehi seyyaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya mānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ…pe… ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “sadisassa seyyohamasmīti māno”.

872. Therein, what is the conceit of an equal person, ‘I am superior’? Here, a certain person is equal to others by birth, clan, noble birth... or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as superior to them. Relying on that, he generates conceit. Whatever conceit of such a kind, conceiving, the state of having conceived... the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called the conceit of an equal person, ‘I am superior’.

(56) Sadisassa sadisohamasmīti māno

(56) The conceit of an equal person, ‘I am equal’

873. Tattha katamo sadisassa sadisohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco sadiso hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi sadisaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya mānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “sadisassa sadisohamasmīti māno”.

873. Therein, what is the conceit of an equal person, ‘I am equal’? Here, a certain person is equal to others by birth, clan, noble birth... or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as equal to them. Relying on that, he generates conceit. Whatever conceit of such a kind, conceiving, the state of having conceived, loftiness, haughtiness, a banner, extolling, the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called the conceit of an equal person, ‘I am equal’.

(57) Sadisassa hīnohamasmīti māno

(57) The conceit of an equal person, ‘I am inferior’

874. Tattha [V 0.0408] katamo sadisassa hīnohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco sadiso hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi hīnaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya omānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo omāno omaññanā omaññitattaṃ hīḷanā ohīḷanā ohīḷitattaṃ attuññā attavaññā attaparibhavo – ayaṃ vuccati “sadisassa hīnohamasmīti māno”.

874. Therein, what is the conceit of an equal person, ‘I am inferior’? Here, a certain person is equal to others by birth, clan, noble birth... or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as inferior to them. Relying on that, he generates self-disparagement. Whatever self-disparagement of such a kind, thinking oneself inferior, the state of thinking oneself inferior, contempt, disdain, the state of being disdained, knowing oneself as inferior, self-contempt, and self-abasement—this is called the conceit of an equal person, ‘I am inferior’.

(58) Hīnassa seyyohamasmīti māno

(58) The conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am superior’

875. Tattha katamo hīnassa seyyohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco hīno hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi seyyaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya mānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati [T 0.0480] unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “hīnassa seyyohamasmīti māno”.

875. Therein, what is the conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am superior’? Here, a certain person is inferior to others by birth, clan, noble birth... or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as superior to them. Relying on that, he generates conceit. Whatever conceit of such a kind, conceiving, the state of having conceived, loftiness, haughtiness, a banner, extolling, the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called the conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am superior’.

(59) Hīnassa sadisohamasmīti māno

(59) The conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am equal’

876. Tattha [M 0.0369] katamo hīnassa sadisohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco hīno hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi sadisaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya mānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo [P 0.0355] sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “hīnassa sadisohamasmīti māno”.

876. Therein, what is the conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am equal’? Here, a certain person is inferior to others by birth, clan, noble birth... or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as equal to them. Relying on that, he generates conceit. Whatever conceit of such a kind, conceiving, the state of having conceived, loftiness, haughtiness, a banner, extolling, the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called the conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am equal’.

(60) Hīnassa hīnohamasmīti māno

(60) The conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am inferior’

877. Tattha katamo hīnassa hīnohamasmīti māno? Idhekacco hīno hoti jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi sadisaṃ attānaṃ dahati; so taṃ nissāya omānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo omāno omaññanā omaññitattaṃ hīḷanā [V 0.0409] ohīḷanā ohīḷitattaṃ attuññā attavaññā attaparibhavo – ayaṃ vuccati “hīnassa hīnohamasmīti māno”.

877. Therein, what is the conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am inferior’? Here, a certain person is inferior by birth, clan, noble birth... or by some other reason whatsoever, and he places himself as inferior to others. Relying on that, he generates self-disparagement. Whatever self-disparagement of such a kind, thinking oneself inferior, the state of thinking oneself inferior, contempt, disdain, the state of being disdained, knowing oneself as inferior, self-contempt, and self-abasement—this is called the conceit of an inferior person, ‘I am inferior’.

(61) Māno

(61) Conceit

878. Tattha katamo māno? Yo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “māno”.

878. Therein, what is conceit? Whatever conceit, conceiving, the state of having conceived, loftiness, haughtiness, a banner, extolling, the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called ‘conceit’.

(62) Atimāno

(62) Excessive Conceit

879. Tattha katamo atimāno? Idhekacco jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena vatthunā parehi attānaṃ atimaññati. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo [T 0.0481] dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “atimāno”.

879. Therein, what is excessive conceit? Here, a certain person, on the basis of birth, clan, noble birth... or some other reason whatsoever, excessively conceives of himself in comparison with others. Whatever conceit of such a kind, conceiving, the state of having conceived, loftiness, haughtiness, a banner, extolling, the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called ‘excessive conceit’.

(63) Mānātimāno

(63) Conceit-and-excessive-conceit

880. Tattha katamo mānātimāno? Idhekacco jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā…pe… aññataraññatarena vatthunā pubbakālaṃ parehi sadisaṃ attānaṃ dahati, aparakālaṃ attānaṃ seyyaṃ dahati. Yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “mānātimāno”.

880. Therein, what is conceit-and-excessive-conceit? Here, a certain person, on the basis of birth, clan, noble birth... or some other reason whatsoever, at first places himself as equal to others, but later places himself as superior. Whatever conceit of such a kind, conceiving, the state of having conceived, loftiness, haughtiness, a banner, extolling, the mind’s desire for prominence—this is called ‘conceit-and-excessive-conceit’.

(64) Omāno

(64) Self-disparagement

881. Tattha katamo omāno? Idhekacco jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena [M 0.0370] vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vā sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā omānaṃ jappeti. Yo evarūpo omāno omaññanā omaññitattaṃ hīḷanā ohīḷanā ohīḷitattaṃ attuññā attavaññā attaparibhavo – ayaṃ vuccati “omāno”.

881. Herein, what is inferiority conceit? Here, someone engenders inferiority conceit on the basis of birth, or clan, or family lineage, or beauty of complexion, or wealth, or study, or occupation, or craft, or branch of knowledge, or learning, or ready wit, or on the basis of some other reason. Whatever inferiority conceit, thinking little of oneself, the state of thinking little of oneself, self-contempt, self-despising, the state of despising oneself, self-belittlement, self-scorn, and self-disparagement of this sort—this is called “inferiority conceit.”

(65) Adhimāno

(65) Over-conceit

882. Tattha [V 0.0410] katamo adhimāno? Appatte pattasaññitā, akate katasaññitā, anadhigate adhigatasaññitā, asacchikate sacchikatasaññitā, yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “adhimāno”.

882. Herein, what is over-conceit? It is the perception of having attained what has not been attained, the perception of having done what has not been done, the perception of having realized what has not been realized, and the perception of having personally experienced what has not been personally experienced. Whatever conceit, conceiving, the state of conceiving, haughtiness, loftiness, a banner, exaltation, and the mind’s desire for prominence of this sort—this is called “over-conceit.”

(66) Asmimāno

(66) The 'I am' conceit

883. Tattha [P 0.0356] katamo asmimāno? Rūpaṃ asmīti māno, asmīti chando[T 0.0482], asmīti anusayo, vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇaṃ asmīti māno, asmīti chando, asmīti anusayo, yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “asmimāno”.

883. Herein, what is the 'I am' conceit? The conceit 'I am form,' the desire 'I am,' the underlying tendency 'I am'; regarding feeling... regarding perception... regarding formations... the conceit 'I am consciousness,' the desire 'I am,' the underlying tendency 'I am.' Whatever conceit, conceiving, state of having conceived, haughtiness, loftiness, a banner, exaltation, and the mind’s desire for prominence of this sort—this is called the 'I am' conceit.

(67) Micchāmāno

(67) Wrong conceit

884. Tattha katamo micchāmāno? Idhekacco pāpakena vā kammāyatanena pāpakena vā sippāyatanena pāpakena vā vijjāṭṭhānena pāpakena vā sutena pāpakena vā paṭibhānena pāpakena vā sīlena pāpakena vā vatena pāpakena vā sīlabbatena pāpikāya vā diṭṭhiyā aññataraññatarena vatthunā mānaṃ jappeti, yo evarūpo māno maññanā maññitattaṃ unnati unnāmo dhajo sampaggāho ketukamyatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “micchāmāno”.

884. Herein, what is wrong conceit? Here, a certain person engenders conceit by means of an evil occupation, or an evil craft, or an evil branch of knowledge, or evil learning, or evil ready wit, or evil conduct, or an evil observance, or an evil rite and ritual, or an evil view, or by some other reason whatsoever. Whatever conceit, conceiving, state of having conceived, haughtiness, loftiness, a banner, exaltation, and the mind’s desire for prominence of this sort—this is called 'wrong conceit'.

(68) Ñātivitakko

(68) Thought concerning relatives

885. Tattha katamo ñātivitakko? Ñātake ārabbha gehasito takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “ñātivitakko”.

885. Herein, what is thought concerning relatives? Concerning relatives, any household-based thought, reflection, or wrong intention—this is called 'thought concerning relatives'.

(69) Janapadavitakko

(69) Thought concerning the country

886. Tattha [V 0.0411] katamo janapadavitakko? Janapadaṃ ārabbha gehasito takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “janapadavitakko”.

886. Herein, what is thought concerning the country? Concerning the country, any household-based thought, reflection, or wrong intention—this is called 'thought concerning the country'.

(70) Amaravitakko

(70) Thought concerning immortality

887. Tattha katamo amaravitakko? Dukkarakāritāpaṭisaṃyutto vā diṭṭhigatapaṭisaṃyutto vā gehasito takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “amaravitakko”.

887. Herein, what is thought concerning immortality? Any household-based thought, reflection, or wrong intention that is connected with the practice of austerities or connected with views—this is called 'thought concerning immortality'.

(71) Parānuddayatāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko

(71) Thought connected with compassion for others

888. Tattha [M 0.0371] katamo parānuddayatāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko? Idhekacco gihīhi saṃsaṭṭho [T 0.0483] viharati sahanandī sahasokī, sukhitesu sukhito, dukkhitesu dukkhito, uppannesu kiccakaraṇīyesu attanā vā yogaṃ āpajjati. Yo tattha gehasito takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “parānuddayatāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko”.

888. Herein, what is thought connected with compassion for others? Here, a certain monk lives intermingled with householders, rejoicing with them and sorrowing with them; he is happy when they are happy and sorrowful when they are sorrowful; and when duties and obligations arise, he personally applies himself to them. Whatever household-based thought, reflection, or wrong intention is there—this is called 'thought connected with compassion for others'.

(72) Lābhādipaṭisaṃyutto vitakko

(72) Thought Connected with Gain, Honor, and Fame

889. Tattha katamo lābhasakkārasilokapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko? Lābhasakkārasilokaṃ ārabbha gehasito takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “lābhasakkārasilokapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko”.

889. Herein, what is thought connected with gain, honor, and fame? Any household-based thought, reflection, or wrong intention concerning gain, honor, and fame—this is called 'thought connected with gain, honor, and fame'.

(73) Anavaññattipaṭisaṃyutto vitakko

(73) Thought Connected with Non-disparagement

890. Tattha katamo anavaññattipaṭisaṃyutto vitakko? Idhekacco jātiyā vā gottena vā kolaputtiyena vā vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā dhanena vā ajjhenena vā kammāyatanena vā sippāyatanena vā vijjāṭṭhānena vā sutena vā paṭibhānena vā aññataraññatarena vatthunā mā [V 0.0412] maṃ pare [P 0.0357] avajāniṃsūti. Yo tattha gehasito takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “anavaññattipaṭisaṃyutto vitakko”.

890. Herein, what is thought connected with non-disparagement? Here, someone thinks: 'May others not disparage me because of my birth, or clan, or family status, or beauty, or wealth, or learning, or sphere of work, or sphere of craft, or branch of knowledge, or scriptural learning, or eloquence, or for some other reason.' Whatever household-based thought, reflection, or wrong intention is there—this is called 'thought connected with non-disparagement'.

Ekakaṃ.

The Section on Ones.

2. Dukaniddeso

2. Exposition of Pairs

(1) Kodho ca upanāho ca

(1) Anger and Resentment

891. (Ka) tattha katamo kodho? Yo kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “kodho”.

891. Herein, what is anger? Whatever is anger, getting angry, the state of being angry; hatred, being hateful, the state of being hateful; animosity, malevolence, the state of being malevolent; opposition, antagonism; ferocity; surliness; displeasure of the mind—this is called 'anger.'

(Kha) tattha katamo upanāho? Pubbakālaṃ kodho, aparakālaṃ upanāho. Yo evarūpo upanāho upanayhanā upanayhitattaṃ aṭṭhapanā ṭhapanā [T 0.0484] saṇṭhapanā anusaṃsandanā anuppabandhanā daḷhīkammaṃ kodhassa – ayaṃ vuccati “upanāho”.

Herein, what is resentment? Anger at a former time is resentment at a later time. Whatever resentment of this sort, the bearing of a grudge, the state of bearing a grudge, the harboring, maintaining, sustaining, continuing, persisting, the hardening of anger—this is called 'resentment.'

(2) Makkho ca paḷāso ca

(2) Contempt and Contentiousness

892. (Ka) tattha katamo makkho? Yo makkho makkhāyanā makkhāyitattaṃ makkhiyanā makkhiyitattaṃ (sī. ka.) niṭṭhuriyaṃ niṭṭhuriyakammaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “makkho”.

892. Herein, what is contempt? Whatever is contempt, being contemptuous, the state of being contemptuous; harshness, harsh action—this is called 'contempt.'

(Kha) tattha [M 0.0372] katamo paḷāso? Yo paḷāso paḷāsāyanā palāsāyanā palāsāyitattaṃ (syā.) paḷāsāhāro vivādaṭṭhānaṃ yugaggāho appaṭinissaggo – ayaṃ vuccati “paḷāso”.

Herein, what is contentiousness? Whatever is contentiousness, being contentious, taking up contentiousness, a basis for dispute, picking a quarrel, a refusal to let go—this is called 'contentiousness.'

(3) Issā ca macchariyañca

(3) Envy and Stinginess

893. (Ka) tattha [V 0.0413] katamā issā? Yā paralābhasakkāragarukāramānanavandanapūjanāsu issā issāyanā issāyitattaṃ usūyā usūyanā usūyitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “issā”.

893. Herein, what is envy? Whatever envy, being envious, the state of being envious; jealousy, being jealous, the state of being jealous, in regard to the gains, honor, respect, reverence, salutations, and veneration of others—this is called 'envy.'

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ macchariyaṃ? Pañca macchariyāni – āvāsamacchariyaṃ, kulamacchariyaṃ, lābhamacchariyaṃ, vaṇṇamacchariyaṃ, dhammamacchariyaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ maccheraṃ maccharāyanā maccharāyitattaṃ vevicchaṃ kadariyaṃ kaṭukañcukatā aggahitattaṃ paggahitattaṃ (sī. ka.) dha. sa. 1127 cittassa – idaṃ vuccati “macchariyaṃ”.

Herein, what is stinginess? There are five kinds of stinginess: stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding beauty, and stinginess regarding the Dhamma. Whatever stinginess of this sort, being stingy, the state of being stingy, unwillingness to share, avarice, acrimony, a grasping state of mind—this is called 'stinginess.'

(4) Māyā ca sāṭheyyañca

(4) Deceit and Fraudulence

894. (Ka) tattha katamā māyā? Idhekacco kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā, vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā, manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā tassa paṭicchādanahetuṃ pāpikaṃ icchaṃ paṇidahati. “Mā maṃ jaññā”ti icchati. “Mā maṃ jaññā”ti saṅkappeti. “Mā maṃ jaññā”ti vācaṃ bhāsati. “Mā [P 0.0358] maṃ jaññā”ti kāyena parakkamati. Yā evarūpā māyā māyāvitā accāsarā vañcanā nikati vikiraṇā pariharaṇā gūhanā parigūhanā chādanā paṭicchādanā anuttānīkammaṃ anāvikammaṃ vocchādanā pāpakiriyā – ayaṃ vuccati “māyā”.

894. (a) Herein, what is deceit? Here, a certain person, having engaged in misconduct by body, speech, and mind, forms a wicked desire in order to conceal it. He wishes, 'May they not know me.' He resolves, 'May they not know me.' He utters words to the effect, 'May they not know me.' He makes a bodily effort so that 'they may not know me.' Whatever of this sort is trickery, trickiness, dissimulation, deception, fraud, obfuscation, evasion, hiding, concealing, covering up, repeatedly covering up, not making plain, not making manifest, thoroughly covering up, evil action—this is called 'deceit.'

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ sāṭheyyaṃ? Idhekacco saṭho [T 0.0485] hoti parisaṭho. Yaṃ tattha saṭhaṃ saṭhatā sāṭheyyaṃ kakkaratā kakkariyaṃ kakkhaḷatā kakkhaḷiyaṃ (syā.) parikkhattatā pārikkhattiyaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “sāṭheyyaṃ”.

(b) Herein, what is fraudulence? Here, a certain person is crafty and thoroughly crafty. Whatever craftiness, the state of being crafty, fraudulence, harshness, the state of being harsh, entrenched craftiness, the state of being entrenchedly crafty—this is called 'fraudulence.'

(5) Avijjā ca bhavataṇhā ca

(5) Ignorance and Craving for Becoming

895. (Ka) tattha katamā avijjā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjā”.

895. (a) Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not-knowing, not-seeing… pe… the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'ignorance.'

(Kha) tattha katamā bhavataṇhā? Yo bhavesu bhavacchando bhavarāgo bhavanandī bhavataṇhā bhavasineho bhavapariḷāho bhavamucchā bhavajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavataṇhā”.

(b) Herein, what is craving for becoming? Whatever desire for becoming, passion for becoming, delight in becoming, craving for becoming, affection for becoming, fever for becoming, infatuation with becoming, absorption in becoming—this is called 'craving for becoming.'

(6) Bhavadiṭṭhi ca vibhavadiṭṭhi ca

(6) The View of Becoming and the View of Non-becoming

896. (Ka) tattha [M 0.0373][V 0.0414] katamā bhavadiṭṭhi? “Bhavissati attā ca loko cā”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavadiṭṭhi”.

896. (a) Herein, what is the view of becoming? 'The self and the world will exist'—whatever such view, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp—this is called 'the view of becoming.'

(Kha) tattha katamā vibhavadiṭṭhi? “Na bhavissati attā ca loko cā”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati vibhavadiṭṭhi.

(b) Herein, what is the view of non-becoming? 'The self and the world will not exist'—whatever such view, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp—this is called 'the view of non-becoming.'

(7) Sassatadiṭṭhi ca ucchedadiṭṭhi ca

(7) The View of Eternalism and the View of Annihilationism

897. (Ka) tattha katamā sassatadiṭṭhi? “Sassato attā ca loko cā”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “sassatadiṭṭhi”.

897. (a) Herein, what is the view of eternalism? ‘The self and the world are eternal’—whatever view of this sort, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp—this is called ‘the view of eternalism.’

(Kha) tattha katamā ucchedadiṭṭhi? “Ucchijjissati attā ca loko cā”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “ucchedadiṭṭhi”.

(b) Herein, what is the view of annihilationism? ‘The self and the world will be annihilated’—whatever view of this sort, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp—this is called ‘the view of annihilationism.’

(8) Antavādiṭṭhi ca anantavādiṭṭhi ca

(8) The view of finitude and the view of infinitude.

898. (Ka) tattha [P 0.0359] katamā antavādiṭṭhi? “Antavā attā ca loko cā”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “antavādiṭṭhi”.

898. (a) Herein, what is the view of finitude? ‘The self and the world are finite’—whatever view of this sort, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp—this is called ‘the view of finitude’.

(Kha) tattha katamā anantavādiṭṭhi? “Anantavā attā ca loko cā”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho [T 0.0486] – ayaṃ vuccati “anantavādiṭṭhi”.

(b) Herein, what is the view of infinitude? ‘The self and the world are infinite’—whatever view of this sort, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp—this is called ‘the view of infinitude’.

(9) Pubbantānudiṭṭhi ca aparantānudiṭṭhi ca

(9) Views concerning the past and views concerning the future.

899. (Ka) tattha katamā pubbantānudiṭṭhi? Pubbantaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “pubbantānudiṭṭhi”.

899. (a) Herein, what is a view concerning the past? Whatever view, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp that arises concerning the past—this is called ‘a view concerning the past’.

(Kha) tattha [V 0.0415] katamā aparantānudiṭṭhi? Aparantaṃ ārabbha yā uppajjati diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “aparantānudiṭṭhi”.

(b) Herein, what is a view concerning the future? Whatever view, a held view… pe… a perverse grasp that arises concerning the future—this is called ‘a view concerning the future’.

(10) Ahirikañca anottappañca

(10) Lack of shame and lack of moral dread.

900. (Ka) tattha katamaṃ ahirikaṃ? Yaṃ na hirīyati hiriyitabbena, na hirīyati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati “ahirikaṃ”.

900. (a) Herein, what is lack of shame? That one is not ashamed of what one should be ashamed of, that one is not ashamed of the attainment of evil, unwholesome states—this is called ‘lack of shame’.

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ anottappaṃ? Yaṃ na ottappati ottappitabbena na ottappati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati “anottappaṃ”.

(b) Herein, what is lack of moral dread? That one does not dread what one should dread, that one does not dread the attainment of evil, unwholesome states—this is called ‘lack of moral dread’.

(11) Dovacassatā ca pāpamittatā ca

(11) Difficulty in being admonished and friendship with evil people.

901. (Ka) tattha katamā dovacassatā? Sahadhammike vuccamāne dovacassāyaṃ dovacassiyaṃ dovacassatā vippaṭikulaggāhitā vipaccanīkasātatā anādariyaṃ anādaratā agāravatā appatissavatā – ayaṃ vuccati “dovacassatā”.

901. (a) Herein, what is difficulty in being admonished? When one is being spoken to in accordance with the Dhamma, there is the state of being difficult to speak to, the quality of being difficult to admonish, taking things oppositionally, delighting in contrariness, disrespect, the state of being disrespectful, lack of reverence, and lack of compliance—this is called ‘difficulty in being admonished’.

(Kha) tattha [M 0.0374] katamā pāpamittatā? Ye te puggalā assaddhā dussīlā appassutā maccharino duppaññā, yā tesaṃ sevanā nisevanā saṃsevanā bhajanā sambhajanā bhatti sambhatti sampavaṅkatā – ayaṃ vuccati “pāpamittatā”.

(b) Herein, what is friendship with evil people? Whatever frequenting, consorting with, close association, service, devotion, and complete inclination towards those persons who are faithless, immoral, of little learning, miserly, and unwise—this is called ‘friendship with evil people’.

(12) Anajjavo ca amaddavo ca

(12) Dishonesty and harshness.

902. (Ka) tattha katamo anajjavo? Yo anajjavo anajjavatā jimhatā vaṅkatā kuṭilatā – ayaṃ vuccati “anajjavo”.

902. (a) Herein, what is dishonesty? Whatever is dishonesty, the state of being not straightforward, crookedness, deviousness, fraudulence—this is called ‘dishonesty’.

(Kha) tattha katamo amaddavo[T 0.0487]? Yā amudutā amaddavatā kakkhaḷiyaṃ phārusiyaṃ kakkhaḷatā kaṭhinatā kathinatā (syā. ka.) ujucittatā amudutā – ayaṃ vuccati “amaddavo”.

(b) Herein, what is harshness? Whatever is lack of softness, lack of gentleness, roughness, coarseness, harshness, stiffness, and rigidity of mind—this is called ‘harshness’.

(13) Akkhanti ca asoraccañca

(13) Impatience and lack of gentle composure.

903. (Ka) tattha [P 0.0360][V 0.0416] katamā akkhanti? Yā akkhanti akkhamanatā anadhivāsanatā caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “akkhanti”.

903. (a) Herein, what is impatience? Whatever is impatience, intolerance, inability to endure, fierceness, ill-temper, and mental displeasure—this is called ‘impatience.’

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ asoraccaṃ? Kāyiko vītikkamo vācasiko vītikkamo kāyikavācasiko vītikkamo – idaṃ vuccati “asoraccaṃ”. Sabbampi dussīlyaṃ asoraccaṃ.

(b) Herein, what is lack of gentle composure? Bodily transgression, verbal transgression, and bodily and verbal transgression—this is called ‘lack of gentle composure.’ All immorality is lack of gentle composure.

(14) Asākhalyañca appaṭisanthāro ca

(14) Unfriendliness and inhospitality.

904. (Ka) tattha katamaṃ asākhalyaṃ? Yā sā vācā kaṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā asamādhisaṃvattanikā tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Yā tattha asaṇhavācatā asakhilavācatā pharusavācatā – idaṃ vuccati “asākhalyaṃ”.

904. (a) Herein, what is unfriendliness? It is when one speaks such speech as is thorny, rough, bitter to others, abusive, bordering on anger, and unconducive to concentration. Whatever is ungentle speech, unaffable speech, harsh speech—this is called ‘unfriendliness.’

(Kha) tattha katamo appaṭisanthāro appaṭisandhāro (ka.)? Dve paṭisanthārā – āmisapaṭisanthāro ca dhammapaṭisanthāro ca. Idhekacco appaṭisanthārako hoti āmisapaṭisanthārena vā dhammapaṭisanthārena vā – ayaṃ vuccati “appaṭisanthāro”.

(b) Herein, what is inhospitality? There are two kinds of hospitality: material hospitality and hospitality with the Dhamma. Here, a certain person is inhospitable, offering neither material hospitality nor hospitality with the Dhamma—this is called ‘inhospitality.’

(15) Indriyesu aguttadvāratā ca bhojane amattaññutā ca

(15) Unguardedness in the sense faculties and lack of moderation in eating.

905. (Ka) tattha katamā indriyesu aguttadvāratā? Idhekacco cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… [M 0.0375] jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena [T 0.0488] phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati[V 0.0417]. Yā imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ agutti agopanā anārakkho asaṃvaro – ayaṃ vuccati “indriyesu aguttadvāratā”.

905. (a) Herein, what is unguardedness in the sense faculties? Here, having seen a form with the eye, someone grasps its signs and features. Since, if he were to dwell with the eye faculty unrestrained, evil unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flood in, he does not practice restraint over it, he does not guard the eye faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear... pe... having smelled an odor with the nose... pe... having tasted a flavor with the tongue... pe... having felt a tangible with the body... pe... having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, he grasps its signs and features. Since, if he were to dwell with the mind faculty unrestrained, evil unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flood in, he does not practice restraint over it, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the mind faculty. Whatever is the lack of guarding, protecting, watching over, and restraining these six sense faculties—this is called ‘unguardedness in the sense faculties.’

(Kha) tattha katamā bhojane amattaññutā? Idhekacco appaṭisaṅkhā ayoniso āhāraṃ āhāreti davāya madāya maṇḍanāya vibhūsanāya. Yā tattha asantuṭṭhitā amattaññutā appaṭisaṅkhā bhojane – ayaṃ vuccati “bhojane amattaññutā.”

(b) Herein, what is lack of moderation in eating? Here, someone unreflectively and unwisely takes food: for amusement, for intoxication, for physical charm, for beautification. Whatever lack of contentment, lack of moderation, and lack of reflection in regard to food there is—this is called ‘lack of moderation in eating.’

(16) Muṭṭhassaccañca asampajaññañca

(16) Forgetfulness and lack of clear comprehension.

906. (Ka) tattha katamaṃ muṭṭhassaccaṃ? Yā assati ananussati appaṭissati assati assaraṇatā adhāraṇatā pilāpanatā sammusanatā – idaṃ vuccati “muṭṭhassaccaṃ”.

906. (a) Herein, what is forgetfulness? Whatever is unmindfulness, non-recollection, non-remembrance, lack of mindfulness, lack of memory, lack of retention, lapsing, oblivion—this is called 'forgetfulness'.

(Kha) tattha [P 0.0361] katamaṃ asampajaññaṃ? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – idaṃ vuccati “asampajaññaṃ”.

(b) Herein, what is lack of clear comprehension? Whatever is ignorance, not seeing... pe... the bolt of ignorance, delusion which is an unwholesome root—this is called 'lack of clear comprehension'.

(17) Sīlavipatti ca diṭṭhivipatti ca

(17) Failure in virtue and failure in view.

907. (Ka) tattha katamā sīlavipatti? Yo kāyiko vītikkamo vācasiko vītikkamo kāyikavācasiko vītikkamo – ayaṃ vuccati “sīlavipatti”. Sabbampi dussīlyaṃ sīlavipatti.

907. (a) Herein, what is failure in virtue? Whatever is a bodily transgression, a verbal transgression, or a bodily and verbal transgression—this is called 'failure in virtue.' All immorality is failure in virtue.

(Kha) tattha katamā diṭṭhivipatti? “Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho [T 0.0489] – ayaṃ vuccati “diṭṭhivipatti”. Sabbāpi micchādiṭṭhi diṭṭhivipatti.

(b) Herein, what is failure in view? The view such as: 'There is no fruit of what is given, no fruit of what is sacrificed... pe... there are no beings who, having realized this world and the next for themselves by direct knowledge, make them known'—whatever is such a view, a viewpoint... pe... a perverse grasp—this is called 'failure in view.' All wrong view is failure in view.

(18) Ajjhattasaṃyojanañca bahiddhāsaṃyojanañca

(18) The internal fetter and the external fetter.

908. (Ka) tattha [V 0.0418] katamaṃ ajjhattasaṃyojanaṃ? Pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni – ajjhattasaṃyojanaṃ. (Kha) pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni – bahiddhāsaṃyojanaṃ.

908. (a) Herein, what is the internal fetter? The five lower fetters are the internal fetter. (b) The five higher fetters are the external fetter.

Dukaṃ.

The Dyads.

3. Tikaniddeso

3. Exposition of the Triads

(1) Tīṇi akusalamūlāni

(1) The three unwholesome roots.

909. Tattha [M 0.0376] katamāni tīṇi akusalamūlāni? Lobho, doso, moho.

909. Herein, what are the three unwholesome roots? Greed, hatred, and delusion.

(Ka) tattha katamo lobho? Yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandirāgo cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho parigedho saṅgo paṅko ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī jālinī saritā visattikā sotaṃ visaṭā visadā (sī. ka.) dha. sa. 1141 āyūhanī āyūhinī (ka.) dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti vanaṃ vanatho santhavo sandhavo (ka.) sineho apekkhā paṭibandhu āsā āsīsanā āsīsitattaṃ āsiṃsanā āsiṃsitattaṃ (sī. syā.) rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā jappā abhijappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā sādhukamyatā adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā [P 0.0362] patthanā pihanā sampatthanā kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā saddataṇhā rūpataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chadanaṃ bandhanaṃ upakkileso [T 0.0490] anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddulaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “lobho”.

(a) Herein, what is greed? Whatever is passion, intense passion, compliance, accord, delight, delight in passion, intense passion of the mind, desire, infatuation, clinging, craving, intense craving, attachment, the mire, agitation, deceit, generation, production, sewing, netting, a river, adhesion, a spreading stream, exertion, a companion, aspiration, the guide to becoming, a forest, a thicket, intimacy, affection, expectation, a bond, hope, wishing, the state of wishing, hope for forms, hope for sounds, hope for smells, hope for tastes, hope for tangibles, hope for gains, hope for wealth, hope for sons, hope for life, murmuring, intense murmuring, the act of murmuring, the state of having murmured, greediness, being greedy, the state of being greedy, fawning, desire for what is agreeable, unrighteous passion, inordinate greed, desire, longing, aspiration, yearning, intense aspiration, sensual craving, craving for existence, craving for non-existence, craving for forms, craving for the formless, craving for cessation, craving for sounds, craving for smells, craving for tastes, craving for tangibles, craving for mental phenomena, the flood, the yoke, the bond, grasping, the covering, the hindrance, the screen, the tie, the defilement, the underlying tendency, the obsession, the creeper, wanting, the root of suffering, the origin of suffering, the source of suffering, Māra’s snare, Māra’s hook, Māra’s domain, the river of craving, the net of craving, the leash of craving, the ocean of craving, covetousness, greed which is an unwholesome root—this is called 'greed'.

(Kha) tattha [V 0.0419] katamo doso? “Anatthaṃ me acarī”ti āghāto jāyati, “anatthaṃ me caratī”ti āghāto jāyati, “anatthaṃ me carissatī”ti āghāto jāyati, “piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari”…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… “anatthaṃ carissatī”ti āghāto jāyati, “appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari”…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… “atthaṃ carissatī”ti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati. Yo evarūpo cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ [M 0.0377] byāpatti byāpajjanā byāpajjitattaṃ virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati “doso”.

(b) Herein, what is hatred? Resentment arises at the thought: 'He has done me harm.' Resentment arises at the thought: 'He is doing me harm.' Resentment arises at the thought: 'He will do me harm.' Resentment arises at the thought: 'He has done harm to someone dear and pleasing to me'... pe... 'He will do harm.' Resentment arises at the thought: 'He has done good to someone not dear and displeasing to me'... pe... 'He will do good.' Or resentment arises without cause. Whatever is such resentment of mind, resistance, repugnance, opposition, irritation, exasperation, rage, hatred, malice, malevolence, corruption of mind, wrath, being wrathful, the state of being wrathful, hatred, being hateful, the state of being hateful, ill will, malevolence, the state of malevolence, opposition, antagonism, fierceness, surliness, displeasure of mind—this is called 'hatred'.

(Ga) tattha katamo moho? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatā paṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃ, yaṃ evarūpaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “moho”. Imāni tīṇi akusalamūlāni.

(c) Herein, what is delusion? Ignorance concerning suffering, ignorance concerning the origin of suffering, ignorance concerning the cessation of suffering, ignorance concerning the path leading to the cessation of suffering; ignorance concerning the past, ignorance concerning the future, ignorance concerning the past and the future; ignorance concerning specific conditionality and dependently arisen phenomena. Whatever is such ignorance, not seeing... pe... the bolt of ignorance, delusion which is an unwholesome root—this is called 'delusion'. These are the three unwholesome roots.

(2) Tayo akusalavitakkā

(2) Three Unwholesome Thoughts

910. Tattha [T 0.0491] katame tayo akusalavitakkā? Kāmavitakko, byāpādavitakko, vihiṃsāvitakko.

910. Herein, what are the three unwholesome thoughts? The thought of sensual desire, the thought of ill will, and the thought of cruelty.

(Ka) tattha katamo kāmavitakko? Kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmavitakko”.

(a) Herein, what is the thought of sensual desire? Thought connected with sensual desire, applied thought, wrong intention—this is called 'the thought of sensual desire'.

(Kha) tattha [P 0.0363] katamo byāpādavitakko? Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “byāpādavitakko”.

(b) Herein, what is the thought of ill will? Thought connected with ill will, applied thought, wrong intention—this is called 'the thought of ill will'.

(Ga) tattha [V 0.0420] katamo vihiṃsāvitakko? Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “vihiṃsāvitakko”. Ime tayo akusalavitakkā.

(c) Herein, what is the thought of cruelty? Thought connected with cruelty, applied thought, wrong intention—this is called 'the thought of cruelty.' These are the three unwholesome thoughts.

(3) Tisso akusalasaññā

(3) Three Unwholesome Perceptions

911. Tattha katamā tisso akusalasaññā? Kāmasaññā, byāpādasaññā, vihiṃsāsaññā.

911. Herein, what are the three unwholesome perceptions? The perception of sensual desire, the perception of ill will, and the perception of cruelty.

(Ka) tattha katamā kāmasaññā? Kāmapaṭisaṃyuttā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmasaññā”.

(a) Herein, what is the perception of sensual desire? Perception connected with sensual desire, perceiving, the state of having perceived—this is called 'the perception of sensual desire'.

(Kha) tattha katamā byāpādasaññā? Byāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “byāpādasaññā”.

(b) Herein, what is the perception of ill will? Perception connected with ill will, perceiving, the state of having perceived—this is called 'the perception of ill will'.

(Ga) tattha katamā vihiṃsāsaññā? Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyuttā saññā sañjānanā sañjānitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “vihiṃsāsaññā”. Imā tisso akusalasaññā.

(c) Herein, what is the perception of cruelty? Perception connected with cruelty, perceiving, the state of having perceived—this is called 'the perception of cruelty.' These are the three unwholesome perceptions.

(4) Tisso akusaladhātuyo

(4) Three Unwholesome Elements

912. Tattha katamā tisso akusaladhātuyo? Kāmadhātu, byāpādadhātu, vihiṃsādhātu.

912. Herein, what are the three unwholesome elements? The element of sensual desire, the element of ill will, and the element of cruelty.

Tattha [M 0.0378] katamā kāmadhātu? Kāmavitakko kāmadhātu. Byāpādavitakko byāpādadhātu. Vihiṃsāvitakko vihiṃsādhātu.

Herein, what is the element of sensual desire? The thought of sensual desire is the element of sensual desire. The thought of ill will is the element of ill will. The thought of cruelty is the element of cruelty.

(Ka) tattha katamo kāmavitakko? Kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmavitakko”.

(a) Herein, what is the thought of sensual desire? Thought connected with sensual desire, applied thought, wrong intention—this is called 'the thought of sensual desire'.

(Kha) tattha katamo byāpādavitakko[T 0.0492]? Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “byāpādavitakko”.

(b) Herein, what is the thought of ill will? Thought connected with ill will, applied thought, wrong intention—this is called 'the thought of ill will'.

(Ga) tattha [V 0.0421] katamo vihiṃsāvitakko? Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati “vihiṃsāvitakko”. Imā tisso akusaladhātuyo.

(c) Herein, what is the thought of cruelty? Thought connected with cruelty, applied thought, wrong intention—this is called 'the thought of cruelty.' These are the three unwholesome elements.

(5) Tīṇi duccaritāni

(5) Three Kinds of Misconduct

913. Tattha katamāni tīṇi duccaritāni? Kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ.

913. Herein, what are the three kinds of misconduct? Bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct.

(Ka) tattha katamaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro – idaṃ vuccati “kāyaduccaritaṃ”.

(a) Herein, what is bodily misconduct? Destroying life, taking what is not given, and sexual misconduct—this is called 'bodily misconduct'.

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ vacīduccaritaṃ? Musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo – idaṃ vuccati “vacīduccaritaṃ”.

(b) Herein, what is verbal misconduct? False speech, slanderous speech, harsh speech, and frivolous talk—this is called 'verbal misconduct'.

(Ga) tattha katamaṃ manoduccaritaṃ? Abhijjhā[P 0.0364], byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati “manoduccaritaṃ”.

(c) Herein, what is mental misconduct? Covetousness, ill will, and wrong view—this is called 'mental misconduct'.

(Ka-ga) tattha katamaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ? Akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ, akusalaṃ vacīkammaṃ vacīduccaritaṃ, akusalaṃ manokammaṃ manoduccaritaṃ.

(a–c) Herein, what is bodily misconduct? Unwholesome bodily action is bodily misconduct; unwholesome verbal action is verbal misconduct; unwholesome mental action is mental misconduct.

Tattha katamaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ? Akusalā kāyasañcetanā akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ, akusalā vacīsañcetanā akusalaṃ vacīkammaṃ, akusalā manosañcetanā akusalaṃ manokammaṃ. Imāni tīṇi duccaritāni.

Herein, what is unwholesome bodily action? Unwholesome bodily volition is unwholesome bodily action; unwholesome verbal volition is unwholesome verbal action; unwholesome mental volition is unwholesome mental action. These are the three kinds of misconduct.

(6) Tayo āsavā

(6) Three Taints

914. Tattha katame tayo āsavā? Kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, avijjāsavo.

914. Herein, what are the three taints? The taint of sensuality, the taint of becoming, and the taint of ignorance.

(Ka) tattha katamo kāmāsavo? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmarāgo kāmanandī kāmataṇhā [V 0.0422] kāmasineho kāmapariḷāho kāmamucchā kāmajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmāsavo”.

(a) Herein, what is the taint of sensuality? Whatever sensual desire, sensual lust, sensual delight, sensual craving, sensual affection, sensual fever, sensual obsession, and sensual clinging there is for sensual pleasures—this is called 'the taint of sensuality'.

(Kha) tattha [M 0.0379] katamo bhavāsavo? Yo bhavesu bhavacchando…pe… bhavajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavāsavo”.

(b) Herein, what is the taint of becoming? Whatever desire for becoming …pe… clinging to becoming—this is called 'the taint of becoming'.

(Ga) tattha katamo avijjāsavo? Dukkhe aññāṇaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī [T 0.0493] moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “avijjāsavo”. Ime tayo āsavā.

(c) Herein, what is the taint of ignorance? Ignorance concerning suffering …pe… the bar of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'the taint of ignorance.' These are the three taints.

(7) Tīṇi saṃyojanāni

(7) Three Fetters

915. Tattha katamāni tīṇi saṃyojanāni? Sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.

915. Herein, what are the three fetters? Identity view, doubt, and grasping of rules and observances.

(Ka) tattha katamā sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto – rūpaṃ attato samanupassati rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā rūpaṃ rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā viññāṇaṃ viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “sakkāyadiṭṭhi”.

(a) Therein, what is identity view? Here, an uninstructed worldling, who is not a seer of the noble ones, is unversed in the noble Dhamma and untrained in the noble Dhamma; who is not a seer of true persons, is unversed in the Dhamma of true persons and untrained in the Dhamma of true persons, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He regards feeling …pe… perception …pe… formations …pe… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever such view, a held view …pe… a perverse grasping—this is called 'identity view'.

(Kha) tattha katamā vicikicchā? Satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati, dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati, saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati, sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, aparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati, pubbantāparante kaṅkhati vicikicchati[P 0.0365], idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati. Yā evarūpā kaṅkhā kaṅkhāyanā kaṅkhāyitattaṃ thambhitattaṃ cittassa manovilekho – ayaṃ vuccati “vicikicchā”.

(b) Therein, what is doubt? One doubts about the Teacher; one doubts about the Dhamma; one doubts about the Saṅgha; one doubts about the training; one doubts about the past; one doubts about the future; one doubts about both the past and the future; one doubts about phenomena that are dependently arisen through this conditionality. Whatever such doubt, doubting, doubtfulness, stiffness of mind, mental indecisiveness—this is called 'doubt'.

(Ga) tattha [V 0.0423] katamo sīlabbataparāmāso? “Ito bahiddhā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi sīlabbatena suddhī”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “sīlabbataparāmāso”. Imāni tīṇi [T 0.0494] saṃyojanāni.

(c) Therein, what is the grasping of rules and observances? The view held by ascetics and brahmins outside of this dispensation that 'purification comes through moral rules, through observances, or through moral rules and observances.' Whatever such view, a held view …pe… a perverse grasping—this is called 'the grasping of rules and observances.' These are the three fetters.

(8) Tisso taṇhā

(8) The Three Cravings

916. Tattha katamā tisso taṇhā? Kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā.

916. Therein, what are the three cravings? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence.

Tattha katamā bhavataṇhā? Bhavadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavataṇhā”.

Therein, what is craving for existence? Lust accompanied by the view of eternalism, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for existence'.

Tattha [M 0.0380] katamā vibhavataṇhā? Ucchedadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “vibhavataṇhā”. Avasesā taṇhā kāmataṇhā.

Therein, what is craving for non-existence? Lust accompanied by the annihilationist view, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for non-existence.' The remaining craving is craving for sensual pleasures.

Tattha katamā kāmataṇhā? Kāmadhātupaṭisaṃyutto rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmataṇhā”.

Therein, what is craving for sensual pleasures? Lust connected with the sense-sphere realm, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for sensual pleasures'.

( ) (tattha katamā bhavataṇhā) Rūpadhātuarūpadhātupaṭisaṃyutto rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavataṇhā”.

Lust connected with the form realm and the formless realm, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for existence'.

( ) (tattha katamā vibhavataṇhā) (?) Ucchedadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “vibhavataṇhā”. Imā tisso taṇhā.

Lust accompanied by the annihilationist view, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for non-existence.' These are the three cravings.

(9) Aparāpi tisso taṇhā

(9) Another Three Cravings

917. Tattha [T 0.0495] katamā aparāpi tisso taṇhā? Kāmataṇhā, rūpataṇhā, arūpataṇhā.

917. Therein, what are the other three cravings? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for form, and craving for the formless.

(Ka) tattha katamā kāmataṇhā? Kāmadhātupaṭisaṃyutto rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmataṇhā”.

(a) Therein, what is craving for sensual pleasures? Lust connected with the sense-sphere realm, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for sensual pleasures'.

(Kha) tattha [P 0.0366][V 0.0424] katamā rūpataṇhā? Rūpadhātupaṭisaṃyutto rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “rūpataṇhā”.

(b) Therein, what is craving for form? Lust connected with the form realm, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for form'.

(Ga) tattha katamā arūpataṇhā? Arūpadhātupaṭisaṃyutto rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “arūpataṇhā”. Imā tisso taṇhā.

(c) Therein, what is craving for the formless? Lust connected with the formless realm, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for the formless.' These are the three cravings.

(10) Aparāpi tisso taṇhā

(10) Another Three Cravings

918. Tattha katamā aparāpi tisso taṇhā? Rūpataṇhā, arūpataṇhā, nirodhataṇhā.

918. Therein, what are the other three cravings? Craving for form, craving for the formless, and craving for cessation.

(Ka) tattha katamā rūpataṇhā? Rūpadhātupaṭisaṃyutto rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “rūpataṇhā”.

(a) Therein, what is craving for form? Lust connected with the form realm, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for form'.

(Kha) tattha katamā arūpataṇhā? Arūpadhātupaṭisaṃyutto rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “arūpataṇhā”.

(b) Therein, what is craving for the formless? Lust connected with the formless realm, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for the formless'.

(Ga) tattha katamā nirodhataṇhā? Ucchedadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “nirodhataṇhā”. Imā tisso taṇhā.

(c) Therein, what is craving for cessation? Lust accompanied by the annihilationist view, passion, intense passion of the mind—this is called 'craving for cessation.' These are the three cravings.

(11) Tisso esanā

(11) The Three Seekings

919. Tattha [M 0.0381] katamā tisso esanā? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā.

919. Therein, what are the three seekings? The seeking for sensual pleasure, the seeking for existence, and the seeking for the holy life.

(Ka) tattha katamā kāmesanā? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando…pe… kāmajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmesanā”.

(a) Therein, what is the seeking for sensual pleasure? Whatever sensual desire for sensual pleasures... whatever absorption in sensual pleasures—this is called 'the seeking for sensual pleasure'.

(Kha) tattha katamā bhavesanā? Yo bhavesu bhavacchando…pe… bhavajjhosānaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavesanā”.

(b) Therein, what is the seeking for existence? Whatever desire for existence... whatever absorption in existence—this is called 'the seeking for existence'.

(Ga) tattha [V 0.0425] katamā brahmacariyesanā? “Sassato loko”ti vā, “asassato loko”ti – vā…pe… “neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti vā yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “brahmacariyesanā”.

(c) Therein, what is the seeking for the holy life? The view that 'the world is eternal' or 'the world is not eternal'... or 'the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death'—whatever such view, a held view... a perverse grasping—this is called 'the seeking for the holy life'.

(Ka) tattha katamā kāmesanā, kāmarāgo, tadekaṭṭhaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “kāmesanā”.

(a) Therein, what is the seeking for sensual pleasure? Lust for sensual pleasures, and the unwholesome bodily, verbal, and mental action associated with it—this is called 'the seeking for sensual pleasure'.

(Kha) tattha katamā bhavesanā, bhavarāgo tadekaṭṭhaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “bhavesanā”.

(b) Therein, what is the seeking for existence? Lust for existence, and the unwholesome bodily, verbal, and mental action associated with it—this is called 'the seeking for existence'.

(Ga) tattha katamā brahmacariyesanā, antaggāhikā [P 0.0367] diṭṭhi tadekaṭṭhaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “brahmacariyesanā”. Imā tisso esanā.

(c) Therein, what is the seeking for the holy life? A view holding to an extreme, and the unwholesome bodily, verbal, and mental action associated with it—this is called 'the seeking for the holy life.' These are the three seekings.

(12) Tisso vidhā

(12) The Three Conceits

920. Tattha [T 0.0496] katamā tisso vidhā? “Seyyohamasmī”ti vidhā, “sadisohamasmī”ti vidhā, “hīnohamasmī”ti vidhā – imā tisso vidhā.

920. Therein, what are the three conceits? The conceit 'I am superior,' the conceit 'I am equal,' and the conceit 'I am inferior'—these are the three conceits.

(13) Tīṇi bhayāni

(13) The Three Fears

921. Tattha katamāni tīṇi bhayāni? Jātibhayaṃ, jarābhayaṃ, maraṇabhayaṃ.

921. Therein, what are the three fears? The fear of birth, the fear of aging, and the fear of death.

(Ka) tattha katamaṃ jātibhayaṃ? Jātiṃ paṭicca bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso utrāso – idaṃ vuccati “jātibhayaṃ”.

(a) Therein, what is the fear of birth? The fear, terror, consternation, horripilation, and mental dread that arises on account of birth—this is called 'the fear of birth'.

(Kha) tattha katamaṃ jarābhayaṃ? Jaraṃ paṭicca bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso utrāso – idaṃ vuccati “jarābhayaṃ”.

(b) Therein, what is the fear of aging? The fear, terror, consternation, horripilation, and mental dread that arises on account of aging—this is called 'the fear of aging'.

(Ga) tattha [M 0.0382][V 0.0426] katamaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ? Maraṇaṃ paṭicca bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso utrāso – idaṃ vuccati “maraṇabhayaṃ”. Imāni tīṇi bhayāni.

(c) Therein, what is the fear of death? The fear, terror, consternation, horripilation, and mental dread that arises on account of death—this is called 'the fear of death.' These are the three fears.

(14) Tīṇi tamāni

(14) Three Darknesses

922. Tattha katamāni tīṇi tamāni? Atītaṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, anāgataṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, etarahi vā paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – imāni tīṇi tamāni.

922. Therein, what are the three darknesses? With regard to the past, one doubts, is uncertain, is not resolved, and is not confident; with regard to the future, one doubts, is uncertain, is not resolved, and is not confident; with regard to the present, one doubts, is uncertain, is not resolved, and is not confident—these are the three darknesses.

(15) Tīṇi titthāyatanāni

(15) Three Sectarian Tenets

923. Tattha katamāni tīṇi titthāyatanāni? Idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – “yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbe katahetū”ti; idha panekacco samaṇo [T 0.0497] vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – “yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ issaranimmānahetū”ti; idha panekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – “yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ [P 0.0368] vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ ahetu appaccayā”ti – imāni tīṇi titthāyatanāni.

923. Therein, what are the three sectarian tenets? Here, some recluse or brahmin holds such a doctrine and view: ‘Whatever this person experiences—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—all that is due to past deeds.’ Again, here some recluse or brahmin holds such a doctrine and view: ‘Whatever this person experiences—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—all that is due to creation by a God.’ Again, here some recluse or brahmin holds such a doctrine and view: ‘Whatever this person experiences—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—all that is without cause or condition.’ These are the three sectarian tenets.

(16) Tayo kiñcanā

(16) Three Impediments

924. Tattha katame tayo kiñcanā katamāni tīṇi kiñcanāni (?) dī. ni. 3.305? Rāgo kiñcanaṃ, doso kiñcanaṃ, moho kiñcanaṃ – ime tayo kiñcanā.

924. Therein, what are the three impediments? Lust is an impediment, hatred is an impediment, and delusion is an impediment. These are the three impediments.

(17) Tīṇi aṅgaṇāni

(17) Three Defilements

Tattha katamāni tīṇi aṅgaṇāni? Rāgo aṅgaṇaṃ, doso aṅgaṇaṃ, moho aṅgaṇaṃ – imāni tīṇi aṅgaṇāni.

Therein, what are the three defilements? Lust is a defilement, hatred is a defilement, and delusion is a defilement. These are the three defilements.

(18) Tīṇi malāni

(18) Three Stains

Tattha [V 0.0427] katamāni tīṇi malāni? Rāgo malaṃ, doso malaṃ, moho malaṃ – imāni tīṇi malāni.

Therein, what are the three stains? Lust is a stain, hatred is a stain, and delusion is a stain. These are the three stains.

(19) Tīṇi visamāni

(19) Three Wrongnesses

Tattha katamāni tīṇi visamāni? Rāgo visamaṃ, doso visamaṃ, moho visamaṃ – imāni tīṇi visamāni.

Therein, what are the three wrongnesses? Lust is wrongness, hatred is wrongness, and delusion is wrongness. These are the three wrongnesses.

(20) Aparānipi tīṇi visamāni

(20) Another Three Wrongnesses

Tattha katamāni aparānipi tīṇi visamāni? Kāyavisamaṃ, vacīvisamaṃ, manovisamaṃ – imāni tīṇi visamāni.

Therein, what are the other three wrongnesses? Bodily wrongness, verbal wrongness, and mental wrongness. These are the three wrongnesses.

(21) Tayo aggī

(21) Three Fires

Tattha [M 0.0383] katame tayo aggī? Rāgaggi, dosaggi, mohaggi – ime tayo aggī.

Therein, what are the three fires? The fire of lust, the fire of hatred, and the fire of delusion. These are the three fires.

(22) Tayo kasāvā

(22) Three Taints

Tattha katame tayo kasāvā? Rāgakasāvo, dosakasāvo, mohakasāvo – ime tayo kasāvā.

Therein, what are the three taints? The taint of lust, the taint of hatred, and the taint of delusion. These are the three taints.

(23) Aparepi tayo kasāvā

(23) Another Three Taints

Tattha katame aparepi tayo kasāvā? Kāyakasāvo, vacīkasāvo, manokasāvo – ime tayo kasāvā.

Therein, what are the other three taints? The bodily taint, the verbal taint, and the mental taint. These are the three taints.

(24. Ka) assādadiṭṭhi

(24a) The View of Gratification

925. Tattha [V 0.0428] katamā assādadiṭṭhi? Idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo [T 0.0498] vā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhī – “natthi kāmesu doso”ti. So kāmesu pātabyataṃ āpajjati. Ayaṃ vuccati “assādadiṭṭhi”.

925. Therein, what is the view of gratification? Here, some recluse or brahmin holds such a doctrine and view: ‘There is no fault in sensual pleasures.’ He indulges in sensual pleasures. This is called the view of gratification.

(Kha) attānudiṭṭhi

(24b) The View Pertaining to Self

Tattha katamā attānudiṭṭhi? Idha assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto – rūpaṃ attato samanupassati rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā rūpaṃ rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā viññāṇaṃ viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “attānudiṭṭhi”.

Therein, what is the view pertaining to self? Here, an uninstructed worldling, who has no regard for the noble ones and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, who has no regard for true persons and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in the self, or the self as in form. He regards feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in the self, or the self as in consciousness. Any such view, held view, … distorted grasp—this is called the view pertaining to self.

(Ga) micchādiṭṭhi

(24c) Wrong View

Tattha [P 0.0369] katamā micchādiṭṭhi? “Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī”ti – yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ…pe… vipariyāsaggāho – ayaṃ vuccati “micchādiṭṭhi”. Sassatadiṭṭhi assādadiṭṭhi, sakkāyadiṭṭhi attānudiṭṭhi, ucchedadiṭṭhi micchādiṭṭhi.

Therein, what is wrong view? ‘There is nothing given, nothing offered… there are no recluses and brahmins who, having realized it for themselves by direct knowledge, make known this world and the other world.’ Any such view, held view, … distorted grasp—this is called wrong view. The view of gratification is the view of eternalism; the view pertaining to self is the identity view; this wrong view is the view of annihilationism.

(25. Ka) arati

(25a) Discontent

926. Tattha katamā arati? Pantesu vā senāsanesu aññataraññataresu vā adhikusalesu dhammesu arati aratitā anabhirati anabhiramaṇā ukkaṇṭhitā paritassitā – ayaṃ vuccati “arati”.

926. Therein, what is discontent? Discontent, the state of being discontented, lack of delight, not taking delight, vexation, and anxiety in regard to remote lodgings or to any of the higher wholesome states—this is called discontent.

(Kha) vihesā

(25b) Vexation

Tattha [V 0.0429] katamā vihesā? Idhekacco pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā rajjuyā vā aññataraññatarena satte viheṭheti, yā evarūpā heṭhanā viheṭhanā [T 0.0499] hiṃsanā vihiṃsanā rosanā virosanā parūpaghāto – ayaṃ vuccati “vihesā”.

Therein, what is vexation? Here, a certain person vexes beings with their hand, with a clod, with a stick, with a weapon, with a rope, or with one or another such thing. Whatever of such a nature is harming, vexing, injuring, tormenting, oppressing, greatly oppressing, and assault on others—this is called 'vexation'.

(Ga) adhammacariyā

(25c) Unrighteous Conduct

Tattha [M 0.0384] katamā adhammacariyā? Kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā, vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā, manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā – ayaṃ vuccati “adhammacariyā”.

Therein, what is unrighteous conduct? Unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct by way of body, unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct by way of speech, unrighteous conduct and wrong conduct by way of mind—this is called 'unrighteous conduct'.

(26. Ka) dovacassatā

(26a) Being Difficult to Admonish

927. Tattha katamā dovacassatā? Sahadhammike vuccamāne dovacassāyaṃ dovacassiyaṃ dovacassatā vippaṭikulaggāhitā vipaccanīkasātatā anādariyaṃ anādaratā agāravatā appatissavatā – ayaṃ vuccati “dovacassatā”.

927. Therein, what is being difficult to admonish? When spoken to in accordance with the Dhamma, it is the state of being difficult to admonish, the quality of being difficult to admonish, the characteristic of being difficult to admonish, the grasping of things in a contrary way, the state of habitual opposition, disrespect, the state of being disrespectful, irreverence, and the state of being unreceptive—this is called 'being difficult to admonish'.

(Kha) pāpamittatā

(26b) Association with Bad Friends

Tattha katamā pāpamittatā? Ye te puggalā assaddhā dussīlā appassutā maccharino duppaññā, yā tesaṃ sevanā nisevanā saṃsevanā bhajanā sambhajanā bhatti sambhatti taṃsampavaṅkatā – ayaṃ vuccati “pāpamittatā”.

Herein, what is association with bad friends? There are those persons who are faithless, immoral, of little learning, miserly, and of little wisdom. Whatever associating with them, constantly associating with them, intimately associating with them, keeping company with them, intimately keeping company with them, devotion to them, great devotion to them, and the state of being inclined towards them—this is called 'association with bad friends'.

(Ga) nānattasaññā

(Ga) Diverse perceptions

Tattha katamā nānattasaññā? Kāmasaññā, byāpādasaññā, vihiṃsāsaññā – ayaṃ vuccati “nānattasaññā”. Sabbāpi akusalā saññā nānattasaññā.

Herein, what are diverse perceptions? Perception of sensual pleasure, perception of ill will, perception of cruelty—this is called 'diverse perceptions.' All unwholesome perceptions are diverse perceptions.

(27. Ka) uddhaccaṃ

(27. Ka) Restlessness

928. Tattha [V 0.0430] katamaṃ uddhaccaṃ? Yaṃ cittassa uddhaccaṃ avūpasamo cetaso vikkhepo bhantattaṃ cittassa – idaṃ vuccati “uddhaccaṃ”.

928. Herein, what is restlessness? Whatever is the restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, distraction of the intellect, and agitation of the mind—this is called 'restlessness'.

(Kha) kosajjaṃ

(Kha) Idleness

Tattha katamaṃ kosajjaṃ? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu [P 0.0370] vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppadānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo – idaṃ vuccati [T 0.0500] “kosajjaṃ”.

Herein, what is idleness? It is the abandonment of the mind and the giving over to abandonment in regard to bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, or mental misconduct, or to the five strands of sensual pleasure; and in the development of wholesome states, it is the state of not acting with care, the state of not acting with persistence, the state of not acting to completion, a sluggish disposition, the state of having laid down desire, the state of having laid down the burden, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, lack of resolve, lack of application, and negligence—this is called 'idleness'.

(Ga) pamādo

(Ga) Heedlessness

Tattha katamo pamādo? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppadānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo, yo evarūpo pamādo pamajjanā pamajjitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “pamādo”.

Herein, what is heedlessness? It is the abandonment of the mind and the giving over to abandonment in regard to bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, or mental misconduct, or to the five strands of sensual pleasure; and in the development of wholesome states, it is the state of not acting with care, the state of not acting with persistence, the state of not acting to completion, a sluggish disposition, the state of having laid down desire, the state of having laid down the burden, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, lack of resolve, lack of application, and negligence. Whatever such heedlessness, the manner of being heedless, and the state of being heedless—this is called 'heedlessness'.

(28. Ka) asantuṭṭhitā

(28. Ka) Discontent

929. Tattha [M 0.0385] katamā asantuṭṭhitā? Itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi pañcahi vā kāmaguṇehi asantuṭṭhassa bhiyyokamyatā, yā evarūpā icchā icchāgatā asantuṭṭhitā rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “asantuṭṭhitā”.

929. Herein, what is discontent? It is the desire for more on the part of one who is discontented with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, or with the five strands of sensual pleasure. Whatever such longing, state of longing, discontent, lust, strong lust, and strong lust of the mind—this is called 'discontent'.

(Kha) asampajaññatā

(Kha) Lack of clear comprehension

Tattha [V 0.0431] katamā asampajaññatā? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ…pe… avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “asampajaññatā”.

Herein, what is lack of clear comprehension? Whatever ignorance, not seeing… the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root—this is called 'lack of clear comprehension'.

(Ga) mahicchatā

(Ga) Excessive desire

Tattha katamā mahicchatā? Itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi pañcahi vā kāmaguṇehi asantuṭṭhassa bhiyyokamyatā, yā evarūpā icchā icchāgatā mahicchatā rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo – ayaṃ vuccati “mahicchatā”.

Herein, what is excessive desire? It is the desire for more on the part of one who is discontented with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, or with the five strands of sensual pleasure. Whatever such longing, state of longing, excessive desire, lust, strong lust, and strong lust of the mind—this is called 'excessive desire'.

(29. Ka) ahirikaṃ

(29. Ka) Lack of shame

930. Tattha katamaṃ ahirikaṃ? Yaṃ na hirīyati hirīyitabbena, na hirīyati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati “ahirikaṃ”.

930. Herein, what is lack of shame? It is not being ashamed of what should be shameful; not being ashamed of the attainment of evil, unwholesome states—this is called 'lack of shame'.

(Kha) anottappaṃ

(Kha) Lack of moral dread

Tattha katamaṃ anottappaṃ? Yaṃ na ottappati ottappitabbena, na [T 0.0501] ottappati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā – idaṃ vuccati “anottappaṃ”.

Herein, what is lack of moral dread? It is not dreading what should be dreaded; not dreading the attainment of evil, unwholesome states—this is called 'lack of moral dread'.

(Ga) pamādo

(Ga) Heedlessness

Tattha katamo pamādo? Kāyaduccarite vā vacīduccarite vā manoduccarite vā pañcasu vā kāmaguṇesu cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppadānaṃ [P 0.0371] kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asakkaccakiriyatā asātaccakiriyatā anaṭṭhitakiriyatā olīnavuttitā nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā anāsevanā abhāvanā abahulīkammaṃ anadhiṭṭhānaṃ ananuyogo pamādo, yo evarūpo pamādo pamajjanā pamajjitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati “pamādo”.

Herein, what is heedlessness? It is the abandonment of the mind and the giving over to abandonment in regard to bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, or mental misconduct, or to the five strands of sensual pleasure; and in the development of wholesome states, it is the state of not acting with care, the state of not acting with persistence, the state of not acting to completion, a sluggish disposition, the state of having laid down desire, the state of having laid down the burden, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, lack of resolve, lack of application, and negligence. Whatever such heedlessness, the manner of being heedless, and the state of being heedless—this is called 'heedlessness'.

(30. Ka) anādariyaṃ

(30. Ka) Disrespect

931. Tattha [V 0.0432] katamaṃ anādariyaṃ? Yaṃ anādariyaṃ anādaratā agāravatā appatissavatā anaddā anaddāyanā anaddāyitattaṃ anādā anādāyanā anādāyitattaṃ (syā.) asīlyaṃ acittīkāro – idaṃ vuccati “anādariyaṃ”.

931. Herein, what is disrespect? Whatever disrespect, lack of regard, irreverence, lack of deference, disregard, the manner of disregarding, the state of disregarding, lack of good conduct, and lack of esteem there is—this is called 'disrespect'.

(Kha) dovacassatā

(Kha) Being difficult to admonish

Tattha katamā dovacassatā? Sahadhammike vuccamāne dovacassāyaṃ dovacassiyaṃ dovacassatā vippaṭikulaggāhitā vipaccanīkasātatā anādariyaṃ [M 0.0386] anādaratā agāravatā appatissavatā – ayaṃ vuccati “dovacassatā”.

Herein, what is being difficult to admonish? When one is spoken to with reason, whatever difficulty in admonition, the state of being difficult to admonish, the quality of being difficult to admonish, taking things in a contrary way, persistence in opposition, disrespect, lack of regard, irreverence, and lack of deference there is—this is called 'being difficult to admonish'.

(Ga) pāpamittatā

(Ga) Having bad friends

Tattha katamā pāpamittatā? Ye te puggalā assaddhā dussīlā appassutā maccharino duppaññā, yā tesaṃ sevanā nisevanā saṃsevanā paṭisevanā bhajanā sambhajanā bhatti sambhatti taṃsampavaṅkatā – ayaṃ vuccati “pāpamittatā”.

Herein, what is having bad friends? There are those persons who are faithless, immoral, of little learning, miserly, and of little wisdom.
