Tattha katamāni nava iñjitāni? “Asmī”ti iñjitametaṃ, “ahamasmī”ti iñjitametaṃ[V 0.0458], “ayamahamasmī”ti iñjitametaṃ “bhavissa”nti iñjitametaṃ, “rūpī bhavissa”nti iñjitametaṃ, “arūpī bhavissa”nti iñjitametaṃ, “saññī bhavissa”nti iñjitametaṃ, “asaññī bhavissa”nti iñjitametaṃ, “nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa”nti iñjitametaṃ – imāni nava iñjitāni.

964. Herein, what are the nine agitations? 'There is being' is an agitation; 'I am' is an agitation; 'This I am' is an agitation; 'I will be' is an agitation; 'I will be with form' is an agitation; 'I will be formless' is an agitation; 'I will be percipient' is an agitation; 'I will be non-percipient' is an agitation; 'I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient' is an agitation. These are the nine agitations.

(6-9) Nava maññitādīni

(6-9) Nine Conceits, and so forth

965. Tattha katamāni nava maññitāni… nava phanditāni… nava papañcitāni… nava saṅkhatāni? “Asmī”ti saṅkhatametaṃ, “ahamasmī”ti saṅkhatametaṃ[T 0.0528], “ayamahamasmī”ti saṅkhatametaṃ, “bhavissa”nti [P 0.0391] saṅkhatametaṃ, “rūpī bhavissa”nti saṅkhatametaṃ, “arūpī bhavissa”nti saṅkhatametaṃ, “saññī bhavissa”nti saṅkhatametaṃ[M 0.0405], “asaññī bhavissa”nti saṅkhatametaṃ, “nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa”nti saṅkhatametaṃ – imāni nava saṅkhatāni.

965. Herein, what are the nine conceits… nine pulsations… nine proliferations… nine fabrications? 'There is being' is a fabrication; 'I am' is a fabrication; 'This I am' is a fabrication; 'I will be' is a fabrication; 'I will be with form' is a fabrication; 'I will be formless' is a fabrication; 'I will be percipient' is a fabrication; 'I will be non-percipient' is a fabrication; 'I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient' is a fabrication. These are the nine fabrications.

Navakaṃ.

The Nines.

10. Dasakaniddeso

10. Explanation of the Tens

(1) Dasa kilesavatthūni

(1) Ten Bases of Defilement

966. Tattha katamāni dasa kilesavatthūni? Lobho, doso, moho, māno, diṭṭhi, vicikicchā, thinaṃ, uddhaccaṃ, ahirikaṃ, anottappaṃ – imāni dasa kilesavatthūni.

966. Herein, what are the ten bases of defilement? Greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, sloth, restlessness, lack of shame, and lack of fear of wrongdoing—these are the ten bases of defilement.

(2) Dasa āghātavatthūni

(2) Ten Grounds for Resentment

967. Tattha katamāni dasa āghātavatthūni? “Anatthaṃ me acarī”ti āghāto jāyati, “anatthaṃ me caratī”ti āghāto jāyati, “anatthaṃ me carissatī”ti āghāto jāyati, “piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari”…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti [V 0.0459] āghāto jāyati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghāto jāyati, aṭṭhāne vā pana āghāto jāyati – imāni dasa āghātavatthūni.

967. Herein, what are the ten grounds for resentment? Resentment arises, thinking: “He has done me harm.” Resentment arises, thinking: “He is doing me harm.” Resentment arises, thinking: “He will do me harm.” Resentment arises, thinking: “He has done harm to one who is dear and pleasing to me,” … “he is doing harm…” … “he will do harm to one who is dear and pleasing to me.” Resentment arises, thinking: “He has done good to one who is disliked and displeasing to me,” … “he is doing good…” … “he will do good to one who is disliked and displeasing to me.” Or else, resentment arises without cause. These are the ten grounds for resentment.

(3) Dasa akusalakammapathā

(3) Ten Unwholesome Courses of Action

968. Tattha katame dasa akusalakammapathā? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi – ime dasa akusalakammapathā.

968. Herein, what are the ten unwholesome courses of action? Taking life, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter, covetousness, ill will, and wrong view—these are the ten unwholesome courses of action.

(4) Dasa saṃyojanāni

(4) Ten Fetters

969. Tattha katamāni dasa saṃyojanāni? Kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ[T 0.0529], mānasaṃyojanaṃ, diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ, vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanaṃ, bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ, issāsaṃyojanaṃ, macchariyasaṃyojanaṃ, avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ – imāni dasa saṃyojanāni.

969. Herein, what are the ten fetters? The fetter of sensual desire, the fetter of aversion, the fetter of conceit, the fetter of views, the fetter of doubt, the fetter of attachment to rites and rituals, the fetter of desire for existence, the fetter of envy, the fetter of stinginess, and the fetter of ignorance—these are the ten fetters.

(5) Dasa micchattā

(5) Ten Wrongnesses

970. Tattha katame dasa micchattā? Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi[P 0.0392], micchāñāṇaṃ, micchāvimutti – ime dasa micchattā.

970. Herein, what are the ten wrongnesses? Wrong view, wrong thought, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, and wrong liberation—these are the ten wrongnesses.

(6) Dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi

(6) Wrong View with Ten Bases

971. Tattha katamā dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi? Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi [M 0.0406] paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā samaggatā (ka.) sammā paṭipannā [V 0.0460] ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentīti – ayaṃ dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi.

971. Herein, what is the wrong view with ten bases? There is no result of what is given, there is no result of great sacrifice, there is no result of small sacrifice; there is no fruit or result of actions well done and badly done; there is no this world, there is no other world; there is no mother, there is no father; there are no spontaneously arisen beings; there are in the world no recluses and brahmins who are rightly directed and rightly practiced, who, having realized for themselves through direct knowledge, declare this world and the other world. This is the wrong view with ten bases.

(7) Dasavatthukā antaggāhikā diṭṭhi

(7) The View Holding to an Extreme with Ten Bases

972. Tattha katamā dasavatthukā antaggāhikā diṭṭhi? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā – ayaṃ dasavatthukā antaggāhikā diṭṭhi.

972. Herein, what is the view holding to an extreme with ten bases? ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal’; ‘The world is finite,’ or ‘The world is infinite’; ‘The life-principle is the same as the body,’ or ‘The life-principle is different from the body’; ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’—this is the view holding to an extreme with ten bases.

Dasakaṃ.

The Decad.

11. Taṇhāvicaritaniddeso

11. Exposition of the Courses of Craving

(1) Ajjhattikassa upādāya

(1) With Reference to the Internal

973. Tattha [T 0.0530] katamāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni ajjhattikassa upādāya? Asmīti hoti, itthasmīti hoti, evasmīti hoti, aññathāsmīti hoti, bhavissanti hoti, itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti, evaṃ bhavissanti hoti, aññathā bhavissanti hoti, asasmīti hoti, sātasmīti hoti, siyanti hoti, itthaṃ siyanti hoti, evaṃ siyanti hoti, aññathā siyanti hoti, apāhaṃ [P 0.0393] siyanti hoti, apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti, apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti, apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti.

973. Herein, what are the eighteen courses of craving with reference to the internal? There is ‘I am,’ there is ‘I am like this,’ there is ‘I am thus,’ there is ‘I am otherwise,’ there is ‘I will be,’ there is ‘I will be like this,’ there is ‘I will be thus,’ there is ‘I will be otherwise,’ there is ‘I am eternal,’ there is ‘I am non-eternal,’ there is ‘I might be,’ there is ‘I might be like this,’ there is ‘I might be thus,’ there is ‘I might be otherwise,’ there is ‘Indeed, may I be,’ there is ‘Indeed, may I be like this,’ there is ‘Indeed, may I be thus,’ there is ‘Indeed, may I be otherwise.’

974. Kathañca asmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ anavakārī (sī. ka.) karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ asmīti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, asmīti mānaṃ paṭilabhati[V 0.0461], asmīti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – itthasmīti vā evasmīti vā aññathāsmīti vā.

974. And how does ‘I am’ come to be? Without making a distinction in any phenomenon, one obtains the desire ‘I am,’ the conceit ‘I am,’ and the view ‘I am’ with regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. When that exists, these become proliferated: ‘I am like this,’ or ‘I am thus,’ or ‘I am otherwise.’

(2) Kathañca [M 0.0407] itthasmīti hoti? Khattiyosmīti vā, brāhmaṇosmīti vā, vessosmīti vā, suddosmīti vā, gahaṭṭhosmīti vā, pabbajitosmīti vā, devosmīti vā, manussosmīti vā, rūpīsmīti vā, arūpīsmīti vā, saññīsmīti vā, asaññīsmīti vā, nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ itthasmīti hoti.

And how does ‘I am like this’ come to be? ‘I am a noble,’ or ‘I am a brahmin,’ or ‘I am a merchant,’ or ‘I am a worker,’ or ‘I am a householder,’ or ‘I am a renunciant,’ or ‘I am a deva,’ or ‘I am a human,’ or ‘I am possessed of form,’ or ‘I am formless,’ or ‘I am percipient,’ or ‘I am non-percipient,’ or ‘I am neither percipient nor non-percipient’—thus ‘I am like this’ comes to be.

(3) Kathañca evasmīti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ paraṃ puggalaṃ (syā.) upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo tathāhaṃ khattiyosmīti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇosmīti vā, yathā so vesso tathāhaṃ vessosmīti vā yathā so suddo tathāhaṃ suddosmīti vā, yathā so gahaṭṭho tathāhaṃ [T 0.0531] gahaṭṭhosmīti vā, yathā so pabbajito tathāhaṃ pabbajitosmīti vā, yathā so devo tathāhaṃ devosmīti vā, yathā so manusso tathāhaṃ manussosmīti vā, yathā so rūpī tathāhaṃ rūpīsmīti vā, yathā so arūpī tathāhaṃ arūpīsmīti vā, yathā so saññī tathāhaṃ saññīsmīti vā, yathā so asaññī tathāhaṃ asaññīsmīti vā, yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ evasmīti hoti.

And how does ‘I am thus’ come to be? By comparing with another person: ‘Just as that person is a noble, so I am a noble,’ or ‘Just as that person is a brahmin, so I am a brahmin,’ or ‘Just as that person is a merchant, so I am a merchant,’ or ‘Just as that person is a worker, so I am a worker,’ or ‘Just as that person is a householder, so I am a householder,’ or ‘Just as that person is a renunciant, so I am a renunciant,’ or ‘Just as that person is a deva, so I am a deva,’ or ‘Just as that person is a human, so I am a human,’ or ‘Just as that person is possessed of form, so I am possessed of form,’ or ‘Just as that person is formless, so I am formless,’ or ‘Just as that person is percipient, so I am percipient,’ or ‘Just as that person is non-percipient, so I am non-percipient,’ or ‘Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so I am neither percipient nor non-percipient’—thus ‘I am thus’ comes to be.

(4) Kathañca aññathāsmīti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo nāhaṃ tathā khattiyosmīti vā yathā so brāhmaṇo nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇosmīti vā, yathā so vesso nāhaṃ tathā vessosmīti vā, yathā so suddo nāhaṃ tathā suddosmīti vā, yathā so gahaṭṭho nāhaṃ tathā gahaṭṭhosmīti vā, yathā so pabbajito nāhaṃ tathā pabbajitosmīti vā, yathā so devo nāhaṃ tathā devosmīti vā, yathā so manusso nāhaṃ tathā manussosmīti [P 0.0394] vā, yathā so rūpī nāhaṃ tathā rūpīsmīti vā, yathā so arūpī nāhaṃ tathā arūpīsmīti vā, yathā so saññī nāhaṃ tathā saññīsmīti vā, yathā so asaññī nāhaṃ tathā asaññīsmīti vā, yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ aññathāsmīti hoti.

And how does ‘I am otherwise’ come to be? By comparing with another person: ‘Just as that person is a noble, so I am not a noble,’ or ‘Just as that person is a brahmin, so I am not a brahmin,’ or ‘Just as that person is a merchant, so I am not a merchant,’ or ‘Just as that person is a worker, so I am not a worker,’ or ‘Just as that person is a householder, so I am not a householder,’ or ‘Just as that person is a renunciant, so I am not a renunciant,’ or ‘Just as that person is a deva, so I am not a deva,’ or ‘Just as that person is a human, so I am not a human,’ or ‘Just as that person is possessed of form, so I am not possessed of form,’ or ‘Just as that person is formless, so I am not formless,’ or ‘Just as that person is percipient, so I am not percipient,’ or ‘Just as that person is non-percipient, so I am not non-percipient,’ or ‘Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so I am not one who is neither percipient nor non-percipient’—thus ‘I am otherwise’ comes to be.

(5) Kathañca [M 0.0408] bhavissanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā [T 0.0532] rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ bhavissanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, bhavissanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati[V 0.0462], bhavissanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – itthaṃ bhavissanti vā, evaṃ bhavissanti vā, aññathā bhavissanti vā.

And how does ‘I will be’ come to be? Without making a distinction in any phenomenon, one obtains the desire ‘I will be,’ the conceit ‘I will be,’ and the view ‘I will be’ with regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. When that exists, these become proliferated: ‘I will be like this,’ or ‘I will be thus,’ or ‘I will be otherwise.’

(6) Kathañca itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Khattiyo bhavissanti vā, brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā, vesso bhavissanti vā, suddo bhavissanti vā, gahaṭṭho bhavissanti vā, pabbajito bhavissanti vā, devo bhavissanti vā, manusso bhavissanti vā, rūpī bhavissanti vā, arūpī bhavissanti vā, saññī bhavissanti vā, asaññī bhavissanti vā, nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti.

And how does ‘I will be like this’ come to be? ‘I will be a noble,’ or ‘I will be a brahmin,’ or ‘I will be a merchant,’ or ‘I will be a worker,’ or ‘I will be a householder,’ or ‘I will be a renunciant,’ or ‘I will be a deva,’ or ‘I will be a human,’ or ‘I will be possessed of form,’ or ‘I will be formless,’ or ‘I will be percipient,’ or ‘I will be non-percipient,’ or ‘I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’—thus ‘I will be like this’ comes to be.

(7) Kathañca evaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo tathāhaṃ khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ bhavissanti hoti.

And how does ‘I will be thus’ come to be? By comparing with another person: ‘Just as that person is a noble, so I will be a noble,’ or ‘Just as that person is a brahmin, so I will be a brahmin,’… or ‘Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’—thus ‘I will be thus’ comes to be.

(8) Kathañca aññathā bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ aññathā bhavissanti hoti.

And how does ‘I will be otherwise’ come to be? By comparing with another person: ‘Just as that person is a noble, so I will not be a noble,’ or ‘Just as that person is a brahmin, so I will not be a brahmin,’… or ‘Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient, so I will not be one who is neither percipient nor non-percipient’—thus ‘I will be otherwise’ comes to be.

(9) Kathañca [T 0.0533] asasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ niccosmi dhuvosmi sassatosmi avipariṇāmadhammosmīti – evaṃ asasmīti hoti.

And how does ‘I am eternal’ come to be? Without making a distinction in any phenomenon, with regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, one thinks: ‘I am permanent, I am stable, I am eternal, I am of an unchanging nature.’ Thus, ‘I am eternal’ comes to be.

(10) Kathañca [P 0.0395] sātasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ ucchijjissāmi vinassissāmi na bhavissāmīti – evaṃ sātasmīti hoti.

And how does ‘I will be annihilated’ come to be? Without making a distinction in any phenomenon, with regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, one thinks: ‘I will be cut off, I will perish, I will not exist.’ Thus, ‘I will be annihilated’ comes to be.

(11) Kathañca siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati[M 0.0409][V 0.0463], siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – itthaṃ siyanti vā, evaṃ siyanti vā, aññathā siyanti vā.

And how does ‘I might be’ come to be? Without making a distinction in any phenomenon, with regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, one obtains the desire ‘I might be,’ one obtains the conceit ‘I might be,’ and one obtains the view ‘I might be.’ When that is present, these proliferations arise: ‘I might be in this way,’ or ‘I might be thus,’ or ‘I might be otherwise.’

(12) Kathañca itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Khattiyo siyanti vā, brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, vesso siyanti vā, suddo siyanti vā, gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, pabbajito siyanti vā, devo siyanti vā, manusso siyanti vā, rūpī siyanti vā, arūpī siyanti vā, saññī siyanti vā, asaññī siyanti vā, nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti.

And how does 'I might be in this way' come to be? It is the thought: 'I might be a khattiya,' or 'I might be a brahmin,' or 'I might be a vessa,' or 'I might be a sudda,' or 'I might be a householder,' or 'I might be one who has gone forth,' or 'I might be a deva,' or 'I might be a human,' or 'I might be one with form,' or 'I might be one without form,' or 'I might be one with perception,' or 'I might be one without perception,' or 'I might be one with neither perception nor non-perception.' Thus, 'I might be in this way' comes to be.

(13) Kathañca evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo tathāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī [T 0.0534] tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti.

And how does 'I might be likewise' come to be? By comparing with another person, one thinks: 'Just as that person is a khattiya, so too I might be a khattiya,' or 'Just as that person is a brahmin, so too I might be a brahmin,'... and so on... 'Just as that person is one with neither perception nor non-perception, so too I might be one with neither perception nor non-perception.' Thus, 'I might be likewise' comes to be.

(14) Kathañca aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti.

And how does 'I might be otherwise' come to be? By comparing with another person, one thinks: 'Just as that person is a khattiya, I might not be a khattiya in that way,' or 'Just as that person is a brahmin, I might not be a brahmin in that way,'... and so on... 'Just as that person is one with neither perception nor non-perception, I might not be one with neither perception nor non-perception in that way.' Thus, 'I might be otherwise' comes to be.

(15) Kathañca apāhaṃ siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ anavakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ apāhaṃ siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, apāhaṃ siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, apāhaṃ siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti vā, apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti vā, apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti vā.

And how does 'Indeed, I might be' come to be? Without distinguishing any phenomenon, with regard to form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, one obtains the desire 'Indeed, I might be,' one obtains the conceit 'Indeed, I might be,' one obtains the view 'Indeed, I might be.' When that is present, these proliferations arise: 'Indeed, I might be in this way,' or 'Indeed, I might be likewise,' or 'Indeed, I might be otherwise.'

(16) Kathañca apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Apāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ vesso siyanti vā, apāhaṃ suddo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, apāhaṃ pabbajito siyanti [P 0.0396] vā, apāhaṃ devo siyanti vā, apāhaṃ manusso siyanti vā, apāhaṃ rūpī siyanti vā, apāhaṃ arūpī siyanti vā, apāhaṃ saññī [V 0.0464] siyanti vā, apāhaṃ asaññī siyanti [M 0.0410] vā, apāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti. (17) Kathañca apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo apāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo [T 0.0535] apāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī apāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti.

(16) And how does 'Indeed, I might be in this way' come to be? It is the thought: 'Indeed, I might be a khattiya,' or 'Indeed, I might be a brahmin,' or 'Indeed, I might be a vessa,' or 'Indeed, I might be a sudda,' or 'Indeed, I might be a householder,' or 'Indeed, I might be one who has gone forth,' or 'Indeed, I might be a deva,' or 'Indeed, I might be a human,' or 'Indeed, I might be one with form,' or 'Indeed, I might be one without form,' or 'Indeed, I might be one with perception,' or 'Indeed, I might be one without perception,' or 'Indeed, I might be one with neither perception nor non-perception.' Thus, 'Indeed, I might be in this way' comes to be. (17) And how does 'Indeed, I might be likewise' come to be? By comparing with another person, one thinks: 'Just as that person is a khattiya, so too, indeed, I might be a khattiya,' or 'Just as that person is a brahmin, so too, indeed, I might be a brahmin,'... and so on... 'Just as that person is one with neither perception nor non-perception, so too, indeed, I might be one with neither perception nor non-perception.' Thus, 'Indeed, I might be likewise' comes to be.

(18) Kathañca apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo apāhaṃ na tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo apāhaṃ na tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī apāhaṃ na tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti.

And how does 'Indeed, I might be otherwise' come to be? By comparing with another person, one thinks: 'Just as that person is a khattiya, indeed, I might not be a khattiya in that way,' or 'Just as that person is a brahmin, indeed, I might not be a brahmin in that way,'... and so on... 'Just as that person is one with neither perception nor non-perception, indeed, I might not be one with neither perception nor non-perception in that way.' Thus, 'Indeed, I might be otherwise' comes to be.

Imāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni ajjhattikassa upādāya.

These are the eighteen courses of craving based on what is internal.

(2) Bāhirassa upādāya

(2) Based on the external

975. Tattha katamāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni bāhirassa upādāya? Iminā asmīti hoti, iminā itthasmīti hoti, iminā evasmīti hoti, iminā aññathāsmīti hoti, iminā bhavissanti hoti, iminā itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti, iminā evaṃ bhavissanti hoti, iminā aññathā bhavissanti hoti, iminā asasmīti hoti, iminā sātasmīti hoti, iminā siyanti hoti, iminā itthaṃ siyanti hoti, iminā evaṃ siyanti hoti, iminā aññathā siyanti hoti, iminā apāhaṃ siyanti hoti, iminā apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti, iminā apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti, iminā apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti.

975. Herein, what are the eighteen courses of craving based on the external? Through this, the attachment 'I am' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I am in this way' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I am likewise' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I am otherwise' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I shall be' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I shall be in this way' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I shall be likewise' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I shall be otherwise' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I am eternal' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I am non-eternal' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I might be' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I might be in this way' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I might be likewise' occurs; through this, the attachment 'I might be otherwise' occurs; through this, the attachment 'Indeed, I might be' occurs; through this, the attachment 'Indeed, I might be in this way' occurs; through this, the attachment 'Indeed, I might be likewise' occurs; through this, the attachment 'Indeed, I might be otherwise' occurs.

976. (1) Kathañca [V 0.0465] iminā asmīti hoti? Kañci [P 0.0397] dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā asmīti chandaṃ paṭilabhati[T 0.0536], iminā asmīti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā asmīti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – iminā itthasmīti vā, iminā evasmīti vā, iminā aññathāsmīti vā.

976. (1) And how does the attachment 'I am' occur through this? Without distinguishing any phenomenon, regarding form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one obtains the desire 'I am through this,' one obtains the conceit 'I am through this,' one obtains the view 'I am through this.' When that is present, these become proliferated: 'I am in this way through this,' or 'I am likewise through this,' or 'I am otherwise through this.'

(2) Kathañca [M 0.0411] iminā itthasmīti hoti? Iminā khattiyosmīti vā, iminā brāhmaṇosmīti vā, iminā vessosmīti vā, iminā suddosmīti vā, iminā gahaṭṭhosmīti vā, iminā pabbajitosmīti vā, iminā devosmīti vā, iminā manussosmīti vā, iminā rūpīsmīti vā, iminā arūpīsmīti vā, iminā saññīsmīti vā, iminā asaññīsmīti vā, iminā nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ iminā itthasmīti hoti.

(2) And how does the attachment 'I am in this way through this' occur? 'Through this I am a khattiya,' or 'through this I am a brahmin,' or 'through this I am a vessa,' or 'through this I am a sudda,' or 'through this I am a householder,' or 'through this I am one who has gone forth,' or 'through this I am a deva,' or 'through this I am a human,' or 'through this I am one with form,' or 'through this I am formless,' or 'through this I am one with perception,' or 'through this I am without perception,' or 'through this I am one with neither perception nor non-perception'—thus the attachment 'I am in this way through this' occurs.

(3) Kathañca iminā evasmīti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā tathāhaṃ khattiyosmīti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇosmīti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ iminā evasmīti hoti.

(3) And how does the attachment 'I am likewise through this' occur? By comparing with another person, 'Just as that person is a khattiya through this, so too am I a khattiya through this,' or 'Just as that person is a brahmin through this, so too am I a brahmin through this,'… and so on… 'Just as that person is one with neither perception nor non-perception through this, so too am I one with neither perception nor non-perception through this'—thus the attachment 'I am likewise through this' occurs.

(4) Kathañca iminā aññathāsmīti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā nāhaṃ tathā khattiyosmīti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇosmīti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññīsmīti vā – evaṃ iminā aññathāsmīti hoti.

(4) And how does the attachment 'I am otherwise through this' occur? By comparing with another person, 'Just as that person is a khattiya through this, I am not a khattiya in that way,' or 'Just as that person is a brahmin through this, I am not a brahmin in that way,'… and so on… 'Just as that person is one with neither perception nor non-perception through this, I am not one with neither perception nor non-perception in that way'—thus the attachment 'I am otherwise through this' occurs.

(5) Kathañca [T 0.0537] iminā bhavissanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā bhavissanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā bhavissanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā bhavissanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – iminā itthaṃ bhavissanti vā, iminā evaṃ bhavissanti vā, iminā aññathā bhavissanti vā.

And how does 'I shall be through this' occur? Without particularizing any phenomenon, regarding form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one obtains the desire, 'I shall be through this'; one obtains the conceit, 'I shall be through this'; one obtains the view, 'I shall be through this.' When that is present, these proliferations arise: 'I shall be thus through this,' or 'I shall be just so through this,' or 'I shall be otherwise through this.'

(6) Kathañca [V 0.0466] iminā itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Iminā khattiyo bhavissanti vā…pe… [P 0.0398] iminā arūpī bhavissanti vā, iminā saññī bhavissanti vā, iminā asaññī bhavissanti vā, iminā nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ iminā itthaṃ bhavissanti hoti.

And how does 'I shall be thus through this' occur? 'Through this I shall be a khattiya,'… and so on… 'through this I shall be formless,' or 'through this I shall be possessed of perception,' or 'through this I shall be without perception,' or 'through this I shall be neither percipient nor non-percipient'—thus does 'I shall be thus through this' occur.

(7) Kathañca iminā evaṃ bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā tathāhaṃ khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so [M 0.0412] brāhmaṇo iminā tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ iminā evaṃ bhavissanti hoti.

And how does 'I shall be just so through this' occur? By comparing with another person: 'Just as that person is a khattiya through this, so too shall I be a khattiya'; or 'Just as that person is a brahmin through this, so too shall I be a brahmin,'… and so on… 'Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient through this, so too shall I be neither percipient nor non-percipient.' Thus does 'I shall be just so through this' occur.

(8) Kathañca iminā aññathā bhavissanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya [T 0.0538] yathā so khattiyo iminā nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo bhavissanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo bhavissanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissanti vā – evaṃ iminā aññathā bhavissanti hoti.

And how does 'I shall be otherwise through this' occur? By comparing with another person: 'Just as that person is a khattiya through this, I shall not be a khattiya in that way'; or 'Just as that person is a brahmin through this, I shall not be a brahmin in that way,'… and so on… 'Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient through this, I shall not be neither percipient nor non-percipient in that way.' Thus does 'I shall be otherwise through this' occur.

(9) Kathañca iminā asasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ avakārī (sī.) karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā niccosmi dhuvosmi sassatosmi avipariṇāmadhammosmīti – evaṃ iminā asasmīti hoti.

And how does 'I am eternal through this' occur? Having particularized a certain phenomenon, regarding form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one thinks: 'Through this I am permanent, I am stable, I am eternal, I am not subject to change.' Thus does 'I am eternal through this' occur.

(10) Kathañca iminā sātasmīti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā ucchijjissāmi vinassissāmi na bhavissāmīti – evaṃ iminā sātasmīti hoti.

And how does 'I am non-eternal through this' occur? Having particularized a certain phenomenon, regarding form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one thinks: 'Through this I shall be cut off, I shall perish, I shall not exist.' Thus does 'I am non-eternal through this' occur.

(11) Kathañca iminā siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – iminā itthaṃ siyanti vā, iminā evaṃ siyanti vā, iminā aññathā siyanti vā.

And how does 'I might be through this' occur? Having particularized a certain phenomenon, regarding form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one obtains the desire, 'I might be through this'; one obtains the conceit, 'I might be through this'; one obtains the view, 'I might be through this.' When that is present, these proliferations arise: 'I might be thus through this,' or 'I might be just so through this,' or 'I might be otherwise through this.'

(12) Kathañca [V 0.0467] iminā itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Iminā khattiyo siyanti vā, iminā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, iminā vesso siyanti vā, iminā suddo siyanti vā, iminā gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, iminā pabbajito siyanti vā, iminā devo siyanti vā, iminā manusso siyanti vā, iminā rūpī siyanti vā, iminā arūpī siyanti vā, iminā [T 0.0539] saññī [P 0.0399] siyanti vā, iminā asaññī siyanti vā, iminā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā itthaṃ siyanti hoti.

And how does 'I might be thus through this' occur? 'Through this I might be a khattiya,' or 'Through this I might be a brahmin,' or 'Through this I might be a vessa,' or 'Through this I might be a sudda,' or 'Through this I might be a householder,' or 'Through this I might be one who has gone forth,' or 'Through this I might be a deva,' or 'Through this I might be a human,' or 'Through this I might be possessed of form,' or 'Through this I might be formless,' or 'Through this I might be possessed of perception,' or 'Through this I might be without perception,' or 'Through this I might be neither percipient nor non-percipient.' Thus does 'I might be thus through this' occur.

(13) Kathañca [M 0.0413] iminā evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā tathāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā tathāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā tathāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā evaṃ siyanti hoti.

And how does 'I might be just so through this' occur? By comparing with another person: 'Just as that person is a khattiya through this, so too might I be a khattiya'; or 'Just as that person is a brahmin through this, so too might I be a brahmin,'… and so on… 'Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient through this, so too might I be neither percipient nor non-percipient.' Thus does 'I might be just so through this' occur.

(14) Kathañca iminā aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā nāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā nāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā nāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā aññathā siyanti hoti.

And how does 'I might be otherwise through this' occur? By comparing with another person: 'Just as that person is a khattiya through this, I might not be a khattiya in that way'; or 'Just as that person is a brahmin through this, I might not be a brahmin in that way,'… and so on… 'Just as that person is neither percipient nor non-percipient through this, I might not be neither percipient nor non-percipient in that way.' Thus does 'I might be otherwise through this' occur.

(15) Kathañca iminā apāhaṃ siyanti hoti? Kañci dhammaṃ avakāriṃ karitvā rūpaṃ…pe… vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ iminā apāhaṃ siyanti chandaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā apāhaṃ siyanti mānaṃ paṭilabhati, iminā apāhaṃ siyanti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Tasmiṃ sati imāni papañcitāni honti – iminā apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti vā.

And how does 'Might I indeed be through this' occur? Having particularized a certain phenomenon, regarding form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness, one obtains the desire, 'Might I indeed be through this'; one obtains the conceit, 'Might I indeed be through this'; one obtains the view, 'Might I indeed be through this.' When that is present, these proliferations arise: 'Might I indeed be thus through this,' or 'Might I indeed be just so through this,' or 'Might I indeed be otherwise through this.'

(16) Kathañca iminā apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti? Iminā apāhaṃ khattiyo siyanti vā, iminā [T 0.0540] apāhaṃ brāhmaṇo siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ vesso siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ suddo siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ gahaṭṭho siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ pabbajito siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ devo siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ manusso siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ rūpī siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ arūpī siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ saññī [V 0.0468] siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ asaññī siyanti vā, iminā apāhaṃ nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā apāhaṃ itthaṃ siyanti hoti.

And how does 'Might I indeed be thus through this' occur? 'Through this might I indeed be a khattiya,' or 'Through this might I indeed be a brahmin,' or 'Through this might I indeed be a vessa,' or 'Through this might I indeed be a sudda,' or 'Through this might I indeed be a householder,' or 'Through this might I indeed be one who has gone forth,' or 'Through this might I indeed be a deva,' or 'Through this might I indeed be a human,' or 'Through this might I indeed be possessed of form,' or 'Through this might I indeed be formless,' or 'Through this might I indeed be possessed of perception,' or 'Through this might I indeed be without perception,' or 'Through this might I indeed be neither percipient nor non-percipient.' Thus does 'Might I indeed be thus through this' occur.

(17) Kathañca iminā apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā apāhaṃ tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā apāhaṃ tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā apāhaṃ tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā apāhaṃ evaṃ siyanti hoti.

And how does the attachment, 'May I indeed be so by means of this,' arise? By comparing with another person, one thinks: 'Just as that noble is by means of this, so may I indeed be a noble,' or 'Just as that brahmin is by means of this, so may I indeed be a brahmin,' ...and so on... 'Just as that one who is neither percipient nor non-percipient is by means of this, so may I indeed be neither percipient nor non-percipient.' In this way, by means of this, the attachment, 'May I indeed be so,' arises.

(18) Kathañca [M 0.0414] iminā apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti? Parapuggalaṃ [P 0.0400] upanidhāya yathā so khattiyo iminā apāhaṃ na tathā khattiyo siyanti vā, yathā so brāhmaṇo iminā apāhaṃ na tathā brāhmaṇo siyanti vā…pe… yathā so nevasaññīnāsaññī iminā apāhaṃ na tathā nevasaññīnāsaññī siyanti vā – evaṃ iminā apāhaṃ aññathā siyanti hoti.

And how does the attachment, 'May I indeed be otherwise by means of this,' arise? By comparing with another person, one thinks: 'Just as that noble is by means of this, may I indeed not be a noble in that way,' or 'Just as that brahmin is by means of this, may I indeed not be a brahmin in that way,' ...and so on... 'Just as that one who is neither percipient nor non-percipient is by means of this, may I indeed not be neither percipient nor non-percipient in that way.' In this way, by means of this, the attachment, 'May I indeed be otherwise,' arises.

Imāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni bāhirassa upādāya.

These are the eighteen wanderings of craving dependent on the external.

Iti imāni aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni ajjhattikassa upādāya, imāni [T 0.0541] aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni bāhirassa upādāya, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni honti. Iti evarūpāni atītāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, anāgatāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, paccuppannāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā aṭṭhataṇhāvicaritasataṃ hoti.

Thus, these eighteen wanderings of craving are dependent on the internal, and these eighteen wanderings of craving are dependent on the external; having gathered and condensed them together, there are thirty-six wanderings of craving. Thus, there are thirty-six such wanderings of craving in the past, thirty-six in the future, and thirty-six in the present; having gathered and condensed them together, there are one hundred and eight wanderings of craving.

977. Tattha katamāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle veyyākaraṇe vuttāni bhagavatā? Cattāro sassatavādā, cattāro ekaccasassatikā, cattāro antānantikā, cattāro amarāvikkhepikā, dve adhiccasamuppannikā, soḷasa saññīvādā, aṭṭha asaññīvādā, aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā, satta ucchedavādā, pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā – imāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle veyyākaraṇe vuttāni bhagavatāti.

977. Herein, what are the sixty-two views stated by the Blessed One in the Brahmajāla, the Exposition? Four eternalist views, four partial-eternalist views, four views on the finite and infinite, four views of the eel-wrigglers, two views on fortuitous origination, sixteen views concerning perception, eight views concerning non-perception, eight views concerning neither perception nor non-perception, seven annihilationist views, and five views on Nibbāna in this very life—these are the sixty-two views stated by the Blessed One in the Brahmajāla, the Exposition.

Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Minor Topics is concluded.

18. Dhammahadayavibhaṅgo

18. Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma

1. Sabbasaṅgāhikavāro

1. The All-Inclusive Section

978. Kati [M 0.0415][P 0.0401][V 0.0469] khandhā, kati āyatanāni, kati dhātuyo, kati saccāni, kati indriyāni, kati hetū, kati āhārā, kati phassā, kati vedanā, kati saññā, kati cetanā, kati cittāni?

1. How many aggregates, how many bases, how many elements, how many truths, how many faculties, how many roots, how many nutriments, how many contacts, how many feelings, how many perceptions, how many volitions, how many consciousnesses?

Pañcakkhandhā, dvādasāyatanāni, aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo, cattāri [T 0.0542] saccāni, bāvīsatindriyāni, nava hetū, cattāro āhārā, satta phassā, satta vedanā, satta saññā, satta cetanā, satta cittāni.

978. There are five aggregates, twelve bases, eighteen elements, four truths, twenty-two faculties, nine roots, four nutriments, seven contacts, seven feelings, seven perceptions, seven volitions, and seven consciousnesses.

979. Tattha katame pañcakkhandhā? Rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime vuccanti “pañcakkhandhā”.

Among these, what are the five aggregates? The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness—these are called the five aggregates.

980. Tattha katamāni dvādasāyatanāni? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ – imāni vuccanti “dvādasāyatanāni”.

979. Among these, what are the twelve bases? The eye-base, form-base, ear-base, sound-base, nose-base, odor-base, tongue-base, taste-base, body-base, tangible-base, mind-base, and dhamma-base—these are called the twelve bases.

981. Tattha katamā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo? Cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu[P 0.0402], gandhadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu, rasadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyadhātu, phoṭṭhabbadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – imā vuccanti “aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo”.

980. Among these, what are the eighteen elements? The eye-element, form-element, eye-consciousness-element, ear-element, sound-element, ear-consciousness-element, nose-element, odor-element, nose-consciousness-element, tongue-element, taste-element, tongue-consciousness-element, body-element, tangible-element, body-consciousness-element, mind-element, dhamma-element, and mind-consciousness-element—these are called the eighteen elements.

982. Tattha katamāni cattāri saccāni? Dukkhasaccaṃ, samudayasaccaṃ, nirodhasaccaṃ, maggasaccaṃ – imāni vuccanti “cattāri saccāni”.

981. Among these, what are the four truths? The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin of suffering, the truth of the cessation of suffering, and the truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering—these are called the four truths.

983. Tattha katamāni bāvīsatindriyāni? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ[T 0.0543], saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ, anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ – imāni vuccanti “bāvīsatindriyāni”.

982. Among these, what are the twenty-two faculties? The eye-faculty, ear-faculty, nose-faculty, tongue-faculty, body-faculty, mind-faculty, femininity-faculty, masculinity-faculty, life-faculty, pleasure-faculty, pain-faculty, joy-faculty, displeasure-faculty, equanimity-faculty, faith-faculty, energy-faculty, mindfulness-faculty, concentration-faculty, wisdom-faculty, the faculty of ‘I shall know the unknown,’ the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge—these are called the twenty-two faculties.

984. Tattha [M 0.0416] katame nava hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū.

983. Among these, what are the nine roots? Three wholesome roots, three unwholesome roots, and three indeterminate roots.

Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho kusalahetu, adoso kusalahetu, amoho kusalahetu – ime tayo kusalahetū.

984. Among these, what are the three wholesome roots? Non-greed as a wholesome root, non-hatred as a wholesome root, and non-delusion as a wholesome root—these are the three wholesome roots.

Tattha katame tayo akusalahetū? Lobho akusalahetu, doso akusalahetu, moho akusalahetu – ime tayo akusalahetū.

Among these, what are the three unwholesome roots? Greed as an unwholesome root, hatred as an unwholesome root, and delusion as an unwholesome root—these are the three unwholesome roots.

Tattha katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ vā dhammānaṃ vipākato kiriyābyākatesu vā dhammesu alobho, adoso, amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū. Ime vuccanti “nava hetū”.

Among these, what are the three indeterminate roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion, which are either the result of wholesome states or are present in functionally indeterminate states—these are the three indeterminate roots. These are called the nine roots.

985. Tattha katame cattāro āhārā? Kabaḷīkārāhāro kabaḷiṃkāro āhāro (sī. syā.), phassāhāro, manosañcetanāhāro[P 0.0403], viññāṇāhāro – ime vuccanti “cattāro āhārā”.

Among these, what are the four nutriments? Physical nutriment, contact as nutriment, mental volition as nutriment, and consciousness as nutriment—these are called the four nutriments.

986. Tattha [V 0.0471] katame satta phassā? Cakkhusamphasso, sotasamphasso, ghānasamphasso, jivhāsamphasso, kāyasamphasso, manodhātusamphasso, manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso – ime vuccanti “satta phassā”.

985. Among these, what are the seven contacts? Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-element-contact, and mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called the seven contacts.

987. Tattha katamā satta vedanā? Cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā [T 0.0544] vedanā – imā vuccanti “satta vedanā”.

987. Among these, what are the seven feelings? Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-element-contact, and feeling born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called the seven feelings.

988. Tattha katamā satta saññā? Cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā – imā vuccanti “satta saññā”.

988. Among these, what are the seven perceptions? Perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-element-contact, and perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called the seven perceptions.

989. Tattha [M 0.0417] katamā satta cetanā? Cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā – imā vuccanti “satta cetanā”.

989. Among these, what are the seven volitions? Volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, volition born of mind-element-contact, and volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called the seven volitions.

990. Tattha katamāni satta cittāni? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ[P 0.0404], kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – imāni vuccanti “satta cittāni”.

990. Among these, what are the seven consciousnesses? Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-element, and mind-consciousness-element—these are called the seven consciousnesses.

2. Uppattānuppattivāro

2. The Section on Arising and Non-Arising

1. Kāmadhātu

1. The Sense-Sphere

991. Kāmadhātuyā kati khandhā, kati āyatanāni, kati dhātuyo, kati saccāni, kati [V 0.0472] indriyāni, kati hetū, kati āhārā, kati phassā, kati vedanā, kati saññā, kati cetanā, kati cittāni?

991. In the sense-sphere, how many aggregates, how many sense bases, how many elements, how many truths, how many faculties, how many roots, how many nutriments, how many contacts, how many feelings, how many perceptions, how many volitions, and how many consciousnesses are there?

Kāmadhātuyā pañcakkhandhā, dvādasāyatanāni, aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo, tīṇi saccāni, bāvīsatindriyāni, nava hetū, cattāro āhārā, satta phassā, satta vedanā, satta saññā, satta cetanā, satta cittāni.

In the sense-sphere there are five aggregates, twelve sense bases, eighteen elements, three truths, twenty-two faculties, nine roots, four nutriments, seven contacts, seven feelings, seven perceptions, seven volitions, and seven consciousnesses.

992. Tattha katame kāmadhātuyā pañcakkhandhā? Rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā pañcakkhandhā”.

992. Therein, what are the five aggregates in the sense-sphere? The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—these are called 'the five aggregates in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katamāni kāmadhātuyā dvādasāyatanāni? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ[T 0.0545], sotāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ – imāni vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā dvādasāyatanāni”.

Therein, what are the twelve sense bases in the sense-sphere? The eye base, the form base, the ear base, the sound base, the nose base, the odor base, the tongue base, the taste base, the body base, the tangible object base, the mind base, and the mental object base—these are called 'the twelve sense bases in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katamā kāmadhātuyā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo? Cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu, gandhadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu, rasadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyadhātu, phoṭṭhabbadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu[M 0.0418], manoviññāṇadhātu – imā vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo”.

Therein, what are the eighteen elements in the sense-sphere? The eye element, the form element, and the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the sound element, and the ear-consciousness element; the nose element, the odor element, and the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the taste element, and the tongue-consciousness element; the body element, the tangible object element, and the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the mental object element, and the mind-consciousness element—these are called 'the eighteen elements in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katamāni kāmadhātuyā tīṇi saccāni? Dukkhasaccaṃ, samudayasaccaṃ, maggasaccaṃ – imāni vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā tīṇi saccāni”.

Therein, what are the three truths in the sense-sphere? The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, and the truth of the path—these are called 'the three truths in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katamāni kāmadhātuyā bāvīsatindriyāni? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ…pe… aññātāvindriyaṃ – imāni vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā bāvīsatindriyāni”.

Therein, what are the twenty-two faculties in the sense-sphere? The eye faculty, the ear faculty... up to... the faculty of one who has final knowledge—these are called 'the twenty-two faculties in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katame kāmadhātuyā nava hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū…pe… ime vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā nava hetū”.

Therein, what are the nine roots in the sense-sphere? Three wholesome roots, three unwholesome roots, and three indeterminate roots—these are called 'the nine roots in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha [P 0.0405][V 0.0473] katame kāmadhātuyā cattāro āhārā? Kabaḷīkārāhāro, phassāhāro, manosañcetanāhāro, viññāṇāhāro – ime vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā cattāro āhārā”.

Therein, what are the four nutriments in the sense-sphere? Material food, contact as nutriment, mental volition as nutriment, and consciousness as nutriment—these are called 'the four nutriments in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katame kāmadhātuyā satta phassā? Cakkhusamphasso sotasamphasso, ghānasamphasso, jivhāsamphasso, kāyasamphasso, manodhātusamphasso, manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso – ime vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā satta phassā”.

Therein, what are the seven contacts in the sense-sphere? Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-element-contact, and mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called 'the seven contacts in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katamā kāmadhātuyā satta vedanā? Cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā – imā vuccatti “kāmadhātuyā satta vedanā”.

Therein, what are the seven feelings in the sense-sphere? Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-element-contact, and feeling born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called 'the seven feelings in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katamā kāmadhātuyā satta saññā? Cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā – imā vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā satta saññā”.

Therein, what are the seven perceptions in the sense-sphere? Perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-element-contact, and perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called 'the seven perceptions in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha [M 0.0419] katamā kāmadhātuyā satta cetanā? Cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā – imā vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā satta cetanā”.

Therein, what are the seven volitions in the sense-sphere? Volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact, volition born of body-contact, volition born of mind-element-contact, and volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called 'the seven volitions in the sense-sphere'.

Tattha katamāni kāmadhātuyā satta cittāni? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – imāni vuccanti “kāmadhātuyā satta cittāni”.

Therein, what are the seven consciousnesses in the sense-sphere? Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind-element, and the mind-consciousness-element—these are called 'the seven consciousnesses in the sense-sphere'.

2. Rūpadhātu

2. The Form-Sphere

993. Rūpadhātuyā [V 0.0474] kati khandhā, kati āyatanā, kati dhātuyo, kati saccāni, kati indriyāni…pe… kati cittāni?

993. In the form-sphere, how many aggregates, how many sense bases, how many elements, how many truths, how many faculties… how many consciousnesses are there?

Rūpadhātuyā pañcakkhandhā, cha āyatanāni, nava dhātuyo, tīṇi saccāni[T 0.0546], cuddasindriyāni, aṭṭha hetū, tayo āhārā, cattāro phassā, catasso vedanā, catasso saññā, catasso cetanā, cattāri cittāni.

In the form element there are five aggregates, six sense bases, nine elements, three truths, fourteen faculties, eight roots, three nutriments, four contacts, four feelings, four perceptions, four volitions, and four consciousnesses.

994. Tattha katame rūpadhātuyā pañcakkhandhā? Rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā pañcakkhandhā”.

994. Herein, what are the five aggregates in the form element? The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—these are called “the five aggregates in the form element”.

Tattha katamāni rūpadhātuyā cha āyatanāni? Cakkhāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ – imāni vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā cha āyatanāni”.

Herein, what are the six sense bases in the form element? The eye base, the form base, the ear base, the sound base, the mind base, and the mental-object base—these are called “the six sense bases in the form element”.

Tattha katamā rūpadhātuyā nava dhātuyo? Cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – imā vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā nava dhātuyo”.

Herein, what are the nine elements in the form element? The eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, the mind element, the mental-object element, and the mind-consciousness element—these are called “the nine elements in the form element”.

Tattha katamāni rūpadhātuyā tīṇi saccāni? Dukkhasaccaṃ, samudayasaccaṃ, maggasaccaṃ – imāni vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā tīṇi saccāni”.

Herein, what are the three truths in the form element? The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, and the truth of the path—these are called “the three truths in the form element”.

Tattha [M 0.0420] katamāni rūpadhātuyā cuddasindriyāni? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ[P 0.0406], upekkhindriyaṃ, saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ, anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ – imāni vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā cuddasindriyāni”.

Herein, what are the fourteen faculties in the form element? The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the mind faculty, the life faculty, the joy faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, the wisdom faculty, the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown', the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge—these are called “the fourteen faculties in the form element”.

Tattha [V 0.0475] katame rūpadhātuyā aṭṭha hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, dve akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū.

Herein, what are the eight roots in the form element? Three wholesome roots, two unwholesome roots, and three indeterminate roots.

Tattha katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho kusalahetu, adoso kusalahetu, amoho kusalahetu – ime tayo kusalahetū.

Herein, what are the three wholesome roots? Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hatred is a wholesome root, and non-delusion is a wholesome root—these are the three wholesome roots.

Tattha katame dve akusalahetū? Lobho akusalahetu, moho akusalahetu – ime dve akusalahetū.

Herein, what are the two unwholesome roots? Greed is an unwholesome root, and delusion is an unwholesome root—these are the two unwholesome roots.

Tattha katame [T 0.0547] tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ vā dhammānaṃ vipākato kiriyābyākatesu vā dhammesu alobho, adoso, amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū. Ime vuccanti rūpadhātuyā aṭṭha hetū.

Herein, what are the three indeterminate roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion, as the resultant of wholesome states or in functional indeterminate states—these are the three indeterminate roots. These are called “the eight roots in the form element”.

Tattha katame rūpadhātuyā tayo āhārā? Phassāhāro, manosañcetanāhāro, viññāṇāhāro – ime vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā tayo āhārā”.

Herein, what are the three nutriments in the form element? Contact as nutriment, mental volition as nutriment, and consciousness as nutriment—these are called “the three nutriments in the form element”.

Tattha katame rūpadhātuyā cattāro phassā? Cakkhusamphasso, sotasamphasso, manodhātusamphasso, manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso – ime vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā cattāro phassā”.

Herein, what are the four contacts in the form element? Eye-contact, ear-contact, mind-element-contact, and mind-consciousness-element-contact—these are called “the four contacts in the form element”.

Tattha katamā rūpadhātuyā catasso vedanā…pe… catasso saññā…pe… catasso cetanā…pe… cattāri cittāni? Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃ, manodhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – imāni vuccanti “rūpadhātuyā cattāri cittāni”.

Herein, what are the four feelings in the form element… the four perceptions… the four volitions… the four consciousnesses? Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element—these are called “the four consciousnesses in the form element”.

3. Arūpadhātu

3. The Formless Element

995. Arūpadhātuyā [M 0.0421] kati khandhā…pe… kati cittāni?

3. In the formless element, how many aggregates… and so on… how many consciousnesses?

Arūpadhātuyā cattāro khandhā, dve āyatanāni, dve dhātuyo, tīṇi saccāni, ekādasindriyāni[V 0.0476], aṭṭha hetū, tayo āhārā, eko phasso, ekā vedanā, ekā saññā, ekā cetanā, ekaṃ cittaṃ.

995. In the formless element, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, three truths, eleven faculties, eight roots, three nutriments, one contact, one feeling, one perception, one volition, and one consciousness.

996. Tattha [P 0.0407] katame arūpadhātuyā cattāro khandhā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime vuccanti “arūpadhātuyā cattāro khandhā”.

Therein, what are the four aggregates in the formless element? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—these are called “the four aggregates in the formless element”.

Tattha katamāni arūpadhātuyā dve āyatanāni? Manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ – imāni vuccanti “arūpadhātuyā dve āyatanāni”.

996. Therein, what are the two bases in the formless element? The mind base and the mental-object base—these are called “the two bases in the formless element”.

Tattha katamā arūpadhātuyā dve dhātuyo? Manoviññāṇadhātu[T 0.0548], dhammadhātu – imā vuccanti “arūpadhātuyā dve dhātuyo”.

Therein, what are the two elements in the formless element? The mind-consciousness element and the mental-object element—these are called “the two elements in the formless element”.

Tattha katamāni arūpadhātuyā tīṇi saccāni? Dukkhasaccaṃ, samudayasaccaṃ, maggasaccaṃ – imāni vuccanti “arūpadhātuyā tīṇi saccāni”.

Therein, what are the three truths in the formless element? The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, and the truth of the path—these are called “the three truths in the formless element”.

Tattha katamāni arūpadhātuyā ekādasindriyāni? Manindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ, saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ – imāni vuccanti “arūpadhātuyā ekādasindriyāni”.

Therein, what are the eleven faculties in the formless element? The mind faculty, the life faculty, the joy faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, the wisdom faculty, the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge—these are called “the eleven faculties in the formless element”.

Tattha katame arūpadhātuyā aṭṭha hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, dve akusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū…pe… ime vuccanti “arūpadhātuyā aṭṭha hetū”.

Therein, what are the eight roots in the formless element? Three wholesome roots, two unwholesome roots, and three indeterminate roots… these are called “the eight roots in the formless element”.

Tattha katame arūpadhātuyā tayo āhārā? Phassāhāro, manosañcetanāhāro, viññāṇāhāro – ime vuccanti “arūpadhātuyā tayo āhārā”.

Therein, what are the three nutriments in the formless element? Contact as nutriment, mental volition as nutriment, and consciousness as nutriment—these are called “the three nutriments in the formless element”.

Tattha katamo arūpadhātuyā eko phasso? Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso – ayaṃ vuccati “arūpadhātuyā eko phasso”.

Therein, what is the one contact in the formless element? Mind-consciousness-element-contact—this is called “the one contact in the formless element”.

Tattha [M 0.0422][V 0.0477] katamā arūpadhātuyā ekā vedanā…pe… ekā saññā…pe… ekā cetanā…pe… ekaṃ cittaṃ? Manoviññāṇadhātu – idaṃ vuccati “arūpadhātuyā ekaṃ cittaṃ”.

Therein, what is the one feeling in the formless element?… and so on… the one perception… and so on… the one volition… and so on… the one consciousness? The mind-consciousness element—this is called “the one consciousness in the formless element”.

4. Apariyāpannaṃ

4. The Unincluded

997. Apariyāpanne kati khandhā…pe… kati cittāni?

In the unincluded, how many aggregates are there… and so on… how many consciousnesses?

Apariyāpanne cattāro khandhā, dve āyatanāni, dve dhātuyo, dve saccāni, dvādasindriyāni, cha hetū, tayo āhārā, eko [P 0.0408] phasso, ekā vedanā, ekā saññā, ekā cetanā, ekaṃ cittaṃ.

4. In the unincluded, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, two truths, twelve faculties, six roots, three nutriments, one contact, one feeling, one perception, one volition, and one consciousness.

998. Tattha katame apariyāpanne cattāro khandhā? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho[T 0.0549], saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho – ime vuccanti “apariyāpanne cattāro khandhā”.

998. Herein, what are the four aggregates in the unincluded? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—these are called 'the four aggregates in the unincluded'.

Tattha katamāni apariyāpanne dve āyatanāni? Manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ – imāni vuccanti “apariyāpanne dve āyatanāni”.

Herein, what are the two bases in the unincluded? The mind base and the phenomena base—these are called 'the two bases in the unincluded'.

Tattha katamā apariyāpanne dve dhātuyo? Manoviññāṇadhātu, dhammadhātu – imā vuccanti “apariyāpanne dve dhātuyo”.

Herein, what are the two elements in the unincluded? The mind-consciousness element and the phenomena element—these are called 'the two elements in the unincluded'.

Tattha katamāni apariyāpanne dve saccāni? Maggasaccaṃ, nirodhasaccaṃ – imāni vuccanti “apariyāpanne dve saccāni”.

Herein, what are the two truths in the unincluded? The truth of the path and the truth of cessation—these are called 'the two truths in the unincluded'.

Tattha katamāni apariyāpanne dvādasindriyāni? Manindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ, saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ, anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ – imāni vuccanti “apariyāpanne dvādasindriyāni”.

Herein, what are the twelve faculties in the unincluded? The faculty of mind, the faculty of life, the faculty of joy, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of 'I shall know the unknown', the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has finally known—these are called 'the twelve faculties in the unincluded'.

Tattha katame apariyāpanne cha hetū? Tayo kusalahetū, tayo abyākatahetū.

Herein, what are the six roots in the unincluded? Three wholesome roots and three indeterminate roots.

Tattha [V 0.0478] katame tayo kusalahetū? Alobho kusalahetu, adoso kusalahetu, amoho kusalahetu – ime tayo kusalahetū.

Herein, what are the three wholesome roots? The wholesome root of non-greed, the wholesome root of non-hatred, and the wholesome root of non-delusion—these are the three wholesome roots.

Tattha [M 0.0423] katame tayo abyākatahetū? Kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākato alobho, adoso, amoho – ime tayo abyākatahetū. Ime vuccanti “apariyāpanne cha hetū”.

Herein, what are the three indeterminate roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion as the result of wholesome states—these are the three indeterminate roots. These are called 'the six roots in the unincluded'.

Tattha katame apariyāpanne tayo āhārā? Phassāhāro, manosañcetanāhāro, viññāṇāhāro – ime vuccanti “apariyāpanne tayo āhārā”.

Herein, what are the three nutriments in the unincluded? The nutriment of contact, the nutriment of mental volition, and the nutriment of consciousness—these are called 'the three nutriments in the unincluded'.

Tattha katamo apariyāpanne eko phasso? Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso – ayaṃ vuccati “apariyāpanne eko phasso”.

Herein, what is the one contact in the unincluded? Contact of the mind-consciousness element—this is called 'the one contact in the unincluded'.

Tattha [T 0.0550] katamā apariyāpanne ekā vedanā…pe… ekā saññā…pe… ekā cetanā…pe… ekaṃ cittaṃ? Manoviññāṇadhātu [P 0.0409] – idaṃ vuccati “apariyāpanne ekaṃ cittaṃ”.

Herein, what is the one feeling in the unincluded?… and so on… the one perception… and so on… the one volition… and so on… the one consciousness? The mind-consciousness element—this is called 'the one consciousness in the unincluded'.

3. Pariyāpannāpariyāpannavāro

3. The Section on the Included and the Unincluded

1. Kāmadhātu

1. The Sensuous Realm

999. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati kāmadhātupariyāpannā, kati na kāmadhātupariyāpannā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati kāmadhātupariyāpannā, kati na kāmadhātupariyāpannā?

999. Of the five aggregates, how many are included in the sensuous realm, and how many are not included in the sensuous realm?… and so on… Of the seven consciousnesses, how many are included in the sensuous realm, and how many are not included in the sensuous realm?

1000. Rūpakkhandho kāmadhātupariyāpanno; cattāro khandhā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

1000. The aggregate of form is included in the sensuous realm; the four aggregates may be included in the sensuous realm, or they may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Dasāyatanā [V 0.0479] kāmadhātupariyāpannā; dve āyatanā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

Ten bases are included in the sensuous realm; two bases may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Soḷasa dhātuyo kāmadhātupariyāpannā; dve dhātuyo siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

Sixteen elements are included in the sensuous realm; two elements may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Samudayasaccaṃ kāmadhātupariyāpannaṃ; dve saccā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā; dukkhasaccaṃ siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannaṃ, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannaṃ.

The truth of the origin is included in the sensuous realm; two truths are not included in the sensuous realm; the truth of suffering may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Dasindriyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā; tīṇindriyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā; navindriyā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

Ten faculties are included in the sensuous realm; three faculties are not included in the sensuous realm; nine faculties may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Tayo akusalahetū kāmadhātupariyāpannā; cha hetū siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

Three unwholesome roots are included in the sensuous realm; six roots may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Kabaḷīkāro [M 0.0424] āhāro kāmadhātupariyāpanno; tayo āhārā siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

Physical nutriment is included in the sensuous realm; the three nutriments may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Cha phassā kāmadhātupariyāpannā; manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso [T 0.0551] siyā kāmadhātu pariyāpanno, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpanno.

Six contacts are included in the sensuous realm; contact of the mind-consciousness element may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

Cha vedanā…pe… cha saññā… cha cetanā… cha cittā kāmadhātupariyāpannā; manoviññāṇadhātu siyā kāmadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na kāmadhātupariyāpannā.

Six feelings… and so on… six perceptions… six volitions… six consciousnesses are included in the sensuous realm; the mind-consciousness element may be included in the sensuous realm, or may not be included in the sensuous realm.

2. Rūpadhātu

2. The Form Realm

1001. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati rūpadhātupariyāpannā, kati na rūpadhātupariyāpannā [V 0.0480] …pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati rūpadhātupariyāpannā, kati na rūpadhātupariyāpannā?

1001. Of the five aggregates, how many are included in the form realm, and how many are not included in the form realm? …and so on… Of the seven consciousnesses, how many are included in the form realm, and how many are not included in the form realm?

1002. Rūpakkhandho na rūpadhātupariyāpanno; cattāro khandhā [P 0.0410] siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā.

1002. The aggregate of form is not included in the form realm; the four aggregates may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Dasāyatanā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā; dve āyatanā siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Ten bases are not included in the form realm; two bases may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Soḷasa dhātuyo na rūpadhātupariyāpannā; dve dhātuyo siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Sixteen elements are not included in the form realm; two elements may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Tīṇi saccāni na rūpadhātupariyāpannā; dukkhasaccaṃ siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannaṃ, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannaṃ.

Three truths are not included in the form realm; the truth of suffering may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Terasindriyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā; navindriyā siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Thirteen faculties are not included in the form realm; nine faculties may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Tayo akusalahetū na rūpadhātupariyāpannā; cha hetū siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Three unwholesome roots are not included in the form realm; six roots may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Kabaḷīkāro āhāro na rūpadhātupariyāpanno; tayo āhārā siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Physical nutriment is not included in the form realm; the three nutriments may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Cha phassā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā; manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā rūpadhātupariyāpanno, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpanno.

Six contacts are not included in the form realm; contact of the mind-consciousness element may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

Cha [T 0.0552][M 0.0425][V 0.0481] vedanā…pe… cha saññā… cha cetanā… cha cittā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā; manoviññāṇadhātu siyā rūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na rūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Six feelings… and so on… six perceptions… six volitions… six consciousnesses are not included in the form realm; the mind-consciousness element may be included in the form realm, or may not be included in the form realm.

3. Arūpadhātu

3. The Immaterial Realm

1003. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati arūpadhātupariyāpannā, kati na arūpadhātupariyāpannā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati arūpadhātupariyāpannā, kati na arūpadhātupariyāpannā?

1003. Of the five aggregates, how many are included in the immaterial realm, and how many are not included in the immaterial realm?…pe… Of the seven consciousnesses, how many are included in the immaterial realm, and how many are not included in the immaterial realm?

1004. Rūpakkhandho na arūpadhātupariyāpanno; cattāro khandhā siyā arūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā.

1004. The form aggregate is not included in the immaterial realm; the four aggregates are sometimes included in the immaterial realm, and sometimes not included in the immaterial realm.

Dasāyatanā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā; dve āyatanā siyā arūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Ten bases are not included in the immaterial realm; two bases are sometimes included in the immaterial realm, and sometimes not included in the immaterial realm.

Soḷasa dhātuyo na arūpadhātupariyāpannā; dve dhātuyo siyā arūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Sixteen elements are not included in the immaterial realm; two elements are sometimes included in the immaterial realm, and sometimes not included in the immaterial realm.

Tīṇi saccāni na arūpadhātupariyāpannāni.

Three truths are not included in the immaterial realm.

Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā arūpadhātupariyāpannaṃ, siyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannaṃ.

The truth of suffering is sometimes included in the immaterial realm, and sometimes not included in the immaterial realm.

Cuddasindriyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā; aṭṭhindriyā siyā [P 0.0411] arūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Fourteen faculties are not included in the immaterial realm; eight faculties are sometimes included in the immaterial realm, and sometimes not included in the immaterial realm.

Tayo akusalahetū na arūpadhātupariyāpannā; cha hetū siyā arūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Three unwholesome roots are not included in the immaterial realm; six roots are sometimes included in the immaterial realm, and sometimes not included in the immaterial realm.

Kabaḷīkāro [V 0.0482] āhāro na arūpadhātupariyāpanno; tayo āhārā siyā arūpadhātupariyāpannā, siyā na arūpadhātupariyāpannā.

Physical nutriment is not included in the immaterial realm; three nutriments are sometimes included in the immaterial realm, and sometimes not included in the immaterial realm.
