Rūpakkhandho abyākato. Cattāro khandhā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dasāyatanā abyākatā. Dvāyatanā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Soḷasa dhātuyo [M 0.0446] abyākatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Samudayasaccaṃ akusalaṃ. Maggasaccaṃ kusalaṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ abyākataṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā kusalaṃ, siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ.

The aggregate of form is indeterminate. The four [mental] aggregates are sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate. Ten bases are indeterminate. Two bases are sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate. Sixteen elements are indeterminate. Two elements are sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate. The truth of origin is unwholesome. The truth of the path is wholesome. The truth of cessation is indeterminate. The truth of suffering is sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate.

Dasindriyā [T 0.0579] abyākatā. Domanassindriyaṃ akusalaṃ. Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ kusalaṃ. Cattārindriyā siyā kusalā, siyā abyākatā. Cha indriyā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā.

Ten faculties are indeterminate. The faculty of displeasure is unwholesome. The faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown' is wholesome. Four faculties are sometimes wholesome and sometimes indeterminate. Six faculties are sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate.

Tayo kusalahetū kusalā. Tayo akusalahetū akusalā. Tayo abyākatahetū abyākatā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro abyākato. Tayo āhārā siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Cha phassā abyākatā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā kusalo, siyā akusalo, siyā abyākato. Cha vedanā… cha saññā… cha cetanā… cha cittā abyākatā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā.

Three wholesome roots are wholesome. Three unwholesome roots are unwholesome. Three indeterminate roots are indeterminate. Physical nutriment is indeterminate. Three nutriments are sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate. Six contacts are indeterminate. Contact of the mind-consciousness element is sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate. Six feelings, six perceptions, six volitions, and six consciousnesses are indeterminate. The mind-consciousness element is sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, and sometimes indeterminate.

2. Vedanātikaṃ

2. The Triad of Feeling

1039. Pañcannaṃ [V 0.0505] khandhānaṃ kati sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kati adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā?

1039. Of the five aggregates, how many are associated with pleasant feeling, how many are associated with painful feeling, and how many are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? …and so on… Of the seven consciousnesses, how many are associated with pleasant feeling, how many are associated with painful feeling, and how many are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?

Dve khandhā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Tayo khandhā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā.

Two aggregates should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Three aggregates may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Dasāyatanā [P 0.0431] na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Manāyatanaṃ siyā [T 0.0580] sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya [M 0.0447] sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi.

The ten sense bases should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The mind-base may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The dhamma-base may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, or it should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Dasa dhātuyo na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Pañca dhātuyo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kāyaviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Dhammadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi.

The ten elements should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Five elements are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The body-consciousness element may be associated with pleasant feeling or may be associated with painful feeling. The mind-consciousness element may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The dhamma-element may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, or it should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Dve [V 0.0506] saccā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Nirodhasaccaṃ na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya [T 0.0581] sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi.

Two truths may be associated with pleasant feeling or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The truth of cessation should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The truth of suffering may be associated with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; or it should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Dvādasindriyā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Cha indriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Tīṇindriyā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā[P 0.0432], siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttantipi.

Twelve faculties should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Six faculties may be associated with pleasant feeling or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Three faculties may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The life faculty may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, or it should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Doso [M 0.0448] akusalahetu dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Satta hetū siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Moho akusalahetu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, siyā dukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto.

Hatred, an unwholesome root, is associated with painful feeling. Seven roots may be associated with pleasant feeling or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Delusion, an unwholesome root, may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Kabaḷīkāro āhāro na vattabbo sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttoti pi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttotipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttotipi. Tayo āhārā siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā.

Physical food should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The three foods may be associated with pleasant feeling, may be associated with painful feeling, or may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Pañca phassā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Kāyaviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā [T 0.0582] sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā [V 0.0507] sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto.

Five contacts are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Contact of the body-consciousness element may be associated with pleasant feeling or with painful feeling. Contact of the mind-consciousness element may be associated with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

Satta vedanā na vattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttātipi. Pañca saññā… pañca cetanā… pañca cittā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, kāyaviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā.

Seven feelings should not be said to be associated with pleasant feeling, nor with painful feeling, nor with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Five perceptions... five volitions... five consciousnesses are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The body-consciousness element may be associated with pleasant feeling or with painful feeling. The mind-consciousness element may be associated with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

3. Vipākattikaṃ

3. The Triad on Results

1040. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati vipākā, kati vipākadhammadhammā, kati nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati vipākā, kati vipākadhammadhammā, kati nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā?

1040. Of the five aggregates, how many are results, how many are result-producing phenomena, and how many are neither results nor result-producing phenomena? ... Of the seven types of consciousness, how many are results, how many are result-producing phenomena, and how many are neither results nor result-producing phenomena?

Rūpakkhandho nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Cattāro khandhā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

The aggregate of form is neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon. The four aggregates may be results, may be result-producing phenomena, or may be neither results nor result-producing phenomena.

Dasāyatanā [M 0.0449][P 0.0433] nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Dvāyatanā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

The ten bases are neither results nor result-producing phenomena. The two bases may be results, may be result-producing phenomena, or may be neither results nor result-producing phenomena.

Dasa dhātuyo nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Pañca dhātuyo vipākā. Manodhātu siyā vipākā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Dve dhātuyo siyā vipākā siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

The ten elements are neither results nor result-producing phenomena. The five elements are results. The mind-element may be a result, or may be neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon. The two elements may be results, may be result-producing phenomena, or may be neither results nor result-producing phenomena.

Dve [T 0.0583] saccā vipākadhammadhammā. Nirodhasaccaṃ nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā vipākaṃ, siyā vipākadhammadhammaṃ, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṃ.

The two truths are result-producing phenomena. The truth of cessation is neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon. The truth of suffering may be a result, may be a result-producing phenomenon, or may be neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon.

Sattindriyā [V 0.0508] nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Tīṇindriyā vipākā. Dvindriyā vipākadhammadhammā. Aññindriyaṃ siyā vipākaṃ, siyā vipākadhammadhammaṃ. Navindriyā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

The seven faculties are neither results nor result-producing phenomena. The three faculties are results. The two faculties are result-producing phenomena. The faculty of final knowledge may be a result, or may be a result-producing phenomenon. The nine faculties may be results, may be result-producing phenomena, or may be neither results nor result-producing phenomena.

Cha hetū vipākadhammadhammā. Tayo abyākatahetū siyā vipākā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

The six roots are result-producing phenomena. The three indeterminate roots may be results, or may be neither results nor result-producing phenomena.

Kabaḷīkāro āhāro nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Tayo āhārā siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Pañca phassā vipākā. Manodhātusamphasso siyā vipāko, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā vipāko, siyā vipākadhammadhammo, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Pañca vedanā… pañca saññā… pañca cetanā… pañca cittā vipākā. Manodhātu siyā vipākā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā.

Edible food is neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon. The three nutriments may be results, may be result-producing phenomena, or may be neither results nor result-producing phenomena. The five contacts are results. Contact of the mind-element may be a result, or may be neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon. Contact of the mind-consciousness-element may be a result, may be a result-producing phenomenon, or may be neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon. The five feelings… the five perceptions… the five volitions… the five consciousnesses are results. The mind-element may be a result, or may be neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon. The mind-consciousness-element may be a result, may be a result-producing phenomenon, or may be neither a result nor a result-producing phenomenon.

4. Upādinnattikaṃ

4. The Triad on States Produced by Kamma

1041. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati upādinnupādāniyā, kati anupādinnupādāniyā, kati anupādinnaanupādāniyā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati upādinnupādāniyā, kati anupādinnupādāniyā, kati anupādinnaanupādāniyā?

1041. Of the five aggregates, how many are produced by kamma and subject to clinging, how many are not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and how many are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging? … Of the seven types of consciousness, how many are produced by kamma and subject to clinging, how many are not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and how many are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging?

Rūpakkhandho [M 0.0450] siyā upādinnupādāniyo, siyā anupādinnupādāniyo [T 0.0584]4. Cattāro khandhā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

The aggregate of form is in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, and in some cases not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. The four mental aggregates are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and in some cases are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging.

Pañcāyatanā [P 0.0434] upādinnupādāniyā. Saddāyatanaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Cattāro āyatanā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā. Dvāyatanā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

Five bases are produced by kamma and subject to clinging. The sound base is not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. Four bases are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, and in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging. Two bases are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and in some cases are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging.

Dasa [V 0.0509] dhātuyo upādinnupādāniyā. Saddadhātu anupādinnupādāniyā. Pañca dhātuyo siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

Ten elements are produced by kamma and subject to clinging. The sound element is not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. Five elements are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, and in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging. Two elements are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and in some cases are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging.

Samudayasaccaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Dve saccā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā upādinnupādāniyaṃ, siyā anupādinnupādāniyaṃ.

The truth of the origin is not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. Two truths are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging. The truth of suffering is in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, and in some cases not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging.

Navindriyā upādinnupādāniyā. Domanassindriyaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Tīṇindriyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Navindriyā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Tayo akusalahetū anupādinnupādāniyā. Tayo kusalahetū siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. Tayo abyākatahetū siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

Nine faculties are produced by kamma and subject to clinging. The faculty of displeasure is not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. Three faculties are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging. Nine faculties are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and in some cases are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging. The three unwholesome roots are not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging. The three wholesome roots are in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and in some cases are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging. The three indeterminate roots are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and in some cases are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging.

Kabaḷīkāro āhāro siyā upādinnupādāniyo, siyā anupādinnupādāniyo. Tayo āhārā siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā[T 0.0585].

Edible food is in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, and in some cases not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. The three other nutriments are in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but are subject to clinging, and in some cases are neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging.

Pañca phassā upādinnupādāniyā. Manodhātusamphasso siyā upādinnupādāniyo, siyā anupādinnupādāniyo. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā upādinnupādāniyo, siyā anupādinnupādāniyo, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Pañca vedanā… pañca saññā… pañca cetanā… pañca cittā upādinnupādāniyā. Manodhātu siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā.

Five contacts are produced by kamma and subject to clinging. Mind-element contact is in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, and in some cases not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. Mind-consciousness-element contact is in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging, and in some cases is neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging. Five feelings… five perceptions… five volitions… five consciousnesses are produced by kamma and subject to clinging. The mind-element is in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, and in some cases not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging. The mind-consciousness-element is in some cases produced by kamma and subject to clinging, in some cases not produced by kamma but is subject to clinging, and in some cases is neither produced by kamma nor subject to clinging.

5. Vitakkattikaṃ

5. The Triad of Applied Thought

1042. Pañcannaṃ [M 0.0451] khandhānaṃ kati savitakkasavicārā, kati avitakkavicāramattā, kati [V 0.0510] avitakkaavicārā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati savitakkasavicārā, kati avitakkavicāramattā, kati avitakkaavicārā?

1042. Of the five aggregates, how many are with applied thought and with sustained thought, how many are without applied thought but with sustained thought only, and how many are without applied thought and without sustained thought? … Of the seven consciousnesses, how many are with applied thought and with sustained thought, how many are without applied thought but with sustained thought only, and how many are without applied thought and without sustained thought?

Rūpakkhandho avitakkaavicāro. Tayo khandhā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Saṅkhārakkhandho siyā savitakkasavicāro, siyā avitakkavicāramatto, siyā avitakkaavicāro siyā na vattabbo savitakkasavicārotipi[P 0.0435], avitakkavicāramattotipi, avitakkaavicārotipi.

The aggregate of form is without applied thought and without sustained thought. Three aggregates may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, may be without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or may be without applied thought and without sustained thought. The aggregate of formations may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought; or it is a case where it should not be said that it is with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Dasāyatanā avitakkaavicārā. Manāyatanaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ savitakkasavicārantipi, avitakkavicāramattantipi, avitakkaavicārantipi.

Ten sense bases are without applied thought and without sustained thought. The mind-base may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. The dhamma-base may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought; or it is not to be said that it is with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Pannarasa dhātuyo avitakkaavicārā. Manodhātu [T 0.0586] savitakkasavicārā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Dhammadhātu siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā, siyā na vattabbā savitakkasavicārātipi, avitakkavicāramattātipi, avitakkaavicārātipi.

Fifteen elements are without applied thought and without sustained thought. The mind-element is with applied thought and with sustained thought. The mind-consciousness-element may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. The dhamma-element may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought; or it is not to be said that it is with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Samudayasaccaṃ savitakkasavicāraṃ. Nirodhasaccaṃ avitakkaavicāraṃ. Maggasaccaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkavicāramattaṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ, siyā na vattabbaṃ savitakkasavicārantipi, avitakkavicāramattantipi, avitakkaavicārantipi.

The truth of origin is with applied thought and with sustained thought. The truth of cessation is without applied thought and without sustained thought. The truth of the path may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. The truth of suffering may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought; or it is not to be said that it is with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Navindriyā avitakkaavicārā. Domanassindriyaṃ savitakkasavicāraṃ. Upekkhindriyaṃ siyā savitakkasavicāraṃ, siyā avitakkaavicāraṃ. Ekādasindriyā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā.

Nine faculties are without applied thought and without sustained thought. The faculty of displeasure is with applied thought and with sustained thought. The faculty of equanimity may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. Eleven faculties may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Tayo [M 0.0452][V 0.0511] akusalahetū savitakkasavicārā. Cha hetū siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro avitakkaavicāro. Tayo āhārā siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Pañca phassā avitakkaavicārā. Manodhātusamphasso savitakkasavicāro. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā savitakkasavicāro, siyā avitakkavicāramatto, siyā avitakkaavicāro. Pañca vedanā… pañca saññā… pañca cetanā… pañca cittā avitakkaavicārā manodhātu savitakkasavicārā[T 0.0587], manoviññāṇadhātu siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā.

The three unwholesome roots are with applied thought and with sustained thought. Six roots may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. Physical nutriment is without applied thought and without sustained thought. The three nutriments may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. The five contacts are without applied thought and without sustained thought. Contact associated with the mind-element is with applied thought and with sustained thought. Contact associated with the mind-consciousness-element may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought. The five feelings… the five perceptions… the five volitions… the five consciousnesses are without applied thought and without sustained thought. The mind-element is with applied thought and with sustained thought. The mind-consciousness-element may be with applied thought and with sustained thought, or without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or without applied thought and without sustained thought.

(1) Rūpadukaṃ

(1) The Dyad of Materiality

1043. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati rūpā, kati arūpā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati rūpā, kati arūpā?

1043. Of the five aggregates, how many are material, how many are immaterial?… Of the seven consciousnesses, how many are material, how many are immaterial?

Rūpakkhandho rūpaṃ. Cattāro khandhā arūpā. Dasāyatanā [P 0.0436] rūpā. Manāyatanaṃ arūpaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ siyā rūpaṃ, siyā arūpaṃ. Dasa dhātuyo rūpā. Satta dhātuyo arūpā. Dhammadhātu siyā rūpā, siyā arūpā. Tīṇi saccāni arūpā. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā rūpaṃ, siyā arūpaṃ. Sattindriyā rūpā. Cuddasindriyā arūpā. Jīvitindriyaṃ siyā rūpaṃ, siyā arūpaṃ. Nava hetū arūpā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro rūpaṃ. Tayo āhārā arūpā. Satta phassā arūpā. Satta vedanā… satta saññā… satta cetanā satta cittā arūpā.

The aggregate of materiality is material. The four aggregates are immaterial. Ten sense bases are material. The mind-base is immaterial. The dhamma-base may be material or may be immaterial. Ten elements are material. Seven elements are immaterial. The dhamma-element may be material or may be immaterial. Three truths are immaterial. The truth of suffering may be material or may be immaterial. Seven faculties are material. Fourteen faculties are immaterial. The life faculty may be material or may be immaterial. Nine roots are immaterial. Physical nutriment is material. The three nutriments are immaterial. Seven contacts are immaterial. Seven feelings… seven perceptions… seven volitions… seven consciousnesses are immaterial.

(2) Lokiyadukaṃ

(2) The Mundane Dyad

1044. Pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā? Dvādasannaṃ āyatanānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā? Aṭṭhārasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā? Catunnaṃ saccānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā…pe… sattannaṃ cittānaṃ kati lokiyā, kati lokuttarā?

1044. Of the five aggregates, how many are mundane, how many supramundane? Of the twelve sense bases, how many are mundane, how many supramundane? Of the eighteen elements, how many are mundane, how many supramundane? Of the four truths, how many are mundane, how many supramundane?… Of the seven consciousnesses, how many are mundane, how many supramundane?

Rūpakkhandho lokiyo. Cattāro khandhā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Dasāyatanā lokiyā[V 0.0512]. Dve āyatanā siyā lokiyā[M 0.0453], siyā lokuttarā. Soḷasa dhātuyo lokiyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Dve saccā lokiyā. Dve saccā lokuttarā.

The aggregate of materiality is mundane. The four aggregates may be mundane or may be supramundane. Ten sense bases are mundane. Two sense bases may be mundane or may be supramundane. Sixteen elements are mundane. Two elements may be mundane or may be supramundane. Two truths are mundane. Two truths are supramundane.

Dasindriyā lokiyā. Tīṇindriyā lokuttarā. Navindriyā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Tayo akusalahetū lokiyā. Cha hetū siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro lokiyo. Tayo āhārā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā[T 0.0588]. Cha phassā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphasso siyā lokiyo, siyā lokuttaro. Cha vedanā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Cha saññā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Cha cetanā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarā. Cha cittā lokiyā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā lokiyā, siyā lokuttarāti.

Ten faculties are mundane. Three faculties are supramundane. Nine faculties may be mundane or may be supramundane. Three unwholesome roots are mundane. Six roots may be mundane or may be supramundane. Physical nutriment is mundane. Three nutriments may be mundane or may be supramundane. Six contacts are mundane. Contact of the mind-consciousness-element may be mundane or may be supramundane. Six feelings are mundane. Feeling born of contact of the mind-consciousness-element may be mundane or may be supramundane. Six perceptions are mundane. Perception born of contact of the mind-consciousness-element may be mundane or may be supramundane. Six volitions are mundane. Volition born of contact of the mind-consciousness-element may be mundane or may be supramundane. Six consciousnesses are mundane. The mind-consciousness-element may be mundane or may be supramundane.

Abhiññā dve sārammaṇā, diṭṭhā kusalavedanā;

Vipākā ca upādinnā, vitakkaṃ rūpalokiyāti.

The [triad] of what is to be directly known, the two dyads concerning objects, the seen [triad], the wholesome [triad], the feeling [triad]; the resultant [triad] and the clung-to [triad], the applied thought [triad], the materiality [dyad], and the mundane [dyad].

Dhammahadayavibhaṅgo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma is concluded.

Vibhaṅgapakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Book of Analysis is concluded.
